c1.text: Stems conspicuously jointed, bearing at each joint a small whorl of black or red-brown leaves (sometimes white-margined) that are united at the base; sporangia aggregated in a terminal strobilus [Fig. ], borne on the underside of peltate sporangiophores
Stems not conspicuously jointed, the leaves not arranged in distinct and remote whorls; sporangia aggregated in a terminal strobilus or not, but never borne on peltate sporangiophores

c2.text: Leaves or entire plant floating on the surface of the water (or stranded on mud as water levels decline); sporangia borne in sporocarps
Leaves not floating on surface of water (though often borne below the surface in Isoetaceae); sporangia borne on the surface of leaves, sometimes ± concealed

c3.text: Plants rooted in the substrate, with 4-parted, clover-like leaves
Plants free-floating, with simple leaves

c4.text: Floating leaf blades mostly 5–15 mm long, with abundant and conspicuous branched hairs on the upper surface
Floating leaf blades 0.5–0.6 (–2) mm long, papillose, but lacking hairs on the upper surface

c5.text: Leaves narrow, with unexpanded, grass-like or quill-like blades; sporangia embedded in the leaf bases near the surface of the substrate [Fig. ]; plants aquatic
Leaves various, but not quill-like; sporangia variously positioned, but usually elevated above the substrate; plants of upland or wetland communities

c6.text: Plants entirely filamentous, forming felt-like colonies on rock, in caves, and under sheltered overhangs
Plants not filamentous, with moss-like or fern-like aspect, on various substrates

c7.text: Leaves small, up to 1.1 cm long, scale-like, with a single midvein; sporangia usually aggregated in a terminal strobili (arranged in alternating zones on the shoot in the Huperziaceae)
Leaves 1–200 cm long, foliaceous, prominently veined; sporangia variously organized, but not borne in terminal strobili

c8.text: Strobili quadrangular in cross-section (terete in Selaginella selaginoides ); leaves with a small, adaxial ligule; spores of 2 sizes, the larger more than 0.3 mm wide
Strobili terete in cross-section or the sporophylls not aggregated into a strobilus; leaves without a ligule; spores of 1 size, less than 0.05 mm wide

c9.text: Sporophylls aggregated in a terminal strobilus [Figs. , ], stalked, with lateral membranes, senescing after spore dispersal; gemmiphores not produced; plants anisotomously branched

Sporophylls arranged in alternating zones on the shoot [Fig. ], unstalked, without lateral membranes, remaining green for the life of the plant; gemmiphores produced on mature plants; plants isotomously branched

c10.text: Plants vines, with palmately lobed leaf blades
Plants not vines, the leaf blades unlobed, pinnately lobed, or pinnately divided

c11.text: Sporangia thick-walled, lacking an annulus, commonly bearing more than 1000 spores; leaves not circinate in bud
Sporangia thin-walled, with an annulus, bearing up to 512 spores; leaves circinate in bud

c12.text: Sporangium with an inconspicuous annulus composed of a group of apical, thick-walled cells on either side of the sporangial opening, bearing 256–512 spores; spore-bearing leaves or leaflets brown at maturity, conspicuously different from the vegetative leaves or leaflets

Sporangium with a well-developed annulus that forms a complete or nearly complete ring around the sporangium, usually bearing only 16–64 spores; spore-bearing leaves or leaflets normally green and similar to, or slightly different from, the vegetative leaves or leaflets (very different in Matteuccia and Onoclea )

c13.text: Sori located at the leaf margin; indusium formed, at least in part, by a revolute leaf margin or portion of the margin (i.e., false indusium) [Fig. ]; spores tetrahedral or tetrahedral-globose

Sori not located at the margin (except in Dryopteris marginalis ) [Fig. ]; indusium absent or present, but not formed by a revolute leaf margin (formed by a highly modified, revolute leaf margin in Matteuccia and Onoclea ); spores oblong, reniform, bilateral, or winged

c14.text: Petiole apparently forking into 2 main divisions; sori borne on surface of the false indusium, this best viewed through dissection; ultimate segments without a distinct midrib (in part)
Petiole not appearing to fork into 2 divisions; sori borne on surface of leaf blade near margin and covered by false indusium; ultimate segments with a midrib

c15.text: Leaf blade broad-deltate to ovate-deltate, (25–) 40–70 cm wide; nectaries present at base of leaf divisions, appearing as dark, oval areas in early season; base of petiole with 10 or more vascular bundles (in part)
Leaf blade narrow-oblong to lanceolate or broad-lanceolate, 1.5–18 cm wide; nectaries absent; base of petiole with 1 or 2 vascular bundles

c16.text: Sori discrete, spherical, borne in circular or slightly bivalvate cups formed by fusion of the true indusium with the false indusium; false indusium merely a reflexed tooth or lobe (in part)
Sori becoming confluent as marginal bands, not borne in cup-like structures; false indusium formed by a ± elongate, revolute margin (in part)

c17.text: Some of the sporangia modified to form sporangiasters (i.e., tiny, stalked, and stipitate-glandular bodies mixed within the sorus); indusium absent; leaves evergreen, coriaceous, once-pinnate [Figs. , ]
Sporangiasters absent; indusium usually present, sometimes inconspicuous (absent in Gymnocarpium and Phegopteris ); leaves evergreen or deciduous, herbaceous to coriaceous, variously divided

c18.text: Sori closely aligned in a single, chain-like row immediately adjacent to and on either side of the costa or costule (depending on the leaf division); indusium elongate and flap-like, opening toward the costa or costule (depending on leaf division); veins of leaf blade rejoining to form 1 or 2 (or more) rows of aereoles along the costa, then forking until meeting the margin

Sori variously arranged, when in rows parallel to the costa or costule then not immediately adjacent to them, rather on or adjacent to veinlets; indusium round to elongate, when elongate then opening away from the associated veinlet; veins of leaf blade unforked or freely forking, but not rejoining to form 1 or more rows of aereoles (except in Asplenium rhizophyllum )

c19.text: Scales of the stem prominently clathrate-reticulate; indusia elongate and flap-like; petiole with 2 vascular bundles, these united distally into 1 X-shaped bundle

Scales of the stem not prominently clathrate-reticulate; indusia elongate and flap-like, circular, reniform, lacerate, or absent; petiole with 2–7 vascular bundles, when 2, united into 1 U-shaped bundle distally

c20.text: Plants pubescent with needle-like, unicellular, transparent hairs (scales may be present as well)
Plants glabrous or pubescent, when pubescent the hairs pigmented, glandular, multicellular and/or flattened (these flattened “hairs” are actually microscales)

c21.text: Leaves conspicuously dimorphic—fertile leaves bearing sporangia hidden by highly modified, indurate, revolute leaf segments and vegetative leaves either pinnately lobed (pinnate only at base) and with reticulate venation or vegetative leaves with lower leaflets greatly reduced in size compared with medial leaflets; spores green

Leaves monomorphic to weakly dimorphic; sterile leaves with simple or forking veins that do not rejoin, at least once-divided, and with basal leaflets that do not very gradually reduce in size; spores yellow or light brown to brown

c22.text: Indusium inferior, composed of lacerate or filamentous segments at maturity; veins not reaching margin of leaf segments, ending in hydathodes near the margin; petioles articulated near base, this recognizable as a small, swollen node (not articulated in W. obtusa ) (in part)

Indusium absent or present, sometimes inconspicuous, superior when present, attached centrally or laterally, not divided; veins reaching margin of leaf segments (except in Dryopteris ); petioles not articulated near base

c23.text: Indusium round to reniform; petiole base with 3–7 vascular bundles; teeth of leaf segments often bristle-tipped
Indusium broad-linear, hooked, or horse-shoe-shaped, or absent [Figs. , ]; petiole base with 2 vascular bundles; teeth of leaf segments not bristle-tipped (in part)

c1.text: Seeds borne singly, partly concealed by a red, fleshy aril; abaxial surface of the flat leaves bearing pale yellow, longitudinal, stomatal lines

Seeds 1–400, borne in woody or fleshy strobili, lacking a fleshy, red aril [Figs. , , ]; abaxial surface of the flat to tetragonous leaves without yellow lines (though sometimes with white or gray stomatal lines)

c2.text: Leaves opposite or whorled, imbricate and concealing the branchlet (the branchlet visible in Juniperus communis ), persistent on dried specimens; strobili with peltate scales, or with opposite, basifixed scales, or the scales fleshy and coalesced into a berry-like form [Fig. ]; each scale of a strobilus bearing 1–20 ovules, without free subtending bracts

Leaves alternate, fascicled, or in dense tufts on short shoots, not concealing the branchlet, deciduous from dried specimens; strobili with flat, alternately arranged, basifixed scales [Figs. , ]; each scale of a strobilus bearing 2 ovules, subtended by a free bract

c1.text: Plants thalloid, not differentiated into stems and leaves, 0.5–15 mm long, free floating on or near the surface of water [Fig. ] (in part)
Plants not thalloid, differentiated into stems and leaves, usually much longer or taller; habit various, but when floating usually rooted in the substrate

c2.text: Flowers replaced by, or modified into, vegetative propagules
Flowers not replaced by vegetative bulbils

c3.text: Plants from a conspicuous bulb [Fig. ], with a strong odor of onion or garlic; stems ± scapose (in part)
Plants without a conspicuous, bulbous base, lacking the odor of onion; stems with leaves

c4.text: Leaves terete or elliptic in cross-section and with complete, transverse septa (in part)
Leaves flat, without complete transverse septa (though partial septa may be present)

c5.text: Plants submersed aquatics, with flaccid underwater leaves (in part)
Plants terrestrial, with firmer leaves

c6.text: Inflorescence a panicle [Fig. ]; leaves arranged in 2 ranks, with collar-like ligules (in part)
Inflorescence a spike, with flowers in an umbel-like cluster; leaves arranged in 3 ranks, with ligules, but these inconspicuous and not collar-like (in part)

c7.text: Gynoecium composed of 2 or more distinct carpels and each carpel with a single stigma [Fig. ]; plants aquatic or of hydric habitats
Gynoecium composed of 1 carpel or 2 or more connate carpels and then the ovary surmounted by 2 or more stigmas; plants aquatic or terrestrial

c8.text: Leaf blades triquetrous in cross-section; perianth petaloid, composed of green-pink sepals and pink petals; flowers with 9 stamens and 6 carpels

Leaf blades either flat, ± terete, or capillary; perianth either absent, entirely sepaloid, or composed of green sepals and white petals; flowers with 1–many stamens and 3–many carpels, but not consistently 9 and 6, respectively

c9.text: Perianth present, showy, differentiated into sepals and petals; petals white
Perianth, if present, reduced, not differentiated into sepals and petals; petals (or inner tepals), if present, usually green, yellow-green, or brown

c10.text: Plants emersed; leaves ± terete in cross-section
Plants submersed (except often the inflorescence, which is held above the water surface); leaves flat or capillary

c11.text: Each carpel with 2 ovules; inflorescence bracteate; each leaf with a terminal pore [Fig. ]
Each carpel with 1 ovule; inflorescence without bracts; leaves without terminal pores

c12.text: Each flower with 4 tepal-like appendages and 4 stamens; fruits sessile; stipules distinct from the leaves or basally connate with a distinct tip; plants primary of fresh or fresh-tidal waters (in part)
Each flower with 0 tepals and 2 stamens; fruits long-stipitate; stipules completely connate to the leaves; plants of brackish waters

c13.text: Plants aquatic or marine, with thin, flaccid, often translucent, submersed or floating leaves; flowers unisexual

Plants of upland or wetland habitats, with firmer leaves that are usually, at least partly, emersed (or at least the leaves holding their form when removed from the water); flowers bisexual, or, less commonly, unisexual

c14.text: Flowers in dense, spherical clusters [Fig. ], each flower with 1 stigma (in part)
Flowers not in spherical clusters, each flower with 2–6 or more stigmas

c15.text: Flowers with a perianth composed of 3 sepals and 3 petals; androecium usually with 2 or 9 stamens; gynoecium composed of 3–6 weakly united carpels; leaves whorled (at least in part) or all basal (in part)
Flowers without a perianth; androecium with 1 stamen; gynoecium composed of a single, unilocular, uni- or bicarpellate ovary; leaves alternate or opposite

c16.text: Pollen filiform; gynoecium with 2 stigmas; leaves mostly alternate; plants perennial, with rhizomes, marine
Pollen globose; gynoecium with 2–4 stigmas; leaves opposite; plants annual, without rhizomes, of fresh water habitats (in part)

c17.text: Inflorescence a spadix
Inflorescence various, but not a spadix

c18.text: Leaves ensiform, unifacial, parallel-veined; ovary 2- or 3-locular; anthers introrse; spathe-like bract (actually the distal portion of a sympodial leaf) narrow, grass-like, not concealing the spadix
Leaves with broad and flat, bifacial, pinnately veined blades; ovary unilocular; anthers extrorse; spathe broad, partially or entirely concealing the spadix (least so in Calla ) (in part)

c19.text: Flowers anemophilous or self-pollinated, without a perianth or with an inconspicuous perianth of scales, bristles, or sepaloid tepals
Flowers clearly entomophilous, with an evident, showy perianth

c20.text: Flowers arranged in a solitary, terminal, involucrate, white to gray, pseudanthial cluster; roots conspicuously septate
Flowers arranged otherwise; roots lacking conspicuous septa

c21.text: Inflorescence consisting of a dense, elongate, cylindrical spike, the carpellate portion below, the staminate portion above; fruit a wind-dispersed, 1-seeded follicle (in part)
Inflorescence otherwise; fruit a capsule, achene, utricle, or caryopsis

c22.text: Fruit a 3- or many-seeded capsule; perianth of 6 sepaloid tepals [Figs. , ] (in part)
Fruit indehiscent; perianth of 2–6 inconspicuous tepals, scales, bristles, or absent altogether

c23.text: Ovary with 1 stigma (2 stigmas in Sparganium eurycarpum ); perianth of 2–6 tepals; inflorescence a dense, spherical cluster [Fig. ] (in part)
Ovary with 2 or 3 stigmas; perianth of scales, bristles, or absent; inflorescence variously open to compact

c24.text: Leaves arranged in 3 ranks or absent and represented by bladeless sheaths; stems usually solid, very often triangular in cross-section; flowers spirally arranged (distichous in Cyperus and Dulichium ) [Figs. , , ], ; fruit an achene [Figs. , , ] (in part)

Leaves arranged in 2 ranks; stems usually hollow, almost never triangular in cross-section; flowers and floral scales distichously arranged [Figs. , , ]; fruit a caryopsis or rarely a utricle (in part)

c25.text: Ovary inferior
Ovary superior

c26.text: Flowers zygomorphic [Figs. , , ], with 1 or 2 stamens; pollen cohering in pollinia; seeds minute, dust-like
Flowers actinomorphic [Figs. , ], with 3 or 6 stamens; pollen separate, not cohering in masses; seeds larger

c27.text: Plants vines, dioecious
Plants upright, not twining, synoecious

c28.text: Inflorescence conspicuously white-tomentose; perianth tomentose
Inflorescence not tomentose; perianth glabrous or minutely pilose

c29.text: Flowers with 3 stamens; leaves equitant; seeds without phytomelan
Flowers with 6 stamens; leaves not equitant; seeds usually with phytomelan

c30.text: Perianth pubescent on the abaxial (i.e., outside) surface; leaves pubescent; plants from corms
Perianth glabrous; leaves glabrous; plants from bulbs

c31.text: Flowers borne in the axils of firm, imbricate bracts, aggregated in a dense, ellipsoid to ovoid, terminal spike; leaf blades grass-like; petals yellow
Flowers not from the axils of imbricate bracts, commonly in more open inflorescences; leaf blades various; petal color various

c32.text: Sepals sepaloid, green
Sepals petaloid, of a color similar to that of the petals

c33.text: Leaf blades grass-like, with parallel venation; inflorescence composed of more than 1 flower; fruit a capsule
Leaf blades broad, with pinnately branched secondary veins [Fig. ]; inflorescence composed of a solitary, terminal flower; fruit a berry (in part)

c34.text: Perianth zygomorphic [Fig. ], the upper lip bearing 1 or 2 closely spaced yellow spots; stamens adnate to the corolla (in part)
Perianth actinomorphic, lacking yellow spots; stamens free or adnate to the corolla

c35.text: Leaves palmately veined (with pinnately branched secondary veins), with a well defined petiole and blade, with stipular tendrils [Fig. ]
Leaves parallel-veined, generally lacking a well defined petiole and blade, without tendrils

c36.text: Actual leaves scale-like; upper branches filiform, green, simulating leaves, clustered in the leaf axils
Leaves foliaceous; upper branches not clustered in the leaf axils

c37.text: Flowers with 3 stamens; plants aquatic, with flaccid leaves (in part)
Flowers with 6 stamens (rarely only 4); plants of upland or seasonally saturated soils, with firmer leaves

c38.text: Tepals evidently connate; filaments adnate to the tepals or free in Hostaceae
Tepals distinct or nearly so; filaments free or adnate in Allium , Convallaria , and Streptopus

c39.text: Tepals 4–18 cm long including the basal, connate portion; anthers versatile
Tepals 0.6–2.2 cm long; anthers basifixed or versatile

c40.text: Leaf blades lanceolate to broad-ovate, 5–200 cm wide; inflorescence a raceme
Leaf blades linear to lanceolate, 0.8–5 cm wide; inflorescence a solitary flower or an umbel-like helicoid cyme

c41.text: Tepals yellow or orange, the basal, connate portion 1.5–3 cm long; plants mostly 5–15 dm tall, from tuberous roots, with flowers borne on an evident scape
Tepals pink to purple or white (rarely yellow), the basal, connate portion longer than 8 cm; plants shorter than 3 dm, from corms, with short, obscure, subterranean scapes (in part)

c42.text: Inflorescence axillary or a secund raceme; fruit a berry (in part)
Inflorescence a raceme with spirally arranged flowers; fruit a capsule

c43.text: Perianth minutely roughened on the abaxial (i.e., outside) surface [Fig. ]; pedicels ascending; leaf blades 5–26 mm wide
Perianth not roughened on the abaxial surface; pedicels spreading-ascending to drooping, especially the lower ones [Fig. ]; leaf blades 2–8 mm wide (10–20 mm wide in Chionodoxa ) (in part)

c44.text: Plants with a large rosette of firm leaves that have fibrous margins and a spinose apex; tepals thick and fleshy
Plants with or without basal rosettes, but the basal leaves (if present) lacking marginal fibers and apical spines; tepals relatively thinner

c45.text: Flowers in a many-flowered umbel at the summit of a scape; seeds with phytomelan; plants with the odor of onion or garlic (in part)

Flowers arranged otherwise (forming an umbel with 3–6 flowers in Clintonia ) at the summit of a scape or leafy stem; seeds without phytomelan (except in Ornithogalum ) plants without the odor of onion or garlic

c46.text: Scape viscid-pubescent; leaves both equitant and distichous
Stem or scape glabrous or pubescent, but not viscid; leaves not set edge to stem, spirally arranged or, less commonly, distichous

c47.text: Leaves in 1 or 2 whorls; styles elongate, capillary, exceeding the tepals in length; fruit a purple to black berry (in part)
Leaves arranged otherwise; styles shorter; fruit a capsule or berry, the berry blue, red, or becoming red

c48.text: Styles 3, separate to the base; fruit a septicidal capsule (loculicidal in Stenanthium )
Styles 1, divided or lobed only in the apical portion; fruit a berry or loculicidal capsule

c49.text: Styles simple, unspotted, tepals 2-12 mm long; inflorescence a terminal raceme or panicle (in part)
Styles distally bifid, maculate; tepals 20–25 mm long; inflorescence of few to several flowers in the axils of leaves (in part)

c50.text: Stems from a bulb or corm; fruit a capsule, circular or bluntly angled in cross-section
Stems from rhizomes; fruit a berry, or a capsule with triquetrous cross-section in Uvularia

c51.text: Aerial stems leafy; tepals 30–100 mm long (in part)
Aerial stems scapose; tepals 12–33 mm long

c52.text: Tepals white with an abaxial green stripe or entirely blue; inflorescence a raceme (sometimes a solitary flower in Othocallis ); leaf blades not mottled (in part)
Tepals yellow; inflorescence a solitary flower; leaf blades adaxially mottled (in part)

c53.text: Tepals white; inflorescence terminal, a raceme or panicle [Fig. ] (in part)
Tepals yellow, green-white, yellow-green, or pink; inflorescence axillary, an umbel, or a solitary, terminal flower

c54.text: Tepals yellow; fruit a capsule; leaves borne on an aerial stem (in part)
Tepals green-white, pink, or green-yellow; fruit a berry; leaves all basal or borne on an aerial stem (in part)

/dkey/group-4/.title: Group 4: Woody angiosperms with opposite or whorled leaves

c1.text: Plants 5–30 mm tall, parasitic on Picea , Larix , and Pinus [Fig. ]; anthers sessile
Plants much taller or longer at maturity, not parasitic; anthers with filaments

c2.text: Leaves compound
Leaves simple

c3.text: Fruit an inflated, thin-walled capsule with 3 lobes [Fig. ]; gynoecium with 3 styles that are basally distinct and apically coherent
Fruit otherwise; gynoecium with 1 style that is often terminated by a lobed or branched stigmatic surface

c4.text: Perianth zygomorphic; fruit a capsule
Perianth actinomorphic or absent; fruit an achene, schizocarp, drupe, or samara

c5.text: Plants trees with palmately compound leaves; capsule 3–5 cm long (in part)
Plants lianas with pinnately compound leaves; capsule 10–15 cm long (in part)

c6.text: Plants lianas (though woody only near base); flowers with numerous stamens; fruit an achene terminated by an elongate, plumose style [Fig. ] (in part)
Plants upright shrubs or trees; flowers with 2–12 stamens; fruit otherwise

c7.text: Leaflets punctate with aromatic glands; winter buds naked, enclosed by petiole base (in part)
Leaflets not punctate; winter buds covered by scales, not enclosed in petiole base

c8.text: Fruit a samaroid schizocarp; ovary bilobed, compressed; androecium composed of 4–12 stamens, commonly 8 (in part)
Fruit a samara or drupe; ovary not bilobed, not compressed; androecium composed of 2 or 5 stamens

c9.text: Perianth absent; androecium composed of 2 stamens; fruit a samara; flowers usually unisexual; trees at maturity (in part)
Perianth present and gamopetalous; androecium composed of 5 stamens; fruit a drupe; flowers bisexual; shrubs at maturity (in part)

c10.text: Apical portions of the stem succulent; leaves minute and scale-like, 1–3 mm long [Fig. ]; stems appearing jointed; plants of Atlantic coast shores (in part)
Apical portions of the stem herbaceous to woody; leaves with foliaceous blades, mostly longer; stems not appearing jointed; plants of inland habitats

c11.text: Leaves and leaf scars whorled
Leaves and leaf scars opposite

c12.text: Perianth zygomorphic; fruit a slender, elongate capsule 20–45 cm long; seeds winged, the wings terminating in hairs (in part)
Perianth actinomorphic; fruit an achene-like schizocarp or a subglobose capsule 0.4–0.7 cm long; seeds without prominent wings

c13.text: Inflorescence a cyme [Fig. ]; flowers each with 8 or 10 stamens; petals pink-purple, 10–15 mm long; stems woody in the basal portion, surrounded by loose, spongy tissue, the buds barely emerging through the tissue (in part)
Inflorescence a dense, spherical cluster [Fig. ]; flowers each with 4 stamens; petals white, 5–8 mm long; stems woody throughout, not surrounded by spongy tissue, the buds clearly visible (in part)

c14.text: Leaves and branchlets conspicuously white- and/or brown-lepidote [Fig. ]; plants dioecious (in part)
Leaves and branchlets without abundant scales; plants synoecious, polygamous, or dioecious

c15.text: Leaf blades 6–15 mm long, crowded and imbricate [Fig. ]; pulvinate plants of exposed, alpines areas above 1000 m elevation (in part)
Leaf blades longer than 20 mm, not crowded; plants of lower elevation habitats (except sometimes Viburnum edule )

c16.text: Inflorescence a capitulum; fruit a resin-dotted cypsela (in part)
Inflorescence not pseudanthial; fruit a schizocarp, capsule, follicle, berry, or drupe, or 10–35 achenes enclosed in a fleshy hypanthium

c17.text: Perianth of 15–30 brown-purple tepals; gynoecium with 10–35 carpels; androecium with 10–20 stamens and 10–25 staminodes seated inside the cycle of stamens
Perianth with fewer petaloid segments; gynoecium with 1–5 carpels; androecium otherwise, mostly with fewer stamens

c18.text: Inflorescence mixed (i.e., thyrsoid), the indeterminate axis bearing cymose lateral branches, lateral branches manifesting as dense verticillasters of 6–10 flowers; fruit a schizocarp, separating into 4 achene-like mericarps; foliage pleasantly fragrant (in part)

Inflorescence not thyrsoid (appearing thyrsoid in Decodon , but then each cyme subtended by foliage leaves); fruit a capsule, follicle, or drupe, or a schizocarp in Acer that splits into 2 samara-like mericarps; foliage not especially fragrant

c19.text: Stems woody only in the basal portion and surrounded by loose, spongy tissue, the buds barely emerging through the tissue; stamens dimorphic, of 2 different lengths (in part)
Stems woody ± throughout, not surrounded by spongy tissue, the buds clearly visible; stamens monomorphic

c20.text: Fruit a samaroid schizocarp; ovary bilobed and compressed (in part)
Fruit a capsule, follicle, or drupe; ovary not, or inconspicuously, lobed, not compressed

c21.text: Flowers without perianth; fruit a follicle
Flowers with perianth; fruit a capsule, berry, achene, or drupe

c22.text: Perianth 5-merous
Perianth 4-merous

c23.text: Corolla 50–70 mm long; ovary superior; fruit a capsule 30–40 mm long; seeds winged
Corolla 3–50 mm long; ovary inferior; fruit a drupe, berry, or achene, or a capsule 8–15 mm long; seeds without evident wings

c24.text: Flowers with 8 or 10 stamens; corolla apopetalous (in part)
Flowers with 4 or 5 stamens; corolla gamopetalous

c25.text: Style absent or very short; corolla of fertile flowers actinomorphic, white, 4–8 mm long (some species with sterile, enlarged, marginal flowers) (in part)
Style elongate; corolla actinomorphic or zygomorphic, white, pink, yellow, red, or purple, 3–50 mm (in part)

c26.text: Leaf blades sessile, punctate with pellucid dots; petals yellow (in part)
Leaf blades petiolate (though the petioles sometimes short), lacking pellucid dots; petals white, yellow, green-white, blue, or brown-purple

c27.text: Flowers with 2 or 4 stamens
Flowers with 5–many stamens; corolla apopetalous

c28.text: Corolla gamopetalous
Corolla apopetalous

c29.text: Flowers with 4 stamens; leaf blades white-tomentose on the abaxial surface (in part)
Flowers with 2 stamens; leaf blades glabrous or pubescent on the abaxial surface, but not white-tomentose (in part)

c30.text: Fruit a drupe; leaf blades with arcuate venation; styles present; branches terete (in part)
Fruit a capsule; leaf blades not with arcuate venation; styles absent; branches often ± quadrangular (in part)

c31.text: Petals yellow; leaf blades sessile and pellucid-punctate (in part)
Petals white, brown-purple, green-white, or ± yellow in Euonymus alatus ; leaf blades petiolate (though the petioles sometimes short), without pellucid dots

c32.text: Fruit a drupe; leaf blades entire, with arcuate venation [Fig. ] (in part)
Fruit a capsule; leaf blades toothed, with pinnate venation (in part)

/dkey/group-5/.title: Group 5: Woody angiosperms with alternate leaves

c1.text: Inflorescence a capitulum; fruit a cypsela (in part)
Inflorescence not pseudanthial; fruit various, but not a cypsela

c2.text: Leaves compound
Leaves simple

c3.text: Perianth zygomorphic
Perianth actinomorphic

c4.text: Corolla usually papillionaceous; filaments connate, conspicuously so in most genera (distinct in Cladrastis ), not seated on a nectar disk; fruit a legume (in part)
Corolla not papillionaceous; filaments distinct, seated on a nectar disk; fruit a bladdery-inflated, 3-valved capsule (in part)

c5.text: Leaves palmately compound
Leaves pinnately compound

c6.text: Leaflets retuse at the apex; sepals numbering 3 or 6, petaloid, purple brown; gynoecium of 3 distinct carpels (i.e., the flowers with 3 pistils)
Leaflets tapering to the apex; sepals numbering 5, sepaloid, green; gynoecium of 2–5 connate carpels (i.e., the flowers with 1 pistil)

c7.text: Plants climbing by means of tendrils produced opposite the leaves, unarmed; inflorescence a panicle; ovary superior (in part)
Plants not climbing, armed with prickles; ultimate unit of inflorescence an umbel; ovary inferior (in part)

c8.text: Leaves twice pinnately compound (only once pinnately compound on spurs in Gleditsia ); fruit a legume (in part)
Leaves once pinnately compound; fruit not a legume

c9.text: Inflorescence a unisexual ament, the staminate drooping; flowers small, with an inconspicuous perianth; fruit a drupe with a fibrous exocarp and nut-like endocarp [Fig. ]
Inflorescence not an ament, uni- or bisexual, none drooping; flowers with an evident perianth; fruit a fleshy drupe, samara, follicle, pome, or aggregate

c10.text: Leaf blades punctate with pellucid dots; fruit a fleshy follicle, an orbicular samara, or a drupe (in part)
Leaf blades not punctate; fruit mainly otherwise, though a few genera with drupe fruits

c11.text: Leaflets entire except for 1 or more coarse teeth near the base; fruit a samara
Leaflets toothed to lobed; fruit not a samara

c12.text: Ultimate unit of the inflorescence an umbel; styles swollen at the base forming a stylopodium (in part)
Ultimate unit of the inflorescence not an umbel; styles without a stylopodium

c13.text: Perianth monochlamydeous, only the sepals present; wood yellow (in part)
Perianth dichlamydeous, both sepals and petals present; wood not yellow

c14.text: Flowers with a hypanthium, bisexual; plants with a watery sap; stems armed or unarmed (in part)
Flowers without a hypanthium, commonly unisexual; plants with a milky or watery sap (note: when watery, the sap poisonous); stems unarmed

c15.text: Plants lianas
Plants erect to mat-forming, but not climbing

c16.text: Leaves with sheathing stipules; perianth segments with the midvein abaxially winged, especially in fruit; fruit a trigonous achene (in part)

Leaves exstipulate, or the stipules minute and caducous (e.g., Actinidiaceae) or evident in the Vitaceae, but these not sheathing the entire circumference of the stem; perianth segments lacking an evident, abaxial, longitudinal wing; fruit a berry, drupe, or capsule

c17.text: Calyx gamosepalous, 3-lobed, with a strongly curved basal tube, petaloid [Fig. ]; flowers with 6 stamens (in part)
Calyx gamosepalous, aposepalous, or obsolete, without a strongly curved tube, sepaloid; flowers with 5 or 12–100 stamens (when stamens are present)

c18.text: Corolla gamopetalous; anthers dehiscing by terminal pores or clefts; some of the leaf blades with a distinct pair of small lobes or leaflets [Fig. ] (in part)
Corolla apopetalous (cohering at the summit in Vitis ); anthers dehiscing by longitudinal slits; leaf blades simple or lobed, the lobes, when present, not confined to the base of the blade

c19.text: Leaf blades with peltate attachment of petioles; flowers with 6–9 petals and 12–24 stamens; fruit a drupe
Leaf blades with basal attachment of petioles; flowers with 5 petals and 5 or 18–100 stamens (when stamens are present); fruit a berry or capsule

c20.text: Leaves palmately veined or palmately lobed [Fig. ]; tendrils and inflorescences produced opposite the leaves; fruit a berry, white to blue or dark blue to black (rarely red or green) (in part)
Leaves pinnately veined; tendrils absent; inflorescences terminal or axillary; fruit a capsule or green-yellow berry

c21.text: Stamens 5, the anthers basifixed; fruit an orange-yellow to orange capsule 6–13 mm long; pith continuous (in part)
Stamens 18–100, the anthers versatile; fruit a green-yellow berry 20–30 mm long; pith diaphragmed

c22.text: Plants with a milky latex; fruit a multiple, usually fleshy (dry in Broussonetia ) (in part)
Plants with a watery sap; fruit simple or aggregate, dry or fleshy

c23.text: Stamens monadelphous; epicalyx of (6–) 8–15 bractlets present (in part)
Stamens distinct (connate for a short distance at the base in Halesia and cohered or connate in 2 species of Salix ); epicalyx absent

c24.text: Fruit a dark red to nearly black drupe with thin flesh on a peduncle (7–) 10–20 (–25) mm long; leaf blades asymmetrical at the base, usually strongly so, with 1 or both sides cordate (in part)
Fruit otherwise; leaf blades ± symmetrical or, less commonly, asymmetrical at the base, narrow-cuneate to cordate

c25.text: Flowers unisexual
Flowers bisexual

c26.text: Leaves palmately 3- to 5-lobed; carpellate flowers in dense, spherical clusters; fruit a spherical aggregate of achenes or capsules
Leaves not palmately lobed (except in some 3-lobed leaves of Sassafras ); flowers not in dense, spherical clusters; fruit otherwise

c27.text: Bark exfoliating, creating a mottled pattern of colors; fruit an aggregate of narrow achenes; leaf blades with broad-triangular lobes that are coarsely and sparsely serrate
Bark not exfoliating; fruit an aggregate of capsules; leaf blades with narrow-triangular to triangular lobes that are finely and closely serrate

c28.text: Plants up to 50 cm tall, with numerous, crowded leaves with linear to narrow-elliptic blades 3–8 mm long [Fig. ]; fruit a dry or fleshy drupe (in part)
Plants usually taller, with larger, broader leaf blades; fruit various

c29.text: Inflorescence an ament (the carpellate flowers solitary or in small clusters in the Fagaceae); perianth absent or tiny and inconspicuous
Inflorescence not an ament; perianth present, evident

c30.text: Winter buds either covered by a single, cap-like scale or with the lowest scale centered over the leaf scar; fruit a capsule, containing comose seeds
Winter buds with 2 or more scales, the lowest scale not centered over the leaf scar; fruit an achene, samara, or nut

c31.text: Foliage with abundant, aromatic, yellow or brown resin glands; plants dioecious
Foliage eglandular or with relatively nonaromatic glands; plants monoecious

c32.text: Ovary 3- or 6-locular; carpellate flowers solitary or in small clusters; fruit a nut [Figs. , ]
Ovary 2-locular; carpellate flowers commonly in aments; fruit an achene, samara, or nut

c33.text: Corolla of carpellate flowers (these usually with 8 sterile anthers) 15–20 mm long; perianth 4-merous; fruit a yellow-brown berry 20–40 mm long
Corolla 1–15 mm long; perianth 4- to 10-merous; fruit a red, yellow, silver, or blue to black drupe or berry 4–15 mm long

c34.text: Pith diaphragmed; carpellate flowers epigynous; staminate flowers with 8–15 stamens (in part)
Pith continuous; carpellate flowers hypogynous or perigynous; staminate flowers with 4–9 stamens

c35.text: Staminate flowers with 9 stamens; anthers dehiscing by uplifting valves; plants with aromatic foliage and wood
Staminate flowers with 4–8 stamens; anthers dehiscing by longitudinal slits; plants without aromatic foliage and wood

c36.text: Ovary with 2–4 stigmas, the style 2- to 4-lobed; stamens antepetalous (in part)
Ovary with 1 stigma, the style unbranched; stamens antesepalous

c37.text: Leaf blades and branchlets with abundant silver scales; plants sometimes armed with thorns; petals absent [Fig. ]; styles elongate (in part)
Leaves and branchlets not lepidote; plants unarmed; petals present; styles very short, nearly absent (in part)

c38.text: Leaf blades entire, with abundant silver scales; plants sometimes armed with thorns (in part)
Leaf blades entire, toothed, or lobed, not lepidote; plants unarmed or armed

c39.text: Corolla zygomorphic; fruit a legume (in part)
Corolla (or petaloid portions of flower) actinomorphic; fruit not a legume

c40.text: Corolla of 4 yellow, linear petals; plants flowering in the fall during and after the falling of the leaves
Corolla of 4–10 variously colored petals or petal-like members (petaloid hypanthium in Dirca ), the petals not strap-shaped with parallel margins; plants flowering prior to leaf fall

c41.text: Fruit an elliptic to suborbicular samara (fruit unwinged in Ulmus parvifolia ); flowers tiny, anemophilous, precocious (serotinous in Ulmus parvifolia ); leaf blades double-serrate in most species
Fruit not a samara; flowers variously pollinated, generally entomophilous, precocious to serotinous; leaf blades entire, serrate, or lobed

c42.text: Peduncle of the inflorescence adnate to a conspicuous, elongate bract; the numerous stamens commonly connate into 5 antepetalous groups (in part)

Peduncle of the inflorescence without bracts or, when bracteate, free from the bract; stamens 4–many, distinct (shortly connate at the base in Halesia , but that species with 4-merous, gamopetalous flowers)

c43.text: Pith diaphragmed; gynoecium composed of a single carpel (very rarely 2 carpels) (in part)
Pith continuous; gynoecium composed of 1–66 (–73) carpels

c44.text: Gynoecium with (9–) 19–66 (–73) carpels [Fig. ]; androecium with laminar filaments; fruit an aggregate of samaras or an agreggate of follicles that each bear a large seed covered by a pink to red or red-orange aril

Gynoecium with 1–10 carpels; androecium usually with slender filaments; fruit otherwise, usually a drupe, berry, pome, achene, capsule, or aggregate (when an aggregate, as in some Rosaceae, usually with fleshy carpels)

c45.text: Perianth composed of 2 or more whorls, both the sepals and petals present

c46.text: Flowers with a conspicuous hypanthial tube, the petaloid members yellow or pink to purple (rarely white); stamens 8
Flowers with a short, inconspicuous hypanthial tube, or lacking one altogether, petaloid members absent or white; stamens 4 or 5

c47.text: Stamens antepetalous; leaves commonly subopposite; branches often ending in a short, spine-like process (in part)
Stamens antesepalous; leaves alternate; branches without spines (in part)

c49.text: Stamens numbering more than the petals [Fig. ]
Stamens as many as the petals [Fig. ]

c50.text: Stamens numbering more than 10, more than twice as many as the petals
Stamens numbering 10 or fewer, up to twice as many as the petals

c51.text: Stamens adnate to the base of the corolla; calyx light yellow, the lobes 1–1.5 mm long, ciliate on the margins; ovary epigynous; fruit a blue (rarely white) drupe 3–8 mm long
Stamens not inserted at the base of the corolla; calyx otherwise; ovary perigynous in flower (but becoming epigynous in fruit in some species); fruit not as above (in part)

c52.text: Stamens numbering 8, the filaments shortly connate at the base and distinct above; fruit 4-winged, dry, 1- to 3-seeded; flowers with 1 style
Stamens 5–10, the filaments not monadelphous at the base; fruit otherwise; flowers with 2–5 styles (in part)

c54.text: Plants with broad-based prickles along the stems and branches; inflorescence a corymb-like panicle of umbels (in part)
Plants unarmed or with bristles or thin prickles; inflorescence a raceme or corymb (rarely a solitary flower)

c55.text: Plants usually armed with stout thorns; stamens antesepalous [Fig. ] (in part)
Plants unarmed or with a slender, spine-like process at the apex of some branches; stamens antepetalous (in part)

c56.text: Plants armed with spines [Fig. ]; perianth composed of 6 sepals in 2 cycles and 6 petals in 2 cycles; anthers dehiscing by uplifting valves (in part)
Plants unarmed or with thorns in Lycium ; perianth composed of fewer parts; anthers dehiscing by longitudinal slits or apical pores

c57.text: Sepals dimorphic, the 2 outer smaller than the 3 inner [Figs. , ]; petals yellow or red in Lechea
Sepals monomorphic; petals white, pink, red, purple, green, or green-white

c58.text: Stamens numbering the same as the petals and antepetalous, often enclosed by the petals (especially in bud), or the petals absent and the stamens alternating with the sepals (in part)
Stamens fewer than, as many as, or more than the petals, alternating with the petals, not enclosed by the petals (recessed in pouches in the corolla in Kalmia )

c59.text: Stamens fewer than or as many as the petals or inner tepals
Stamens numbering more than the petals

c60.text: Ovary 2-locular; fruit a red berry 10–20 mm in diameter; plants usually with thorns (in part)
Ovary 3- to 8-locular; fruit otherwise; plants unarmed

c61.text: Androecium of 4 stamens seated on a lobed, nectary disk; leaf blades 3–5 mm long, scale-like, subampexicaul; perianth 4-merous, with a corolla shorter than 2 mm

Androecium of 5–10 stamens (only 4 in some Ilex ), not seated on a conspicuous nectar disk; leaf blades various, though usually longer and/or with a petiole; perianth mostly 5-merous, infrequently only 4-merous, the corolla longer than 2 mm

c62.text: Styles short, the stigma nearly sessile on the summit of the ovary; sepals present, though small and inconspicuous (in part)
Styles elongate, the stigma elevated above the summit of the ovary; sepals usually evident (in part)

c63.text: Plants evidently pubescent with compound hairs; ovary 3-locular; leaf blades with plane margins, deciduous
Plants glabrous or with simple hairs; ovary 2- to 9-locular; leaf blades sometimes with revolute margins and/or evergreen (in part)

/dkey/group-6/.title: Group 6: Herbaceous angiosperms with inferior ovaries

c1.text: Inflorescence a capitulum (the capitula with only 1 flower in Echinops ); anthers of disk flowers connate in a ring around the style; fruit a cypsela (in part)
Inflorescence not a capitulum (a capitulum-like cyme in some Caprifoliaceae); anthers not connate in a ring (except in Lobelia ); fruit otherwise (except in some Caprifoliaceae)

c2.text: Flowers unisexual
Flowers bisexual

c3.text: Plants vines, with tendrils; corolla gamopetalous [Fig. ]
Plants not vines, without tendrils; corolla apopetalous (very inconspicuous and reduced to a rim of sepals in Hippuris )

c4.text: Plants aquatic, with thin, flaccid, submersed leaves; flowers anemophilous, with an inconspicuous perianth
Plants terrestrial, with thicker, firm leaves; flowers entomophilous, with a well-developed perianth

c5.text: Leaves pectinately divided into narrow segments or the leaves reduced to minute scales or bumps on the stem, mostly alternate or whorled [Figs. , , ]; flowers with 4 or 8 stamens (in part)
Leaves simple, whorled; flowers with a single stamen (in part)

c6.text: Leaves simple; fruit a drupe; inflorescence an axillary cymule of 3 flowers— the 2 lateral flowers usually staminate, the central bisexual (in part)
Leaves compound or evidently lobed; fruit not a drupe; inflorescence otherwise

c7.text: Leaf blades 1- to 3-times pinnately compound; fruit an achene enclosed in an indurate hypanthium or a follicle (in part)
Leaf blades palmately divided into 3–7 broad segments; fruit a schizocarp [Figs. , ] (in part)

c8.text: Stems very succulent, jointed, with flattened, oblong to suborbicular segments [Fig. ], the areoles (i.e., modified nodes) with glochids and sometimes 1 or 2 spines; perianth consisting of numerous, spirally arranged tepals [Fig. ]
Stems not consisting of succulent, pad-like segments, unarmed (mostly) or armed; perianth 2- to 6-merous

c9.text: Leaves usually 4–6 per node, entire, with arcuate venation; flowers pseudanthial, small, collectively subtended by 4 large, white, petaloid bracts (in part)
Leaves 1–12 per node, entire, toothed, or lobed, without arcuate venation; flowers not pseudanthial, lacking petaloid bracts

c10.text: Calyx 3-merous, gamosepalous, petaloid (in part)
Calyx not 3-merous (except in some Galium ), connate or not, sepaloid (petaloid sepals in Aizoaceae and petaloid tepals in Comandraceae), not red-brown

c11.text: Plants aquatic
Plants of upland or wetland habitats, but typically not growing in standing water

c12.text: Plants with a rosette of floating leaves that have petioles swollen near midlength forming a float; hypanthium with 4 stout horns, these persistent on the fruit (in part)
Plants without a conspicuous rosette of floating leaves, lacking specialized petioles with floats; hypanthium lacking horns

c13.text: Leaves with a prominent, sheathing base; inflorescence an umbel [Figs. , ] (in part)
Leaves lacking a prominent, sheathing base; inflorescence of axillary flowers or a raceme

c14.text: Leaves compound, all basal, with 3 thick, fleshy leaflets [Fig. ]; fruit a 2-valved capsule (in part)
Leaves simple or compound, not confined to the base of a plant, not with 3 thick leaflets; fruit an achene-like drupe or a 4- or 5-valved capsule

c15.text: Leaves whorled, simple; flowers with a single stamen (in part)
Leaves alternate or opposite, simple, lobed, or compound; flowers with 3, 5, or 8 stamens

c16.text: Perianth 4-merous; flowers with 4 stamens; fruit a 4-valved capsule (in part)
Perianth 3- or 5-merous; flowers with 3 or 5 stamens; fruit indehiscent or a 5-valved capsule

c17.text: Leaves pinnately lobed or pinnately compound (merely toothed in the emersed leaves of Proserpinaca palustris ) [Figs. , , ]; perianth composed of only 3 sepals; flowers with 3 antesepalous stamens (in part)
Leaves simple and unlobed; perianth composed of 5 sepals and 5 petals; flowers with 5 antepetalous stamens

c18.text: Inflorescence a capitulum-like cyme [Figs. , , ]; ovary and fruit partially enclosed in a gamophyllous, tubular involucel that may be expanded apically (in part)
Inflorescence not resembling a capitulum; ovary and fruit not enclosed in a tubular involucel

c19.text: Gynoecium with 5–10 carpels; leaf blades conspicuously papillose, the papillae not requiring high magnification to see; fruit woody, subglobose, indehiscent, with 4–6 wings, each wing projecting into an apical horn (in part)
Gynoecium with 2–6 carpels; leaf blades without easily viewed papillae; fruit otherwise

c20.text: Perianth 2- to 4-merous
Perianth 5-merous or absent altogether (sepals numbering 2 in the Portulacaceae; petals rarely 4 or 6 in Portulaca )

c21.text: Leaf blades cordate-clasping the stem [Fig. ]; ovary mostly trilocular; fruit usually a 3-valved capsule (in part)
Leaf blades sessile or petiolate, but not clasping the stem; ovary bilocular or quadrilocular; fruit otherwise

c22.text: Corolla gamopetalous [Figs. , ]; stamens 3 or 4; leaves opposite or whorled, stipulate (though the stipule sometimes reduced to an interpetiolar line) (in part)
Corolla apopetalous above the hypanthium or absent in 1 species of Ludwigia [Figs. , ]; stamens 2, 4, or usually 8; leaves alternate or opposite, exstipulate (in part)

c23.text: Leaves opposite; flowers with 3 or 4 stamens (5 in Triosteum ) (in part)
Leaves alternate or all basal (often both alternate and opposite in Portulaca , a prostrate, fleshy-leaved herb); flowers with 5–many stamens

c24.text: Inflorescence an umbel [Figs. , ]; fruit a schizocarp or, less commonly, a berry; leaves compound (rarely simple), usually with a sheathing petiole base; styles swollen at the base forming a stylopodium; calyx a series of small teeth around the rim of the receptacle or absent (rarely well-developed) (in part)

Inflorescence otherwise (except in Primula ); fruit a capsule, pyxis, or drupe; leaves simple (trifoliate in Menyanthes ), mostly without a sheathing petiole base; gynoecium without a stylopodium; calyx of evident sepals (or apparently absent in the Comandraceae)

c25.text: Leaves compound, with 3 thick, fleshy leaflets; petals conspicuously pubescent on the adaxial (i.e., inner) surface [Fig. ] (in part)
Leaves simple; petals glabrous on the adaxial surface (with a tuft of hairs near the base in Comandra )

c26.text: Flowers with mostly 15–20 stamens; herbage pubescent with barbed hairs
Flowers with 5–10 stamens; herbage glabrous or with hairs that lack barbs

c27.text: Flowers with mostly 6–10 stamens; petals yellow; prostrate weeds (in part)
Flowers with 5 stamens; petals (or tepals) white, red, green-purple, blue, or purple; plants not prostrate weeds

c28.text: Perianth monochlamydeous; fruit a drupe (dryish in Comandra ); leaf blades ± entire (in part)
Perianth dichlamydeous; fruit a capsule; leaf blades entire or toothed (in part)

/dkey/group-7/.title: Group 7: Herbaceous angiosperms with superior ovaries and zygomorphic flowers

c1.text: Perianth with a nectary spur [Figs. , , ]
Perianth lacking a nectary spur

c2.text: Plants insectivorous by means of bladders or viscid leaf blades [Figs. , , ]; flowers with 2 stamens; placentation free-central
Plants not insectivorous; flowers with 4–6 stamens; placentation axile or parietal

c3.text: Stamens numerous; both the calyx and corolla spurred, the 2 upper petals prolonged backward into a spur that extends into the upper, spurred sepal; leaf blades palmately divided (in part)
Stamens 4–12; either the calyx or corolla spurred, but not both (hypanthium with a spur in Cuphea ); leaf blades not palmately divided (palmately lobed in some Viola )

c4.text: Corolla 6-merous; androecium with 11 or 12 stamens; flowers perigynous (in part)
Corolla 3- to 5-merous; androecium with 4–8 stamens; flowers hypogynous

c5.text: Androecium with 8 stamens; leaf blades with peltate petioles
Androecium with 4–6 stamens; leaf blades with basifixed petioles

c6.text: Calyx spurred (note: the calyx is, in part, petaloid and can be misinterpreted as part of the corolla) [Fig. ]; capsule dehiscing elastically; gynoecium with 5 carpels
Corolla spurred [Figs. , ]; capsule not dehiscing elastically; gynoecium with 2 or 3 carpels

c7.text: Calyx of 2, often caducous, sepals; flowers with 6 stamens; leaf blades decompound (in part)
Calyx of 5 sepals; flowers with 4 or 5 stamens; leaf blades variously simple to lobed, but not many times dissected

c8.text: Corolla apopetalous [Fig. ]; flowers with 5 stamens; gynoecium with 3 carpels, therefore, the capsule with 3 valves
Corolla gamopetalous [Fig. ]; flowers with only 4 functional stamens; gynoecium with 2 carpels, therefore, the capsule with 2 valves (in part)

c9.text: Upper sepal much larger than the other 4, petaloid, arched, forming a helmet-shaped structure that conceals the 2 petals; leaf blades palmately divided, with pinnately lobed segments (in part)
Calyx without a single, larger, helmet-shaped sepal, sepaloid or petaloid; petals 3–8, not concealed by the calyx; leaf blades otherwise

c10.text: Calyx with 2 sepals; androecium of 3 stamens; fruit a capsule with 1–3 seeds (in part)
Calyx with 4–6 sepals; androecium of 2–25 stamens, but not 3; fruit a capsule, silique, legume, schizocarp, or achene

c11.text: Fruit a legume or schizocarp; gynoecium with 1 carpel; stamens monadelphous or diadelphous (distinct in Baptisia , Chamaecrista , Senna , and Thermopsis ); lower 2 petals fused into a keel (only the banner petal present in Amorpha , lower 2 petals distinct in Chamaecrista and Senna ) [Figs. , , ] (in part)
Fruit a capsule, silique, schizocarp, or achene; gynoecium with 2 or more carpels; stamens distinct (monadelphous in Polygala ); lower 2 petals variously distinct or connate

c12.text: Corolla apopetalous; androecium of 6–27 stamens
Corolla gamopetalous; androecium of 2–8 stamens

c13.text: Leaf blades pinnately compound with 7–13 leaflets, punctate with transparent glands; gynoecium with 5 carpels (in part)
Leaf blades entire to lobed or compound, when pinnately compound with only 3 leaflets, not glandular-punctate; gynoecium with 2–4 carpels

c14.text: Petals 4–6, the apical portion bearing a fringe of linear to oblanceolate segments that are ± equal to the length of the petal [Fig. ]; gynoecium with 3 or 4 carpels; fruit a capsule; leaf blades entire to pinnately lobed
Petals 4, the apical portion lacking a fringe; gynoecium with 2 carpels; fruit a silique; leaf blades palmately compound or pinnately trifoliate (in part)

c15.text: Calyx composed of 3 small sepals and 2 large, petaloid sepals [Figs. , ]; flowers with 6 or 8 monadelphous stamens
Calyx composed mostly of 4 or 5 sepaloid sepals, but not as in the Polygalaceae; flowers with 2–5 distinct stamens

c16.text: Carpels 2, each carpel lobed, often evidently so, therefore, the gynoecium appearing to be composed of 4 carpels, separating at maturity into 4 half-carpellate segments; fruit a schizocarp
Carpels 2, each carpel unlobed, therefore, the gynoecium appearing to be composed of 2 carpels (appearing unicarpellate in Phryma , but the stigmas 2); fruit a capsule or achene

c17.text: Inflorescence a helicoid cyme [Figs. , , ]; leaves alternate; stems terete or angled (in part)
Inflorescence not appearing as a coiled raceme [Figs. , , ]; leaves opposite; stems usually quadrangular

c18.text: Style with a conspicuously lobed stigma; carpels weakly lobed; inflorescence indeterminate (e.g., spike, raceme) [Figs. , ]; placentation marginal; plants without aromatic foliage (in part)

Style usually with an inconspicuous stigma; carpels usually evidently lobed; inflorescence mixed (i.e., thyrsoid), with cymose lateral branches, sometimes the inflorescence condensed in dense verticillasters of flowers, only rarely completely indeterminate [Figs. , , ]; ovules attached to lateral partitions and not the carpel margins; plants commonly with mint-, pennyroyal-, or citrus-scented foliage (in part)

c19.text: Fruit an achene; ovary unilocular and uniovulate; calyx tightly reflexed in fruit [Fig. ] (in part)
Fruit a capsule; ovary bilocular or unilocular in holoparasitic genera, with 2 or more ovules; calyx not reflexed in fruit

c20.text: Fruit a drupe-like capsule 10–20 cm long, with a fleshy exocarp that separates from the woody endocarp, prolonged at the apex into a curved beak that splits into 2 halves at maturity; plants pubescent with stipitate glands, the gland composed of 4 or more mucilage-filled cells (in part)
Fruit a capsule without a fleshy exocarp, not terminated by a long, 2-pronged beak; plants stipitate-glandular or not, but never slimy-pubescent

c21.text: Anthers with 1 locule, dehiscing by a single, transverse, distal slit, not sagittate at the base (in part)
Anthers with 2 locules, dehiscing by 2 longitudinal slits or the locules connate near the apex and opening by a distal, V-shaped slit, usually sagittate at the base

c22.text: Plants holoparasitic, lacking chlorophyll; ovary unilocular, with parietal placentation (in part)
Plants autotrophic or hemiparasitic, with chlorophyll; ovary 2-locular or 4-locular, with axile placentation

c23.text: Hemiparasitic plants with orobanchin (i.e., usually darkening in drying); corolla galeate (without a galea in Agalinis and Aureolaria ) [Figs. , ] (in part)
Autotrophic herbs, usually not darkening in drying; corolla not galeate (with a galea in Chelone )

c24.text: Androecium with 2 stamens, each stamen with 2 pollen sacs positioned perpendicular to one another—the upper pollen sac positioned transversely to the filament, the lower 1 positioned parallel to the filament; fruit an explosively dehiscent, loculicidal capsule
Androecium with 1–4 stamens, the stamens with parallel to somewhat divergent pollen sacs (with respect to each other); fruit a loculicidal or septicidal capsule, but not explosively dehiscent

c25.text: Calyx with a pronounced, tubular, connate portion [Fig. ]; capsule dehiscence loculicidal; stigma with 2 plate-like lobes that close after contact (in part)
Calyx connate at the base, but the connate portion not elongate; capsule dehiscence septicidal; stigmas with 2 lobes that remain open after contact (these plate-like in Gratiola )

c26.text: Lower pair of stamens (which are sterile in our species) with the filament axis bent completely back on themselves and then curved again, therefore, the filaments appearing forked
Lower pair of stamens without a conspicuously curved filament axis

c27.text: Amphibious plants of tidal shores with horizontal stems emitting at the nodes clusters of linear leaves and sometimes also peduncles bearing a solitary flower with a ± actinomorphic corolla (in part)

Terrestrial or non-tidal wetland plants with prostrate to, more commonly, upright stems and variable leaf shapes, though mostly wider than linear, with inflorescences borne on a stem bearing flowers with weakly to conspicuously zygomorphic corollas (in part)

/dkey/group-8/.title: Group 8: Herbaceous angiosperms with superior ovaries, actinomorphic flowers, and 2 or more distinct carpels

c1.text: Leaves peltate [Figs. , ]; plants aquatic
Petiole, if present, attached at the base of the leaf blade; plants terrestrial or sometimes aquatic in Caltha , Comarum , Mentha , Ranunculus , and Saururus

c2.text: Leaf blades orbicular, without basal lobes [Fig. ]; carpels individually sunken in the spongy receptacle; fruit a nut, loosely borne in cavities of the firm, accrescent receptacle [Fig. ]
Leaf blades elliptic, with basal lobes [Fig. ]; carpels free from the receptacle; fruit a leathery follicle, not enclosed by the receptacle (in part)

c3.text: Inflorescence a cylindrical, usually nodding spike produced on a peduncle opposite the leaves with 175–300 flowers that lack perianth and have 3–5 (usually 4) carpels that are basally connate and mature as rugose mericarps (in part)
Inflorescence not combinging the above characteristics, usually of a different type (e.g., cyme, raceme), with fewer flowers, and/or with perianth

c4.text: Corolla gamopetalous; carpels 2, each carpel evidently lobed, therefore, the gynoecium appearing to be composed of 4 carpels, separating at maturity into 4 half-carpellate segments
Corolla apopetalous or absent; carpels 1–many, not schizocarpic (except Malvaceae)

c5.text: Inflorescence a helicoid cyme [Figs. , , ]; leaves alternate (opposite in Cryptantha and Plagiobothrys ); stems terete or angled (in part)

Inflorescence mixed (i.e., thyrsoid), with cymose lateral branches, sometimes the inflorescence condensed in dense verticillasters of flowers, only rarely completely indeterminate [Figs. , , ]; leaves opposite; stems usually square (in part)

c6.text: Stamens monadelphous [Fig. ]; anthers unilocular; fruit a schizocarp (in part)
Stamens distinct; anthers bilocular; fruit otherwise

c7.text: Flowers lacking a hypanthium
Flowers with a hypanthium

c8.text: Plants ± succulent with fleshy, simple leaf blades; carpels with a small, scale-like, nectariferous appendage at the base; stamens usually 10 or fewer per flower (up to 80 in Sempervivum ); fruit a follicle
Plants not succulent, with thinner, simple, lobed, or compound leaf blades; carpels without a scale-like, nectariferous appendage; stamens usually many per flower; fruit an achene, berry, or follicle

c9.text: Intrastaminal nectar disk present; calyx sepaloid, with coriaceous, persistent sepals
Intrastaminal nectar disk absent; calyx sepaloid or petaloid, usually membranaceous to herbaceous and deciduous (in part)

c10.text: Leaves with simple blades, without stipules; flowers with 2 or 4 carpels; fruit a capsule (in part)
Leaves with simple to compound blades, stipulate (without stipules in Aruncus ); flowers with 2–many carpels; fruit an achene, drupe, or follicle, either solitary or in an aggregate (in part)

/dkey/group-9/.title: Group 9: Herbaceous angiosperms with superior ovaries, actinomorphic flowers, connate petals, and a solitary carpel or 2 or more connate carpels

c1.text: Plants parasitic, with haustoria, lacking chlorophyll; stems twining, pink-yellow to orange, with scale-like leaves [Figs. , ] (in part)

Plants autotrophic, without haustoria, with chlorophyll (without chlorophyll in Pterospora ); stems, when present, upright or twining, usually green for some period during the growing season, with foliaceous leaves (scale-like in Bartonia and Pterospora )

c2.text: Depressed, pulvinate [Fig. ], evergreen, alpine herbs of elevation exceeding 1000 meters; inflorescence a solitary, peduncled flower (in part)
Plants of various habit, but commonly upright or vining, with deciduous leaves, of lower elevation habitats; inflorescence various, but commonly composed of more than 1 flower

c3.text: Leaves all basal (opposite and borne on a stem in Plantago arenaria ); calyx and corolla inconspicuous, the corolla scarious, 3- or, more commonly, 4-merous [Figs. , ] (in part)
Leaves borne on a stem (all basal in Limosella , Menyanthes , and Primula ); calyx and/or corolla evident, at least 1 of which is petaloid, usually 4- or 5-merous

c4.text: Plants often with milky latex; carpels connate at the summit only, with a common stigma; fruit a pair of follicles
Plants with watery sap; carpels connate throughout or only in the basal portion; fruit an achene, berry, schizocarp, capsule, or pyxis

c5.text: Leaves with sheathing stipules (i.e., ocreae; these absent in Chorizanthe ) [Fig. ]; pedicels of the flowers subtended by sheathing bracteoles (i.e., ocreolae; except Chorizanthe , a species with flowers subtended by involucres); perianth mostly monochlamydeous, composed of ± petaloid tepals; fruit an achene (in part)
Leaves without sheathing stipules; pedicels without sheathing bracteoles; perianth dichlamydeous; fruit otherwise

c6.text: Stems prostrate, emitting at nodes a tuft of 5–10 narrow leaves and 1 or more, 1-flowered peduncles; plants of tidal shores (in part)

Stems upright or vining, the leaves normally 1 or 2 from a node, sometimes more; inflorescence various, usually with more than 1 flower; plants not of tidal shores (of coastal shorelines in Mertensia maritima and Heliotropium )

c7.text: Plants aquatic, with densely crowded, dissected leaves; inflorescence an umbel or raceme, the peduncle and axis of each individual raceme inflated and hollow, constricted at the nodes and bearing a whorl of flowers [Fig. ] (in part)
Plants aquatic or terrestrial, the leaves not both densely crowded and dissected; inflorescence without an inflated peduncle and axis

c8.text: Foliage leaves opposite or whorled
Foliage leaves alternate or all basal (appearing opposite in some Solanaceae due to forking of the stem)

c9.text: Carpels 2, each carpel lobed, often evidently so, therefore, the gynoecium appearing to be composed of 4 carpels, separating at maturity into 4 half-carpellate segments; fruit a schizocarp; flowers with 4 stamens (5 in Boraginaceae); stems quadrangular (terete or angled in Boraginaceae)
Carpels 1–3, not separating at maturity; fruit a capsule or pyxis; flowers with 4–7 stamens; stems mostly terete or angled

c10.text: Inflorescence a helicoid cyme [Figs. , , ]; flowers with 5 stamens; stems terete or angled (in part)
Inflorescence not appearing as a coiled raceme [Figs. , , ]; flowers with 4 stamens; stems quadrangular

c11.text: Style usually with an inconspicuous stigma; carpels evidently lobed; inflorescence mixed (i.e., thyrsoid), with cymose lateral branches, these usually arranged in dense verticillasters of flowers, ovules attached to lateral partitions and not the carpel margins [Figs. , ]; plants with mint-, pennyroyal-, or citrus-scented foliage (in part)
Style with a conspicuously lobed stigma; carpels weakly lobed; inflorescence indeterminate (e.g., spike, raceme) [Figs. , ]; placentation marginal; plants without aromatic foliage (in part)

c12.text: Stamens antepetalous [Fig. ]; ovary with 1 stigma; placentation free-central (in part)
Stamens antesepalous; ovary usually with a 2- or 3-lobed stigma; placentation parietal or axile

c13.text: Gynoecium with 3 carpels and 3 stigmas; placentation axile; calyx with scarious intervals between the green, longitudinal ribs (in part)
Gynoecium with 2 carpels and 2 stigmas; placentation parietal; calyx without scarious intervals between longitudinal ribs

c14.text: Leaf blades entire; capsule dehiscence septicidal; surface of vegetative organs ± glabrous (though the margins sometimes with cilia) (in part)
Leaf blades pinnately lobed; capsule dehiscence loculicidal; surface of at least some vegetative parts pubescent (in part)

c15.text: Inflorescence a helicoid cyme [Figs. , , ]; fruit a schizocarp (a 2-valved capsule in Hydrophyllum ) (in part)
Inflorescence otherwise; fruit a capsule, pyxis, or berry (the berry sometimes dry in the Solanaceae)

c16.text: Flowers with 10 stamens and 5 carpels; stipitate-glandular, mycoparasitic herbs lacking chlorophyll (in part)
Flowers with 4 or 5 stamens and 2 or 3 carpels; autotrophic herbs (except Bartonia ), with or without stipitate glands

c17.text: Leaves reduced to scales on the stem [Fig. ]; flowers 2.5–4 mm long (in part)
Leaves foliaceous, not scale-like; flowers longer

c18.text: Plants aquatic; leaves either floating or with 3 fleshy leaflets [Figs. , ] (in part)
Plants terrestrial; the leaves neither floating nor with 3 fleshy leaflets

c19.text: Stamens antepetalous; placentation free-central
Stamens antesepalous; placentation basal, parietal, or axile

c20.text: Leaves confined to the base of the stem; corolla ± salverform (in part)
Leaves borne on the stem; corolla ± rotate [Fig. ] (in part)

c21.text: Ovary with 4 or 6 ovules; fruit a 4- or 6-seeded capsule; plants climbing or trailing (twining only at the tip in Calystegia spithamaea ) (in part)
Ovary usually with more than 6 ovules; fruit usually a many-seeded capsule, berry, or pyxis; plants upright (climbing or trailing in Solanum dulcamara )

c22.text: Gynoecium composed of 3 carpels (2 in Navarretia ); calyx with scarious intervals between the green, longitudinal ribs (calyx of uniform texture in Collomia ); fruit a 3-valved capsule (2-valved in Navarretia ) (in part)
Gynoecium composed of 2 carpels (3–5 in Nicandra ); calyx of ± uniform texture; fruit a berry, 2-valved capsule, or pyxis

c23.text: Stamens each flanked by a pair of small scales; fruit a loculicidal capsule dehiscing by 2 valves (in part)
Stamens without associated scales; fruit usually a septicidal capsule opening by 2–4 valves, berry, or pyxis

c24.text: Fruit an unarmed capsule; anthers with 1 locule, opening by a single, transverse, distal slit; inflorescence a raceme or panicle (in part)

Fruit a berry, prickly capsule, or pyxis; anthers with 2 locules, opening by a pair of pores or longitudinal slits; inflorescence of solitary flowers in the axils of leaves or cymose (note: the cymes sometimes appear raceme- or panicle-like) (in part)

/dkey/group-10/.title: Group 10: Herbaceous angiosperms with superior ovaries, actinomorphic flowers, distinct petals or the petals lacking, and 2 or more connate carpels

c1.text: Plants submerged aquatics, attaching to the substrate by fleshy disks; flowers without perianth, borne singly in the axils of leaves, subtended by a tubular spathe

Plants aquatic or terrestrial, but not attaching to the substrate by fleshy disks; flowers with at least 1 whorl of perianth (sometimes so in only 1 sex of flower; lacking perianth in Callitriche , Euphorbia , and Saururus ), borne variously, not subtended by a tubular spathe

c2.text: Inflorescence a cylindrical, usually nodding spike produced on a peduncle opposite the leaves with 175–300 flowers that lack perianth and have 3–5 (usually 4) carpels that are basally connate and mature as rugose mericarps (in part)
Inflorescence not combinging the above characteristics, usually of a different type (e.g., cyme, raceme), with fewer flowers, and/or with perianth

c3.text: Placentation laminar; plants aquatic, with conspicuous elliptic or orbicular floating leaf blades with 2 basal lobes [Fig. ], arising directly from a rhizome (in part)
Placentation otherwise; plants terrestrial or aquatic; leaf blades various, but not at once floating, basally lobed, and arising from an underwater rhizome

c4.text: Inflorescence a cyathium, with a single carpellate flower and 2 or more staminate flowers borne in a cupuliform involucre, the margin of the involucre sometimes subtended by petaloid glands, the entire arrangement resembling a single flower; plants often with milky latex (in part)
Inflorescence not pseudanthial; plants with watery sap (milky or colored latex in the Papaveraceae)

c5.text: Calyx of 2, often caducous, sepals; petals wrinkled in bud; plants with milky or colored latex (in part)

Calyx of 3 or more sepals (2 sepals in the Portulacaceae and some Elatinaceae), or the perianth monochlamydeous and with 3 or more tepals, or the perianth absent; petals arranged otherwise in bud (wrinkled in the Lythraceae); plants with watery sap

c6.text: Plants insectivorous by means of viscid hairs or pitcher-shaped leaves [Figs. , ], of organic soils; leaves all basal
Plants not insectivorous, of mineral or organic soils; leaves variously arranged

c7.text: Leaf blades with viscid, glandular-hairs, flat, the margins not connate; inflorescence a raceme; styles 3, distinct

Leaf blades without glandular hairs, the margins connate, thereby forming a tube that is retrorsely pubescent on the adaxial (i.e., inside) surface [Fig. ]; inflorescence a single flower; styles 5, connate, modified into a 5-rayed, umbrella-shaped body

c8.text: Leaves opposite or whorled (sometimes the upper alternate in Chrysosplenium ) [Figs. , , ]
Leaves alternate or all basal [Figs. , , ]

c9.text: Leaves paripinnate, 1 of each node conspicuously larger than the other; fruit a schizocarp, each mericarp with 2 divergent horns and a central row of tubercles and transversely divided into 3–5 1-seeded compartments

Leaves simple, lobed, or compound, when pinnately compound then imparipinnate, those of a given node ± equal in size; fruit an achene, berry, pyxis, silique, silicle, capsule, or a schizocarp but then lacking horns and tubercles and not transversely divided into compartments

c10.text: Plants free-floating, rootless, aquatic; leaves 2- to 4-times dichotomously forked [Fig. ]; perianth composed of 7–15 basally connate sepals; fruit an achene with 2–15 marginal spines

Plants usually rooted, terrestrial or aquatic; leaves not dichotomously forked; perianth otherwise (consisting of up to 10 basally connate sepals in some Euphorbiaceae); fruit various, but not an achene with marginal spines

c11.text: Basal leaves peltate, 30–40 cm wide; fruit a yellow berry 40–50 mm wide (in part)
None of the leaves peltate, narrower; fruit an achene, capsule, pyxis, silique, or schizocarp

c12.text: Leaf blades punctate with pellucid dots, sessile; petals yellow or flesh-colored to pink (in part)
Leaf blades not pellucid-punctate, sessile or petiolate; petals variously colored, usually not yellow or flesh-colored (yellow in 1 species of Portulaca and some Linum ) or absent

c13.text: Leaf blades scale-like and sessile; flowers sunken into the fleshy, jointed stem [Fig. ]; plants coastal halophytes (in part)
Leaf blades foliaceous (though they may be small), sessile or petiolate; flowers not sunken into a fleshy, jointed stem; plants of various habitats

c14.text: Plants aquatic (though sometimes stranded after water level decline); androecium with 1–3 stamens
Plants terrestrial or of wetland habitats; androecium with 4–10 stamens

c15.text: Leaves crowded at the apex forming a floating rosette (not forming a rosette in 2 species) [Fig. ]; flowers unisexual, without perianth; fruit a schizocarp (in part)
Leaves not crowded at the apex; flowers bisexual, with sepals and petals; fruit a capsule

c16.text: Perianth monochlamydeous
Perianth dichlamydeous

c17.text: Perianth petaloid
Perianth sepaloid or inconspicuous

c18.text: Leaves whorled, 3–8 per node; placentation axile (in part)
Leaves opposite; placentation basal or free-central (axile in Sesuvium )

c19.text: Sepals with subterminal, slender, horn-like appendages; fruit a pyxis (in part)
Sepals lacking subterminal appendages; fruit an achene or capsule

c20.text: Flowers in a cyme, with a sepaloid involucre subtending 1–5 flowers and a petaloid calyx [Fig. ]; fruit an achene, enclosed in an indurate calyx (collectively called an anthocarp); cultivated and escaped plants
Flowers axillary, with only a petaloid calyx; fruit a 5-valved capsule; native plants of coastal saltmarshes (in part)

c21.text: Flowers with 7–20 or more stamens; style branches bifid or laciniately divided; fruit a capsule-like schizocarp with 2 or 3 mericarps (in part)
Flowers with 1–8 stamens; style branches simple (though the stigmatic surface may be fringed in some fashion); fruit a 2- to 10-valved capsule or utricle

c22.text: Stamens 4–8, set in the notches of an 8-lobed disk that fills much of the center of the flower; fruit a 2-valved capsule (in part)
Stamens 1–5, not set on a disk; fruit an achene or a 3- to 10-valved capsule

c23.text: Flowers unisexual; fruit an achene
Flowers bisexual; fruit a capsule (a utricle in Scleranthus )

c24.text: Ovary with 2 styles; leaf blades palmately lobed or divided; staminate flowers each with 5 stamens (in part)
Ovary with 1 style; leaf blades simple, without lobes or divisions; staminate flowers each with 4 stamens or 5 in Laportea (in part)

c25.text: Ovary with 3–5 locules; placentation axile; leaves whorled (in part)
Ovary with a single locule; placentation free-central; leaves opposite (in part)

c26.text: Calyx of 2 sepals [Fig. ]; stamens antepetalous (in part)
Calyx of 3 or more sepals [Figs. , , ]; stamens antesepalous

c27.text: Flowers 4-merous [Figs. , ]
Flowers 3-, 5-, or 6-merous [Figs. , , ]

c28.text: Leaf blades palmately lobed or palmately divided; androecium composed of 6 tetradynamous stamens; fruit a silique or silicle (in part)
Leaf blades simple; androecium composed of 4 or 8 stamens; fruit a capsule

c29.text: Anthers dehiscing by a single, terminal pore; filaments twisted, thereby bringing all the stamens to 1 side of the flower at anthesis; leaf blades 20–70 mm long
Anthers dehiscing by longitudinal slits; filaments not twisted to 1 side; leaf blades 2–23 (–30) mm long

c30.text: Sepals (1–) 1.5–3 mm long, entire at the apex; leaf blades linear-subulate; capsules 2–4 mm long (in part)
Sepals 0.7– 1 mm long, 3-cleft at the apex; leaf blades ovate to oblong; capsules 0.6–0.9 mm long (in part)

c31.text: Anthers dehiscing by 2 terminal pores; stigmas large, peltate, orbicular, with 4 or 5 lobes (in part)
Anthers dehiscing by longitudinal slits; stigmas smaller, linear to capitate, without lobes

c32.text: Style branches bifid or laciniately divided [Fig. ]; fruit a capsule-like schizocarp with 3 mericarps (in part)
Style branches simple (though the stigmatic surface may be fringed in some fashion); fruit a 2- to 10-valved capsule or a schizocarp separating into 5 mericarps

c33.text: Leaf blades palmately lobed or pinnately divided; fruit a schizocarp, with 5 1-seeded mericarps that elastically dehisce from a persistent, central column [Fig. ]
Leaf blades simple and unlobed; fruit a capsule

c34.text: Flowers perigynous, with intersepalar appendages; ovary 2-locular (in part)
Flowers hypogynous (perigynous in Scleranthus ), without intersepalar appendages; ovary 1- or 10-locular

c35.text: Capsule with 10 locules; placentation apical-axile; stamens alternating with small staminodes in some species; calyx aposepalous (in part)
Capsule with a single locule; placentation free-central or parietal; androecium without staminodes; calyx apo- or gamosepalous

c36.text: Androecium with 6 stamens in 2 whorls, the outer whorl shorter than the inner; flowers sessile; placentation parietal

Androecium with 1–10 stamens in 1 or 2 whorls, when in 2 whorls the stamens not dissimilar as to length; flowers pedicellate (sessile in Herniaria and Scleranthus ); placentation free-cental (in part)

c37.text: Leaf blades compound, trifoliate, with obcordate leaflets [Fig. ]; petals white with pink stripes or yellow
Leaf blades simple to compound, but not as above; petals variously colored or absent

c38.text: Flowers with 4 petals (very rarely 0 or 2); androecium with 6 stamens arranged in tetradynamous fashion (rarely only 2 stamens, numbering 6 but not tretradynamous in Cleome ); fruit a silique or silicle
Flower with 0–6 petals; androecium with a variable number of stamens, but never 6 and tetradynamous; fruit otherwise

c39.text: Flowers, except sometimes for the lower ones, ebracteate [Figs. , , ]; stamens usually 6 (rarely only 2), the outer pair shorter than the other 4; silique or silicle usually divided into 2 locules by an unvascularized septum (in part)
Flowers subtended by bracts; stamens 6, all elongate; silique unilocular (in part)

c40.text: Stamens monadelphous, the filaments forming a conspicuous tube surrounding the style [Fig. ]; gynoecium composed of 5–40 carpels (in part)
Stamens distinct or connate at only the very base; gynoecium composed of 1–6 (–7) carpels

c41.text: Leaves with tubular, sheathing stipules (i.e., ocreae); flowers subtended by tubular, sheathing bracteoles (i.e., ocreolae) (in part)
Leaves without tubular, sheathing stipules; flowers not subtended by tubular, sheathing bracteoles

c42.text: Leaf blades simple, toothed, or lobed but not divided

c43.text: Perianth 3-merous, the sepals not petaloid; flowers solitary on thin peduncles from the axils of leaves; fruit a schizocarp

Perianth (3–) 4- to 6-merous, the sepals petaloid; flowers borne in cymes or racemes, or borne singly at the summit of the stem or tips of branches, or singly on scapes; fruit a blue seed or an achene, berry, follicle, or capsule

c44.text: Anthers dehiscing by flaps; stamens as many as the petals and opposite them (i.e., antepetalous); fruit an exposed, blue seed or a capsule (in part)
Anthers dehiscing by longitudinal slits; stamens numbering more than the petals; fruit an achene, berry, or follicle

c45.text: Leaf blades 2- or 3-times divided or dissected into numerous, very narrow segments; fruit a follicle or berry; sepals caducous or not (in part)
Leaf blades 1-time divided ; fruit an achene enclosed in an indurate hypanthium or a follicle; sepals not caducous (in part)

c46.text: Perianth, at least in part, petaloid (though caducous in Hydrastis )

c47.text: Stamens 10 per flower; fruit a 5- to 7-lobed and locular capsule [Fig. ]
Stamens 1–5 per flower (as many as 20 or more in some Euphorbiaceae); fruit an achene, utricle, pyxis, berry, multiple, or 3-locular capsule or capsule-like schizocarp

c48.text: Flowers perigynous, bisexual; leaf blades palmately lobed (in part)
Flowers hypogynous, unisexual or sometimes bisexual in the Amaranthaceae; leaf blades simple to pinnately lobed (palmately lobed in Ricinus , which has a peltate attachment of the petiole)

c49.text: Filaments stout, nearly as wide as the anthers, white, primarily responsible for the flower color; leaf blades thick and evergreen
Filaments more slender, not as wide as the anthers, not imparting an evident white color to flowers; leaf blades thinner and deciduous

c50.text: Ovary 3-locular (1-locular in Crotonopsis ); styles 2 or 3, each 1 bifid [Fig. ]; fruit a capsule-like schizocarp with 2 or 3 mericarps (an achene in Crotonopsis ) (in part)
Ovary 1-locular; styles 1–3, without additional branching (though the stigmatic surface may be fringed in some fashion); fruit an achene, utricle, multiple, or pyxis

c51.text: Sepals usually dry and scarious; filaments distinct or, more commonly, connate at least near the base; ovary with 3 stigmas (in part)
