Sepals membranaceous to herbaceous (hyaline in Axyris ); filaments distinct; ovary with usually 1 or 2 stigmas

c52.text: Proximal portion of first pair of primary lateral veins at the very margin of the leaf blade (i.e., the basiscopic side of the vein exposed for a short distance); stems with minute, uncinate hairs; fruit a multiple of achenes (in part)

First pair of primary lateral veins not at the margin of the leaf blade (i.e., both the basiscopic and acroscopic sides bordered by green leaf tissue) or the leaf blades with 1 nerve and lateral veins lacking; stems variously glabrous to pubescent, but lacking uncinate hairs; fruit an achene, utricle, or pyxis

c53.text: Ovary with 1 stigma; flowers unisexual; plants sometimes with stinging hairs (in part)
Ovary with 2 (–5) stigmas; flowers unisexual or bisexual; plants without stinging hairs (in part)

c54.text: Plants lacking chlorophyll, the stems white to pink, yellow to brown, or pink to red; leaves reduced and scale-like [Fig. ] (in part)
Plants with chlorophyll, the stems and/or leaves green; leaves foliaceous

c55.text: Anthers dehiscing by 2 apical pores; leaves all basal; fruit a 5-valved capsule (in part)
Anthers dehiscing by longitudinal slits; leaves and fruits various

c56.text: Gynoecium with 5–12 (–15) styles; fruit a berry
Gynoecium with 2–7 styles; fruit a capsule, pyxis, or utricle

c57.text: Flowers with 5 sepals and consistently with 10 styles, arranged in a raceme; berry dark purple; leaf blades unlobed
Flowers with 3 caducous sepals and with a variable number of styles, solitary at the summit of the stem; berry red; leaf blades palmately lobed (in part)

c59.text: Perianth 6-merous; sepals alternating with appendages at the rim of the hypanthium; petals crumpled in bud (in part)
Perianth 5-merous; sepals not alternating with appendages; petals mostly imbricate in bud, not crumpled

c60.text: Androecium with 5 stamens and 5 trifid, white staminodes; petals 10–18 mm long; flowers with 4 carpels; fruit a 4-locular capsule (in part)
Androecium with 10 stamens; petals 2–6 mm long; flowers with 2 carpels; fruit a follicle or a 1- or 2-locular capsule (in part)

c61.text: Calyx definitely gamosepalous; halophytic plants of Atlantic coast shores
Calyx aposepalous or nearly so, connate at only the very base, if at all; plants not halophytic

c62.text: Calyx composed of 2 sepals; stems prostrate; fruit a pyxis (in part)
Calyx composed of 5 sepals; stems upright; fruit a capsule

c63.text: Gynoecium of 5 carpels; capsule 10-valved; leaves borne on a stem (in part)
Gynoecium of 2 or 4 carpels; capsule 2- or 4-valved; leaves all basal or essentially so

c64.text: Androecium with 5 stamens and 5 trifid, white staminodes; petals 10–18 mm long; flowers with 4 carpels; fruit a 4-locular capsule (in part)
Androecium with 10 stamens; petals 2–6 mm long; flowers with 2 carpels; fruit a follicle or a 1- or 2-locular capsule (in part)

c1.text: Aerial stems monomorphic, unbranched, persisting more than one year (i.e., evergreen); strobilus with an apiculus at its apex [Fig. ]; stomates sunken below the surface, arranged in single lines on each side of stem grooves (view at 30 ×)

Aerial stems monomorphic or dimorphic (i.e., the vegetative and spore-bearing stems differing in appearance), commonly with regular whorls of branches (except in unbranched forms of E. fluviatile and E. palustre ), deciduous at the end of the growing season; strobilus rounded at its apex; stomates on the surface, scattered or in bands on each side of stem grooves

c2.text: Stems 14- to 50-ridged; leaves articulated to and deciduous from the sheaths; central cavity greater than 50% of the stem diameter; strobili 10–20 mm tall
Stems 3- to 12-ridged; leaves not articulated to the sheaths and persistent on them; central cavity up to 35% of the stem diameter; strobili 2–10 mm tall

c3.text: Stems tortuous, 6-ridged, 0.5–1 mm thick; sheaths with 3 leaves; central cavity absent; vallecular cavities 3
Stems erect and straight, 3- to 12-ridged, 1–4.5 mm thick; leaves numbering the same as the ridges; central cavity evident; vallecular cavities 5–12

c4.text: Strobili appearing in summer, borne on firmer, green, photosynthetic stems that persist throughout the season (i.e., stems monomorphic); length of the first internode of each branch shorter than its subtending stem sheath (or sometimes the branches absent) [Figs. , ]; grooves of branches rounded (i.e., U-shaped in cross-section)

Strobili appearing in spring, borne on soft, pink to light brown stems, the green, photosynthetic stems forming or appearing later (i.e., stems dimorphic); length of the first internode of each branch equal to or exceeding its subtending stem sheath [Fig. ]; grooves of branches channeled (i.e., C-shaped in cross-section)

c5.text: Leaves numbering 12–24 per sheath, 1.5–3 mm long, dark throughout or with a narrow, white band [Fig. ]; stems with 9–25 low ridges; central cavity 75% or more of the stem diameter
Leaves numbering 5–10 per sheath, 2–5 mm long, with prominent white margins [Fig. ]; stems with 5–10 prominent ridges; central cavity less than 35% of the stem diameter

c6.text: Leaves red-brown, cohering in 3 or 4 large groups, papery; branches of the stem compound (i.e., again branched)
Leaves largely brown to black, separate or in 4 or more small groups, firm; branches of the stem simple (except sometimes in damaged plants)

c7.text: Reproductive stems without stomates, promptly senescing; leaves of the main axis dark at the margin or with a very thin, obscure white margin, those of the branches subulate; central cavity ca. 25% of the stem diameter; stem internodes smooth to moderately scabrous

Reproductive stems with stomates, becoming green and branched; leaves of the main axis with a prominent white margin, those of the branches triangular; central cavity 35–50% of the stem diameter; stem internodes evidently scabrous

c1.text: This genus contains exactly one species.
This genus contains exactly one species.
This genus contains exactly one species.
Megaspores echinate with thin, sharp spines; leaves deciduous
Megaspores variously ornamented, but without a spiny texture; leaves persisting more than 1 year

c2.text: Megaspores 0.4–0.56 mm in diameter, averaging less than 0.5 mm, patterned with an unbroken reticulum [Fig. ]
Megaspores 0.4–0.75 mm in diameter, averaging more than 0.5 mm, cristate, rugulate, or reticulate with broken or anastomosing ridges

c3.text: Leaves with abundant stomates, bright green; plants aquatic to amphibious, occasionally emergent; girdle of megaspores obscure
Leaves with few or no stomates, dark green to red-green or red-brown; plants aquatic, usually submerged; girdle evident (obscure in I. prototypus )

c4.text: Megaspores 0.55–0.75 mm in diameter, averaging more than 0.6 mm; leaves abruptly tapering to the tip; plants typically submerged 1–3 (–5) m
Megaspores 0.4–0.65 mm in diameter, averaging less than 0.6 mm; leaves gradually tapering to the tip; plants submerged to 1 (–3) m

c5.text: Megaspores with a papillate girdle, cristate to reticulate with sharp or roughened crests [Fig. ]
Megaspores with a smooth girdle, reticulate with low, rounded ridges

c6.text: Velum covering the entire sporangium [Fig. ]; leaves very rigid and straight to the tip; sporangium wall unpigmented; girdle of the megaspore obscure
Velum covering less than half the sporangium [Fig. ]; leaves pliant and curling at the tip; sporangium wall brown-streaked; girdle evident

c7.text: Megaspores with a papillate girdle, cristate to reticulate with irregular, roughened crests
Megaspores with a smooth girdle, reticulate with smooth, rounded crests [Fig. ]

c1.text: This genus contains exactly one species.
Trophophylls monomorphic, spirally arranged, not in distinct ranks [Fig. ]; axillary trophophylls absent at branching points
Trophophylls dimorphic, arranged in 4 ranks, the 2 lateral ranks with larger leaves than the 2 median ranks [Fig. ]; axillary trophophylls present at branching points

c2.text: Trophophylls thin, spinulose-toothed, acuminate, with stomates scattered over the abaxial surface; strobili terete; sporophylls ascending to spreading, mostly 10-ranked [Fig. ]; rhizophores absent
Trophophylls thicker, ciliolate, bristle-tipped, with stomates restricted to an abaxial groove; strobili tetragonous; sporophylls appressed, 4-ranked; rhizophores present

c3.text: Median trophophylls acute to acuminate at apex, rarely attenuate and then often apically keeled and the vein not reaching tip; megaspores 0.29–0.35 (–0.38) mm in diameter, closely reticulate, dull
Median trophophylls with a long-attenuate, often recurved, apex, not keeled, the vein prolonged into the tip; megaspores 0.33–0.4 mm in diameter, more loosely reticulate, shiny

c1.text: Upright shoots unbranched, lacking winter bud constrictions, produced from horizontal shoots that travel over the surface [Fig. ]; horizontal shoots lacking winter bud constrictions [Fig. ]; plants primarily of hydric habitats

Upright shoots branched, with winter bud constrictions, produced from subterranean or superficial horizontal shoots; horizontal shoots with winter bud constrictions (except Dendrolycopodium ), these marked by a zone of small, congested trophophylls; plants primarily of mesic to xeric habitats

c2.text: Sporophylls green, superficially similar to the trophophylls of the upright shoots, arranged in 10 or more vertical ranks, 2.9–9 mm long; strobilus stalks with abundant and imbricate trophophylls; trophophylls of the horizontal shoots monomorphic; plants deciduous, overwintering by a thickened tip of stem (i.e., turion)

Sporophylls stramineous at maturity, clearly differentiated from the trophophylls of the upright shoots, arranged in 4–10 vertical ranks, 2.7–3.3 mm long; strobilus stalks with few and remote trophophylls; trophophylls of the horizontal shoots dimorphic, the lateral trophophylls markedly wider than the median trophophylls; plants evergreen

c3.text: Branches 1–4.4 mm wide inclusive of the trophophylls, flat to quadrangular, with 4 ranks of trophophylls (terete and with 5 ranks of trophophylls in one species) [Fig. ]; branching of strobilus stalks, when present, dichotomous

Branches 5–12 mm wide, terete (somewhat compressed in D. obscurum ), with 6 or more ranks of trophophylls; branching of strobilus stalks, when present, pseudomonopodial (i.e., falsely appearing to have a main axis from which branches arise)

c4.text: Strobili borne on stalks; trophophylls of the upright shoot branches arranged in alternating pseudowhorls of 6–10, tipped with a colorless hair 1.5–4 mm long
Strobili sessile; trophophylls of the upright shoot branches arranged in alternating pseudowhorls of 3–5, merely pointed or with a minute, but firm, spine-like tip

c5.text: Upright shoots with an obvious main axis from which repeatedly forked branches arise (i.e., the shoots dendroid), bearing trophophylls that are merely pointed at the apex; horizontal shoots subterranean, lacking winter bud constrictions

Upright shoots with 1–4 subdichotomous branches (i.e., the shoots not dendroid and the main axis usually obscure), bearing trophophylls with a minute, but firm, spinule 0.4–1 mm long at the apex; horizontal shoots at or near the surface, with winter bud constrictions

c1.text: Trophophylls dimorphic, those in the apical portion of the shoot noticeably shorter and more ascending than those near the base [Fig. ]; gemmiphores borne throughout the apical portion of plant; lateral leaves of gemmae 0.5–1.1 (–1.2) mm wide, narrow-acute to acute at the apex; shoots determinate, the entire stem turning yellow on senescence

Trophophylls nearly monomorphic, those near the apex neither conspicuously smaller nor more ascending than those near the base; gemmiphores borne in a single whorl at the apex of a season’s growth; lateral leaves of gemmae 1.3–2.5 mm wide, obtuse to rounded at apex; shoots indeterminate, the base eventually turning yellow and rotting away

c2.text: Trophophylls obovate, definitely widest beyond the middle, with 1–8 evident teeth [Fig. ], lacking stomates on the adaxial surface; shoots with evident winter bud constrictions

Trophophylls lanceolate to narrow-triangular, widest below the middle, entire or rarely with obscure, papilla-like teeth, with abundant stomates on the adaxial surface (i.e., 30–90 per leaf surface); shoots with obscure winter bud constrictions

c1.text: This genus contains exactly one species.
Trophophores (i.e., vegetative portion of leaf blades) simple, entire; venation reticulate; sporangia borne on a compact, linear sporophore
Trophophores lobed or compound (rarely simple in B. tenebrosum ), the ultimate segments entire or toothed [Figs. , ]; venation forking; sporangia borne on pinnately branched sporophores [Figs. , ]

Fertile leaves with monomorphic leaflets, borne on a blade separate from the vegetative leaves; axil of leaflets on vegetative leaves bearing a tuft of white hairs (these turning light brown with age) on the abaxial side
Fertile leaves with dimorphic leaflets—some leaflets bearing sporangia and some not; axil of vegetative leaflets without a tuft of hairs
Petiole apparently forking into two main divisions; sori borne on the surface of a false indusium, this best viewed through dissection; ultimate segments without a distinct midrib
Petiole not appearing to fork into two divisions; sori borne on the surface of the leaf blade near margin and covered by a false indusium; ultimate segments with a midrib

c2.text: Leaf blade tissue pubescent with septate hairs; ultimate segments of reproductive leaves 3–5 mm long
Leaf blade tissue not pubescent (though the petioles and rachises may be pubescent); ultimate segments of reproductive leaves 5–75 mm long

c3.text: Leaf blades thin, herbaceous to membranaceous, withering by late summer; rhizome scales colorless; leaves dimorphic—the reproductive ones with more elongate and relatively narrower segments compared with the vegetative ones; veins not reaching margins of ultimate segments

Leaf blades thick, coriaceous, persistent; rhizome scales red-brown; leaves monomorphic to hemidimorphic (e.g., the reproductive leaves somewhat longer and more divided than the vegetative leaves in P. atropurpurea ); veins reaching margins of ultimate segments

c1.text: Sori discrete, spherical, borne in circular or slightly bivalvate cups formed by fusion of the true indusium with the false indusium; false indusium merely a reflexed tooth or lobe; leaf blade narrow-oblong to lanceolate or broad-lanceolate, 12–25 (–30) cm wide; nectaries absent; base of petiole with 1 or 2 vascular bundles

Sori in a marginal band not borne in cup-like structures; false indusium formed by a ± elongate, revolute margin; leaf blade broad-deltate to ovate-deltate, (25–) 40–70 cm wide; nectaries present at base of leaf divisions, these appearing as dark, oval areas in early season; base of petiole with 10 or more vascular bundles

Sporangiasters more than 40 per sorus; scales of rhizome and petiole golden brown; spores smaller than 52 μm in diameter; leaflet apex usually pointed; leaf blades tending to be more triangular, widest near the base [Fig. ]

Sporangiasters fewer than 40 per sorus; scales of rhizome and petiole golden brown with a dark brown central strip; spores larger than 58 μm in diameter; leaflet apex usually rounded; leaf blades tending to be more oblong, widest near the middle [Fig. ]
Leaves monomorphic, with 15–20 pairs of distinct, lobed leaflets; veins forming 1 row of areoles adjacent to the costae or costules
Leaves dimorphic, with 7–10 pairs of leaflets, the sterile leaflets more or less confluent and serrulate; veins forming 2 or more rows of areoles adjacent to the costae
Leaf blades simple, frequently rooting at the tip; venation reticulate; sori irregularly scattered over the blade
Leaf blades 1- to 3-times divided [Figs. , ], not rooting at the tip; venation free (i.e., the veins not rejoining); sori in paired rows on the leaflets

c2.text: At least the larger leaflets divided into leafules [Figs. , ]; leaf blades deltate or deltate-ovate to lanceolate or obovate, with 2–10 pairs of leaflets
None of the leaflets divided; leaf blades linear to narrow-oblanceolate, with (6–) 15–45 pairs of leaflets

c3.text: Leaf blades usually with 2–5 pairs of leaflets [Fig. ], dull blue-green in life; leaflets mostly rhombic to obtriangular-obovate
Leaf blades usually with (4–) 5–10 pairs of leaflets [Fig. ], shiny green in life; leaflets triangular-lanceolate to triangular-ovate

c4.text: Leaves dimorphic—the fertile erect and tall, the sterile prostrate or arching and short; leaflets with a basal auricle
Leaves monomorphic; leaflets without a basal auricle

c5.text: Rachis red-brown to nearly black throughout; leaflets oblong to oval, the middle ones 2.5–4 mm wide (i.e., measured parallel with the leaf axis); petioles 0.15–0.25 times the length of the blade
Rachis green; leaflets deltate to rhombic, the middle ones 4–5 mm wide; petioles 0.25–0.5 (–1) times the length of the blade

c1.text: Leaf blades ± triangular; some of the basal leaflets connected by a wing of tissue along the rachis; costae not grooved adaxially; indusium absent
Leaf blades narrow-lanceolate to elliptic; none of the basal leaflets connected by a wing of tissue; costae grooved adaxially; indusium present

c2.text: Abaxial surface of costae without scales; veins of ultimate segments not forking near margin; leaf blades with either red to orange resinous glands (e.g., P. simulata ) or greatly reduced lower leaflets (e.g., P. noveboracensis )

Abaxial surface of costae with small, tan scales; veins of ultimate segments of vegetative blades usually forking near margin; leaf blades lacking both red to orange glands and greatly reduced lower leaflets

c1.text: Sterile leaves deeply lobed, divided only in the basal portion if at all; blade deltate, widest at the base; venation reticulate; sori enclosed in spherical leafules
Sterile leaves once-divided; blade elliptic to narrowly oblanceolate, widest above the middle; venation free (i.e., the veins forking and not rejoining); sori enclosed in linear leaflets

Indusium inferior, composed of lacerate or filamentous segments at maturity; veins not reaching margin of leaf segments, ending in hydathodes near the margin [Fig. ]; petioles articulated near base, this recognizable as a small, swollen node (not articulated in W. obtusa )

Indusium absent or present, sometimes inconspicuous, superior when present, attached centrally or laterally, not divided; veins reaching margin of leaf segments [Fig. ]; petioles not articulated near base

c2.text: Indusium absent; leaf blades triangular to pentagonal [Fig. ]; rhizome long and slender; leaflets weakly articulated to rachis; basal leaflets noticeably larger than next-apical pair

Indusium present, though inconspicuous in Cystopteris ; leaf blades lanceolate to triangular; rhizome relatively short; leaflets not articulated to rachis; basal leaflets not or only slightly larger than next-apical pair

c3.text: Indusium ovate to lanceolate, short, inconspicuous, attached laterally and arched over sorus; vascular bundles at the base of the petiole round or oblong in cross-section
Indusium linear, hooked at one end, or horseshoe-shaped, elongate, evident; vascular bundles at the base of the petiole lunate in cross-section

c4.text: Sori hooked at one end, some crossing the veinlets [Fig. ]; indument of rachis and costae usually of stipitate glands (rarely indument absent)
Sori straight or slightly falcate, not crossing the veinlets [Fig. ]; indument of rachis and costae absent or of septate hairs only

c5.text: Leaf blade 1.5- to 2-times divided; petiole with 2 rows of sharp or blunt marginal teeth on the swollen base (note: this feature absent in many collections but visible in the field)
Leaf blade once divided; petiole base lacking marginal teeth

c1.text: Indusium peltate (i.e., attached at the center by a stalk); leaflets or leafules with a basal auricle
Indusium attached laterally at a distinct sinus; leaflets and leafules lacking a basal auricle
Winter bud scales blunt at the apex, slightly keeled; leaf blades gradually tapering to the apex [Fig. ]
Winter bud scales sharply pointed to cuspidate, definitely keeled or folded; leaf blades abruptly tapering to the apex [Fig. ]

c2.text: Low shrubs with straggling, diffusely branched habit; leaf blades 1–2 (–2.4) mm wide; stomates in 5–7 (–9) rows in each band; petioles gradually curved or with an abrupt bend near the junction of the branch, not clasping the branchlet; seeds round or somewhat compressed near apex, but not angled

Plants upright; leaf blades 2–3 mm wide; stomates in (7–) 9–14 (–19) rows in each band; petioles with an abrupt bend near the junction of the blade, clasping the branchlet; seeds 4- or 5-angled near apex

c1.text: Seed cones fleshy and resembling a firm berry, the scales not opening [Fig. ]; seeds not winged; abaxial glands on leaves elliptic to elongate
Seed cones woody, the scales opening and exposing the axis; seeds winged; abaxial glands on leaves circular or oval to elliptic

c2.text: Branchlets terete or tetragonous; alternating pairs of leaves similar; seed cones nearly spherical, with peltate scales; abaxial leaf glands circular [Fig. ]

Branchlets flat; alternating pairs of leaves dimorphic—those of the upper and lower rank flat, those of the lateral ranks folded; seed cones ellipsoidal, with basifixed scales; abaxial leaf glands oval to elliptic [Fig. ]

c1.text: Leaves, at least in part, borne in fascicles or spirally arranged tufts of 2–60 on short shoots
Leaves all borne singly

c2.text: Leaves annually deciduous, those of the short shoots in spirally arranged tufts of 10–60 [Fig. ]; each scale of a strobilus without an umbo; bracts exserted in basal portion of strobilus
Leaves persisting more than 1 year, those of the short shoots in fascicles of 2–5; each scale of a strobilus with an umbo; bracts hidden by scales

c3.text: Winter buds very resinous, the individual scales concealed by resin; strobili erect, with deciduous scales; leaves attached directly to branchlet and expanded to a circular base

Winter buds not, or only slightly, resinous, the individual scales visible; strobili pendant at maturity [Figs. , ], with persistent scales; leaves either attached to peg-like projections (i.e., sterigmata) from branchlet and narrowed to the attachment or attached directly to the branchlet with an expanded elliptic base

c4.text: Bracts of seed cone conspicuously exserted, 3-lobed at apex, the central lobe longer than the lateral lobes; young bark with resin blisters; leaves attached directly to the branchlet and expanded to an elliptic base
Bracts of seed cone not exserted, not 3-lobed at apex; bark lacking resin blisters; leaves attached to peg-like projections from branchlet and narrowed to the attachment

c5.text: Leaf blades flat, petiolate, rounded at apex, dimorphic—longer, spreading ones and shorter, often appressed, ones; terminal shoot nodding
Leaf blades tetragonous, sessile, pointed at apex, monomorphic; terminal shoot erect

c1.text: Plants thalloid, not differentiated into stems and leaves, 0.5–15 mm long, floating on or near the surface of water [Figs. , ]
Plants not thalloid, differentiated into stems and leaves, much larger, terrestrial or emergent aquatics

c2.text: Thalli without roots, lacking veins; flowers without a spathe; thallus buds produced from a single, terminal pouch or cavity at base of parent thallus
Thalli with roots, with 1 or more veins; flowers with a small, membranous spathe; thallus buds from 2 lateral pouches at parent thallus base

c3.text: Thalli ovoid to globose or boat-shaped (i.e., flattened above and rounded below), without air spaces [Figs. , ]; flower produced from cavity along median line of upper thallus surface
Thalli flat, elongate, narrowly sabre-shaped, with air spaces [Fig. ]; flower produced from a cavity at the side of the median line of upper thallus surface

c4.text: Each thallus with 2–21 roots, the lower surface red-purple, the upper surface with (3–) 5–16 (–21) veins
Each thallus with a single root, the lower surface green (purple in L. turionifera ), the upper surface with 1–3 (–5) nerves

c5.text: Thalli with (5–) 7–16 (–21) veins, 1–1.5 times as long as wide; roots numbering 7–21 per thallus, only 1 or 2 perforating the small, membranous scale at thallus base
Thalli with (3–) 5–7 veins, 1.5–2 times as long as wide; roots numbering 2–7 (–12), all perforating the small, membranous scale at thallus base

c6.text: Leaves compound, with 3–13 (–21) leaflets; flowers concealing only the basal portion of the axis of the spadix
Leaves simple; flowers concealing most or all of the axis of the spadix

c7.text: Spathe absent; adaxial surface of leaf blades dark blue-green with a conspicuous velvety sheen created by a waxy epidermal layer
Spathe present; leaf blades otherwise

c8.text: Spathe adaxially white, open, nearly flat, not concealing the spadix; fruit a cluster of distinct, red berries; plants from a long, creeping rhizome

Spathe green, or green to brown and marked with purple, convolute, concealing the basal portion of the spadix; fruit a cluster of green to brown berries or mature carpels submerged in the fleshy spadix; plants from erect rhizomes or fibrous roots

c9.text: Mature leaf blades rounded or cordate at the base, lacking a prominent vein that extends into the short, basal lobes (when present); spadix subglobose; flowers with 4 tepals; fruit of mature carpels submerged in the fleshy spadix; plants malodorous

Leaf blades sagittate to hastate, with pronounced basal lobes and a conspicuous vein extending into each lobe; spadix elongate; flowers without perianth; fruit a green to brown berry; plants not malodorous

c1.text: Leaves flat, (15–) 20–80 mm wide, produced in early season and soon withering, usually not present during anthesis; capsule prominently 3-lobed
Leaves flat or terete, 1–20 mm wide, not early withering, present during anthesis; capsule only slightly lobed or not produced

c2.text: Umbels composed entirely of flowers, without bulbils
Umbels with most or all of the flowers replaced by bulbils

c3.text: Pedicels 10–50 mm long, longer than the flowers; scapes 3–20 mm in diameter; bulbs 3–10 cm in diameter; flowers 3–7 mm long; leaf blades semicircular in cross-section, 3–20 mm wide
Pedicels 2–6 mm long, shorter than to nearly equaling the flowers; scapes 3–5 mm in diameter; bulbs 1.5–2 cm in diameter; flowers 8–12 mm long; leaf blades terete in cross-section, 2–7 mm wide

c4.text: Bulbs covered with an outer layer of fibrous reticulum [Fig. ]; leaf-bearing nodes confined to the basal of scape; inflorescence subtended by 3 or 4 spathiform bracts (note: the bracts are often caducous, so fewer may be present at time of observation)

Bulbs covered with a membranaceous-scaly outer layer, fibers (if present) not forming a reticulum; leaf-bearing nodes extending to midpoint of scape or higher; inflorescence subtended by 1 or 2 spathiform bracts

c5.text: Umbel subtended by 2 persistent, spathiform bracts; flowers 6–8 mm long, on pedicels 15–60 mm long
Umbel subtended by a solitary, caducous, spathiform bract; flowers 3–5 mm long, on pedicels 10–20 mm long

c6.text: Leaf blade hollow in the basal half, terete, 2–4 mm in diameter; bulbs 1–2 cm in diameter
Leaf blade solid, flat, 5–20 mm wide; bulbs (1.5–) 3–8 cm in diameter

c1.text: Seeds 3 per capsule, with a caruncle (this modified into a tuft of hairs in L. parviflora ); plants pubescent with white hairs, especially at the summit of the leaf sheaths and the basal margins of the leaf blades; leaf sheaths closed (i.e., with connate margins)
Seeds many per capsule, lacking a caruncle (though with white appendages at each end in some species); plants glabrous; leaf sheaths open
Leaves opposite; flowers unisexual; staminate flowers with 1 stamen; stigma funnelform
Leaves alternate; flowers bisexual, with 2 or 4 stamens; stigma slender to capitate

c2.text: Leaf blades narrow-linear, 0.2–1.5 mm wide, all submersed, cross-septate throughout; stipules connate to the blade for a distance of 4–30 mm, commonly more than 10 mm; spikes submersed or sometimes floating, with well-separated lower whorls of flowers, on thin, flexuous peduncles; drupes not compressed, with an indistinctly coiled embryo

Leaf blades filiform to orbicular, 0.1–75 mm wide, all submersed or some floating, cross-septate only in the central lacunar bands (if present); stipules distinct from the blade or connate for a distance of less than 10 mm (long-connate in P. robbinsii ); spikes usually with contiguous whorls of flowers, on thick, stiff peduncles, usually emersed; drupes compressed, with a distinctly coiled embryo (indistinctly coiled in P. robbinsii )

c1.text: Spikelets appearing spiny, either enclosed in a bur-like fascicle of reduced branches or with an enlarged, uncinate-prickly glume [Figs. , ]
Spikelets not spiny, although pubescence or bristles may be present [Figs. , , ]

c2.text: Spikelets with 2 or more evident florets [Figs. , , ]
Spikelets with only 1 evident floret (members of the subfamily Panicoideae key under this lead) [Figs. , , ]

c3.text: Inflorescence an open to dense panicle [Figs. , , ]
Inflorescence a solitary, terminal spike or raceme, or a panicle with 2 or more secund, spike-like branches [Figs. , , ]

c4.text: Spikelets dimorphic with the 2 types paired—the lower spikelet of the pair sterile, flabellate, consisting of 2 glumes and several narrow, acuminate lemmas, concealing the upper, fertile spikelets with 2–4 florets
Spikelets of a single plant monomorphic

c5.text: At least 1 of the glumes (often both) nearly equaling to surpassing the body of the most apical lemma of each spikelet, partially or completely concealing the florets [Figs. , ]
Both glumes shorter than the body of the most apical lemma of the spikelet, the florets largely visible [Figs. , , ]

c6.text: Glumes or lemmas or both folded (i.e., V-shaped in cross-section), sometimes with a low to pronounced keel
Glumes and lemmas flat, arched, or rounded over the abaxial surface, lacking a keel

c7.text: Inflorescence a panicle with secund, spike-like branches [Fig. ]
Inflorescence an open to dense panicle, the branches not both secund and spike-like (often neither) or a secund spike [Figs. , ]

c8.text: Inflorescence composed of a single, terminal spike, raceme, or spike-like panicle, the branches, when present, scarcely discernible [Figs. , , ]
Inflorescence a congested to open panicle with visible branching, or composed of 2 or more spikes, racemes, or rames

c9.text: Glumes often as long as or longer than the lemmas and concealing the florets; spikelets usually arranged in obvious pairs or triplets with 1 spikelet sessile or shortly pedicellate and the remaining pedicellate (sometimes the pedicellate spikelet reduced and represented by only a pedicel; not organized in pairs or triplets in Milium ) [Fig. ]
One (i.e., the lower) or both glumes shorter than the lemmas or the glumes absent; spikelets not organized in pairs or triplets (sometimes in groups of 2 or 3 in Digitaria and Paspalum ) [Fig. ]

c1.text: Perianth at maturity composed of elongate capillary bristles that greatly exceed the subtending floral scales, creating a “woolly” or “cottony” appearance to the individual spikes [Fig. ]
Perianth absent or present, when present not composed of greatly elongated capillary bristles, mostly contained within the floral scales [Figs. , , ]

c2.text: Perianth bristles strongly bent, curled, and tangled; inflorescences with 50–500 spikes (in part)
Perianth bristles relatively straight, silky; inflorescences with 1–10 (–30) spikelets

c3.text: Perianth bristles numbering 10–25 per flower; spikelets solitary or 2–10 (–30) per inflorescence, 10–50 mm long in fruit, subtended by 1 or more foliaceous bracts or by 10–15 sterile, basal scales; principal leaf blades up to 45 cm long

Perianth bristles mostly 6 in each flower; spikelets solitary, 5.4–8 mm tall in fruit, subtended by a solitary involucral bract that resembles an enlarged, basal scale; leaf blades up to 1 cm long (in part)

c4.text: Carpellate flowers subtended by an enclosing, sac-like scale (i.e., a perigynium) [Figs. , , , ], the stigmas protruding through an orifice at the top; flowers unisexual, lacking perianth
Carpellate flowers subtended by flat or folded scales, never enclosed in a sac-like scale [Figs. , , ]; flowers bisexual or some unisexual (all unisexual in Scleria ), with or without perianth

c5.text: Spikes 1 per stem
Spikes usually 2 or more per stem

c6.text: Involucral bract solitary, erect, appearing to be a continuation of the stem, therefore, the inflorescence falsely appearing to emerge from the side of the stem; leaf blades flaccid, submerged or the tips floating (in part)
Involucral bracts (if present) not resembling a continuation of the stem, therefore, the inflorescence appearing terminal; leaf blades either not produced or firm

c7.text: Achenes crowned by a persistent tubercle or expanded style base, usually of different color and texture than body of achene [Figs. , , ]; leaf sheaths lacking blades
Achenes not crowned by a tubercle; at least the upper leaf sheaths blade-bearing (in part)

c8.text: Scales of spikes distichous (i.e., arranged in 2 ranks) [Fig. ]
Scales of spikes spirally arranged (i.e., arranged in 3 or more ranks)

c9.text: Inflorescence partly or wholly axillary; flowers with a perianth composed of bristles; style persistent on the achene as a slender beak; leaves borne on the stem
Inflorescence terminal; flowers lacking perianth; style deciduous from the achene; leaves basally disposed

c10.text: Spikelets with 3–30 alternate floral scales [Figs. , ]; inflorescence dense to open, commonly with branches (i.e., not all spikes sessile); achenes biconvex to trigonous in cross-section, when biconvex the edge of the achene fitting into a groove in the rachilla

Spikelets with 2 (rarely 3) subopposite floral scales, the basal scale subtending a bisexual flower, the apical scale subtending a staminate flower; inflorescence densely capitate, with sessile spikes; achenes biconvex, the edge not fitting into a groove in the rachilla

c11.text: Flowers all unisexual; achenes white, gray, or gray-brown, with a hardened disk at the base (i.e., a hypogynium; the hypogynium vestigial in S. verticillata )
Flowers bisexual or some unisexual; achenes mostly gray-brown or pale brown to dark brown or black, without a hypogynium

c12.text: Principal involucral bract solitary, erect, appearing to be a continuation of the stem, therefore, the inflorescence falsely appearing to emerge from the side of the stem
Principal involucral bract erect to spreading, flat, folded, or setaceous, accompanied by additional bracts, not seeming a continuation of the stem, the inflorescence appearing terminal

c13.text: Achenes 0.5–0.7 mm long; spikelets 1–3 (–5) mm long; perianth consisting of a single, diminutive scale; floral scales 0.5–1 mm long
Achenes 1.3–4 mm long; spikelets 5–15 mm long; perianth consisting of bristles [Fig. ], these sometimes caducous; floral scales 2–6 mm long (in part)

c14.text: Achenes with an evident, apical tubercle that covers much or all of the achene summit, the tubercle clearly differentiated from the achene body by color and/or texture [Figs. , , ]
Achenes without tubercles or with small, relatively inconspicuous style bases [Figs. , ]

c15.text: Perianth dimorphic––an outer set of 3 retrorse-barbellate bristles and an inner set of 3 stipitate blades terminating in acuminate or awned apices [Fig. ]; leaf sheaths pubescent
Perianth monomorphic, of smooth to retrorse-barbellate bristles, or absent [Fig. ]; leaf sheaths glabrous

c16.text: Plants annual, with soft stem bases and fibrous roots, 5–30 cm tall
Plants perennial, with hardened stem bases and rhizomes, 30–200 cm tall

c17.text: Stems capillary; leaves up to 0.5 mm wide, with two lateral tufts of hairs at the junction of the blade and sheath; style base persistent in fruit and forming a tiny tubercle
Stems flat; larger leaves 1–3 mm wide, none with two lateral tufts, but with a ligule of short hairs; style base not persistent in fruit

c18.text: Perianth absent; achenes terete in cross-section; each spike with 1–3 empty, basal scales and an apical, bisexual flower, the remaining scales subtending staminate flowers
Perianth usually present, caducous in some species (rarely absent); achenes lenticular or biconvex to trigonous in cross-section; spikes comprised entirely of bisexual flowers

c19.text: Scales pubescent on the abaxial surface; rhizomes with tuberous thickenings; spikes (7–) 10–40 mm long; achenes 2.3–5.5 mm long; leaves without ligules
Scales glabrous on the abaxial surface; rhizomes without tubers; spikes 2–12 mm long; achenes 0.6–1.6 mm long; leaves with ligules (in part)

c1.text: This genus contains exactly one species.
Androecium composed of 6 stamens; gynoecium with a single whorl of carpels on a small, flat receptacle; inflorescence a panicle
Androecium composed of 7–40 stamens; gynoecium with several whorls of carpels on a convex receptacle, forming a subglobose cluster; inflorescence usually a raceme or an umbel

c2.text: Roots not septate; flowers all bisexual; achenes longitudinally ribbed; inflorescence usually an umbel (i.e., with a single whorl of pedicels)

Roots septate; at least the lower flowers of the inflorescence unisexual; achenes not longitudinally ribbed, but sometimes with lateral wings; inflorescence usually a raceme, with (1–) 2–10 whorls of pedicels

c1.text: This genus contains exactly one species.
Leaves usually equaling the height of the flowering stem, arching outward from the sheath [Fig. ], 0.5–1 mm wide; racemes 2–5 (–7) cm tall
Leaves usually shorter than the flowering stem, erect, 0.8–1.4 mm wide; racemes 6–45 cm tall

c2.text: Flowers with 6 carpels and 6 stigmas; mature schizocarps 1.5–2 mm wide, ca. 2 times as long as wide, the cluster of 6 mericarps on a slender, non-wing-angled axis; ligule apically 2-lobed
Flowers with 3 carpels and 3 stigmas; mature schizocarps 0.8–1.2 mm wide, ca. 5–7 times as long as wide, the cluster of 3 mericarps on a triquetrous axis; ligule not lobed

c1.text: This genus contains exactly one species.

Spikes spherical, most or all of carpellate ones subtended by prominent, leafy bracts [Figs. , ]; fruit an achene with a persistent stigma beak; leaves flaccid to firm, parallel-veined and checkered with rectangular areoles
Spikes cylindric, the carpellate ones without leafy bracts; fruit a wind-dispersed follicle; leaves firm, parallel-veined
Leaves opposite; flowers without a perianth; androecium with 1 stamen; gynoecium composed of a single, unilocular, unicarpellate ovary; fruit an achene

Leaves whorled (at least in part) or all basal; flowers with a perianth composed of 3 sepals and 3 petals; androecium with usually 2 or 9 stamens; gynoecium composed of 3–6 carpels; fruit usually ± capsule-like or berry-like

c2.text: Leaves differentiated into blades and petioles, the blades broad-ovate to cordate-orbicular, floating on the surface or becoming emergent in dense vegetation, with evidently non-parallel primary lateral veins [Fig. ]
Leaves not differentiated into blades and petioles, the linear to narrow-ovate blades submersed and with ± parallel veins [Figs. , ]

c3.text: Primary lateral veins of leaf blade forming a 75- to 90-degree (or greater) angle with the midvein [Fig. ]; filaments distinct most of their length; petals broad-obovate, 1.5 times or more or long as the sepals; anthers oval in outline; stipules 2, distinct from the petiole; seeds without blunt, cylindrical hairs

Primary lateral veins of leaf blade forming a 30- to 80-degree angle with the midvein; filaments connate more than their length into a column; petals linear to narrow-oblong, up to 1.5 times as long as the sepals; anthers linear in outline; stipule 1, basally connate to the petiole; seeds covered with blunt, cylindrical hairs

c4.text: Leaves all basal, 10–110 cm long, with a prominent, broad, central lacunar band [Fig. ]; staminate flowers with 2 stamens
Leaves borne on an elongate stem, mostly in whorls of 3–8, 0.4–4 cm long, without a prominent, central lacunar band; staminate flowers with 3–9 stamens

c5.text: Leaves with prickles on the abaxial midrib; intravaginal squamules (i.e., small, stipule-like scales in the leaf axils) fringed with orange-brown hairs; staminate flowers with 3 stamens
Leaves without prickles; intravaginal squamules entire or fringed with clear hairs; staminate flowers with 7–9 stamens

c6.text: Leaves numbering 2–4 per node, usually in whorls of 3 [Fig. ]; petals inconspicuous, up to 4.5 mm long, scarcely, if at all, longer than the sepals
Leaves numbering 4–8 per node, usually in whorls of 5 or more; petals more showy, 9–11 mm long, much longer than the sepals

c1.text: This genus contains exactly one species.

Secondary veins of dried leaf blades up to ca. 0.5 times the width of the midvein (i.e., leaves with 1 prominent midvein and numerous finer, secondary veins); fruits not produced; sympodial leaf often as tall as or shorter than the vegetative leaves; vegetative leaves (5–) 10–20 mm wide, often crisped or undulate; flowers 3–4 mm long

One or more of the secondary veins of dried leaf blades ca. 0.75–1 times as wide as the midvein (i.e., leaves with 2–6 prominent veins as well as numerous finer, secondary veins); fruit produced, an obpyramidal berry; sympodial leaf usually as tall as or taller than vegetative leaves; vegetative leaves 3–10 (–12) mm wide, not crisped, entire; flowers 2–3 mm long

Inflorescence subglobose, pale gray to white, 4–5 (–10) mm wide; bractlets evidently pubescent with clavate hairs; flowering scape with (4–) 5–7 ridges; each rosette of leaves producing usually a single flowering scape; plants of fresh water habitats

Inflorescence hemispherical, gray to light yellow-brown, 3–4 mm wide; bractlets sparsely pubescent with clavate hairs; flowering scape with 4 or 5 ridges; each rosette of leaves producing 1–4 flowering scapes; plants of tidal shores
Labellum deeply concave to saccate (at least in the basal portion), forming a small to very evident pouch [Fig. ]
Labellum neither inflated nor saccate, not forming a pouch [Figs. , , ]

c2.text: Labellum saccate in only the basal portion, 1.8–12 mm long; inflorescence a spike or raceme, with 5–72 flowers [Fig. ]
Labellum saccate ± throughout, 10–67 mm long; inflorescence a solitary flower or a spike-like raceme with 2 or 3 (–4) flowers

c3.text: Principal leaves all basal, usually white-striped or white-reticulated [Fig. ]; labellum white to white-green
Principal leaves borne on the stem, alternate, without white markings; labellum purple to purple-brown with pink near the apex or dark red

c4.text: Labellum with 2 apical horns and a prominent fringe of yellow bristles; plants with 1 leaf; flowers with 1 fertile anther; stem arising from a corm
Labellum without a pair of apical horns, lacking evident yellow bristles [Figs. , ]; plants with 2 or more leaves; flowers with 2 fertile anthers; stem arising from a short to elongate rhizome

c5.text: Labellum basally prolonged into a hollow spur (the spur short and saccate in Coeloglossum ) [Figs. , ]
Labellum lacking a spur (flowers with a small, inconspicuous, adnate spur in Corallorhiza formed by the 2 lateral sepals) [Figs. , , ]

c6.text: Flowers bilaterally asymmetrical (i.e., appearing lopsided); leaf single, abaxially purple, produced in autumn, withering by early spring, therefore, the flowering plants without well-formed leaves
Flowers bilaterally symmetrical; leaves 2 or more, less commonly single, abaxially green, produced in spring and present during flowering

c7.text: Labellum white with magenta spots, 3-lobed, the middle lobe notched at the apex; leaf single, basal
Labellum not spotted, variously shaped but never 3-lobed with a notched middle lobe; leaves 1–several, basal or arranged on a stem

c8.text: Stems conspicuously angled; labellum unlobed, typically white and strongly contrasting in color from the pink-magenta sepals and lateral petals (rarely all the perianth of similar color); viscidia enclosed in a single, 2-lobed bursicle

Stems terete; labellum unlobed, lobed, or fringed, ± similar in color to the remainder of the perianth (those Platanthera with 2 basal leaves usually have the sepals more strongly tinged with green than the petals); viscidia free, not enclosed in a bursicle

c9.text: Labellum 3-lobed, the middle lobe much shorter than the lateral 2 [Fig. ]; viscidia covered by membranes; orifice of spur covered by a membrane with a small opening; floral bracts conspicuous, usually evidently exceeding the flowers

Labellum variously shaped but never 3-lobed with a very reduced middle lobe [Figs. , , ]; viscidia not covered by membranes; orifice of spur open; floral bracts inconspicuous to (rarely) shortly exceeding the flowers

c10.text: Labellum simple, sometimes with apical teeth or a marginal fringe, but without 3 evident lobes (in part)
Labellum clearly lobed into 3 segments

c11.text: Labellum 5–25 mm long, fringed on the margin [Fig. ]; leaf blades entire (in part)
Labellum 3.5–5 mm long, with entire lobes; leaf blades denticulate

c12.text: Flowers not resupinate, the labellum the uppermost petal; labellum with a conspicuous brush of yellow-tipped hairs; leaves articulated, this appearing as a thin, transverse line near the base of the leaf
Flowers resupinate, the labellum the lowest petal; labellum with or without hairs or ornamentation of some type; leaves not articulated

c13.text: Leaves whorled at the summit of the stem
Leaves or scales alternate or opposite, borne at base of plant and/or distributed along the stem

c14.text: Flowers subtended by foliaceous, ovate bracts [Fig. ]; labellum ornamented with 3 parallel, green, papillose ridges [Fig. ]
Flowers subtended by rather inconspicuous, usually scale-like bracts; labellum ornamented or not, never with 3 parallel, green ridges

c15.text: Flowers large, the labellum (12–) 17–35 mm long; flowers usually solitary
Flowers smaller, the labellum 1.3–12 mm long; flowers 3–180 per inflorescence

c16.text: Leaves flat, numbering 1–3 on the stem, present at anthesis, the largest 7–25 (–32) mm wide; sepals and lateral petals distinct, the outer spreading
Leaves obscurely plicate, solitary on the stem, not fully formed at anthesis, 2–4 (–12) mm wide; sepals and lateral petals connate at the base, the outer erect

c17.text: Principal leaves arranged in a single, opposite pair on the stem; labellum 2-lobed due to a conspicuous apical notch [Figs. , ]

Principal leaves 1–several, borne at base of plant and/or distributed along the stem; labellum entire or 3-lobed, without a single apical notch (with a prominent notch in Malaxis , but then with a small lobe at the base of the central notch) [Figs. , ]

c18.text: Flowers predominantly white or cream (except for a yellow or green central area on the labellum in some species), sometimes tinged with yellow or green; leaves and stem bracts above them numbering 5 or more; labellum with a pair of basal callosities
Flowers not predominantly white or cream, variously colored and/or spotted; leaves and stem bracts (when present), numbering 4 or fewer; labellum without a pair of basal callosities

c19.text: Plants leafless at flowering time, with sheathing bracts only, arising from coral-like rhizomes; plants without chlorophyll, the stems brown to purple, or yellow-green in one species

Plants with leaves at flowering time ( Aplectrum sometimes leafless at flowering, but the withered remnant usually present at stem base), arising from corms; plants chlorophyllous, the leaves and stems ± green at anthesis

c20.text: Leaf solitary, evidently plicate, produced at distal end of corm in late season and persistent through the winter, usually withering by flowering; labellum white with magenta spots (rarely all white-yellow); capsules pendent

Leaf solitary or paired, not or only obscurely plicate, produced in spring, present during flowering, withering before winter; labellum green to yellow-green or brown-purple to pale purple, without spots; capsules spreading to erect

c21.text: Plants with 2 leaves, in a pair near the base of the stem; labellum 4–12 mm long; capsules 9–13 mm long
Plants with a single leaf (rarely 2 and then not paired), borne on the stem; labellum 1.3–2.3 mm long; capsules mostly 5–8 mm long

c1.text: Leaves with 3–5 lobes, with bulbils in the axils, usually opposite in the distal portion of the stem; staminate inflorescences in fascicles of (1–) 3–5 in the axils of leaves; plants tuberous

Leaves without lobes, the margin entire to undulate, without bulbils in the axils, alternate in the distal portion of the stem; staminate inflorescences solitary in the axils of leaves; plants rhizomatous
This genus contains exactly one species.

Styles broad, petaloid, with paired crests at the apex [Fig. ]; anthers concealed, appressed to abaxial surface of style branches; sepals, petals, stamens, and carpels adnate at the base forming a floral tube that surmounts the ovary (in part)
Styles not petaloid, without crests; anthers visible, not appressed to style branches; sepals, petals, stamens and carpels not adnate near base (though Crocus with basally connate tepals)

c2.text: Plants without aerial stems; fruit borne at or even below the ground level; tepals with an elongate, basally connate portion
Plants with evident, above-ground stems; fruit borne well above ground level; tepals distinct or with a very short (i.e., discernable only with close observation) basally connate portion

c3.text: Leaf blades 10–20 mm wide; tepals light orange to red (rarely yellow); filaments distinct (in part)
Leaf blades 0.8–5 mm wide; tepals white to blue or blue-violet; filaments basally connate

c1.text: This genus contains exactly one species.
Perianth with a conspicuous cup-like to tubular corona; tepals 15–35 mm long
Perianth without a corona; tepals 7–22 (–25) mm long

c2.text: Inflorescence with 2–7 flowers; tepals of ± equal length; scape hollow
Inflorescence with 1 flower; tepals distinctly unequal; scape solid

c1.text: Keel of lateral sepals firm, ciliate except at the red-fimbriate tip; leaves twisted; base of plant abruptly bulbous
Keel of lateral sepals weak, scarious, entire to lacerate; leaves plane; base of plant not abruptly bulbous

c2.text: Sheaths minutely papillose; leaves 0.8–2 (–3) mm wide; floral scales 3–4 (–4.5) mm long, erose or minutely fimbriate along the margins, lacking a well-defined, green central region; lateral sepals red at apex, the keel entire or lacerate near the apex
Sheaths smooth; leaves 2–15 mm wide; floral scales (4–) 5–8 mm long, entire, with a well-defined, green central area [Fig. ]; lateral sepals not red at apex, the keel lacerate much of its length

c3.text: Tips of lateral sepals exserted beyond floral scales; seeds (0.6–) 0.7 (–0.8) mm long; spikes 10–20 (–25) mm tall, the apex usually rounded
Tips of lateral sepals concealed by floral scales [Fig. ]; seeds 0.5 mm long; spikes 5–15 mm tall, the apex usually acute

c1.text: Corolla weakly zygomorphic—one of the petals usually smaller than the other 2; inflorescence subtended by a folded spathe; flowers with 3 fertile stamens and usually 3 sterile stamens with cruciform anthers
Corolla actinomorphic; inflorescence subtended by leaves; flowers with 6 fertile stamens
Sepals and petals clearly different, the sepals green; leaves borne in a single whorl at the summit of the stem, pinnately veined [Fig. ]; fruit a berry
Sepals and petals similar [Fig. ], the sepals green or petaloid; leaves ± all basal or alternate, parallel veined; fruit a capsule

c2.text: Ovary partly inferior; anthers mesifixed; seeds twisted and flattened at the ends, unwinged; plants arising from bulbs, lacking rhizomes
Ovary superior; anthers basifixed; seeds variously shaped but with marginal angles, wings, or with a wing-like aril; plants with rhizomes (bulbs sometimes also present)

c3.text: Leaf blades narrow-linear, 20–70 ×0.5–3 cm; bulbs 30–80 mm long
Leaf blades narrow-oblanceolate or spatulate to elliptic or ovate, 5–55 ×1–20 cm; bulbs absent or present and 6–17 mm long

c4.text: Tepals 2–4 mm long, white in staminate flowers, green-white in carpellate flowers (fading or drying yellow), lacking basal nectaries; inflorescence with an unbrached axis, ebracteate; capsule dehiscence loculicidal; plants dioecious

Tepals 5–12 mm long, green to yellow-green or green-white to light yellow, with 1 or 2 nectary glands at base; inflorescence branched, with bracts; capsule dehiscence septicidal; plants synoecious or polygamous

c1.text: Inflorescence densely and many flowered, commonly with more than 50 flowers; perianth blue-purple (rarely white), the upper middle lobe with 2 contiguous, yellow spots; fruit achene-like, with a single seed
Inflorescence open to dense, with 2–15 flowers; perianth white, yellow, or blue, with or without spots, but never with 2 yellow spots; fruit a capsule, with 7–30 seeds

c2.text: Petioles at least slightly inflated; perianth blue, the lobes 16–37 mm long; flowers with 6 stamens; plants typically free-floating
Petioles absent or not inflated; perianth white or yellow, the lobes 3–11 mm long; flowers with 3 stamens; plants rooted in substrate

c1.text: Plants vines (i.e., stems herbaceous), without prickles [Fig. ]; ovules 2 (rarely 1) per locule
Plants lianas (i.e., stems woody), with prickles, especially toward the base; ovule 1 per locule

c2.text: Leaf blades glaucous on the abaxial surface; anthers longer than filaments
Leaf blades not glaucous; anthers equal to or shorter than filaments

c3.text: Prickles thin, bristly, nearly black at maturity; peduncle 1.5–6.5 cm long; berry not glaucous
Prickles stout, green with red to dark brown tips at maturity; peduncle 0.5–1.5 cm long; berry glaucous

c1.text: This genus contains exactly one species.

Leaf blades lanceolate to broad-lanceolate, 10–17 × (3–) 5–7.5 cm, with 5 or 6 pairs of lateral veins; flowers gradually expanding apically, with pale purple tepals; anthers purple; scape mostly 40–50 cm tall

Leaf blades ovate to cordate-ovate, 20–30 × (10–) 15–20 cm, with 7–9 pairs of lateral veins; flowers abruptly expanding apically, with purple-blue tepals; anthers spotted with purple; scape mostly 80-95 cm tall
Flowers red-orange, not fragrant; tepals reticulate-veined; capsules rarely maturing
Flowers yellow, fragrant; tepals parallel-veined; capsules maturing (i.e., containing seeds)
Tepals connate in the lower portion, forming an elongate basal tube, pink to purple or white (rarely yellow); scape very short (plants appearing stemless); ovary subterranean; plants from a corm
Tepals distinct, yellow; stem evident, bearing leaves and flowers [Fig. ]; ovary elevated well above the ground on an aerial stem; plants from rhizomes
Leaves all basal (though not apparent due to sheathing nature of petioles); inflorescence a secund raceme of white flowers with drooping pedicels subtended by scarious bracts 4–10 mm long
Leaves borne on a stem [Fig. ]; inflorescence not combining above features

c2.text: Tepals evidently connate and forming a tube, 10–22 mm long; inflorescence of axillary flowers or 1- to 10 (–15)-flowered racemes; berry dark blue to black; rhizome thick and knotty, mostly 10–30 mm thick [Fig. ]
Tepals distinct, 1.5–6 mm long; inflorescence a terminal raceme or panicle; berry initially, or ultimately becoming, red; rhizome mainly more slender, 1–14 mm thick

c1.text: This genus contains exactly one species.
Tepals evidently connate for some distance [Fig. ]; stamens epipetalous
Tepals essentially distinct (i.e., connate for less than their total length) [Fig. ]; stamens free or inserted near the base of the tepals

c2.text: Perianth urceolate to cylindric [Fig. ]; tepals connate for most of their length; leaf blades 2–8 mm wide; racemes with usually 12–20 flowers, dense [Fig. ], with sterile flowers near the apex that often show slightly reduced size and somewhat paler color
Perianth open-campanulate; tepals 15–25 mm long, connate for less than their length; leaf blades 10–20 mm wide; racemes with usually 4–10 flowers, open, without apical sterile flowers

c3.text: Tepals white, each with a green abaxial stripe, 15–30 mm long; stamens dimorphic as to length, with flat filaments; leaves mostly 20–60 cm long, with a white adaxial stripe
Tepals blue (rarely white), 12–16 mm long; stamens monomorphic, the filaments not conspicuously flattened; leaves mostly 10–15 cm long, lacking a white stripe

c1.text: This genus contains exactly one species.
This genus contains exactly one species.
Tepals white and spotted with red or purple on the adaxial surface, the outer 3 prominently saccate at the base; each style apically bifid, maculate
Tepals variously colored, but not white with dark spots, not prominently saccate; styles neither bifid near apex nor spotted

c2.text: Tepals green-yellow, green-white, or pink (red-purple to purple in the rare hybrid Streptopus × ‌oreopolus ), 0.6–1.6 cm long; fruit a berry; stems arising from rhizomes (the rhizomes tuberous in Medeola )
Tepals yellow, orange, red or white, (1.3–) 1.5–10 cm long; fruit a capsule; stems arising from bulbs or corms

c3.text: Styles 3, distinct; tepals recurved from near the base; leaves borne on an aerial stem in 1 or 2 whorls
Style 1, the stigma obscurely lobed to 3-parted; tepals spreading or recurving from near the middle; leaves all basal or alternate

c4.text: Flowers in an umbel at the summit of a scape, with green-yellow tepals; leaves all basal; fruit a blue berry
Flowers solitary or paired in the axils of foliage leaves, with green-white, pink, or red-purple to purple tepals; leaves borne alternately on an aerial stem; fruit a red berry

c5.text: Leaves appearing all basal (actually borne on a slender, mainly subterranean stem), usually mottled with lighter markings; capsules 12–15 mm tall (up to 22 mm tall in the naturalized E. albidum ); spring ephemerals, the above-ground portions of the plant usually senescing by July

Leaves borne on the stem ( Gagea with both basal and stem leaves), not mottled; capsules 15–77 mm tall (shorter in Gagea , but that species usually with 3–5 flowers per inflorescence); plants persisting through the summer in typical years

c6.text: Anthers mesifixed; tepals with basal nectaries; stems with usually more than 5 leaves, whorled (alternate in 1 species)
Anthers basifixed; tepals without basal nectaries; stems with 2–5 alternate leaves or 2 opposite leaves

c7.text: Stigmas sessile; stems with 2–5 alternate leaves; tepals 20–82 mm long
Stigmas elevated on a style; stems with 2 opposite leaves; tepals 13–17 mm long

c1.text: This genus contains exactly one species.
This genus contains exactly one species.
Leaves alternate, pinnately compound; fruit a 3-locular or partially 3-locular, bladdery-inflated capsule
Leaves opposite, simple [Figs. , ], palmately compound, or pinnately compound in 1 species; fruit a samara-like schizocarp or a 1- to 3-locular, non-inflated capsule

c2.text: Vines climbing by axillary tendrils; leaves ternately or biternately compound; petals white to red
Woody plants without tendrils; leaves pinnately compound with 7–15 leaflets; petals yellow

c3.text: Leaves simple or pinnately compound; perianth actinomorphic; fruit a samara-like schizocarp, without prickles
Leaves palmately compound; perianth zygomorphic; fruit a capsule, commonly with small prickles

c1.text: Leaves whorled, the blades simple, entire or with short lobes; trees with upright stems; corolla largely white or yellow
Leaves opposite, the blades pinnately divided into 5–13 serrate leaflets; lianas with trailing or climbing stems; corolla largely red or orange
Plants woody, with yellow inner bark; fruit a sparsely pubescent follicle
Plants herbaceous; fruit an achene, berry, or glabrous follicle

c2.text: Fruit an achene [Figs. , , ]; ovaries with 1 ovule
Fruit a follicle, capsule, or berry [Fig. ]; ovaries with 2 or more ovules

c3.text: Calyx composed of 5 spurred sepals; receptacle continuing to elongate through and after anthesis, the cluster of achenes becoming slender-conical and 16–50 ×1–3 mm
Calyx composed of 4–20 sepals that are not spurred; receptacle not continuing to elongate after anthesis, the cluster of achenes relatively broader compared with length

c4.text: Petals present, yellow or both white and yellow; sepals (3–) 5, sepaloid
Petals absent or inconspicuous; sepals 4–20, petaloid or sepaloid in some species of Thalictrum

c5.text: Flowers with 5 sepals [Fig. ]; seeds both beaked (though the beak sometimes tiny) and lacking a prominent, corky appendage distal to the seed [Fig. ]
Flowers with 3 (–4) sepals; achenes either beakless or with a prominent, corky appendage distal to the seed

c6.text: Flowers with 5–8 petals; leaf blades prominently lobed with deep sinuses [Fig. ]; roots all slender; achenes with both a terminal beak and a prominent, corky appendage prolonged distal to the seed
Flowers with 7–11 petals; leaf blades entire to crenate; some roots tuberous-thickened; achenes lacking both a terminal beak and a corky appendage distal to the seed

c7.text: Plants trailing or climbing vines; sepals valvate in bud; style plumose [Fig. ]; stem leaves opposite

Plants upright, not vining; sepals imbricate in bud; style not plumose; stem leaves alternate or lacking (note: the opposite or whorled leaves found on the stems of some Thalictrum and Anemone are involucral leaves associated with the inflorescence)

c8.text: Stem leaves alternate; sepals 1.5–5 mm long, often inconspicuous and sometimes caducous (in part)

Stem leaves lacking, but appearing opposite or whorled in most species (these leaves actually involucral bracts associated with the inflorescence); sepals 5–25 mm long, conspicuous, usually persisting through anthesis

c9.text: Leaf blades palmately lobed or palmately compound (subternately divided in A. multifida ); style present; achenes lacking evident veins on lateral surfaces
Leaf blades pinnately compound in ternate fashion [Fig. ]; style absent (i.e., the stigma sessile); achenes with evident veins or ribs on lateral surfaces (in part)

c10.text: Flowers zygomorphic
Flowers actinomorphic

c11.text: Upper sepal arched or hooded; petals not spurred
Upper sepal neither arched nor hooded, prolonged into a spur; upper petal or all the petals spurred

c12.text: Flowers with 4 distinct petals and 3 carpels; ultimate lobes of leaf blades 5–25 mm wide; plants perennial, from fasciculate roots
Flowers with 2 connate petals and 1 carpel; ultimate lobes of leaf blades narrower than 1.5 mm; plants annual, from a slender taproot

c13.text: Leaf blades pinnately dissected into filiform segments; gynoecium of 5–10 connate carpels; fruit a capsule
Leaf blades toothed to divided, but the divisions not threadlike; gynoecium of 1–15 distinct carpels; fruit a follicle or berry

c14.text: Leaf blades palmately lobed [Fig. ]; perianth consisting of only 3 petaloid, caducous sepals; inflorescence a solitary flower borne at the top of a leafy stem [Fig. ]; mature fruit a red berry

Leaf blades simple or compound, but not palmately lobed; perianth either with both sepals and petals present or with 4–9 petaloid sepals; inflorescence either with 2 or more flowers or a solitary flower borne on a scape (solitary and terminal in Trollius and also rarely in Caltha ); mature fruit a follicle or berry (a red berry in some Actaea )

c15.text: Leaf blades not pinnately compound, either simple or palmately divided; calyx composed of 5–9 petaloid, pale yellow to bright yellow or orange-yellow sepals
Leaf blades pinnately compound, often in ternate fashion; perianth not yellow, the calyx with 5 or fewer sepals

c16.text: Leaf blades palmately divided to the base; flowers with 10–15 (–25) yellow staminodes 3–6 mm long; inflorescence with a solitary, terminal flower
Leaf blades simple; flowers lacking staminodes; inflorescence terminal or both terminal and axillary, with 1–7 flowers

c17.text: Perianth inconspicuous and often partly or entirely caducous, the sepals 2.5–4 (–6) mm long; inflorescence a raceme or panicle [Fig. ]; fruit a berry or a follicle in A. racemosa [Fig. ]; ultimate segments of leaf blades sharply cleft and toothed

Perianth conspicous, not caducous, the petaloid sepals (4–) 5–25 mm long; inflorescence a solitary flower or a 1- to 10-flowered cyme; fruit a follicle; ultimate segments of leaves crenately toothed or crenately lobed

c18.text: Sepals red or blue to people (rarely white); petals conspicuous, prolonged into long spurs [Fig. ], 15–31 mm long including the spur; leaves borne on an aerial, leafy stem, the blades 2- or 3-times compound
Sepals white; petals represented by small, clavate-spatulate staminodia, without spurs, 2.5–3 mm long; leaves all basal, the blades once-compound

c1.text: Flowers weakly zygomorphic; petals 20–25 mm long; stamens declined and upwardly curved near apex
Flowers actinomorphic; petals up to 10 mm long; stamens ± straight

c2.text: Herbaceous plants with bipinnatifid leaves; fruit a 4- or 5-lobed capsule; flowers all bisexual, with yellow petals 8–10 mm long

Shrubs or trees with pinnately compound leaves; fruit a samara, drupe, or follicle; some or all of the flowers on a given plant unisexual (the unisexual flowers in Ptelea by imperfect or abortive stamens), with green-white, yellow-white, or yellow-green petals up to 7 mm long

c3.text: Leaves with 3 leaflets; fruit a ± orbicular samara; plants polygamous (i.e., some flowers bisexual, others unisexual, in the latter case the carpellate flowers functionally unisexual due to imperfect or abortive stamens)
Leaves with 5–13 leaflets; fruit a drupe or fleshy follicle; plants dioecious (i.e., all the flowers unisexual)

c4.text: Leaves opposite; branches unarmed; fruit a drupe
Leaves alternate; branches armed with prickles; fruit a fleshy follicle

c1.text: Leaf blades pinnately compound with 5–13 (–15) leaflets; corolla absent; fruit a samara
Leaf blades simple or sometimes pinnately compound with 3 leaflets in Forsythia ; corolla present and conspicuous; fruit a drupe or capsule

c2.text: Flowers precocious, with yellow corollas; leaf blades toothed; branchlets with hollow or chambered pith
Flowers not appearing well in advance of leaf emergence, with white or light blue-purple corollas (infrequently red-blue or red-purple); leaf blades entire; branchlets with solid pith

c3.text: Corolla not salverform, with elongate lobes that are much longer than the basal, connate portion
Corolla salverform, the lobes not conspicuously longer than the basal, connate, tubular portion

c4.text: Fruit a capsule; anthers included within the connate, tubular portion of the corolla (exserted in S. reticulata ); branchlets relatively stout, usually thicker than 2 mm
Fruit a drupe; anthers shortly exserted from the tubular, connate portion of the corolla [Figs. , ]; branchlets slender, usually thinner than 2 mm

c1.text: Leaf blades pinnately divided into 3–11 leaflets; drupe with 3–5 pyrenes; terminal bud absent
Leaf blades simple, lobed or unlobed [Figs. , ]; drupe with a single seed; terminal bud present
Leaves opposite
Leaves alternate or all basal

c2.text: Stems appearing jointed; leaves connate into a sheath that surrounds the stem, with scarcely projecting distinct tips [Fig. ]; flowers in groups of 3, sunken into the fleshy stem [Figs. , ]
Stems not appearing jointed; leaves neither connate nor scale-like; flowers not arranged in groups of 3, not sunken into the stem

c3.text: Flowers unisexual; stems and inflorescence glabrous or farinose, but not pubescent; leaves glabrous or farinose, but not pubescent; filaments distinct; fruits concealed by a pair of accrescent bracteoles [Fig. ]; leaf blades entire or, more commonly, toothed or with a pair of lobes near the base [Fig. ] (in part)

Flowers bisexual; stems sparsely to densely villous or villous-tomentose; leaves pubescent on one or both surfaces (at least on the abaxial midrib); filaments connate (at least at the base); fruits not concealed by a pair of accrescent bracteoles (though often concealed by the persistent perianth); leaf blades entire

c4.text: Spikes 20–28 mm in diameter, white, yellow, red, or purple, showy; style terminated by 2 subulate or filiform stigmas; plants annual, from fibrous roots

Spikes 6–8 mm in diameter, mainly white or gray to white-green or gray-green, not especially showy; styles terminated by a single capitate stigma or the stigma minutely 2-lobed; plants annual with a taproot or perennial

c5.text: Filaments monadelphous, the connate tube suggesting a gamopetalous corolla; leaf blades linear to narrow-lanceolate; rachis of inflorescence moderately to densely villous-tomentose; calyx segments ± monomorphic; plants annual

Filaments connate only at the very base; leaf blades obovate to orbicular; rachis of inflorescence glabrous or sparsely pubescent; calyx segments polymorphic—the outer 2 longest and spine-tipped, the next inner shorter and narrower, the inner 2 shortest and with hairs along the abaxial keel; plants perennial

c6.text: Sepals usually dry and scarious; filaments distinct or, more commonly, connate near the base; ovary with 3 stigmas (often only 2 in A. palmeri ) [Fig. ]
Sepals membranaceous to herbaceous (hyaline in Axyris ); filaments distinct; ovary with 2 (–5) stigmas

c7.text: Flowers unisexual; utricle 1-seeded; inflorescence not fasciated
Flowers bisexual; utricle 6- to 10-seeded; inflorescence fasciated

c8.text: Leaves stellate-pubescent on the abaxial surface; sepals hyaline; fruit obovate in outline, with a bilobed wing at the apex
Leaves glabrous, farinose, or pubescent, but not stellate-pubescent; sepals usually pigmented; fruit orbicular to obovate or oblong in outline, without a bilobed wing at the apex

c9.text: Plants monoecious or dioecious (i.e., flowers unisexual); fruit or seed concealed by a pair of accrescent bracteoles [Fig. ]

Plants synoecious (i.e., with bisexual flowers only) or sometimes polygamous (i.e., with bisexual and unisexual flowers); fruit visible or concealed by a persistent calyx, the bracteoles not accrescent

c10.text: Stigmas 2; herbage glabrous or sparsely to densely farinose (in part)
Stigmas 4 or 5; herbage glabrous

c11.text: Leaf blades linear to narrow-lanceolate or oblanceolate in outline, entire, sessile or subsessile (with obscure petioles up to 3 mm long in Kochia ) [Fig. ]

Leaf blades oblong or lanceolate to ovate or triangular, entire, toothed, or lobed, at least the lower ones petioled (caution: the lower leaves in some Chenopodium and often all the leaves in Cycloloma deciduous by fruiting) [Fig. ]

c12.text: Leaves tipped with spines (especially those from the upper portion of the stem)
Leaves not tipped with spines, at most pointed

c13.text: Flowers with usually 2 styles and 5 stamens; fruits globose to ovoid, with a horizontally oriented seed
Flowers with usually 5 styles and 3 stamens; fruits compressed, with a vertically oriented seed

c14.text: Stems, leaves, and/or perianth villous or short-pilose with eglandular hairs
Plants glabrous or farinose or stipitate-glandular in Dysphania

c15.text: Fruiting sepals with a prominent, transverse wing on the abaxial surface
Fruiting sepals without a wing, with either conical tubercles or hooked spines on the abaxial surface [Fig. ]

c16.text: Leaves terete to planoconvex in cross-section; flowers borne in groups of 1–7, usually 3, in the axils of the leaves
Leaves flat, at least in the basal portion; flowers borne variously, but not consistently in groups of 3

c17.text: Plants glabrous or farinose, but not glandular (in part)
Plants with stipitate glands or subsessile glands (in part)

c18.text: Fruiting perianth with a continuous, transverse wing; inflorescence a diffusely branched panicle with solitary flowers at each node

Fruiting perianth lacking a horizontally oriented wing; inflorescence usually either a panicle with spike-like branches or of axillary clusters of flowers, the flowers occurring singly or in glomerules at each node

c19.text: Ovary semi-inferior; roots moderately to strongly swollen, dark red, yellow, or white
Ovary superior; roots not swollen, usually pale or brown

c20.text: Calyx composed of 1 sepal, not enclosing the fruit at maturity; androecium composed of 1 stamen
Calyx composed of 3–5 sepals, enclosing and often somewhat concealing the fruit at maturity; androecium composed of 1–5 stamens, commonly 5

c21.text: Plants glabrous or farinose, but not glandular (in part)
Plants with stipitate glands or subsessile glands (in part)

c1.text: Leaves dimorphic—submersed ones that are opposite and finely dissected and floating ones that are alternate, borne in a crowded rosette, and have rhombic blades borne on inflated petioles [Fig. ]; fruit indehiscent, caltrop-shaped, with 4 stout horns
Leaves monomorphic, neither dissected nor with inflated petioles [Figs. , , ]; fruit a capsule

c2.text: Corolla zygomorphic; hypanthium swollen or spurred near the base on one side; flowers with (6–) 11 or 12 (–14) stamens
Corolla actinomorphic; hypanthium neither asymmetrically swollen nor spurred; flowers with 4–10 stamens or commonly 12 in Lythrum salicaria

c3.text: Hypanthium cylindric to narrow-cupuliform, 2 or more times taller than wide, with 6 or 12 conspicuous veins; perianth (5–) 6 (–7)-merous; leaf blades sessile or subsessile (narrowed to the base in L. virgatum )

Hypanthium hemispheric to broad-cupuliform, ± as tall as wide, without evident veins or with 4–8 evident veins; perianth (3–) 4 or 5 (–7)-merous; leaf blades borne on short petioles or narrowly tapering to an ill-defined petiole

c4.text: Petals evident, 10–15 mm long, deciduous [Fig. ]; flowers with 8 or 10 stamens; intersepalar appendages linear, much narrower and longer than the sepals; leaf blades 50–150 mm long; plants perennial, with ± woody bases surrounded by loose, spongy tissue

Petals minute, 0.5–1 mm long, caducous [Fig. ]; flowers with (3–) 4 (–6) stamens; intersepalar appendages triangular, ± similar in size and shape to the sepals; leaf blades 10–30 (–50) mm long; plants annual

c1.text: Plants woody; inflorescence a densely flowered, spherical cluster [Fig. ]; corolla slender-funnelform
Plants herbaceous; inflorescence not a spherical cluster; corolla salverform, rotate, cupuliform, or funnelform

c2.text: Leaves 2 at each node (i.e., opposite) [Figs. , ]; fruit fleshy or dehiscent; corolla pubescent on the adaxial (i.e., inside) surface (glabrous in Houstonia caerulea )

Leaves 3–12 at a node (i.e., whorled; rarely only 2 leaves at some of the nodes in Galium ) [Figs. , ]; fruit dry, schizocarpic, consisting of 2 indehiscent, 1-seeded carpels [Figs. , ]; corolla glabrous (pubescent on the abaxial surface in Galium circaezans )

c3.text: Flowers united by their hypanthia [Fig. ]; fruit a berry; plants creeping, with evergreen leaves
Flowers separate, not united [Fig. ]; fruit a capsule or schizocarp; plants prostrate to erect, sometimes tufted, with deciduous leaves

c4.text: Fruit a schizocarp, separating into 2 mericarps; ovules solitary in each locule; flowers borne in the axils of leaves; stipules terminated by a fringe of erect bristles
Fruit a capsule; ovules 4 or more in each locule; flowers borne at the apex of the stem, either solitary or in cymes; stipules entire, without a fringe

c5.text: Sepals triangular; corolla blue or pink, funnelform; inflorescence subtended by an involucre composed of a whorl of basally connate leaves

Sepals obsolete; corolla white, green-white, yellow, yellow-green, green-purple, or purple, or blue-purple in Asperula , usually rotate; inflorescence not subtended by an involucre or subtended by one composed of distinct leaves

c6.text: Corolla 5-merous; fruit fleshy
Corolla 3- or 4-merous [Figs. , ]; fruit dry

c7.text: Corolla blue-purple, funnelform, with a prolonged, slender, basal, connate portion 4–5.5 mm long that is longer than the lobes; flowers with closely subtending, narrow bracteoles, borne on pedicels shorter than or as long as the ovary

Corolla various shades of white, yellow, or purple, rotate or cupuliform (funnelform in G. odoratum ), the basal, connate portion up to ca. 1.5 mm long, shorter than or as long as the lobes; flowers without closely subtending bracteoles, often borne on pedicels longer than the ovary [Figs. , ]

c1.text: Leaves alternate; thorns commonly present; flowers with 4 stamens; plants synoecious or polygamous (i.e., some of the flowers staminate, the others bisexual)
Leaves opposite; thorns absent; staminate flowers with 8 stamens; plants dioecious
Leaves opposite, with entire blades 0.5–1.5 cm long; flowers lacking staminodes
Leaves all basal, with toothed blades 2–10 cm long; flowers with 5 staminodes

c2.text: Flowers numerous, borne in a raceme; corolla 3–5 mm long; stamens monadelphous; anthers 1-locular
Flowers solitary, at the summit of a scape [Fig. ]; corolla 15–25 mm long; stamens distinct; anthers 2-locular

c1.text: Capitula composed entirely of bisexual ray flowers [Figs. , , ]; plants usually with a milky latex

Capitula composed entirely of disk flowers or both ray and disk flowers, the ray flowers, when present, restricted to the margin of the capitulum and unisexual or sterile [Figs. , , ]; plants commonly without a milky latex

c2.text: Capitula without marginal, zygomorphic flowers that bear a ray, all the flowers tubular and actinomorphic, with or without apical teeth or lobes [Figs. , , ]
Capitula with zygomorphic ray flowers near the periphery, the rays sometimes minute and inconspicuous in drying [Figs. , , ]

c3.text: Pappus composed of capillary bristles (at least in large part), each bristle smooth, barbellate, or plumose [Fig. ]
Pappus composed entirely of scales (each scale divided at the apex into many bristles in Dyssodia ), or awns, a short crown, or entirely absent [Fig. ]

c4.text: Rays of various colors, but not yellow or orange
Rays largely or entirely yellow or orange (sometimes yellow only at the base and white distally in Glebionis coronaria and Layia platyglossa ; the rays

c5.text: Pappus composed partly or entirely of capillary bristles (short scales may also be present; ray flowers sometimes lacking pappus) [Figs. , ]
Pappus composed entirely of scales (each scale divided at the apex into many bristles in Dyssodia ), or awns, or a crown, or completely absent

c1.text: This genus contains exactly one species.
Calyx with a small, but evident, tranverse ridge on the upper side, the upper lip deciduous in fruit [Fig. ]
Calyx without a protuberance on the upper side, persistent in fruit

c2.text: Corolla apparently composed of a lower lip only, the upper lip either very small or displaced and part of the lower lip [Figs. , ]
Corolla either clearly zygomorphic and with an evident upper and lower lip or nearly actinomorphic [Figs. , , ]

c3.text: Lower lip 5-lobed, the 2 small, lateral lobes representing the laterally displaced lobes of the upper lip; inflorescence elongate, raceme-like, 5–20 cm tall, leafy-bracted only at the base

Lower lip 3- or 4-lobed, the upper lip present, but very small; inflorescence either of verticillasters in the axils of foliage leaves or of flowers in leafy-bracted, spike-like inflorescences 4–8 cm tall
