c4.text: Flowers with only 2 stamens, the other 2 stamens absent or represented by small staminodes (caution: the pollen sacs are separated by a connective in Salvia , creating the appearance of 4 anthers in some species) [Figs. , ]
Flowers with 4 stamens [Figs. , ]

c5.text: Corolla yellow to pale yellow, the distal margin of the lower lip fringed [Fig. ]; inflorescence a terminal panicle

Corolla white, ochroleucous, pink, red to purple, or blue (yellow and spotted with purple in Mondarda punctata ), lacking a prominently fringed lower lip; inflorescence of verticillasters in axils of foliage or bracteal leaves, sometimes the verticillasters congested to form a dense cluster of flowers

c6.text: Calyx strongly zygomorphic; corolla blue to purple-blue (often pale blue to pale purple in Blephilia , which has red-purple to purple spots)
Calyx actinomorphic or nearly so; corolla white, ochroleucous, pink, or red to purple (often blue-purple in Monarda fistulosa )

c7.text: Verticillasters with pedicellate flowers in the axils of foliage leaves; corolla 3–4 mm long
Verticillasters with sessile or short-pedicellate flowers in the axils of reduced, bract-like leaves, sometimes congested and forming terminal clusters of flowers; corolla 8–30 mm long

c8.text: Inflorescence usually composed of 5–18 or more separate verticillasters of flowers; anthers attached to a narrow connective that is articulated to the filament, the upper end of the connective bearing a single pollen sac, the lower end of the connective either with a deformed pollen sac or without a pollen sac

Inflorescence composed of 1–5 closely crowded verticillasters of flowers, collectively forming dense, terminal clusters; anthers without a narrow connective, with 2 pollen-bearing sacs that are contiguous

c9.text: Corolla white, weakly zygomorphic, 1.8–4.4 mm long; flowers in dense but separate verticillasters in the axils of foliage leaves
Corolla only rarely white, strongly zygomorphic, 15–45 mm long; flowers in dense, crowded verticillasters at the tips of the stems and branches [Fig. ], sometimes also in dense, axillary clusters

c10.text: Basal, connate portion of the corolla (i.e., the tube) longer than and somewhat concealing the stamens
Basal, connate portion of the corolla shorter than the stamens, the stamens readily visible during anthesis [Figs. , ]

c11.text: Inflorescence terminal, spike-like, the flowers subtended by reduced, bract-like leaves and separated by conspicuously shortened internodes relative to the vegetative portion of the stem; leaf blades linear to oblong or lanceolate

Inflorescence axillary, composed of few to many flowers in the axils of foliage leaves and separated by internodes of normal length (only the uppermost flowers with reduced bracts and/or internodes); leaf blades broad-elliptic to cordate-reniform

c12.text: Corolla blue to purple, exceeding the calyx in lenth; calyx lobes without awns, the upper lobe with a obcordate appendage at the apex; plants woody near the base

Corolla yellow or black to dark red-brown with yellow on the lower lip, shorter than to approximately equaling the calyx; calyx lobes with prominent awns 1–2 mm long, the upper lobe lacking an appendage; plants herbaceous throughout

c13.text: Stems conspicuously white-tomentose; corolla white; lobes of the calyx numbering 10, with reflexed and spinulose apices; plants from a taproot
Stems retrorse-scabrous, hirsute, or glabrous; corolla blue-purple; lobes of the calyx numbering 5, awned at the apex; plants from rhizomes and stolons (in part)

c14.text: Inflorescence axillary, composed of few to many flowers in the axils of foliage leaves and separated by internodes of normal length (only the uppermost flowers with reduced bracts and/or internodes) [Fig. ]

Inflorescence terminal or axillary, spike-like, raceme-like, or panicle-like, the flowers subtended by reduced, bract-like leaves and/or separated by conspicuously shortened internodes relative to the vegetative portion of the stem

c15.text: Calyx actinomorphic or nearly so
Calyx zygomorphic, with an upper and lower lip

c16.text: Corolla nearly actinomorphic, the 4 or 5 lobes nearly equal in length (i.e., not bilabiate; the upper lobe slightly wider than the others and often emarginate at the apex in Mentha )
Corolla zygomorphic, definitely bilabiate

c17.text: Each verticillaster with numerous, crowded flowers; corolla with usually 4 lobes, the upper usually emarginate; ovary lobed to the point of appearing as 4 nearly distinct segments (in part)
Each verticillaster with 2–6 loosely disposed flowers; corolla with 5 lobes; ovary lobed, but the segments clearly connate ca. their length (in part)

c18.text: Flowers with short pedicels
Flowers sessile or subsessile

c19.text: Stems prostrate or trailing; each flower bearing axil with (2–) 3 flowers; upper pair of stamens longer than the lower pair (in part)
Stems erect; each flower-bearing axil with 4–8 flowers; upper pair of stamens shorter than the lower pair

c20.text: Principal leaf blades palmately lobed; corolla 8–12 mm long, the upper lip conspicuously villous
Leaf blades simple; corolla 10–30 mm long, the upper lip glabrous or sparsely pilose

c21.text: Apex of sepals terminated by short, stiff spines; anthers dehiscing by latitudinal valves; mericarps broad-obovoid, rounded at the apex; lower lip of the corolla with a pair of projections near the sinuses on the adaxial (i.e., upper) surface [Fig. ] (in part)

Apex of sepals acuminate, but not spiny; anthers dehiscing by longitudinal valves; mericarps three-angled, truncate or subtruncate at the apex; lower lip of the corolla without a pair of projections near the base of the lobes (in part)

c22.text: Corolla 4-lobed, nearly actinomorphic, the upper lobe slightly wider than the others and often emarginate at the apex (rarely with 5 subequal lobes) (in part)
Corolla zygomorphic, definitely bilabiate

c23.text: Upper calyx lip with broad-triangular lobes, the lobes wider than long; corolla white or yellow (rarely becoming pink), the connate portion curved upward; leaf blades ovate to deltate-ovate; plants citrus-scented

Upper calyx lip with narrow-triangular lobes, the lobes longer than wide; corolla pale purple, red-purple, or pink (rarely white), the connate portion straight; leaf blades ovate, elliptic, oblong, or narrower; plants without a citrus scent (in part)

c24.text: Inflorescence an open, panicle-like cyme
Inflorescence spike-like (sometimes capitate) or raceme-like

c25.text: Stamens with arcuate-curved filaments [Fig. ]; leaf blades linear to rhombic-lanceolate; ovary lobed but the segments clearly connate ca. their length (in part)
Stamens relatively straight; leaf blades elliptic or ovate to broad-ovate; ovary lobed to the point of appearing as 4 nearly distinct segments

c26.text: Each node of the inflorescence with 2 flowers, 1 each in the axil of a bract
Each node of the inflorescence with 4 or more flowers

c27.text: Leaf blades lanceolate or oblanceolate to elliptic, 1–2.5 cm wide, green; petioles absent on all but the lowest leaves; corolla (14–) 16–35 mm long
Leaf blades ovate-oblong to broad-ovate, 2.8–10 cm wide, tinged or suffused with purple; petioles 30–50 mm long; corolla 3–4 mm long

c28.text: Upper lip of the corolla concavely arched, appearing as a small hood (i.e., the corolla galeate) [Figs. , ]
Upper lip of the corolla flat or upwardly curved, not hood-like [Fig. ]

c29.text: Apex of sepals terminated by short, stiff spines; anthers dehiscing by latitudinal valves; lower lip of the corolla with a pair of projections near the sinuses on the adaxial (i.e., upper) surface [Fig. ] (in part)
Apex of sepals acuminate, but not spiny; anthers dehiscing by longitudinal valves; lower lip of the corolla without a pair of projections near the base of the lobes

c30.text: Calyx zygomorphic; filaments bifid near the apex, the lower of the tooth-like branches bearing the anther; floral bracts broadly rounded at the apex
Calyx actinomorphic or nearly so; filaments not bifid at the summit; floral bracts obtuse to acuminate at the apex

c31.text: Inner (i.e., upper) pair of stamens slightly to noticeably longer than the outer pair; calyx with 15 nerves
Inner pair of stamens slightly shorter than the outer pair; calyx with 5 or 10 nerves

c32.text: Corolla 8–12 mm long, usually spotted on the lower lip; upper and lower pair of stamens ± parallel, both ascending under the upper lip of the corolla; anther sacs divergent
Corolla 4–9 mm long, unspotted; upper pair of stamens (i.e., the longer pair) downwardly directed, the lower pair of stamens upwardly oriented; anther sacs ± parallel (in part)

c33.text: Median portion of inflorescence with conspicuously reduced bracteal leaf blades compared with the upper vegetative leaves; mericarps ovoid or obloid, rounded to obtusely pointed at the apex
Median portion of the inflorescence with scarcely reduced bracteal leaf blades compared with the upper vegetative leaves; mericarps three-angled, truncate or subtruncate at the apex (in part)

c34.text: Stamens, at least the longer pair, upwardly curved, closely ascending under the upper corolla lip and not surpassing it [Fig. ]
Stamens individually straight or nearly so, at least the longer pair protruding from the corolla (except in carpellate plants of Mentha , which have smaller flowers and included anthers) [Fig. ]

c35.text: Uppermost lobe of the calyx wider than the other 4; calyx with 15 nerves; floral bracts spinose-serrate at least near the base (entire in D. thymiflorum )
Upper 3 lobes of the calyx differing from the other 2; calyx with 10–13 nerves; floral bracts entire to crenate-serrate

c36.text: Corolla 5–7 mm long; leaf blades linear to narrow-oblanceolate; each flower subtended by minute bracts shorter than the calyx; plants annual, without stolons, 1–3 dm tall

Corolla 12–15 mm long; leaf blades narrow-ovate or ovate to ovate-oblong; each flower subtended by ciliate, linear-subulate bracts about as long as the calyx; plants perennial from short stolons, 2–5 dm tall (in part)

c37.text: Middle lobe of upper calyx lip suborbicular, with winged margins that are decurrent on the calyx tube, forming a concave cap over the top of the calyx; corolla with a 4-lobed upper lip and a single-lobed lower lip
Middle, upper lobe of the calyx subulate to triangular, not forming a cap over the entire calyx; corolla nearly actinomorphic or zygomorphic and then with a 3-lobed lower lip

c38.text: Leaf blades with entire margins
Leaf blades with toothed margins

c39.text: Plants diffusely branched, mat-forming; leaf blades 5–10 mm long; calyx pubescent inside the connate tube
Plants upright; leaf blades 10–95 mm long; calyx ± glabrous inside the connate tube

c40.text: Calyx 10- to 13-nerved; anthers with parallel pollen sacs; verticillasters with densely crowded flowers, forming capitate cymes at the apex of the stems and branches (in part)
Calyx 15-nerved; anthers with divergent pollen sacs; verticillasters with 3–7 flowers in the axils of bracts, forming a terminal, spike-like inflorescence

c41.text: Inflorescence secund [Fig. ]; anthers with divergent pollen sacs; plants annual, without rhizomes
Inflorescence not secund; anthers with ± parallel pollen sacs; plants rhizomatous perennials (sometimes from a woody caudex in Agastache )

c42.text: Corolla nearly actinomorphic, the lower lip unspotted (in part)
Corolla zygomorphic, the lower lip spotted with purple in commonly observed species

c43.text: Calyx 15-nerved; upper lip of corolla somewhat convex and subgaleate; lower lip of corolla unspotted (in part)
Calyx 10- to 13-nerved; upper lip of corolla relatively flat or upwardly curved, not forming a hood; lower lip of corolla commonly spotted with purple (in part)

c1.text: This genus contains exactly one species.
This genus contains exactly one species.
Filaments toothed near apex, dimorphic, the outer ones longer; pith hollow; leaf blades and young branchlets pubescent with stellate hairs
Filaments without apical teeth, monomorphic; pith solid; plants pubescent with simple hairs or glabrous

c2.text: Fertile flowers with 5 petals 1–3 mm long and 10 stamens; marginal flowers of inflorescence often enlarged, sterile, with only 3 or 4 petaloid sepals (enlarged flowers sometimes absent) [Fig. ]; fruit with 10–15 ribs, dehiscing by pores; winter buds axillary to the petioles

Flowers with 4 petals 15–30 mm long and 20–40 stamens [Fig. ]; marginal flowers of inflorescence neither enlarged nor sterile [Fig. ]; fruit without ribs, dehiscing by longitudinal valves; winter buds embedded in the petiole bases

c1.text: Plants herbaceous or suffrutescent; flowers with 3 or 4 stamens (with 5 stamens in Triosteum )
Plants definitely woody; flowers with 5 stamens (with 4 stamens in Kolkwitzia )

c2.text: Flowers and fruits sessile in the axils of leaves [Fig. ]; stamens 5 per flower; fruit an orange-red or orange-yellow drupe
Flowers and fruits borne on a peduncle [Figs. , , ]; stamens 3 or 4 per flower; fruit an achene or cypsela (sometimes with sterile locules and therefore the fruits asymmetrical)

c3.text: Flowers borne in a capitulum-like cyme [Figs. , , ]; corolla 4-lobed (5-lobed in Scabiosa ); ovary and fruit partially enclosed in a gamophyllous, tubular involucel that may be expanded apically
Flowers borne separately in an open inflorescence [Figs. , ]; corolla 5-lobed; ovary and fruit not enclosed in an involucel

c4.text: Stem, and often the involucral bracts and abaxial leaf midrib, with prickles [Fig. ]; receptacular bracts awn-tipped
Stem, bracts, and leaves without prickles; receptacular bracts absent or present and pointed at the apex, but without awn-tips

c5.text: Calyx-teeth or -setae (6–) 8–16 (–24); receptacle pubescent, without scales
Calyx-teeth or -setae 4 or 5 or absent altogether; receptacle glabrous, with scales

c6.text: Involucral bracts ± ovate, rigid, in more than 3 series; marginal flowers of cyme enlarged and falsely radiate
Involucral bracts narrow-lanceolate to lanceolate, herbaceous, in 1–2 (–3) series; marginal flowers of cyme enlarged or not

c7.text: Corolla 5-lobed; marginal flowers of cyme enlarged and falsely radiate; stem leaves once or twice pinnately lobed with deep sinuses (i.e., appearing pinnately compound)
Corolla 4-lobed; marginal flowers of cyme not notably enlarged [Fig. ]; stem leaves simple

c8.text: Calyx-setae 4 or 5; involucel 4-angled and pubescent
Calyx-setae absent; involucel 8-angled and glabrous

c9.text: Stems trailing [Fig. ]; corolla 10–15 mm long; androecium with 4 stamens; flowers nodding, paired [Fig. ]
Stems upright; corolla 1.5–7 mm long; androecium with 3 stamens; flowers neither nodding nor paired [Fig. ]

c10.text: Stem leaves pinnately divided [Fig. ]; calyx composed of 5–20 narrow segments, these inconspicuous at anthesis but unrolling and forming a plumose, pappus-like crown in fruit; plants perennial
Stem leaves simple; calyx obsolete or minute; plants annual

c11.text: Stamens 4 per flower; pedicels and ovary densely bristly pubescent; fruit a bristly achene
Stamens 5 per flower; pedicels and ovary glabrous or pubescent, but not bristly pubescent; fruit a capsule, berry, or drupe

c12.text: Leaf blades regularly serrate; fruit a capsule
Leaf blades entire or with a few, irregular, tooth-like lobes; fruit fleshy

c13.text: Corolla 12–20 mm long, zygomorphic, yellow, turning red in age; capsules glabrous; seeds not winged; petioles glabrous to sparsely pubescent
Corolla 25–30 mm long, nearly actinomorphic, dark red when open (sometimes white or pink); capsules pubescent; seeds winged; petioles ± densely pubescent

c14.text: Corolla 10–50 mm long; ovary with 2 or 3 locules, each locule bearing several ovules; fruit red, blue, or black; leaf blades strictly entire; leaf scars with 3 vascular bundles

Corolla 2–8 mm long; ovary 4-locular, 2 of the locules with several abortive ovules, the other 2 locules with a solitary, fertile ovule; fruit white (red in one rare introduction); leaves entire or with irregular, tooth-like lobes; leaf scars with 1 vascular bundle

c1.text: Petals pink to flesh-colored; stamens 9, connate into 3 distinct groups, alternating with conspicuous, orange glands
Petals yellow to orange-yellow; stamens 5–many, distinct or connate into 3–5 groups, without hypogynous glands

Amphibious plants of tidal shores with horizontal stems emitting from the nodes clusters of linear leaves and sometimes also peduncles bearing a solitary flower with a ± actinomorphic, 5-merous corolla

Terrestrial plants with upright stems and variable leaves wider than linear, with inflorescences borne on a stem bearing flowers with weakly to conspicuously zygomorphic corollas (actinomorphic in Buddleja , but then 4-merous)

c2.text: Plants woody; flowers actinomorphic
Plants herbaceous (though often with firm, persistent stems); flowers weakly to conspicuously zygomorphic [Figs. , ]

c3.text: Foliage leaves all basal or alternate; corolla weakly zygomorphic, rotate [Fig. ]; androecium composed of 5 stamens, all of which bear pollen; plants biennial
Foliage leaves opposite; corolla zygomorphic, bilabiate [Fig. ]; androecium composed of 5 stamens—4 pollen-bearing, 1 sterile; plants perennial

c1.text: Flowers with 5–8 petals, of 2 types—staminate with 8–15 stamens and functionally carpellate with 5–10 stamens that have nonfunctional anthers; pith diaphragmed; leaves alternate
Flowers with 4 petals, of 1 type—bisexual with 4 stamens; pith of woody species solid; leaves opposite, whorled, or alternate

c2.text: Aerial stems herbaceous, 0.1–0.2 m tall, with whorled leaves (sometimes opposite at some nodes); petals terminated by awns; leaves strongly dimorphic, those of the lower nodes many times smaller than those of the upper node (+/- monomorphic in rare putative hybrid individuals); inflorescence pseudanthial, a corymb-like cyme subtended by 4 white, petaloid bracts
Aerial stems woody, 1–10 m tall, with opposite or whorled leaves; petals not awned at apex; leaves essentially monomorphic; inflorescence pseudanthial or not, with or without showy, petaloid bracts

c3.text: Inflorescence pseudoanthial, with 4, white to yellow-white or pink, petaloid bracts [Fig. ]; flowers sessile; petals green-white to yellow; fruits separate or fused together into a multiple, red; terminal flower bud large, globose or discoid

Inflorescence not pseudanthial, with minute and usually caducous bracts [Fig. ]; flowers pedicellate [Fig. ]; petals ± white; fruits separate, white to blue, black, or green; terminal flower bud smaller, ovoid

c1.text: Leaves alternate; perianth 5-merous; fruit an orange or orange-yellow capsule; some of the flowers unisexual; plants lianas by means of twining stems with terete branchlets

Leaves opposite [Fig. ]; perianth 4-merous; fruit a pink or purple capsule; flowers bisexual; plants upright shrubs (liana usually by means of aerial roots in 1 species) often with quadrangular or 4-winged branchlets
Leaf blades simple or reduced to a tendril
Leaf blades compound (sometimes the upper 1-foliate in Cytisus )

c2.text: Plants armed by means of reduced, spine-tipped phyllodes; legume mostly enclosed in the persistent calyx
Vegetative portions of plants unarmed; fruit visible most of its length

c3.text: Leaf blade reduced to a tendril; flowers solitary (rarely paired) on slender peduncles (in part)
Leaf blade broad, not tendril-like; flowers arranged in racemes, fascicles, or umbels

c4.text: Leaf blade obovate to narrow-obovate, gradually tapering toward the base into the petiole; legume spirally coiled, armed with thin prickles along the outer surface of the spiral

Leaf blades linear to lanceolate or elliptic, or elliptic to broad-cordate-ovate, either sessile or rather abruptly transitioning from blade to petiole; fruit not spirally coiled (but curved in Coronilla ), without prickles

c5.text: Plants herbaceous, annual; fruits plump, ± terete in cross-section
Plants woody, perennial; legumes compressed

c6.text: Stipules adnate to the stem forming conspicuous, decurrent wings [Fig. ]; corolla 9–11 mm long; fruit a legume, very inflated, straight
Stipules not adnate to the stem (though connate to each other), not forming decurrent wings; corolla 4–8 mm long; fruit a schizocarp, not bladder-like, curved (in part)

c7.text: Leaves without petioles, the blades elliptic to lanceolate; flowers serotinous, with a yellow corolla; legume 1.5–3 cm long
Leaves with petioles, the blades broad-cordate-ovate; flowers precocious, with a deep pink corolla; legume 6–10 cm long

c8.text: Leaves pinnately compound with more than 3 leaflets [Figs. , , ]
Leaves palmately compound or with 3 or fewer leaflets [Figs. , , ]

c9.text: Plants definitely woody
Plants herbaceous

c10.text: Leaf blade surface with minute, glandular dots; corolla with 1 petal––the banner petal

Leaf blade surface without glandular dots; corolla with 5 petals (note: the 2 lower petals fused to form the keel and thus the corolla appearing as 4 petals in Caragana , Cladrastis , Colutea , Robinia , and Wisteria )

c11.text: Plants lianas; petals blue, blue-purple, or purple (rarely white or pink)
Plants trees or shrubs; petals largely or wholly white, yellow, or pink to red-purple

c12.text: Leaves bipinnately compound with strongly asymmetrical leafules, the midvein of the leafule at or near one margin [Fig. ]; each flower with numerous stamens
Leaves pinnately or bipinnately compound, when bipinnately compound with ± symmetrical leafules, the midvein of the leafules aligned along the center of the blade; each flower with 5–10 stamens

c13.text: Perianth actinomorphic; stamens distinct, with versatile anthers; legume (6–) 8–40 (–50) cm long; leaves pinnately or bipinnately compound
Perianth zygomorphic; stamens diadelphous (distinct in Cladrastis ), with basifixed anthers; legume 4–10 cm long; leaves pinnately compound

c14.text: Leaves all bipinnate, with petioles 20–40 mm long and entire leafules; hypanthium 6–10 mm long; legume (6–) 8–15 (–25) cm long

Leaves pinnate on spurs and bipinnate on new, terminal growth, with petioles up to 20 mm and obscurely crenate leaflets or leafules (depending on division of blade); hypanthium 3–5 mm long; legume 15–40 (–50) cm long

c15.text: Leaflets alternately arranged along the rachis, (4–) 6–15 (–20) cm long
Leaflets oppositely or suboppositely arranged along the rachis [Fig. ], 1–6 cm long

c16.text: Leaves paripinnate [Fig. ]; inflorescence a fascicle with 2–4 flowers; winter bud not concealed by petiole base
Leaves imparipinnate [Fig. ]; inflorescence a raceme with 2–20 (or more) flowers; winter bud concealed within or surrounded by base of petiole

c17.text: Corolla yellow; legume very inflated; calyx with subequal lobes
Corolla white or pink to pink-purple; legume flat; calyx ± bilabiate

c18.text: Some or all of the filaments distally widened; inflorescence a dense umbel (a solitary, peduncled flower in Lotus unifoliatus ) [Fig. ]
All of the filaments slender, not dilated near the apex; inflorescence a raceme, spike, or a solitary flower

c19.text: Inflorescence subtended by palmately lobed bracts; terminal leaflet usually considerably longer than the adjacent lateral leaflets; fruit enclosed in the calyx
Inflorescence without palmately lobed bracts; terminal leaflet of ± similar length to the adjacent lateral leaflets; fruit much longer than the calyx and visible most or all of its length

c20.text: Corolla yellow (later becoming orange marked with red); leaf blades appearing to have 5 leaflets, the basal 2, which are actually stipules, separated from the apical 3; fruit a legume
Corolla pink and/or white; leaf blades with 11–25 evenly spaced leaflets; fruit a schizocarp

c21.text: Schizocarp terete or angled, not flat, 20–50 mm long, weakly constricted between the seeds; calyx zygomorphic; corolla 10–15 mm long, usually pink and white; plants perennial
Schizocarp ± flat, 10–25 mm long, strongly constricted between the seeds; calyx nearly actinomorphic; corolla 6–8 mm long, usually pink with purple lines; plants annual

c22.text: Leaves paripinnate (i.e., the terminal leaflet absent or modified into a tendril) [Figs. , , ]
Leaves imparipinnate (i.e., the terminal leaflet present) [Figs. , ]

c23.text: Leaves with 30–60 leaflets (the upper leaves with fewer leaflets); fruit 10–20 cm long, transversely septate
Leaves with 2–22 leaflets; fruit 0.6–9 cm long (5–20 (–30) cm in Vicia faba , a rare escape), not transversely septate

c24.text: Androecium monadelphous; anthers dimorphic—alternately obloid and globose; fruit developing underground, indehiscent, with a fibrous-reticulate pericarp; tendrils lacking
Androecium diadelphous; anthers monomorphic; fruit developing above ground, dehiscent, the pericarp not fibrous-reticulate; tendrils present (absent in Vicia faba )

c25.text: Stipules foliaceous, ± as large as or larger than the leaflets; style longitudinally folded
Stipules small to prominent, usually smaller than the leaflets [Figs. , ]; style not longitudinally folded

c26.text: Calyx lobes all 2–4 times as long as the basal, connate portion; legume 10–14 ×5–9 mm, with 1 or 2 seeds
Calyx lobes (or at least some of them) less than 2 times as long as the basal, connate portion; legume 6–300 mm long, when less than 14 mm long only 3–5 mm wide, with 2–15 or more seeds

c27.text: Styles slightly widened and flattened in the apical portion, pubescent along the distal, inner surface; wing petals essentially free from the keel petals; leaves with 2–12 leaflets 15–80 mm long; stems winged in some species (in part)

Styles filiform-terete, pubescent in a ring around the apex, or on the outer surface, or glabrous; wing petals cohering to the keel petals; leaves with 4–22 leaflets 5–35 mm long (40–100 mm in V. faba ); stems angled or ridged, but not winged

c28.text: Sepals distinct; stamens distinct or shortly connate near base [Fig. ]; uppermost petal internal to the adjacent lateral petals in bud; petioles (or rachises in 1 species) with 1 or more prominent glands on the adaxial surface
Sepals connate; stamens monadelphous or diadelphous; uppermost petal external to the adjacent lateral petals in bud; petiole lacking prominent, adaxial glands

c29.text: Stipules longitudinally striate; pedicels subtended by two bracteoles; stamens with well-formed anthers; legume elastically dehiscent, not transversely septate
Stipules without longitudinal striae; pedicels ebracteate; upper 3 stamens without well-formed anthers; legume indehiscent or inertly dehiscent, with transverse septa

c30.text: Leaf blades with minute glandular scales or dots (at least on one surface)
Leaf blades without glandular scales or dots

c31.text: Wing petals tiny, much shorter than keel; legume 1-seeded, woody, prominently rugose with raised veins, the lower margin toothed

Wing petals larger, at least as long as the keel; legume with 1 or more seeds, membranaceous to coriaceous, not prominently rugose, lacking teeth on the lower margin (but covered in uncinate prickles in Glycyrrhiza )

c32.text: Inflorescence a raceme with pale yellow flowers; wing and keel petals attached to the receptacle; stamens concealed in intact flowers; fruit 12–15 mm long, armed with uncinate prickles

Inflorescence a dense, obloid to cylindrical spike with white to blue-purple flowers; wing and keel petals attached laterally or apically to the basal, connate portion of the stamens; stamens shortly exserted and visible; fruit 2.5–3 mm long, unarmed

c33.text: Leaves with 5–7 leaflets; corolla purple-brown; climbing or trailing vines with tuberous rhizomes
Leaves with 7–31 leaflets; corolla purple or white; upright to decumbent herbs, but not trailing, without tuberous rhizomes

c34.text: Leaflets coarsely serrate near apex; fruit stipitate-glandular
Leaflets entire; fruit not stipitate-glandular

c35.text: Racemes terminal or opposite the leaves; corolla distinctly bicolored—the banner petal yellow to ochroleucous, the wing and keel petals pink to pale purple; style barbellate
Racemes axillary; corolla not bicolored, purple with varying degress of pink, red, or blue tinting, or white to ochroleucous; style not barbellate

c36.text: Stipules semisagittate to hastate (i.e., with 1 or 2 basal lobes); fruit 30–50 mm long, longitudinally striate
Stipules without basal lobes; fruit 5–30 (–35) mm long, without longitudinal striae

c37.text: Fruit a schizocarp with 2–5 mericarps; raceme secund in flower
Fruit a legume; raceme spirally arranged in flower

c38.text: Keel obtusely to acutely pointed; plants with short, but evident, stems; leaflets 1.3–3.5 times as long as wide (4–5 times as long as wide in A. eucosmus )
Keel abruptly short-pointed; plants acaulescent or nearly so; leaflets 3.5–6 times as long as wide

c39.text: Plants definitely woody
Plants herbaceous or sub-woody

c40.text: Branchlets 4- or 5-angled; inflorescence composed of solitary or paired flowers in the axils of the upper leaves; legume pubescent only on the margin
Branchlets terete; inflorescence a pendulous raceme 15–25 cm long; legume pubescent over the surface

c41.text: Leaves palmately compound with 7–17 leaflets; androecium with monadelphous filaments and dimorphic anthers—one type of anther subglobose and versatile, the other linear and basifixed

Leaves pinnately or palmately compound with 3 or fewer leaflets; androecium with distinct or diadelphous filaments (monadelphous in Hylodesmum and submonadelphous in Pueraria ) and monomorphic anthers

c42.text: Leaflets toothed, at least minutely in the apical portion [Fig. ]
Leaflets entire or sometimes with 1–3 lobes in Pueraria and Strophostyles

c43.text: Stipules entire, 1-nerved, the distinct portion 8 or more times as long as wide; inflorescence (1–) 4–20 cm tall during anthesis, usually 4–15 times as tall as wide [Fig. ]
Stipules entire or toothed, 2- or 3-nerved, the distinct portion commonly less than 8 times as long as wide; inflorescence 0.3–10 cm tall, rarely exceeding 3 times as tall as wide

c44.text: Leaflets all with petiolules of ± similar length (in part)
Terminal leaflet on a petiolule distinctly longer than the petiolules of the lateral leaflets [Fig. ]

c45.text: Calyx actinomorphic; fruit curved to coiled as many as 7 times (rarely straight in M. falcata ) [Fig. ]
Calyx zygomorphic; fruit straight or slightly curved

c46.text: Corolla marcescent; 5 or all of the filaments dilated near the apex; legume shorter than 10 mm, included or barely exserted from the persistent calyx (in part)
Corolla deciduous; all the filaments slender at the apex; legume 10–16 mm long, long-exserted from the persistent calyx

c47.text: Leaves paripinnate, the terminal leaflet modified into a tendril (in part)
Leaves imparipinnate, the terminal leaflet present

c48.text: Terminal leaflet much larger than the orbicular to reniform lateral leaflets (i.e., usually more than 2.5 times as long); fruit a schizocarp, prominently curved, without uncinate hairs (in part)

Terminal leaflet not or only somewhat larger than the lateral leaflets (i.e., usually less than 1.5 times as long, sometimes much larger in a few species of Desmodium and Hylodesmum , but those species with narrower lateral leaflets); fruit a schizocarp with uncinate hairs or a legume, ± straight

c49.text: Stamens distinct; corolla yellow (white to yellow-white or light-purple to blue-purple in some Baptisia )
Stamens diadelphous, 9 stamens connate into a group with 1 separate stamen (monadelphous in Hylodesmum and submonadelphous in Pueraria ); corolla pink to purple, white, or yellow-white

c50.text: Petioles 10–25 mm long; legume strongly compressed, 40–80 mm long; ovary sessile or borne on a stipe up to 3 mm long in fruit
Petioles 2–10 mm long, becoming nearly obsolete on upper leaves; legume turgid or inflated, 7–50 (–60) mm long; ovary stipitate, the stipe 5–15 mm long in fruit

c51.text: Leaflets without stipels [Fig. ]; ovary with 1 ovule, maturing as a 1-seeded, indehiscent fruit

Leaflets usually with stipels [Fig. ]; ovary with 2 or more ovules, maturing as a fruit with 2 or more seeds ( Amphicarpaea also producing more or less apetalous flowers from near the base of the plant with 1 ovule)

c52.text: Petiolule of terminal leaflet clearly longer than the petiolules of the lateral leaflets (i.e., the leaves pinnately compound); stipules subulate or setaceous, not striate; calyx lobes acuminate; plants perennial

Petiolule of terminal leaflet ± the same length as the petiolules of the lateral leaflets (i.e., the leaves palmately compound); stipules narrow-ovate, striate [Fig. ]; calyx lobes blunt; plants annual

c53.text: Fruit a schizocarp; plants erect or ascending (prostrate in Desmodium rotundifolium )
Fruit a legume; plants trailing, twining, or climbing (i.e., vines; with upright stems in Glycine and sometimes in Phaseolus vulgaris )

c54.text: Stamens monadelphous; distinct portion of the calyx (i.e., the lobes) less than 50% as long as the connate portion (i.e., the tube); lower margin of schizocarp deeply incised such that the sinuses extend completely to the upper suture; schizocarp borne on a stipe exceeding the length of the persistent stamens, glabrous on the upper suture

Stamens diadelphous; distinct portion of the calyx more than 50% as long as the connate portion; lower margin of schizocarp moderately incised such that the sinuses do not extend the entire distance to the upper suture; schizocarp borne on a stipe that is shorter than the persistent stamens, uncinate-pubescent on the upper suture

c55.text: Bracts of pedicels obtuse to rounded at the apex; flowers without subtending bracteoles; plants with dimorphic flowers—petaliferous flowers with 10 diadelphous stamens and maturing as a 3- or 4-seeded aerial fruit, and more or less apetalous flowers with fewer than 10 distinct stamens and maturing as a 1-seeded, often subterranean, fruit
Bracts of pedicels acute at the apex; flowers with closely subtending bracteoles that overlap the calyx (caution: the bracteoles caducous in Pueraria ); plants with monomorphic, petaliferous flowers

c56.text: Corollas 5–7 mm long; plants upright; inflorescence a raceme

Corollas 8–25 mm long (as short as 3.6 mm in the very rare introduction Strophostyles leiosperma ); plants vining (sometimes upright in Phaseolus vulgaris ); inflorescence a pseudoraceme (i.e., with 2 or more flowers produced from some nodes)

c57.text: Keel petal relatively straight; style glabrous; leaflets ovate to suborbicular, 0.8–1.2 times as long as wide
Keel petal conspicuously arched or coiled inward; style pubescent; leaflets lanceolate or narrow-elliptic to ovate or rhombic, 1–8 (–10) times as long as wide

c58.text: Plants pubescent with hairs that are not hooked at the tip and are visible at low magnification; some leaflets often with a lateral lobe on one or both sides; calyx with 4 lobes due to fusion of 2 lobes; keel petals arched inward [Fig. ]; inflorescence capitate, spike-like
Plants with minute, uncinate hairs (note: view at 20 × or higher magnification); leaflets unlobed; calyx with 5 lobes; keel petals coiled inward [Fig. ]; inflorescence elongate, raceme-like

c1.text: This genus contains exactly one species.
Petals separate at the base but cohering at the apex, deciduous together; bark exfoliating in longitudinal strands, without lenticels [Fig. ]; pith brown; seeds usually pyriform
Petals distinct, falling separately; bark close, not exfoliating, with lenticels [Fig. ]; pith white; seeds ± triangular-obovoid

c2.text: Nectary disk entirely adnate to the ovary; tendrils terminating in expanded, adhesive disks (without disks in P. vitacea ); leaf blades palmately compound (often merely palmately lobed in P. tricuspidata )
Nectary disk free from ovary and appearing as a cup-shaped ring; tendrils not terminating in adhesive disks; leaf blades simple, toothed to lobed

c1.text: Gynoecium with 2–5 carpels, maturing as a drupe or a berry with 2–5 pyrenes or seeds, respectively; plants woody or herbaceous
Gynoecium with 2 carpels, maturing as schizocarp that separates into 2 mericarps; plants herbaceous

c2.text: Plants lianas, with aerial roots; leaves evergreen
Plants trees, shrubs, or herbs, without aerial roots; leaves deciduous

c3.text: Leaf blades 2 or more times pinnately divided; gynoecium with usually 5 carpels, therefore, the fruit with 5 pyrenes
Leaf blades palmately lobed or once palmately divided; gynoecium with 2 or 3 carpels, therefore, the fruit with 2 or 3 pyrenes or seeds (up to 5 carpels and seeds in Eleutherococcus )

c4.text: Plants herbaceous, unarmed, with a single whorl of leaves near the summit of the stem; petals imbricate in bud; styles distinct
Plants woody, armed, with many alternate leaves; petals valvate in bud; styles basally connate

c5.text: Leaf blades palmately lobed; petiole 8–50 cm long
Leaf blades palmately divided; petiole up to 12 cm long

c6.text: Inflorescence composed of dense, head-like clusters of ± sessile flowers [Fig. ], each flower subtended by a bractlet; most leaf blades spinulose-toothed
Inflorescence dense to open, with pedicellate flowers (sessile in some Hydrocotyle ) [Fig. ],

c7.text: Bractlets of umbel connate basally, white to pink, usually equal to or longer than the umbel they subtend; schizocarps covered with bladdery, triangular scales
Bractlets of umbel (when present) distinct, green, and/or shorter than umbel, commonly with all three traits; schizocarps without scales (though sometimes with hairs, bristles, or prickles)

c8.text: Umbels simple [Fig. ]; stems prostrate, creeping over the substrate
Umbels compound [Figs. , , ]; stems ascending to erect

c9.text: Leaves with orbicular to ovate-orbicular blades, the blades crenate to inconspicuously lobed, not hollow, without septa [Fig. ]
Leaves phyllodial, linear, entire, hollow, each with 4–6 transverse septa

c10.text: Stem leaves simple and entire
Stem leaves divided (simple and toothed in the tidal form of Sium suave )

c11.text: Leaf blades palmately divided into 3–7 broad segments; plants polygamous, with staminate flowers in separate umbellets or intermixed with the bisexual flowers; ovary and fruit with uncinate bristles [Figs. , ]

Leaf blades compound to decompound; plants mostly synoecious (polygamous in Taenidia ); ovary and fruit glabrous or provided with hairs, bristles, or prickles, but these not hooked at the tip (except in Torilis )

c12.text: Ovary and fruit pubescent, bristly, or prickly
Ovary and fruit glabrous

c13.text: Ultimate segments of leaf blades narrow-linear to filiform, up to 1 mm wide, all entire
Ultimate segments of leaf blades linear to ovate or obovate, wider than 1 mm, often toothed

c14.text: Bractlets at base of umbellets bilobed at apex; mericarp with a quadrangular body 6–15 mm long, tipped by an elongate, flattened beak 20–70 mm long
Bractlets simple or pinnately dissected or absent; mericarps 2–20 mm long, without a beak or with a short, inconspicuous beak 1–2 mm long

c15.text: Bracts of inflorescence pinnately dissected [Fig. ]; central flower of inflorescence usually purple
Bracts of inflorescence simple or absent; central flower of inflorescence white, colored similar to the other flowers

c16.text: Inflorescence with 15–150 primary branches; upper leaf sheaths dilated, wider than 10 mm; schizocarps strongly compressed parallel with the commissure
Inflorescence with 2–15 (–20) primary branches; upper leaf sheaths not conspicuously dilated and narrower than 10 mm; schizocarps weakly compressed perpendicular to the commissure

c17.text: Principal leaf blades once divided into 3 (rarely as many as 7) segments [Fig. ], the segments again lobed and 5–30 (–60) cm long; schizocarp 7–12 mm long, with promiment oil tubes (in part)
Principal leaf blades 2 or 3 times pinnately compound, the ultimate segments 2–4 (–7) cm long; schizocarp 4–7 mm long, with inconspicuous oil tubes (in part)

c18.text: Ultimate segments of leaf blades narrower than 10 mm; ovary and fruit with stiff, thin, ascending to spreading prickles [Fig. ]
Ultimate segments of leaf blades wider than 10 mm; ovary and fruit with hairs or appressed-ascending bristles [Figs. , ]

c19.text: Principal leaf blades twice pinnately compound; schizocarps 10–22 mm long, narrow-clavate in outline [Figs. , ]
Principal leaf blades simple to once pinnately compound; schizocarps 3–5 mm long, ovate in outline (in part)

c20.text: Principal stem leaf blades with ultimate segments wider than 10 mm, frequently wider than 15 mm, the segments clearly recognizable and often of uniform shape, not further dissected into narrow lobes
Principal stem leaf blades with ultimate segments narrower than 10 mm (frequently narrower than 6 mm), the segments less organized and the limits of each not always obvious

c21.text: Upper leaf sheaths dilated, wider than 10 mm [Fig. ]; inflorescence with 15–150 primary branches

Upper leaf sheaths not dilated, narrower than 10 mm; marginal flowers of umbel not or only slightly enlarged, the outer petals entire or bifid, similar to the inner petals; schizocarp 2–8 mm long, without conspicuous oil tubes (except in Pastinaca )

c22.text: Principal leaf blades once divided into 3 (rarely as many as 7) segments [Fig. ], the segments again lobed and 5–30(–60) cm long; marginal flowers of umbel enlarged, zygomorphic, the outer petals often bifid (in part)

Principal leaf blades 2 or 3 times pinnately compound, the ultimate segments 2–4(–7) cm long; marginal flowers of umbel not or only slightly enlarged, actinomorphic, the outer petals usually entire (in part)

c23.text: Schizocarp 1.5–2 mm long; umbels mostly sessile or shortly pedunculate from the axils of leaves (some terminal ones with evident peduncles also present)
Schizocarp 2–10 mm long; umbels, whether lateral or terminal, mostly with evident peduncles

c24.text: Principal leaf blades with 3 leaflets, the leaflets sometimes with conspicuous lobes but not again divided (the basal leaves with simple blades in Thaspium )
Principal leaf blades with more than 3 leaflets

c25.text: Flowers with white petals and minute sepals; primary branches of umbel distinctly unequal in length [Fig. ]; basal leaf blades compound; schizocarp 5–8 mm long
Flowers with purple petals and small, but evident, sepals; primary branches of umbel ± equal in lengh; basal leaf blades simple; schizocarp 3.5–5 mm long

c26.text: Principal leaf blades (or the emersed ones in Sium ) once pinnately compound
Principal leaf blades two or three times pinnately compound

c27.text: Basal leaf blades simple, cordate at base; central flower of each umbellet sessile, the others pedicelled; stylopodium wanting (in part)
Basal leaf blades compound (simple in a tidal form of Sium suave ); all the flowers pedicellate; stylopodium present

c28.text: Petals yellow; schizocarp conspicuously compressed parallel to the commissure [Fig. ], with conspicuous lateral wings much wider than the abaxial ribs (in part)
Petals white; schizocarp weakly compressed perpendicular to the commissure [Fig. ], the lateral ribs not evidently wider than the abaxial ribs

c29.text: Leaflets of emersed leaves linear to narrow-ovate, with veins not consistently directed to teeth or sinuses; bractlets at base of umbellets present; native plants of wetlands, when submersed with bi- or tri-pinnately dissected lower leaf blades

Leaflets ovate to suborbicular, the veins generally directed to the tips of teeth or lobes; bractlets at base of umbellets usually absent; introduced plants of fields and disturbed ground, not producing highly dissected blades (in part)

c30.text: Leaflets entire; umbellets near margin of inflorescence bearing bisexual flowers around the periphery and staminate flowers toward the middle, the umbellets near the center of the inflorescence entirely staminate
Leaflets toothed; umbellets not varying as to sex of flowers

c31.text: Central flower of each umbellet sessile, the others pedicelled; stylopodium wanting (in part)
All the flowers pedicelled; stylopodium present

c32.text: Central rachis of leaf prominently foliaceous-winged below the terminal triad of leaf segments
Central rachis of leaf not wing-margined

c33.text: Veins of the leaf blade segments directed to the sinuses [Fig. ]; stems hollow and cross-septate near the base; sepals well-developed, triangular (in part)
Veins of the leaf blade segments mostly directed to the tips of the teeth or lobes; stems solid or hollow at base, but without cross septa; sepals minute or obsolete (present in Ligusticum )

c34.text: Ultimate segments of leaf blades usually entire in the basal to ; bractlets at base of umbellet mostly numbering 6–10
Ultimate segments of leaf blades ± uniformly serrate or serrulate; bractlets at base of umbellet absent or few (present in Angelica lucida )

c35.text: Petals yellow to green-yellow; sepals obsolete; schizocarp conspicuously compressed parallel to the commissure; introduced plants of fields and disturbed ground
Petals white; sepals well-developed, triangular; schizocarp weakly compressed perpendicular to the commissure; native plants of Atlantic coast beaches

c36.text: Petals yellow; schizocarp 5–7 mm long, conspicuously compressed parallel to the commissure [Fig. ], with deciduous or inconspicuous styles (in part)
Petals white; schizocarp 3–4 mm long, compressed perpendicular to the commissure, with persistent, reflexed styles extending back to near midlength of fruit [Fig. ]

c37.text: Ultimate segments of leaf blades narrow-linear to filiform, up to 1 mm wide, all entire (the lower leaves in Coriandrum with broader segments); mature schizocarps spicy or pleasantly aromatic (except Bifora and Ptilimnium )
Ultimate segments of leaf blades linear to ovate or obovate, wider than 1 mm, often toothed; mature schizocarps rank-scented or weakly aromatic (strongly aromatic in Myrrhis )

c38.text: Bracts at base of primary umbel often pinnately divided into filiform segments; sepals present, ± equal in size; native plants of saline marshes

Bracts at base of primary umbel absent or present and simple; sepals none or present in Coriandrum and then distinctly unequal in size; spice plants escaped from cultivation ( Bifora foliage unpleasantly aromatic)

c39.text: Petals yellow; umbel with (10–) 15–40 primary branches; styles short and stout in anthesis, up to 0.5 mm long excluding stylopodium; bractlets at base of umbellets absent
Petals white to pink; umbel with 3–14 (–16) primary branches; styles slender, 0.5–2 mm long excluding stylopodium; bractlets (at least 1) usually present at base of umbellets

c40.text: Principal leaves with petiolar sheaths 1–2.5 (–3) cm long; schizocarp compressed parallel with commissure, with prominent lateral wings; plants annual

Principal leaves with petiolar sheaths 3–9 (–10) cm long; schizocarp subterete or slightly compressed perpendicular to the commissure, the lateral wings no more prominent than those of the abaxial surface; plants short-lived perennial

c41.text: Schizocarp nearly biglobose, each mericarp subglobose, faintly rugulose-patterned; umbel with 3–8 primary branches

Schizocarp not biglobose, each mericarp hemispherical or narrower, ridged or ribbed, but not rugulose; umbel commonly with 8 or more primary branches or less in Coriandrum , but that species with the lower leaf blades merely lobed with relatively broad segments

c42.text: Umbel with 3–7 (–8) primary branches; schizocarp subglobose, tardily separating; marginal flowers of umbel with sepals and conspicuously enlarged petals 3–4 mm long

Umbel with (6–) 8–14 (–16) primary branches; schizocarp oblong to elliptic in outline, readily separating into 2 mericarps; marginal flowers of umbel ± similar to the central ones, without sepals and with petals not over 2 mm long

c43.text: Schizocarps 15–25 mm long; primary branches of umbel dimorphic (especially in fruit), those bearing only staminate flowers thinner and shorter than those bearing bisexual flowers
Schizocarps 1.5–10 mm long; primary branches of umbel ± monomorphic

c44.text: Schizocarp with a smooth body, lacking ribs or wings (only the apical beak ribbed in A. sylvestris ) [Fig. ]; bractlets at base of umbellets narrow-ovate (linear in A. cerefolium ), with conspicuously ciliate or fimbriate margins
Schizocarp with a ribbed and/or winged body; bractlets setaceous to lanceolate, not or only minutely ciliate, or absent

c45.text: Plants bearing vegetative bulbils on the upper parts, these subtended by broad-based, acuminate-tipped bracts (in part)

c46.text: Stems spotted with red-purple; bractlets subtending the umbellets lanceolate to ovate or triangular, conspicuously wider than the pedicels they subtend

Stems not spotted with red-purple; bractlets setaceous to narrow-lanceolate or narrow-oblanceolate, scarcely, if at all, wider than the pedicels they subtend (narrow-lanceolate to lanceolate and somewhat wider in Peucedanum )

c47.text: Petals yellow to green-yellow; schizocarp somewhat compressed perpendicular to the commissure, with thin ribs narrower than the intervals between them
Petals white; schizocarp subterete or conspicuously compressed parallel to the commissure, the thick ribs wider than the intervals between them

c48.text: Primary branches of umbel very unequal, the outer branches 2–3 times (or more) longer than the central branches; outer flowers of umbel zygomorphic; schizocarp subterete

Primary branches of umbel only somewhat unequal, the outer branches shorter than to as much as 2 times as long as the central branches; outer flowers of umbel not or scarcely zygomorphic; schizocarp somewhat to conspicuously compressed parallel to the commissure

c49.text: Schizocarp suborbicular in outline, with low, blunt abaxial ribs; bractlets subtending the umbellets narrow-lanceolate to lanceolate; stems hollow
Schizocarp elliptic to oblong or ovate-oblong in outline, with prominently raised, thin-edged, abaxial ribs; bractlets subtending the umbellets linear to narrow-lanceolate; stems solid

c50.text: Branches of inflorescence glabrous; schizocarp (4.5–) 5–6 (–8) mm long; native plants of swamps, stream banks, and riparian forests
Branches of inflorescence puberulent on the angles; schizocarp 3–4 mm long; non-native plants of waste areas and yards

c1.text: Leaves with 11–19 leaflets, the middle lateral leaflets the largest; branchlets with chambered pith; drupe with an indehiscent exocarp (i.e., husk); each staminate ament borne separately; staminate flowers with 8–40 stamens and glabrous anthers

Leaves with 5–9 (–11) leaflets, the terminal leaflet the largest; branchlets with solid pith; drupe with a 4-valved, dehiscent exocarp; staminate aments borne in clusters of 3; staminate flowers with 3–10 stamens and pilose anthers
This genus contains exactly one species.
Leaf blades simple, the margins entire, toothed, or lobed [Figs. , ]
Leaf blades compound [Figs. , , ]

c2.text: Plants herbaceous, less than 1 m tall
Plants trees or shrubs (i.e., woody), commonly taller than 1 m

c3.text: Androecium with 4 stamens; petals absent; bractlets present and alternating with the sepals (i.e., an epicalyx is present); gynoecium with 1 (–3) ovaries, permanently enclosed within the hypanthium
Androecium with many stamens; petals present (absent in apetalous flowers of R. dalibarda ); bractlets absent; gynoecium with 5–many ovaries, not enclosed within the hypanthium (in part)

c4.text: Gynoecium apocarpous, composed of 3–many distinct carpels; fruit an achene, follicle, capsule, or aggregate of drupes (a drupe in Rhodotypos )
Gynoecium syncarpous and composed of 2–5 carpels or consisting of a single carpel; fruit a pome, drupe, or 5-angled capsule

c5.text: Leaves opposite; fruit a drupe
Leaves alternate; fruit an achene, capsule, follicle, or aggregate of drupes

c6.text: Petals yellow; fruit an achene (i.e., both dry and indehiscent)
Petals white to pink or red-purple; fruit an aggregate of drupes, follicle, or capsule (i.e., not both dry and indehiscent)

c7.text: Fruit fleshy, indehiscent; petals 15–30 mm long; leaf blades 10–20 cm long (in part)
Fruit dry, dehiscent; petals 2–7 mm long; leaf blades 3–10 cm long

c8.text: Leaf blades toothed or double-toothed (often 3-lobed in S. × ‌vanhouttei ); stipules lacking; carpels not inflated in fruit, dehiscing on 1 suture
Leaf blades usually 3-lobed; stipules present (or at least stipule scars present on the branchlets); carpels prominently inflated in fruit, dehiscing on both sutures

c9.text: Leaf blades entire (sometimes serrate near the apex on vigorous shoots in Exochorda )
Leaf blades serrate to lobed (often subentire over part of the margin in Prunus pumila and some Amelanchier )

c10.text: Flowers solitary at the apex of leafy branchlets, 4–5 cm in diameter; fruit a pome 30–50 mm in diameter; leaf blades 5–10 ×3–5 cm
Flowers borne 2–10 together in a raceme or corymb-like cyme, up to 3.5 cm in diameter; fruit a pome 5–7 mm in diameter or a capsule; leaf blades 0.7–6.5 ×0.5–3.5 cm

c11.text: Inflorescence a raceme of 4–10 flowers; petals white, 12–20 mm long; fruit a 5-angled capsule with deep sinuses containing winged seeds
Inflorescence a corymb or corymb-like cyme with 2–4 flowers; petals pink, 3–4 mm long; fruit a red pome with (1–) 2 (–3) pyrenes

c12.text: Flowers with 1 style; fruit a drupe; ovary superior
Flowers with 2–5 styles; fruit a pome; ovary inferior, or at least partly so in fruit (note: the ovary is superior in flower in the following genera)

c13.text: Inflorescence a raceme (+/- a fascicle in A. bartramiana ); ovary and fruit 10-locular
Inflorescence a cyme, umbel, or fascicle, in any case lacking an elongate, main axis; ovary and fruit 2- to 5-locular

c14.text: Carpels hard and bony, difficult to open to expose the seeds; styles distinct; plants usually armed with evident thorns; leaf blades often lobed or with lobe-like teeth, especially on long shoots [Figs. , , ]

Carpels papery or cartilaginous, easily opened to expose the seeds; styles connate at the base (distinct in Pyrus ); plants unarmed or with thorns in Chaenomeles (often with thorn-like short shoots in Malus and Pyrus ); leaf blades unlobed (usually lobed in Malus sieboldii )

c15.text: Leaf midrib with a row of glands on the adaxial surface; petals 4–6 mm long; fruit 0.4–1 cm in diameter, astringent at maturity
Leaf midrib without a row of glands on the adaxial surface; petals 15–25 mm long (5–7 mm long in Sorbus alnifolia ); fruit 0.6–12 cm in diameter, sweet or sour-sweet at maturity

c16.text: Leaf blades prominently double toothed; petals 5–7 mm long (in part)
Leaf blades single toothed (sometimes lobed in some Malus ); petals 15–25 mm long

c17.text: Branchlets usually with thorns; carpels each with many ovules; stipules large and conspicuous, mostly 5–10 mm long
Branchlets without thorns (though the short-shoots often thorn-like); carpels each with 2 ovules; stipules small and/or caducous

c18.text: Styles distinct; anthers ± red (i.e., anthocyanic); orifice of hypanthium nearly closed by a ring of tissue; pome pyriform or globose, with abundant sclerenchyma cells (i.e., with a gritty feel); inflorescence a corymb-like raceme; leaves involute in bud, with a thick, waxy cuticle on the adaxial surface

Styles connate at the base; anthers yellow to white (i.e., non-anthocyanic); orifice of hypanthium open; pome globose to ovoid, without or with few sclerenchyma cells (i.e., without a gritty feel); inflorescence a fascicle; leaves convolute or conduplicate in bud, without a thick, waxy cuticle adaxially

c19.text: Leaves pinnately compound with 3 leaflets or palmately compound [Figs. , ]
Leaves once- or twice-pinnately compound, always with more than 3 leaflets [Fig. ]

c20.text: Gynoecium with 2–6 (–10) carpels
Gynoecium with many carpels [Figs. , ]

c21.text: Petals white (sometimes pale pink); inflorescence at the apex of a leafy stem
Petals yellow; inflorescence on a ± naked peduncle originating from near the ground level, or sometimes with a small leaf or 2 immediately below the cyme

c22.text: Leaflets toothed along the margins and at the apex; petals 5–10 mm long; androecium with many stamens (in part)
Leaflets 3 (–5) toothed at the very apex, the margins entire for much of their length; petals ca. 1 mm long; androecium with 5 stamens

c23.text: Styles elongate, jointed near or above the middle, the basal portion with a hooked tip, becoming indurate and persistent in fruit, the apical portion deciduous [Fig. ]; lower and upper stem leaves distinctly different in size, shape, and division (in part)
Styles short, not jointed near middle, deciduous in fruit [Fig. ]; lower and upper stem leaves relatively similar in outline, though the upper somewhat reduced in size

c24.text: Flowers without bractlets alternating with the sepals; carpels maturing as small drupes that are coherent in fruit; plants often armed with bristles or prickles (in part)
Flowers with bractlets that resemble the sepals and alternate with them (i.e., the sepals appear to number (8–) 10 per flower); carpels maturing as achenes; plants unarmed

c25.text: Bractlets definitely larger than the sepals, with 3 conspicous teeth at the apex; receptacle enlarged in fruit but rather dry and insipid tasting; petals yellow (in part)

Bractlets of ± similar size as the sepals or smaller, lacking conspicuous apical teeth (though the margins may have small teeth); receptacle either enlarged in fruit and sweet-tasting or not enlarged and remaining dry; petals white to pink or ochroleucous to yellow

c26.text: Receptacle enlarged in fruit and becoming fleshy, sweet-tasting at maturity; petals white or tinged with pink; bractlets ± subequal in size to the sepals
Receptacle neither enlarged nor fleshy in fruit; petals yellow or white; bractlets in most species narrower and/or shorter than the sepals

c27.text: Style originating from the side of the carpel (i.e., lateral) [Fig. , L]; petals white; surface of ovary and achenes pubescent; leaflets entire for most of the margin and with 3 (–5) teeth at the very apex

Style originating from or very near the apex of the carpel (i.e., terminal) [Fig. , R]; petals yellow (white in P. alba ); surface of ovary and achenes glabrous; leaflets with teeth or lobes usually distributed over more of the margin, restricted to the very apex in a few species (in part)

c28.text: Plants trees or shrubs (i.e., woody)
Plants herbaceous (sometimes woody at the very base)

c29.text: Flowers with 2–5 carpels; inflorescence a many-flowered cyme or panicle, usually with 25 or more flowers
Flowers with many carpels; inflorescence a solitary flower, a corymb, a cyme, or a raceme, most species with an inflorescence with fewer than 25 flowers

c30.text: Rachis of leaves adaxially with clusters of dark glands at the nodes; flowers with 2–4 carpels, partly epigynous; leaflet margins serrate to obscurely double-serrate [Fig. ]; inflorescence a flat- to round-topped cyme; fruit a pome (in part)
Rachis of leaves lacking dark glands; flowers with 5 carpels, perigynous; leaflet margins double-serrate; inflorescence a tall panicle; fruit a follicle

c31.text: Plants unarmed; leaflets entire; fruit and hypanthium not fleshy; petals yellow (often white or ochroleucous in planted populations)
Plants usually armed with bristles or prickles; leaflets toothed; fruit fleshy or enclosed in a fleshy hypanthium; petals white to pink to red-purple or ochroleucous

c32.text: Fruit an aggregate of achenes, surrounded and concealed by a fleshy hypanthium; stipules connate to the petiole for at least half their length [Fig. ]; plants perennial

Fruit an aggregate of drupes, not surrounded by a hypanthium and, therefore, clearly visible [Fig. ]; stipules distinct from the petiole; plants biennial—producing vegetative stems the first year and reproductive the second (in part)

c33.text: Leaves twice-pinnately compound; fruit dehiscent
Leaves once-pinnately compound; fruit indehiscent

c34.text: Flowers with 4 petaloid sepals, 0 petals, and 0–2 carpels
Flowers with 5 sepaloid sepals, 5 petals, and 2–many carpels

c35.text: Flowers with 2 carpels; hypanthium armed with hooked bristles [Figs. , ]; inflorescence an elongate raceme
Flowers with 5–many carpels; hypanthium not armed; inflorescence a solitary flower, a corymb, or a cyme

c36.text: Styles elongate, jointed near or above the middle, the basal portion with a hooked tip, becoming indurate and persistent in fruit, the apical portion deciduous [Fig. ]; lower and upper stem leaves distinctly different in size, shape, and division (in part)
Styles short, not jointed near the middle, deciduous in fruit; lower and upper stem leaves relatively similar in outline, though the upper somewhat reduced in size

c37.text: Flowers without bractlets alternating with the sepals; petals white or pink to pink-red; carpels 5–15 per flower, arranged in a single whorl

Flowers with bractlets that resemble the sepals and alternate with them (i.e., the sepals appearing to number (8–) 10 per flower); petals yellow, white, or red; carpels many per flower, spirally arranged in several cycles

c38.text: Flowers solitary at the tips of leafless peduncles produced from the nodes of an eventually prostrate to spreading stem
Flowers few to numerous, arranged in cymes borne at the summit of a leafy stem

c39.text: Leaves pinnately compound with 5–31 principal leaflets, conspicuously pubescent with gray-white tomentum on the abaxial surface (this sometimes partially concealed by lustrous, sericeous hairs); style lateral, emerging from the side of the carpel [Fig. , L]

Leaves palmately compound with 3–5 leaflets, glabrous or moderately pubescent with villous or sericeous hairs on the abaxial surface; style terminal, emerging from near the apex of the carpel [Fig. , R] (in part)

c40.text: Petals ochroleucous; style subbasal, emerging from near the base of the carpel; plants viscid-pubescent, especially above, the hairs with brown septa; stamens mostly 25–30 per flower
Petals red or yellow; style terminal or lateral; plants not viscid-pubescent; stamens mostly 20 per flower

c41.text: Petals red; style originating from the side of the carpel (i.e., lateral) [Fig. , L]; principal leaves with 5–7 pinnately arranged leaflets; wetland species
Petals yellow; style originating from near the apex of the carpel (i.e., terminal) [Fig. , R]; leaves with 3–7 palmately or subpalmately arranged leaflets; primarily upland plants (in part)

c1.text: Leaves simple, entire; fruiting panicle with long-plumose, sterile pedicels
Leaves pinnately compound, the leaflets entire or, more commonly, toothed; fruiting panicle without long-plumose sterile pedicels (though the fertile pedicels may be short-pubescent)

c2.text: Drupes red, conspicuously pubescent; inflorescence terminal or borne laterally on the previous season’s branchlets, the flowers and fruits crowded; leaves with 7–31 leaflets or only 3 leaflets in R. aromatica ; petals often pubescent on the adaxial surface
Drupes white to yellow, glabrous or sparsely pubescent; inflorescence axillary, relatively more open; leaves with 3–13 leaflets; petals glabrous

c1.text: Achenes trigonous and with 3 evident wing-angles; leaf blades 12–40 (–57) ×10–30 (–61) cm, cordate-ovate to deltate, borne on stout petioles; androecium with 9 stamens

Achenes lenticular or trigonous, but without wings or with an partially encircling, marginal wing on a lenticular achene in Oxyria ; leaf blades shorter and/or narrower, with relatively thinner petioles; androecium with 3–8 stamens (9 in Chorizanthe )

c2.text: Achenes with a partially encircling, marginal wing; perianth with 4 tepals
Achenes without wings; perianth with (4–) 5 or 6 tepals

c3.text: Outer 3 tepals of carpellate flowers each with a conspicuous spine (note: this most evident in fruit); plants clearly monoecious—the carpellate flowers with 6 tepals positioned below the staminate ones with 5 tepals

None of the tepals bearing spines (though with a spiny involucre in Chorizanthe ); plants predominantly synoecious or dioecious (sometimes polygamous), the two types of flowers (when present) with the same number of tepals

c4.text: Flowers subtended by a 6-parted involucre, the involucre with 3 longer members alternating with 3 shorter members, each member tipped by an awn; androecium with 9 stamens
Flowers not subtended by an awn-tipped involucre; androecium with 3–8 stamens

c5.text: Tepals 6, sepaloid or herbaceous, in 2 series of 3—the outer series spreading to reflexed, the inner series erect and distinctly enlarged in fruit (not accrescent in R. acetosella ) [Figs. , ]
Tepals (4–) 5, often petaloid, usually in a single series, all erect to ascending, of ± equal size relative to one another in fruit or the outer tepals slightly larger than the inner [Figs. , , ]

c6.text: Tepals nearly distinct, remaining small in fruit; achene exserted beyond the remnant tepals for much of its length; filaments winged; nectaries stalked

Tepals connate at base for a distance up to 57% of their total length [Figs. , ], at least somewhat accrescent in fruit; achene enclosed in remnant tepals or the tip exserted; filaments unwinged; nectaries absent or present and then not stalked

c7.text: Tepals with trifid veins (i.e., with three main branches at the base); flowers with nectaries, these appearing as mamillae around the stamens; stamens monomorphic, not enlarged at base

Tepals with dendritic veins (i.e., with a single main vein that smaller veins branch off from) or sometimes the vein unbranched [Fig. ]; flowers without nectaries; stamens dimorphic, the inner larger, often enlarged at the base

c8.text: Tepals connate at the base for or less of their length; gynoecium with 3 carpels and 3 styles or the flowers sterile or replaced by bulbils; androecium with 8 stamens; plants perennial, with basally disposed leaves, unbranched stems, and a solitary, terminal inflorescence [Fig. ]

Tepals connate for or more their length into a cup-like structure (except in P. wallichii ); gynoecium with 2 or 3 carpels and 1 style that is apically bifid or trifid (with 2 styles in P. virginiana ); androecium with 5–8 stamens; plants annual or perennial, with chiefly cauline leaves, unbranched or branched stems, and commonly 2 or more terminal or terminal and axillary inflorescences (commonly solitary and terminal in P. amphibian and P. coccinea )

c9.text: Erect to prostrate herbs up to 7 (–10) dm tall; stipules bilobed (usually not in P. articulatum ); papillae absent from base of filaments; outer tepals keeled, but not winged, in fruit; flowers with 3–8 stamens

Robust, upright herbs 10–40 dm tall or vines; stipules truncate to obliquely pointed at apex (i.e., not bilobed); papillae present at the base of the filaments; outer tepals with a conspicuous keel or wing in fruit; flowers with 8 stamens

c1.text: Plants without aerial stems, herbaceous; calyx actinomorphic, the basal, tubular portion straight; flowers with 12 stamens
Plants with aerial stems, woody or herbaceous; calyx zygomorphic, the basal, tubular portion nearly straight or strongly bent [Fig. ]; flowers with 6 stamens

c2.text: Leaf blades 1–5 cm wide, pinnately veined; inflorescence originating from base of stem near ground level; capsule globose, 8–20 mm long

Leaf blades 5–35 cm wide, palmately veined; inflorescence originating from the axils of leaves; capsule cylindric to ovoid or ellipsoid (sometimes globose or pyriform in A. clematitis ), 20–80 mm long

c3.text: Plants herbaceous; inflorescence a fascicle of flowers from the axil or, less commonly, a solitary flower; calyx nearly straight, with a single, terminal lobe; annulus absent; capsules 20–50 mm long

Plants lianas (i.e., woody); inflorescence of a solitary, axillary flower; calyx strongly curved, with 3 terminal lobes [Fig. ]; annulus (i.e., a circular flange at junction of calyx tube and limb) present; capsules 60–80 mm long

c1.text: Inflorescences (2–) 3- to many-flowered, with both peduncles and pedicels (note: the inflorescence is leafy-bracteate in Hyoscyamus ) [Figs. , , ]
Inflorescence consisting of solitary flowers in the axils of leaves (rarely in pairs or trios), with only pedicels, the peduncles absent or obsolete [Fig. ]

c2.text: Corolla zygomorphic, the upper lip 2-lobed; stamens 4, fewer than the lobes of the corolla
Corolla ± actinomorphic; stamens 5, numbering the same as the corolla lobes (“(except in Salpiglossis , which has 4 stamens)

c3.text: Corolla ± rotate [Figs. , ]; anthers dehiscing by terminal pores or small clefts (dehiscing by longitudinal slits in S. lycopersicon ); fruit a berry
Corolla funnelform or salverform [Figs. , ]; anthers dehiscing by longitudinal slits; fruit a capsule or pyxis

c4.text: Androecium with 4, didynamous stamens; corolla lobes conspicuously emarginate
Androecium with 5, equal stamens that are not paired; corolla lobes truncate to acute

c5.text: Inflorescence a leafy-bracteate, ± secund raceme; corolla dull yellow to green-yellow with a purple basal, interior region, conspicuously reticulate-veined with purple veins; fruit a pyxis, circumscissile above the middle
Inflorescence a panicle or secund raceme (but then with very small bracts) [Figs. , ]; corolla variously colored, but without purple reticulations; fruit a capsule that dehisces by 2–4 apical valves

c6.text: One anther conspicuously smaller than the other 4; calyx connate only at the very base; leaves opposite; fruit a 2-valved capsule;

All 5 anthers of similar size; calyx connate at least half its length (connate only near the base in Nicandra , but then each sepal with 2 basal auricles); leaves alternate or falsely appearing opposite in some genera; fruit a berry or 4-valved capsule

c7.text: Flowers 7–24 cm long; fruit berry-like capsule armed with long, soft prickles, with 4 locules (at least in the basal portion), solitary on the stem
Flowers 0.6–2.5 cm long; fruit a 2-locular berry (with 3–5 locules in Nicandra ), usually more than 1 per stem (solitary in Nicandra )

c8.text: Calyx connate only at the very base, each sepal with 2 basal auricles; corolla 20–25 mm long; gynoecium with 3–5 carpels
Calyx connate at least half its length, the sepals lacking basal auricles; corolla 6–20 mm long; gynoecium with 2 carpels

c9.text: Plants woody, usually armed with thorns; corolla blue to purple; leaves borne on petioles 3–10 mm long, the blades with entire margins
Plants herbaceous, unarmed; corolla yellow to white; principal leaves either borne on petioles longer than 10 mm or the blades toothed or both

c10.text: Fruiting calyx usually inflated and larger than the berry it contains [Fig. ], essentially closed at the apical end, membranaceous to scarious, often with 10 prominent ribs; corolla campanulate to open-campanulate
Fruiting calyx not inflated, filled by the berry it contains, open at the apical end, herbaceous, without prominent ribs; corolla ± rotate

c1.text: This genus contains exactly one species.
This genus contains exactly one species.
Plants herbaceous, annual; proximal portion of first pair of primary lateral veins at the very margin of the leaf blade (i.e., the basiscopic side of the vein exposed for a short distance) [Fig. ]
Plants woody, perennial; first pair of primary lateral veins not at the margin of the leaf blade (i.e., both the basiscopic and acroscopic sides bordered by green leaf tissue)

c2.text: Leaf blades entire and unlobed, pinnately veined; branches often with axillary spines; fruit yellow-green, spherical, 6–12 cm wide

Leaf blades toothed, usually at least some on the plant lobed, either with obvious palmate venation or with 3 main veins from the base of the blade; branches without axillary spines; fruit short-cylindric, spherical, or pyriform in outline, 1–8 cm wide

c3.text: Flowers enclosed in a fleshy receptacle and accessible only by a small apical opening; terminal winter bud surrounded by a pair of stipules
Flowers not enclosed in the receptacle, visible without dissection [Fig. ]; terminal winter bud not concealed by stipules

c4.text: Style bifid [Fig. ]; carpellate aments and fruits short-cylindric; petioles 2–5 cm long; branchlets glabrous or pubescent, but the hairs not long and spreading
Style undivided; carpellate aments and fruits spherical; petioles 5–10 cm long; branchlets densely hirsute

c1.text: Plants woody, trees up to 35 m tall; peduncle of the inflorescence adnate to a conspicuous, elongate bract [Figs. , ]; stamens pentadelphous; fruit a nut-like drupe
Plants herbaceous or shrubs to 6 m tall in Hibiscus syriacus ; inflorescence without an adnate bract; stamens monadelphous; fruit a capsule or schizocarp

c2.text: Gynoecium with 5 wholly connate carpels [Fig. ]; fruit a capsule; filaments connate, forming a tube, bearing anthers along the sides of the tube [Fig. ], crowned with 5 teeth at the summit of the filament tube

Gynoecium with 5–40 basally connate carpels [Figs. , ]; fruit a schizocarp, the carpels separating at maturity into indehiscent or dehiscent mericarps; filaments connate, forming a tube, bearing anthers primarily near the apex (along the sides in Lavatera ) [Fig. ], without teeth at summit of filament tube

c3.text: Epicalyx with 3, ovate, laciniately toothed bractlets; styles short, the stigmas almost sessile on the ovary; petals white; seeds covered with long, white hairs

Epicalyx with (6–) 8–15 linear, entire bractlets; style branches elongate, clearly elevating the stigmas above the ovary; petals yellow, pink, red-pink, blue, light purple, or white (when white usually with a red or purple base); seeds without long hairs

c4.text: Calyx connate for most of its length, splitting on one side and early deciduous; mature fruit 6–25 cm long, more than 2 times as long as wide
Calyx basally connate for ca. its length, not splitting, persistent in fruit; mature fruit 1–3.5 cm long, less than 2 times as long as wide

c5.text: Epicalyx absent
Epicalyx of 3–9 bractlets present

c6.text: Gynoecium with (5–) 10–15 (–30) carpels, mature carpels each with 3–9 seeds and terminated by a slender, solitary beak 3–6 mm long; petals 7–13 mm long, yellow; leaf blades entire to crenate, with or without low, obscure lobes

Gynoecium with 5–12 (–15) carpels, mature carpels each with 1 seed and either lacking a beak or terminated by 1 or 2 beaks up to 3 mm long; petals 3–10 mm long, white, yellow, or pink to light purple or light blue-purple; leaf blades conspicuously lobed (merely toothed in Sida spinosa )

c7.text: Gynoecium with (5–) 10–15 (–30) carpels, the mature ones terminated by a slender beak 3–6 mm long and with 3–9 seeds; leaf blades (5–) 10–15 (–20) cm long, broad-ovate to orbicular
Gynoecium with 6–8 carpels, the mature ones terminated by a slender apiculus mostly 0.5–1 mm long and with 3 seeds; leaf blades 3–7 cm long, ovate

c8.text: Plants dioecious (i.e., with unisexual flowers on separate plants); styles with the stigmatic surface along the inner surface; mature carpels apically beakless or minutely apiculate
Plants synoecious (i.e., with bisexual flowers); styles with the stigmatic surface at the capitate apex; mature carpels apically terminated by 1 or 2 erect beaks

c9.text: Petals white or yellow; lateral walls of separating mericarps persistent
Petals pink to light purple or light blue-purple; lateral walls of separating mericarps eventually disintegrating

c10.text: Styles with the stigmatic surface at the capitate apex; mature carpels 2-beaked at the apex, each with 2 seeds (1 seed in Malvastrum )
Styles with the stigmatic surface along the inner surface; mature carpels beakless, each with a single seed

c11.text: Petals yellow; leaf blades coarsely toothed or with inconspicuous lobes
Petals red to red-purple; leaf blades evidently lobed

c12.text: Petals 3–8 mm long; flowers mostly solitary or paired in the axils of leaves; terminal lobe of leaf blade only slightly exceeding the adjacent lateral lobes
Petals 8–13 mm long; flowers (1–) 2–12 from the axils of leaves; terminal lobe of leaf blade elongate, more than 2 times as long as the adjacent lateral lobes

c13.text: Epicalyx with 3 bractlets that are wholly distinct (connate in Lavatera ); gynoecium with 8–15 (–20) carpels
Epicalyx with 6–9 bractlets that are connate at the base; gynoecium with 15–40 carpels

c14.text: Bractlets of epicalyx distinct; mericarps not covered by an expansion of the central axis of the fruit at maturity
Bractlets of epicalyx connate at base; mericarps covered by a disk-like expansion of the central axis of the fruit at maturity (i.e., in fruit)

c15.text: Petals 30–50 mm long; staminal tube pentagonal in cross-section, glabrous; mericarps divided by an internal septum into an upper and lower locule, the upper locule empty
Petals 15–20 mm long; staminal tube terete in cross-section, pubescent; mericarps unilocular

c1.text: Plants tall shrubs or small trees; leaf blades simple, unlobed; fruit a drupe
Plants herbs or vines; leaf blades palmately lobed or palmately divided; fruit an achene

c2.text: Leaf blades palmately lobed; stems vining, retrorsely spinulose; petioles with forked hairs; fruits concealed by large, accrescent bracteoles, collectively the infructescence appearing as “hops” [Fig. ]
Leaf blades palmately divided; stems erect, not spinulose; petioles without forked hairs; fruits subtended, but not concealed, by accrescent bracteoles, the infructescence not appearing as “hops”

c1.text: Carpellate inflorescences paired (rarely solitary or in trios); middle lobe of leaf blade as long as or longer than wide
Carpellate inflorescences solitary (rarely paired); lobes of leaf blade shorter than wide
This genus contains exactly one species.
Corolla apopetalous, or absent in Corema [Figs. , ]
Corolla gamopetalous [Figs. , , ]

c2.text: Plants lacking chlorophyll, the stems and capsules white, pink to red, or yellow to light brown; leaves reduced, scale-like, without green pigment
Plants with chlorophyll, the stems and capsules variously colored; leaves evident, though sometimes scale-like, photosynthetic

c3.text: Inflorescence a solitary flower; stems glabrous, usually white (rarely pink); sepals similar to the subtending bracts; anthers dehiscing by 2 clefts across the top; stigmas glabrous

Inflorescence a raceme with 2–16 flowers; stems pubescent, yellow to light brown or pink to red; sepals not similar to the subtending bracts; anthers dehiscing by a single cleft; stigmas sparsely to densely villous around the margin

c4.text: Herbaceous plants with leaves all basal
Woody or suffrutescent plants with alternate or opposite leaves

c5.text: Flower solitary; petals widely spreading, forming a rotate corolla
Flowers borne in racemes; petals inwardly arching, forming a campanulate or subglobose corolla

c6.text: Flowers borne in a secund raceme, with an actinomorphic corolla; petals bituberculate at the base; style straight, exserted beyond the petals, with a 10-lobed hypogynous disk at the base

Flowers borne on a spirally arranged raceme, with a weakly zygomorphic corolla (actinomorphic in P. minor ); petals without tubercles; style either strongly curved and exserted beyond the petals or straight and about equaling the petals, lacking a 10-lobed hypogynous disk at the base

c7.text: Leaf blades linear to narrow-elliptic, ca. 1 mm wide; perianth inconspicuous; stamens, when present, 2 or 4 per flower
Leaf blades lanceolate, oblanceolate, elliptic-oblong, or elliptic-ovate to ovate, wider than 1 mm; perianth conspicuous; stamens 5–10 per flower

c8.text: Flowers on pedicels from the axils of leaves, with 3 sepals, 3 petals, usually 4 stamens, and usually 6–9 stigmas; fruit a fleshy drupe [Fig. ]; leaf blades entire
