Flowers in small, terminal clusters, with 3 or 4 sepals, 0 petals, 2 stamens (when present), and 2–5 stigmas (when present); fruit a dry drupe; leaf blades minutely denticulate

c9.text: Leaves opposite, sometimes verticillate, serrate; stamens 10 per flower
Leaves alternate, entire; stamens 5–8 per flower

c10.text: Corolla 4-merous, pink to red; leaf blades 8–18 mm long, glaborous or sparsely pubescent; flowers with 8 stamens; fruit a red berry (in part)
Corolla 5-merous, white; leaf blades 20–50 mm long, densely villous-tomentose on the abaxial surface; flowers with 5–7 stamens; fruit a septicidal capsule (in part)

c11.text: Ovary inferior
Ovary superior

c12.text: Perianth 4-merous; plants low, commonly prostrate or trailing
Perianth 5-merous; plants ascending (depressed in extreme conditions)

c13.text: Leaves glabrous; ovary wholly inferior; fruit a red or dark blue to black berry; plants without wintergreen odor (in part)
Leaves pubescent; ovary partly inferior; fruit a white berry; plants with wintergreen odor in life (in part)

c14.text: Ovary 4- or 5-locular, with numerous ovules; leaves lacking resin dots and stipitate glands (in part)
Ovary 10-locular, with 10 ovules; leaves resin-dotted or stipitate-glandular [Fig. ]

c15.text: Corolla campanulate to salverform or rotate, not constricted in the apical portion [Figs. , , ]
Corolla globose, ovoid, urceolate, or tubular, slightly to strongly constricted in the apical portion [Figs. , , ]

c16.text: Corolla rotate, 10-saccate, the anthers fitting in the corolla sacs and later springing forward [Fig. ] (in part)
Corolla campanulate to salverform, not saccate

c17.text: Perianth 4-merous; fruit a 4-locular capsule or berry
Perianth 5-merous; fruit a 2-, 3-, or 5-locular capsule

c18.text: Leaves alternate; corolla deciduous; fruit a white berry; flowers with 4 stamens; subshrubs with prostrate, trailing stems, with wintergreen odor in life (in part)
Leaves opposite or in whorls of 3 or 4; corolla persistent; fruit a capsule; flowers with 8 stamens; shrubs with straggling to upright stems, without wintergreen odor

c19.text: Leaves in whorls of 3 or 4 [Fig. ], without basal auricles; calyx shorter than the corolla (in part)
Leaves opposite, the larger with 2 basal auricles; calyx much longer than the corolla

c20.text: Leaf blades 2–4 mm long, bristle-like [Fig. ]; stamens with spreading or deflexed spurs; plants with moss-like aspect
Leaf blades 3–200 mm long, broader, not resembling bristles; stamens lacking spurs; plants not resembling mosses

c21.text: Leaf blades 3–8 mm long, opposite; corolla 3–5 mm long; fruit a capsule with 2 or 3 locules (in part)
Leaf blades 10–200 mm long, alternate; corolla 14–45 mm long; fruit a capsule (berry-like in Epigaea ) with 5 locules

c22.text: Calyx ebracteate; corolla rotate to campanulate or broad-funnelform [Figs. , ]; anthers opening by 2 pores; fruit a septicidal capsule; upright shrubs (depressed in the alpine R. lapponicum ) (in part)
Calyx subtended by 2 bracts; corolla ± salverform; anthers opening by longitudinal slits; fruit a berry-like capsule; prostrate and trailing shrubs

c23.text: Leaves in whorls of 3 or 4; perianth 4-merous (in part)
Leaves alternate; perianth 5-merous

c24.text: Non-photosynthetic plants with pink to red or red-brown (eventually brown), stipitate-glandular stems bearing scale-like leaves and a terminal raceme of flowers [Fig. ]
Photosynthetic plants with green leaves, with or, more commonly, without stipitate glands, bearing various types of inflorescence

c25.text: Calyx closely subtended by 2 bracteoles (i.e., the bracteoles overlapping the calyx much of their length); inflorescence a solitary flower from the axils of normal foliage leaves or from the axils of reduced, bract-like leaves

Calyx not subtended by 2 bracteoles, though sometimes the associated pedicel may possess 2 bracteoles (these near the apex of the pedicel in Eubotrys ); inflorescence composed of 2 or more flowers (sometimes a solitary flower in Phyllodoce )

c26.text: Calyx and abaxial surface of leaf blades lepidote-scaly; plants 30–150 cm tall; stamens without awns; plants without wintergreen odor; fruit a loculicidal capsule
Calyx and leaf blades without lepidote scales; plants up to 20 cm tall; each pollen sac of an anther with 2 awns; plants with wintergreen odor in life; fruit a red, berry-like capsule (in part)

c27.text: Corolla purple; leaf blades 4–10 ×1–1.3 mm; pedicels stipitate-glandular
Corolla white to pink; leaf blades 10–150 ×2–50 mm; pedicels without stipitate glands

c28.text: Inflorescence produced from the axils of leaves, laterally from the apex of the previous season’s branch, or distributed along leafless branches; anthers essentially lacking apical awns or each with 4 awns
Inflorescence terminal; anthers each with 2 apical awns (without apical awns in Pieris )

c29.text: Anthers with basal awns; flowers borne in umbel-like clusters from the axils of leaves or these distributed along leafless branches forming a compound, raceme-like or panicle-like inflorescence; sutures of capsule prior to dehiscence a broad, pale strip ca. 0.5 mm wide [Fig. ]; winter buds with 2 scales

Anthers lacking awns; flowers borne in axillary racemes or laterally from the apex of the previous seasons branch; sutures of capsule prior to dehiscence a thin strip ca. 0.1 mm wide; winter buds with 3 or more scales

c30.text: Leaf blades evergreen, coriaceous, lustrous; each pedicel with 2 bracteoles borne near the base
Leaf blades deciduous, membranaceous, dull; each pedicel with 2 bracteoles borne near the apex just below the calyx

c31.text: Corolla 5-saccate at base, the sacs alternating with the calyx lobes; inflorescence a panicle; leaf blades 10–25 mm wide
Corolla not 5-saccate at base; inflorescence a few-flowered raceme or umbel-like raceme; leaf blades 2–12 (–18) mm wide

c32.text: Leaves pubescent on the abaxial surface, conspicuously revolute; sepals valvate in bud; fruit a loculicidal capsule
Leaves glabrous, with flat margins; sepals imbricate in bud; fruit a fleshy drupe

c33.text: Leaf blades entire, persistent and living throughout the season, not conspicuously veiny, with unwinged petioles; branchlets pubescent; inflorescence with 5–12 flowers; drupes red; pyrenes partly or entirely concrescent

Leaf blades serrate, marcescent, conspicuously rugose-reticulate-veined, with winged petioles [Fig. ]; branchlets glabrous; inflorescence with 2 or 3 flowers [Fig. ]; drupes purple to purple-black; pyrenes distinct

c1.text: Winter buds covered by more than one scale; aments drooping; flowers subtended by a cup-like disk, without basal glands, each staminate flower with 5–80 stamens
Winter buds covered by 1 scale; aments erect to spreading [Figs. , ]; flowers not subtended by a disk, with 1–4 basal glands, each staminate flower with 1–8 stamens
Leaves stipulate, with pinnately lobed blades; bracts exceeding the fruit, persistent, forming an enclosing bur
Leaves exstipulate, the blades entire or toothed but without lobes [Fig. ]; bracts shorter than to equaling the fruit, not forming a bur

c2.text: Carpellate bracts 2, accrescent, clasping the achene in fruit; achene flattened, not concealed with a thick layer of wax; staminate aments borne at the apex of the previous year’s branchlet; leaf blades serrate in the distal ; winter buds dark brown, ovoid, acute at the apex; preformed staminate aments present

Carpellate bracts 4–6, small and inconspicuous, even in fruit; achene subglobose, covered with a thick layer of blue-white wax; staminate aments borne below the apex of the previous year’s branchlet; leaf blades variably serrate in the distal ; winter buds red, subglobose, obtuse at the apex; preformed staminate aments absent

c1.text: Nuts triangular in cross-section; pith terete or obscurely angled in cross-section; winter buds slender-fusiform, 8–19 mm long; bark smooth and light gray, even in age (unless roughened by cankers from disease); staminate flowers in dense, spherical clusters
Nuts terete or compressed; pith with 5 prominent points; winter buds ovoid to globose, up to 10 mm long; bark gray to brown, furrowed in age; staminate flowers in slender aments

c2.text: Carpellate flowers numbering 2–4 per involucre; involucre covered with spine-like bracts [Fig. ], enclosing 1–3 nuts at maturity; winter buds not clustered toward distal end of twig
Carpellate flowers 1 per involucre; involucre not appearing spiny, enclosing 1 nut at maturity; winter buds clustered toward distal end of twig [Fig. ]

c1.text: Leaf blades abaxially with black glands; mature stems with gray bark and slightly raised, longitudinal ridges; involucre a hastate-shaped, leaf-like bract; winter buds quadrangular in cross-section

Leaf blades without black glands (though resin or resin glands may be present); mature stems with smooth or exfoliating bark, variously colored (rarely uniformly gray), without longitudinal ridges; involucre a firm or woody scale, an enclosing husk, or an inflated, bladder-like bract; winter buds ± terete in cross-section

c2.text: Involucre an inflated, bladder-like bract, the carpellate inflorescence resembling a hop-like cluster; mature stems with gray-brown bark that exfoliates in vertical strips; winter bud scales conspicuously longitudinally striate

Involucre a husk or a flat scale, the carpellate inflorescence resemling a cluster of fruits, an ament, or a cone; mature stems with variously colored bark, but this not exfoliating in vertical strips (though sometimes exfoliating and curling in horizontal strips or patches); winter bud scales not, or scarcely, longitudinally striate

c3.text: Fruit a nut 10–15 mm long, enclosed in an husk-like involucre 15–70 mm long [Fig. ]; staminate flowers without perianth; anthers pilose at the tip
Fruit a samara 1.2–4.5 mm long, subtended by, but not enclosed in, flat scales 2.5–13 mm long; staminate flowers with a minute calyx; anthers glabrous

c4.text: Carpellate scales thin, decicuous with the fruit; androecium with 4 monothecal half-anthers; winter buds sessile; phyllotaxis
Carpellate scales thick, woody, long-persistent after the fruits are shed; androecium with 4 dithecal anthers; winter buds stalked (nearly sessile in A. viridis ); phyllotaxis

c1.text: This genus contains exactly one species.
Leaf blades simple or with a lateral lobe on one or both sides; inflorescence peduncled, a raceme or panicle, produced at the tips of the previous year’s branchlets; tepals accrescent; drupe blue
Leaf blades simple; inflorescence sessile, a pseudoumbel, produced in the axils along the previous year’s branchlets; tepals deciduous; drupe red
Leaf blades with 3 prominent veins from the base [Fig. ]; petals with an evident claw; fruit a dry, capsule-like drupe; inflorescence a terminal umbel composed of numerous flowers
Leaf blades pinnately veined; petals absent or present and with a short claw; fruit a fleshy drupe; inflorescence axillary, either a solitary flower or a few-flowered umbel

c2.text: Leaf blades with entire margins; winter buds naked; style undivided; flowers bisexual
Leaf blades with toothed margins; winter buds covered by scales; style divided for part of its length; flowers functionally unisexual

c1.text: Perianth 4- or 5-merous; sepals minute, deciduous in fruit; petals linear to linear-oblong, yellow-white, distinct; stamens free; leaves without stipules; branchlets and winter buds purple

Perianth 4- to 8-merous; sepals evident, persistent in fruit; petals obovate, white, connate at the base; stamens adnate to the corolla tube for a short distance; leaves with a stipular vestige on each side; branchlets and winter buds gray to brown

c2.text: Leaf blades thick, coriaceous, evergreen
Leaf blades thinner, herbaceous, deciduous

c3.text: Leaf blades with a spine-tip and often with 2 or more remote, spine-tipped teeth per margin, (30–) 50–100 mm long; carpellate flowers 4-merous; drupe red (rarely yellow), 7–10 mm thick
Leaf blades merely toothed, without spines [Fig. ], 15–50 mm long; carpellate flowers 6- to 8-merous (4-merous in I. crenata ); drupe black, 4–5 (–8) mm thick

c4.text: Leaf blades dull or barely sublustrous, with marginal spines that are +/- in plane with the leaf blade or slightly declined below the plane of the blade (i.e., usually not more than 30 degrees); flowers and fruits solitary or in solitary, peduncled cymes on the branchlets of the current season

Leaf blades highly lustrous, especially adaxially, with marginal spines that are oriented strongly above or below the plane of the blade (i.e., some usually more than 30 degrees); flowers and fruits usually clustered, produced from the axils on branches of the previous season

c5.text: Leaf blades with 1–3 teeth per margin [Fig. ], the teeth usually restricted to the apical of the blade; flowers 6- to 8-merous; drupe 4–5 mm thick
Leaf blades with (3–) 4–10 teeth per margin, the teeth usually not restricted to the apical portion of the blade; flowers 4-merous; drupe 6–8 mm thick

c6.text: Sepals eciliate [Fig. ]; staminate flowers on peduncles 8–16 mm long; drupe usually orange-red
Sepals ciliate (also sometimes pubescent on the abaxial surface) [Fig. ]; staminate flowers borne on peduncles 1–4 mm long; drupe usually deep red

c7.text: Carpellate flowers 4- or 5 (–6)-merous, with ciliate-margined petals [Fig. ]; pyrenes striate-ribbed on outer surface
Carpellate flowers 5- to 8-merous, with entire or inconspicuously erose-margined petals; pyrenes smooth on outer surface

c1.text: This genus contains exactly one species.
Flowers serotinous, appearing in late summer; samaras not winged; mature leaf blades 1.5–2.5 cm wide, with (4–) 5 or more lateral veins forking well before reaching margin per half of leaf

Flowers precocious, appearing in early spring; samaras winged; mature leaf blades 2–8 (–10) cm wide, when less than 3 cm wide then no more than 3 lateral veins forking well before reaching margin per half of leaf

c2.text: Mature leaf blades 2–3.5 cm wide, ± single serrate on the margin; samaras glabrous and eciliate
Mature leaf blades 2.5–8 (–10) cm wide, double serrate (at least in the distal half) [Fig. ]; samaras pubescent and/or ciliate (though the pubescence sometimes limited to a small region of the fruit)

c3.text: Lateral veins of leaf blade not forking until near the margin (rarely some leaf blades with 1 vein forking well before reaching margin) [Fig. ]; samara marginally ciliate through most or all of its margin
Usually 2 or more lateral veins of leaf blade forking well before reaching the margin [Figs. , ]; samaras eciliate or ciliate only near the apex (though pubescent on surface of body or wing)

c4.text: Inflorescence a dense fascicle usually shorter than 2.5 cm; samaras glabrous over the surface of body and wing; branches lacking irregular corky wings
Inflorescence a raceme-like cyme, up to 5 cm long; samaras pubescent over the surface of body and wing; branches often irregularly winged with 2 or more corky plates

c5.text: Leaf blades with marginal cilia; winter bud scales red, pubescent with red tomentum near the margins; samara pubescent on only the body

Leaf blades without marginal cilia; winter bud scales red-brown to brown or dark brown, with white or pale cilia near the margins; samara pubescent on only the central vein of wing or near apical margin

c6.text: Leaf blade with a strongly inequilateral base, with one side partially concealing the petiole, the apex sometimes with 3 acuminate lobes [Fig. ]; branches lacking corky wings; calyx with prominent lobes, the sinuses between them extending ca. half the distance to the base; samara elliptic to obovate, pubescent on central vein of wing, with the seed positioned near the middle

Leaf blade with a weakly to moderately inequilateral base, neither side concealing the petiole, the apex without additional lobes; branches often irregularly winged with 2 or more corky plates; calyx with short lobes, the sinuses between them extending much less than half the distance to the base; samara ± orbicular at maturity (narrower during development), pubescent near apical margin, with the seed positioned distal to middle

c1.text: Leaf blades with 2–10 lateral lobes (usually 4), the apex truncate to shallowly notched; tepals streaked with an orange band near the base; fruit an aggregate of samaras; winter buds with 2 scales

Leaf blades simple, the apex obtuse to acuminate; tepals without orange bands [Fig. ]; fruit an aggregate of follicles, the seed with a brightly colored aril suspended from the dehisced fruit by the slender funiculus; winter buds with 1 scale

Sepals well-developed, spreading, petaloid; hypanthium pubescent; stamens and style included within the perianth; flowers white to pink to purple; drupes 6–10 mm long; leaf blades narrow-oblanceolate to oblong

Sepals minute, represented by tiny lobes at the summit of the tubular hypanthium [Fig. ]; hypanthium glabrous; stamens and style exserted beyond the perianth [Fig. ]; flowers yellow; drupes 12–15 mm long; leaf blades ovate to broad-oblong-obovate or obovate
This genus contains exactly one species.
This genus contains exactly one species.
Inflorescence a raceme, with (3–) 4–20 or more flowers [Figs. , ]; pedicels articulated at the summit, the fruits falling from them; branchlets unarmed (armed in R. lacustre )

Inflorescence a solitary flower or a corymb-like cluster of 2–4 (–5) flowers [Fig. ]; pedicels not articulated at the summit, the fruits remaining on them; branchlets often armed with slender prickles and/or bristles, especially at the nodes

c2.text: Ovary and fruit pubescent with bristly, gland-tipped hairs [Fig. ]
Ovary and fruit glabrous or with sessile, resinous glands [Fig. ]

c3.text: Stems with thin prickles; racemes spreading to drooping; petals broad-flabellate to orbicular; berries purple or black
Stems unarmed; racemes ascending to erect [Fig. ]; petals cuneate-obovate; berries dark red

c4.text: Hypanthium above the ovary tubular, 9–15 mm long; sepals gold-yellow; mature leaf blades 20–35 (–50) mm long, each lobe with 0–3 (–7) apical teeth

Hypanthium above the ovary campanulate or scutelliform, up to 4.5 mm long; sepals green-purple or green-white to yellow; mature leaf blades (25–) 30–90 mm long, abundantly toothed, the teeth not restricted to the apical portion of the lobe

c5.text: Leaf blades, winter buds, and branchlet apices resin-dotted [Fig. ]; berries black; hypanthium above the ovary cupuliform
Leaf blades, winter buds, and branchlet apices without resin glands; berries red (rarely translucent white in R. rubrum ); hypanthium above the ovary scutelliform

c6.text: Pedicels 0.1–2 mm long, much exceeded by the conspicuous, lanceolate bracts [Fig. ]; racemes with 6–15 flowers; calyx lobes glabrous or very sparsely pubescent on the abaxial surface; ovary without resin glands; branchles with prominent decurrent ridges extending from the nodes that are noticeably raised above the branch surface, without a fetid odor when bruised

Pedicels 2–8 mm long, much longer than the minute, ovate bracts; racemes with 4–10 flowers; calyx lobes pubescent on the abaxial surface; ovary with at least a few sessile resin glands; branchles with obscure decurrent ridges that are barely raised above the branch surface, with a fetid odor when bruised

c7.text: Axis of raceme and pedicels stipitate-glandular; anther sacs adjacent to one another; lateral leaf lobes commonly directed forward; terminal leaf lobe deltate; calyx lobes green-purple; stems straggling to ascending

Axis of raceme and pedicels without glands; anther sacs widely separated by a broad connective; lateral leaf lobes spreading; terminal leaf lobe ovate; calyx lobes yellow to green; stems ascending to erect

c8.text: Berry covered with slender prickles at maturity, these appearing as stalked glands on the ovary during flowering [Fig. ]; tubular portion of the hypanthium above the ovary longer than the calyx lobes in most flowers [Fig. ]

Berry glabrous, glandular, or bristly, but without prickles, the ovary not stipitate-glandular during flowering (except usually in R. uva-crispa ); tubular portion of the hypanthium above the ovary equaling or shorter than the calyx lobes

c9.text: Flowers in anthesis with stamens evidently longer than the sepals; peduncles 5–20 mm long; styles 7–14 mm long
Flowers in anthesis with stamens shorter than to barely longer than the sepals; peduncles 2–6 mm long; styles 2.5–8 mm long

c10.text: Stamens 6–8 mm long; hypanthium purple to green-purple; calyx lobes 4–5 mm long; nodal prickles 2–5 (–11) mm long
Stamens 9–12 mm long; hypanthium white to cream-white; calyx lobes 5–7.5 mm long; nodal prickles 7–17 mm long

c11.text: Hypanthium, sepals, and berry pubescent (often also with some gland-tipped bristles); sepals 5–7 mm long, round-obovate; nodal prickles stout, 10–15 mm long
Hypanthium, sepals, and fruit glabrous (rarely the hypanthium and fruit sparsely pubescent); sepals 3–4 mm long, oblong to broad-oblong; nodal prickles slender, 3–8 mm long

c1.text: Plants woody, with stipular spines [Fig. ]; perianth yellow
Plants herbaceous, without spines; perianth white to pink or green-yellow, green-purple, purple, or purple-brown (rarely yellow)

c2.text: Perianth 4-merous; leaves pinnately compound with (2–) 9 leaflets that are asymmetrically cordate at the base; inflorescence a raceme or panicle

Perianth 5- to 9-merous [Fig. ]; leaves palmately lobed or pinnately compound and then with leaflets that are cuneate, rounded, or truncate at the base (sometimes asymmetrically so); inflorescence a solitary flower or cyme

c3.text: Leaf blades lobed, the basal ones peltate; inflorescence a solitary flower; perianth white or pink; anthers dehiscing by longitudinal slits; ovary maturing as a berry

Leaf blades 2–4 times pinnately compound, basifixed to the petioles; inflorescence a cyme; perianth green-yellow, green-purple, purple, or purple-brown (rarely yellow); anthers dehiscing by uplifting valves; ovary ruptured by the 2 enlarging seeds, the stalked, blue seeds ripening fully exposed

c1.text: Petaliferous flowers with 3 inconspicuous, red petals; petals flat in bud; plants overwintering by a basal rosette of crowded, leafy branches
Petaliferous flowers with 5 conspicuous, yellow petals; petals wrinkled in bud; plants lacking a basal rosette of crowded branches

c2.text: Leaf blades narrow-oblong to elliptic or elliptic-oblanceolate [Figs. , ], 20–30 (–40) mm long, widest near or above the middle, not imbricate; plants erect to ascending (with horizontal branches in 1 species), not forming mats, with stellate pubescence on the stem; style very short, not over 1 mm long; flowers of 2 types—chasmogamous flowers with large, conspicuous petals and cleistogamous flowers with reduced petals or lacking petals altogether

Leaf blades linear-subulate or narrow-ovate to triangular, 1–6 mm long, widest below the middle, densely imbricate; plants diffusely branched, forming low mats and mounds, with simple pubescence on the stem; style ca. 2 mm long; flowers of 1 type—all chasmogamous, with conspicuous petals

c1.text: This genus contains exactly one species.
This genus contains exactly one species.
Ovary and fruit evidently prickly with narrow prickles [Figs. , ]; petals shorter than 1 cm; fruit 1.3–6 cm long
Ovary and fruit smooth, verrucose, or with small prickles in longitudinal stripes; petals 1 cm long or longer; fruit 4–60 (–90) cm long

c2.text: Petals yellow; fruit fleshy, with many seeds; leaf blades with deep, rounded sinuses (in part)
Petals white to green-white or green; fruit not fleshy, with 1 or 4 seeds; leaf blades with shallow sinuses or with moderately deep, V-shaped sinuses

c3.text: Fruit inflated, 4-seeded, 3–5 cm long, solitary [Fig. ], dehiscent by 2 apical pores; staminate corolla 6-merous; herbage glabrous or nearly so
Fruit not inflated, 1-seeded, 1.3–1.5 cm long, in clusters of 3–10 [Fig. ], indehiscent; staminate corolla 5-merous; herbage conspicuously pubescent

c4.text: Staminate pedicels with a reniform to orbicular, foliaceous bract; fruits bluntly verrucose, splitting at maturity to reveal seeds with bright red arils
Staminate pedicels ebracteate; fruits smooth or with small prickles in longitudinal strips, not dehiscent, the seeds without red arils

c5.text: Petals white; corolla rotate; fruit woody when mature
Petals yellow to orange-yellow; corolla campanulate, open-campanulate, or rotate; fruit fleshy when mature

c6.text: Leaf blades pinnately lobed, the segments ± round at the apex; fruit exocarp green with irregular white or green-white stripes, the mesocarp red
Leaf blades simple or palmately lobed and then with angular or pointed segments; fruit exocarp green, blue, or orange, the mesocarp white, yellow, orange, tan, or green

c7.text: Petals 5–10 cm long; anthers connivent; tendrils branched one or more times
Petals 1–3 cm long; anthers separate; tendrils simple

c8.text: Corolla campanulate, the free portion of the petals connate ca. their length; ovary and fruit short-pubescent; leaf blade irregularly dentate, but not lobed

Corolla open-campanulate, the free portion of the petals connate less than their length; ovary and fruit spiny or roughened in longitudinal bands, but not pubescent (except in C. melo ); leaf blades prominently to obscurely lobed (in part)

c1.text: Perianth 3-merous; flowers with 3 stamens and 3 carpels; leaves alternate, the blades of the emersed ones foliaceous
Perianth 4-merous; flowers with 4 or 8 stamens and 4 carpels; leaves opposite or alternate or both on the same plant, the blades of the emersed ones commonly reduced and bract-like
Leaves 6–12 at each node, with entire blades; flowers with a single stamen borne at the summit of the ovary; calyx a minute rim around the apex of the ovary

Leaves 1 or 2 at each node (but crowded in the apical portion in Callitriche ) or all basal, entire or toothed (in whorls of 3–6 in Veronicastrum , but then with serrate blades); flowers with 1–5 stamens, these not borne at the summit of the ovary; calyx absent or present and borne near the base of the ovary

c2.text: Perianth absent; plants aquatic, with opposite leaves that are often crowded in the apical portion and forming a floating rosette [Fig. ]
Perianth present; plants terrestrial (aquatic in Littorella ); leaves not forming a floating rosette near the apex of the stem

c3.text: Perianth inconspicuous, 3- or 4-merous, with an actinomorphic, scarious corolla [Figs. , , ]; leaves all basal (opposite and borne on a stem in P. arenaria ) [Fig. ]
Perianth conspicuous and showy, with a zygomorphic, 5-merous corolla (appearing 4-merous in Veronica and Veronicastrum [Figs. , , ]; leaves borne on a stem

c4.text: Scape 1- to 3-flowered [Fig. ]; fruit an achene, 1-locular, 1-seeded; plants aquatic, with slender stolons
Scape many-flowered; fruit usually a pyxis, 2- or 3-locular, 2- to many-seeded; plants terrestrial or of tidal wetlands, without stolons

c5.text: Corolla with a slender, basal spur or a saccate swelling protruding between the 2 lower calyx lobes, and with a palate [Figs. , ]; foliage leaves usually alternate (sometimes the lower opposite, especially in Antirrhinum and Chaenorhinum )
Corolla lacking a slender, basal spur, without a palate except in Chelone and 1 species of Penstemon ; foliage leaves opposite or whorled (alternate in Digitalis )

c6.text: Corolla with a saccate (i.e., pouch-like) swelling on the lower side; plants both with flowers arranged in a terminal raceme and with capsules dehiscing by terminal pores

Corolla with a slender, basal spur [Figs. , ]; plants either with flowers in terminal racemes (but then with capsules opening by terminal slits) or with capsules dehiscing by apical pores (but then with solitary flowers in the axils of leaves)

c7.text: Calyx lobes ± subequal, shorter than the basal, connate portion of the corolla; corolla 25–45 mm long; plants 40–80 (–120) cm tall, perennial
Calyx lobes unequal, all longer than the basal, connate portion of the corolla; corolla 10–15 mm long; plants (5–) 20–50 cm tall, annual

c8.text: Inflorescence a terminal raceme; capsules dehiscing by terminal slits; seeds with angular faces
Inflorescence a solitary flower in the axils of leaves; capsules dehiscing by 2 terminal pores (the pores eventually extending to the capsule base in Cymbalaria ); seeds ellipsoid to ovoid

c9.text: Palate composed of 2 short, white ridges; seeds both ± smooth on the faces and wingless
Palate composed of a single, usually yellow or orange, ridge; seeds either with rugose or reticulate patterning or with wings or wing-like angles

c10.text: Stems upright; capsules pubescent, asymmetrical, one locule larger than the other
Stems prostrate; capsules glabrous, symmetrical, both locules of ± equal size

c11.text: Leaf blades palmately veined, with 5–9 tooth-like lobes; stems rooting at the nodes in contact with the soil
Leaf blades pinnately veined, entire (rarely the lower minutely denticulate); stems not rooting at the nodes

c12.text: Foliage leaves alternate; inflorescence a secund raceme [Fig. ]
Foliage leaves opposite or whorled; inflorescence various, but not a secund raceme

c13.text: Androecium composed of 5 stamens—4 pollen-bearing stamens and 1 sterile stamen
Androecium composed of 2 or 4 stamens—all pollen bearing or 2 of the 4 composed of filaments only

c14.text: Corolla subgaleate; sepals subtended by bractlets; sterile stamen shorter than the pollen-bearing stamens; seeds winged
Corolla without a galea [Figs. , ]; sepals not subtended by bractlets; sterile stamen nearly equal in length to the pollen-bearing stamens; seeds without wings

c15.text: Corolla apparently composed of 4 lobes due to fusion of the upper 2 petals [Fig. ]; calyx composed of 4 sepals (5 sepals in Veronica officinalis ); inflorescence a spike or raceme (the bracteal leaves ± similar to the foliage leaves in some Veronica , but then usually alternately arranged) [Figs. , , ]

Corolla composed of 2 lips—the upper lip 2-lobed, the lower lip 3-lobed [Fig. ]; calyx composed of 5 sepals; inflorescence of solitary or whorled flowers in the axils of oppositely arranged foliage leaves [Fig. ]

c16.text: Leaves opposite, sometimes the upper alternate (rarely some whorled in V. longifolia and V. spuria ); lobes of the corolla longer than the basal tube; capsules, before dehiscence, emarginate or lobed at the apex
Leaves mostly in whorls of 3–7; lobes of the corolla shorter than the basal tube; capsules, before dehiscence, tapering to the apex, not lobed

c17.text: Sepals evidently connate in the basal portion; corolla 4–6 mm long, the lower lip blue, the middle lobe of the lower corolla lip declined below the lateral lobes and enfolding the 4 pollen-bearing stamens

Sepals distinct nearly or quite to the base [Fig. ]; corolla 5–16 mm long, the lower lip yellow, white, or yellow and white, the middle lobe of the lower corolla lip neither conspicuously declined below the lateral lobes nor enfolding the 2 pollen-bearing stamens [Fig. ]

c1.text: Flowers borne in axillary cymes, lacking a hypanthium, usually in groups of 2–4, the lateral flowers functionally staminate and deciduous, the central flower bisexual; tepals green-purple
Flowers borne in terminal, panicle-like cymes, with a hypanthium, all bisexual; tepals white
This genus contains exactly one species.
Leaf blades compound, with 3 leaflets, emersed [Fig. ]; petals pubescent on the adaxial surface [Fig. ], lacking glands; inflorescence a raceme or panicle
Leaf blades simple, floating [Fig. ]; petals glabrous on the adaxial surface [Fig. ], bearing a yellow gland near the base of each lobe; inflorescence an umbel
Perianth 2-merous [Fig. ]; fruit indehiscent, covered with uncinate bristles; leaves opposite; petals white
Perianth 4- to 6-merous; fruit dehiscent (indehiscent in some Oenothera ), without uncinate bristles; leaves opposite or alternate; petals absent, or white to pink to purple, or yellow

c2.text: Sepals persistent in fruit; androecium with 4 stamens; hypanthium not prolonged beyond the summit of the ovary
Sepals deciduous in fruit; androecium with 8 stamens; hypanthium prolonged beyond the summit of the ovary (except in Chamerion )

c3.text: Flowers zygomorphic, the petals all oriented toward one side of the flower [Fig. ]; fruit indehiscent, with 2–6 seeds 1.5–3.5 mm long (in part)
Flowers actinomorphic [Fig. ]; fruit dehiscent, with many seeds 0.3–2 mm long

c4.text: Seeds comose; leaves opposite (especially the lower ones) or alternate throughout in Chamerion ; hypanthium not, or only shortly, extending beyond the ovary; petals white to pink to pink-purple
Seeds not comose; leaves alternate; hypanthium extending beyond the summit of the ovary; petals yellow (sometimes fading to red) or pink to light purple or red-purple (rarely white) in Clarkia

c5.text: Hypanthium shortly extending beyond the summit of the ovary; petals 2–16 mm long, notched at the apex; stamens in 2 series, erect to ascending; stigma unlobed or with 4 lobes; new shoots produced from turions, rosettes, or sobols

Hypanthium not extending beyond the summit of the ovary; petals 10–20 mm long, ± entire at the apex; stamens in 1 series, declined; stigma with 4 conspicuous lobes; new shoots produced from lateral roots (or sometimes by sobols)

c6.text: Petals pink to light purple or red-purple (rarely white), with a pair of small lobes or recurved teeth on the claw; anthers basifixed
Petals yellow (sometimes fading to red), lacking lobes or teeth on the claw; anthers mesifixed (i.e., versatile)

c7.text: Petals with 1 or 2 red dots near the base; stigma capitate or hemispherical
Petals without basal red dots; stigma with 4 lobes (caution: the lobes short in O. serrulata ) (in part)

c1.text: This genus contains exactly one species.
Calyx lobes white or pink to purple adaxially, with small, horn-like, subterminal appendages; leaves opposite, the blades 1–2.5 (–3) ×0.1–0.5 cm, linear to spatulate or ovate, and cuneate at the base
Calyx lobes yellow adaxially, without subapical appendages; leaves alternate, the blades (0.4–) 1–10 ×2.5–8 cm, ovate-rhombic to triangular, and broad-cuneate to truncate at the base
Corolla zygomorphic [Figs. , ]; stamens connate
Corolla actinomorphic [Figs. , ]; stamens distinct or connate only at base

c2.text: Flowers and fruits solitary, sessile or subsessile in the axils of leaves [Fig. ]; capsules slender-cylindric; plants annual
Flowers and fruits solitary or borne in a spike, raceme, or glomerule, sessile or pedicellate [Figs. , , ]; capsules globose or ovoid to obovoid or obconic; plants perennial

c3.text: Corolla slenderly tubular, cleft into 5 lobes; anthers connate at base; capsule dehiscing by 2 apical valves; inflorescence a dense, capitulum-like umbel that is subtended by a foliaceous involucre [Fig. ]

Corolla ± campanulate (narrow-campanulate in one species of Campanula ); anthers distinct; capsule dehiscing by basal, lateral, or subapical pores; inflorescence open and not congested (congested in Campanula glomerata )

c4.text: Inflorescence a terminal panicle of primarily erect to ascending flowers [Fig. ]
Inflorescece of solitary pedicellate flowers, or of sessile glomerulate flowers, or a spike or raceme, the flowers spreading to nodding or erect [Figs. , , ]

c1.text: This genus contains exactly one species.
Leaves opposite [Figs. , ]; flowers with 3 or 5 stamens
Leaves alternate; flowers with 3–15 stamens

c2.text: Plants perennial, from a corm (annual from a minute tuber-like body in 1 species); stems with 2 leaves; leaf blades 30–200 mm long; petals 9–15 mm long; androecium with 5 stamens; capsules with 3–6 seeds
Plants annual; stems with many leaves; leaf blades 3–20 mm long; petals 1–2 mm long; androecium with 3 stamens; capsules with 1–3 seeds (in part)

c3.text: Flowers sessile or subsessile; gynoecium with 4–8 stigmas; fruit a pyxis; ovary partly inferior
Flowers pedicellate; gynoecium with 3 stigmas; fruit a capsule; ovary superior

c4.text: Petals red, 4–15 mm long; androecium with 3–15 stamens; capsules with 10–20 seeds
Petals white to pale pink, 4–6.5 mm long; androecium with 3 stamens; capsules with 1–3 seeds (in part)

c1.text: Leaves simple, with a viscid adaxial surface, without traps [Fig. ]; flowers solitary [Fig. ], without bracts; calyx with 5 lobes; plants terrestrial, of wet cliffs and gullies

Leaf-like branches simple to highly dissected, not viscid, bearing bladder-like traps on the divisions or on separate branches [Figs. , ]; flowers solitary or borne in racemes, each subtended by a bract; calyx with 2 lobes; plants aquatic or of wetlands
This genus contains exactly one species.
Leaves opposite or whorled, the blades sharply serrate; petioles provided with large, dark glands; Perianth blue or purple to pink or white; capsule obovoid

Leaves alternate, the blades crenate-serrate; petioles lacking glands or infrequently with slender, dark glands near the apex at the junction of the blade; corolla orange-yellow or pale yellow; capsule slender-clavate in outline

c2.text: Perianth orange-yellow (rarely bright yellow, pink, or white), spotted with red-brown (rarely unspotted); spur 7–10 mm long, strongly curved, projecting forward; saccate portion of the spurred sepal longer than wide

Perianth pale yellow (rarely yellow-white or white), sparingly dotted with red-brown; spur 4–6 mm long, curved at a right angle, not projecting forward [Fig. ]; saccate portion of the spurred sepal wider than long

c1.text: Perianth zygomorphic, spurred or saccate at the base [Figs. , , ]; plants with a watery latex; petals not crumpled in bud; stamens 6 per flower, the filaments diadelphous; leaf blades finely divided into narrow segments [Fig. ]

Perianth actinomorphic, without a nectary spur [Figs. , ]; plants with a milky or colored latex (watery in Eschscholzia ); petals often crumpled in bud (therefore, wrinkled on expansion); stamens ca. 16–100 or more per flower, the filaments distinct; leaf blades lobed to 1.5 times divided (finely divided in Eschscholzia )

c2.text: The 2 outer petals dissimilar, only 1 of which is spurred; flowers borne laterally on the pedicels [Fig. ]
The 2 outer petals similar and spurred (but the spurs short in Adlumia ) [Figs. , ]; flowers borne on pendulous pedicels [Figs. , ]

c3.text: Ovary narrow-cylindric; flowers 7–25 (–30) mm long; fruit dehiscent, (14–) 16–45 (–50) mm long, with more than 1 seed, with a persistent style; seed with an aril
Ovary subglobose; flowers 6–9 mm long; fruit indehiscent, 2.5–3 mm long, 1-seeded, with a deciduous style; seed without an aril

c4.text: Corolla pink to pink-purple with a yellow apex; inflorescence a panicle-like cyme, with minute, pale green bracts 1–2 mm long; capsules erect to ascending, 25–45 (–50) mm long [Fig. ]

Corolla pale yellow, bright yellow, or purple (rarely white, pink, red, or blue-purple); inflorescence a raceme, with conspicuous, usually foliaceous bracts 3–8 mm long; capsules spreading to drooping, (14–) 16–25 (–30) mm long

c5.text: Plants climbing by means of tendril-like, reduced leaflets and their petiolules; corolla connate, except at the very apex, persistent, becoming spongy, enclosing the capsule
Plants not climbing; corolla connate only at the base, deciduous

c6.text: Stems scapose (i.e., without leaves); corolla 10–25 mm long, the inner petals of ± similar color as the outer petals; stems arising from bulbs or from a scaly rhizome
Stems leafy; corolla 30–50 mm long, the inner petals of different color from the outer petals (except in white-flowered forms); stems arising from a rhizome

c7.text: Leaves 1, basal, the blade ± orbicular in outline [Fig. ]; corolla with 8–12 petals [Fig. ]; latex red
Leaves several to many, borne on a stem, the blade not orbicular in outline [Fig. ]; corolla with 0 or 4–6 petals [Fig. ]; latex yellow or white

c8.text: Foliage spiny; capsules prickly; flowers with (2–) 3 sepals and (4–) 6 petals
Foliage without spines; capsules unarmed; flowers with 2 sepals and 0 or 4 petals

c9.text: Sepals connate, shed together in flower; gynoecium with 4–8 distinct, linear stigmas; leaf blades finely pinnately or palmately divided into narrow segments; latex watery
Sepals distinct, shed separately in flower; stigmas either 2-lobed or connate and forming a 4- to 18-lobed disk; leaf blades lobed to 1.5 times divided; latex white or colored

c10.text: Petals variously colored, but never yellow; stigmas forming a 4- to 18-lobed disk; capsules dehiscing by 4–18 subapical pores; latex white
Petals absent or present and yellow to orange-yellow; stigmas 2-lobed; capsules with 2–4 valves that dehisce to the base; latex yellow or orange-yellow

c11.text: Flowers solitary on short peduncles, with petals 20–30 mm long; fruit 15–30 cm long at maturity
Flowers arranged in umbels or panicles, without petals or with petals 4–12 mm long; fruit 0.8–5 cm long at maturity

c12.text: Corolla present, of 4 yellow petals; sepals sepaloid, green; leaf blades pinnately divided, the leaflets again lobed; flowers few, in an umbel
Corolla absent; sepals petaloid, ± white; leaf blades pinnately lobed; flowers numerous, in a large panicle

c1.text: Sepals lacking basal auricles; corolla green-white; stamens connate, forming a sheath that surrounds the carpels, none of them appendaged; leafy-stemmed plants 30–90 (–100) cm tall [Fig. ]

Sepals with basal auricles; corolla white, yellow, blue to purple, or multicolored (but not green-white); stamens connivent but not fused, the two lower ones with appendages that are prolonged backwards into the nectary spur; scapose or leafy-stemmed plants 2–45 cm tall [Figs. , , ]
Leaf blades entire (rarely with a few, minute, hyaline teeth near the base)
Leaf blades lobed or dissected

c2.text: Pedicels 1–3 mm long; corolla with 4 petals, each petal either entire or with 4 short lobes; capsules 3–4 mm long
Pedicels 4–6 mm long (elongating to 16 mm in fruit); corolla with 6 petals, each petal divided at the apex into 9–15 linear-spatulate segments; capsules 9–11 mm long (in part)

c3.text: Petals green-white; filaments persistent until maturation of fruit; gynoecium with 4 carpels; capsules with 4 apical teeth
Petals green to green-yellow or yellow; filaments deciduous before maturation of fruit; gynoecium with 3 carpels; capsules with 3 apical teeth

c4.text: Petals apically entire or with 2 or 3 linear-spathulate segments [Fig. ]; capsules 4.5–5.5 mm wide; seeds lustrous, smooth; most leaf blades pinnatifid with 1 or 2 (–4) pairs of lobes
Petals divided at the apex into 9–15 linear-spathulate segments; capsules 7–11 mm wide; seeds dull, undulate-rugose; leaf blades entire or sometimes the upper ones with 2 or 3 lobes (in part)

c1.text: Petals retuse at the apex (sometimes merely truncate); flowers with (6–) 10–27 stamens; fruit elevated on a gynophore 0–2 (–6) mm long
Petals entire at the apex; flowers with 6 stamens; fruit elevated on a gynophore 1–80 (–152) mm long

c2.text: Principal leaves with 5–7 leaflets and a pair of short spines at the base of the petioles; stem viscid-pubescent; petals 20–30 (–45) mm long, all oriented toward one side of the flower; gynophores 45–80 (–152) mm long in fruit
Leaves with 3 leaflets and unarmed petioles; stem glabrous (sparsely villous when young); petals 7–12 mm long, nearly evenly distributed around the flower; gynophores 1–15 (–20) mm long in fruit

c1.text: Leaves few, clustered near the tip of the stem, the blades elliptic to oval; inflorescence with 1–4 flowers that are 13–19 mm long; androecium with 6 stamens; plants perennial from creeping rhizomes

Leaves usually many and spaced throughout the stem, the blades linear to narrow-elliptic or narrow-obovate; inflorescence with many flowers that are 3–6 mm long; androecium with 7 or 8 stamens; plants annual, biennial, or perennial, but without creeping rhizomes

c2.text: Chasmogamous (i.e., petaliferous) flowers borne in loose racemes, on spreading or recurving pedicels 1.5–3.5 mm long [Fig. ]; cleistogamous flowers produced after the chasmogamous flowers, borne on secund, prostrate or shallowly subterranean racemes
Chasmogamous flowers borne in relatively more dense, spike-like racemes, the pedicels up to 1.5 mm long; cleistogamous flowers not produced

c3.text: Plants perennial, with clustered stems arising from a hard, knotty root; leaf blades (13–) 30–80 ×3–15 (–30) mm, irregularly serrulate
Plants annual, the solitary stems arising from a taproot; leaf blades 10–40 × 1–5 mm, entire

c4.text: Wing sepals acuminate to awn-tipped at the apex [Fig. ], minutely roughened on the adaxial surface; raceme 10–15 (–20) mm thick [Fig. ]
Wing sepals rounded to obtuse at the apex, not roughened on the adaxial surface; raceme 2–10 (–14) mm thick [Fig. ]

c5.text: Leaves 1 at each node; wing sepals 2–5 (–6.3) mm long; racemes blunt at the apex (sometimes apiculate in P. nuttallii due to the flower buds); bracts persistent, each appearing as a minute, upcurved hook, remaining on the raceme axis after the falling of the fruits

Leaves 2–5 at each of the lower nodes (sometimes the upper nodes with only 1 leaf) [Fig. ]; wing sepals 0.9–2.6 mm long; racemes tapering to a slender point; bracts deciduous from the base of the fruiting raceme, the fallen fruits leaving only a pedicel scar

c6.text: Wing sepals 3–5 (–6.3) mm long; ca. 2 times as long as the corolla; racemes 6–10 (–14) mm thick
Wing sepals 2–2.5 mm long, ± as long as the corolla; racemes 4–6 mm thick

c7.text: Wing sepals usually to as long as fruit [Fig. ]; most nodes (except sometimes the upper) bearing 2–5 leaves; flowers white to pink to purple; axis of raceme not or scarcely elongating in fruit, the lowest internode 0.3–1.7 (–3.3) mm long

Wing sepals ± as long as the fruit; most nodes (except the lower ones) bearing a single leaf; flowers predominantly green-white to white; axis of raceme elongating in fruit, the lowest internode (1.2–) 2.3–8.4 mm long

c1.text: Each carpel of the ovary with 2–many ovules; fruit a 2-valved capsule with 1–80 seeds; at least the lower leaf blades lobed or compound (entire to coarsely toothed in some Phacelia )
Each carpel of the ovary with 2 ovules; fruit a schizocarp separating into (1–) 4 mericarps; leaf blades simple and mostly entire

c2.text: Flowers solitary in the axils of opposite the leaves; at least the lower leaves opposite; corolla 5–8 mm long, ± equaled or exceeded by the calyx
Flowers arranged in helicoid cymes or subdichotomously branched cymes; leaves alternate; corolla 7–12 mm long, exceeding the calyx

c3.text: Inflorescence a subdichotomously branched cyme, lacking an elongate central axis; plants from fibrous roots
Inflorescence a helicoid cyme, with 1 or more elongate, sympodial axes; plants from taproots

c4.text: Ovary unlobed or inconspicuously lobed; style terminating the summit of the ovary; stigma peltate-annular, surmounted by a cone-like process
Ovary with deep sinuses, appearing as 4 ± distinct carpels; style arising from between the lobes; stigma not peltate-annular

c5.text: Corolla rotate [Fig. ]; anthers 5–9 mm long, with conspicuous linear appendages ca. 3 mm long
Corolla tubular, funnelform, or salverform [Figs. , , ]; anthers shorter, without appendages

c6.text: Corolla weakly zygomorphic [Fig. ], the tubular, connate portion sometimes also bent
Corolla actinomorphic [Figs. , , ], the tubular portion straight

c7.text: Apex of corolla tube lacking fornices, the tube appearing open; stamens exserted beyond the corolla; mericarps without a stipe-like process, attaching directly to the receptacle; receptacle flat, without a pit

Apex of corolla tube with fornices, these appearing to close off the tube; stamens included within the corolla tube; mericarps attached to the receptacle by a stipe-like process, this fitting into a pit in the receptacle (in part)

c8.text: Ovary and mericarps with barbed prickles, at least on the marginal or abaxial surfaces [Figs. , ]
Ovary and mericarps smooth or textured, sometimes muricate, but never with barbed prickles

c9.text: Plants annual; each flower closely subtended by a bract
Plants biennial or perennial; all or most of the flowers without closely associated bracts

c10.text: Corolla 5–8 mm wide; mericarps attached to one another by the apical third of their inner faces; mericarps 3.5–5 mm long
Corolla 2–3 mm wide; mericarps attached to one another along the middle third of their inner faces; mericarps 2–3 mm long

c11.text: Stems retrorsely prickly hispid [Fig. ], weak and scrambling; inflorescence axillary, of 1–3 flowers borne on short, recurved pedicels; calyx accrescent in fruit, becoming 10–20 mm wide, compressed, firm, and evidently reticulate-veiny, with dentate margins

Stems glabrous to hispid-pubescent, but not retrorsely prickly hispid, weak and sprawling to rigid and erect; inflorescence of 1 or more helicoid cymes or consisting of crowded flowers in the upper leaf axils in Lithospermum and Buglossoides ; calyx not notably accrescent in fruit, ± circular in cross-section, not or scarcely veiny, with entire margins

c12.text: Corolla yellow to orange, the apex of the tube without fornices (though the tube obstructed by pubescent bulges near the orifice in Amsinckia lycopsoides )

Corolla white, yellow-white, pink, red-purple, blue, purple, or brown (pale yellow in Symphytum tuberosum , with a yellow center in some Myosotis ), the apex of the tube with fornices (lacking fornices in Buglossoides arvensis and Mertensia virginica )

c13.text: Corolla salverform, with wide-spreading, rounded to obtuse lobes [Fig. ]; style included within tubular portion of corolla [Fig. ]
Corolla ± tubular, with erect, acuminate lobes [Fig. ]; style evidently exserted from the corolla [Fig. ]

c14.text: Lower 1–4 nodes of the stem producing opposite leaves
Stem leaves all alternate

c15.text: Mericarp attachment scar grooved on inner median surface, the groove flaring open or forking at the base of the mericap, without a raised keel apical to the attachment scar; basal leaves usually present during early flowering (these early deciduous)
Mericarp with a raised attachment scar on the inner median surface, with a raised keel apical to the attachment scar; basal leaves absent, all leaves borne on the stem

c16.text: Corolla tubular or narrow-funnelform, the lobes erect to ascending [Figs. , ]
Corolla salverform or funnelform, the lobes spreading [Figs. , ]

c17.text: Leaf blades conspicuously white-spotted; stems with stipitate glands; tube of corolla obstructed by 5 tufts of hairs
Leaf blades without white spots; stems lacking stipitate glands; tube of corolla obstructed by 5 scales or lacking fornices altogether (with hairs at the base of the corolla tube in Nonea )

c18.text: Leaf blades and stems glabrous; mericarps without a stipe-like process, attaching directly to the receptacle; receptacle flat, without a pit
Leaf blades and stems hispid-hirsute; mericarps attached to the receptacle by a stipe-like process, this fitting into a pit in the receptacle

c19.text: Style exserted beyond the corolla; fornices present
Style not exserted beyond the corolla; fornices absent, the tube of the corolla obstructed by tufts of hairs

c20.text: Flowers, except sometimes the lower, not subtended by bracts; corolla lobes convolute in bud (i.e., arranged so that one margin is exposed and the other margin covered by the adjacent petal); mericarps smooth

Flowers all or mostly all subtended by bracts; corolla lobes imbricate in bud (i.e., arranged so that the outer members have both margins exposed, the inner members have both margins covered); mericarps wrinkled or pitted, or smooth in Lithospermum

c21.text: Limb of the corolla 7–15 mm wide; mericarps attached to the receptacle by a stipe-like process, this fitting into a pit in the receptacle (in part)
Limb of the corolla up to 4 mm wide; mericarps without a stipe-like process, attaching directly to the receptacle; receptacle flat, without a pit

c22.text: Plants perennial; corolla 4–5 mm long; leaves with 2 or 3 conspicuous, lateral veins; mericarps lustrous, white to white-brown, smooth
Plants annual (rarely biennial); corolla 5–8 mm long; leaves without conspicuous, lateral veins; mericarps dull brown, wrinkled and pitted or roughened

c1.text: Calyx usually more than twice as long as the mature fruit, the portion extending beyond the fruit often contorted; style more than 3 times as long as the ovary; sterile style lobe protruding beyond stigmatic surface; connective of upper pair of anthers usually with a glandular appendage; schizocarps black; limb of corolla 11–24 mm wide

Calyx usually less than twice as long as the mature fruit, the portion extending beyond the fruit usually not contorted; style less than 3 times as long as the ovary; sterile style lobe not protruding beyond stigmatic surface; connective of anthers without appendages; schizocarps red-brown; limb of corolla 2–7 mm wide

Plants aquatic, without aerial stems, forming colonies by slender stolons in submersed populations (annuals in emersed plants); flowers 1–3 mm wide; androecium with 2 stamens; leaf blades narrower than 2 mm

Plants terrestrial or aquatic, with aerial stems, not colonial (forming terrestrial colonies by creeping stems in Mazus miquelii ); flowers wider than 3 mm; androecium with 4 stamens; leaf blades much wider than 2 mm

c2.text: Inflorescence a spike-like raceme, the pedicels very short [Fig. ]; fruit an achene
Inflorescence a raceme or of solitary flowers from the axils of foliage leaves, in either case borne on evident pedicels [Fig. ]; fruit a capsule

c3.text: Bracts subtending the flowers alternate; basal, connate portion of the calyx not ribbed or winged, much shorter than the lobes
Bracts subtending the flowers opposite [Fig. ]; basal, connate portion of the calyx 5-ribbed (the ribs sometimes wing-angled), longer than the lobes

c1.text: Flowers in mostly 8- to 20-flowered racemes; corolla 35–55 mm long; fruit 10–20 cm long, tipped by long, arching, horn-like beak that is ultimately split into two halves
Flowers solitary in the axils of leaves; corolla 15–33 mm long; fruit 2–3 cm long, tipped by a short, broad, straight beak that is ultimately split into two halves
Plants without chlorophyll, the stems yellow to brown or purple; leaf blades reduced to scales; ovary unilocular, with parietal placentation
Plants with chlorophyll, with green stems and/or leaves in life; leaf blades foliaceous [Figs. , ]; ovary bilocular, with axile placentation

c2.text: Stems branched, usually many times; flowers dimorphic—the upper with a well-developed corolla and appearing bisexual, the lower carpellate with a small and unopening corolla that is forced off by the developing ovary; plants parasitic on Fagus
Stems simple or rarely few-branched; flowers monomorphic; plants parasitic on various species of plants

c3.text: Calyx with 5 subequal lobes or with 2 lateral lobes separated by a deep apical and basal sinus and each lobe usually bifurcate (therefore, the calyx usually 4 lobed); stems either subterranean or above-ground and sparsely leafy
Calyx tubular and irregularly toothed, split by a deep basal sinus only; stems above-ground and ± concealed by overlapping leaves

c4.text: Foliage leaves of the stem alternate [Fig. ]; anthers glabrous (sparsely pubescent near apex in Schwalbea )
Foliage leaves of the stem opposite [Fig. ]; anthers pubescent (glabrous in Odontites )

c5.text: Flowers subtended by a pair of bractlets situated at the base of the calyx; calyx with 5 lobes
Flowers without a pair of bractlets; calyx with 2 or 4 lobes (5 lobes in Pedicularis furbishiae )

c6.text: The two anther sacs on each filament similar; corolla 2 or more times as long as the calyx; bracts herbaceous (in part)
The two anther sacs on each filament dissimilar—one attached to the filament near its middle, the other suspended from near its apex; corolla less than 2 times as long as the calyx; bracts petaloid

c7.text: Corolla weakly zygomorphic, not galeate [Figs. , ], 10–50 mm long
Corolla zygomorphic and galeate (i.e., with an upper, hooded lip that invests the stamens) [Figs. , ], 2.5–14 mm long

c8.text: Corolla yellow (sometimes marked with brown or red-brown), 25–50 mm long; leaf blades evidently lobed; capsules ovoid to ellipsoid, acute at the apex; anther locules awned at the base

Corolla pink to purple (rarely white), 10–20 mm long; leaf blades entire; capsules globose to subglobose, rounded at the apex (except sometimes for a mucro); anther locules obtuse to cuspidate at the base

c9.text: Leaf and bract blades palmately veined; corolla white, blue, or purple, usually with darker purple lines, the sides of the upper lip reflexed
Leaf and bract blades pinnately veined; corolla white, yellow, or red, the sides not reflexed

c10.text: Corolla yellow; calyx laterally compressed (i.e., taller than thick), with 2 prominent lateral lobes separated by a deep apical and basal sinus (each lateral lobe bifurcate in Rhinanthus ) [Fig. ]
Corolla red or both white and yellow; calyx not laterally compressed, subequally 4-lobed

c11.text: Each lateral half of the calyx bifurcate (i.e., with 4 total lobes), without foliaceous appendages; calyx accrescent in fruit and becoming very inflated; fruit symmetrical, dehiscing evenly
Lateral halves of calyx unlobed, tipped by a foliaceous appendage; calyx not accrescent in fruit; fruit asymmetrical, dehiscing only or more prominently on the upper side (in part)

c12.text: Corolla red, pubescent; anthers glabrous; capsule shorter than the persistent calyx, with more than 4 seeds
Corolla white with a yellow palate, glabrous; anthers pubescent; capsule longer than the persistent calyx, with 1–4 seeds

c1.text: This genus contains exactly one species.
This genus contains exactly one species.
This genus contains exactly one species.
Floating leaf blades without a sinus [Fig. ]; perianth composed of 3 sepals and 3 petals; carpels 4–8, not embedded in the receptacle

Floating leaf blades (or emergent in Nuphar advena ) with a prominent, basal sinus [Figs. , ]; perianth composed of numerous tepals that become progressively petaloid in centripetal fashion; carpels numerous, sunken into a large, spongy receptacle

c2.text: Leaves strongly dimorphic—submersed, opposite, highly dissected ones and floating, alternate, simple ones 0.6–3 cm long; flowers with 3–6 stamens; underwater parts of plant barely coated with mucilage
Leaves monomorphic, all alternate, floating, simple [Fig. ], 3.5–13.5 cm long; flowers with 18–36 (–51) stamens; underwater parts of plant heavily coated with mucilage [Fig. ]

c3.text: Leaves with angular basal lobes; petioles with 4 large air cavities; flowers white (pink); sepals sepaloid; outer petals petaloid, gradually grading into the stamens toward the center of the flower
Leaves with rounded basal lobes [Figs. , ]; petioles with many small air cavities; flowers yellow; sepals petaloid; petals all stamen-like

c1.text: This genus contains exactly one species.
Plants annual, aquatic or amphibious; flowers solitary in the axils of the leaves; perianth 3- or 4-merous; stamens 3 or 4 per flower (i.e., as many as the petals); leaves connate around the stem
Plants perennial, terrestrial; flowers usually borne in cymes; perianth 4- to 16-merous; stamens usually 8–32 per flower (i.e., twice as many as the petals); leaves not connate around the stem

c2.text: Perianth mostly 12- to 16-merous; stamens mostly 24–32 per flower; leaves in crowded, basal rosettes; plants monocarpic
Perianth mostly 4- or 5-merous; stamens mostly 8 or 10 per flower; leaves borne on a stem; plants polycarpic

c3.text: Leaf blades entire, often very thick (i.e., elliptic, semi-circular, or terete in cross-section) [Fig. ]; leaves alternate, opposite, or whorled; plants forming mats by means of creeping stems (not mat-forming in S. hispanicum )

Leaf blades toothed (sometimes inconspicuously so), broad and flat [Figs. , , ]; leaves alternate (opposite in Phedimus spurius ); plants with upright stems, sometimes basally decumbent in age (mat-forming by creeping stems in Phedimus spurius )

c4.text: Flowers 4-merous (rarely 5-merous), unisexual; reproductive stems produced from the axils of brown, scale-like leaves on a partly subterranean rootstock

Flowers 5-merous [Fig. ], bisexual (sometimes with defective and missing parts in Hylotelephium erythrostictum ); reproductive stems produced from underground, tuberous roots or arising from creeping, horizontal stems

c5.text: Plants forming mats by creeping, horizontal stems; roots not tuberous; leaves opposite
Plants not forming mats; roots tuberous, carrot-shaped; leaves alternate, opposite, whorled, or sometimes varied on a single plant

c6.text: Petals yellow, spreading from base [Fig. ] (in part)
Petals pink to pink-purple, erect to ascending at the base and spreading above [Fig. ]

c7.text: Ovaries and follicles narrowly tapering at base, stipitate, lacking an adaxial outgrowth; petals red-purple to purple or white
Ovaries and follicles not tapering at base, sessile, with an adaxial outgrowith; petals yellow (in part)

c1.text: Margins of leaf blades minutely serrulate with cartilaginous papillae; carpels and follicles usually glabrous
Leaf margins smooth, not minutely serrulate; carpels and follicles pubescent with white tomentum
Perianth 4-merous; petals absent; flowers with 4 or 8 stamens that are set in the notches of an 8-lobed disk; at least the lower leaves opposite
Perianth 5-merous; petals present; flowers with 5 or 10 stamens; leaves alternate or all basal (opposite in Saxifraga oppositifolia )

c2.text: Petals conspicuously pectinately fringed [Fig. ]; inflorescence a slender, simple raceme with flowers borne on short pedicels 1–5 mm long
Petals entire [Fig. ]; inflorescence a raceme, panicle, cyme, or thyrse, or of solitary flowers at the tips of stems, the flowers variously arranged on short to long pedicels

c3.text: Ovary 2-locular, the placentation axile; stamens shorter than to scarcely longer than the petals
Ovary 1-locular, the placentation parietal; stamens long-exserted beyond the petals

c4.text: Stems with leaves (note: these sometimes small but are not confined to branching points of the stem) [Fig. ]; leaf blades lacking foliar crystals, with one or more of the following features: palmately lobed outline, with 1 or more lime encrusted pores, prominently ciliate along the margin, and/or entire through most or all of margin; seeds smooth, tuberculate, or papillate

Stems without leaves (note: bracts found on the main axis of the plant are only present at branching points) [Fig. ]; leaf blades with foliar crystals, the principal ones crenate or dentate through much of the margin (except M. foliolosa ), lacking all of the features present in 4a (except M. foliolosa , which is entire through most of the margin); seeds ribbed

c5.text: Flowers with 10 stamens; inflorescence a raceme; valves of the capsule very unequal, one larger than the other
Flowers with 5 stamens; inflorescence a panicle-like thyrse; valves of the capsule ± equal

c1.text: Plants parasitic, with haustoria, lacking chlorophyll; stems pink-yellow to orange, with scale-like leaves; corolla 1.5–5 mm long [Figs. , , ]
Plants autotrophic, without haustoria, with chlorophyll; stems green or tinged with red, with foliaceous leaves; corolla 15–80 mm long [Figs. , ]

c2.text: Stigma 1, capitate unlobed or with 2 or 3 small lobes; ovary and capsule 2- or 3-locular
Stigmas 2, filiform or obloid, unlobed; ovary and capsule 1-, 2-, or 4-locular

c3.text: Pedicels subtended by 2 foliaceous bracts that are positioned near and partly conceal the calyx [Figs. , ]; corolla 20–70 mm long; stigmas obloid
Pedicels subtended by small bracts that are positioned well below the calyx and do not conceal it; corolla 15–25 mm long; stigmas filiform

c1.text: Flowers with a corona [Figs. , , ]; carpels connate only by the thickened style-head; pollen coherent in masses; seeds always comose
Flowers with only sepals and petals, lacking a corona [Figs. , ]; carpels apically connate with a common style and stigma; pollen grains not cohering in masses; seeds with or without a coma

c2.text: Plants lianas; corolla lobes densely villous adaxially; corona composed of 5 short, bifid, antepetalous lobes alternating with 5 narrow, thread-like lobes 4–8 mm long
Plants herbs or vines; corolla lobes glabrous or minutely pubescent adaxially; corona either a whorl of 5 tubular- or scoop-shaped hoods or a fleshy, lobed cup

c3.text: Stems climbing or twining (at least the apical part of the plant); calyx and corolla lobes ascending to spreading [Fig. ]; corona a fleshy, lobed cup [Fig. ]

Stems upright, neither climbing nor twining; calyx and corolla lobes reflexed [Figs. , ]; corona a whorl of hoods bearing internally near the base a slender, horn-like appendage (the horns absent in A. viridiflora ) [Figs. , ]

c4.text: Flowers solitary from leaf-bearing nodes; corolla 20–50 mm wide in life; trailing plants with upright branches
Flowers in terminal or both terminal and axillary cymes [Fig. ]; corolla up to 10 mm wide in life; upright plants without trailing stems

c5.text: Leaves alternate or irregularly scattered; petals blue; seeds lacking a coma of hairs
Leaves opposite; petals white, tinged or striped with pink, green-white, or yellow; seeds comose

c1.text: Plants aquatic; leaf blades narrowly dissected [Fig. ]; peduncles and axes of the terminal racemes conspicuously inflated, the flowers whorled at the constricted nodes [Fig. ]
Plants terrestrial; leaf blades simple; peduncles and axes of inflorescence not or scarcely inflated, the flowers in a solitary, terminal umbel or in racemes with whorls of flowers

c2.text: Corolla white, the basal, connate portion of the corolla ± equal in lenth to the calyx, constricted at the opening; style very short; plants annual

Corolla pink to purple, red, yellow, or rarely white, the basal, connate portion of the corolla longer than the calyx (+/- equal to the calyx in the yellow-flowered P. veris ), not or scarcely constricted at opening; style elongate; plants perennial

c1.text: Corolla pink, red to orange-red, or blue (rarely white); plants annual; fruit a pyxis
Corolla white or yellow; plants perennial; fruit a longitudinally dehiscent or disintegrating capsule

c2.text: Leaves alternate; pedicels up to 1 mm long; calyx 1.5–3 mm long; corollas 1.4–1.7 (–2) mm long; capsules 1.5–2 mm long, with 5–13 seeds
Leaves opposite; pedicels 3–35 mm long; calyx 3.5–5 mm long; corollas (2–) 3–7 (–10) mm long; capsules 4–6 mm long, with 12–45 seeds

c3.text: Stems with 1 or more small, scale-like leaves below and a single whorl of leaves at the apex; flowers usually 7-merous, with white corollas
Stems with many nodes of opposite or whorled leaves; flowers 5- or 6-merous, with yellow corollas or with a white, petaloid calyx in the halophytic L. maritima

c4.text: Calyx petaloid; corolla absent; flowers axillary and subsessile; plants coastal halophytes with fleshy leaf blades
Calyx sepaloid; corolla present; flowers axillary or in terminal inflorescences, borne on short to elongate pedicels; plants usually not of saline habitats, with herbaceous leaf blades

c5.text: Leaf blades not punctate; androecium with staminodes alternating with stamens, the filaments distinct; lobes of the corolla erose on the apical portion of the margin, cuspidate at the apex [Fig. ]

Leaf blades minutely punctate; androecium without staminodes, the filaments connate near the base (filaments distinct in L. thyrsiflora ); lobes of the corolla entire (glandular-ciliate in L. punctata ), without a cuspidate apex

c6.text: Leaf blades linear to narrow-lanceolate, 2–6 (–7) mm wide, with obscure lateral veins, the margins eciliolate and revolute
Leaf blades broad-linear to ovate, 2–65 mm wide, the lower blades usually wider than 6 mm, with evident lateral veins, the margins ciliolate and flat

c7.text: Leaf blades broad-lanceolate to ovate, rounded (infrequently to subcordate) at the base, the principal ones 15–60 mm wide; petioles usually ciliate their entire length; plants with long, slender rhizomes

Leaf blades broad-linear to narrow-ovate, cuneate (infrequently to rounded) at the base, the principal ones 10–20 mm wide; petioles ciliate only in the basal half, sometimes lacking cilia altogether; plants with short, stout rhizomes (very rarely with slender, elongate rhizomes)

c8.text: Flowers borne in short, dense racemes originating from the middle leaf axils [Fig. ]; filaments distinct, usually of equal length; corolla 6- or 7-merous, the lobes 4–5 mm long, linear, and much shorter than the stamens

Flowers solitary in the axils of leaves or in racemes from the apex of the stem or branches; filaments connate at the base, often of unequal length; corolla 5-merous, the lobes 5–16 mm long, lanceolate to ovate, and as long as or longer than the stamens

c9.text: Leaf blades quadrate to suborbicular, 1–2.5 cm long; stems extensively creeping over the ground
Leaf blades narrow-lanceolate to narrow-ovate, 3–12 cm long; stems erect or ascending

c10.text: Corolla white; leaves alternate
Corolla yellow; leaves opposite or whorled

c11.text: Petals not dotted or streaked with black or red; stems pubescent
Petals dotted or streaked with black or red; stems glabrous or sparsely pubescent

c12.text: Calyx lobes 3–5 mm long, dark-margined with red; lobes of the corolla 8–12 mm long, eciliate; flowers borne in terminal or axillary racemes
Calyx lobes 5–8 mm long, entirely green; lobes of the corolla 12–16 mm long, ciliate with stipitate glands; flowers borne in whorls from the axils of the leaves

c13.text: Flowers borne in a terminal raceme; leaves normally opposite, commonly developing bulbils in the axils; pedicels 8–15 mm long
Flowers borne in whorls from the axils of the leaves; leaves normally whorled, without bulbils; pedicels 20–50 cm long

c1.text: Bracts and calyx lobes spine-tipped; stigmas 2
Bracts and calyx lobes not spine-tipped (though sometimes awn-tipped); stigmas usually 3

c2.text: Leaf blades simple and entire; stamens attached at different heights on the corolla
Leaf blades compound or dissected; stamens attached at the same height on the corolla

c3.text: Most leaves opposite; corolla 12–30 mm wide; calyx with scarious or hyaline intervals between the green, ± herbaceous ribs, ruptured by developing capsule; seeds unchanged when wet
Leaves alternate; corolla narrower than 10 mm; calyx of nearly uniform chartaceous texture, not ruptured by developing capsule; seeds becoming mucilaginous when wet

c4.text: Ultimate segments of leaf blades lanceolate to ovate; corolla campanulate [Fig. ]; calyx herbaceous, somewhat accrescent in fruit
Ultimate segments of leaf blades narrow-linear to narrow-oblanceolate; corolla salverform; calyx firm, not accrescent

c5.text: Corolla red on the abaxial surface, 20–40 mm long; inflorescence a slender, elongate thyrse
Corolla light purple to purple or white on the abaxial surface, 5–13 mm long; inflorescence of cymose clusters

c1.text: Leaves of the stem reduced to scales 0.5–4.5 mm long; flowers 2.5–4 (–7) mm long; lobes of the corolla imbricate in bud
Leaves of the stem foliaceous [Fig. ], (5–) 10–150 mm long; flowers 5–55 mm long; lobes of the corolla convolute in bud

c2.text: Corolla rotate, with lobes much longer than the basal, connate portion [Figs. , ]
Corolla tubular, funnelform, campanulate, or salverform, with lobes shorter than the basal, connate portion

c3.text: Style absent, the stigmas decurrent on the sides of the ovary along the carpel sutures; stamens epipetalous; anthers basifixed
Style present, the stigmas elevated above the ovary; stamens free from the petals; anthers versatile

c4.text: Corolla with (4–) 5–12 lobes [Figs. , ], the lobes lacking a prominent glandular spot; anthers recurving or coiling after anthesis
Corolla with 4 (rarely 5) lobes, each lobe with a prominent, fringed, glandular spot; anthers remaining straight

c5.text: Style evident, slender; corolla salverform, red-purple to pink to nearly white; anthers becoming spirally coiled
Style absent, inconspicuous, or short and stout; corolla cylindric, funnelform, or campanulate, blue to white or green to purple-green; anthers not spirally coiled

c6.text: Inflorescence a panicle-like or corymb-like cyme; style slightly bifid, divided for a short distance below the stigma lobes; stigma lobes semicircular to bluntly triangular from side view, fleshy; capsules narrow-cylindrical
Inflorescence a spike-like cyme; style not divided beneath the stigma lobes; stigma lobes flabellate from side view, only slightly fleshy; capsules ellipsoid

c7.text: Lobes of the corolla with conspicuous, basal spurs in the larger flowers; corolla green to purple-green
Lobes of the corolla lacking spurs; corolla blue to white

c8.text: Sinuses of the corolla folded or plaited, often of a color or texture different from those of the corolla lobes; plants perennial; calyx with a continuous membrane or rim on the inside at the summit; nectary glands located at base of ovary

Sinuses of the corolla neither folded nor plaited, of a color and texture similar to those of the lobes; plants annual or biennial; calyx without a membrane or with a membrane confined to the base of each sinus; nectary glands located at base of corolla

c9.text: Margins of the corolla lobes conspicuously fringed in the apical portion [Fig. ]; corolla 35–55 mm long, usually 4-merous; ovules covering much of the inner surface of the ovary; calyx with a membrane on the inside at the base of each sinus; seeds papillose
Margins of the corolla lobes not fringed; corolla 10–23 mm long, commonly 5-merous; ovules confined to bands along each of the 2 sutures of the ovary; calyx without an internal membrane; seeds smooth

c1.text: This genus contains exactly one species.
Leaf blades palmately lobed with peltate petioles; stamens with repeatedly branched filaments; capsules covered with soft prickles
Leaf blades entire or toothed, but not lobed, with basifixed petioles; stamens with simple filaments; capsules without prickles (though sometimes pubescent)

c2.text: Plants with a milky latex; inflorescence a cyathium; flowers without a calyx, subtended by a cup-like involucre with glands (sometimes with petaloid appendages) at the margin, housing within a single, peduncled, carpellate flower and 1 to several staminate flowers, collectively resembling a single bisexual flower [Figs. , , ]
Plants without latex, the sap watery; inflorescence an axillary cyme; flowers with a calyx, clearly unisexual [Figs. , ]

c3.text: Plants with stellate hairs (the branches of the hairs basally fused in Crotonopsis to form a flat scale on some surfaces); anthers inflexed in bud
Plants glabrous or with simple hairs; anthers erect in bud

c4.text: Abaxial leaf surface with stellate hairs; staminate flowers with 7–14 stamens; fruit dehiscent, 3-locular; seeds with a caruncle
Abaxial leaf surface with stellate hairs that have the branches basally united to form a flat scale; staminate flowers with 5 stamens; fruit indehiscent, 1-locular; seeds without a caruncle

c5.text: Leaves alternate; staminate calyx 4-merous; gynoecium with 3 carpels
Leaves opposite; staminate calyx 3-merous; gynoecium with 2 carpels

c1.text: Leaf blades filiform, scarcely differentiated from the petiole; plants bulbous-based; petals purple, 8–15 ×5–8 mm
Leaf blades broad-linear to tranverse-broad-elliptic, clearly differentiated from the petiole; plants not bulbous-based; petals white to pink, 3–6 ×2–4 mm

c2.text: Leaf blades suborbicular to orbicular [Fig. ], sometimes even wider than long; petioles glandular-pubescent [Fig. ]; seeds light brown, longitudinally striate

Leaf blades obovate to broad-linear, definitely longer than wide; petioles glabrous (sometimes sparsely glandular-pubescent in D. anglica ); seeds red-brown or black, papillose, pitted, or striate-alveolate

c3.text: Stipules distinct from the petiole most of their length; seeds red-brown, papillose; leaf blades (5–) 8–20 (–25) mm long
Stipules connate to the petiole most of their length; seeds black, striate-alveolate or pitted; leaf blades (10–) 15–50 mm long

c4.text: Leaf blades broad-linear, 1.5–3 mm wide; seeds 0.5–1 mm long, finely pitted, the testa close and not extending beyond the ends of the ovule
Leaf blades narrow-obovate to elongate-spatulate, 3–4 mm wide; seeds 1–1.5 mm long, striate-alveolate, the testa loose and extending beyond the ovule at each end

c1.text: This genus contains exactly one species.
This genus contains exactly one species.
Leaves mostly once- or twice-forked, serrate, the ultimate segments flat [Fig. ]; styles 4.5–6 mm long; achenes with 2 basal spines
Leaves mostly 3- or 4-times forked, sparsely serrate, the ultimate segments capillary; styles 5–10 mm long; achenes with 4–15 spines—2 basal and 2–13 lateral

Placentation basal-axile, therefore, the ovules/seeds all set at approximately the same level in the ovary/fruit; seeds marked with transversely elliptic, round-ended areoles, the ends of the areoles more or less meeting the other ends (i.e., not dovetailed with them), therefore, the longitudinal ridges of the seed appearing straight and distinct [Fig. ]; leaf blades 0.7–5 mm long; perianth 2-merous; flowers with 2 stamens

Placentation axile, therefore, the ovules/seeds set at different levels in the ovary/fruit; seeds marked with transversely elongate, 6-sided, angular-ended areoles, the ends of the areoles alternating and dovetailed with areole ends from the adjacent rows, therefore, the longitudinal ridges of the seed broken and less conspicuous [Fig. ]; leaf blades 2.8–8 (–15) mm long; perianth (2–) 3-merous; flowers with (2–) 3 stamens

c2.text: Leaf blades obovate to broad-spatulate, usually rounded at the apex, the larger 1.5–5 mm wide; seeds borne from the lower half of the ovary’s central axis, ascending
Leaf blades linear to lanceolate or narrow-spatulate, truncate or retuse at the apex, 0.5–3 mm wide; seeds borne throughout the length of the ovary’s central axis, divergent

c1.text: This genus contains exactly one species.
Involucres 1-flowered, cup-shaped, not accrescent in fruit; calyx salverform, with a prolonged, tubular, connate portion 20–30 mm long
Involucres 3- to 5-flowered, broad and open, accrescent in fruit [Fig. ]; calyx campanulate, with a short, tubular, connate portion 1–2 mm long

c2.text: Leaf blades ovate to broad-ovate, the larger ones rounded to cordate at the base and borne on petioles 10–30 mm long; inflorescence eglandular
Leaf blades linear to lanceolate or oblong, tapering to the base, sessile or on short petioles up to 5 mm long; inflorescence usually glandular-pubescent

c3.text: Leaf blades linear, usually 5 mm wide or narrower; stem glabrous
Leaf blades narrow-lanceolate to lanceolate or oblong, 5–20 mm wide; stem pubescent

c4.text: Stem pubescent in 2 strips on each internode with short, curved hairs up to 0.5 mm long; anthocarp coarsely tuberculate on the ridges
Stem pubescent, at least at the nodes, with spreading hairs 1–2 mm long; anthocarp relatively smooth on the ridges

c1.text: Leaves alternate
Leaves opposite

c2.text: Plants with conspicuous, stinging hairs; leaf blades serrate; carpellate sepals distinct or nearly so, only 2 of the 4 sepals persistent in fruit, not enclosing the achene in fruit; staminate flowers each with 5 sepals and stamens
