Plants without stinging hairs (or sometimes with a few minute stinging hairs); leaf blades entire; carpellate sepals connate at the base, 4-lobed, accrescent, enclosing the achene in fruit; staminate flowers each with 4 sepals and stamens

c3.text: Plants with conspicuous stinging hairs; carpellate calyx of 4 distinct sepals
Plants without stinging hairs (or sometimes with a few minute stinging hairs); carpellate calyx of 3 sepals or 4 connate sepals

c4.text: Inflorescence a spike [Fig. ]; carpellate sepals connate at the base, 4-lobed, accrescent, enclosing the achene in fruit; leaf blades with rounded cystoliths
Inflorescence a panicle; carpellate sepals distinct or nearly so, 3-lobed, not enclosing the achene in fruit; leaf blades with linear cystoliths

c1.text: Sepals distinct or essentially so (appearing connate in Scleranthus , but the tube actually a hypanthium) [Figs. , , ]; ovary sessile; petals without a prominent, narrow, basal portion (i.e., lacking a claw or the claw obscure)
Sepals connate in the basal portion [Figs. , ]; ovary stipitate; petals with a prominent, narrow, basal portion (i.e., possessing a claw)

c2.text: Leaves with scarious or hyaline stipules [Figs. , ]
Leaves without stipules

c3.text: Leaves alternate (rarely some subopposite); gynoecium with 3 sessile stigmas
Leaves opposite or whorled [Fig. ]; gynoecium with 2–5 stigmas (with 3 stigmas in Polycarpon and Spergularia but these elevated on styles)

c4.text: Flowers without petals [Fig. ]; gynoecium with a single ovule; ovary maturing as a utricle
Flowers with white or pink to red-purple petals (but these sometimes caducous in Polycarpon ); gynoecium with many ovules; ovary maturing as a capsule

c5.text: Sepals white, spongy, each with a prominent awn
Sepals ± green (but white-scarious at the margin in Paronychia , the actual color may be partly obscured by white or gray hairs on the abaxial surface), not spongy, with or without awns

c6.text: Stipules with entire margins, (0.5–) 1–8 mm long; calyx 1–4 mm long, the lobes white-scarious at the margins
Stipules with fringed margins [Fig. ], 0.5–1 (–1.5) mm long; calyx 0.5–1.5 mm long, the lobes green

c7.text: Flowers with a single style that is obscurely lobed near the apex; leaf blades elliptic to ovate or obovate; valves of capsules twisted after dehiscence and forming a tube
Flowers with 3–5 styles; leaf blades linear to broad-linear; valves of capsules spreading to recurved but not twisted into a tube

c8.text: Leaves clustered at the nodes in 2 sets of 6–8, appearing whorled, with small stipules 0.5–1 (–1.5) mm long; flowers usually with 5 styles; capsules with usually 5 valves
Leaves opposite (with axillary fascicles in S. rubra ), with stipules 1–5 mm long; flowers usually with 3 styles; capsules with usually 3 valves

c9.text: Flowers perigynous (i.e., with a cupuliform hypanthium) [Fig. ]; fruit a 1-seeded utricle; perianth sepaloid, composed of only sepals that have a narrow, scarious border

Flowers hypogynous or essentially so; fruit a many-seeded capsule; perianth in part petaloid, composed of both sepals and petals (petals absent and, therefore, the perianth sepaloid in some Sagina and Stellaria )

c10.text: Perianth monochlamydeous, only the sepals present
Perianth dichlamydeous, both the sepals and the petals present [Figs. , ]

c11.text: Flowers with 3 styles; capsule dehiscing by 6 valves; leaves linear-oblong to elliptic, 1.5–6 (–10) mm wide (in part)
Flowers with 4 or 5 styles; capsule dehiscing by 4 or 5 valves; leaves linear-subulate, up to 1 mm wide (in part)

c12.text: Petals deeply notched, in some Stellaria so deeply as to appear as 2 distinct, but proximate, petals [Figs. , ]
Petals entire, at most the apex retuse or erose [Figs. , ]

c13.text: Gynoecium with 3 styles; capsules dehiscing by 6 valves (in part)
Gynoecium with 4 or 5 styles [Fig. ]; capsules dehiscing by 5 valves or by 8 or 10 apical teeth

c14.text: Capsules cylindric, dehiscing by 8 or 10 apical teeth; vegetative leaf blades 1–15 mm wide
Capsules ovoid, dehiscing by 5 valves, each valve notched or shortly bifid at the apex; vegetative leaf blades 10–40 mm wide

c15.text: Plants fleshy; seeds 3–5 mm long; petals and stamens inserted on a conspicuous, 10-lobed disk
Plants not fleshy; seeds 0.4–1.4 mm long; staminal disk inconspicuous

c16.text: Flowers with 4 or 5 styles [Fig. ]; capsules dehiscing by 4 or 5 valves (in part)
Flowers with 3 styles; capsules dehiscing by 3 or 6 valves

c17.text: Inflorescence an umbel with 3–15 flowers; petals minutely erose at apex
Inflorescence a cyme or a solitary flower; petals not erose at apex

c18.text: Seeds 1–1.6 mm long, strophiolate; plants rhizomatous perennials, the stems not tufted
Seeds 0.4–0.8 mm long, not strophiolate; plants annuals or perennials, the stems tufted

c19.text: Capsules dehiscing by 6 valves; leaf blades lanceolate to ovate, 3–5 mm wide
Capsules dehiscing by 3 valves; leaf blades linear to narrow-oblanceolate, 0.3–0.8 mm wide

c20.text: Flowers with 5 (rarely 4) styles or 1 style in staminate individuals of dioecious Silene ; capsules dehiscing by 5 or 10 valves or teeth (or dehiscing by 8 valves in 4-styled flowers)
Flowers with 2 or 3 styles; capsules dehiscing by 4 or 6 valves

c21.text: Style conspicuously pubescent; calyx lobes 20–40 mm long, much longer than the connate portion; petals lacking both auricles and appendages at the junction of the claw and blade
Style glabrous; calyx lobes 2.5–9 mm long, much shorter than the connate portion; petals commonly with auricles and/or appendages at the junction of the claw and blade

c22.text: Plants dioecious (i.e., with unisexual flowers), the staminate flowers with a single, undivided style; capsules dehiscing by 5 valves that eventually split again (in part)
Plants synoecious (i.e., with bisexual flowers); capsules dehiscing by 5 valves or 5 bifid teeth

c23.text: Plants annual; calyx 15–28 mm long; carpophores (5–) 7–12 mm long; leaf blades linear to narrow-lanceolate
Plants perennial; calyx 6–17 mm long; carpophores 0–6 mm long; leaf blades narrow-lanceolate to narrow-oblong or ovate

c24.text: Style bases persistent in fruit and reflexed; capsule unilocular, septicidally dehiscent, each valve lacking a distinct midline; petals 2- or 4-lobed, the lobes varying from short and separated by a shallow sinus to elongate and separated by a deep sinus [Fig. ]

Style bases not persistent in fruit; capsule 5-locular in the basal portion, loculicidally dehiscent, each valve with a distinct midline, sometimes further splitting on this line; petals ± entire at the apex

c25.text: Calyx subtended by 1–3 pairs of scarious or foliaceous bracts [Figs. , ]; seeds disciform
Calyx not subtended by bracts, 5- to 30-nerved; seeds orbicular to reniform

c26.text: Calyx with 5 principal nerves (with an additional 10 fine nerves in 1 species), prominently scarious between the 5 principal nerves
Calyx 20- to 40-nerved [Fig. ], without scarious regions between the nerves

c27.text: Flowers with 3 styles; capsules dehiscing by 6 valves
Flowers with usually 2 styles; capsules dehiscing by 4 valves

c28.text: Capsules borne on a carpophore 7–8 mm long [Fig. ]; pedicels 1–5 mm long; stem and calyx glabrous

Capsules borne on a carpophore as long as 6 mm (5–8 mm long in S. caroliniana ); pedicels (2–) 5–50 mm long; commonly either the stem and/or the calyx pubescent, but both glabrous in a few species (in part)

c29.text: Adaxial surface of petals with a subulate appendage at the junction of the claw and blade; calyx with 20, often inconspicuous, nerves
Petals without an appendage; calyx with 5 nerves

c30.text: Petals 18–22 mm long; seeds globose; calyx nerved with stout ribs, these becoming wing angles in fruit, not at all scarious
Petals 2–15 mm long; seeds subreniform; calyx merely nerved, without prominent wing angles in fruit, evidently scarious between its green nerves [Fig. ]

c1.text: Fruit a silicle (i.e., fruit up to 3 times as long as wide), elliptic or oblong to suborbicular or obtriangular in outline, sometimes with a notch or sinus at the base and/or apex [Figs. , , ]
Fruit a silique (i.e., fruit greater than 3 times as long as wide), narrow-oblong to linear in outline, without a notch or sinus at the base or apex [Figs. , , ]

c2.text: Silicle indehiscent or tardily dehiscent, containing 1–4 (–5) seeds, inflated, corky, or spongy at least between the seeds (firm in Neslia )
Silicle dehiscent, containing 2–many seeds, appearing inflated or not

c3.text: Plants pubescent in part with branched hairs; petals 1–2.5 mm long
Plants glabrous or pubescent entirely with unbranched hairs; petals 3–20 mm long

c4.text: Silicle evidently reticulate-textured, glabrous, tipped by the slender, persistent, uncurved style; petals yellow, 2–2.5 mm long; leaves auriculate clasping

Silicle not reticulate-textured, pubescent with both branched and unbranched, white hairs, with an apical beak that curves away from the inflorescence rachis; petals white, 1–1.3 mm long; leaves petiolate or sessile, but not clasping

c5.text: Silicle 2.5–3 mm long; leaves auriculate-clasping; plants perennial (in part)
Silicle 6–60 mm long; leaves not auriculate-clasping; plants annual

c6.text: Petals 15–20 mm long; silicle 30–60 mm long; plants from a fleshy, elongated taproot (in part)
Petals 5–10 mm long, sometimes reduced in Cakile and bristle-like; silicle 6–25 mm long; plants not from a fleshy, enlarged taproot

c7.text: Petals pale purple to purple or white; leaf blades glabrous; upper segment of fruit lanceoloid to ovoid, without a terminal beak or with a stocky beak [Fig. ] (in part)
Petals yellow; leaf blades hirsute; upper segment of fruit subglobose, terminated by a slender beak 1–4 mm long (in part)

c8.text: Silicle compressed at right angles to the septum, the septum therefore much narrower than the width of the fruit [Fig. ]
Silicle either not compressed or compressed parallel to the septum, in either case the septum as wide as the fruit

c9.text: Leaves subulate, not flat, all basal [Fig. ]; plants aquatic, frequently in submerged populations that become emergent as water levels decline
Leaves not subulate, definitely flat, not confined to the base of the plant except in Teesdalia ; plants terrestrial weeds

c10.text: Silicle with 2 seeds
Silicle with 4 or more seeds

c11.text: Petals all of similar size (or absent) [Fig. ]; silicle with either a short or obsolete style or with a truncate apex or both [Figs. , ] (in part)
Outer two petals larger than the inner two; silicle with a long style projecting from the prominently retuse apex

c12.text: Outer two petal larger than the inner two; median filaments with a white scale at the base; plants scapose
Petals all of similar size; median filaments without a basal scale; plants with leafy stems

c13.text: Silicle oval to orbicular to outline, wing-margined, rounded to broad-cuneate at the base, conspicuously retuse at the apex [Fig. ]; plants glabrous or pubescent with unbranched hairs
Silicle obtriangular to obtriangular-cordate in outline, not wing-margined, cuneate at the base, convex to slightly concave at the apex; plants pubescent with branched hairs

c14.text: Silicle thin and flat, 20–35 mm wide, borne on a gynophore longer than 10 mm [Fig. ]; stem leaf blades ovate to deltate; petals blue-purple

Silicle compressed to plump, narrower than 6 mm, either sessile at the end of the pedicel or on a very short gynophore; stem leaf blades usually narrower or absent; petals white or yellow (sometimes tinged with purple in Lobularia )

c15.text: Petals with a deep, apical notch [Fig. ]; fruiting pedicels erect to appressed (or widely ascending in B. mutabilis ) [Fig. ]; seeds winged
Petals entire at the apex or slightly retuse (deeply notched in Draba verna , a small, scapose annual); fruiting pedicels spreading to ascending; seeds unwinged (winged in Aurinia )

c16.text: Silicle irregularly tuberculate, often asymmetrical (i.e., one locule larger than the other); plants frequently with sessile, tubercle-like glands on the leaf blades
Silicle not tuberculate, usually symmetrical; plants without tubercle- like glands

c17.text: Silicle conspicuously compressed; pubescence, at least in part, of branched hairs
Silicle with definite, convex valves, scarcely compressed if at all; pubescence, if present, of unbranched hairs (except Camelina with some branched hairs)

c18.text: Petals yellow; seeds winged all around
Petals cream to white; seed unwinged

c19.text: Flower-bearing stems arising from a basal rosette of leaves; silicle lanceolate to narrow-oblong or oblong in outline, 4–20 mm long (in part)
Flower-bearing stems lacking a conspicuous basal rosette; silicle broad-ovate or broad-obovate to orbicular in outline, 2–4 mm long

c20.text: Plants pubescent with stellate-branched hairs; silicle with a thin, wing-like margin, with seeds aligned in 2 rows in each locule; fruiting pedicels 2–6 mm long
Plants pubescent with 2-pronged hairs; silicle lacking a thin margin, with seeds aligned in 1 row in each locule; fruiting pedicels 5–10 mm long

c21.text: Plants pubescent with both unbranched and branched hairs (sometimes subglabrous in C. sativa ); leaves conspicuously auriculate-clasping the stem; each valve of the silicle with a thin but visible and often sinuous midnerve
Plants glabrous or pubescent with unbranched hairs; leaves narrowed to the base or auriculate-clasping; each valve of the silicle without a midnerve or with an obscure midnerve

c22.text: Petals white; leaf blades simple; seeds rarely maturing; silicle with a persistent style tip 0.3 mm long

Petals yellow (white in 1 aquatic species); principal leaf blades pinnately lobed, divided, or dissected (simple in R. austriaca and R. amphibia ); seeds usually maturing; silicle with a persistent style tip 0.4–3 mm long [Figs. , ] (in part)

c23.text: Silique indehiscent, separating at maturity into 1-seeded segments, prominently corky or spongy, at least between the seeds, or indurate and cross-septate in Chorispora [Figs. , ]

Silique longitudinally dehiscent (with an apical, indehiscent beak in Brassica , Eruca , and Sinapis ), the open valves revealing the seeds and septum, generally not corky or spongy, lacking cross-septa [Figs. , , ]

c24.text: Stems and axis of inflorescence conspicuously stipitate-glandular; seeds embedded in cavities of the septum
Stems and axis of inflorescence lacking stipitate glands; seeds not embedded in cavities of the septum

c25.text: Petals 15–20 mm long; siliques 40–80 mm long, with 4–12 seeds [Fig. ]; fruiting pedicels 10–25 mm long (in part)
Petals 5–10 mm long, sometimes reduced in Cakile and bristle-like; siliques 6–25 mm long, with 1–3 seeds; fruiting pedicels 1.5–8 mm long

c26.text: Petals pale purple to purple or white; leaf blades glabrous; upper segment of fruit lanceoloid to ovoid, without a prominent, slender beak (in part)
Petals yellow; leaf blades hirsute; upper segment of fruit subglobose, terminated by a prominent, slender beak 1–4 mm long (in part)

c27.text: Leaf blades simple, entire or toothed, but lacking pronounced lobes (except for basal lobes in cordate- or sagittate-shaped leaf blades)
At least the lower leaf blades lobed or divided

c28.text: Plants pubescent partly or entirely with branched hairs [Figs. , ]
Plants glabrous or pubescent entirely with unbranched hairs

c29.text: Middle stem leaves sessile and sagittate- or auriculate-clasping
Middle stem leaves narrowed to base, sometimes ± shortly petiolate [Fig. ]

c30.text: Pubescence of basal leaves, when present, comprised entirely of unbranched hairs or, in part, of short-stalked, 2- to 4 (–7)-rayed hairs, the stalks mostly 0.01–0.06 mm long [Fig. ]; siliques 1–2.5 mm wide (in part)
Pubescence of basal leaves comprised, in part, of long-stalked, 2- to 4-rayed hairs, the stalks mostly 0.12–0.6 mm long [Fig. ]; siliques 0.8–1.3 mm wide

c31.text: Petals pale yellow; outer sepals not saccate at base; middle and upper stem leaves glabrous and glaucous; siliques terete
Petals white, sometimes tinged with pink; outer sepals somewhat saccate at base; middle and upper stem leaves pubescent, not glaucous; siliques compressed (in part)

c32.text: Petals yellow; siliques pubescent with branched hairs; some of the hairs on the leaf blades malpighiaceous (i.e., hairs 2-pronged, less frequently 3-pronged, mesifixed and appressed to the surface) (in part)

Petals white or pink to purple; siliques glabrous or pubescent in some Draba ; hairs of the leaf blades unbranched or branched, but none of them malpighiaceous (except in the rare introduction Arabis procurrens , a species with compressed siliques)

c33.text: Petals 18–25 mm long, white or pink to purple; compound hairs all forked (i.e., with a stalk and 2 ascending branches)

Petals 2–10 mm long, usually white (infrequently pink or rose- purple); compound hairs with 2 or more ascending to spreading branches (i.e., compound hairs not uniformly forked with ascending branches)

c34.text: Siliques narrow-lanceolate or narrow-oblong to ovate or obovate in outline, 4–20 (–22) mm long, up to 5 times as long as wide; seeds aligned in 2 rows in each locule (in part)
Siliques linear in outline, 10–100 mm long, more than 5 times as long as wide; seeds aligned in 1 row in each locule

c35.text: Siliques often torulose; fruiting pedicels (1–) 1.5–6 (–8) mm long
Siliques scarcely, if at all, constricted between the seeds; fruiting pedicels 5–15 mm long

c36.text: Plants 3–10 dm tall, usually with unbranched stems; siliques 2–3.5 mm wide; seeds winged (in part)
Plants 0.8–4 dm tall, frequently branched at the base or with stolons, producing multiple upright stems; siliques 0.8–1.5 mm wide; seeds without wings (winged in Arabis procurrens )

c37.text: Primary leaf blades usually with some form of dentition or lobing; siliques 0.8–1 mm wide; petals 2–8 (–10) mm long (in part)
Primary leaf blades usually entire; siliques 1–1.5 mm wide; petals 8–10 mm long; (in part)

c38.text: Stem leaves conspicuously cordate- or sagittate-clasping at the base
Stem leaves not clasping at the base [Fig. ]

c39.text: Petals 6–25 (–30) mm long, narrowed to a distinct claw; siliques 2–5 mm wide (in part)
Petals 3–12 mm long, narrowed to the base, but usually without a distinct claw; siliques 1–2.5 (–3.5) mm wide

c40.text: Plants annual, with entire leaf blades; petals yellow to yellow-white, 7–12 mm long; siliques quadrangular in cross-section; seeds without wings

Plants biennial or perennial, with at least the lower leaf blades toothed to pinnatifid (rarely all entire); petals 3–10 mm long, white (infrequently yellow-white or light purple); siliques compressed; seeds with a partly or completely encircling wing-margin usually wider than 0.2 mm (in part)

c41.text: At least the basal leaf blades triangular to suborbicular or reniform, broad-rounded to cordate at the base
Leaf blades broad-linear or oblanceolate to elliptic, ovate, or obovate, narrowed to the base

c42.text: Basal leaf blades entire or undulate-margined, the stem leaf blades entire, remotely toothed, or lobed; siliques compressed; septum bordered by a thin wing-like replum set perpendicular to the plane of the septum, therefore, the septum and replum combined are I-beam-shaped in cross-section (in part)
Basal and stem leaf blades prominently dentate; siliques somewhat 4-angled in cross-section; replum essentially the same thickness as the septum, the septum and replum combined flat in cross-section

c43.text: Sepals spreading to reflexed [Fig. ]; siliques with a prominent, apical, indehiscent, conical beak 10–12 mm long (in part)
Sepals erect to ascending; siliques without an apical, indehiscent beak or the beak present and only 1–5 (–6) mm long

c44.text: Siliques quadrangular, erect (i.e., ± appressed to the axis of the inflorescence); petals narrowed to a distinct claw (in part)
Siliques terete to compressed, spreading to erect; petals narrowed to the base, with or without a distinct claw

c45.text: Petals yellow; seeds aligned in 2 rows in each locule (in part)
Petals white to pink or light purple; seeds aligned in 1 row in each locule

c46.text: Siliques 15–35 mm long; septum bordered by a thin wing-like replum set perpendicular to the plane of the septum, therefore, the septum and replum combined are I-beam-shaped in cross-section; dwarf alpine plants 2–10 cm tall (in part)
Siliques 40–100 mm long; replum essentially the same thickness as the septum, the septum and replum combined flat in cross-section; herbs of forests, cliffs, and talus, 10–90 cm tall

c47.text: Slender plants 10–40 cm tall, frequently branched at the base, producing multiple upright stems; siliques 0.8–1 mm wide; seeds without wings (in part)
Stouter plants 30–100 cm tall, usually with unbranched stems; siliques 2–3.5 mm wide; seeds winged (in part)

c48.text: Principal leaf blades palmately lobed or palmately divided into 3–5 segments; stem gradually narrowing at base to a fragile junction with a swollen, fleshy rhizome (in part)

Principal leaves pinnately lobed or pinnately divided; stems in most genera arising from taproots or fibrous roots, when arising from rhizomes the stem widest at the base and narrowing upward and/or continuous with the rhizome

c49.text: Plants pubescent, at least in part, with branched hairs
Plants glabrous or pubescent entirely with unbranched hairs

c50.text: Inflorescence leafy-bracteate, most or all of the pedicels subtended by bracts (in part)
Inflorescence not bracteate, only the lower pedicels, if any, subtended by bracts

c51.text: Leaf blades 1–3 times pinnately divided; branched hairs dendritic
Leaf blades pinnately lobed; branched hairs malpighiaceous (i.e., hairs 2-pronged, less frequently 3-pronged, mesifixed and appressed to the surface) (in part)

c52.text: Stem leaves sessile and auriculate-clasping (only the emergent leaves in Nastustium sometimes with auricles at the base of the petiole) [Figs. , ]
Stem leaves petiolate or sessile, but not clasping the stem

c53.text: Petals white and 2–3 mm long or absent; septum bordered by a thin wing-like replum set perpendicular to the plane of the septum, therefore, the septum and replum combined are I-beam-shaped in cross-section (in part)
Petals yellow, or white in Nasturtium and some Boechera , but then 3–7 mm long; replum essentially the same thickness as the septum, the septum and replum combined flat in cross-section

c54.text: Leaves with pinnately compound blades, the leaflets often petiolulate; plants aquatic, with submersed or floating stems (or prostrate on mud as water levels decline), freely rooting from the nodes (in part)

Middle and upper stem leaves with toothed to pinnately lobed, but not compound, leaf blades, the leaflets connected to each other by at least a wing of tissue along the leaf rachis; plants terrestrial or of wetlands, the stems upright or sometimes prostrate, not or only sparingly rooting from the lower nodes

c55.text: Petals white to yellow-white; seeds with an encircling wing; siliques wide-spreading to recurved at maturity [Fig. ] (in part)
Petals yellow; seeds without wings; siliques ascending to spreading

c56.text: Siliques terminated by an indehiscent beak 7–15 mm long; seeds subglobose (in part)
Siliques without an apical, indehiscent beak, tipped only by a persistent style up to 3 mm long if at all; seeds oblong to quadrate or cordiform (rarely maturing in some Rorippa )

c57.text: Siliques 3–15 (–20) mm long (rarely maturing in some Rorippa ), with seeds aligned in 2 rows in each locule; valves of silique ± nervelss; stems terete (in part)
Siliques 10–80 mm long, with seeds aligned in 1 row in each locule; valves of silique with a prominent midnerve; stems angled

c58.text: Siliques terete or quadrangular in cross-section, each valve strongly convex

c59.text: Petals yellow in life; seeds aligned in 2 rows in each locule (in part)
Petals white to pink to purple; seeds aligned in 1 row in each locule

c60.text: Lower leaf blades pinnately divided [Figs. , ]; septum bordered by a thin wing-like replum set perpendicular to the plane of the septum, therefore, the septum and replum combined are I-beam-shaped in cross-section (in part)
Lower leaf blades pinnately lobed to dentate; replum essentially the same thickness as the septum, the septum and replum combined flat in cross-section (in part)

c61.text: Seeds aligned in 2 rows in each locule
Seeds aligned in 1 row in each locule

c62.text: Silique terminated by a broad, flat, indehiscent beak 5–12 mm long that is to fully as long as the valves; petals white to white-yellow with red-purple veins
Silque without an apical beak or with a short beak 1–3 mm long that is much shorter than the valves; petals entirely white or yellow

c63.text: Petals white; leaves with pinnately compound blades, the leaflets often petiolulate; plants aquatic, with submersed or floating stems (or prostrate on mud as water levels decline), freely rooting from the nodes (in part)

Petals yellow or absent; middle and upper stem leaves with toothed to pinnately lobed, but not compound, leaf blades, the leaflets connected to each other by at least a wing of tissue along the leaf rachis; plants terrestrial or of wetlands, the stems upright or sometimes prostrate, not or only sparingly rooting from the lower nodes

c64.text: Inflorescence leafy-bracteate, most or all of the pedicels subtended by bracts (in part)
Inflorescence not bracteate, only the lower pedicels, if any, subtended by bracts

c65.text: Siliques 3–15 (–20) mm long, the valves of silique ± nerveless; fruiting pedicels 0.5–14 mm long (in part)
Siliques 20–45 mm long, the valves with a prominent midnerve; fruiting pedicels (6–) 10–30 (–35) mm long (in part)

c66.text: Petals white; leaves with pinnately compound blades, the leaflets often petiolulate; plants aquatic, with submersed or floating stems (or prostrate on mud as water levels decline), freely rooting from the nodes (in part)

Petals pale yellow to yellow in life (sometimes white-yellow in the cultivated Brassica oleracea ); middle and upper stem leaves with toothed to pinnately lobed, but not compound, leaf blades, the leaflets connected to each other by at least a wing of tissue along the leaf rachis (those of Sisymbrium altissimum with linear to filiform segments that often lack connecting tissue along the rachis); plants primarily terrestrial weeds with upright stems that do not root from the nodes

c67.text: Seeds subglobose; silique tipped by an indehiscent beak 1–30 mm long
Seeds obloid or ovoid; silique tipped by the persistent style up to 3 mm long

c68.text: Each valve of the silique with 1 prominent nerve; indehiscent beak of fruit terete or angled, without seeds (very rarely with 1 or 2 seeds); sepals erect to ascending (in part)
Each valve of the silique with 3 prominent nerves; indehiscent beak of fruit compressed or compressed-quadrangular, often containing 1 (–3) seeds; sepals spreading to reflexed [Fig. ] (in part)

c69.text: Inflorescence not bracteate, only the lower pedicels, if any, subtended by bracts [Fig. ]; valves of silique with 3 nerves
Inflorescence leafy-bracteate, most or all of the pedicels subtended by bracts; valves of silique with 1 nerve

c1.text: Stem with 1 opposing pair of angles larger, darker, and convex, the other pair of angles smaller, paler, and flat to concave; petals dull light purple to white, usually glabrous; apical, tubular portion of the hypanthium as tall as or taller than the basal, globose portion
Stem with all 4 angles subequal; petals red-purple, usually bristly on the abaxial surface; apical, tubular portion of the hypanthium shorter than the basal, globose portion
Flowers with 4 sepals, petals, stamens, and styles; sepals with 3 apical lobes; leaf blades 2–3 mm long; plants diminutive annuals, 3–10 cm tall

Flowers with 5 sepals, petals, stamens, and styles; sepals without apical lobes, though sometimes ciliate or toothed along the margin; leaf blades 3–35 mm long; plants annual or perennial, 10–100 cm tall

c2.text: Petals blue, 10–23 mm long; capsules 5–10 mm wide; sepals without glands
Petals white or yellow, 3–10 mm long; capsules 2–2.5 mm wide; at least the inner sepals glandular-ciliate, glandular-toothed, or with sessile marginal glands (sometimes entire in L. striatum )

c3.text: Leaf blades with 3 nerves; sepals 7–9 mm long at maturity, the inner ciliolate; plants annual
Leaf blades with 1 nerve, sometimes with 2 additional, obscure nerves; sepals 5–7 mm long at maturity, eciliolate; plants perennial

c4.text: Petals white; lower pedicels 10–25 mm long; staminodes present; plants annual
Petals yellow; pedicels up to 8 (–10) mm long; staminodes absent; plants perennial or annual in L. sulcatum

c5.text: Styles connate at the base for a distance of 0.3–1.5 mm; leaf blades with a pair of dark glands at the base (i.e., stipular glands); plants annual
Styles distinct; leaf blades lacking a pair of basal glands; plants perennial

c6.text: Fruit obturbinoid, as tall as or taller than wide, pointed at the apex [Fig. ], 2–3 mm tall; false septa of fruit incomplete (though the fruit still separating into 10 mericarps at maturity)
Fruit depressed globose, shorter than wide, rounded to bluntly pointed at the apex [Fig. ], 1.3–2 mm tall; false septa of fruit nearly complete

c7.text: Inner sepals evidently glandular-toothed [Fig. ]; leaf blades linear to narrow-lanceolate or lanceolate-elliptic, the larger ones (1–) 1.5–3.5 (–4) mm wide
Inner sepals entire or with sessile, marginal glands; leaf blades elliptic to oblanceolate or obovate, the larger ones 3–10 mm wide

c8.text: Branches striate-angled; inflorescence elongate, panicle-like; true septa of fruit, as well as the false septa, eciliate; pedicels 0.1–4 mm long; carpels convex on the outer surface
Branches ± terete; inflorescence broad, corymb-like; true septa of fruit usually sparsely ciliate; pedicels 1–10 mm long; carpels +/- flat on the outer surface

c1.text: Leaf blades pinnately lobed or pinnately divided [Fig. ]; stamens 10 per flower but the outer series of filaments sterile and lacking anthers; seeds smooth (though usually pubescent); carpel beaks separating from the style column, dehiscing from apex to base, the free portions of the carpel beaks becoming spirally coiled; carpel beaks pubescent on the adaxial (i.e., inner) surface

Leaf blades palmately lobed or palmately divided; stamens 10 per flower, all fertile (except G. pusillum with 3–5 sterile filaments); seeds reticulate or striate (smooth in 2 species); carpel beaks remaining partially adnate to the style column, dehiscing from base to apex [Fig. ], the free portions of the carpel beaks merely outwardly curving; carpel beaks glabrous or nearly so on the adaxial surface
This genus contains exactly one species.
Plants lacking leafy, aerial stems, the petioles and peduncles arising directly from rhizomes or a bulbous base; corolla largely or entirely white or pink-purple to purple, 10–20 mm long
Plants with leafy stems, the petioles and peduncles arising from nodes on the stem; petals yellow, 4–10 mm long

c2.text: Inflorescence consisting of a solitary, peduncled flower; petals white with pink veins (rarely pink-purple throughout) [Fig. ]; sepals without a callus tip; leaves and peduncles arising from slender rhizomes

Inflorescence an umbel with (1–) 2–12 (–18) flowers; petals pink-purple to purple (rarely pink or white); sepals with a pair of orange tubercles at the apex (these confluent and appearing as 1 tubercle in O. violacea ); leaves and peduncles arising from one or more bulbs

c3.text: Leaflets obcordate to obreniform, (5–) 8–15 (–20) mm long, with two marginal oxalate deposits, appearing as small dots on each side of the base of the apical leaflet notch; plants usually arising from a single bulb, the bulb scales 3-nerved

Leaflets obtriangular to broad-obtriangular, 20–50 mm long, lacking marginal oxalate deposits; plants usually arising from a cluster of bulbs (rarely a single bulb), the bulb scales (3–) 5- to 7-nerved

c4.text: Plants uniformly and moderately to densely pubescent with short, appressed hairs (i.e., strigose) on the stems, branches, peduncles, and pedicels (rarely some hairs ascending); seeds brown with gray to white lines on the transverse ridges

Plants glabrous or sparsely to densely pubescent with appressed, spreading, and/or retrorse hairs, if uniformly strigose then only on peduncles and pedicels; seeds brown or rarely with gray to white lines on the transverse ridges

c5.text: Stipules absent [Fig. , R]; pubescence of the stem septate [Fig. , R]; stems solitary (rarely in pairs or trios) from a rhizome; cymes with (3–) 5–7 (–15) flowers; primary root usually not thicker than stem

Stipules present, though small and inconspicuous [Fig. , L]; pubescence of the stem without septa [Fig. , L]; stems either clustered from a crown or taproot or solitary, without horizontal stems or with above-ground horizontal stems (i.e., stolons); cymes with 1–3 (–6) flowers; primary root usually thicker than stem

c6.text: Stems trailing and rooting at the nodes; stipules relatively well developed (though still small), with distinct margins, rectangular; capsule commonly retrosely pubescent throughout, sometimes with intermixed, spreading septate hairs (varying to glabrous)

Stems erect to decumbent, but not rooting at the nodes; stipules very reduced, without distinct margins, appearing as a small, semicircular swelling in the axil of the petiole; capsule glabrous or sparsely pubescent apically or along ridges with appressed hairs, lacking septate hairs

Horizontal shoots, excluding the trophophylls, very slender, 0.5–0.9 mm thick, each segment producing 1 (rarely 2) upright shoot; trophophylls of the horizontal shoot entire; upright shoots rarely taller than 10 cm
Horizontal shoots thicker, 1.2–3.1 mm thick, each segment producing 1–5 upright shoots; trophophylls of the horizontal shoot toothed; upright shoots usually taller than 10 cm [Figs. , ]

c2.text: Horizontal shoots prominently arching over the substrate, rooting 7.5–36 cm distal to the most proximal upright shoot [Fig. ]; sporophylls 5.5–9 mm long, spreading at maturity, with 1–3 slender teeth on each margin
Horizontal shoots prostrate, rooting 1.5–4.8 cm distal to the most proximal upright shoot [Fig. ]; sporophylls 2.9–5 (–5.2) mm long, appressed, entire or rarely with a low tooth on one margin

c1.text: This genus contains exactly one species.

Trophophylls of the lateral branches monomorphic, arranged in 5 ranks, adnate to the terete branches less than 50% of their length, with stomates on both surfaces; strobilus stalks absent (rarely up to 1 cm tall); strobili solitary; plants commonly shorter than 12 cm, compactly branched, without an evident main axis

Trophophylls of the lateral branches di- or trimorphic, arranged in 4 ranks, those of the lateral ranks adnate to the flat or quadrangular branches more than 50% of their length, with stomates on the abaxial (i.e., lower) surface only; strobilus stalks 0.5–15 cm long; strobili 1–4 per stalk; plants commonly taller than 12 cm, usually dendroid

c2.text: Trophophylls of the lower rank 1–2 mm long, similar in length to the trophophylls of the upper rank; branches narrow, quadrangular, 1.2–2 mm wide, blue-green; horizontal shoots subterranean, frequently buried deeper than 5 cm

Trophophylls of the lower rank 0.3–1 (–1.5) mm long, noticeably shorter than the trophophylls of the other ranks; branches wider, flat, 2–4.4 mm wide, green; horizontal shoots superficial, at the surface or immediately below the litter

c3.text: Lateral branches of upright shoots with winter bud constrictions [Fig. ], somewhat irregular, more 3-dimensional and not planar; strobili mostly 10–25 mm tall, without sterile tips; strobilus stalks usually becoming stramineous prior to sporangia dehiscence, mostly 0.4–0.7 mm in diameter, the successive branches separate, appearing as distinct dichotomies

Lateral branches of upright shoots without annual constrictions, with regular and planar aspect; strobili mostly 20–40 mm tall, often some with a slender, sterile tip; strobilus stalks remaining green until after sporangia dehiscence, mostly 0.6–1 mm in diameter, the successive branches in close proximity, the strobili often falsely appearing in a pseudowhorl of 4 [Fig. ]

c1.text: Strobilus stalks with a solitary strobilus, sometimes with a second sessile strobilus; upright shoots with 2 or 3 ascending branches; trophophylls 3–5 mm long; sporophylls usually gradually tapering to the apex

Strobilus stalks with 1–5 strobili, commonly with 2 or more and each with a short stalk-like branch; upright shoots with 3–6 spreading branches; trophophylls 4–6 mm long; sporophylls usually abruptly tapering to the apex

Trophophylls of the upright shoot’s main axis 0.9–1 mm wide, widely ascending to spreading (i.e., diverging at an angle of 45–90 degrees), firm, prickly to the touch; trophophylls of the lateral branches arranged in 2 upper, 2 lower, and 2 lateral ranks [Fig. ]

Trophophylls of the upright shoot’s main axis 0.5–0.7 mm wide, appressed to ascending (i.e., diverging at an angle of less than 30 degrees), pliable; trophophylls of the lateral branches arranged in 1 upper, 1 lower, and 4 lateral ranks [Figs. , ]

c2.text: Lateral branches somewhat compressed; trophophylls of the lower rank of lateral branches shorter than those of the other ranks, those of the lateral ranks twisted, so that one surface faces up, the other surface faces down [Fig. ]; trophophyll margins forming an angle of 27–59 degrees at the apex

Lateral branches terete; trophophylls of the lower rank of lateral branches similar in length to those of the other ranks, those of the lateral ranks not twisted, one surface facing the branch axis, the other surface facing outward [Fig. ]; trophophyll margins forming an angle of 21–36 degrees at the apex

c1.text: Trophophylls of upright shoots with abundant stomates on the adaxial surface (i.e., 25–53 per surface), 3–5.9 mm long, entire or very obscurely toothed, arranged in alternating pseudowhorls of 4, those immediately above the winter bud constrictions triangular to lanceolate or narrow-ovate (i.e., broadest at or very near the base); strobili 8–17 (–21) mm tall

Trophophylls of upright shoots lacking stomates on upper surface (except the trophophylls at and immediately above winter bud constrictions), 5.2–9.8 mm long, obscurely to evidently toothed, arranged in alternating pseudowhorls of 5, those immediately above the winter bud constrictions oblanceolate or sometimes elliptic (i.e., broadest at or above the middle); strobili (15–) 17–43 mm tall
This genus contains exactly one species.
Trophophore 2- to 4-times ternately compound, mostly 5–25 cm long, usually as wide or wider than long, commonly sterile (i.e., without a sporophore) [Figs. , ]; leaf buds pubescent

Trophophore simple or up to twice pinnately divided, mostly 2–10 cm long, often longer than wide, always accompanied by a sporophore (i.e., spore-bearing portion of leaf) [Figs. , ]; leaf buds glabrous

c2.text: Trophophore sessile or nearly so, thin and deciduous, borne high on the common stalk well above the ground; leaf sheath open; leaf bud only partly enclosed by sheathing base of leaf
Trophophore long-stalked, thick and evergreen, borne near the ground on the common stalk; leaf sheath closed; leaf bud completely enclosed by sheathing base of leaf

c3.text: Trophophore highly lacerate-dissected into linear segments (in part)
Trophophore moderately divided into lanceolate to ovate segments

c4.text: Trophophore leafules regularly dissected, divided to the tip; terminal leaflet segment equal to or slightly longer than adjacent, lateral leaf segments; trophophores green in fall and winter

Trophophore leafules irregularly dissected, not divided in the apical portion [Fig. ]; terminal leaflet segment noticeably larger than adjacent, lateral leaf segments; trophophores green or bronze to purple in fall and winter

c5.text: Ultimate segments of trophophore rounded to obtusely pointed, entire to weakly crenulate, mostly 4–8 mm wide at maturity, plane, coriaceous
Ultimate segments of trophophore angular, dentate, mostly 2–5 mm wide at maturity, somewhat channeled and concave abaxially in life, semiherbaceous

c6.text: Trophophore leafules ovate, crenulate to denticulate, rounded to obtusely pointed at apex [Fig. ]; trophophores green in fall and winter; dried roots 0.5–4 mm thick 1 cm from stem (mean=2 mm), pale gray to tan (rarely darker) and with sparse transverse circular ridges in the proximal 1–5 cm

Trophophore leafules lanceolate to trullate, denticulate to lacerate, acute to acuminate at apex [Fig. ]; trophophores usually bronze to purple in fall and winter; dried roots 1.5–5.5 mm thick 1 cm from stem (mean=2.5 mm), dark gray-brown and with abundant transverse circular ridges in the proximal 1–5 cm (in part)

c7.text: Trophophore leaflets linear to narrow-ovate, the apex obtuse to acuminate, the margins shallowly to deeply lobed; at least the tip of the trophophore reflexed in bud

Trophophore leaflets nearly orbicular to obovate or flabellate, the apex rounded to truncate, the margins entire or distally few-lobed; trophophore and sporophore erect in bud or only the extreme tip of trophophore slightly inclined

c8.text: Trophophore oblong to ovate, with 1 main axis, usually stalked; sporophore mainly erect in bud, only the very tip curved over
Trophophore deltate, with 3 axes, usually ± sessile; sporophore reflexed in bud

c9.text: Trophophore very slender and simple to obscurely lobed or with evident lobes, in the latter case usually with a greater distance between the first and second pairs of leaflets than between the second and third pairs of leaflets counting from the base
Trophophore usually with evident lobes, the first and second pairs of leaflets separated by a similar or slightly longer distance than the second and third pairs of leaflets

c10.text: Lowest pair of trophophore lobes or leaflets, when present, not obviously larger than the next apical pair [Fig. ]; lobes on well-developed plants usually square-oblong to obovate-oblong; stalk of trophophore inserted high on common stalk, usually at or above mid-height of plant [Fig. ]; plants primarily of forested wetlands

Lowest pair of trophophore lobes or leaflets, when present, often noticeably larger and more complex than the next apical pair [Fig. ]; lobes varying from oblong to flabellate to reniform; stalk of trophophore usually borne near base of plant (sometimes toward mid-height) [Fig. ]; plants primarily of open areas such as fields, shores, and banks (in part)

c11.text: Lowest pair of trophophore leaflets (or lobes in dwarf individuals) obviously larger and more complex in most plants then next apical pair; many trophophores with a characteristically broad, rounded to obstuse, terminal segment (in part)
Lowest pair of trophophore leaflets slightly, if at all, larger and more cleft or lobed than next apical pair; trophophores typically with small, narrow-flabellate terminal segments

c12.text: Plants pale glaucous-green to white-green in life; lower trophophore leaflets frequently cleft into 2 unequal lobes, the upper lobe larger; sporophore 1.5–4 times as long as the trophophore

Plants in life green or yellow-green to glaucous-green or blue-green; lower trophophore leaflets entire to crenate or lobed, when lobed the lobes usually nearly equal; sporophore 0.8–2 (–2.5) times as long as trophophore

c13.text: Trophophore leaflets overlapping to approximate, usually broad-flabellate; apical leaf segments greatly reduced in size and of a shape different from those of medial segments; medial leaflets 6–18 mm wide
Trophophore leaflets remote, usually cuneate to narrowly flabellate; apical leaf segments slightly reduced and more or less of similar shape as medial segments; medial leaflets 1–9 mm wide

c14.text: Trophophore conspicuously stalked, the stalk often equal to or longer than the distance between the lower pairs of leaflets; trophophore leaflets entire to crenulate or, less frequently, notched, the lower ones spreading to ascending; branches of sporophore spreading to ascending, not or barely overlapping at maturity; mature sporophore with a stalk (0.5–) 1 or more times as long as the trophophore

Trophophore short-stalked, the stalk often shorter than the distance between the lower pairs of leaflets; trophophore leaflets entire to dentate or symmetrically lobed, the lower ones ascending; branches of sporophore ascending to erect (rarely spreading), somewhat to strongly overlapping at maturity; mature sporophore subsessile or short-stalked, the stalk usually shorter than the length of the trophophore

c15.text: Stalk of sporophore usually 0.25–0.5 (–1) times as long as the trophophore; trophophore green to bright yellow-green in life, not clasping to loosely clasping the sporophore at maturity, with narrow-cuneate to oblong leaflets, the lowest pair sometimes with sporangia; rachis of trophophore relatively narrow, up to 0.25 times as wide as the entire trophophore; plants moderately short, commonly 10–15 cm tall, without spherical gemmae at the root bases

Stalk of sporophore less than 0.25 times as long as the trophophore; trophophore pale green to glaucous-green in life, loosely to tightly clasping the sporophore at maturity, with linear to narrow-cuneate segments, the lowest pair almost never with sporangia; rachis of trophophore often relatively broad, up to 0.35 times as wide as the entire trophophore; plants very short and compact, rarely taller than 6 cm, sometimes with minute, spherical gemmae at the root bases

c1.text: This genus contains exactly one species.
Fertile leaflets produced in the middle of the blade, with sterile leaflets basal and apical; leaflets lobed, but not divided to the costae
Fertile leaflets produced at the apex of the blade; leaflets divided

Ultimate segments of leaves ± oblong, rounded to obtuse at the apex [Fig. ], in the same plane with the axis of the blade, thin-herbaceous to herbaceous, bright green to yellow-green; leaf blades lax and arching; plants primarily of rich, mesic forests

Ultimate segments of leaves ± triangular, acute to obtuse at the apex [Fig. ], twisted out of the plane of the axis of the blade (but usually in plane with the blade axis in shaded plants), firm-herbaceous to chartaceous, medium green to blue-green (often bright green in the shade); leaf blades usually stiff and upright (lax in shaded plants); plants of serpentine rocks and soil

c2.text: Medial ultimate segments of leaves on stalks 0.3–1.3 mm long, most stalks shorter than 0.9 mm; false indusia 0.8–2.9 (–3.4) mm long; rhizomes frequently branching and congested, with internodes 1–2 mm long

Medial ultimate segments of leaves on stalks (0.4–) 0.6–1.5 (–1.9) mm long, most stalks longer than 0.9 mm; false indusia 2–5 (–10) mm long; rhizomes occasionally branching (rarely congested), with internodes 4–7.5 mm long

c1.text: This genus contains exactly one species.
This genus contains exactly one species.

Petiole, rachis, and abaxial surface of ultimate segments pubescent with short, curly hairs; leaflet stalks emerging at right angles to the rachis; ultimate segments of fertile leaves mostly 10–75 mm long; leaves hemidimorphic—the fertile leaves larger and with longer ultimate segments

Petiole and rachis glabrous or nearly so, the abaxial surface of ultimate segments glabrous except for occasional hair-like scales near the midrib; leaflet stalks ascending; ultimate segments of fertile leaves mostly 5–20 mm long; leaves essentially monomorphic

This genus contains exactly one species.

Basal leaflets mostly 10–20 cm long, connected to the adjacent pair by a wing; scales on costae narrowly lanceolate, white to light brown, usually 3–5 cells wide at the base; larger leaflets with evidently lobed segments; middle leaflet veins forked or pinnate

Basal leaflets mostly 3–10 cm long, not connected to next pair; scales on costae ovate-lanceolate, brown, usually 6–12 cells wide at the base; larger leaflets with entire or crenate segments; middle leaflet veins often simple
Leaf blades elliptic, gradually reduced in width through the basal half of the blade, lacking red to orange resin glands; indument of rachis, costae, and costules composed of hairs up to 1 mm long
Leaf blades lanceolate to broad-lanceolate, only somewhat reduced in the basal portion, with numerous, red to orange resin glands; indument of rachis, costae, and costules of hairs 0.2–0.4 mm long

This genus contains exactly one species.

Petioles not articulated, therefore the persistent petiole bases of various lengths; leafules dentate with pointed teeth; petiole scales bicolored, with a dark central region; leaf blades (8–) 20–60 cm long

Petioles articulated, therefore the persistent petiole bases mostly of equal length, the articulation point noticeable as a slightly swollen node; leafules entire to crenate; petiole scales concolored; leaf blades 2.5–22 (–25) cm long

c2.text: Plants glabrous, with sessile glands; basal leaflets flabellate; leaf blades 1–1.5 cm wide; petioles green to light brown
Plants with hairs, scales, and/or stalked glands; basal leaflets narrowly ovate to deltate; leaf blades 1–3 cm wide; petioles brown to dark brown

c3.text: Leaflets glabrous or nearly so on the abaxial surface (though scales may be present on the rachis and costae), the larger leaflets with 2 or 3 pairs of leafules; indusium composed of few filaments
Leaflets with scales on the abaxial surface, the larger leaflets with 4–7 pairs of leafules; indusium composed of many filaments

c1.text: Leaf stipitate-glandular on petiole, rachis, and abaxial blade surface; basal leaflets and basiscopic leafules curving toward apex of plant [Fig. ]
Leaf essentially glabrous; basal leaflets and basiscopic leafules spreading, not curving toward plant apex (except in some epipetric populations)

Rachises, costae, and indusia sparsely to densely stipitate-glandular; bulbils often present on the abaxial blade surface (these rare and misshapen in C. laurentiana ); leaf blades widest at or near base
Rachises, costae, and indusia without glandular hairs; plants lacking bulbils; blade lanceolate to elliptic

c2.text: Leaf blade triangular to long-triangular; bulbils frequently present; leaf rachis, costae, costules, and ultimate segments usually with dense glandular hairs; spores mostly 33–38 μm in diameter

Leaf blade ovate to narrow-ovate; bulbils only rarely present, misshapen; leaf rachis, costae, costules, and ultimate segments with sparse glandular hairs (these often absent from herbarium specimens); spores mostly 49–60 μm in diameter

c3.text: Leaves clustered 1–4 cm behind the apex of the rhizome; rhizome pubescent, especially toward apex, with yellow hairs; leafules, especially those of the basal medial portion of the blade, borne on evident stalks; petiole green to stramineous, with dark pigmentation only at the very base; spores mostly 28–34 μm in diameter

Leaves clustered near rhizome apex; rhizome lacking hairs; leafules varying from sessile to short-stalked; petiole with dark brown color not confined to the base, the pigmentation extending apically for a noticeable distance;

c4.text: Basal leafules sessile or nearly so, broadly tapering or rounded at the base, approximate, emerging nearly perpendicular to the costa [Fig. ]; apical portion of blade with deltate to ovate leaflets; margins of leafules serrate; acroscopic margin of leaflet convex due to the fact that the costa of the leaflet is nearly straight; indusia up to 1 mm long

Basal leafules short-stalked, mostly cuneate at the base, remote, emerging at an acute angle to the costa (i.e., ascending) [Fig. ]; apical portion of blade with ovate to narrowly elliptic leaflets; margins of leafules crenate; acroscopic margin of leaflet concave due to the fact that the costa of the leaflet curves slightly upward; indusia up to 0.5 mm long

c1.text: Leaf variegated, such that the distal portion of the leaflets (or much of the plant) suffused with gray to silver
Leaf not variegated, the blade green

c2.text: Petiole scales brown to black-brown; leaf blades elliptic, narrowed to the base, broadest near or just below the middle; leaflets sessile or short-stalked; leafules linear to oblong; indusia ciliate with non-glandular hairs (though the sporangial stalks do have glandular hairs); spores yellow

Petiole scales light brown to brown; leaf blades broad-lanceolate to lanceolate, only slightly narrowed to the base, broadest just above the base; leaflets generally stalked; leafules oblong-lanceolate to narrow-triangular; indusia ciliate with glandular or non-glandular hairs; spores dark brown

c1.text: This genus contains exactly one species.
This genus contains exactly one species.
Leaves once-divided, the fertile leaflets contracted and reduced in size compared with the sterile leaflets; sori often confluent and nearly covering the abaxial leaflet surface
Leaves twice-divided in the basal portion, the fertile leaflets like the sterile and not contracted; sori distinct, not covering the entire abaxial leafule surface
Leaf blades mostly 6–25 cm long, with aromatic glands, densely scaly abaxially; indusia often overlapping
Leaf blades 15–120 cm long, mostly more than 25 cm, lacking aromatic glands (but sometimes with stipitate glands), with few or no abaxial scales; indusia separate

c2.text: Leaf blades (2–) 2.5- to 3.5-times divided near base; leaf segments with bristle- tipped teeth
Leaf blades 1.5- to 2-times divided near base; leaf segments with or without bristle-tipped teeth

c3.text: First basiscopic (i.e., lower) leafule of basal leaflet no longer than adjacent basiscopic leafule and less than 2 times as long as first acroscopic (i.e., upper) leafule of basal leaflet [Fig. ]; plant axes and indusia with glandular hairs; leaf blades remaining green through the winter

First basiscopic leafule of basal leaflet longer than adjacent basiscopic leafule and 2–5 times as long as first acroscopic leafule of basal leaflet [Figs. , ]; plants without glandular hairs (rarely with a few glandular hairs in D. campyloptera ); leaf blades senescing in the fall

c4.text: First pair of leafules of basal leaflet nearly opposite, not more than 4 mm apart, the basiscopic leafule 2 (–3) times the length of the acroscopic one [Fig. ]; blade ovate-lanceolate
First pair of leafules of basal leaflet offset 4–15 mm, the basiscopic leafule (2–) 3–5 times the length of the acroscopic one [Fig. ]; blade ovate-deltate

c5.text: Sori borne at or near margins of leaf segments; leaf blades blue-green; petioles with a dense tuft of white-brown scales at the base
Sori borne between margins and midrib of leaf segments; leaf blades green; petioles with scattered light to dark brown scales

c6.text: Plants with scales of 2 distinct types—one broad, one hair-like; scales abundant on petiole, rachis, and costae; leaves with 20–30 pairs of leaflets; petiole length up to 0.25 times the length of the blade

Plants with scales of various sizes, mostly broad, but not of 2 distinct sizes; scales abundant on only the petiole; leaves with 10–25 pairs of leaflets; petiole length 0.25–0.35 times the length of the blade

c7.text: Scales of the petiole dark brown to black, with a pale border; sori borne close to midrib; basal leaflets ovate-oblong; teeth of leaf segments not bristle-tipped

Scales of the petiole light brown (sometimes dark brown in the center in D. clintoniana ); sori borne midway between margin and midrib; basal leaflets triangular to elongate-triangular; teeth of leaf segments bristle-tipped

c8.text: Fertile leaves deciduous, their leaflets twisted, parallel to the horizon, noticeably larger and more erect than the persistent sterile leaves; basal leaflets triangular to broad-triangular
Fertile leaves persistent, their leaflets not twisted, parallel to the leaf axis, only slightly different from the sterile leaves; basal leaflets narrow-triangular to oblong-triangular

c1.text: Leaves whorled, not concealing the branchlet, monomorphic; seed cones axillary
Leaves opposite, closely imbricate and concealing the young branchlets, dimorphic—longer, subulate ones (i.e., juvenile) and shorter, scale-like ones (i.e., adult); seed cones borne terminally

c2.text: Plants prostrate shrubs with erect branches, up to 0.3 m high; strobilus with a usually curved stalk, 6–8 (–10) mm long, containing 3–5 seeds; apex of scale-like leaves apiculate

Plants upright shrubs or trees, to 15 m tall (rarely depressed in exposed situations); strobilus with a usually straight stalk, 3–6 (–8) mm long, containing 1 or 2 (–3) seeds; apex of scale-like leaves merely acute or with a very obscure apiculus

c1.text: This genus contains exactly one species.
This genus contains exactly one species.
Branchlets spreading; bark of main stem shedding as small, irregular scales; seed cones 1–2 cm long, with 10–15 (–30) scales that are glabrous abaxially [Fig. ]
Branchlets pendulous; bark of main stem shedding as large, plate-like scales; seed cones 2–3.5 cm long, with 40–50 scales that are pubescent abaxially
Leaves in fascicles of 5, with 1 fibrovascular bundle in cross-section; bud scales with entire margins; seed cones 8–20 cm long; umbo terminal
Leaves in fascicles of 2 or 3, with 2 fibrovascular bundles in cross-section; bud scales fringed on the margin; seed cones 3–10 cm long; umbo dorsal

c2.text: Leaves in fascicles of 3; apophyses of mature seed cones red-brown (fading on older, fallen cones)
Leaves in fascicles of 2; apophyses of mature seed cones cream to light brown or gray, or red-brown in P. resinosa

c3.text: Leaves (7–) 9–16 cm long, straight or only slightly twisted; seed cones symmetric, with a straight axis and without unequal development of apophyses
Leaves 2–7 (–8) cm long, noticeably twisted (relatively straight in the planted P. mugo ); seed cones ± asymmetric, with a curved axis and/or obviously unequal development of apophyses on one side

c4.text: Leaves brittle, tending to break when bent; winter buds red-brown; smaller branches orange-brown; seed cones, when falling, leaving some of the basal scales on the branch (i.e., the seed cone hollow-based); umbo unarmed

Leaves pliable, tending not to break when bent; winter buds gray; smaller branches brown to gray-brown; seed cones falling with all the scales intact; umbo armed with a slender prickle (though the prickle often deciduous)

c5.text: Winter buds resinous; growth habit relatively uniform and often with an unbranched main stem; seed cones sessile, with a ± rounded base
Winter buds not resinous; growth habit irregular, the main stem and branches often forked; seed cones stalked, with a ± truncate base

c6.text: Umbo encircled by a thin, dark gray to nearly black ring; low, multi-stemmed shrubs; leaves relatively straight
Umbo without a dark ring; upright, single-stemmed, short to tall trees; leaves twisted

c7.text: Leaves 3–7 cm long, glaucous; larger branches orange-brown; seed cones usually falling after second winter; apophyses elongating toward base of seed cone on one side
Leaves 2–3.5 (–5) cm long, not glaucous; larger branches gray-brown; seed cones serotinous, persisting on plant for many years; apophyses all ± of equal size [Fig. ]

c1.text: Branches deeply grooved, especially the 2- and 3-year-old ones
Branches ungrooved or scarcely grooved

c2.text: Leaves 1.2–2.5 cm long, dark green and hardly (if at all) glaucous; seed cones 4–7 cm long; resin canals of leaves median, located well away from either epidermis (this character best viewed in cross-section with a 20 × hand lens)
Leaves (1.5–) 4–6 cm long, glaucous on both surfaces; seed cones 7–12 cm long; resin canals of leaves located near the abaxial epidermis

c1.text: This genus contains exactly one species.
This genus contains exactly one species.
Seed cones 12–16 cm long; scales elliptic to rhombic, widest near the middle; branches conspicuously pendulous; branchlets red-brown
Seed cones 1.5–6 cm long; scales flabellate, widest at or very near the apex; branches ascending to spreading; branchlets light brown to pink-brown or yellow-brown

c2.text: Branchlets glabrous and glaucous, light brown to pink-brown; seed cones 3–6 cm long; scale apex entire [Fig. ]; winter buds rounded at apex
Branchlets pubescent, not glaucous, yellow-brown; seed cones 1.5–4.5 (–5) cm long; scale apex slightly erose to evidently and irregularly toothed; winter buds acute at apex

c3.text: Pubescence of branchlets, in part, glandular [Fig. ]; leaves gray-green, dull, glaucous; winter buds 3–3.9 mm long, gray-brown; seed cones 1.5–2.5 (–3.5) cm long, persisting on plant for many years; scale apex irregularly toothed

Pubescence of branchlets entirely eglandular; leaves yellow to dark green, lustrous, not glaucous; winter buds 5–8 mm long, red-brown; seed cones 2.3–4.5 (–5) cm long, usually falling from plant by first winter; scale apex erose [Fig. ]

c1.text: Thalli ovoid to globose, 1–1.5 times as deep as wide, without pigment cells in the vegetative tissue, thus the upper surface transparently green in life
Thalli boat-shaped (i.e., flattened above and rounded below) [Figs. , ], 0.3–1 times as deep as wide, with pigment cells in the vegetative tissue, thus the upper surface intensely green in life

c2.text: Thalli rounded at each apex, with a large, prominent papilla in the center of the upper surface, 1–1.5 times as long as wide [Fig. ]
Thalli with a minute, upward-bent point at each apex, lacking a central papilla, 1.3–2 times as long as wide [Fig. ]

c1.text: This genus contains exactly one species.
This genus contains exactly one species.
This genus contains exactly one species.

Thalli (3–) 6–15 mm long, tapering to a long stalk, with distally denticulate margins; lateral thalli remaining attached to the parent thallus by a narrow, green stalk, forming tangled colonies suspended just below the surface of the water
Thalli 1–6 (–8) mm long, sessile or nearly so, with entire margins; lateral thalli separating from the parent thallus or remaining attached by a thin, white stipe and forming floating rosettes

c2.text: Mature thalli with a single vein (the vein sometimes obscure and then the thallus appearing unveined)
Mature thalli with 3 (–5) veins

c3.text: Vein usually not extending past aerenchyma tissue, extending less than of distance from root node to tip of thallus; thalli 1–2.5 (–4) mm long, 1–2 times as long as broad, broad-elliptic to broad-oblong or obovate, usually solitary or paired, symmetrical at the base

Vein usually extending past aerenchyma tissue, extending at least of the distance from the root node to the tip of the thallus; thalli 2–4 mm long, 1.3–3 times as long as wide, elliptic to lanceolate or obovate, often in clusters of (2–) 4–8 (–10), asymmetrical at the base

c4.text: Root sheath winged at base; roots up to 3.5 cm long, usually sharply pointed at apex; thalli without anthocyanic pigment, usually with a distinct apical papilla

Root sheath not winged at base; roots to 15 cm long, frequently longer than 3.5 cm, rounded at apex; thalli often with at least some spotting or diffuse coloring with anthocyanic pigment, with or without a distinct apical papilla

c5.text: Plants sometimes with small green-brown to brown rootless turions, these 0.8–1.6 mm in diameter and sinking to bottom; thalli often with anthocyanic coloration on lower surface, the coloration more intense than that of upper surface, usually with a distinct row of minute papillae along the midvein

Plants without turions; thalli typically green on lower surface, when slightly anthocyanic, the coloration less intense than that of upper surface, with or without a distinct row of minute papillae along the midvein

c1.text: Leaves with 3 (–5) leaflets; spadix 3–9 cm long, apically blunt, much shorter than the spathe; spathe 6–16 cm long
Leaves with (5–) 7–13 (–21) leaflets; spadix 6–20 cm long, tapering to a slender point, much longer than the spathe; spathe 3–6 (–12) cm long
This genus contains exactly one species.
This genus contains exactly one species.
This genus contains exactly one species.
This genus contains exactly one species.
Flowers occurring singly (rarely paired) at the tips of branches
Flowers clustered in glomerules of 3–12 (–20), the glomerules all at the tips of branches or 1 or 2 of the central ones sessile (rarely all congested) [Figs. , , ]

c2.text: Inflorescence an umbel-like cyme, with simple or once-forked branches; seeds with a conspicuous caruncle; plants of low-elevation woodlands, edges, and forest openings, flowering in April through early June
Inflorescence a branched dichasial cyme, with several-forked branches; seeds with a tuft of hairs; plants primarily of boreal and subalpine habitats, flowering from mid-June through July

c3.text: Flowers in 3- to 6-flowered glomerules, these arranged in an open-branched, dichasial cyme; tepals white (rarely pink)
Flowers mostly in 5- to 12-flowered glomerules, these arranged in an umbel-like or spike-like cyme; tepals light brown to dark brown (rarely nearly white)

c4.text: Leaves involute, pointed at the tip; bracts subtending individual glomerules of flowers with conspicuously long-ciliate margins; caruncles of seeds inconspicuous, up to 0.2 mm long; branches of inflorescence, when present, arching or drooping; plants of alpine and subalpine habitats

Leaves ± flat, usually with a blunt, callous tip (the callous tip obscure in L. echinata ); bracts subtending individual glomerules entire or sparingly lacerate-margined; caruncles of seeds mostly conspicuous, 0.2–0.7 mm long; branches of inflorescence ± straight [Figs. , ]; plants of low-elevation habitats

c5.text: Well-developed inflorescences nodding [Fig. ]; bracts subtending glomerules of flowers with long, slender tips, often projecting beyond the glomerules
Inflorescences congested or with arching branches, not nodding; bracts subtending glomerules of flowers obtuse to acuminate at apex, not projecting beyond the glomerules

c6.text: Leaves with a minute point at the tip, the calloused apex narrow and obscure; anther 2–4 times as long as the filament
Leaves with a blunt, rounded tip, the calloused apex evident; anther not more than 2 times as long as filament (except in L. campestris , a rare introduction)

c7.text: Plants bearing pale, swollen leaf bases that appear as bublets [Fig. ]
Plants without pale, swollen leaf bases

c8.text: Stems solitary or a few together; plants with short but evident rhizomes; anther 2–6 times as long as the filament
Stems loosely to densely cepsitose; plants without evident rhizomes; anther 1–2 times as long as the filament or shorter

c9.text: Seeds 0.7–1 mm long, with a caruncle 0.2–0.3 mm long; tepals 1.5–2.6 mm long, clear to pale brown; styles 0.2–0.3 mm long
Seeds 1.1–1.7 mm long, with a caruncle 0.2–0.6 mm long; tepals (2–) 2.5–3.5 mm long, nearly white to dark brown; styles 0.4–0.7 mm long

c1.text: Involucral bract solitary, of similar cross-sectional shape as the stem and appearing to be a continuation of it, therefore, the inflorescence appearing to emerge from the side of the stem (i.e., pseudolateral) [Figs. , ]; leaves bladeless, consisting of sheaths only
Involucral bracts usually 2 or more, differentiated from the stem in some manner, the inflorescence appearing terminal [Fig. ]; leaves with blades

c2.text: Stems cespitose; flowers with 3 stamens (or with 6 stamens in the rare introduction J. inflexus )
Stems produced singly or a few together from an elongate rhizome; flowers with 6 stamens

c3.text: Capsules red-brown to dark brown, (2.5–) 3–4 mm long; stamens numbering 6 per flower, with filaments 0.8–1.5 mm long and anthers 0.8–1 mm long; stems prominently glaucous in life
Capsules tan to green-tan or brown, 1.5–3.2 mm long; stamens numbering 3 per flower, with filaments 0.5–0.8 mm long and anthers 0.5–0.8 mm long; stems green

c4.text: Apical portion of stem relatively lustrous, smooth or nearly so below the inflorescence, the (25–) 30–60 longitudinal striations inconspicuous until drying [Fig. ]; ridges of dried stems capped with dull, low cells
Apical portion of stem relatively dull, evidently ridged below the inflorescence with mostly 10–30 longitudinal grooves [Fig. ]; ridges of dried stems capped with lustrous, papillose cells

c5.text: Involucral bract swollen at the base of the inflorescence, sometimes somewhat reflexed in fruit; leaf sheaths with red-brown bases, the upper ones 15–23 cm long; inflorescence compact, mostly 10–25 mm in diameter; stems with 12–30 longitudinal ridges; tepals spreading from the base in fruit

Involucral bract not swollen, erect in fruit; leaf sheaths with dark red-brown to purple-black bases, the upper ones 5–12 cm long; inflorescence relatively open, mostly 15–80 mm in diameter; stems with 10–20 longitudinal ridges [Fig. ]; tepals ascending or appressed to the capsule in fruit

c6.text: Anthers 3–5 times as long as the filaments; tepals usually with a dark stripe on each side of the midvein [Fig. ]; stems smooth in life, irregularly wrinkled when dry
Anthers 0.3–0.5 times as long as the filaments; tepals lacking dark stripes; stems finely grooved

c7.text: Flowers occurring singly on pedicels [Fig. ]; leaves variously flat to terete, never septate; bracteoles present, these a pair of small bracts at the base of the flowers in addition to the pair of bracts at the base of the pedicels

Flowers borne in glomerules (sometimes solitary in J. pelocarpus and J. subtilis ); leaves both terete and septate (except in J. biflorus , J. ensifolius , J. marginatus , and J. stygius ); bracteoles absent, flowers subtended by only a pair of bracts at the base of the pedicel

c8.text: Plants annual with fibrous roots; inflorescence often occupying 33–90% of the total plant height; leaves without auricles
Plants perennial; inflorescences rarely occupying more than 25% of the total plant height; leaves with auricles

c9.text: Inner tepals acute to acuminate, exceeding the capsule [Fig. ]; capsules mostly acute to subacute at apex (rarely truncate); inflorescences relatively open
Inner tepals rounded to acute at the apex, many equaling or shorter than the capsule [Fig. ]; capsules mostly truncate at apex; inflorescences relatively dense

c10.text: Auricles erose; inflorescence of 1–3 flowers; capsules with a beak up to 0.7 mm long; margins of leaf blades minutely serrulate
Auricles entire; inflorescence with several to many flowers; capsules usually beakless (rarely shortly beaked; e.g., J. gerardii ); margins of leaf blades entire

c11.text: Leaves terete or caniculate; tepals shorter than and appressed to the capsule; capsules 3-locular, the septa meeting in the middle

Leaves flat or becoming involute (nearly terete in some J. dichotomus ); tepals equal to or longer than the capsule (often shorter in J. compressus ), ascending to spreading; capsules partially 3-locular, the septa not meeting in the center or 3-locular in J. gerardii and J. secundus

c12.text: Seeds with inconspicuous pale tails at each end less than 0.2 mm long; capsules 2.9–3.5 (–4) mm long, brown to dark brown; inner tepals mostly 1.9–3.4 mm long
Seeds with conspicuous, slender, slightly curved pale tails at each end 0.2–0.4 mm long; capsules (3.3–) 3.8–4.7 mm long, golden brown to light brown; inner tepals mostly 3.2–4 mm long

c13.text: Leaves not confined to the base of the stem, some borne on the upper of the stem; tepals with a dark-stripe on each side of the midvein, the outer with an obtuse apex; stems produced singly or a few together from elongate rhizomes (varying to subcespitose in J. compressus ); plants of saline habitats
Leaves confined primarily to the lower of the stem; tepals lacking dark stripes, the outer acuminate at the apex; stems cespitose; plants of non-saline habitats

c14.text: Anthers 1.1–1.6 (–1.8) mm long, 2–4 times as long as the filament; capsules usually shorter than to equaling the length of the tepals; primary bract of the inflorescence mostly 1–5 cm long, usually not conspicuously exceeding the inflorescence

Anthers 0.6–1 mm long, 1–2 times as long as the filament; capsules usually exceeding the tepals; primary bract of the inflorescence 2–7.5 (–13) cm long, often conspicuously exceeding the inflorescence

c15.text: Auricles scarious, (1–) 1.5–5 mm long; sheath margin pliable, transparent
Auricles scarious to cartilaginous, 0.2–0.6 mm long; sheath margin of firmer texture, often brittle, transparent to opaque

c16.text: Monochasial branches of inflorescence erect to divergent, with crowded to remote flowers, the internodes less than 6 mm long [Fig. ]; ultimate branches of monochasia 1–2 cm long; tepals (2.8–) 3.5–4.5 mm long; capsules more than 75% of the length of the tepals [Fig. ]; plants usually shorter than 7 dm

Monochasial branches of inflorescence erect to ascending, often with inwardly curving branches, with widely scattered flowers, the internodes 6 mm or longer [Fig. ]; ultimate branches of monochasia mostly 3–5 cm long; tepals 2.5–3.5 (–4) mm long; capsules less than 75% of the length of the tepals [Fig. ]; plants mostly 7–9 dm tall

c17.text: Capsule 3-locular; placentation axile; leaves relatively short, often not exceeding midpoint of stem
Capsules only partially 3-locular, the incomplete septa not meeting in the center; placentation parietal; leaves usually extending past midpoint of stem

c18.text: Leaves caniculate to nearly terete, rarely flat; inflorescence varying from compact to open and diffuse, usually with 10–35 or more flowers
Leaves flat, though often involute in age or drying; inflorescence usually compact and few-flowered, often with 10 or fewer flowers, rarely more than 15

c19.text: Leaf blades compressed and equitant (i.e., set edge to stem), imperfectly septate (i.e., the septa inconspicuous and not continuous through the blade width)
Leaf blades elliptic to terete in cross-section, septate (imperfectly septate in J. stygius ) or flat and non-septate, never equitant

c20.text: Capsules 5.5–7 (–9) mm long; seeds 2.8–3.5 mm long including the white tails; leaves terete to elliptic in cross-section, imperfectly septate
Capsules 1.5–5.2 mm long; seeds 0.3–1.9 mm long; leaves either flat or both terete and septate

c21.text: Leaves flat, without septa; capsules subglobose, often with red flecks [Fig. ]
Leaves terete and septate; capsules mostly obloid to ellipsoid or ovoid, without red flecks

c22.text: Widest leaf blades (1.3–) 1.6–2.6 (–3.5) mm wide; anthers (0.2–) 0.3–0.5 (–0.7) mm long, concealed by the tepals; tallest stems (19.2–) 26–44 (–56.8) cm tall; sheath of lowest leaf (17–) 22–38 (–47) mm long; base of stem (0.4–) 2–4.4 (–6) mm thick; inflorescence with (2–) 5–15 (–30) glomerules

Widest leaf blades (2.6–) 3.1–4.5 (­­–5.4) mm wide; anthers (0.5–) 0.6–1 (–1.3) mm long, exserted beyond tepals; tallest stems (27.2–) 50.8–81.2 (–100.7) cm tall; sheath of lowest leaf (32–) 43–78 (–97) mm long; base of stem (3.4–) 5.8–9.6 (–12) mm thick; inflorescence with 20–100 (–200) glomerules

c23.text: Seeds 0.7–1.9 mm long including the pale tails at each end [Fig. ], the body of the seed covered with a translucent, pale white veil (note: view at 20 × magnification); flowers usually with 3 stamens
Seeds 0.3–0.7 mm long, merely pointed at the ends, the body clear yellow-brown to red-brown; flowers with 3 or 6 stamens

c24.text: Seeds 1.1–1.9 mm long, each tail 50–80% as long as the seed body [Fig. ]; glomerules 5- to 50-flowered
Seeds 0.7–1.2 mm long, each tail 10–40% as long as the seed body; glomerules 2- to 10-flowered, rarely with as many as 20 flowers in J. subcaudatus

c25.text: Outer tepals obtuse to subacute at the apex, soft, with conspicuous scarious margins, 1.8­–2.5 mm long; capsules 2.4–3.8 mm long
Outer tepals sharply acute to acuminate, rigid, with narrow scarious margins, 2.1–3.2 mm long; capsules 3–4.8 mm long

c26.text: Branches of inflorescence erect to strictly ascending; capsules 3.2–4.8 mm long, prominently exserted, extending more than 0.7 mm beyond perianth; glomerules with 2–5 (–7) flowers
Branches of inflorescence widely ascending to spreading; capsules 3–3.8 mm long, weakly to prominently exserted, not exceeding tepals by more than 0.6 (–1.3) mm; glomerules with 2–10 (–20) flowers

c27.text: Flowers solitary or paired, sometimes replaced by vegetative bulbils [Fig. ]
Flowers in glomerules of 2–100, not replaced by bulbils

c28.text: Stems upright; inflorescences many-flowered; outer tepals 1.6–2.3 mm long
Stems creeping or floating; entire plant with only 1–3 flowers; outer tepals (1.8–) 2.2–2.8 mm long

c29.text: Leaves dimorphic—those produced by the rhizome submersed and capillary, those produced by the stem emergent and thicker; lowest stem leaf overtopping inflorescence, 3–6 mm thick at midpoint
Leaves monomorphic, none capillary and produced by the rhizome; lowest stem leaf shorter than height of plant, mostly 0.5–3 mm thick

c30.text: Glomerules spheric or subspheric, comprised of (6–) 10–100 flowers
Glomerules hemispheric to obconic, comprised of 2–20 flowers

c31.text: Inflorescences composed of 24–60 glomerules; inner tepals obtuse to subacute at the apex
Inflorescences composed of 1–23 glomerules; inner tepals acuminate at the apex

c32.text: Plants cespitose, without elongate rhizomes; tepals lanceolate to narrow-ovate (in part)
Plants not cespitose, the stems produced singly or a few together from elongate rhizomes; tepals subulate

c33.text: Flowers with usually 3 stamens; capsules included within the perianth, the tips of the valves separate after dehiscence
Flowers with usually 6 stamens; capsules equaling tepals to exserted, the tips of the valves often cohering after dehiscence

c34.text: Auricles 0.5–1 (–1.7) mm long, cartilaginous, dark yellow; glomerules composed of 6–25 (–30) flowers; inner and outer tepals of ± similar length
Auricles (1–) 2–4 mm long, scarious, pale brown; glomerules composed of 25–100 flowers; inner tepals shorter than outer tepals

c35.text: Flowers with usually 3 stamens; plants cespitose; capsules light brown, 1-locular

Flowers with usually 6 stamens; plants not cespitose, produced singly or a few together from elongate rhizomes (sometimes subcespitose in J. articulatus ); capsules brown to dark brown, imperfectly 3-locular (i.e., the septa not extending all the way to the center)

c36.text: Capsule approximately equal in length to tepals; glomerules composed of 5–20 (or more) flowers (in part)
Capsule evidently exserted beyond tepals; glomerules composed of 2–10 flowers

c37.text: Capsules 2.8–3.7 (–4.2) mm long, approximately 1.3–1.5 times as long as the tepals; outer tepals 1.8–2.3(–2.5) mm long
Capsules 4–5.2 mm long, approximately 2 times as long as the tepals; outer tepals (2–)2.6–3.2 mm long

c38.text: Capsules rounded to obtuse at apex, with a mucronate tip [Fig. ]; inner tepals acute to obtuse at apex [Fig. ]; branches of inflorescence strictly ascending
Capsules acute (seldom obtuse) at apex; inner tepals acute to acuminate at apex; branches of inflorescence widely ascending to spreading

c1.text: This genus contains exactly one species.

Stipular sheaths open with overlapping edges; leaf blades commonly acute at the apex, with an apiculus on young plants; stigma borne on a short style, the style persistent on the achene and forming a tiny beak on mature drupes; drupes 3–4.5 mm long
Stipular sheaths closed; leaf blades commonly blunt to obtuse at the apex, sometimes retuse, rarely apiculate; stigma broad and sessile, not forming a beak on mature drupes; drupes 2–3 mm long
Submersed leaf blades narrower than 4 mm wide
