Submersed leaf blades 4 mm wide or wider (those of the axillary shoots may be narrower in some species)

c2.text: Submersed leaf blades with the stipule basally fused to the blade, only the tip of the stipule distinct from the blade [Fig. ]; drupe with an embryo coiled more than 1 full spiral [Fig. ]
Submersed leaf blades with stipules that are distinct from the blade for their entire length [Fig. ]; drupe with an embryo coiled 1 full spiral or less [Fig. ]

c3.text: Submersed leaf blades 0.1–0.4 mm wide, the apex acute to long-tapering; fused portion of the stipule usually shorter than the distinct portion; apex of floating leaves acute
Submersed leaf blades 0.5–2 mm wide, the apex obtuse to acute; fused portion of the stipule usually equal to or longer than the distinct portion; apex of floating leaves obtuse

c4.text: Floating leaves, which are thicker and greatly expanded in width compared with the submersed leaves, produced and generally present on some of the plants in each colony [Fig. ]
Floating leaves not produced, all the leaves submerged [Figs. , ]

c5.text: Floating leaf blades 6–15 mm long, 5- to 9-veined; submersed leaf blades 0.1–1 mm wide, thin, transparent, lacking lacunar cells; spikes (3–) 6–8 mm long; drupes 1.5–2.5 mm long

Floating leaf blades 15–120 mm long, 7- to 37-veined; submersed leaf blades 0.25–10 mm wide, either with abundant lacunar cells or with thick and nearly opaque texture; spikes 10–50 mm long; drupes (2–) 2.5–4.5 mm long

c6.text: Submersed leaf blades (1–) 2–10 mm wide, thin, transparent, with prominent bands of lacunar cells 1–2 mm wide on each side of the midrib [Fig. ]; drupes with abaxial and lateral keels (in part)
Submersed leaf blades 0.25–2 mm wide, thick and nearly opaque, petiole-like, lacking lacunar cells; drupes with only an abaxial keel

c7.text: Submersed leaf blades 0.8–2 mm wide; floating leaf blades 5–10 ×2.5–6 cm, usually subcordate to rounded at the base [Fig. ]; petioles pale at the apex; stipules 4–10 cm long; drupes 3.5–5 mm long, deeply wrinkled on each side, with an inconspicuous abaxial keel

Submersed leaf blades 0.25–1 mm wide; floating leaf blades 2.5–6 ×1–3 cm, cuneate to rounded at the base; petioles usually lacking a pale band at the apex; stipules 2.5–4 cm long; drupes 2–3.5 mm long, not wrinkled on the sides, with a prominent abaxial keel

c8.text: Rhizome elongate; peduncles (3–) 5–25 cm long [Fig. ]; leaf blades 0.1–0.5 mm wide, 1-veined
Rhizome scarcely developed (elongate in P. foliosus ); peduncles 0.5–6 cm long [Fig. ]; leaf blades 0.2–5 mm wide, 1- to 35-veined

c9.text: Stems conspicuously compressed; leaf blades 15- to 25 (–35)-veined; spikes with 7–11 whorls of flowers; drupes 4–4.5 mm long (in part)
Stems terete or slightly compressed; leaf blades 1- to 13-veined; spikes with 1–5 whorls of flowers; drupes 1.5–3.5 mm long

c10.text: Nodal glands absent (very rarely present); spikes 1.5–7 mm long, with 1 or 2 whorls of flowers [Fig. ]; drupes with a conspicuous abaxial keel
Nodal glands present on at least some of the nodes [Fig. ]; spikes 2–18 mm long, with 1–5 whorls of flowers; drupes without an abaxial keel (sometimes with a low keel in P. obtusifolius )

c11.text: Leaf blades acute at apex; drupes 1.4–2.3 (–2.7) mm long, with a single, wing-like and undulate dorsal keel to 0.4 mm tall; peduncles 3–11 (–37) mm long
Leaf blades bristle-tipped (rarely only apiculate or blunt) [Fig. ]; drupes 2.3–4 mm long, with 3 keels, the dorsal keel ridge-like, to 0.2 mm tall; peduncles 6–14 mm long

c12.text: Stipules fibrous, white (brown in P. ogdenii )
Stipules delicate, not fibrous, green, brown, or white

c13.text: Leaf blades obtuse to rounded at the apex, sometimes with an apiculus; winter buds with inner leaves oriented at a right angle to the outer leaves, the outer leaves corrugated at the base, the inner leaves modified into a fan-shaped structure [Fig. ]

Leaf blades obtuse to attenuate at the apex; winter buds flattened, the inner and outer leaves oriented in the same plane, the outer leaves not corrugated at the base (rarely corrugated in P. strictifolius ), the inner leaves undifferentiated or modified into a fusiform structure [Fig. ]

c14.text: Leaf blades with 3–5 (–7) veins, 0.6–2 mm wide, without lacunae; stipules usually white, the margins connate; drupes 1.9–2.1 mm long; inner leaves of winter bud undifferentiated

Leaf blades with 3–9 (–13) veins, 1.2–2.9 mm wide, with 0–3 rows of lacunae on each side of the midrib; stipules usually brown, convolute; drupes 2.5–3 mm long; inner leaves of winter bud commonly rolled into a hard, fusiform structure

c15.text: Leaf blades 1–3.5 mm wide, obtuse to rounded at the apex, sometimes with an apiculus, commonly suffused with red; drupe 2.5–3.5 mm long, with a beak 0.6–0.7 mm long, the embryo coiled 1 full spiral
Leaf blades 0.2–2.5 mm wide, acute to obtuse at the apex, green; drupe 1.5–2.2 mm long, with a beak 0.1–0.6 mm long, the embryo coiled less than 1 full spiral

c16.text: Leaf blades 0.2–0.7 mm wide, acute to long-acute at the apex, 1-veined, with a single row of lacunae on each side of the midvein; peduncles 10–35 mm long; drupes with beak centrally positioned on the edge of fruit; stipules convolute, with inrolled but distinct margins, attenuate at the apex, subherbaceous in texture; spikes 1–3 per plant, the whorls of fruit usually continuous

Leaf blades 0.2–2.5 mm wide, acute to obtuse (rarely apiculate) at the apex, usually 3- or 5-nerved, with 0–5 rows of lacunae on each side of the midvein; peduncles 5–62 mm long; drupe with beak centrally positioned on edge of fruit or positioned toward one margin; stipules convolute with distinct margins or connate with fused margins, in either case obtuse to acute at the apex, scarious to subherbaceous; spikes mostly 1–10 per plant, the whorls of fruit continuous or interrupted

c17.text: Leaf blades with 0–2 rows of lacunae on each side of the midvein, often with none, acute at the apex (rarely apiculate); stipules with united margins for more than ½ their length, forming a tube surrounding the stem, scarious; spikes mostly terminal, 1–3 per plant, with peduncles 10–62 mm long, interrupted and with 2–4 separate whorls of fruits; drupes with beak positioned toward the margin of fruit (rarely centrally positioned on edge)

Leaf blades with 1–5 rows of lacunae on each side of the midvein, acute to obtuse at the apex; stipules convolute, flat or with inrolled but distinct margins, scarious to subherbaceous; spikes terminal and/or axillary, mostly 2–10 per plant, usually more than 3, with peduncles 5–30(–45) mm long, continuous and with 1–3 crowded whorls of fruits; drupes with beak centrally positioned on the edge of fruit (rarely positioned toward the margin)

c18.text: Stipules basally fused to the leaf blade, only the tip of the stipule distinct from the blade; leaf blades usually minutely serrulate, especially in the apical portion, with a pair of auricles at the base; well-formed inflorescences branched [Fig. ]
Stipules of submersed leaves distinct from the leaf blade their entire length; leaf blades entire or toothed in P. crispus ,

c19.text: Leaf margins conspicuously serrulate; beak of drupe 2–3 mm long; turions commonly formed
Leaf margins entire; beak of drupe 0.3–0.9 mm; turions absent or rarely formed

c20.text: Submersed leaf blades sessile and conspicuously cordate-clasping at the base [Fig. ]; floating leaves not produced
Submersed leaf blades sessile or petiolate, not cordate-clasping; floating leaves produced and generally present on some of the plants in each colony or not produced in P. zosteriformis

c21.text: Leaf blades strictly entire, (60–) 80–280 mm long, the apex cucullate and usually splitting when pressed; rhizome spotted with red-brown; stipules persistent; drupes 4–5.7 mm long, with a prominent, abaxial keel

Leaf blades provided with minute, caducous, 1-celled spicules along the margin, 9–130 mm long, the apex flat and not splitting when pressed; rhizome unspotted; stipules disintegrating and remaining as fibers or completely absent; drupes 1.6–4.2 mm long, with an inconspicuous keel or the keel absent

c22.text: Leaf blades ovate to suborbicular, 9–76 (–97) mm long, delicately 7- to 15-veined; stipules disintegrating and absent on the lower part of the stem; drupes 1.6–3 mm long
Leaf blades narrow-ovate to narrow-lanceolate, (16–) 30–130 mm long, coarsely 13- to 21-veined [Fig. ]; stipules disintegrating into persistent fibers; drupes 2.2–4.2 mm long

c23.text: Stems red-brown- or black-spotted [Fig. ]; floating leaf blades rounded to cordate at base; submersed leaf blades usually crisped and arcuate [Fig. ]; drupes 5–6.7 mm long

Stems and petioles unspotted; floating leaf blades cuneate to rounded at the base or absent altogether in P. zosteriformis ; submersed leaf blades usually flat and not arcuate (sometimes crisped and/or arcuate in P. illinoensis ); drupes 1.9–4.3 mm long

c24.text: Submersed leaf blades narrow-lanceolate to lanceolate, with 7–19 veins; floating leaf blades with 15–19 veins; stems black-spotted
Submersed leaf blades ovate to broad-oblanceolate, with 19–49 veins; floating leaf blades with 27–49 veins; stems red-brown-spotted

c25.text: Stems conspicuously compressed; floating leaves not produced; submersed leaf blades 15- to 25 (–35)-veined (in part)
Stems terete to somewhat compressed; floating leaves produced, though not always present; submersed leaf blades 3- to 19 (–21)-veined

c26.text: Stipules (1–) 3–9 cm long; submersed leaf blades with 7–19 (–21) veins, sessile or with petioles up to 13 cm long
Stipules 1–3 cm long; submersed leaf blades with 3–13 veins, sessile

c27.text: Submersed leaves with petioles (2–) 5–13 cm long, the larger leaves with blades 10–35 mm wide and acute at the apex; drupes red to red-brown, the lateral keels with blunt to sharp teeth
Submersed leaves sessile or with petioles up to 4 cm long, the larger leaves with blades 20–45 mm wide and mucronate at apex; drupes gray-green to olive-green, the lateral keels without teeth

c28.text: Submersed leaves distichous, the blades ± linear, with prominent lacunar bands 1–2 mm wide on each side of the midrib; each lacunar band composed of 9–18 rows of cells (in part)

Submersed leaves ± spirally arranged, the blades linear to narrow-obovate, with inconspicuous lacunar bands up to 0.5 mm wide on each side of the midrib; each lacunar band composed of 0–4 rows of cells

c29.text: Submersed leaf blades 4.5–18 (–25) cm long, strictly entire, red-tinged, especially in drying; stems unbranched; drupes (2.5–) 3–3.5 mm long, plump and turgid, the exocarp hard, the embryo coiled 1 full spiral

Submersed leaf blades (1.5–) 3.1–9.1 (–10) cm long, provided with minute, caducous, 1-celled spicules along the margin, green; stems sparingly to many-times branched; drupes 1.9–2.3 mm long, laterally compressed, the exocarp soft, the embryo coiled less than 1 full spiral

c1.text: Bur formed from concrescent branchlets, surrounding and nearly concealing 1–4 spikelets [Fig. ]; glumes without prickles; upper lemma and palea indurate
Bur formed from an enlarged glume [Fig. ], each subtending a single floret; glumes with 5–7 rows of uncinate prickles; lemma and palea not indurate
This genus contains exactly one species.
Spikelets, excluding the awns, 19–26 mm long; glumes 5- to 11-veined
Spikelets, excluding the awns, up to 18 mm long; glumes 1- to 5-veined

c2.text: Rachilla long-pubescent, the longer hairs (2–) 3–7 mm long; ligule of upper stem leaves 5–8 mm long
Rachilla glabrous or pubescent with hairs up to 2 mm long; ligule of upper stem leaves as long as 5 (–6) mm (3–12 mm long in Deschampsia cespitosa and 1–8 mm long in Ventenata )

c3.text: Spikelets with 2 florets [Fig. ]
Spikelets with 3 or more florets [Fig. ]

c4.text: Spikelets 9–15 mm long; upper lemma with an awn 10–16 mm long, terminated by 2 setaceous teeth 1–2 mm long; upper glume 3- to 9-veined (in part)
Spikelets 1.7–11 mm long; upper lemma without an awn or with an awn (0.5–) 1–9 mm long, entire or bifid at the apex; upper glume 1- to 3-veined

c5.text: Lower lemma of spikelet (or both lemmas) lacking an awn
Lower lemma of spikelet (and usually both lemmas) with an awn

c6.text: Neither lemma of spikelet with an awn; reproductive stems glabrous or minutely scabrous (in part)
Upper lemma of spikelet with a bent or hooked awn [Fig. ]; reproductive stems pilose on at least the nodes (glabrous or sparsely pubescent in Holcus mollis )

c7.text: Florets of a given spikelet dimorphic—the lower unisexual, the upper bisexual; lemma awns dimorphic—that of the lower lemma 10–20 mm long and bent near the middle, that of the upper to 6 mm long and straight (very rarely the upper awn is also elongate and bent)
Florets of a given spikelet monomorphic, both bisexual; lemma awns relatively monomorphic, similar in shape, the upper slightly shorter if at all

c8.text: Lemma awns composed of 2 distinctly unlike members—the basal portion brown and spiraled, the apical portion white and distally thickened—the two members separated by a ciliate joint
Lemma awns tapering to the apex, not consisting of 2 articulate members separated by a ring of cilia

c9.text: Awn (when present) attached above the middle of the lemma [Fig. ]; lemma apex bifid
Awn attached below the middle of the lemma [Fig. ]; lemma apex entire to bifid

c10.text: Lemmas with awns 3–9 mm long, the awns conspicuously surpassing the apex of the lemma [Fig. ]; callus of lemma pubescent with hairs up to 1 mm long (in part)

Lemmas unawned or rarely with rudimentary awns shorter than 2 mm, the awns, when present, not or scarcely surpassing the apex of the lemma; callus of lemma pubescent with hairs 1.5–2 mm long (in part)

c11.text: Apex of lemma terminated by 2 setaceous teeth (caution: the terminal teeth are sometimes intertwined and difficult to observe); glumes 2.3–3.3 mm long; rachilla not prolonged beyond upper floret
Apex of lemma entire or erose, but without terminal teeth; longer glumes 2.7–6.1 mm long; rachilla prolonged beyond upper floret

c12.text: Glumes slightly shorter than to slightly exceeding the lemmas [Fig. ]; anthers 1.3–3 mm long; stems with prominent tufts of basal leaves (in part)
Glumes much exceeding lemmas, approximately twice as long [Fig. ]; anthers 0.4–0.8 mm long; stems without prominent tufts of basal leaves

c13.text: Lemma apex dissected into numerous, spreading awns
Lemma without awns or with a single awn

c14.text: Upper glume 3- to 9-nerved; upper lemma with an awn 10–16 mm long arising from the abaxial keel, terminated by 2 setaceous teeth 1–2 mm long (in part)

Upper glume 1- to 3-veined (up to 5 (–7)-veined in Danthonia , but that genus usually with more than 3 florets per spikelet); upper lemma without an awn or with an awn to 10.5 mm long, with or without apical teeth, the awn (when present) emerging from between the apical teeth or from the abaxial keel

c15.text: Spikelets with 3–12 florets; lemmas with an awn arising from between 2 terminal teeth; spikelets 7–16 mm long
Spikelets with 3 or 4 florets; lemmas with or without awns, the awns, when present, not arising from between apical teeth; spikelets 3.2–9 mm long

c16.text: Upper floret bisexual, of different form from the 2 lower, unisexual and staminate florets; 2 lower lemmas evidently pubescent over the surfaces, at least near the apex (note: the hairs visible at low magnification)

Florets all bisexual, progressively reduced in size upward; lemmas minutely and/or rather sparsely scabrous-hirtellous over their surfaces (note: the callus and rachilla segments may be evidently pubescent; lemmas pilose in some forms of Trisetum spicatum )

c17.text: Panicle branches densely pubescent; apex of lemma entire; rachilla segments glabrous or pubescent with hairs shorter than 1 mm
Panicle branches antrorsely scabrous; apex of lemma bifid; rachilla segments pubescent with hairs 0.4–2 mm long, these usually longer than 1 mm in the distal portion of the segment

c18.text: Lemmas with awns 3–9 mm long, the awns conspicuously surpassing the apex of the lemma [Fig. ]; callus of lemma pubescent with hairs up to 1 mm long (in part)
Lemmas unawned or with awns shorter than 2 mm, the awns, when present, not or scarcely surpassing the apex of the lemma; callus of lemma pubescent with hairs 1.5–2 mm long (in part)

c1.text: Leaf blades narrowed to a short pseudopetiole
Leaf blades not narrowed to a petiole-like structure

c2.text: Branches from midpoint of stem solitary; reproductive stems terete; spikelets pedicellate
Branches from midpoint of stem in pairs, strongly unequal; reproductive stems grooved on one side; spikelets sessile

c3.text: Plants robust, typically 1.5–4 m tall, forming extensive colonies by stout rhizomes; inflorescence appearing plumose due to long-pubescent rachilla segments
Plants of short to moderate stature, mostly shorter than 2 m, colonial or not; inflorescence not appearing plumose

c4.text: Lemmas with 3 veins
Lemmas with 5 or more veins (the intermediate veins sometimes inconspicuous)

c5.text: Callus and/or nerves of the lemma pubescent
Callus and nerves of the lemma glabrous

c6.text: Lemmas entire at the apex, without awns [Fig. ], arachnoid-pubescent on the callus in most species [Fig. ]; ligule membranaceous (in part)
Lemmas bifid at the apex, with an awn emerging from between the lobes (note, the lateral lobes may terminate in long awns), pubescent, but not with arachnoid hairs; ligule a band of hairs

c7.text: Lemmas with 3 slender, elongate awns—1 terminal awn and 2 lateral awns; upper glume bifid at the apex
Lemmas with 1 slender awn or 3 excurrent mucros; upper glume entire at the apex

c8.text: Inflorescence terminal, long-exserted from upper leaf sheaths; paleas glabrous or inconspicuously short-pubescent; lateral veins of lemma shortly excurrent as short awns
Inflorescence terminal and axillary, usually partly included in the leaf sheaths; paleas densely villous on the apical portion of the 2 keels; lateral veins of lemma not excurrent

c9.text: Lemmas keeled on the abaxial surface (except E. intermedia ), longer than the paleas; anthers 0.2–1.2 mm long; rachilla typically not disarticulating, the floral scales falling from it
Lemmas rounded on the abaxial surface, shorter than the paleas; anthers 1.5–3 mm long; rachilla disarticulating

c10.text: Panicle composed of dense, somewhat secund, glomerules of spikelets on a few, stiff branches
Panicle composed of pedicellate spikelets on spirally arranged branches

c11.text: Plants dioecious (i.e., the flowers of a given plant unisexual and all of one type), of coastal saltmarshes
Plants synoecious (i.e., the flowers of a given plant bisexual), mostly not of saline habitats (except Puccinellia )

c12.text: Leaf sheath fused (i.e., the sheath closed with united edges) at least in the basal half
Leaf sheath with distinct, overlapping edges except at the very base

c13.text: Lemmas entire at the apex, without awns, with parallel veins that do not converge near the apex [Fig. ]
Lemmas bifid at the apex, awned in most species [Fig. ], with arching veins that converge near the apex

c14.text: Callus of the lemma pubescent; styles borne close together from the summit of the ovary; caryopsis free from the palea
Callus of the lemma glabrous; styles separated and borne below the summit of the ovary; caryopsis adnate to the palea

c15.text: Glumes dissimilar in shape—the first (i.e., lower) oblong or tapering to the apex, the second obovate and dilated upwards [Figs. , ]
Glumes relatively similar in shape, though sometimes differing in size, both with parallel or apically tapering margins [Figs. , ]

c16.text: Lemmas awned, the awn attached to the abaxial surface of the lemma well below the apex [Fig. ]
Lemmas unawned or with an awn attached at the apex [Fig. ]

c17.text: Spikelets 9–10 mm long; awn of upper lemmas of spikelet 10–16 mm long; upper glume 3- to 9-veined (in part)
Spikelets 2.3–7.5 mm long; awn of lemmas up to 6.5 mm long; upper glume 1- to 3-veined

c18.text: Awn emerging below the middle of the lemma keel; lemma apex entire (in part)
Awn emerging above the middle of the lemma keel; lemma apex bifid (in part)

c19.text: Florets nearly perpendicular to the axis of spikelet; lemmas cordate at their base
Florets ascending to erect relative to the spikelet axis; lemmas cuneate to rounded or truncate at their base

c20.text: Lemmas usually blunt at the apex, with parallel veins that do not converge near the tip [Figs. , ]
Lemmas usually pointed or awned or both at the apex, with arching veins that converge near the tip

c21.text: Lemmas prominently veined; plants of freshwater habitats
Lemmas inconspicuously veined; plants of saline habitats (e.g., saline to brackish marshes, coastal strands, heavily salted roadways)

c22.text: Rachilla segments with hairs 1.3–2 mm long; callus of lemma pubescent with straight hairs (in part)
Rachilla segments glabrous or minutely scabrous; callus of lemma glabrous or with arachnoid hairs

c23.text: Lemmas prominently keeled, often with arachnoid pubescence on the callus [Fig. ], without awns; leaf tips cucullate (in part)
Lemmas rounded, or keeled only at the apex, with a glabrous callus, usually awned; leaf tips flat

c24.text: Panicles with short, ± secund branches; lemmas obtuse at the apex, unawned; florets disarticulating with a short rachilla segment such that the fallen florets appear stipitate

Panicles with short to long branches, not secund; lemmas acute to acuminate (obtuse), awned in most species [Fig. ]; florets disarticulating without a short rachilla segment or with 1 but then the floret not appearing stipitate

c25.text: Plants annual; flowers remaining closed (i.e., cleistogamous; anthers usually 1 per floret, up to 1 mm long
Plants perennial; flowers open-pollinated (i.e., chasmogamous) or proliferating in one species; anthers 3 per floret, (0.5–) 0.7–4 mm long

c26.text: Auricles present at summit of leaf sheath [Fig. ]; apical half of the lemma with a prominent, scarious margin ca. 0.5 mm wide; leaf blades flat, (2–) 3–18 mm wide
Auricles absent; lemmas with firm margins or very narrow, inconspicuous, scarious margins; leaf blades involute, conduplicate, or flat, 0.2–3 mm wide or up to 10 mm in F. subverticillata

c1.text: Lemmas with 2, 3, or 5 conspicuous lobes or teeth at the apex
Lemmas entire or inconspicuously bilobed at the apex

c2.text: Lemmas 3- or 5-lobed at the apex and with 3 awns; spikelets not sunken into cavities of the inflorescence rachis; inflorescence a panicle consisting of an axis and spike-like branches; disarticulation occurring at the base of the short, spike-like branches, these falling from the panicle axis (in part)

Lemmas with 2 or 3 tooth-like lobes at the apex, usually only 1 of these prolonged into an evident awn (note: the awns usually longest on spikelets in the apical portion of the inflorescence); spikelets appearing sunken into obvious cavities in the thickened rachis; inflorescence a cylindrical spike; disarticulation at the nodes of the spike

c3.text: Inflorescence a solitary spike or raceme, the spikelets produced from nodes that alternate on each side of the rachis [Figs. , ]
Inflorescence a panicle with 2 or more secund, spike-like branches [Fig. ]

c4.text: All but the uppermost spikelets borne on short pedicels (i.e., the inflorescence a raceme)
All the spikelets sessile (i.e., the inflorescence a spike) [Figs. , ]

c5.text: Spikelets solitary at each node of the inflorescence [Fig. ]
Spikelets numbering 2–4 at each node, although only 1 may be fertile [Figs. , ]

c6.text: Spikelets arranged with the narrow side toward the rachis; only the glume away from the rachis developed, the other obsolete
Spikelets arranged with the broad side toward the rachis; both glumes developed

c7.text: Plants annual, short persisting crop species; glumes 1- or 3-veined
Plants perennial, native or introduced species; glumes 5- or 7-veined

c8.text: Glumes with 1 vein, linear-subulate; keel of lemmas ciliate
Glumes with 3 veins, ovate; keel of lemmas glabrous

c9.text: Spikelets crowded on short internodes 0.5–2 (–3) mm long, ascending to spreading
Spikelets less crowded, at least the lower internodes mostly longer than 4 mm, appressed to appressed-ascending

c10.text: Glumes gradually tapering from near midlength and ± imperceptively passing into a short awn-tip
Glumes tapering from the apical third, unawned or somewhat abruptly tapering to an awn

c11.text: Glumes acute at the apex, unawned or merely with a tiny mucro up to 0.5 (–0.7) mm long [Fig. ]
Glumes long-acute at the apex, usually with an awn 0.5–10 mm long (in part)

c12.text: Spikelets consistently 3 at each node, the outer pair usually pedicellate and staminate or sterile (in part)
Spikelets 2–4 at each node, commonly 2, all bisexual and fertile

c13.text: Plants annual; lemmas with awns 50–100 mm long
Plants cespitose or rhizomatous perennials; lemmas awnless or with awns up to 40 mm long

c14.text: Plants mostly self-pollinating, with small anthers 1–3 mm long, cespitose, lacking rhizomes or with short rhizomes; lemmas mostly awned (in part)
Plants mostly outcrossing, with large anthers mostly 4–9 mm long, not cespitose, with elongate, stout rhizomes; lemmas mostly without awns

c15.text: Panicle with branches digitately arranged (i.e., all or nearly all originating from the same point) [Fig. ] or with branches in 1–3 closely spaced whorls
Panicle with branches racemosely arranged along an elongate axis

c16.text: Rachis of branches extending beyond distal most flowers 1–5 mm; upper glume with an awn 1–2.5 mm long
Rachis of branches ending in a functional or rudimentary spikelet, not extending as a bristle-tip; glumes unawned or the upper one with a short awn to 0.3 mm

c17.text: Lemmas awned, pubescent on the marginal veins and callus; spikelets with 2 or 3 (–5) florets
Lemmas unawned, glabrous; spikelets with 5–7 florets

c18.text: Spikelets nearly circular in outline, with 1 or 2 florets, the upper, when present, sterile; glumes obovate, cross-wrinkled, the tips crossing (in part)
Spikelets not circular in outline, either clearly longer than wide or ± obovate, with 2–20 bisexual florets; glumes linear to elliptic to ovate, not cross-winkled, the tips separate

c1.text: Spikelets nearly circular in outline; glumes obovate, cross-wrinkled, the tips crossing (in part)
Spikelets not at all circular in outline; glumes linear to lanceolate, not cross-winkled, the tips separate

c2.text: Panicle with (2–) 4–6 (–9) digitately arranged branches, lacking an elongate, central axis; plants mat-forming by stolons (and often also rhizomes)
Panicle with (1–) 2–80 branches variously attached to an elongate axis; plants without evident stolons

c3.text: Lemmas entire or bilobed at the apex, unawned or merely apiculate, exceeded by the paleas [Figs. , ]; spikelets with a solitary, bisexual floret; ligules 0.3–3 mm long
Lemmas 3-lobed or 5-lobed at the apex, with 3 awns, exceeding the paleas; spikelets usually with a reduced, sterile floret distal to the bisexual floret; ligules 0.1–0.5 mm long (in part)

c1.text: Inflorescence a solitary, terminal spike; spikelets arising from shallow cavities on the rachis, with a single, minute glume

Inflorescence a panicle or raceme (i.e., the spikelets at least shortly pedicellate), usually branched (though the branches sometimes difficult to discern); spikelets not arising from cavities on the rachis, with 2 glumes (glumes essentially absent in Leersia )

c2.text: Inflorescence a dense, cylindrical, spike-like panicle, the branches virtually absent
Inflorescence an open or dense panicle, the branches identifiable

c3.text: Inflorescence overtopped by the upper leaves, usually partly sheathed or included in the subtending, apically inflated leaf sheath
Inflorescence exceeding the leaves, usually well exserted and not included in the upper leaf sheaths

c4.text: Glumes without awns, connate at the base; paleas wanting
Glumes with awns, distinct at the base; paleas present, subequal in length to the lemmas

c5.text: Glumes shorter than and not concealing the floret, the first glume with 2 (–3) awns, the second with a single awn (in part)
Glumes exceeding the length of the floret and concealing it [Fig. ], glumes awnless or each glume with a single awn

c6.text: Glumes tapering to a long point, but not awned, slightly swollen at the base; lemmas pubescent
Glumes awned [Fig. ], not swollen at the base; lemmas glabrous over the surface

c7.text: Awn of glumes 3–8 mm long; lemmas with awns; glumes hispidulous, bilobed at the apex, the awn emerging from between the lobes (in part)
Awn of glumes 0.7–3 mm long; lemmas without awns; glumes prominently ciliate on the keels [Fig. ], otherwise glabrous, entire at the apex, the awn terminal

c8.text: Lemmas indurate and lustrous at maturity, of much firmer texture than the glumes
Lemmas soft and dull at maturity, not of conspicuously firmer texture than the glumes

c9.text: Lemmas awnless; spikelets with 1 fertile floret and at its base 2 sterile, rudimentary florets represented by pubescent scales
Lemmas with awns; spikelets without basal, sterile florets

c10.text: Lemmas pubescent on only the callus, with 3 persistent awns [Figs. , ]; callus of lemmas slender and acute; plants annual (perennial in 1 species) (in part)
Lemmas pubescent over the abaxial surface, with a single awn articulated and eventually deciduous from the summit of the lemma [Fig. ]; callus of lemmas short and oblique; plants perennial

c11.text: Panicle open to somewhat congested, the branches spreading to ascending, each branch bearing usually 2 or more spikelets; uppermost leaf blades well-developed, 1–35 cm long; basal leaves deciduous (in part)

Panicle very narrow, raceme-like, with appressed branches, each branch bearing usually a single spikelet; uppermost leaf blades absent or with a blade shorter than 1 cm; basal leaves evergreen (in part)

c12.text: Glumes virtually obsolete, reduced to minute cupules; nodes densely and conspicuously pubescent with spreading, white hairs [Fig. ]
Glumes present and evident; nodes glabrous or pubescent, but not pubescent with spreading, white hairs

c13.text: Floret stipitate, with 1 stamen; spikelets articulated below the glumes and falling intact leaving the pedicel behind
Floret sessile, with mostly 3 stamens; spikelets articulated above the glumes, the florets falling and leaving the empty glumes behind (disarticulating below the glumes in Polypogon )

c14.text: Spikelets 10–15 mm long; plants growing on sandy beaches of the Atlantic coast and Lake Champlain
Spikelets 1–9 (–10) mm long; plants growing in a wide variety of habitats, but not regularly of coastal sands

c15.text: Ligule of hairs; lemmas 1-veined (in part)
Ligule a membrane; lemmas 3- or 5-veined (the veins sometimes faint)

c16.text: Glumes shorter than the lemmas or the lemmas awned from the very apex or both; caryopsis tightly enclosed by the lemma (in part)

At least 1 of the glumes equaling the length of the floret; awn of the lemma, if present, originating from below the apex on the keel of the lemma or from between 2 terminal lobes; caryopsis loosely enclosed by the lemma

c17.text: Glumes obtuse; inflorescence a raceme with usually 6–8 spikelets; delicate annuals 3–10 cm tall
Glumes acute to acuminate; inflorescence a panicle, with more than 8 spikelets; annual or mostly perennial plants (5–) 10–200 cm tall

c18.text: Lemma glabrous on the callus (pubescent in Agrostis elliottiana ); palea nerveless, or, less often, 2-nerved, delicate, up to 65% as long as the lemma; rachilla not prolonged

Lemma evidently, though sometimes shortly, pubescent on the callus [Figs. , ]; palea 2-nerved, membranaceous, to fully as long as the lemma; rachilla prolonged beyond the upper floret as a minute bristle

c19.text: Spikelets disarticulating above the glumes, borne on pedicels (0.1–) 0.3–9.6 mm long; lemmas (0.8–) 1.2–2.6 mm long
Spikelets disarticulating below the glumes, borne on stipes 0.1–0.6 mm long; lemmas 0.5–1.5 mm long (in part)

c20.text: Awn straight, inserted just below the apex and between the terminal teeth of the lemma, 5–12 mm long; pubescence of the callus of the lemma ca. as long as the lemma; plants annual
Awn often bent, definitely originating from below the apex of the lemma, up to 3 mm long; pubescence of the callus of the lemma to fully as long as the lemma; plants perennial

c1.text: Lemmas 3- or 5-lobed at the apex, with 3 awns; ligules 0.1–0.5 mm long (in part)
Lemmas entire or bilobed at the apex, awnless or with a single awn; ligules 0.5–16 mm long

c2.text: Inflorescence a spike, with spikelets positioned on alternating sides of the rachis [Figs. , ]; spikelets 6–150 mm long including the awns (in part)
Inflorescence a spike-like panicle, with spirally arranged or verticillate spikelets [Fig. ]; spikelets 1.6–6 (–8) mm long including the awns

c3.text: Glumes without awns, the upper with 3–9 veins; spikelets subtended by 1–12 bristles (in part)
Glumes with an awn, both with 1 vein; spikelets not subtended by bristles (in part)

c1.text: Spikelets not organized into pairs or triplets, all pedicellate in an open panicle; disarticulation above the glumes, the falling floret leaving the glumes behind

Spikelets organized into pairs or triplets, some sessile (all pedicellate in Miscanthus , but that genus with glumes subtended by a ring of long, silky hairs); disarticulation below the glumes or between the rame segments, in either case the spikelets falling intact

c2.text: Spikelets unisexual, with the carpellate inflorescences or carpellate portion of inflorescence borne below the staminate ones or staminate portions [Fig. ]
At least the lower spikelet of each pair or triplet bisexual

c3.text: Reproductive stems decumbent, creeping over the ground or other low vegetation; spikelets solitary at each node, the pediceled spikelet absent, represented only a pedicel up to 3 (–4) mm long
Reproductive stems ascending to erect, not creeping; spikelets solitary, paired, or in trios at each node, when solitary, with a pedicel usually longer than 3 mm

c4.text: Spikelets in homogamous and homomorphic pairs (i.e., both spikelets of a pair of similar sex and similar morphology, respectively) [Fig. ]
Spikelets in heterogamous and heteromorphic pairs or trios (i.e., spikelets of a pair or trio not of similar sex nor of similar morphology, respectively)

c5.text: Spikelets in sessile-pedicellate pairs (i.e., one spikelet of a pair sessile, the other borne on a short pedicel) [Fig. ]; terminal inflorescence of (1–) 2–4 (–6) branches originating from the summit of the peduncle, without or with a very short rachis less than 4 cm long

Spikelets in unequal-pedicellate pairs (i.e., both spikelets of a pair pedicellate, but 1 spikelet on a shorter pedicel than the other); terminal inflorescence usually with more than 15 branches distributed along a rachis 4–15 cm long

c6.text: Fully formed spikelet solitary at each node, the pedicelled spikelet represented by only its pedicel
Spikelets paired or in trios at each node, with 1 or 2 pedicelled spikelets, these usually smaller than the sessile spikelet

c7.text: Sessile spikelet lacking an awn; pedicels and rame internodes glabrous; mat-forming, stoloniferous plants with reproductive stems 10–35 cm tall (in part)
Sessile spikelet with an awn; pedicels and rame internodes pubescent; cespitose or rhizomatous plants with reproductive stems 40–300 cm tall

c8.text: Pedicels and rame internodes pubescent with white hairs [Fig. ]; glumes glabrous or scaberulous; peduncles subtended by, or even partly included in, a modified, shortened leaf (in part)
Pedicels and rame internodes pubescent with yellow-brown hairs; lower glume hirsute; peduncles not closely subtended by a modified leaf

c9.text: Each inflorescence peduncle supporting a solitary rame (though each plant may have many peduncles)
Each inflorescence peduncle supporting 2 or more rames or branches

c10.text: Inflorescence solitary and terminal; pedicels and rame internodes glabrous; reproductive stems 10–35 cm tall (in part)
Inflorescences both terminal and axillary; pedicels and rame internodes pubescent; reproductive stems 30–210 cm tall

c11.text: Inflorescence a panicle with compound branches distributed along an elongate axis, the ultimate branches of the panicle being rames; pedicel of pedicellate spikelet 1–3.3 mm long
Inflorescence composed of simple, digitately arranged rames, lacking an elongate central axis; pedicel of pedicellate spikelet (2.7–) 3–5.8 mm long (in part)

c1.text: Plants monoecious, the carpellate and staminate inflorescences or portions of inflorescences clearly different from one another; glumes absent, highly reduced, or collapsed (i.e., not evident); robust, annual grasses 1–5 (–6) m tall

Plants synoecious or polygamous, the inflorescence with at least some (or entirely of) bisexual flowers; glumes present (though sometimes the lower one absent); short to tall, annual or perennial grasses 0.15–2.5 (–3) m tall

c2.text: Each inflorescence with 2 types of flowers, the staminate positioned below the carpellate; carpellate spikelets with elongate awns; aquatic grasses
Each inflorescence with only 1 type of flower, the carpellate inflorescences axillary, the staminate inflorescences terminal; carpellate spikelets lacking awns; cultivated grasses

c3.text: Lemmas without awns [Fig. ]
Lemmas with awns [Figs. , , ]

c4.text: Spikelets at maturity with 1 pair of lemmas and paleas indurate and lustrous, of much firmer texture than the glumes
Spikelets with soft to firm lemmas, the lemmas dull and not conspicuously indurate

c5.text: Spikelets each subtended by 1–12 bristles [Fig. ]; inflorescence a solitary, terminal, spike-like panicle [Figs. , ] (in part)
Spikelets not subtended by bristles; inflorescence an open to dense panicle

c6.text: Upper leaves (or all the leaves) without ligules (in part)
Leaves with ligules of hairs, membranes, or ciliate membranes

c7.text: Panicle branches both unbranched and secund [Figs. , ]
Panicle branches rebranched (at least the lower ones) or not secund or usually both [Figs. , , ]

c8.text: Spikelets lanceoloid to ellipsoid; upper (i.e., fertile) lemma somewhat indurate, firm but flexible, the margin with a hyaline border and flat (in part)
Spikelets ovoid or obovoid to spherical; upper lemma prominently indurate, rigid to the edges and lacking a hyaline border, the very edges slightly involute

c9.text: Plants with both aerial and subterranean inflorescences, only the subterranean ones producing fruits; lower glumes absent
Plants with only aerial inflorescences, at least some spikelets producing fruits; lower glumes present, though sometimes very small

c10.text: Upper (i.e., fertile) lemma somewhat indurate, firm but flexible, the margin with a hyaline border and flat (in part)
Upper lemma prominently indurate, rigid to the edges and lacking a hyaline border, the very edges slightly involute

c11.text: Upper lemma transversely rugose; panicle branches spike-like, secund, with a triquetrous axis

Upper lemma not transversely rugose (verrucose in Panicum verrucosum , but the warts not aligned in rows); panicle branches open-branched to highly congested, not secund (+/- secund in Sorengia ), without a triquetrous axis

c12.text: Inflorescence dense, spike-like, concealing at least the apical of the inflorescence rachis; pedicels with a disk-like apex; upper glume saccate at base
Inflorescence an open to somewhat congested panicle, the inflorescence rachis visible; pedicels not or barely thickened at apex, not disk-like; upper glume not saccate

c13.text: Basal leaves lanceolate to ovate, of distinctly different shape and/or length than the stem leaves and forming an overwintering rosette (elongate and similar to stem leaves in 2 species); many species producing branches from the lower and middle stem nodes in summer, these sometimes rebranching; reduced secondary panicles produced bearing cleistogamous flowers and often partly concealed by subtending leaves; plants perennial

Basal leaves linear to lanceolate, similar to the stem leaves, not forming an overwintering rosette; many species not producing branches from the lower and middle nodes, or branches produced but not rebranched; secondary panicles similar to the terminal panicles, chasmogamous; plants annual or perennial

c14.text: Spikelets borne on short pedicels mostly 0.5–1.5 mm long, ± secund [Fig. ]; leaf sheaths strongly compressed; apex of lemma and palea of upper floret lacking papillae
Spikelets borne on pedicels (0.5–) 1–20 mm long, not secund; leaf sheaths ± terete or compressed in P. dichotomiflorum ; apex of lemma and palea of upper floret with simple or compound papillae

c15.text: Spikelet with an upper bisexual, fertile floret and a lower inconspicuous, sterile floret, articulated below the glumes, the entire spikelet falling and leaving the pedicel behind; upper glume and lower lemma usually of ± similar appearance and texture (in part)
Spikelet with 1 bisexual, fertile floret, articulated above the glumes, the floret falling leaving the empty glumes behind; upper glume and lemma not of similar appearance and texture

c16.text: Lemmas 1-veined, unawned; ligule of hairs (in part)
Lemmas 3-veined, awned in most species; ligule a membrane (in part)

c17.text: Upper leaves (or all the leaves) without ligules (in part)
Leaves with ligules of hairs, membranes, or ciliate membranes

c18.text: Lemmas with 3 awns at the apex; plants annual (or perennial in 2 species) (in part)
Lemmas with a single awn from the apex; plants perennial

c19.text: Lemmas indurate and lustrous, conspicuously firmer than the glumes, pilose over the abaxial surface (only in the basal in Piptochaetium ); awn of lemma articulated, persistent or eventually deciduous

Lemmas firm, but not indurate, dull, glabrous or scaberulous, pubescent only on the nerves or callus if at all (minutely pubescent between the nerves in some Muhlenbergia ); awn of lemma not articulated, persistent

c20.text: Lemma awn 45–70 mm long; spikelets 9–13 mm long excluding the awns; lemmas with 3 distinct zones—villous in basal , glabrous in the middle, and scabrous near the apex [Fig. ]
Lemma awn 0.5–14 mm long; spikelets 3.5–9 mm long excluding the awns; lemmas sparsely to densely pubescent ± throughout

c21.text: Panicle open to somewhat congested, the branches spreading to ascending, each branch usually bearing 2 or more spikelets; uppermost leaf blades well-developed, 1–35 cm long; basal leaves deciduous (in part)

Panicle very narrow, raceme-like, with appressed branches, each branch usually bearing a single spikelet; uppermost leaf blades absent or with a blade shorter than 1 cm; basal leaves evergreen (in part)

c22.text: First glume diminutive or obsolete; rachilla prolonged, located near the abaxial surface of the palea and appearing as a minute bristle; plants with rhizomes
First glume present and evident (except in M. schreberi , which lacks rhizomes); rachilla not prolonged; plants with or without rhizomes (in part)

c1.text: Perianth bristles at most 1.5 times the length of the achene, retrorsely barbed (often smooth in S. georgianus ), straight or merely curved or perianth bristles entirely absent
Perianth bristles greatly exceeding the achenes when extended, smooth, bent and curled

c2.text: Leaves 14–22 (–26) on each stem; floral scales red-brown, orbicular or nearly so; spikelets mostly broad-ovoid

Leaves 3–12 on each stem; floral scales green-brown or brown to black, elliptic to broad-elliptic; spikelets cylindrical or narrow-ellipsoid to narrow-ovoid or ovoid (rarely broad-ovoid, as sometimes in S. cyperinus )

c3.text: Perianth bristles barbed in the apical 60–90% with sharp, stout, thick-walled teeth; achenes 0.6–1 mm wide
Perianth bristles smooth or barbed only in the apical 10–60% with rounded, slender teeth; achenes 0.3–0.6 mm wide

c4.text: Lower sheaths green or white-brown to brown; branches of inflorescence arching to drooping; plants cespitose, with short, brown rhizomes; achenes 0.6–0.8 mm wide
Lower sheaths conspicuously anthocyanic; branches of inflorescence ascending to divaricately spreading; plants spreading by long, anthocyanic rhizomes; achenes (0.6–) 0.8–1 mm wide

c5.text: Styles bifid; achenes lenticular to plano-convex, with firmly attached, persistent perianth bristles; branches of inflorescence scabrous only in the distal portion
Styles trifid; achenes compressed-trigonous, with weakly attached, sometimes caducous, perianth bristles; branches of inflorescence antrorsely scabrous their entire length

c6.text: Perianth bristles numbering 0–3 per flower, up to 0.7 times as long as the achene, smooth or with barbs only near the very apex
Perianth bristles numbering mostly 5 or 6 per flower, more than 0.6 times as long as the achene, barbed in the apical half

c7.text: Longer perianth bristles shorter than to equaling the length of the 0.8–1.1-mm- long achenes; floral scales appearing black under low magnification; spikelets 2–3.5 mm long; leaf blades 5–9 (–10) mm wide; basal leaves and sheaths usually with few and inconspicuous cross-septa

Longer perianth bristles exceeding the length of the 1–1.3-mm-long achenes; floral scales appearing brown under low magnification; spikelets mostly 3.5–5 mm long; leaf blades 7–17 (–18) mm wide; basal leaves and sheaths with many prominent cross-septa

c8.text: Perianth bristles largely contained within the floral scales, even in fruit, and therefore not obviously visible; achenes 1–1.2 mm long; floral scales with evident green midribs, even at maturity of the fruit

Perianth bristles exserted beyond the floral scales, in fruit providing a “woolly” aspect to the inflorescence; achenes 0.6–1 mm long; floral scales with pale, brown, or relatively inconspicuously colored midribs

c9.text: Achenes red-brown; floral scales 2–3.1 mm long; plants spreading by means of elongate rhizomes, often forming large circular colonies; base of involucral bracts glutinous
Achenes white to pale brown; floral scales 1.1–2.2 mm long; plants with short, branching rhizomes, forming dense tussocks; base of involucral bracts not glutinous

c10.text: Spikelets mostly or all in glomerules of 2 or more; floral scales mostly shorter than 1.5 mm; achenes maturing in August and September
Spikelets mostly or entirely solitary, sessile or pedicellate; floral scales 1.4–1.8 mm long; achenes maturing in late June through July

c11.text: Involucels and base of involucral bracts very dark brown to black; stems mostly 1–3 mm thick below the inflorescence; leaf blades 2–5 mm wide; floral scales rounded at apex or with a very tiny mucro to 0.05 mm long; achenes maturing late June through early July

Involucels and base of involucral bracts brown, sometimes with a dark edge; stems mostly 2–5 mm thick below the inflorescence; leaf blades 3–10 mm wide; floral scales rounded at the apex to, more commonly, mucronate, the mucro to 0.1 mm long; achenes maturing in mid- through late July

c1.text: Spikelets solitary, erect, with 10–15 sterile scales in the basal portion, not subtended by foliaceous involucral bracts [Fig. ]; plants cespitose
Spikelets 2–many, spreading or drooping on peduncles; scales all fertile; foliaceous involucral bracts present; stems produced singly or a few together from a rhizome

c2.text: Involucral bract 1 per inflorescence (sometimes with another very reduced, scale-like bract), erect; leaf blades 1–2 (–3) mm wide, channeled
Involucral bracts (1–) 2–5 per inflorescence, somewhat spreading; leaves (1.5–) 2–6 (–8) mm wide, flat, at least in the basal half

c3.text: Uppermost leaf blade 3–25 cm long, as long or longer than its sheath; stems scabrous near the top; peduncles scabrous; involucral bract (8–) 15–60 mm long, green to red-brown at the base; floral scales colored or at least tinged with red-brown

Uppermost leaf blade 1–4 cm long, shorter than its sheath; stems smooth; peduncles pubescent but not scabrous; involucral bract 6–20 mm long, gray to black at the base; floral scales black or dark gray

c4.text: Scales with 3–7 veins, red-brown near the margin; flowers with 1 stamen; perianth bristles at least tinged with red-brown (rarely entirely white)

Scales with 1 central vein (i.e., the midrib; occasionally with inconspicuous, short lateral veins in E. viridicarinatum ), green or gray to black near the margin; flowers with 3 stamens; perianth bristles white

c5.text: Midrib of scales inconspicuous near the tip; summit of the sheath darkened [Fig. ]; anthers 2–5 mm long; peduncles smooth or scabrous
Midrib of scales prominent to the tip and apically dilated; summit of the sheath not darkened; anthers 0.8–2 mm long; peduncles scabrous

c1.text: Stems terete, smooth
Stems trigonous, usually scabrous on the angles

c2.text: Perianth bristles white, flattened, 3–5 times longer than the inflorescence; spikelets with 9–20 flowers
Perianth bristles pale brown to brown, terete, much shorter than inflorescence and usually included within the subtending floral scales; spikelets with 3–8 flowers

c3.text: Floral scales obtuse at apex, the upper scales with an evanescent midrib; leaves 0.5–0.8 (–1) mm wide, up to as tall as the stems at flowering, much shorter than the stems at fruiting; plants of high-pH river shore ledges

Floral scales mucronate at apex, all with an excurrent midrib; leaves 0.8–2 mm wide, equal in height or taller than the stems, even at fruiting; plants of dry-mesic to mesic deciduous forests, often with Quercus in the canopy

c1.text: Spikes entirely staminate (i.e., no perigynia present)
At least some of the spikes partly or entirely carpellate

c2.text: Spikes 1 per stem; rachilla often present in perigynium
Spikes normally 2 or more per stem (except depauperate individuals); rachilla absent from perigynium

c3.text: Stigmas 2; achenes lenticular to biconvex
Stigmas 3; achenes trigonous to terete

c4.text: Spikes all similar and sessile, bearing staminate flowers at base or apex; bracteoles usually absent from the base of each spike
Spikes dissimilar and some or all usually peduncled, with staminate flowers borne in separate or mixed spikes; bracteoles usually present at the base of each spike

c5.text: Perigynia pubescent or scabrous with hairs or scabrules several times longer than wide
Perigynia glabrous (though long-papillose in some species)

c6.text: Bract of lowest carpellate spike consisting of a blade only, the sheath absent or extremely short, usually not exceeding 4 mm (or the bract absent altogether)
Bract of lowest carpellate spike consisting of a blade and a prolonged, closed sheath, usually longer than 4 mm

c1.text: Plants submerged aquatics with flaccid leaves, often forming extensive vegetative colonies; spikelets solitary on a stiff, emergent stem
Plants rarely submerged, the leaf blades, when present, commonly stiffer, associated with reproductive shoots; spikelets usually 2 or more per inflorescence

c2.text: Plants annual, with cespitose stems; rhizomes absent or very short (i.e., ca. 1 mm long); anthers 0.4–0.6 mm long; stems ca. 0.5–1 mm thick at the midpoint
Plants perennial, often forming extensive colonies from elongate rhizomes; anthers 1.5–3.5 mm long; stems ca. 1–10 mm thick at the midpoint

c3.text: Leaf-bearing nodes confined to the very base of the stem; achenes pitted to nearly smooth [Fig. ], with or without perianth bristles; amphicarpic flowers absent

Leaf-bearing nodes basal and one on the stem; achenes with prominent, transverse, wavy ridges, almost always lacking perianth bristles; amphicarpic flowers frequently present, enclosed in the basal leaf sheaths

c4.text: Achenes noticeably pitted, 1.75–2 mm long, rounded near base, biconvex; floral scales with a distinct midvein, lacking a green midstrip; perianth bristles, when present, stout and distinctly tapered apically; primary involucral bract often divergent [Fig. ]

Achenes nearly smooth, 1.5–1.8 mm long, wedge-shaped near base, mostly plano-convex; floral scales with an obscure midvein, possessing a broad green midstrip; perianth bristles, when present, slender throughout [Fig. ]; primary involucral bract usually erect

c5.text: Stems terete or nearly so in cross-section; basal sheaths lacking elongate blades
Stems sharply trigonous or even triquetrous in cross-section; basal sheaths producing elongate blades

c6.text: Spikelets all or mostly single at the ends of the pedicels; floral scales smooth along the margin; achenes trigonous in cross-section, with a style beak 0.3–1 mm long, with 4 (or 5) perianth bristles, usually 2 much shorter than the others

Spikelets all or mostly in glomerules of 2–7 at the ends of the pedicels; floral scales ciliate, at least near the apex; achenes plano-convex or with a low, abaxial ridge, with a style beak 0.1–0.5 mm long, with (5–) 6 (–7) perianth bristles, generally of subequal length

c7.text: Stems firm, with 10–12 aerenchymal lacunae in cross-section at stem height, each lacuna 0.3–0.5 mm in diameter; spikelets mostly in glomerules of 3–7; floral scales with a gray background, (3–) 3.5–4 mm long, with a contorted (rarely straight) awn 0.5–2 mm long; achenes 2–2.8 mm long, with a style beak 0.2–0.5 mm long

Stems soft, with 2–4 aerenchymal lacunae in cross-section at stem height, each lacuna 1–2.5 mm in diameter; spikelets mostly in glomerules of 2 or 3; floral scales with a pale orange-brown to dark red-brown background, 2–3.5 mm long, with a usually straight awn 0.2–0.8 mm long; achenes 1.7–2.3 mm long, with a style beak 0.1–0.3 mm long

c8.text: Achenes equilaterally trigonous to compressed-trigonous in cross-section, with a prominent style beak 0.5–2 mm long; floral scales essentially entire at apex, with a central nerve and 2–10 faint to evident veins on the sides; leaves often half to fully as tall as the stem; apical appendage of anthers rounded, smooth

Achenes plano-convex to obscurely compressed-trigonous in cross-section, with a tiny style beak shorter than 0.5 mm; floral scales with an apical notch 0.1–1 mm deep from which the awn emerges, with only a single central nerve, the sides lacking veins; leaves often half as tall as stem or shorter; apical appendage of anthers elongate, spinulose along margin

c9.text: Inflorescence congested, lacking elongate branches, usually with 1–4 spikelets; floral scales 4–5 mm long; style beak 0.5–1 mm long
Inflorescence open, with elongate branches, with 3–20 pedicellate spikelets; floral scales 5–7 mm long; style beak 0.7–2 mm long

c10.text: Stems with deeply concave sides and wing-angles; primary involucral bract 1–6 cm long; floral scales with an apical notch 0.1–0.4 mm deep, with an awn 0.2–0.5 mm long; uppermost leaf blade shorter than to about equaling the length of its associated sheath

Stems with shallowly concave to flat sides and sharp angles; primary involucral bract 3–20 cm long; floral scales with an apical notch (0.3–) 0.5–1 mm deep, with an awn 0.5–1.5 (–2.5) mm long; uppermost leaf blade usually several times longer than its associated sheath

c1.text: Floral scales longitudinally striate, usually with red-brown to purple spots on the adaxial (i.e., inner) surface; spikes hardly, if at all, thicker than the stem at height
Floral scales without fine longitudinal striae, lacking spots on the adaxial surface; spikes noticeably thicker than upper portion of stem

c2.text: Reproductive stems triangular in cross-section; rhizomes often producing flaccid, capillary, leaf-like stems; spikes 4- to 8-flowered, 7–20 (–25) mm tall; floral scales with a keeled midrib
Reproductive stems terete or quadrangular in cross-section; rhizomes not producing capillary stems; spikes many-flowered, 15–50 (–60) mm tall; floral scales with an obscure central keel

c3.text: Reproductive stems both terete and septate
Reproductive stems quadrangular, lacking septa

c4.text: Tubercle not obviously differentiated from and nearly confluent with the summit of the achene, forming a stylar beak [Fig. ]
Tubercle obviously differentiated from the achene, set apart by differences in color and/or texture [Figs. , , ]

c5.text: Stems 1–2 mm thick at midpoint, (15–) 40–100 cm tall, often some arching and rooting at the tip; spikes mostly 10- to 20-flowered; caudex short and thick, the plants lacking rhizomes
Stems up to 1 mm thick at midpoint, 3–40 cm tall, none arching and tip-rooting; spikes mostly 2- to 9-flowered; rhizomes present, long and slender, often terminated by a thickened bud

c6.text: Achenes 1.9–2.6 mm long; floral scales 2.5–5 mm long; plants primarily of high-pH wetlands and shores
Achenes 0.9–1.3 mm long; floral scales 1.5–2 (–2.5) mm long; plants primarily of brackish water flats and shores

c7.text: Achenes gray at maturity, longitudinally striate, with numerous, fine horizontal cross-lines, ca. 2 times as tall as wide [Fig. ]; floral scales all bearing flowers, arranged in 2 or 3 vertical ranks

Achenes not combining the above characteristics (i.e., lacking conspicuous longitudinal striae, usually no more than 1.5 times as tall as wide); floral scales not all subtending flowers, usually the basal 1 (or more) empty, arranged in more than 3 vertical ranks

c8.text: Achenes planoconvex to biconvex in cross-section; styles bifid (trifid in E. obtusa )
Achenes bluntly triangular to terete in cross-section; styles trifid

c9.text: Base of tubercles with a slight to prominent constriction at the junction of achene [Fig. ]; plants perennial, with rhizomes (these often difficult to detect in E. flavescens )
Base of tubercle not constricted at junction of achene; plants annual, with fibrous roots [Fig. ]

c10.text: Stems cespitose, with slender, often inconspicuous, rhizomes; leaf sheaths prolonged at summit into a white, scarious tip; anthers 0.7–1 mm long
Stems occurring singly or a few together, produced along obvious, firm rhizomes; leaf sheaths firm at summit; anthers 1–3 mm long

c11.text: Glumes 2 (rarely 3), lanceolate to triangular, each sheathing ± (up to ) of the base of the spike
Glume solitary, suborbicular, nearly encircling the base of the spike and sheathing or more of it

c12.text: Achenes minutely but visibly and regularly patterened with cellular reticulations [Fig. ]; tubercles 0.15–0.3 (–0.5) mm tall; leaf sheaths firm, many with a thickened, coriaceous collar at the summit
Achenes obscurely patterened, nearly smooth [Fig. ]; tubercles 0.35–0.8 mm tall; leaf sheaths herbaceous at summit, not or only slightly thickened

c13.text: Floral scales subcoriaceous, lustrous, the lower and middle ones of the spikelet 3–5 mm long; spikes with (5–) 10–20 (–30) flowers; plants of tidal and/or saline-influenced shores

Floral scales membranaceous, not or scarcely lustrous, the lower and middle ones of the spikelet 1.8–3 mm long; spikes with (15–) 20–40 (–50) flowers; plants primarily of non-tidal wetlands and shores

c14.text: Perianth bristles numbering 5–7 per achene, retrorsely barbellate, exceeding the length of the achene body (and often the tubercle as well)
Perianth bristles lacking or, if present, numbering 2–4, smooth, and shorter than the achene body [Fig. ]

c15.text: Tubercles 0.5–0.9 mm wide, 0.65–0.97 times as wide as the achene; flowers usually with 3 stamens
Tubercles 0.35–0.5 mm wide, 0.46–0.72 times as wide as the achene; flowers usually with 2 stamens

c16.text: Styles usually trifid; tubercles 0.2–0.4 mm tall, 0.29–0.67 times as tall as wide; perianth bristles usually exceeding tubercle in length; spikes commonly ovoid (in part)

Styles bifid or sometimes trifid; tubercles 0.12–0.23 mm tall, 0.1–0.38 times as tall as wide; perianth bristles often not exceeding the tubercle; spikes commonly ellipsoid to ellipsoid-cylindric (in part)

c17.text: Tubercles 0.46–0.83 mm wide, 0.65–0.97 times the width of the achene; flowers with usually 3 stamens
Tubercles 0.24–0.45 mm wide, 0.46–0.68 times the width of the achene; flowers with 2 stamens

c18.text: Tubercles 0.12–0.23 mm tall, 0.1–0.38 times as tall as wide; styles bifid or sometimes trifid; plants occurring on lake borders and in pools and seepages (in part)
Tubercles 0.2–0.4 mm tall, 0.29–0.67 times as tall as wide; styles trifid or sometimes bifid; plants occurring on river shores and lake borders (in part)

c19.text: Floral scales acute and somewhat keeled at the apex; tubercles mostly 0.1–0.2 mm tall; perianth bristles absent or up to 0.15 mm long; plants occurring on sand shores that are not or only minimally tidal

Floral scales rounded and not keeled at the apex; tubercles mostly 0.2–0.3 mm tall [Fig. ]; perianth bristles absent or up to 0.45 mm long; plants occurring on sand, silt, or mud shores that are usually fresh-tidal (rarely on shores of impounded lakes)

c20.text: Stems cespitose, arising from fibrous roots or a caudex (i.e., rhizomes lacking); plants annual (perennial in E. melanocarpa )
Stems produced singly or a few together along an obvious rhizome; plants perennial

c21.text: Tubercle as wide as the achene; stems compressed
Tubercle clearly narrower than achene; stems terete to capillary, but not obviously compressed

c22.text: Achenes dark brown to nearly black at maturity, smooth on the surface, with a low tubercle much shorter than the achene body [Fig. ]; perianth bristles shorter than the achene; plants perennial from a stout caudex; stems infrequently arching and rooting or proliferating from tip

Achenes brown to brown-green at matuity, with regular, conspicuous excavations on the surface (i.e., resembling honeycomb), with a large tubercle ± as tall as the achene body; perianth bristles longer than the achene; plants annual from fibrous roots; stems upright, not tip rooting

c23.text: Achenes green to brown-green, 1.2–1.5 mm long, topped with an elongate, cone-shaped tubercle; floral scales 1.7–2.5 mm long; longer perianth bristles exceeding combined length of achene and tubercle

Achenes pale, nearly white, 0.5–1 mm long, topped by a minute, depressed-conic tubercle; floral scales 1–1.5 mm long; longer perianth bristles up to as long as the combined length of the achene and tubercle

c24.text: Achenes with prominent keel-like angles; rhizomes firm, 3–6 mm thick
Achenes rounded on the angles, without keels; rhizomes flexible, 0.5–3 mm thick

c25.text: Stems conspicuously compressed, 2–5 times as wide as thick, 0.5–1.8 mm wide; apical portion of floral scales in the basal portion of the spike often bifid, with a hyaline, colorless region 0.6–1.2 mm long that is longer than wide

Stems angled to somewhat compressed, 1–2 (–3) times as wide as thick, 0.15–0.8 mm wide; apical portion of floral scales in the basal portion of the spike entire to emarginate, with a hyaline, colorless region that is up to 0.7 mm long and is wider than long to as long as wide

c26.text: Summit of leaf sheath lacking a tooth-like lobe; achenes 0.6–0.7 ×0.45–0.55 mm; anthers 0.3–0.7 mm long; floral scales 1–1.4 mm long; rhizomes 0.5–1 mm thick
Summit of leaf sheath usually with a tooth-like lobe; achenes 0.7–1.2 ×0.6–0.9 mm; anthers 1.5–2 mm long; floral scales 1.5–3.5 mm long; rhizomes 1–3 mm thick

c27.text: Achenes 1.1–1.5 ×0.95–1.25 mm, finely patterned with cellular reticulations; stems 0.5–1.5 mm thick at the midpoint
Achenes 0.6–1.2 ×0.45–0.9 mm, regularly patterned with conspicuous excavations (i.e., resembling honeycomb); stems 0.2–0.8 mm thick at the midpoint

c28.text: Stems usually 6- to 8-angled; achenes yellow to orange-yellow, somewhat persistent after the falling of the floral scales, with 12–20 horizontal ridges through the length of the achene [Fig. ]
Stems 4- or 5-angled; achenes green to brown-green (rarely yellow), deciduous with the falling scales, with 6–10 (–14) horizontal ridges through the length of the achene

c1.text: This genus contains exactly one species.
Styles bifid; achenes lenticular to biconvex in cross-section; edge of achene facing and fitting into a groove in rachilla
Styles trifid; achenes triangular in cross-section; one surface of achene facing and resting flat on rachilla

c2.text: Achenes broad-obovate to nearly suborbicular in outline, minutely marked with elongate, superficial cells and irregular, pale transverse lines at maturity; floral scales broad-ovate; flowers with usually 3 stamens
Achenes ovate to oblong, obovate, or narrow-obovate in outline, unmarked; floral scales narrow-oblong to ovate; flowers with 2 stamens (upper flowers sometimes with 3 stamens)

c3.text: Floral scales pigmented, in part, with anthocyanins (i.e., red-brown to purple-brown), rarely pale throughout, without a projecting mucro at the apex; achenes ovate to obovate in outline, rounded to broad-acute at apex, compressed to biconvex in cross-section

Floral scales lacking anthocyanic pigments, stramineous, gold-brown, to brown (sometimes light chestnut-brown), with a short mucro at the apex; achenes oblong in outline, truncate to obtuse at apex, biconvex (sometimes widely so) in cross-section

c4.text: Style divided nearly to its base, usually persistent in fruit; anthocyanic pigments most prominent along medial and apical margin of floral scales and along upper edges of midribs, with a conspicuous pale area between the midrib and margin [Fig. ]

Style connate in the basal , often deciduous from the fruits; anthocyanic pigments most prominent in basal and medial portion of floral scales, fading toward apex, the pigmented region not outlining a conspicuous pale region on each side of the scale [Fig. ]

c5.text: Achenes narrow-obovate in outline; floral scales 2.5–3.5 mm long
Achenes oblong in outline; floral scales 1.5–2.3 mm long

c6.text: Plants annual, with soft stem-bases from a fibrous root-system, lacking rhizomes and knotty tubers
Plants perennial, with firm stem-bases arising from rhizomes, knotty tubers, or a swollen corm-like base [Fig. ]

c7.text: Floral scales with 2 keels in the basal 30–60%; flowers with 1 stamen
Floral scales either with a single keel or merely nerved and lacking keels altogether; flowers with 2 or 3 stamens (only 1 stamen in C. squarrosus )

c8.text: Floral scales squarrose at apex [Fig. ]; flowers with 1 stamen; dwarf plants 5–20 cm tall, when fresh with a sweet scent suggesting Melilotus or Ulmus rubra
Floral scales not outcurved at tip [Fig. ]; flowers with 2 or 3 stamens; plants predominantly taller, 10–80 cm in height, without a sweet scent

c9.text: Floral scales 7- to 13-nerved, (1.5–) 2–4.5 (–5) mm long
Floral scales 3- to 5-nerved, 0.5–1.7 mm long

c10.text: Floral scales (3–) 3.2–4.5 (–5) mm long; spikelets disarticulating from the base and falling intact; achenes broad-linear to narrow-oblong in outline; stems usually arising from a swollen, corm-like base (in part)

Floral scales (1.5–) 2–2.8 (–3.2) mm long; spikelets disarticulating into segments at maturity, each segment consisting of a floral scale and a winged rachilla joint; achenes elliptic to narrow-obovate in outline; stems not arising from a corm-like base

c11.text: Floral scales broad-obovate to suborbicular; achenes 1–1.5 mm long, brown to nearly black at maturity
Floral scales ovate; achenes 0.7–1 mm long, pale gray-brown to nearly white at maturity

c12.text: Spikes ascending to appressed; distance between floral scales on same side of rachis 0.7–0.9 mm; floral scales tipped by a mucro 0.05–0.12 mm long
Spikes spreading; distance between floral scales on same side of rachis 1.1–1.5 mm; floral scales tipped by a mucro 0.2–0.25 mm long

c13.text: Spikelets radiating from the summit of short axes, forming subcapitate clusters; rachilla lacking a prominent wing-margin; roots brown
Spikelets serially disposed along elongate axes, forming cylindric clusters; rachilla wing-margined; roots anthocyanic

c14.text: Spikelets with 3–5 floral scales, crowded into dense, cylindrical to subglobose clusters, mainly only the tips of the spikelets visible in life
Spikelets with 3–20 (–50) floral scales, loosely to moderately crowded, many spikelets visible throughout their length [Fig. ]

c15.text: Spikelets (3.5–) 4–7 mm long, with membranaceous, yellow-brown to brown floral scales 3.5–4.5 mm long; spikes globose to short-ovoid; achenes 1.5–2.3 mm long; bracts scabridulous along adaxial surface (especially distally); stems growing singly or loosely cespitose

Spikelets 2.2–4 (–4.5) mm long, with coriaceous, brown to yellow-brown or red-brown floral scales 1.8–2.5 mm long; spikes obloid-ovoid; achenes 1.2–1.7 mm long; bracts smooth along adaxial surface, scabridulous only along margins; stems densely cespitose

c16.text: Floral scales with 2 keels in the basal 30–60%; flowers with 1 stamen
Floral scales either with a single keel or merely nerved and lacking keels altogether; flowers with 3 stamens

c17.text: Spikelets flat, serially disposed on elongate axes, forming cylindric clusters [Fig. ]
Spikelets compressed to subterete, radiating from the summit of short axes, forming hemispherical to subglobose clusters [Figs. , ]

c18.text: Floral scales (3–) 3.5–4.5 (–5) mm long, keeled along their midrib, persistent and falling with the rachis; plants lacking well-developed rhizomes, the stems emerging from a tuberous base; achenes broad-linear to narrow-oblong in outline (in part)
Floral scales 2.3–3 mm long, not or scarcely keeled, deciduous from the rachis; plants with long, slender rhizomes ending in tubers; achenes oblong to narrow-obovate in outline

c19.text: Floral scales with 3–5 nerves arranged close to the center of the scale (i.e., the sides largely nerveless); achenes up to 1 mm long; spikelets often proliferated into vegetative propagules
Floral scales with 7–13 nerves, these more widely distributed and only the very margin nerveless; achenes 1.4–3 (–3.5) mm long; spikelets not proliferous

c20.text: Floral scales suborbicular; achenes with 1 or more evidently concave faces, up to 1.5 times as long as wide
Floral scales broad-elliptic to oblong or ovate; achenes with flat or slightly concave faces, 2 or more times as long as wide

c21.text: Stems often scabrous near apex; floral scales with a short awn 0.5–1 mm long; achenes 2–3 (–3.5) mm long; spikelets ascending [Fig. ]
Stems smooth; floral scales blunt or with a minute mucro up to 0.2 mm long; achenes 1.4–2.2 mm long; basal spikelets of cluster horizontally spreading to reflexed [Fig. ]

c22.text: Involucral bracts ascending to sometimes spreading-ascending, with smooth to obscurely scabrous margins, numbering 3–7 per cluster; rachilla broadly wing-margined; inflorescence with (2–) 4–10 elongate rays; anthers 0.7–1 mm long

Involucral bracts mostly spreading to reflexed, with scabrous margins, numbering 2–4 per cluster; rachilla sharp-edged to narrowly winged; inflorescence with a solitary, sessile cluster or also with 1–4 rays [Fig. ]; anthers 0.3–0.6 mm long

c1.text: This genus contains exactly one species.

Hypogynium vestigial, therefore, the achene base ± continuous with the achene body and without a basal zone of different color and texture; leaf blades 0.5–2 mm wide; plants annual, from fibrous roots

Hypogynium present, therefore, the achene with a distinct basal zone of different color and texture; leaf blades 1–9 mm wide; plants perennial, from firm, nodulose rhizomes or annual with fibrous roots in S. reticularis

c2.text: Achene body lustrous and smooth; hypogynium unlobed and without tubercles, densely beset with minute, white to light brown papillae; leaf blades 3–9 mm wide
Achene body dull to sublustrous, either pitted or papillate-verrucose; hypogynium either lobed or with tubercles, without minute papillae; leaf blades 1–3.5 mm wide

c3.text: Hypogynium with 3 oblong lobes, without tubercles; achene body reticulate-patterned with polygonal pits; inflorescence a panicle of clusters, with visible branches

Hypogynium without lobes, bearing 6 globose tubercles arranged in 3 pairs; achene body papillate-verrucose, these projections sometimes arranged to provide the appearance of irregular transverse ridges; inflorescence a dense terminal cluster, sometimes with 1 or 2 axillary clusters as well

c1.text: This genus contains exactly one species.
Achenes 15–25 mm long including the 10–20 (–21) mm long tubercles; leaf blades 3–10 (–15) mm wide; style undivided or bifid only at tip
Achenes 1–3 mm long including the 0.1–1.7 mm long tubercle; leaf blades 0.2–3 (–5) mm wide; style deeply bifid

c2.text: Stems not cespitose, produced from slender rhizomes, achene body 4–5 mm long; achene tubercle 10–15 mm long; spikes solitary or in clusters of 2–6
Stems cespitose, without rhizomes; achene body 5–6 mm long; achene tubercle (15–) 18–20 (–21) mm long; spikes mostly in dense clusters of 10–30

c3.text: Plants annual; perianth bristles absent [Fig. ]; inflorescences open, diffuse, cyme-like or panicle-like; spikes brown to nearly black, stalked

Plants perennial; perianth bristles present (though sometimes caducous in R. torreyana ) [Figs. , ]; inflorescences of remote to congested clusters of spikes; spikes white to pale brown or red-brown to deep brown, usually clustered

c4.text: Tubercle depressed-triangular, 0.1–0.3 mm tall; achene body distinctly but irregularly transverse-rugose, with the marginal edges interrupted at the tubercle base
Tubercle narrow-triangular, 0.5–0.9 mm tall; achene body obscurely transverse-rugose, with the marginal edges flowing into the tubercle base

c5.text: Perianth bristles retrorsely barbellate (smooth in rare forms of R. capillacea and R. capitellata , antrorsely barbellate in rare forms of R. capitellata ) [Fig. ]; base of achene narrowed to a stipe-like process
Perianth bristles antrorsely barbellate (sometimes caducous, and therefore absent in fruit, in R. torreyana ) [Fig. ]; base of achene cuneate, not narrowed to a stipe-like process

c6.text: Flowers with 10–12 perianth bristles, these often antrorsely setose near base; floral scales white to light yellow-brown
Flowers with 6 perianth bristles, without antrorsely oriented hairs at the base [Fig. ]; floral scales pale brown to red-brown or deep brown

c7.text: Leaf blades filiform, 0.2–0.4 mm wide; spikes all ascending, in ovoid to ellipsoid clusters; achene body elliptic in outline, 1.5–2 mm long
Leaf blades ± flat, 1.5–3 mm wide; basal spikes of each cluster spreading, the spikes in turbinate to hemispherical clusters; achene body obovate in outline [Fig. ], 1.2–1.5 mm long

c8.text: Perianth bristles firmly attached to achene, reaching to base of tubercle or longer [Fig. ]; tubercle (0.7–­) 1–1.3 (–1.5) mm long; achene bodies very finely transversely rugose (i.e., pattern not evident without high magnification)

Perianth bristles weakly attached to achene, sometimes caducous, not extending more than the length of achene body; tubercle 0.2–0.3 (–0.5) mm long; achene bodies finely transversely rugose with irregular horizontal ridges separated by intervals of narrow, vertical alveolae

c1.text: Plants annual from fibrous roots; anthers 0.5–0.7 mm long; flowers with 1–3 stamens; leaf sheaths subglabrous to hirsute
Plants perennial from short rhizomes and corm-like offshoots; anthers 0.7–1 mm long; flowers with 3 stamens; leaf sheaths hispid-hirsute
