Inflorescence normally with elongate branches; styles mostly trifid; achenes compressed-trigonous to equilaterally trigonous; perianth bristles present on mature achenes [Fig. ], sometimes a few caducous; achene exocarp layer 0.15–0.5 times as deep as the mesocarp layer; plants of fresh to slightly brackish shores

Inflorescence normally congested and lacking elongate branches; styles bifid or trifid; achenes plano-convex to compressed-trigonous; perianth bristles rarely present on mature achenes; achene exocarp layer ± 2 times as deep as the mesocarp layer; plants of saline to brackish shores

c2.text: Widest leaf blades 2–6 mm wide; spikes slender, mostly 3–5 mm in diameter; achenes 2.5–3.3 mm long, with a minute, persistent style beak; veins of leaf sheaths gradually diverging near summit, leaving an obtriangular, veinless area

Widest leaf blades 7–22 mm wide; spikes thicker, mostly 5–10 mm in diameter; achenes 3–5.5 mm long, with an evident style beak 0.1–0.8 mm long [Fig. ]; veins of leaf sheaths nearly reaching summit before abruptly diverging

c3.text: Achenes 3.8–5.5 mm long, usually equilaterally trigonous, with isodiametric exocarp cells; perianth bristles firmly attached to achene, equaling the length of the achene [Fig. ]; anthers yellow

Achenes 3–4.3 mm long, usually compressed-trigonous, with exocarp cells 1.5–3 times as tall as wide; perianth bristles weakly attached to achene, 0.5–1 times the length of the achene; anthers dark yellow to orange-yellow

c4.text: Floral scales opaque, papery-textured, with awns ca. 0.5 mm wide at the base; anthers yellow when fresh, becoming orange-brown to red-brown after dehiscence or in drying; achenes dark brown, often compressed-trigonous; apex of leaf sheath opposite the leaf blade with abruptly diverging veins, green and firm-textured, prolonged

Floral scales translucent, membranous-textured, with awns ca. 0.25 mm wide at the base; anthers yellow when fresh, becoming pale yellow or pale yellow-brown after dehiscence or in drying; achenes light brown to dark brown, lenticular or rarely compressed-trigonous; apex of leaf sheath opposite the leaf blade with gradually diverging veins, with a hyaline obtriangular area, not prolonged

c1.text: Leaves linear, 0.2–2 (–3) cm wide; abaxial edge of achenes with 2 grooves; style ± coiled
Emersed leaves with narrow-lanceolate to ovate blades 3–12 cm wide; abaxial edge of achenes with a single groove; style merely curved

c2.text: Achenes 1.8–3 mm long; petals 3.8–4.5 ×3–3.9 mm, noticeably longer than the sepals; styles 0.4–0.6 mm long
Achenes 1.5–2.2 mm long; petals 1.8–2.5 ×1.4–2 mm, scarcely, if at all, longer than the sepals; styles 0.2–0.4 mm long

c1.text: This genus contains exactly one species.
Sepals of carpellate flowers appressed in fruit [Fig. ]; pedicels recurved (rarely spreading) in fruit [Fig. ]
Sepals reflexed in fruit; pedicels ascending to spreading in fruit

c2.text: Lower flowers bisexual; leaves represented by thick, spongy phyllodia (2–) 2.5–8 (–8.5) mm wide at the midpoint in drying (sometimes with a small, expanded blade at the apex)

Lower flowers carpellate; leaves represented by phyllodia that are flattened or lenticular in cross-section and 0.7–2.7 mm wide at the midpoint in drying (sometimes with a small, expanded blade at the apex)

c3.text: Leaves 5–30 cm long; peduncles 5–40 cm long; plants predominantly of brackish, tidal shores
Leaves 30–90 (–250) cm long; peduncles 10–200 cm long; plants predominantly of fresh, moderately moving rivers

c4.text: Filaments smooth [Fig. ]; leaves usually with blades that possess basal lobes
Filaments rough, beset with minute hairs [Fig. ]; leaves either without blades or with blades that usually lack basal lobes

c5.text: Bracts of inflorescence thick and herbaceous, distinct or with margins connate less than 25% of their total length; achenes with 1–3 facial wings; inflorescence with 2–4 whorls of pedicels
Bracts of inflorescence thin and scarious, with margins connate 25% or more of their total length; achenes with 0 or 1 facial wings; inflorescence with 2–10 whorls of pedicels

c6.text: Beak of the achene 0.1–0.5 mm long, erect; petals 7–10 mm long; achenes 1.8–2.6 mm long; floating leaves with sagittate-ovate blades produced on some deep-water plants; emersed leaves with a broad-lanceolate to triangular-ovate central lobe and borne on recurving petioles

Beak of the achene 0.6–1.8 mm long, horizontally spreading; petals 10–20 mm long; achenes 2.5–4 mm long; floating leaves with expanded blades not produced; emersed leaves with highly variable blades, the central lobe ranging from linear to broad-ovate, borne on ascending petioles

c7.text: Leaves all phyllodial, elliptic to terete in cross-section, generally tapering from near the base to the apex
Leaves phyllodial and with ± parallel margins that taper somewhat abruptly to the apex or with an expanded blade, in either case flattened

c8.text: Lowest whorl of carpellate flowers borne on pedicels 1–3 cm long; flowering stem straight, without a distinct bend; achenes 1.5–2 (–2.8) mm long, with a short beak 0.1–0.3 mm long; leaf blades (when formed) narrow-lanceolate to broad-lanceolate

Lowest whorl of carpellate flowers sessile or on short pedicels up to 0.5 cm long; flowering stem often with a conspicuous bend at the lowest whorl of flowers; achenes 2.5–4 mm long, with a beak 0.8–1.4 mm long; leaf blades (when formed) lanceolate to oblong-ovate or elliptic-ovate

c1.text: All or most flowers and fruits with 2 stigmas; all or most ovaries with 2 locules; body of achenes truncate or abruptly tapering to the beak, with 3–7 angles (i.e., not terete in cross-section), not constricted near center, 4–8 mm wide
Flowers and fruits with 1 stigma; ovary with 1 locule; body of achenes tapering to beak, terete or weakly angled in cross-section, often slightly constricted near center, up to 4 mm wide

c2.text: Flowering stems with 1 staminate spike; fruiting spikes 5–12 mm in diameter; beak of achene 0.5–1.5 mm long
Flowering stems with 2–20 staminate spikes; fruiting spikes 10–35 mm in diameter; beak of achene 1.5–7 mm long

c3.text: Beak of mature fruit flattened and strongly curved; tepals adnate to fruit stipe for ca. their length; anthers (0.5–) 0.6–0.7 (–0.9) mm long; stigmas (0.4–) 0.7–0.8 (–0.9) mm long
Beak of mature fruit ± terete, straight or only slightly curved (sometimes strongly curved in S. androcladum ); tepals free from fruit stipe; anthers 0.8–1.5 mm long; stigmas (0.6–) 0.8–4 mm long

c4.text: Both the sessile carpellate spikes of the main axis and the peduncle bases of the lateral branches borne directly in the axil of leaves or bracts [Fig. ]; tepals ± opaque, with a dark brown pad of tissue near apex, the apical margins emarginate to entire

Some of the sessile carpellate spikes of the main axis and/or the peduncle bases of the lateral branches borne above the axil of leaves or bracts [Fig. ]; tepals ± translucent, without a pad of dark tissue at the apex, the apical margins distinctly erose

c5.text: Fruiting spikes 25–35 mm in diameter; achenes usually dull in basal half and lustrous in apical half, with a beak (4–) 4.5–7 mm long; anthers 1–1.6 mm long; lateral branches of inflorescence, when present, bearing only staminate spikes

Fruiting spikes 15–25 mm in diameter; achenes usually dull throughout, with a beak (1.5–) 3–4 (–5) mm long; anthers 0.8–1.2 mm long; lateral branches of inflorescence, when present, bearing 1–3 carpellate spikes in addition to staminate spikes [Fig. ]

c6.text: Leaves usually erect and emergent, though sometimes flaccid and floating, the distal portion with a prominent abaxial keel or triangular in cross-section; beak of fruit 2–4.5 (–6) mm long; at least some of the staminate spikes separated by short internodes [Fig. ]
Leaves flaccid and floating (or submerged), the distal portion flat, without an abaxial keel; beak of fruit 1.5–2 (–2.2) mm long; staminate spikes contiguous

c1.text: Carpellate spikes (20–) 24–36 mm thick in fruit; leaves glaucous when fresh, the widest ones 10–23 (–29) mm wide when fresh, 5–20 mm wide when dry; compound pedicels on denuded inflorescence axis bristle-like, 1.5–3.5 mm tall [Fig. ]; carpellate bracteoles absent; stigmas persistent on mature fruit, ovate to broad-lanceolate in outline, 0.1–0.2 (–0.25) mm wide at the widest point; carpellate spike and staminate spike contiguous, rarely separated by a gap as much as 4 cm; staminate scales colorless to stramineous; mucilage glands at transition from blade to sheath usually colorless, obscure

Carpellate spikes 13–22 mm thick in fruit; leaves not glaucous, the widest ones 4–12 mm wide when fresh, 3–8 (–10) mm wide when dry; compound pedicels on denuded axis peg-like, 0.5–0.7 mm tall [Fig. ]; carpellate bracteoles present; stigmas sometimes deciduous in fruit, narrow-lanceolate in outline, 0.04–0.08 (–0.1) mm wide at the widest point; carpellate spike and staminate spike separated by a gap of 1–8 cm; staminate scales stramineous to medium brown; mucilage glands at transition from blade to sheath brown, visible in mid- to late season
Each margin of the leaf blade with 7–17 spinules [Fig. ], these either minute and unicellular or larger and multicellular; apex of leaf sheath truncate or auriculate [Fig. ]
Each margin of the leaf blade with 18–100 minute, unicellular spinules; apex of leaf sheath convexly tapering into base of blade (rarely truncate in N. guadalupensis )

c2.text: Axis of seeds curved; style situated at center of seed apex; leaf blades usually recurved in age, the margins with multicellular teeth that are often visible to the unaided eye; staminate flowers 1.9–2.2 mm long

Axis of seeds straight; style situated off to one side of seed apex; leaf blades ascending to spreading, the margins with minute, unicellular teeth that usually require magnification to resolve; staminate flowers 1.5–2 mm long

c3.text: Testa of seeds dull, minutely pitted and appearing so even at low magnification; seeds fusiform, widest at the middle; anthers 4-locular (rarely 1-locular); leaves 0.2–2.1 mm wide
Testa of seeds glossy, very minutely pitted and appearing ± smooth at low magnification; seeds narrow-obovoid to broad-obovoid, widest above the middle; anthers 1-locular; leaves 0.2–0.6 mm wide

Leaves 1.1–5 mm wide, averaging 2 mm, relatively firm, blunt at the apex, the upper densely crowded and overlapping; staminate flowers elevated on a long, slender, pedicel- like hypanthium 2–30 cm long [Fig. ], with a spathe 8–13.5 mm long, with sepals 3–4 mm long; carpellate flowers with sepals 2.0–3.5 mm long

Leaves 0.9–1.7 (–2.4) mm wide, averaging 1.3 mm, weak, pointed at the apex, the upper not densely crowded; staminate flowers sessile, with a spathe 2–4 mm long, with sepals ca. 2 mm long; carpellate flowers with sepals 1–1.8 mm long

c5.text: Inflorescence an upright panicle, pubescent; petals 2–3 mm long; branchlets and bud scales pubescent; bark brown to gray-brown; leaf blades 6–12.5 cm long

Inflorescence a drooping raceme, ± glabrous [Fig. ]; petals 5–10 mm long; branchlets and bud scales glabrous; bark green to green-brown, with slender, longitudinal, pale stripes; leaf blades 12–18 (–20) cm long

c6.text: Inflorescence an upright panicle; mericarps nearly parallel, diverging at an angle of less than 30 degrees; leaf blades green on the abaxial surface
Inflorescence either a dense, umbel-like fascicle or a drooping panicle; mericarps diverging at an angle of 30–90 degrees; leaf blades thinly glaucous on the abaxial surface

c7.text: Leaf blades dark green and lustrous on the adaxial suface, 3-lobed
Leaf blades light green and dull on the adaxial surface, unlobed or sometimes with 3 obscure lobes

c8.text: Flowers coetaneous or serotinous, in drooping panicles; sepals green, 4–5 mm long; leaf blades crenate-serrate, the secondary veins prominent on the adaxial surface; collateral winter buds absent

Flowers precocious, in dense, umbel-like fascicles [Fig. ]; sepals red, 1–3 mm long; leaf blades serrate, the secondary veins visible, but not prominent, on the adaxial surface; collateral winter buds often present on some branchlets on the plant

c9.text: Flowers with petals; mericarps usually diverging at an angle of 170–180 degrees; broken petioles yielding a milky latex; leaf blades green on the abaxial surface

Flowers without petals (i.e., with only sepals); mericarps usually diverging at an angle of 60–120 degrees; broken petioles yielding a watery latex; leaf blades glaucous on the abaxial surface (green on the abaxial surface in A. nigrum )

c10.text: Leaf blades mostly 4–7 cm long, ciliate, abaxially pubescent, with short, blunt lobes; corymb pubescent; mericarps usually pubescent
Leaf blades (5–) 10–15 cm long, eciliate, abaxially glabrous or with hairs in the junctions of veins, with prominent, pointed lobes; corymb ± glabrous; mericarps glabrous

c11.text: Flowers precocious, borne in dense clusters on very short pedicels that barely exceed the associated bud scales (pedicels later elongating as fruits mature); ovary and fruit pubescent; nectary disk absent or vestigial; winter buds red, blunt at the apex; branchlets often with collateral buds; central lobe of the leaf more than 50% as long as the blade and narrowed near the base; bark on mature trees with long, curling plates

Flowers ± coetaneous, evidently pedicellate; ovary and fruit glabrous; extrastaminal nectary disk present; winter buds brown, pointed at the apex; branchlets without collateral buds; central lobe of the leaf up to 50% as long as the blade and not narrowed near the base [Fig. ]; bark on mature trees with furrows

c12.text: Leaf blades abaxially glaucous and glabrous (rarely green) at maturity (sometimes pubescent on the veins or rarely across the surface with appressed to ascending hairs), relatively plane (i.e., the sides not drooping); bark gray to gray-brown, with loose-edged plates on mature trees; middle lobe of leaf blades often with ± parallel basal margins [Fig. ]; petioles without foliaceous outgrowths, not pubescent through their length

Leaf blades green and abaxially pubescent across the surface with spreading to erect hairs, the sides often drooping; bark dark brown and furrowed; middle lobe of leaf blades usually ± triangular and tapering from base to apex; petioles of vigorous shoots sometimes with foliaceous outgrowths that ± conceal the axillary buds, sometimes pubescent through their length

c1.text: Petals 5, white marked with red or yellow near the base of the blade, all but the lowermost petal with a cordate-based claw; leaves with (5–) 7 (–9) leaflets; winter buds resinous; fruit 5–6 cm wide
Petals 4, yellow to green-yellow, all with blades tapering to the claw; leaves with 5 (–7) leaflets; winter buds not resinous; fruit 3–5 cm wide

Corolla yellow, with orange stripes and purple spots on the adaxial limb, up to 2.5 cm long; leaf blades often 3- to 5-lobed, each lobe terminating in a slender point, usually glabrous on the abaxial surface (varying to pubescent); capsule 5–8 mm thick
Corolla white, with yellow stripes and purple-brown spots on the adaxial limb, 3.7–5 cm long; leaf blades unlobed, pubescent on the abaxial surface; capsule 6–15 mm thick

c2.text: Limb of corolla (2–) 3–4 cm wide, the adaxial surface densely spotted with purple-brown; capsule 6–10 mm thick, with a thin placenta; seed wings typically acute to acuminate at the apices and terminated by a narrow tuft of hairs, the width of the tuft usually less than the width of the seed wing [Fig. ]; leaf blades distinctly and abruptly acuminate at apex

Limb of corolla 4–6 cm wide, the adaxial surface sparsely spotted with purple-brown; capsule 10–15 mm thick, with a stout, quadrangular placenta; seed wings typically obtuse to rounded or obliquely truncate at the apices, terminated by a broad fringe of hairs, the fringe usually more than the width of the seed wing [Fig. ]; leaf blades long-acute to short-acuminate at the apex, the acumination (when present) usually more gradual

c1.text: This genus contains exactly one species.
This genus contains exactly one species.
This genus contains exactly one species.
Plants aquatic, with submersed leaf blades that are finely divided into narrow segments less than 1 mm wide (the emersed leaves, if present, with broader segments) [Fig. ]
Plants terrestrial, of wetlands, or sometimes aquatic, with leaf blades that are simple or divided with relatively broad segments [Figs. , , ]

c2.text: Petals white with yellow bases [Fig. ]; leaf segments capillary; achenes coarsely wrinkled on the surface, with a beak 0.2–0.5 mm long
Petals yellow; leaf segments flat; achenes smooth on the surface, with a beak 0.4–1.8 mm long

c3.text: Petals 7–12 mm long; achenes 1.8–2.2 mm long, the lower portion thickened and spongy; achene beak 1–1.8 mm long; styles 0.8–1.2 mm long (in part)
Petals 3–7 mm long; achenes 1–1.6 mm long, not thickened in the lower half; achene beak 0.4–0.8 mm long; styles 0.2–0.4 mm long (in part)

c4.text: All the leaf blades simple and unlobed [Fig. ]
Either the lower leaf blades or those borne on the stem or both conspicuously lobed to compound [Figs. , ]

c5.text: Leaf blades cordate to reniform [Fig. ]; achenes with longitudinal nerves
Leaf blades linear to lanceolate; achenes without longitudinal nerves

c6.text: Leaf blades 0.4–8 mm wide; plants with filiform, arching stolons; petals 1–5 mm long; achenes essentially smooth
Lower leaf blades (6–) 8–24 mm wide; plants lacking stolons, though rooting at the base of the stem; petals 5–8 mm long; achenes reticulate-patterned

c7.text: Leaves dimorphic—the basal ones simple with ovate to reniform blades and borne on elongate petioles, the stem ones becoming with conspicuously lobed blades and becoming sessile upward; nectary scale fused to petals on 3 sides, forming a pocket that encloses the nectary

Leaves ± monomorphic, relatively similar in general pattern, gradually becoming smaller upward, with shorter sinuses, and/or with shorter petioles; nectary scale separate from petal for at least 50% of its length and forming a flap over the nectary or the scale poorly developed and forming a crescent-shaped to circular ridge that surrounds but does not cover the nectary

c8.text: Petals 6–8 mm long; achenes 1.8–2.2 mm long
Petals 1–3.5 mm long; achenes 1.1–2 mm long

c9.text: Stems villous, the hairs usually discernable to the naked eye; base of some roots tuberous-thickened and 1–2 mm thick; basal leaf blades usually broad-cuneate to truncate at base; receptacle glabrous

Stems glabrous (infrequently with some tiny, sparse hairs that can be seen with magnification); none of the roots tuberous-thickened, the base 0.2–1.5 mm thick; basal leaf blades usually cordate to subcordate at base; receptacle sparsely pubescent

c10.text: Beak of achene 0.6–1 mm long, strongly curved [Fig. ]; sepals pubescent on abaxial surface
Beak of achene 0.1–0.2 mm long, straight to barely curved; sepals glabrous on abaxial surface

c11.text: At least the larger leaves with definite, unwinged petiolules (i.e., these leaves compound) [Fig. ]
Leaves with flattened, winged, sometimes ill-defined petiolules (i.e., the leaves lobed but not compound) [Fig. ]

c12.text: Petals 2–5 mm long, as long as or shorter than the sepals; anthers up to 1 mm long
Petals 6–15 mm long, usually longer than the sepals; anthers 1.2 mm long or longer

c13.text: Sepals reflexed along a defined, transverse fold 2–3 mm above the base [Fig. ]; plants either perennial with stems bulbous-thickened at base or annual
Sepals spreading (sometimes reflexed from the very base in age); plants perennial, the stems not thickened at the base

c14.text: Achene faces smooth; petals 9–13 mm long; plants perennial, with stems bulbous-thickened at base
Achene faces usually sparsely papillose (rarely smooth); petals 7–10 mm long; plants annual, without bulbous-thickened stems (in part)

c15.text: Some roots tuberous-thickened, the others slender; petals usually widest at or below middle; stems erect to ascending, not rooting at the nodes
Roots all slender; petals usually widest distal to the middle; stems decumbent to creeping and often rooting at the nodes (or upright and not rooting in R. hispidus )

c16.text: Styles short, curved, the persistent stigma spread out over upper side of style; achene beak (0.7–) 0.8–1.2 (–1.4) mm long
Styles elongate, with a terminal, deciduous stigma; achene beak (0.8–) 1.5–2.6 (–3) mm long

c17.text: Stems spreading to procumbent, 50–80 (–91) cm long at anthesis, sometimes rooting at the nodes; plants of hydric soils (e.g., swamps, marshes, ditches)
Stems upright, 14–45 (–60) cm tall at anthesis, never rooting at the nodes; plants of mesic to dry-mesic, upland woodlands and forests

c18.text: Stems floating or prostrate and rooting at the nodes; achenes plump, without a sharp or wing-like keel
Stems erect, rooting at only the base; achenes flattened, with a sharp or wing-like keel between the faces

c19.text: Petals 7–12 mm long; achenes 1.8–2.2 mm long, the lower portion thickened and spongy; achene beak 1–1.8 mm long; styles 0.8–1.2 mm long (in part)
Petals 3–7 mm long; achenes 1–1.6 mm long, not thickened in the lower half; achene beak 0.4–0.8 mm long; styles 0.2–0.4 mm long (in part)

c20.text: Achene faces usually sparsely papillose (rarely smooth); sepals reflexed along a defined, transverse fold 2–3 mm above the base; plants annual (in part)
Achene faces smooth; sepals spreading or reflexed from the very base; plants perennial from rhizomes, caudices, or bulbous bases or annual in R. sceleratus

c21.text: Petals 7–11 (–15) mm long, longer than the sepals; sepals spreading; receptacle glabrous; achenes 2–3 ×1.8–2.4 mm

Petals 2–5 mm long, equal to or shorter than sepals; sepals reflexed from near the base (sometimes spreading in R. sceleratus ); receptacle pubescent (sometimes glabrous in R. sceleratus ); achenes 1–2.2 ×0.8–1.8 mm

c22.text: Anthers up to 1 mm long; style absent; achenes in a cylindric cluster, each with a very short, straight beak ca. 0.1 mm long; stems not thickened at the base; nectary scale forming a crescent-shaped to circular ridge that surrounds but does not cover the nectary
Anthers longer than 1 mm; style present; achenes in a spherical cluster, each with a hooked beak 1–1.4 mm long; stems bulbous-thickened at the base; nectary scale forming a flap over the nectary

c1.text: This genus contains exactly one species.
This genus contains exactly one species.
Flowers and fruits solitary in axils of leaves [Fig. ], with petaloid staminodes between the sepals and stamens; sepals 20–60 mm long
Flowers and fruits in many-flowered cymes or panicles; sepals 5–22 mm long, white to cream

c2.text: Sepals 4 per flower, light red-purple to blue-purple, 25–60 mm long; style pubescent ± throughout its length in fruit
Sepals 6 per flower, usually white, 20–30 mm long; style apically glabrous in fruit

c3.text: Stems ascending to erect, not vining; leaves with 5–9 leaflets; achene beak 12–20 mm long
Stems vining (i.e., trailing or climbing on other vegetation); leaves with 3 or 5 leaflets; achene beak 20–60 mm long

c4.text: Leaves with 3 leaflets; flowers unisexual, the carpellate ones with 40–70 carpels
Leaves with 3 or 5 leaflets; flowers bisexual (sometimes some staminate flowers mixed in the same inflorescence), with 5–10 carpels (20 or more in C. vitalba )

c5.text: Sepals adaxially glabrous and abaxially tomentose along margins; leaflet margins entire; flowers with 10 or fewer carpels
Sepals adaxially and abaxially tomentose; leaflet margins entire to crenate or dentate; flowers with 20 or more carpels

c1.text: Leaves subtending the inflorescence opposite (though sometimes appearing whorled when the leaves are divided to the base); sepals 5–18 mm long, conspicuous, usually persisting through anthesis
Stem leaves alternate; sepals 1.5–5 mm long, often inconspicuous and sometimes caducous

c2.text: Leaflets mostly with 3 lobes, each lobe entire and without additional sublobes; filaments usually white, sometimes tinged with purple, somewhat to prominently dilated distally (slender throughout in T. dasycarpum ); anthers 0.5–2.7 (–3) mm long (up to 3.6 (–4) mm long in T. dasycarpum )

Leaflets with 4 or more lobes, these often appearing as 3 lobes and each lobe with 1–3 tooth-like sublobes [Fig. ]; filaments colored, usually red-purple to purple or yellow to green-yellow, ± slender throughout; anthers 2–4.5 mm long

c3.text: Filaments ± slender throughout; anthers 1–3.6 (–4) mm long, usually with a prominent apiculus at the apex
Filaments somewhat to prominently dilated distally; anthers 0.5–2.7 (–3) mm long, without an apiculus at the apex or a poorly developed one

c4.text: Abaxial surface of leaflets with sessile or stalked glands or white-papillose; achenes usually stipitate-glandular
Abaxial surface of leaflets lacking glands or papillae; achenes glabrous or pubescent with eglandular hairs

c5.text: Lowest branch of the inflorescence subtended by a short-petioled leaf, the petiole shorter than 30 mm; achenes inwardly curved; plants with rhizomes, flowering from early June through early August

Lowest branch of the inflorescence subtended by a long-petioled leaf, the petiole 30–60 mm long; achenes straight; plants arising from a stout caudex, without rhizomes, flowering from early May through early June

c1.text: Leaves dimorphic—the basal ones with 3 (–5)-lobed blades [Fig. ], the stem ones subtending the flower with simple, lanceolate blades; stem leaves closely subtending the flower
Leaf blades compound or lobed with deep sinuses in A. canadensis , the basal and cauline ones ± similar; stem leaves remotely subtending the flower

c2.text: Apex of leaf lobes rounded to bluntly pointed; sinuses, at most, extending to middle of leaf blade; stem leaves (i.e., bracts) rounded at the apex; achenes 1–1.4 mm wide
Apex of leaf lobes acute to acuminate [Fig. ]; sinuses indented beyond middle of leaf blade [Fig. ]; bracts acute to obtuse at the apex; achenes 1.4–1.8 mm wide

c3.text: Carpels and achenes glabrous or thinly pubescent, but not tomentose [Fig. ]; achenes in capitate to spherical clusters; plants with rhizomes (these tuberous in A. blanda )
Carpels and achenes densely pubescent, the achenes with long, tomentose hairs [Fig. ]; achenes in oblong to cylindric clusters; plants commonly without rhizomes

c4.text: Sepals blue (rarely white), numbering 8–14 (–18) per flower; rhizomes tuberous
Sepals white to pink (rarely blue or purple), numbering (4–) 5–7 (–12) per flower; rhizomes without tubers (but with caudices in A. canadensis )

c5.text: Leaves subtending flowers without petioles or these obscure; stems branched, with 1–6 flowers; sepals white; achenes broadly wing-margined; above-ground stems produced from caudices on rhizomes

Leaves subtending flowers with evident petioles; stems simple, with 1 flower; sepals pink to white (rarely blue or purple in A. nemorosa ); achenes merely with a sharp margin; above-ground stems produced directly from rhizomes

c6.text: Flowers with 5 sepals; rhizomes white or brown to black, 1–3 mm thick
Flowers with (5–) 6 or 7 (–12) sepals; rhizomes brown to black, 3–5 mm thick

c7.text: Leaf blades dissected into numerous, narrow segments (1.5–) 2–3.5 (–5) mm wide, those subtending the inflorescence sessile or nearly so; styles deciduous from achenes
Leaf blades divided into 3–5 broad segments (4–) 6–30 (–40) mm wide, those subtending the inflorescence distinctly petioled; styles persistent on achenes

c8.text: Inflorescence subtended by (3–) 5–9 leaves (i.e., involucral bracts); peduncles naked; cluster of achenes 2–4.5 cm tall, 2–5 times as tall as broad; styles crimson; beak of the achene 0.3–1 mm long

Inflorescence subtended by 2–3 (–5) leaves; peduncles with 2 additional subtending leaves; cluster of achenes 1.5–3 cm tall, mostly 1–1.5 times as tall as broad; styles pale or crimson-tipped; beak of the achene 1–1.5 mm long

c1.text: Leaf blades compound or lobed with very deep sinuses, usually with less than 2 (–4) mm of tissue from the base of the sinus to the base of the blade, the central leaflet or lobe lobed again with sinuses extending more than the distance to the midrib of the lobe; stems erect; seeds winged on the angles and rugose on the faces, but without thin plates and ridge segments

Leaf blades lobed with moderately deep sinuses, usually with more than 2 mm of tissue from the base of the sinus to the base of the blade, the central lobe toothed or lobed with sinuses extending less than the distance to the midrib of the lobe; stems erect, reclining, or climbing; seeds ornamented with thin plates and ridge segments
This genus contains exactly one species.
All the bracts of the inflorescence simple, sometimes the lowermost one dissected; sepals dark blue (rarely pink or white); upper lobe of petals 3.5–5 mm long
Lower bracts of the inflorescence (at least the lower 2, and usually more) dissected into 3 or more lobes; sepals blue, purple, red-purple, or white; upper lobe of petals 5–8 mm long

c2.text: Bracteoles on pedicels not touching the sepals, positioned 4–20 mm from the flower; spur 12–20 mm long; seeds dark brown to black; upper lobe of petals apically cleft for 0.2–1 mm
Bracteoles on pedicels touching the sepals, positioned 1–5 mm from the flower; spur 8–12 mm long; seeds red-brown; upper lobe of petals apically cleft for 0.5–1.5 mm

c1.text: Inflorescence, a solitary flower, subtended by an involucre composed of a whorl of bracts that are pinnately dissected into filiform segments; capsule smooth on outer surface, with 10 locules; ultimate segments of upper leaves linear
Inflorescence not subtended by an involucre; capsule tuberculate on outer surface, with 5 locules; ultimate segments of upper leaves broad-linear to narrow-lanceolate
This genus contains exactly one species.
This genus contains exactly one species.
This genus contains exactly one species.
Axis of inflorescence usually branched (i.e., the inflorescence a panicle); stigma borne on a short, stout style; fruit a follicle; petals represented by linear staminodes that are bifid at apex
Axis of inflorescence simple (i.e., the inflorescence a raceme) [Fig. ]; stigma sessile or subsessile; fruit a berry [Fig. ]; petals entire at apex

c2.text: Pedicels of infructescence slender, 0.3–0.7 mm in diameter [Fig. ]; berries red (rarely white); stigma narrower than ovary; leaflets commonly pubescent on the abaxial surface
Pedicels of infructescence thick, 1–2.5 mm in diameter; berries white (rarely red); stigma wider than ovary; leaflets glabrous or nearly so on the abaxial surface

c1.text: Perianth red (the sepals sometimes green at the apex); spurs straight to arching [Fig. ]; follicle with a persistent style beak 15–20 mm long
Perianth blue to purple (rarely white); spurs strongly curved inward; follicle with a persistent style beak 5–10 mm long
This genus contains exactly one species.
This genus contains exactly one species.
This genus contains exactly one species.
This genus contains exactly one species.
This genus contains exactly one species.
This genus contains exactly one species.

Leaflets borne on short petiolules 3–15 mm long, 5–9 per leaf; flowers with a calyx, which is persistent on the fruit and recognizable as a lobed cupule at the base of the samara; wing of samara decurrent on ca. of the body or less; terminal winter bud adjacent to the distal-most pair of lateral buds [Figs. , ]
Leaflets sessile, 7–13 (–15) per leaf; flowers without a calyx; wing of samara decurrent nearly to the base of the body; terminal winter bud separated from the distal-most pair of lateral buds

c2.text: Branchlets brown to blue-brown, glabrous; leaflets papillose on the abaxial surface, glabrous; terminal winter bud rounded [Fig. ]; leaf scar prominently concave on distal margin [Fig. ]; wing of samara extending ca. of the distance to the base of the body; leaf scars with a concave upper margin; petiolules not winged

Branchlets gray-brown, pubescent; leaflets not papillose on the abaxial surface, pubescent (sometimes only sparsely so); terminal winter bud acute [Fig. ]; leaf scar straight or slightly concave on distal margin [Fig. ]; wing of samara extending ca. of the distance to the base of the body; leaf scars with a straight or slightly concave upper margin; petiolules commonly winged

c3.text: Leaf rachis with thick patches of tomentum at the nodes where the leaflets attach; leaflets 7–14 (–16) × (2.5–) 3–6.5 cm
Leaf rachis glabrous to puberulent, but without patches of tomentum; leaflets (3–) 5–11 ×1–3 (–4) cm

c1.text: Calyx lobes (5–) 6–7 mm long; branchlets spreading to drooping; pith hollow through internodes and solid at the nodes; leaf blades broad-cunate to rounded at the base, sometimes 3-lobed or 3-foliate

Calyx lobes 2–4.5 mm long; branchlets mostly ascending to arching; pith chambered though the internodes and chambered or solid at the nodes; leaf blades mostly cuneate to broad-cunate at the base, simple (sometimes 3-lobed in F. intermedia )

c2.text: Pith chambered through the nodes; branchlets green to yellow-green; petals yellow with a green tinge
Pith solid at the nodes; branchlets yellow-brown to brown; petals pale to deep yellow

c1.text: This genus contains exactly one species.

Basal, connate portion of the corolla about as long as or slightly longer than the calyx lobes [Fig. ]; filaments relatively long, exserted beyond the connate, tubular portion of the corolla [Fig. ]; corolla white to cream

Basal, connate portion of the corolla 2.5–8 times as long as the calyx lobes; filaments very short, not exserted beyond the connate, tubular portion of the corolla, the anthers subsessile; corolla usually light purple, though sometimes white, blue, purple, or red-purple

c2.text: Terminal winter bud absent, the main axis of the branchlet not continuing growth in subsequent seasons; panicles produced only from lateral buds
Terminal winter bud present, the main axis of the branchlet continuing growth the following season; panicles produced, in part, from terminal buds

c3.text: Corolla with a ± cylindrical connate portion and spreading lobes; panicle tending to arch or even droop; anthers inserted near opening of corolla
Corolla with a slender-funnelform connate portion and ascending lobes; panicle upright; anthers inserted well below opening of corolla

c1.text: Branchlets either glabrous or minutely and uniformly puberulent; leaf blades glabrous
Branchlets pilose and/or pubescent with hairs of distinctly different lengths; leaf blades pubescent at least on the abaxial midrib or sometimes glabrous in L. obtusifolium

c2.text: Basal, connate portion of corolla 5–8 mm long, 1.5–3 times longer than the lobes [Fig. ]; anthers surpassing the tips of the corolla lobes; panicle and branchlets glabrous

Basal, connate portion of corolla 2.5–3 mm long, approximately as long as the lobes or a little shorter [Fig. ]; anthers not surpassing the tips of the corolla lobes; panicle and usually the branchlets minutely and uniformly puberulent

c3.text: Basal, connate portion of corolla 2.5–3 mm long, slightly shorter than to approximately as long as the lobes [Fig. ], usually barely exserted from calyx; anthers 1–2 mm long, typically exserted beyond the tips of the corolla lobes; panicles 6–10 cm tall, relatively open, often interspersed with non-flowering branchlets; pedicels 1–5 mm long

Basal, connate portion of corolla 5–8 mm long, 1.5–3 times as long as the lobes (rarely only as long as lobes) [Fig. ], evidently exserted from calyx; anthers 2–3 mm long, not surpassing the tips of the corolla lobes; panicles 1.5–4 cm tall, relatively compact, not usually interspersed with non-flowering branchlets; pedicels (0–) 0.5–2 mm long

c1.text: Inflorescence with a main axis that extends beyond the lowermost branches [Fig. ]; pith of branches orange-brown; winter buds large, ovoid; drupes red (rarely yellow) at maturity
Inflorescence branched from near the base and lacking a prominent main axis; pith of branches white; winter buds small, conical; drupes becoming purple-black to black at maturity
Leaf blades 3-lobed (sometimes the most apical pair of the shoot with simple blades) [Fig. ]
Leaf blades not lobed [Figs. , ]

c2.text: Bud scales 3 or more, generally at least sparsely pubescent; branchlets pubescent with stellate hairs; petioles lacking glands; drupe dark blue to dark purple
Bud scales 2 (sometimes appearing as 1), glabrous; branchlets glabrous or stipitate-glandular, not stellate-pubescent; petioles with raised glands; drupe red

c3.text: Marginal flowers of inflorescence not enlarged, fertile, similar in morphology to other flowers in the inflorescence; leaves without stipules, the blades usually toothed in the sinuses; petiole glands usually at very summit near edge of leaf blade; winter buds dark purple

Marginal flowers of inflorescence enlarged and neutral; leaves with slender stipules, the blades usually lacking teeth in the sinuses; petiole glands usually near apex of petiole but separated a short distance from the blade; winter buds red

c4.text: Winter buds naked [Fig. ]; branchlets, winter buds, leaves, and inflorescence axes stellate-pubescent; drupes red (eventually turning very dark)

Winter buds perulate; stellate hairs absent or present and then generally restricted to the leaves (abundant in V. plicatum , also on the winter buds in V. sieboldii ); drupes dark blue to dark purple (red in V. dilatatum , at first pink in V. sieboldii )

c5.text: Marginal flowers of inflorescence not enlarged, fertile, similar in morphology to other flowers in the inflorescence; leaf blades 5–12 cm long; pubescence gray; stems erect
Marginal flowers of inflorescence enlarged and sterile; leaf blades 10–18 cm long; pubescence yellow-brown to red-brown; stems straggling or loosely ascending

c6.text: Leaf blades with prominent, subpalmate or pinnate, simple to twice-forked (infrequently thrice-forked) veins that extend to the tip of each tooth; winter buds with 2 or 4 visible scales
Leaf blades with many-forked, less conspicuous, pinnate veins that anastomose near the margin and do not extend to the tip of each tooth; winter buds with 2 visible, valvate scales

c7.text: Inflorescence a panicle, with opposite branches; leaf blades elliptic-obovate, cuneate at the base, with a strong smell of green pepper when bruised

Inflorescence an umbel-like cyme, with whorled lower branches; leaf blades narrow-ovate or ovate to oblong-ovate or suborbicular, rounded to cordate at the base (rarely broad-cuneate), without a strong smell when bruised

c8.text: Winter buds with 2 visible, valvate outer scales
Winter buds with 4 visible scales, the outer imbricate, the inner valvate

c9.text: Winter buds scurfy-pubescent; flowers all fertile, ca. 5 mm in diameter; leaf blades abaxially appressed-pubescent; drupe red at maturity

Winter buds stellate-pubescent; usually all the flowers of cyme enlarged, 15–30 mm in diameter, and sterile; leaf blades abaxially glabrate to sparsely appressed-pubescent; drupe at first red, turning blue-black (but this rarely produced in New England populations)

c10.text: Leaves stipulate, with petioles 2–15 mm long [Fig. ]; stylopodium pubescent; stone of drupe compressed
Leaves exstipulate, with petioles 8–25 mm long; stylopodium glabrous; stone of drupe plump

c11.text: Cymes elevated on peduncles 5–50 mm long [Fig. ]; leaf blades entire to crenulate (rarely crenulate-serrulate) [Fig. ]; outer bud scales ribbed with vein primordia and upon bud expansion developing into foliage leaves

Cymes sessile or rarely slightly elevated on peduncles up to 5 mm long; leaf blades serrulate; outer bud scales not ribbed, upon bud expansion either soon detaching or slightly expanding but not long persistent

c12.text: Some leaf blades acuminate at apex; petioles 10–20 (–35) mm long, with an undulate- or denticulate-margined wing
Leaf blades acute to obtuse at apex; petioles 5–12 mm long, without or with an obscure wing margin

c1.text: Plants perennial, with woody rhizomes; all 3 flowers of each cluster inserted at the same level [Fig. ]
Plants annual, without rhizomes; the middle flower of each cluster conspicuously elevated above the 2 lateral flowers [Fig. ]

c2.text: Leaf and scale apex acute to acuminate, with a prominent mucro; inflorescence 4.5–6.2 mm thick, notably wider than the stem; flowers all concealed by bracts
Leaf and scale apex rounded to acute [Fig. ], without a mucro; inflorescence 2.9–5 mm thick, usually of similar thickness to that of the stem; central flower exceeding the bract and visible

c3.text: Inflorescences cylindric to long-tapering, the terminal with (5–) 7–23 (–25) fertile segments; scarious margin of leaves 0.3–0.4 mm wide; flowers with exserted stamens; fertile segments cylindric [Fig. ]

Inflorescences swollen and rounded near apex, the terminal with (3–) 5–10 (–14) fertile segments; scarious margin of leaves narrower than 0.3 mm; flowers not exserting stamens, or sometimes, but then after dehiscence; fertile segments widened in the apical portion

c1.text: Principal leaf blades coarsely dentate and with Kranz-type venation (i.e., with a fine reticulum of dark green veins, seen at 10 × magnification after scraping surface of leaf blade)

Principal leaf blades ± entire or with a single pair of tooth-like lobes near the base of the blade (rarely the blades sparsely and irregularly dentate, particularly near the apex) and with normal dicotyledenous venation (i.e., many vein branches free and not rejoining to form a reticulum)

c2.text: Flowers borne both in small axillary glomerules and in terminal spikes 20–50 (–110) mm long; brown fruits 1.5–2 mm long
Flowers borne in small axillary glomerules and in terminal spikes up to 20 mm long; brown fruits 2–2.5 mm long

c3.text: Principal leaf blades sparsely dentate and with a pair of larger teeth near the base or ± entire except for a pair of lobe-like teeth near the base; fruiting bracteoles tuberculate and echinate on the faces
Principal leaf blades coarsely dentate (rarely some ± entire); fruiting bracteoles tuberculate to ± smooth on the faces

c4.text: Fruiting bracteoles obovate-orbicular to obtriangular, with 3–5 (–7) apical teeth [Fig. ]; lower leaf blades oval or broad-oblong to broad-obovate, rounded to acute at the apex; fruits with the radicle apical

Fruiting bracteoles triangular or ovate to rhombic-triangular or rhombic, without apical teeth (though the lateral margins of the bracteoles may be toothed); lower leaf blades linear to triangular-hastate, acute to acuminate at the apex; fruits with the radicle basal or lateral

c5.text: Inflorescence with leafy bracts nearly to tip [Fig. ]; black fruits rare or absent
Inflorescence with leafy bracts only near base [Fig. ]; black fruits common, sometimes even more abundant on a given plant than the larger brown fruits

c6.text: Carpellate flowers dimorphic—some with no perianth and ovate-orbicular to suborbicular bracteoles and others with a 5-merous perianth and no bracteoles; fruits trimorphic­­—vertically oriented brown fruits, vertically oriented black fruits enclosed within bracteoles, and horizontally oriented black fruits partly enclosed in a 5-merous perianth
Carpellate flowers monomorphic, all lacking perianth but with a pair of accrescent bracteoles; fruits dimorphic—vertically oriented brown fruits and vertically oriented black fruits

c7.text: Lower leaf blades linear to lanceolate or narrow-oblong, lacking a basal pair of outward-pointing, tooth-like lobes

Lower leaf blades (and often the middle ones) lanceolate or oblong to triangular-hastate, with a basal pair of outward-pointing, tooth-like lobes (caution: the lower leaves are frequently deciduous by maturation of the fruits)

c8.text: Brown fruits orbicular, as long as wide, basally rounded; tip of radicle ascending to outwardly pointed
Brown fruits elliptic-orbicular, wider than long, basally flattened; tip of radicle inwardly curved (in part)

c9.text: Brown fruits elliptic-orbicular, wider than long, basally flattened [Fig. ]; tip of radicle inwardly curved (in part)
Brown fruits orbicular, as long as wide, basally rounded; tip of radicle ascending to outwardly pointed

c10.text: Lower leaf blades triangular-hastate with outwardly pointed basal lobes, the base truncate to subcordate [Fig. ]; brown fruits 1.5–2.5 mm long; black fruits 1–1.5 mm wide; bracteoles with a spongy inner layer

Lower leaf blades broad-lanceolate to ovate or triangular with outwardly or forwardly pointed lobes, the base cuneate to broad-cuneate or rounded; brown fruits 2.5–3.5 (–4) mm long; black fruits 1.2–2.9 mm long; bracteoles lacking a spongy inner layer

c11.text: Obligate halophyte of coastal saltmarshes; foliage (especially the margins) and stems often conspicuously tinged with red; black fruits 2–2.9 mm long
Ruderal weed, not of saltmarshes; foliage and stems green or rarely with weak red-tinging; black fruits 1.2–2 mm long

c1.text: This genus contains exactly one species.
This genus contains exactly one species.
This genus contains exactly one species.
Plants bearing 2 rigid, sharp-pointed spines (2–) 5–11 (–25) mm long at most nodes; terminal spike with staminate flowers in apical portion and carpellate flowers near the base
Plants without nodal spines; terminal spikes either entirely unisexual or with scattered flowers of each sex

c2.text: Plants dioecious; carpellate flowers lacking sepals or with 1 or 2 vestigial ones (or with 5 sepals in A. palmeri ); fruit an indehiscent utricle or an irregularly rupturing utricle (or a pyxis in A. palmeri )
Plants monoecious; flowers with a calyx of 3–5 sepals (rarely only 2), the carpellate sepals persistent in fruit; fruit a pyxis or less commonly indehiscent

c3.text: Carpellate flowers with 5 spatulate sepals 2–4 mm long and often only 2 style branches; bracteoles of staminate flowers (2.5–) 3–4 mm long; fruit circumscissily dehiscent

Carpellate flowers lacking sepals or with 1 or 2 vestigial ones shorter than 1 mm and 3 style branches; bracteoles of staminate flowers 0.6–1.5 mm long; fruit indehiscent or irregularly dehiscent (dehiscent in rare forms of A. tuberculatus )

c4.text: Utricle 2.2–3.5 (–4) mm long, fleshy, not dehiscent; seeds 1.9–3 mm long; bracteoles of staminate flowers 0.6–1 (–1.3) mm long, the midrib weakly excurrent; leaf blades linear to lanceolate; plants primarily of saline and brackish wetlands and shores

Utricle 1.5–2 mm long, membranaceous, sometimes dehiscent, though irregularly in most forms; seeds 0.8–1 mm long; bracteoles of staminate flowers 1–1.5 mm long, the midrib evidently excurrent; leaf blades lanceolate to ovate [Fig. ]; plants of fresh water wetlands and shores, gardens, dumps, and open rights-of-way

c5.text: Inflorescence composed entirely of small, axillary glomerules 2–11 mm in diameter [Fig. ]; leaf blades 0.5–4.2 (–7) cm long

Inflorescence composed of a terminal spike or panicle 20–300 mm tall, as well as often axillary spikes or glomerules [Figs. , ]; leaf blades 1–30 cm long, the larger usually longer than 4 cm (shorter in A. deflexus )

c6.text: Fruit warty-rugose, evidently exceeding the sepals
Fruit neither warty nor rugose, not or only somewhat exceeding the sepals

c7.text: Carpellate sepals 2.5–3 (–4) mm long; fruit indehiscent, fleshy, 2.5–4 (–5) mm long; seed oval in outline, 1.7–2.2 (–2.5) mm long; leaf blades fleshy, obovate to orbicular [Fig. ]

Carpellate sepals 0.8–2.7 mm long; fruit circumscissilely dehiscent (indehiscent in A. blitum ), dry, 0.9–2.2 (–2.5) mm long; seeds orbicular in outline, 0.7–1.6 (–1.8) mm long; leaf blades herbaceous, elliptic or oblong to obovate, rhombic-ovate, or spatulate [Fig. ]

c8.text: Leaf blades shallowly to deeply retuse at the apex [Fig. ]; fruit indehiscent
Leaf blades rounded to obtuse at the apex (rarely with an inconspicuous apical notch); fruit circumscissilely dehiscent

c9.text: Bracteoles of carpellate flowers 1–2.5 mm long, subequal in length with the sepals; carpellate flowers with 4 or 5 sepals 1.2–2.7 mm long; seeds 1.3–1.6 (–1.8) mm long; plants prostrate
Bracteoles of carpellate flowers 2–2.6 mm long, mostly 2–3 times as long as the sepals; carpellate flowers with 3 sepals 0.8–1.2 mm long; seeds 0.7–1 (–1.2) mm long; plants upright, bushy branched

c10.text: Carpellate flowers with 2 or 3 sepals; fruit indehiscent (i.e., a utricle)
Carpellate flowers with (3–) 5 sepals; fruit circumscissilely dehiscent (i.e., a pyxis)

c11.text: Fruits rugose when dry; terminal panicle mostly 10–20 cm tall; stems erect, 2–10 dm tall; fruit 1–1.6 mm long; seed orbicular in outline
Fruits smooth to slightly wrinkled; terminal panicle mostly 2–5 cm tall; stems prostrate to erect, 1–4 (–5) dm tall; fruit 2.3–2.6 mm long; seed obovate in outline

c12.text: Seeds dark brown to black; bracteoles exceeding the stigma branches in intact infructescences (except in A. dubius ); inflorescence not showy, dull green (sometimes tinged with red in A. hybridus )

Seeds white-yellow to red-brown (often dark brown in ornamental forms); bracteoles equaling or exceeded by stigma branches in intact infructescences; inflorescence often large and showy, usually red to purple (less frequently yellow or white)

c13.text: Bracteoles shorter than 2 mm; styles spreading; seeds 0.8–1 mm long
Bracteoles 2.5–6 (–8) mm long; styles erect to ascending; seeds 1–1.4 mm long

c14.text: Carpellate sepals rounded to truncate to emarginate at the apex, (2–) 2.5–3.5 (–4) mm long, outwardly curved; terminal inflorescence usually with many short, crowded, thick branches [Fig. ]
Carpellate sepals acute to subacute at the apex, 1.2–3 mm long, erect; terminal inflorescence unbranched or with a few, widely spaced, long branches or with many, crowded, slender branches [Fig. ]

c15.text: Bracteoles 4.5–6 (–8) mm long, 2–3 (–4) times as long as the sepals; sepals numbering 3–5, with yellow midveins, evidently unequal, 1 sepal 2.2–3 mm long, the others 1.2–1.6 mm long; apex of fruit gradually narrowed; inflorescence with few, erect, rigid, widely spaced branches

Bracteoles 2.5–4 (–6) mm long, 1.2–2 times as long as the sepals; sepals numbering 5, with green midveins, subequal or 1 longer, 1.5–2.5 (–3) mm long; fruit abruptly narrowed to apex; inflorescence with few to many, slender, lax or flexuous branches [Fig. ]

c16.text: Terminal inflorescence with stiff, thick branches 9–14 mm wide; bracteoles subequal in length to the stigma branches in intact infructescences [Fig. ]; stigma branches thick at the base; fruit ± truncate at apex

Terminal inflorescence with lax, narrower branches 4–10 (–12) mm wide; bracteoles shorter than the stigma branches in intact infructescences; stigma branches slender at the base; fruit gradually or abruptly tapering to apex

c17.text: Sepals narrow-oblong, acute at the apex, not overlapping with one another; stigma branches erect from the base; bracteoles 2–3 mm long, equal to or slightly longer than the sepals
Sepals obovate to spatulate, obtuse to rounded at the apex, overlapping with one another; stigma branches spreading from the base; bracteoles 3–4 mm long, 1.2–1.5 times as long as the sepals

c1.text: This genus contains exactly one species.

This genus contains exactly one species.
Leaf blades linear, fleshy in life, 1–2 mm wide in drying, gradually narrowed to a firm, spine tip 0.5–1.5 mm long; plants of Atlantic coast shores

Leaf blades narrow-linear to filiform, not or only scarcely fleshy in life, narrower than 1 mm wide drying, abruptly narrowed to a relatively soft, pointed tip; plants of human-disturbed or eroded soils

c2.text: Inflorescence usually interrupted in the basal half, at maturity with reflexed bracts that are not imbricate and ± abruptly narrowed to a spinulose or mucronulate apex; sepals usually with a transverse, membranous wings; fruiting calyx 4–10 mm in diameter

Inflorescence relatively dense, with contiguous spikes, at maturity with appressed bracts that are imbricate and gradually narrowed to a spinulose apex; sepals without a transverse wing or with a narrow, erose wing; fruiting calyx 2–5 mm in diameter

c1.text: This genus contains exactly one species.
This genus contains exactly one species.
Perianth segments each with a curved spine on the abaxial surface [Fig. ]; leaf blades flat, linear to lanceolate or narrow-elliptic; axis of inflorescence straight

Three (rarely only 2) of the perianth segments with a conical (i.e., non-hooked) projection on the abaxial side; leaf blades semicircular in cross-section, linear to filiform; axis of inflorescence flexuous
Sepals rounded on the abaxial surface, ± equal in size [Fig. ]; utricle 1–2 mm long
Sepals keeled on the abaxial surface or 1 or 2 of them larger and corniculate-appendaged; utricle 1–1.5 mm long

c2.text: Sepals unequal at maturity, 1–3 of them larger and corniculate-appendaged; anthers 0.3–0.4 mm long
Sepals ± equal in size, keeled at maturity [Fig. ]; anthers 0.2–0.3 mm long

c1.text: Fruits arranged vertically or both vertically and horizontally in the calyx; calyx with 3–5 sepals [Fig. ]
Fruits arranged horizontally in the calyx; calyx with 5 sepals [Figs. , , ]

c2.text: Plants perennial from a thick, woody root system; leaf blades entire except for the basal pair of outwardly pointing lobes; achenes 1.5–2 mm wide; styles persistent on the fruit, 0.8–1.5 mm long; calyx with 4 or 5 sepals
Plants annual from a taproot; leaf blades dentate or serrate (sometimes ± entire in C. rubrum var. humile );

c3.text: Principal leaf blades lanceolate to elliptic or oblong, conspicuously farinose on the abaxial surface; glomerules of flowers 1.8–2.5 mm wide; most fruits horizontally oriented, some vertically oriented [Fig. ]
Principal leaf blades triangular to rhombic-ovate (rarely oblong), green or sparsely farinose on the abaxial surface; glomerules of flowers 2–12 mm wide; most or all fruits vertically oriented

c4.text: Glomerules of flowers 2–5 mm wide; sepals at maturity herbaceous (somewhat fleshy in var. humile ); horizontal seeds frequently present; vertical seeds with a basal radicle; plants coastal halophytes

Glomerules of flowers (3–) 5–12 mm wide; sepals at maturity fleshy; fruits all vertically oriented; horizontal seeds absent; vertical seeds with an apical radicle; plants inland weeds of forest openings and disturbed areas

c5.text: Glomerules without subtending bracteal leaves (except sometimes the lower ones of each branch); seeds with convex sides, not grooved around periphery; flowers maturing from apex of inflorescence toward base
Glomerules subtended by bracts; seeds with a flattened groove around the periphery; flowers maturing from base of inflorescence toward apex

c6.text: Sepals flat or with an inconspicuous keel on the abaxial surface, at maturity conforming to the outline of the fruit and the outline of the calyx appearing ± circular (except where individual sepals spread or reflex away from fruit) [Fig. ]; stems, leaf blades, and sepals usually glabrous and green (plants sometimes sparsely farinose on some surfaces, especially when young)

Sepals keeled on the abaxial surface, not conforming to the fruit, the calyx appearing pentagonal or star-shaped [Fig. ]; stems, leaf blades, and sepals moderately to densely farinose (foliage sometimes ± glabrous in forms of C. album )

c7.text: Leaf blades entire, or rarely with a single tooth on each margin; stems quadrangular; sepals apiculate at the apex
At least the lower leaf blades with prominent teeth; stems terete to angled, but not quadrangular; sepals retuse or obtuse to acute at the apex, without an apiculus

c8.text: Pericarp evidently separating from mature seed [Fig. ]; leaf blades lanceolate to oblong-ovate, entire or with short, ascending teeth
Pericarp firmly attached to weakly separating from mature seed; leaf blades ovate or rhombic-ovate to triangular, sinuate-dentate to coarsely dentate

c9.text: Flowers developing asynchronously (i.e., flowers and fruits will be present in the same glomerule until late season when only fruits are present); achenes 1.5–2.5 mm wide
Flowers developing synchronously (i.e., all the flowers in a glomerule of similar stage); achenes 1–1.5 mm wide

c10.text: Achenes 1–1.2 mm wide, with rounded margins; inflorescence typically much longer and standing well above the principal foliage leaves
Achenes 1.2–1.5 mm wide, with acutely keeled margins; inflorescence typically shorter than to shortly exceeding the principal foliage leaves (in part)

c11.text: Pericarp of mature fruits brown, minutely echinate (view at 20 ×), eventually separating and flaking away, leaving the lustrous, black seed [Fig. ]
Pericarp of mature fruits pale to dark, smooth, irregularly roughened, or cellular-reticulate, remaining firmly attached to the seed [Figs. , ]

c12.text: Leaf blades predominantly narrow-ovate, the larger usually wider than 10 mm and with some form of dentition or lobing; native plants of high-pH outcrops and woodlands
Leaf blades linear to lanceolate or oblong, (2–) 4–10 mm wide, entire to weakly lobed; naturalized plants of disturbed, often saline, soils

c13.text: Achenes with acutely keeled margins; leaf blades irregularly dentate (in part)
Achenes with rounded margins; leaf blades entire to serrate or infrequently dentate

c14.text: Principal leaf blades ± linear, 1–3 mm wide, with a single vein, entire; achenes 0.8–1 (–1.1) mm wide
Leaf blades narrow-lanceolate to rhombic, ovate, or triangular, 5–75 (–90) mm wide, pinnately veined, entire to, more commonly, toothed or lobed; achenes 0.9–2 mm wide

c15.text: Achenes (1–) 1.3–2 mm wide, with a conspicuously cellular-reticulate pericarp [Fig. ]; a minute style base (up to 0.2 mm long) sometimes present below the stigma branches
Achenes 0.9–1.5 (–1.6) mm wide, with a smooth or obscurely marked pericarp; style base absent, the 2 stigma branches sessile at the summit of the ovary

c16.text: Sepals of many flowers spreading to reflexed at maturity, not covering the oval achene [Fig. ]; lower leaf blades usually serrate with small, low teeth
Sepals curved over the orbicular achene and concealing it (rarely some flowers with exposed fruits) [Fig. ]; lower leaf blades variable, usually prominently serrate or with tooth-like lobes

c1.text: Calyx connate except at the very apex, prominently reticulate-veiny, completely enclosing the mature fruit [Fig. ]; leaves not aromatic, the blades lacking glands

Calyx distinct or connate only at base, not reticulate-veiny, enclosing the fruit or not at maturity; leaves aromatic, the blades with either resin glands or glandular hairs (very rarely lacking both)

c2.text: Fruits mostly vertically oriented in the calyx, oval in outline, 0.5–0.7 mm wide
Fruits mostly horizontally oriented in the calyx, suborbicular or oval in outline, 0.6–1 mm wide

c3.text: Sepals with a fimbriate keel on the abaxial (i.e., outer) surface; glomerules of flowers 4–6 mm wide
Sepals lacking a keel on the abaxial surface; glomerules of flowers 1.2–2.8 (–3.5) mm wide

c4.text: Leaf blades 1.3–4.5 cm long, the lower typically pinnately lobed; pericarp of fruit often with translucent white strips or blotches, lacking glands, firmly adherent to seed; gynoecium with 2 stigmas; flowers mostly solitary, many with pedicels

Larger leaf blades (2–) 4.5–8 (–12) cm long, serrate to laciniately toothed; pericarp of fruits lacking translucent white marks, glandular, not adherent to seed and separating at maturity; gynoecium with 3 stigmas; flowers in small glomerules, sessile

c5.text: Sepals acute to acuminate at the apex, glandular-pubescent, lacking tubercles; cymes densely arranged on raceme-like branches
Sepals acute to obtuse, with sessile glands, with a single tubercle on the abaxial surface; cymes diffusely arranged on raceme- to panicle-like branches

c6.text: Glomerules of flowers subtended by obvious bracts; lower leaf blades typically serrate; plants flowering in summer through fall

Glomerules of flowers lacking bracts throughout or with very small bracts shorter than the glomerules [Fig. ]; lower leaf blades typically laciniately serrate; plants flowering in late summer through fall

Corolla narrower than 25 mm; calyx 7–12 mm long in flower
Corolla wider than 25 mm; calyx (10–) 14–18 mm long in flower

Inflorescence an elongate thyrse borne at the summit of the stem and branches, the primary one mostly 10–40 cm tall; flowers with 12 stamens, trimorphic; petals 7–12 mm long; leaf blades 3–10 cm long, 2 or 3 at each node

Inflorescence composed of solitary or paired flowers in the axils of leaves; flowers with 4–6 stamens, mono- or dimorphic (with 12 stamens and trimorphic in L. junceum ); petals 2–6 mm long; leaf blades 0.8–4 cm long, usually 1 at each of the middle and upper nodes (regularly opposite in L. lineare )

c2.text: Intersepalar appendages 2.5–3 mm long, usually longer than the sepals; plants generally pubescent on the stem and/or leaf blades (very rarely glabrous); leaf blades truncate to subclasping at the base (very rarely tapering)
Intersepalar appendages ca. 1 mm long, about as long as or shorter than the sepals; plants glabrous throughout; leaf blades tapering to the base

c3.text: Flowers with 12 stamens; hypanthium spotted with red near the base; petals 5–6 mm long
Flowers with 4–6 stamens; hypanthium without red spots; petals 2–5 mm long (up to 6 mm long in L. alatum )

c4.text: Leaf blades narrow-oblong to lanceolate or narrow-ovate, 4–10 mm wide, rounded to truncate or subcordate at the base; hypogynous disk present, appearing as a thickened ring around the base of the ovary; plants perennial
Leaf blades linear to narrow-oblong, 1–6 mm wide, cuneate at the base [Fig. ]; hypogynous disk absent; plants annual or perennial

c5.text: Vegetative leaves chiefly alternate (the lower nodes sometimes with opposite leaves), mostly longer than the associated internodes; plants annual, usually bearing flowers from near the stem base and upward; intersepalar appendages definitely longer than the calyx lobes; flowers monomorphic as to style length

Vegetative leaves chiefly opposite, mostly shorter than the associated internodes; plants perennial, usually without flowers at the lower nodes; intersepalar appendages ± as long as the calyx lobes; flowers dimorphic—pin flowers with long styles and thrum flowers with short styles
