Calyx with 2 sepals; corolla salverform, 8–11 mm long; gynoecium with 2 linear stigmas; fruit 6–9 mm long, glabrous or villous
Calyx with 4 sepals; corolla funnelform, 5–6 mm long; gynoecium with a single, capitate stigma; fruit 2.5–6 mm long, strigose to hirsute

Lower leaves borne on an evident petiole; corolla lobes horizontally spreading, glabrous; flowers borne singly on an elongate peduncle 20–70 mm long; capsule compressed; seeds globular, with a deep, round cavity on the inner face

Lower leaves sessile or with an obscure petiole; corolla lobes ascending to recurved, pubescent within the basal, connate tube; flowers borne multiple together in a cyme on pedicels 2–5 mm long [Fig. ]; fruit not compressed; seeds meniscoid, with a ridge across the depression on the inner face

c2.text: Stem leaf blades broad-lanceolate to narrow-oblong, (4–) 5–12 mm wide, rounded at the base; sepals 3–6 mm long at anthesis
Stem leaf blades broad-linear to narrow-oblong, 2–5 mm wide, narrowed to the base; sepals 1.5–2.5 (–2.7) mm long at anthesis

c1.text: This genus contains exactly one species.
This genus contains exactly one species.
This genus contains exactly one species.
Primary axis and main branches of plants with (2–) 4 leaves at each node [Figs. , ]
Primary axis and main branches with 5–12 leaves at each node [Fig. ]

c2.text: Principal leaves with 3 or 5 nerves [Fig. ]; schizocarps bristly (sometimes glabrous in G. boreale ) [Fig. ]
Principal leaves with 1 nerve [Figs. , ]; schizocarps without bristles [Fig. ]

c3.text: Corolla white to cream-white; leaf blades broad-linear, 1–2.5 mm wide; bristles of the schizocarp, when present, not hooked at the apex; angles of the stem commonly retrorse-scabrous

Corolla green-purple, purple, or yellow-green; leaf blades ovate to obovate or elliptic to oval, 5–25 mm wide; bristles of the schizocarp hooked at the apex [Fig. ]; angles of the stem glabrous or pubescent, but not retrorse-scabrous

c4.text: Flowers all pedicellate at the tips of the inflorescence branches; leaf blades 10–30 mm long
Some of the flowers sessile along the branches of the inflorescence [Fig. ]; leaf blades 20–80 mm long

c5.text: Flowering stems with 2–4 (–5) nodes; distal leaf blades larger than proximal leaf blades; corolla yellow-white
Flower stems with more than 6 nodes; leaf blades of ± uniform size along the stem; corolla green-white to purple

c6.text: Leaf blades oval to elliptic, widest usually near the middle, obtuse at the apex [Fig. ]; petals commonly pubescent on the abaxial surface, acute at the apex [Fig. ]
Leaf blades elliptic to lanceolate, widest usually below the middle, acute to acuminate at the apex; petals glabrous, acuminate at the apex

c7.text: Cymes branched 3 or more times, bearing 5 or more flowers [Fig. ]; some of the pedicels spreading, especially in fruit (in part)
Cymes branched 1 or 2 times, bearing 2–4 flowers [Figs. , ]; pedicels mostly erect to ascending (often divaricately spreading in G. tinctorium )

c8.text: Corollas mostly 3-merous, 0.8–2.5 mm in diameter, the obtuse lobes as wide as or wider than long; stems often retrorse-scabrous on the angles [Fig. ], usually not densely short-bearded just below the nodes; plants developing prostrate, basal offshoots late in the season

Corollas 4-merous, 2–3.5 mm in diameter, the acute lobes longer than wide; stems not scabrous on the angles [Fig. ], densely short-bearded just below the nodes [Fig. ]; plants not developing basal offshoots in late season

c9.text: Fruiting pedicels ± straight, stiff, lacking scabrules, usually some divaricately spreading (sometimes somewhat arcuate and/or with a few scabrules in G. tinctorium ssp. floridanum ) [Fig. ]; corolla 1.5–2.5 mm in diameter
Fruiting pedicels arcuate, scabrous or, less commonly, smooth, mostly erect to ascending [Fig. ]; corolla 0.8–1.5 (–1.6) mm in diameter

c10.text: Corolla 0.8–1 mm in diameter; leaf blades 5–8 (–12) × (0.8–) 1–2 (–3) mm; mature schizocarps 1.8–2 (–2.3) mm wide; fruiting peduncles 1.5–5 mm long, smooth
Corolla 1.2–1.5 (–1.6) mm in diameter; leaf blades (7–) 8–20 (–25) × (1–) 1.2–5 (–6) mm; mature schizocarps (2–) 2.2–3.5 (–4) mm wide; fruiting peduncles (2–) 3–15 (–20) mm long, scabrous or smooth

c11.text: Leaf blades 10–30 ×1–6 mm, ascending to spreading; mericarps 4–5 mm in diameter, tuberculate, usually only 1 developing; stems 2–8 dm tall
Leaf blades 8–15 ×1–3 mm, spreading to deflexed; mericarps 2–3 mm in diameter, smooth, usually both developing; stems 1–4 dm tall

c12.text: Leaf blades blunt at the apex [Figs. , ]
Leaf blades sharply pointed to cuspidate at the apex

c13.text: Cymes branched 3 or more times, bearing 5 or more flowers; some of the pedicels spreading, especially in fruit; corollas 4-merous, 2.5–3.3 mm wide, the lobes longer than wide (in part)
Cymes branched 1 or 2 times, bearing 2–4 flowers; pedicels mostly erect or ascending; corollas mostly 3-merous, 0.8–2.5 mm wide, the lobes as wide as or wider than long

c14.text: Corolla 0.5–1 mm in diameter, yellow-red; schizocarps 1–1.4 mm wide, finely papillose on the surface

Corolla 1–7 mm in diameter, white, green-white, or yellow; schizocarps 2–6 mm wide, smooth or uncinate-bristly (papillose with pointed projections in G. tricornutum , but then the schizocarps 3–5 mm wide)

c15.text: Pedicels strongly recurved to deflexed post anthesis; schizocarps papillose with pointed projections
Pedicels erect to spreading; schizocarps smooth or uncinate-bristly

c16.text: Stems scabrous on the angles of the internodes (at least on the proximal internodes), reclining to upright; inflorescences relatively few-flowered, each with 2–5 flowers, usually once- or twice-branched (note: a given plant can bear multiple such inflorescences)

Stems glabrous or pubescent on the internodes, but without scabrules, usually upright; inflorescences relatively many-flowered, each with 5–20 or more flowers, usually 2 or more times branched, collectively forming a large, open, cymose panicle [Fig. ]

c17.text: Leaves (6–) 8 per node; plants annual, with a short taproot; mericarps 2–4 (–5) mm in diameter
Leaves (4–) 6 per node; plants perennial, with creeping rhizomes; mericarps 1.5–2 mm in diameter

c18.text: Schizocarps glabrous; leaf blades 8–20 ×2–6 mm, retrorsely scabrous on the margin; corolla white
Schizocarps uncinate-bristly [Fig. ]; leaf blades 15–85 ×4–13 mm, antrorsely scabrous on the margin; corolla green-white

c19.text: Corolla funnelform, 4–7 mm in diameter; schizocarps covered with uncinate bristles; stems retrorsely hispid at the nodes
Corolla rotate, 2–3 (–5) mm in diameter; schizocarps smooth; stems glabrous or pubescent, but without a distinct ring of hairs at the nodes

c20.text: Leaf blades narrow-linear, 0.5–2 (–3) mm wide, the margins prominently revolute (sometimes the margins even recurved as far as the midrib), (6–) 8–12 per node; lobes of corolla merley acute at apex (rarely with an obscure apiculus in G. verum )
Leaf blades linear to elliptic, (1–) 2–10 mm wide, not or only slightly revolute, 6–8 per node; lobes of corolla apiculate at apex or usually merely acute in G. sylvaticum

c21.text: Corollas yellow, rotate, 2–3.5 mm in diameter; schizocarps 1–1.5 mm wide
Corollas white, cupuliform, 4–6 mm in diameter; schizocarps 1.5–2 mm wide

c22.text: Leaf blades 20–40 mm long, glaucous abaxially, distinctly paler than the adaxial surface; pedicels capillary, mostly 0.05–0.1 mm thick
Leaf blades 10–25 (–40) mm long, not glaucous abaxially, only somewhat paler than the adaxial surface; pedicels relatively thicker, mostly 0.08–0.2 mm thick

c23.text: Corolla 2–3 (–3.3) mm in diameter; pedicels usually longer than the diameter of the flower; inflorescence lax and open, the branches divaricately spreading post anthesis
Corolla (2.5–) 3–5 mm in diameter; pedicels usually shorter than the diameter of the flower; inflorescence relatively dense, the branches ascending to spreading post anthesis

c1.text: Leaves deciduous; plants flowering in spring
Leaves persistent; plants flowering in late summer and fall

c2.text: Leaf blades oblong-lanceolate to narrow-lanceolate, 3–8 times as long as wide; branchlets and leaf blades with silver scales only; calyx lobes yellow on the adaxial surface, about as long as the basal connate portion of the calyx; fruit yellow or silver

Leaf blades elliptic to ovate-oblong, up to 3 times as long as wide; branchlets and leaf blades abaxially often with some brown scales in addition to the silver scales; calyx lobes yellow-white on the adaxial surface, about as long as the basal connate portion of the calyx; fruit red with some silver scales

c1.text: This genus contains exactly one species.
This genus contains exactly one species.
This genus contains exactly one species.
This genus contains exactly one species.
Pappus absent; plants annual; rays yellow
Pappus present in some form; plants annual, biennial, or perennial; rays of various colors

c2.text: Involucral bracts membranaceous to herbaceous, not prominently keeled; peduncles not swollen; stems with foliaceous leaves
Involucral bracts becoming enlarged with an indurate, keeled midrib after anthesis; peduncles conspicuously swollen; stem with minute, bracteal leaves

c3.text: Pappus composed partly or entirely of scales (bristles may also be present)
Pappus composed entirely of slender bristles

c4.text: Pappus composed entirely of scales, the scales numerous; rays blue (rarely pink or white); involucre 9–15 mm tall
Pappus of 5 scales and 5–10 slender bristles; rays yellow; involucre 4–7 mm tall

c5.text: Pappus composed of two different elements—5 or 10 flat scales (these sometimes inconspicuous) along with 5–35 capillary bristles [Fig. ]; involucre composed of bracts of ± equal length, 4–14 mm tall; plants annual or perennial
Pappus of 5 or fewer bristle-tipped scales; involucre composed of two dissimilar series of bracts, the outer ones much shorter than the inner ones, 7–16 mm tall; plants annual

c6.text: Pappus bristles smooth or barbellate, but not pinnately branched [Fig. ]
Pappus bristles plumose (i.e., pinnately branched) [Fig. ]

c7.text: Cypsela body terete or several-angled (note: this character can often be successfully assessed with the flowering ovary)
Cypsela body evidently compressed

c8.text: Cypsela body muricate, at least in the apical portion, tipped by a long, slender beak [Fig. ]
Cypsela without sharp projections, with or without an apical beak [Figs. , ]

c9.text: Flowers pink, purple, white, yellow-white, or green-white; capitula with 5–16 (–26) flowers [Fig. ]
Flowers yellow, orange, or red-orange; capitula with 8–100 flowers [Figs. , ]

c10.text: Plants taprooted annuals or biennials; pappus bristles white, relatively soft; involucre composed of 2 series of principal bracts, the outer much shorter than the inner

Plants fibrous-rooted perennials, from short or long rhizomes or a caudex; pappus bristles sordid white to light brown, relatively stiff; involucre variable, either composed of 2 series of principal bracts (i.e., a long inner series and a short, outer series) or with 3 or more series of principal bracts

c11.text: Cypsela body without an enlarged disk at the apex where the pappus attaches, also lacking a beak; capitula with 80–250 flowers
Cypsela with an enlarged disk at the apex where the pappus attaches, with or without a beak [Figs. , ]; capitula with 5–56 flowers

c12.text: Capitula with 5 flowers
Capitula with 13–55 flowers

c13.text: Plants annual or biennial, without rhizomes; involucre 6–12 mm long in flower, becoming 12–15 mm long in fruit (except L. hirsuta , with involucres 15–22 mm long in fruit and cypsela bodies with a single nerve on each face); cypsela body with 1 or 3–9 nerves on each face
Plants perennial, from deep-seated rhizomes; involucre 12–15 mm long in flower, becoming 15–20 mm in fruit; cypsela body with 4–6 nerves on each face

c14.text: Involucre composed of 1 series of involucral bracts of equal length; leaf blades long and slender, grass-like; cypsela body 10–25 mm long excluding the beak
Involucre calyculate or with bracts of differing lengths; leaf blades relatively wider, not grass-like; cypsela body 2–7.5 mm long excluding the beak

c15.text: Stems resembling a scape, without leaves or with few, very small leaves; cypsela body 4–7.5 mm long excluding the apical beak
Stems not resembling a scape, definitely leafy; cypsela body 2–4 (–6) mm long excluding the apical beak (when present)

c16.text: Receptacle with chaff; cypselas muricate, the inner terminated by a slender beak
Receptacle without chaff; cypsela body rugulose, without a beak

c17.text: Reproductive stem with (1–) 2–7 capitula, with (7–) 10 or more scale-like bracts, these especially numerous just below the involucres; pubescence of plant strictly simple (i.e., of unbranched hairs); pappus in 1 series of plumose hairs

Reproductive stem with 1 (–2) capitulum, with 0–3 scale-like bracts; pubescence of plant, at least in part, compound, with 2 or more branches; pappus of inner flowers in 2 series, the outer series not plumose

c18.text: Outer series of involucral bracts numbering (8–) 13 or more, lanceolate to broad-linear, 0.5–1.5 (–3) mm wide; cypsela body apically narrowed but without a beak
Outer series of involucral bracts numbering (3–) 5, ovate to broad-lanceolate, 3–5 (–8) mm wide; cypsela body terminated by a slender beak nearly as long as or longer than the body proper

c1.text: Leaf blades spiny-margined [Fig. ]; involucral bracts (at least some of them) with a simple spine tip (the spine tip sometimes short in Cirsium muticum and C. palustre ) [Fig. ]; receptacle densely bristly setose between the disk flowers (except in Onopordum )

Leaf blades without spines; involucral bracts not spine-tipped (except Symphyotrichum ericoides ) or the bracts with palmately or pinnately branched spines [Figs. , , ]; receptacle lacking bristle-like setae (except Centaurea )

c2.text: Leaf blades streaked or blotched with white; lower part of free portion of filaments connate into a tube; pappus dimorphic—an outer series of minutely barbellate, narrow (i.e. bristle-like) scales and an inner series of minute, smooth bristles

Leaf blades not streaked or blotched with white (though sometimes entirely or strongly suffused with white in Cirsium arvense ); free portion of filaments distinct; pappus monomorphic, consisting of minutely barbellate or plumose bristles

c3.text: Pappus bristles plumose (i.e., pinnately branched); stem and branches with or without prickly, decurrent wings
Pappus bristles minutely barbellate; upper stem and branches with conspicuous, prickly and undulate-margined wings formed by decurrent leaf bases

c4.text: Receptacle flat, fleshy, deeply pitted with polygonal depressions that are dentate or short setose around the margins, lacking elongate bristles between the disk flowers; pappus pale red
Receptacle flat to conic, not fleshy, shallowly pitted, densely bristly setose between the disk flowers; pappus ± white

c5.text: Receptacle densely bristly setose; most or all of the involucral bracts tipped with an erose or a fimbriate- to pectinate-fringed appendage, the appendage sometimes spinose (entire in Amberboa ); cypselas attached laterally or obliquely to the receptacle
Receptacle lacking bristle-like setae; involucral bracts with entire or ciliate margins; cypselas attached basally to the receptacle

c6.text: Apical appendage of the involucral bracts erose or fimbriate- to pectinate-fringed, the appendage sometimes spinose; cypsela body with an entire apex, lacking a conspicuous rim around the attachment scar; pappus absent or of minutely barbellate bristles (in part)
Apical appendage of the involucral bracts entire; cypsela body with a minutely denticulate apex, with a conspicuous rim around the attachment scar; pappus absent or of slender scales

c7.text: Pappus double—an inner series of elongate, slender bristles and an outer series of short, scale-like bristles; style branches slender, gradually tapering to the apex, minutely pubescent on the outer surfaces

Pappus single, composed entirely of elongate, slender bristles (pappus double in Crupina , the inner series of black-brown bristles); style branches truncate, rounded, clavate-thickened, or shortly tapering to apex, mostly glabrous or minutely papillose, infrequently pubescent and then the hairs restricted to an apical tuft or an apical appendage

c8.text: Plants pubescent with white or gray tomentum or sericeo-tomentum, at least on the abaxial leaf surface (often also on the stem; some species becoming glabrate late in growing season)
Plants glabrous or pubescent, but not conspicuously tomentose

c9.text: Stems resembling a scape, scaly bracteate, appearing before the leaves; foliage leaves all basal, 5–40 cm wide, palmately lobed (in part)
Stems resembling a scape or not, in either case appearing after the leaves; leaves basal or produced on a stem, 0.2–5.5 cm wide, entire

c10.text: Plants dioecious or monoecious, none of the flowers bisexual (note: central flowers of carpellate Anaphalis appearing bisexual but have an undivided style with an abortive ovary and are functionally staminate)
Plants polygamous—the numerous outer flowers unisexual and carpellate, the few inner flowers bisexual

c11.text: Plants stoloniferous, with conspicuous rosettes of basal leaves, mostly 4–35 cm tall; staminate pappus apically clavate; carpellate pappus connate at the base and falling together; stems subscapose, with reduced, bract-like leaves
Plants not stoloniferous, without conspicuous rosettes of basal leaves, mostly 20–100 cm tall; pappus slender at the apex and distinct, falling separately; stems leafy, the leaf blades 7.5–12 cm long

c12.text: Receptacle with chaff; outer flowers of capitulum (i.e., the carpellate ones) without pappus
Receptacle without chaff; both the outer carpellate flowers and the inner bisexual flowers with pappus

c13.text: Chaff of carpellate flowers blunt at the apex, ± saccate, enclosing a disk flower; receptacle obovoid to abruptly expanded at the apex, 0.4–1.6 times as tall as wide; inner chaff spreading in fruit; cypselas dimorphic—the outer longer than the inner

Chaff of carpellate flowers acuminate to aristate at the apex, not saccate, enfolding (but not enclosing) a disk flower; receptacle clavate, 5–15 times as tall as wide; inner chaff erect to ascending in fruit; cypselas ± monomorphic

c14.text: Involucral bracts yellow-white to sordid white; capitulescence corymb-like, with elongate lower branches; outer disk flowers yellow when fresh

Involucral bracts light brown, yellow-brown, or green-brown to brown (sometimes pink to purple); capitulescence not corymb-like, either tall and slender (i.e., spike-like), subcapitate, or composed of axillary clusters [Figs. , , ]; outer disk flowers purple or at least apically purple when fresh

c15.text: Capitulescence composed of small axillary clusters of capitula [Fig. ]; involucre 2–3 mm tall; axis of plant often profusely branched; pappus bristles distinct but joined at the base by short, interlocking cilia

Capitulescence spike-like or subcapitate, in either case terminal [Figs. , ]; involucre 3–7 mm tall; axis of plant simple to sparingly branched; pappus bristles either connate at the base into a ring or distinct and without interlocking cilia

c16.text: Capitulescence consisting of a terminal cluster of capitula 10–15 mm in diameter, subtended by 3–5 leaf-like bracts, sometimes also with some smaller axillary clusters; stem leaves subclasping, with revolute margins
Capitulescence spike-like, tall and slender (subcapitate in depauperate plants), the axillary capitula subtended by a solitary leaf-like bract; stem leaves not clasping, with ± plane margins

c17.text: Body of cypsela glabrous; involucre 3–5 mm tall; pappus bristles basally connate into a ring, the entire set falling as a unit; body of cypsela 0.4–0.9 mm long; plants annual or biennial, of low elevations
Body of cypsela sparsely strigose; involucre 5–7 mm tall; pappus bristles basally connate or not; body of cypsela 1–1.5 mm long; plants perennial, boreal or alpine

c18.text: Leaves opposite or whorled (those of the upper stem sometimes alternate) [Fig. ]
Leaves alternate throughout the stem

c19.text: Plants vines; involucre with 4 principal bracts
Plants herbs; involucre with more than 4 principal bracts

c20.text: Leaves both opposite and borne on distinct petioles (rarely the upper leaves sessile)
Leaves opposite and ± sessile (i.e., the petioles, if present, ill defined), or whorled

c21.text: Involucral bracts all of similar length (1 or 2 outer, very small bracts may also be present) [Fig. ]; pappus bristles tapering to a fine point; adaxial (i.e., inner) surface of corolla lobes papillose (i.e., with a layer of projecting cells)
Involucral bracts of (2–) 3 or more conspicuously different lengths; pappus bristles blunt at the apex; adaxial surface of corolla lobes smooth (in part)

c22.text: Leaves in whorls of 3–7 with blades (15–) 20–150 (–180) mm wide; corollas, and often also the involucral bracts, pink to purple; involucres usually cylindric in flower, the margins parallel or slightly upwardly flared

Leaves usually opposite with blades 0.5–40 (–60) mm wide (whorled in E. hyssopifolium and E. torreyanum , but then with blades only 0.5–10 (–17) mm wide); corollas white (pink to purple in rare forms of E. perfoliatum ); involucral bracts variously colored, usually with green and white, but not pink to purple; involucres usually with a distinct upward flare in flower, obviously narrower near base compared with apex (in part)

c23.text: Capitulum with 3–5 flowers, usually only the inner 1 fertile and producing fruit; pappus of fertile flowers double—an outer series of short, triangular-lanceolate scales and an inner series of elongate, black-brown bristles
Capitulum with 5 or more flowers, producing more than 1 fruit; pappus single, all of elongate bristles, white to brown or purple

c24.text: Capitula 3–5 cm in diameter, with 200–450 disk flowers; involucre 10–20 mm long, with bracts that spread from the base during flowering (these becoming deflexed during fruiting
Capitula narrower than 3 cm, with (4–) 6–110 florets; involucre 4–17 mm long,

c25.text: Plants woody, often scurfy-pubescent on the capitulescence branches and involucral bracts, dioecious—the carpellate plants with capitula containing only slender, tubular corollas lacking apical teeth, the staminate plants with apically 5-lobed corollas and abortive ovaries with frequently connate style branches

Plants herbaceous, glabrous or pubescent but not scurfy, either synoecious and with all of the disk corollas of the capitulum with apical lobes or polygamous and then with unlobed, tubular corollas near the periphery and apically lobed corollas near the center of the capitulum

c26.text: All flowers of the capitula bisexual; plants perennial, or annual in most Senecio
At least the marginal flowers of the capitula unisexual and carpellate; plants annual

c27.text: Corollas red-purple (rarely white); capitulescence tall and slender, resembling a raceme; involucre consisting of 3 or more series of bracts of distinctly unequal lengths [Fig. ]

Corollas yellow to orange or green-white to yellow-white (rarely pink-tinged); capitulescence resembling a panicle or corymb; involucre consisting of a single series of long bracts, sometimes calyculate as well [Fig. ] (in part)

c28.text: Involucre evidently pubescent with short, multicelled, glandular-viscid hairs, arranged in several, overlapping series of dissimilar length bracts, commonly tinged with anthocyanin; anthers filiform-tailed

Involucre not glandular-pubescent, in 1 or more series of long, ± equal length bracts (sometimes with a very short, outer series of bracts in Erechtites ), green; anthers cuneate to sagittate at the base, but not tailed

c29.text: Involucre 10–15 mm tall, in 1 series of long, nearly equal length bracts, sometimes calyculate, turbinate-cylindric, conspicuously swollen at the base before anthesis [Fig. ]; leaf blades sharply serrate and sometimes also irregularly lobed; cypsela body 2–5.5 mm long
Involucre 5–11 mm tall, in 3 or 4 series of nearly equal length bracts, without a basal swelling; leaf blades entire; cypsela body up to 2 (–2.2) mm long (in part)

c1.text: Leaf blades spiny margined; involucral bracts tipped by a spine (the spine pinnately branched in Centaurea [Fig. ])
Leaf blades without spiny margins, though spines may occur on other portions of the plant; involucral bracts not tipped by spines (except Ageratum ; though they

c2.text: Capitula 1-flowered, aggregated in clusters forming a false, ± spherical, secondary capitulum that is subtended by a common involucre [Fig. ]; true involucre subtended by a tuft of capillary bristles
Capitula with more than 1 flower, not conspicuously aggregated in secondary capitula; involucre not subtended by a tuft of bristles

c3.text: Pappus composed of 10 outer, longer, minutely barbellate awns and 10 inner, shorter, ciliate awns; cypsela body ± tetete in cross-section; inner involucral bracts tipped by a pectinately fringed and spine-tipped appendage or the apical spine pinnately or palmately branched [Fig. ] (in part)
Pappus absent or composed of many rows of linear scales; cypsela body quadrangular in cross-section; inner involucral bracts lacking fringed appendages and tipped by a simple spine

c4.text: Receptacle bristly setose, hairy, or chaffy, at least near the margin of the capitulum; corollas anthocyanic, cyanic, yellow to orange, green-yellow, green-white, or white (or lacking on some flowers)

Receptacle without bristles or chaff (the persistent floral stipes of Cotula sometimes misinterpreted as chaff); corollas yellow (or usually blue to lavender in Ageratum or lacking in the carpellate flowers of Ambrosia trifida )

c5.text: Pappus of some form present, at least on the inner flowers
Pappus absent

c6.text: Most or all of the leaves opposite [Fig. ]; pappus of 2–6 awns, these usually retrorsely barbellate (rarely antrorsely barbellate or smooth or absent) [Figs. 381, 382, 383]; receptacle with flattened scales (in part)
Leaves alternate; pappus of bristles or scales; receptacle densely bristly

c7.text: Involucral bracts with an entire, attenuate, hooked tip [Fig. ]; leaf blades 15–70 cm wide, usually simple, rounded to cordate at the base
Involucral bracts tipped by an erose or a fimbriate to pectinate-fringed appendage, not hooked [Figs. , , ]; leaf blades up to 6 cm wide, cuneate at the base or pinnately lobed or both (in part)

c8.text: Receptacle densely bristly setose or long-hairy or naked
Receptacle with scale-like chaff

c9.text: Most or all the involucral bracts tipped by an erose or a fimbriate- to pectinate-fringed appendage [Figs. , , ]; involucre 10–25 mm tall; cypselas attached laterally to the receptacle; style branches with a thickened, often pubescent, ring, the texture of the branches changing to papillate distal to the ring (in part)
Involucral bracts with entire margins; involucre 1–7.5 mm tall; cypselas attached basally to the receptacle; style branches truncate and penicillate (in part)

c10.text: Staminate and carpellate flowers in separate capitula, the staminate capitula usually the uppermost and possessing an undivided style; involucre armed with tubercles, spines, or prickles [Fig. ]; carpellate flowers lacking a corolla

Flowers bisexual or unisexual and then the staminate and carpellate flowers in the same capitulum; involucre unarmed; all the flowers with a corolla (except in Cyclachaena xanthiifolia , in which the carpellate flowers sometimes lack a corolla)

c11.text: Staminate involucre of distinct bracts; carpellate involucre a conspicuous, prickly bur, 8–40 mm tall
Staminate involucre of connate bracts; carpellate involucre with 1 or more series of tubercles or spines [Fig. ], 3–10 mm tall (in part)

c12.text: Plants woody; leaf blades white-tomentose, evergreen, 3-dimensionally pinnately dissected
Plants herbaceous or usually woody in Iva frutescens ; leaf blades glabrous or pubescent, but not white-tomentose, deciduous, simple to 3-times pinnately divided, relatively plane

c13.text: Involucre with 2 series of dimorphic bracts—the outer series larger, herbaceous to foliaceous, the inner series smaller, membranaceous, and usually striate [Fig. ]; pappus of 2–6 awns, these usually retrosely barbellate (rarely antrorsely barbellate or smooth or absent) [Figs. 381, 382, 383] (in part)
Involucre with 1 series of monomorphic, herbaceous or subherbaceous bracts; pappus none

c14.text: Leaves alternate; inner flowers of capitulum (i.e., the disk flowers) bisexual, with a bifid style; plants annual, 1–10 dm tall (in part)
Leaves opposite (the uppermost sometimes alternate); inner flowers of capitulum functionally unisexual, the ovary abortive and the style undivided; plants perennial or coarse annuals, 5–30 dm tall

c15.text: Larger leaves with pinnately lobed and toothed blades [Fig. ]; involucre 6–11 mm tall (in part)
Leaves with simple blades that are toothed or double toothed; involucre 1.5–4 mm tall

c16.text: Capitulescence (or the principal branches in robust plants) raceme-like or spike-like; peduncles 0–3 mm long, many subtended by leaf-like bracts; carpellate flowers with a corolla 0.5–1 mm long
Capitulescence panicle-like; peduncles 1–6 (–12) mm long, few (if any) subtended by leaf-like bracts; carpellate flowers with a corolla 0.1–0.5 mm long, or the corolla absent

c17.text: Leaves whorled [Fig. ]; capitula solitary at the summit of the stem [Fig. ]; amphibious plants usually found growing in shallow water
Leaves alternate or opposite; capitula usually more than one in the axils of leaves, at the tips of branches, and/or at the summit of the stem; terrestrial plants

c18.text: Leaves opposite
Leaves alternate

c19.text: Plants synoecious (i.e., with capitula that have bisexual flowers); pappus present; leaf blades simple to dissected, but none palmately lobed
Plants monoecious (i.e., with separate staminate and carpellate capitula); pappus absent; usually at least some leaf blades palmately lobed [Fig. ] (in part)

c20.text: Leaf blades dissected into narrow segments; pappus composed of 10–20 scales that are cleft into 5–10 bristles at the apex; inner involucral bracts rounded to obtuse at apex (in part)

Leaf blades simple merely toothed; pappus composed of (4–) 5 (–6) scales that are fringed along the margins and terminate in a single, long awn; involucral bracts narrowed to an awn-like point 0.5–2 mm long

c21.text: Pappus of 2–8 firm, but deciduous, awns; involucral bracts squarrose and heavily resinous (in part)
Pappus of scales, a short crown, or none; involucral bracts neither squarrose nor resinous

c22.text: Capitulescence a solitary capitulum at the tips of branches or in the axils of leaves; outermost series of flowers lacking a corolla;; low, procumbent or trailing herbs
Capitulescence with multiple capitula, all the flowers with a corolla; none of the flowers stipitate; erect or ascending herbs or shrubs

c23.text: Capitula at the tips of branches; inner flowers stipitate, the stipes persistent on the receptacle; leaf blades (10–) 20–30 (–70) mm long; cypselas with two evident ribs or wings
Capitula mainly in the axils of leaves; inner flowers not stipitate; leaf blades 5–15 mm long; cypselas with ridged but not winged

c24.text: Capitulescence resembling a spike, raceme, or panicle [Figs. , ]; pappus none (in part)
Capitulescence resembling a corymb or cyme; pappus of scales or a short crown

c25.text: Pappus of 4–10 scales, the longer scales 2–6 mm wide
Pappus a short crown 0.2–0.4 mm long

c26.text: Corollas pink to red (rarely nearly white), with narrow-lanceolate to linear lobes that are mostly more than 2 times as long as wide, all actinomorphic
Corollas yellow, with lanceolate to triangular lobes that are mostly 1–2 times as long as wide, the outer ones enlarged and zygomorphic

c27.text: Leaf blades toothed, sometimes with a few basal lobes as well; cypselas with 5–8 rib-like nerves (in part)
Leaf blades 1- to 3-times pinnatifid; cypselas with 5 or fewer rib-like nerves

c28.text: Receptacle flat or low-convex [Fig. ]; disk corollas 5-lobed; plants 4–15 dm tall (in part)
Receptacle high-convex and pointed [Fig. ]; disk corollas 4-lobed; plants 0.5–4 dm tall (in part)

c1.text: Pappus composed of capillary bristles (also with an additional series of minute, slender scales in some Erigeron, with a short, outer crown in Callistephus ) [Figs. , ]
Pappus composed entirely of scales, awns, or a short crown, or absent

c2.text: Plants subdioecious, each capitulum composed almost entirely of unisexual flowers; stems scaly bracteate; well-developed leaves all basal, the blades palmately lobed [Fig. ] (in part)
Plants polygamous, each capitulum with the ray flowers unisexual and carpellate and the disk flowers bisexual; stems with leaves; leaves various, but neither all basal nor with palmately lobed blades

c3.text: Rays up to 2 mm long, shorter than to scarcely exceeding the pappus, often inconspicuous in drying
Rays 2–35 mm long, exceeding the pappus, evident even in drying [Figs. , ]

c4.text: Involucral bracts glabrous and eciliate; ± glabrous saltmarsh plants (in part)
Involucral bracts pubescent or ciliate or both; plants often with pubescent stems and/or leaf blades, at least with marginal cilia on the leaf blades, not occurring in saltmarshes

c5.text: Involucre with 3 or 4 series of foliaceous bracts of ± equal length; style appendages acute to acuminate (in part)
Involucre with green but not at all foliaceous bracts, the bracts of similar or dissimilar length; style appendage acute to, more commonly, obtuse (in part)

c6.text: Leaf blades pinnately lobed, each lobe terminating in a spine; involucral bracts ± spinulose-margined
Leaf blades entire to toothed (sometimes lobed in Callistephus ), not spiny; involucral bracts without spinulose margins (though the apex sometimes with a spine tip)

c7.text: Surface of ovary with minute stalked glands [Fig. ]; capitula nodding in bud; leaves reduced in size toward the base, the lowest scale-like
Surface of ovary without glands; capitula erect in bud (spreading or sometimes nodding in Ionactis ); leaves larger toward the stem base

c8.text: Capitula frequently in glomerules, with 3–8 ray flowers [Fig. ]; foliage leaves with sessile glands

Capitula usually borne singly at the ends of peduncles, with 7–100 or more ray flowers [Figs. , ]; foliage leaves without glands ( Oligoneuron album with obscure resin glands, and the bracteal leaves of some Symphyotrichum and Eurybia with stipitate glands)

c9.text: Basal leaves gradually tapering to an elongate petiole, the blade and petiole combined commonly 30–40 cm long; involucral bracts usually with a thin anthocyanic stripe along each margin; rare escape in New England

Basal leaves shorter than 30 cm, lacking petioles, and/or abruptly contracted to a petiole; involucral bracts rarely with marginal anthocyanic stripes, anthocyanin, if present, usually distributed near the center and/or apex of the bract (rarely throughout); primarily native plants, though some species weedy

c10.text: Involucral bracts in three series—the outer series foliaceous and green ± throughout, the inner series membranaceous to scarious; capitula solitary and the ends of branches, 6–8 cm in diameter; involucre double—outer series a short, membranous crown, inner series of minutely barbellate bristles

Involucral bracts variable, usually not foliaceous (except in a few Symphyotrichum ); capitula solitary, in glomerules, or few to many along branches; involucre single or double, but not with an outer, membranous crown

c11.text: Involucral bracts of ± equal length (sometimes with some very small bracts near the base of the involucre), green throughout or in large part, but not foliaceous; style appendage acute to, more commonly, obtuse (in part)

Involucral bracts of dissimilar lengths, usually pale at the base with an apically dilated green midzone [Figs. , , ], less commonly foliaceous or anthocyanic (green throughout in Doellingeria ); style appendages acute to acuminate

c12.text: Pappus bristles of 2 distinctly uneven lengths—a very short outer series and 1 or 2 series of elongate bristles of nearly even length [Fig. ]; involucral bracts neither foliaceous nor with a distinct, green apical zone [Fig. ]

Pappus bristles all elongate, in 2 or 3 series of nearly even length [Fig. ]; involucral bracts with a distinct green apical zone or entirely foliaceous in a few species (anthocyanic pigments sometimes also present) [Figs. , , ]

c13.text: Longer series of pappus bristles thickened at the apex; involucral bracts with raised midvein, but not keeled; rays not coiling; disk flowers abruptly expanded apically; ovaries terete
Longer series of pappus bristles slender at the apex; involucral bracts somewhat keeled; rays coiling; disk flowers tubular; ovaries compressed

c14.text: Disk corollas white; leaf blades with sessile resin glands (these sometimes obscure); pappus bristles thickened at apex (in part)

Disk corollas yellow or becoming purple, red, or red-brown; leaf blades without sessile resin glands (though the bracteal leaves stipitate-glandular in a few species); pappus bristles slender at the apex or thickened in some Eurybia

c15.text: Rays 2–3 mm long [Figs. , ]; capitulescence very slender, resembling a thyrse, sometimes with 1 or more elongate, slender, ascending branches resembling the main axis; disk flowers persistently pale yellow (in part)
Rays 3–30 mm long [Figs. , ]; capitulescence resembling a panicle or corymb or infrequently composed of 1 or few capitula; disk flowers yellow, becoming purple, red, or red-brown in age

c16.text: Outer and middle involucral bracts less than 2.5 times as long as wide, rounded to obtuse at the apex, densely ciliate along the margins, with a thumbnail to rhombic shaped chlorophyllous zone at the tip [Fig. ]; capitulescence corymb-like; pappus bristles sometimes thickened at the apex; ovary terete

Involucral bracts more than 3 times as long as wide, obtuse to acuminate at the apex, eciliate or sparingly ciliate along the margins, with a rhombic to basally tapering chlorophyllous zone at the tip or entirely foliaceous [Figs. , , ]; capitulescence commonly panicle-like when well formed; pappus bristles slender at the apex; ovary compressed in most species (in part)

c17.text: Leaves opposite (the upper may be alternate)
Leaves alternate throughout the stem or all basal

c18.text: Leaf blades 10–30 cm long, pinnately lobed with broad lobes [Fig. ]; disk flowers functionally staminate, the ovary abortive and with an undivided style; pappus absent (in part)

Leaf blades 2–12 cm long, simple or pinnately dissected into linear to linear-filiform segments; disk flowers bisexual with a bifid style; pappus present, at least on the disk flowers, though reduced to a tiny crown in some species (absent in Sigesbeckia )

c19.text: Leaf blades pinnately dissected into numerous linear to linear-filiform segments narrower than 1.5 mm; rays 5–40 mm long; cypsela body tapering to a slender, apical beak (in part)
Leaf blades simple or infrequently with a few basal lobes in Coreopsis rosea ; rays up to 13 mm long; cypsela body not taping to an elongate beak

c20.text: Rays 8–13 mm long; disk 5–10 mm wide; leaf blades linear (in part)
Rays 1–2 mm long; disk 3–6 mm wide in flower; leaf blades narrow-lanceolate to ovate [Fig. ]

c21.text: Involucre biseriate and dimorphic—an outer series of longer, spreading to reflexed bracts and an inner series of shorter, erect bracts—conspicuously stipitate-glandular; leaf blades resin-dotted abaxially (in part)
Involucre uniseriate or biseriate, with none of the bracts spreading to reflexed, stipitate-glandular or not; leaf blades not resin-dotted abaxially

c22.text: Disk flowers yellow; capitula with 3–6 rays [Fig. ], commonly 5; pappus of fimbriate scales
Disk flowers white; capitula with numerous ray flowers; pappus a tiny crown

c23.text: Receptacle with spine-like setae; lobes of disk corollas villous-tomentose; pappus composed of 6–10 conspicuously awned scales (in part)
Receptacle either naked, with scale-like chaff (though the chaff may be spinescent at the tip), or bristly; lobes of the disk corollas glabrous; pappus various, but not composed of awned scales

c24.text: Receptacle chaffy, at least toward the middle [Fig. ]
Receptacle without chaff

c25.text: Involucral bracts herbaceous, without a scarious margin, spreading to reflexed; leaf blades simple and ± entire; chaff with a stout, spinescent tip

Involucral bracts dry, scarcely or not at all herbaceous, scarious-margined (without scarious margins in Parthenium ), appressed; leaves pinnately divided (except Achillea ptarmica with simple leaves); chaff without a spine-like tip

c26.text: Pappus usually composed of a pair of scales; disk flowers functionally staminate, the ovary abortive and the style undivided
Pappus absent or represented by a minute crown; disk flowers bisexual, fertile, with a bifid style

c27.text: Rays 5–14 mm long, numbering 10–16 per capitulum [Fig. ]; disk 5–10 mm wide; disk flowers yellow; capitulescence not resembling a corymb, the capitula located at the tips of branches
Rays 2–5 mm long, mostly numbering 4–10 per capitulum (up to 15 in cultivated forms of A. ptarmica ); disk 2–8 mm wide; disk flowers white capitulescence resembling a corymb

c28.text: Stems scapose, the leaves all basal; capitulescence a solitary capitulum
Stems leafy; capitulescence with multiple capitula or solitary in Arctanthemum , Arctotis , Leucanthemum , and Nipponanthemum

c29.text: Pappus of disk flowers composed of 5–8 oblong to ovate, hyaline scales 0.5–4 mm long; cypsela with a conspicuous basal tuft of long, silky hairs
Pappus of disk flowers absent, a short crown, or dimorphic and composed of barbellate awns and shorter awns or flat scales; cypsela lacking a long basal tuft of silky hairs

c30.text: Pappus of disk flowers composed of 2–4 long, barbellate awns and a variable number of shorter bristles or flat scales; style branches not truncate at apex, lacking an apical tuft of hairs
Pappus a short crown or absent; style branches truncate and penicillate

c31.text: Leaves with simple and entire blades, not clasping the stem; pappus of 2 or 3 awns and 7–12 shorter bristles or scales
Leaves with subpalmately lobed blades, narrowed to a winged petiole, expanded at the base and clasping the stem; pappus 2–4 awns and 2–4 scales

c32.text: Leaf blades twice pinnatifid, with linear to filiform ultimate segments; receptacle convex, rounded, or pointed
Leaf blades toothed, subpalmately lobed, or 1- to 2-times pinnatifid into oblong-elliptic to ovate primary segments; receptacle flat or low-convex

c33.text: Receptacle conic, acute at the apex [Fig. ]; cypsela with an oblique attachment scar near base, the body with 3–5 raised, but not wing-like, ribs, lacking apical resin glands; plants pleasantly aromatic (in part)
Receptacle dome-shaped, rounded at the apex; cypsela with basal attachment scar, the body with 3, prominently thickened and almost wing-like ribs, with apical resin glands; plants nearly inodorous

c34.text: Plants subshrubs, with deciduous lower leaves, so most of the stems leaves are clustered near the apex of the shoot; leaf blades somewhat succulent, evergreen [Fig. ]
Plants herbaceous, the leaves not clustered near the stem apex; leaf blades not succulent, deciduous

c35.text: Pappus present, a short crown; capitula 6–20 mm across in life, arranged in corymb-like clusters; disk 4–9 mm wide

Pappus absent (rarely some ray flowers with wall tissue prolonged to appear as a short crown in Leucanthemella and Leucanthemum ); capitula 20–60 mm across in life, solitary at the tips of branches or arranged in corymb-like clusters; disk 10–25 mm wide

c36.text: Leaf blades crenate-dentate, sometimes the larger with a few basal lobes, the lower blades 10–25 cm long (in part)
Leaf blades with 3–9 oblong-elliptic to ovate segments that may be again lobed, none of the blades exceeding 8 cm in length (in part)

c37.text: Ray flowers sterile, not producing fruits; leaf blades glandular-punctate; disk corolla tubes provided with resin glands
Ray flowers fertile, producing fruits; leaf blades without glandular-dots; disk corolla tubes lacking resin glands

c38.text: Disk flowers compressed and winged near base; body of cypsela with 10 ribs; pericarp of cypsela with resin canals
Disk flowers neither compressed nor winged near base; body of cypsela with 5–8 ribs; pericarp of cypsela without resin canals

c39.text: Leaf blades glabrous or subglabrous, the lower flabellate to spatulate, nearly or fully as wide as long; capitulescence consisting of a solitary capitulum; rays white

Leaf blades gray-pubescent, lanceolate or elongate-elliptic to ovate, clearly longer than wide; capitulescence consisting of 1 to several capitula in a corymb-like array; rays commonly yellow, pink, purple, red, or white (but other color forms also exist) (in part)

c1.text: Anthers sagittate-tailed at the base; involucres with 3–7 series of involucral bracts

Anthers cuneate to sagitate at the base, but not tailed; involucres with 1 or 2 series of involucral bracts or with 3–5 series in Chrysopsis , Euthamia , Heterotheca , Oligoneuron , Pityopsis , Solidago

c2.text: Leaf blades lanceolate or elliptic to ovate, 12–200 mm wide; involucres 8–20 mm in diameter; rays 15–40 mm long, conspicuously surpassing the involucres; body of cypsela not contracted just below the attachment of the pappus bristles; pappus bristles 6–10 mm long

Leaf blades linear to narrow-lanceolate, 1–3 (–10) mm wide; involucres 4–7 mm in diameter; rays 4–7 mm long, not or scarcely exceeding the involucres; body of the cypsela abruptly contracted just below the attachment of the pappus bristles; pappus bristles 3–4 (–5) mm long

c3.text: Rays usually yellow with a white tip; receptacle with chaff; disk corollas puberulent
Rays entirely yellow; receptacle without chaff; disk flowers ± glabrous (sometimes sparsely pubescent in Heterotheca )

c4.text: Middle stem leaves with a short, broadly winged petiole that prominently expands and clasps the stem; upper stem leaves cordate-clasping
Middle stem leaves sessile or petioled, but without an expanded, clasping petiole; upper stem leaves not cordate-clasping

c5.text: Lower leaf blades broad-ovate to nearly orbicular, (5–) 7–14 cm wide; involucres 22–40 mm tall; pappus of disk flowers consisting of only bristles; plants perennial, from rhizomes

Lower leaf blades ovate to elliptic or lanceolate, 0.6–5.5 cm wide; involucres 4–8 (–10) mm tall; pappus of disk flowers consisting of both scales and bristles; plants annual or biennial, from taproots (in part)

c6.text: Leaves opposite, except sometimes the upper; rays 15–20 mm long
Leaves alternate throughout the stem; rays shorter than 10 mm (except Chrysopsis with rays 10–20 mm long)

c7.text: Stems with only small, bract-like leaves (i.e., scapose) [Fig. ], appearing and flowering before the cordate-suborbicular blades of the basal leaves are produced; disk flowers sterile
Stems with leaves, these present during flowering [Fig. ]; disk flowers fertile

c8.text: Involucre composed of a single series of long bracts, sometimes also calyculate (i.e., with a short, outer series of bracts) [Fig. ]
Involucre with (2–) 3–5 series of bracts of distinctly unequal lengths [Figs. , ]

c9.text: Plants perennial, with rhizomes and fibrous roots; leaves basally disposed (i.e., prominent clusters of basal leaves present, the stem leaves rapidly reduced in size upwards)

Plants annual or biennial (rarely short-lived perennial), mostly with evident taproots; leaves chiefly cauline (i.e., prominent clusters of basal leaves absent, the stem leaves gradually, if at all, reduced upwards)

c10.text: Rays 4–8 mm long; leaf blades relatively more divided, usually 2- or 3-times pinnatifid; cypsela bodies from near margin of capitulum glabrous, the inner ones pubescent

Rays absent or up to 2 mm long [Fig. ]; leaf blades relatively less divided, usually toothed to pinnatifid; usually all the cypsela bodies of the capitulum similar, either all pubescent or all glabrous in glandular-hairy S. viscosus (in part)

c11.text: Capitulescence not at all flat-topped, resembling a panicle or thyrse or consisting of axillary clusters of capitula [Figs. , ] (in part)
Capitulescence or its divisions flat-topped, resembling a corymb

c12.text: Pappus monomorphic—composed of elongate and slender bristles
Pappus dimorphic—an inner series of elongate, slender bristles and an outer series of short, course bristles or narrow scales

c13.text: Leaves chiefly cauline, the blades linear to narrow-lanceolate, parallel-veined, resinous-punctate [Fig. ]; involucral bracts with a single, median nerve; lower petiole bases not persistent

Leaves basally disposed, the blades elliptic or broad-lanceolate to broad-ovate, pinnately veined, not resinous-punctate; involucral bracts longitudinally few-striate [Fig. ]; lower petiole bases often persistent (in part)

c14.text: Leaf blades linear, arcuate, parallel-veined, sessile, entire [Fig. ]; cypsela body narrow-fusiform; involucre white-pubescent
Lower leaf blades lanceolate or oblanceolate to ovate, ± straight, pinnately veined, ± petiolate, toothed to entire; cypsela body obovoid to obconic; involucre stipitate-glandular

c15.text: Pappus monomorphic, similar on both ray and disk flowers; cypselas monomorphic, all compressed; rays 8–11 ×2–3 mm; stems sericeous to sericeo-tomentose

Pappus dimorphic—absent on ray flowers and present on disk flowers; cypselas dimorphic, those of the ray flowers triangular in cross-section, those of the disk flowers compressed; rays 3–7 (–9) ×1–2 mm; stems hirsute to pilose (in part)

c1.text: Receptacle naked
Receptacle bristly or chaffy, at least toward the margin of the capitulum

c2.text: Capitula tiny, sessile and aggregated in head-like glomerules, each with a single ray flower; involucre up to 1 mm in diameter, with usually 2 bracts; upper leaf blades sessile and often connate at the base

Capitula larger, some or all peduncled, not aggregated in glomerules, each with (1–) 3 or more ray flowers; involucre wider than 1 mm in diameter, with 3 or more bracts; upper leaf blades sessile or petioled, but not basally connate

c3.text: Leaves opposite and with simple, entire blades
Leaves alternate or opposite, the blades toothed to lobed or divided (blades usually entire in Helenium and sometimes in Calendula ,

c4.text: Leaves opposite (at least the lower), the blades once or twice pinnately divided or -lobed; involucral bracts gland-dotted
Leaves alternate, simple or 1–3 times pinnately lobed; involucral bracts not gland-dotted (except in Helenium and Hymenoxys )

c5.text: Pappus monomorphic, composed of 10–20 scales that are cleft into 3–10 divisions or bristles at the apex; involucre biseriate—the outer series with 3–9 bracts, the inner series with 8–22 bracts
Pappus scales dimorphic, none of which are divided at the apex into bristles; involucre either uniseriate or biseriate and then with only 2 outer bracts

c6.text: Capitula with 5–8 ray flowers; inner series of 8 distinct involucral bracts; pappus scales apically cleft into 5–10 bristles (in part)
Capitula with 10–21 ray flowers; inner series of 12–22 involucral bracts that are connate 80% or more of their length; pappus scales apically cleft into 3–5 divisions (in part)

c7.text: Capitula with (1–) 3–8 (up to 100+ in cultivars) ray flowers, the ray 1–18 (–25) mm long; pappus of 3–7 scales—1 or 2 longer scales and 2–5 shorter scales; involucre uniseriate, bracts largely connate
Capitula with (0–) 1 ray flower, the ray 0.8–1.2 mm long; pappus of 8 scales that usually are alternately unequal; involucre biseriate, the bracts distinct

c8.text: Pappus a tiny crown or completely absent
Pappus composed of distinct awns or scales

c9.text: Cypsela bodies tuberculate-rugose on the outer surface (i.e., the surface facing the margin of the capitulum); disk flowers functionally staminate with an abortive ovary, not producing fruit; capitula 4–7 (–10) cm wide in life

Cypsela bodies not tuberculate-rugose on any surface; disk flowers bisexual or unisexual (and then carpellate), producing fruit; capitula up to 4 (–5) cm wide in life (2.5–20 cm in diameter in Chrysanthemum )

c10.text: Capitulescence consisting of (10–) 20–70 (–100) capitula in a compact, corymb-like array (in part)
Capitulescence consisting of 1–3 capitula

c11.text: Herbage glabrous or nearly so; cypselas dimorphic—those of the ray flowers 3-angled with 2 or 3 wing-margins, those of the disk flowers ± cylindrical; plants annual
Herbage gray-pubescent (sometime glabrate in late season); cypselas monomorphic, angled or ribbed, but without wing-angles; plants perennial

c12.text: Rays longer than 10 mm; leaf blades prominently toothed to lobed; introduced plants of settled areas (in part)
Rays up to 4 mm long; leaf blades 2- to 3-times pinnately compound; native plants of northern, ice-scoured river shores (in part)

c13.text: Inner series of involucral bracts connate 80% or more of their length; pappus of apically cleft scales (in part)
Involucral bracts distinct or connate only at base; pappus of awns or simple scales

c14.text: Involucral bracts resinous; pappus composed of 2–8 firm, but deciduous, awns; capitula with 25–40 rays (in part)
Involucral bracts resin-dotted; pappus composed of 5–10 lanceolate to ovate or obovate, awn-tipped scales; capitula with 5–21 rays

c15.text: Involucral bracts reflexed in fruit; mature receptacles ± globose [Fig. ]; stems winged by decurrent leaf bases (not so in H. amarum ); leaf blades simple (rarely pinnately lobed in H. amarum )
Involucral bracts spreading to erect in fruit; mature receptacles hemispherical; stems unwinged; larger leaf blades usually pinnately lobed into very narrow segments

c16.text: Leaves regularly alternate throughout the stem
Leaves opposite or whorled, except sometimes the upper, which are alternate [Fig. ]

c17.text: Receptacle with spine-like setae; lobes of disk corollas villous-tomentose; pappus composed of 6–10 conspicuously awned scales (in part)
Receptacle chaffy with flattened scales; lobes of disk corollas not villous-tomentose; pappus various but not composed of awned scales

c18.text: Involucral bracts in 1 series, laterally compressed and enfolding a ray cypsela; receptacle chaffy only near the margin; plants aromatic, with stipitate glands (at least in the capitulescence) (in part)
Involucral bracts in 1 or more series, flat, not enfolding a ray cypsela; receptacle chaffy throughout; plants aromatic or not, but lacking abundant stipitate glands

c19.text: Capitula with 20–40 ray flowers; involucral bracts dry and scarious-margined
Capitula with 2–21 ray flowers [Fig. ]; involucral bracts herbaceous or foliaceous, commonly without scarious margins

c20.text: Receptacle convex to low-conic; cypsela body with evident lateral wings (very rarely the wings lacking); leaves either auriculate-dilated at base or decurrent on the stem as conspicuous wings
Receptacle conic to columnar [Fig. ]; cypsela body lacking wings or with narrow wing margins; leaves neither abruptly and conspicuously broadened at base nor decurrent as prominent wings

c21.text: Ray flowers subtended by chaffy scales; chaff velutinous at tip; cypsela body compressed
Ray flowers not subtended by chaff; chaff not velutinous at tip; cypsela body ± quadrangular

c22.text: Inner involucral bracts 5- to 7-ribbed, each rib bearing 1 or 2 rows of hooked prickles 1–2 mm long, maturing into a bur in fruit; annuals with prostrate stems commonly rooting from the lower nodes
None of the involucral bracts bearing prickles or maturing as a bur; annual or perennial plants, mostly with ascending stems (except the aquatic Bidens beckii )

c23.text: Leaves, at least the upper, connate-perfoliate; stem square; disk flowers unisexual and staminate, with an undivided style and abortive ovary
Leaves not connate-perfoliate; stem terete or angled; disk flowers bisexual, the style divided and the ovary fertile

c24.text: Plants aquatic, with flaccid stems; leaves (except for the emersed ones) whorled, finely dissected into narrow, flaccid segments; capitulescence commonly a solitary capitulum [Fig. ]; cypselas terete (in part)

Plants terrestrial or of wetlands, with erect stems; leaves opposite, entire or divided into broad, firmer segments; capitulescence commonly composed of 2 or more capitula; cypselas compressed, quadrangular, or ± triangular

c25.text: Involucral bracts conspicuously stipitate glandular, biseriate, dimorphic—the outer longer and spreading, the inner shorter and erect; leaf blades resin-dotted abaxially (in part)

Involucral bracts not stipitate-glandular (though with sessile glands or rarely with glands on short stipes near the margins in Deinandra ), arranged in 1 or more series, when biseriate the outer involucral bracts not both longer than the inner and spreading (except in some Bidens ); leaf blades not resin-dotted abaxially (except in Deinandra and Heliomeris and some Helianthus )

c26.text: Disk corollas densely tomentose basally; involucral bracts uniseriate
Disk corollas glabrous basally; involcural bracts in 2 or more series (in 1 series in Deinandra , but that genus with only 6 disk flowers, rather than 100+ in Guizotia )

c27.text: Chaff in a single series between the ray and disk flowers; pappus composed of 5–12 lanceolate to oblong or linear scales 1–1.5 mm long
Chaff not restricted to a single series ; pappus absent, of 2–4 tooth-like scales, or of 2–4 (–5) awns that are commonly minutely barbellate; involucre with 2 or more series of bracts

c28.text: Ray flowers carpellate and fertile, becoming chartaceous in fruit and persistent on the triangular cypsela [Fig. ]
Ray flowers neutral and lacking carpels (with carpels in Heterosperma , but that genus with pinnately lobed leaves), deciduous at or before maturity of the compressed or quadrangular cypsela

c29.text: Involcural bracts biseriate or triseriate, ± monomorphic [Fig. ]; chaff of the receptacle partially enfolding the disk flowers; cypsela bodies compressed at right angles to the involucral bracts
Involucral bracts biseriate, dimorphic [Fig. ]; chaff flat or nearly so, not or only slightly enfolding the disk flowers; cypsela bodies compressed parallel to the involucral bracts

c30.text: Pappus present, of 2 narrow scales (1–) 1.2–5 mm long positioned at the principal angles and 0–4 shorter scales (note: the scales are readily deciduous); cypsela body glabrous or pubescent; leaf blades 1.2–40 cm wide, at least the larger serrate or serrulate to subentire (rarely entire) and usually 3-nerved (1-nerved in H. maximiliani )
Pappus absent; cypsela body glabrous; leaf blades 0.2–2 cm wide, entire, 1 (–3)-nerved

c31.text: Cypsela body tapering to a slender, apical beak; leaf blades pinnately lobed or dissected into linear or linear-filiform segments up to 1.5 (–3) mm wide (lanceolate an up to 5 mm wide in the rare introduction Cosmos sulphureus ); capitula usually with 3–20 disk flowers

Cypsela body not terminated by a beak; leaf blades simple, lobed, or divided into linear to ovate segments mostly wider than 1.5 mm (narrower in a few Coreopsis ); capitula with (7–) 12–150+ disk flowers

c32.text: Ray flowers 1–3, with rays usually 1–2 mm long; disk flowers 3–10; leaf blades 1–4 cm long
Ray flowers usually 8, with rays 15–50 mm long; disk flowers 10–20; leaf blades 5–12 (–25) cm long (in part)

c33.text: Pappus of 2–6 awns, these usually retrorsely barbellate (rarely antrorsely barbellate or smooth or absent) [Figs. , , ]; outer involucral bracts foliaceous in most species (in part)
Pappus of 2 short, tooth-like scales or none; cypsela wing-margined; outer involucral bracts ± herbaceous (in part)

c1.text: Bracts near the middle of the inflorescence scarcely differentiated from the upper foliage leaves (i.e., the flowers occurring in the axils of leaves) [Fig. ]; principal leaf blades sessile or borne on short petioles up to 4 mm long

Bracts near the middle of the inflorescence conspicuously reduced in size compared with the upper foliage leaves (i.e., the flowers in leafy-bracteate racemes); principal leaf blades on petioles 5–25 (–33) mm long

c2.text: Corolla 12–20 mm long; leaf blades 20–60 mm long, lanceolate to ovate-oblong, commonly 2–4 times as long as wide
Corolla 7–9 mm long; leaf blades 10–16 mm long, narrow-ovate or triangular to suborbicular, usually less than 2 times as long as wide

c3.text: Racemes not secund; median leaf blades lanceolate or oblanceolate, 4–15 mm wide, entire or low-crenate
Racemes secund; median leaf blades narrow-ovate to ovate, 15–50 (–80) mm wide, dentate or serrate

c4.text: Corolla 5–8 mm long, ± straight and not curved upward out of the calyx
Corolla 12–16 (–18) mm long, evidently curved upward out of the calyx

c1.text: Leaf blades once or twice pinnately lobed into ± oblong segments; pedicels 4–8 mm long; calyx conspicuously saccate at the base; plants annual, 10–30 cm tall
Leaf blades merely toothed; pedicels 1–3 mm long; calyx scarcely saccate at the base; plants rhizomatous perennials, (15–) 30–100 cm tall

c2.text: Corolla green-yellow, 9–10 mm long; verticillasters with 1 or 2 flowers, collectively forming what appears to be a lax, secund raceme; leaf blades truncate to cordate at the base
Corolla pink-purple, 11–18 mm long; verticillasters with 3 or more flowers, collectively forming a more crowded, terete raceme; leaf blades cuneate to rounded at the base

c1.text: Plants upright, not forming mats; upper lip of the corolla entire; stems usually evenly pubescent on each face (varying to subglabrous); flowers in verticillasters of 6 or more at each node

Flowers with 4 sepals in unequal groups of 2 and 4 petals [Fig. ]; styles 2; low, compact, mat- or mound-forming shrubs up to 3 dm tall
Flowers with 5 sepals and 5 petals [Figs. , , ]; styles 3 or 5 (rarely 4); shrubs 5–30 dm tall or herbs

c2.text: Plants woody; capsules 3-locular (rarely 4-locular)
Plants herbaceous; capsules 1-, 3-, or 5-locular (rarely 4-locular)

c3.text: Inflorescence of solitary, terminal flowers (rarely as many as 3 flowers together); longer sepals 10–15 mm long; petals 10–20 mm long; placentae of fruit not meeting in the center
Inflorescence a terminal cyme of (1–) 3 or more flowers (and sometimes also of axillary cymules); longer sepals 2–7 mm long; petals 4.5–10 mm long; placentae of fruit meeting in center

c4.text: Terminal cyme with (1–) 3–7 flowers; leaf blades (4–) 7–15 mm wide; capsules 7–14 (–15) ×3–5 mm; seeds 1.5–2 mm long
Terminal cyme with 7 or more flowers; leaf blades 3–7 (–11) mm wide; capsules 4.5–6 ×1.5–3 mm; seeds 0.8–1.3 mm long

c5.text: Flowers with 5 styles; capsules 5-locular, 15–30 mm tall; petals 25–30 mm long
Flowers with 3 (–4) styles; capsules 1- or 3-locular (rarely 4-locular), 2–7 mm tall; petals 2–12 mm long

c6.text: Styles connate or closely connivent, persistent in fruit and appearing as a single, straight beak at the summit of the capsule [Fig. ]; stigmas minute
Styles distinct nearly to the base and often divergent, deciduous in fruit and not appearing as a single beak at the summit of the capsule; stigmas capitate

c7.text: Sepals distinctly unequal, 5–13 (–15) ×2–3 (–8) mm; petals 10–13 mm long, strongly asymmetrical, relatively straight on one margin and srongly convex on the other margin; stamens numbering 120–200, deciduous; seeds 1.5–1.8 mm long; stems branched near or base or throughout and usually clustered together

Sepals subequal to somewhat unequal, (2–) 4–7 ×1–3 mm; petals 5–8 mm long, ± symmetrical to weakly asymmetrical; stamens numbering 60–95, persistent; seeds 0.7–0.8 mm long; stems commonly unbranched until inflorescence and occurring singly

c8.text: Leaf blades with flat margins, elliptic to elliptic-oblong, 1–3 (–4) cm long, 2–3 times as long as wide; sepals oblanceolate to narrow-obovate, widest above the middle
Leaf blades with revolute margins, narrow-lanceolate to narrow-oblong or narrow-elliptic, 3–6 cm long, 4–6 times as long as wide; sepals lanceolate to ovate, widest near or below the middle

c9.text: Ovary and capsule 3-locular (rarely 4-locular); flowers with 20–40(–70) stamens
Ovary and capsule unilocular; flowers with 5–22 stamens

c10.text: Petals conspicuously dotted and streaked with black; sepals with few or no black glands, obtuse to broad-acute at the apex; seeds 0.5–0.7(–1.1) mm long; branches terete, without decurrent ridges; capsules 2.5–6 mm tall, with black glands arranged in longitudinal streaks or broader shapes only

Petals dotted only at margins; sepals copiously dotted and lined with black glands, acuminate at the apex; seeds (0.9–)1–1.2(–1.3) mm long; branches with sharp, decurrent ridges below the leaves; capsules 6–10 mm tall, with black glands arranged both in both longitudinal and oblique streaks

c11.text: Leaf blades subulate to linear-subulate, 1-nerved, appressed, 1–4 mm long; inflorescence frequently monochasial (i.e., with alternate branches)
Leaf blades linear to elliptic, 1- to 7-nerved, spreading to ascending, 3–45 mm long; inflorescence clearly dichasial (i.e., with opposite branches)

c12.text: Capsules ellipsoid, abruptly tapered and rounded at the summit [Fig. ]; sepals linear to linear-lanceolate, broadest at or near the middle; stems decumbent and leafy-bracted at the base

Capsules ellipsoid-conic to conic, gradually tapered and pointed at the summit [Fig. ]; sepals lanceolate, broadest below the middle; stems erect, not leafy-bracted at the base (though with leafy stolons)

c13.text: Bracts of the cyme subulate, not resembling the leaves; sepals acute at the apex, subequal in length to the capsule
Bracts of the cyme elliptic, leaf-like [Fig. ]; sepals obtuse at the apex, conspicuously shorter than the capsule [Fig. ]

c14.text: Leaf blades linear to narrow-oblanceolate, 1–4 (–6) mm wide, 1- or 3-nerved (rarely 5-nerved), narrowly tapering to the base [Fig. ]; petals 2.5–3 mm long
Leaf blades lanceolate to narrow-elliptic or narrow-oblong, 3–9 (–15) mm wide, 5- or 7-nerved, broadly tapering to rounded at the base; petals 3.5–4 mm long

c1.text: This genus contains exactly one species.
This genus contains exactly one species.
Plants pubescent with simple, glandular hairs; filaments pubescent with purple, knob-tipped hairs; capsule subglobose, pubescent with minute hairs or glabrous

Plants pubescent with compound, eglandular hairs; some of the filaments pubescent, usually the 3 upper (i.e., shorter) ones pubescent with white to yellow hairs and the 2 lower (i.e., longer) ones glabrous or nearly so (pubescent with purple hairs in V. nigrum ); capsules ellipsoid to ovoid, densely pubescent

c2.text: Filaments pubescent with purple hairs; bracts 2–5 mm long; basal leaf blades cordate at base
At least the upper 3 filaments pubescent with white to yellow hairs; bracts 8–40 mm long; basal leaf blades cuneate to rounded at the base

c3.text: Axis of inflorescence branched; calyx (1.5–) 2.5–4 mm long; anther reniform, not decurrent
Axis of inflorescence unbranched (though a given plant may have more than 1 inflorescences); calyx 5–12 mm long; anther decurrent on the filament

c4.text: Stigma capitate; inflorescence crowded at maturity, the flowers concealing the axis of the spike; corolla 10–25 (–35) mm wide
Stigma spatulate, decurrent on the sides of the style; inflorescence less dense at maturity, the flowers spaced enough to expose the axis of the spike [Fig. ]; corolla (20–) 25–45 (–55) mm wide

c5.text: Leaves decurrent on the stem nearly or completely to the next leaf; floral bracts 15–40 mm long
Leaves not, or only very shortly, decurrent on the stem; floral bracts 9–15 mm long

c1.text: Sterile filament yellow-green near the apex; capsules 6–10 mm long; pedicels 0.4–0.7 mm thick; leaf blades broad-cuneate to broad-rounded or truncate at the base
Sterile filament dark brown to purple-brown near the apex; capsules 4–7 mm long; pedicels 0.3–0.5 mm thick; leaf blades cordate to broad-rounded at the base

c2.text: Leaf blades acute at the apex; petiole wing-margined, less than as long as the blade; corolla 7–10 mm long
Leaf blades acuminate at the apex; petiole not or scarcely wing-margined, to as long as the blade; corolla 5–8 mm long

c1.text: This genus contains exactly one species.
This genus contains exactly one species.
Bracts of inflorescence truncate to emarginate at apex [Fig. ]; fruits separate; leaf blades with 6 or 7 pairs of veins; petioles 5–15 mm long
Bracts of inflorescence acuminate at apex; fruits fused together into a multiple; leaf blades with (3–) 4 or 5 pairs of veins; petioles 4–6 mm long

Leaves alternate, crowded at the apex of the twig [Fig. ]; petioles (8–) 20–50 mm long; endocarp pitted at apex; branchlets sometimes yellow with minute red-brown to black dots due to infection of Cryptodioporthe corni
Leaves opposite, ± evenly spaced along the twig; petioles 3–15 (–25) mm long; endocarp not pitted; branchlets without above-mentioned fungal infection

c2.text: Drupes black or green at maturity; style conspicuously widened in the apical portion; infructescence with red branches and pedicels
Drupes white to blue at maturity; style of uniform diameter throughout (apically widened in S. amomum ); infructescence with yellow or gray-brown to brown branches and pedicels (red in S. racemosa )

c3.text: Pith of branchlets brown; style conspicuously widened in the apical portion [Fig. ]; sepals 1–2 mm long; drupes blue
Pith white (infrequently light brown in S. racemosa ); style of nearly uniform diameter throughout; sepals shorter than 1 mm; drupes white to blue

c4.text: Winter branchlets gray-brown; inflorescence convex or pyramidal, nearly as tall as wide or taller, with red branches and pedicels when in fruit; leaf blades with 3 or 4 (rarely 5) pairs of lateral veins

Winter branchlets not uniformly gray-brown (see descriptions in couplet 5); inflorescence flat-topped, often wider than tall, with branches yellow or gray-brown to brown; leaf blades with 5–8 pairs of lateral veins

c5.text: Branchlets red to red-purple; drupe white (rarely light blue); leaf blades lanceolate to ovate; seeds brown, with 7–9 yellow stripes; buds without scales, densely pubescent throughout with red-brown and some white hairs

Branchlets green to yellow-green, often mottled with purple or red; drupe light blue (rarely white); leaf blades ovate to suborbicular; seeds light brown, without stripes; buds covered about of their length by sparsely pubescent scales, only the tips of the densely pubescent leaf primordia visible

c1.text: Inflorescence an axillary cyme with usually 2 or 3 flowers; leaf blades broad-ovate to suborbicular, crenate, 1.2–1.7 times as long as wide; pollen white; branchlets with low but prominent and long ridges formed by lines of decurrence extending down from the leaf scars; expanding leaves weakly conduplicate, the inner leaves progressively enfolded by the outer leaves, the margins not or scarcely involute; capsules with (1–) 4–7 (–8) seeds

Inflorescence a terminal panicle with 6 or more flowers [Fig. ]; leaf blades elliptic to oblong or ovate, serrate, 1.8–2.6 times as long as wide; pollen yellow; branchlets lacking ridges formed by lines of decurrence or these obscure; expanding leaves neither conduplicate nor obviously enfolding successively inner leaves, the margins initially tightly involute; capsules with 1–4 (–8) seeds

Petioles 1–3 (–5) mm long; capsules divided to near base into 4 almost separate sections (often 1 or more of these sections abortive); branchlets with (2–) 4 conspicuous corky wings [Fig. ]; leaf blades turning bright red in autumn prior to dropping from plant

Petioles 5–20 mm long; capsules 4-lobed; branchlets without corky wings, though sometimes with low ridges on the angles (branchlets occasionally with corky wings in E. phellomanus ); leaf blades either remaining green or turning yellow-green to yellow or dull red-purple in autumn prior to dropping from plant

c2.text: Plants usually climbing by means of aerial roots (rare forms merely spreading and lacking aerial roots); leaves evergreen; branchlets subterete; capsule pink to nearly white
Plants upright shrubs; leaves deciduous; branchlets 4-angled or 4-winged; capsule purple or red to pink

c3.text: Petals brown-purple; anthers purple; cymes with usually 7–15 flowers; capsule purple; leaf blades pubescent on the abaxial surface with erect hairs up to ca. 0.2 mm long
Petals green-white; anthers yellow; cymes with usually 2–7 flowers; capsule red to pink; leaf blades glabrous or essentially so on the abaxial surface

c4.text: Seeds white with an orange aril; cyme usually with 2–5 flowers, borne on a peduncle 20–35 mm long; branchlets lacking prominent corky wings
Seeds dark brown with a red aril; cyme usually with 7 flowers, borne on a peduncle 5–10 mm long; branchlets sometimes with prominent corky wings [Fig. ]

c1.text: This genus contains exactly one species.
Leaves lacking leaflets, reduced to a tendril; corollas yellow

Leaves with 2 or more well-developed leaflets; corollas white to ochroleucous or pink-purple to purple (yellow only in L. pratensis , a species with racemes of 4–10 flowers vs. solitary or rarely paired in L. aphaca )

c2.text: Leaves with 4–16 leaflets [Fig. ]; native plants
Leaves with 2 leaflets [Fig. ]; non-native plants originating from cultivation

c3.text: Stipules ± symmetrical, with 2 basal lobes, approximately equal in size to the leaflets; leaflets fleshy; legumes mostly 8–11 mm wide
Stipules asymmetrical, with 1 basal lobe [Fig. ], definitely smaller than the leaflets; leaflets scarcely fleshy; legumes 4–7 mm wide

c4.text: Corollas pink-purple to purple; raceme with 3–6 flowers; stipules 1–10 mm long, semisagittate (i.e., with a sharply pointed basal lobe); leaflets elliptic to elliptic-oblong, 2.5–9 times as long as wide

Corollas white to ochroleucous; raceme with 5–15 flowers; stipules 15–30 mm long, some semicordate (i.e., with a rounded or bluntly pointed basal lobe); leaflets ovate to elliptic, 2–2.4 times as long as wide

c5.text: Plants annual, without rhizomes; inflorescence with 1–3 (–4) flowers
Plants perennial, with rhizomes; inflorescence with (3–) 4–10 flowers

c6.text: Leaflets linear to broad-linear; legume glabrous; flowers usually solitary, not especially fragrant
Leaflets ovate or elliptic; legume pubescent; flowers 1–3 (–4) in a raceme, very fragrant

c7.text: Corollas 14–25 mm long; legumes 40–100 ×6–10 mm; stems conspicuously winged
Corollas 10–15 mm long; legumes 20–50 ×4–7 mm; stems without prominent wing-angles

c8.text: Stipules 3–10 mm wide, lanceolate to ovate [Fig. ]; leaflets ovate to lanceolate; corollas 18–25 mm long
Stipules 1–2 (–4) mm wide, narrow-lanceolate; leaflets oblong-lanceolate to narrow-lanceolate; corollas 13–20 mm long

c9.text: Corolla yellow; stipules 10–30 mm long; calyx lobes subequal in length, slender
Corolla red-purple; stipules 5–12 mm long; calyx lobes unequal, broad and short

Ovary and legume glabrous; pedicels 5–10 (­–15) mm long; corollas 15–20 mm long; legumes 10–12 mm wide
Ovary minutely villous and legume initially villous, retaining some pubescence at least along one or both sutures; pedicels mostly 15–20 mm long; corollas 15–25 (–27) mm long; legumes 20–25 mm wide

c2.text: Leaves with 13–19 leaflets; corollas 15–20 mm long; racemes 20–50 (–70) ×6–7 cm, with flowers developing from base to apex
Leaves with 7–13 leaflets; corollas 20–25 (–27) mm long; racemes 10–20 (–30) ×7–9 cm, with flowers opening nearly simultaneously

Corolla white (rarely tinged with pink), 15–20 (–25) mm long; raceme pendulous; ovary and legume glabrous; upper margin of legume with a narrow wing; branchlets glabrous or sparsely pubescent; trees to 25 m tall

Corolla pink to red-purple, 20–25 mm long; raceme suberect to spreading, sometimes pendulous; ovary and legume hispid; upper margin of legume unwinged; branchlets glandular, the glands sessile or stipitate; shrubs to 5 m tall

c2.text: Leaves with 7–13 leaflets that become glabrate abaxially at maturity; branchlets bristly glandular [Fig. ]; bracts not aristate-tipped (note: the bracts are caducous and evident only prior to anthesis); racemes lax and relatively open, with 4–11 flowers

Leaves with 13–25 leaflets that remain permanently appressed-pubescent abaxially (sometimes inconspicuously so); branchlets glandular with sessile or subsessile glands; bracts aristate-tipped; racemes suberect, crowded, with 8–20 flowers

Corolla ochroleucous to pink or red-striate, (4–) 5–9 mm long; basal connate portion of calyx 1–2 mm long; stipules inconspicuous glands; flowers solitary, borne on axillary peduncles; plants annual
Corolla yellow, 10–14 mm long; basal connate portion of calyx 2.5–3.5 mm long; stipules foliaceous, resembling the leaflets; flowers borne in peduncled umbels; plants perennial
