Flowers solitary or in inflorescences of 2–50, in either case borne on a long peduncle 1–10.5 cm long [Fig. ]; style pubescent all around the tip or glabrous in V. hirsuta

Flowers solitary or paired (with up to 7 flowers in V. sepium ), sessile or borne on a peduncle up to 1 cm long, borne in the axils of leaves [Fig. ]; style pubescent on the abaxial (i.e., outer or lower) surface near the apex

c2.text: Corollas 2.5–7 (–8) mm long, white to light purple; flowers solitary or in racemes of 2–5 (–7); legume 6–13 mm long
Corollas (9–) 10–13 (–18) mm long, blue, white and blue, or rarely entirely white; flowers in racemes of 10–50 [Fig. ]; legume 15–40 mm long

c3.text: Legumes hirsute, with (1–) 2 (–3) seeds, obliquely tapering from the sutures and pointed at the tip; lobes of the calyx ± equal length; leaves with (8–) 10–16 leaflets
Legumes glabrous, with usually 4 seeds, equally rounded from the sutures and blunt at the tip; lobes of the calyx distinctly unequal in length; leaves with 4–10 (–12) leaflets

c4.text: Plants perennial; calyx not gibbous or saccate on the upper side, the pedicel appearing to attach to the basal part of the flower; upper calyx lobes broad-triangular; corolla 8–13(–18) mm long; limb of the banner petal ± as long as the claw

Plants annual or biennial; calyx gibbous or saccate on the upper side, the pedicel appearing to attach to the underside of the flower; upper calyx lobes lanceolate to linear-triangular; corolla 12–20 mm long; limb of the banner petal ca. half as long as the claw

c5.text: Terminal leaflet absent, not modified into a tendril; legumes 5–20 (–30) cm long; leaflets 5–10 cm long
Terminal leaflet of at least the upper leaves modified into a tendril; legume 1.5–6 cm long; leaflets 0.8–3 (–3.5) cm long

c6.text: Calyx 3.5–4.5 mm long; corollas 5–6 mm long; tendrils unbranched (sometimes absent on some leaves); legumes 15–25 (–30) ×3–4 mm
Calyx 4–13 mm long; corollas 10–30 mm long; tendrils generally branched [Fig. ]; legumes 20–45 ×3.5–11 mm

c7.text: Banner petal pubescent on abaxial (i.e., outer) surface; stipules entire
Banner petal glabrous on abaxial surface; stipules entire, lobed, or toothed

c8.text: Corollas yellow, commonly with purple streaks, drying drab light purple, 25–30 (–35) mm long; legumes pubescent
Corollas light purple to white, 10–25 (–30) mm long; legumes glabrous or pubescent

c9.text: Calyx actinomorphic or nearly so, the lower lobes scarcely longer than the upper lobes; peduncle and inflorescence axis undeveloped, the inflorescence with 1 or 2 (–3) flowers [Fig. ]; legumes sessile; plants annual

Calyx zygomorphic, the lower lobes distinctly longer than the upper lobes; inflorescence subsessile or shortly peduncled, the axis somewhat developed and up to 10 mm long, with 2–7 contiguous flowers; legumes on a stipe ca. 1.5 mm long; plants perennial from rhizomes

c1.text: Corolla 25–40 mm wide in life, with subequal petals 10–20 mm long; androecium with 10 stamens; anthers longer than 4 mm, commonly ca. 8 mm long; pedicels 8–15 mm long; petiole gland depressed to stalked, scutelliform, 0.5–1.5 mm in diameter

Corolla 8–10 mm wide in life, with very unequal petals, the longer one 6–8 mm long [Fig. ]; androecium with 5 stamens [Fig. ]; anthers shorter than 4 mm, commonly ca. 3 mm long; pedicels 1.5–4 mm long; petiole gland stalked, cupuliform, 0.4–0.8 mm in diameter

Gland located near base of petiole; leaves with 6–8 (–10) pairs of elliptic to oblanceolate leaflets 2.3–3.5 times as long as wide; inflorescence of 9- to 20-flowered axillary and terminal racemes; fruits 7–10 (–12) cm long

Gland located between or immediately below the lowest pair of leaflets; leaves with (2–) 3 pairs of obovate (rarely to elliptic) leaflets 1.3–1.8 times as long as wide; inflorescence of solitary or paired axillary flowers, these sometimes clustered near stem apex; fruits 10–20 cm long

Androecium with 5 stamens; primary leaves with 5–9 leaflets 8–25 mm long; corolla white, with the epistemonous petals (i.e., the wing and keel petals) arising from the apex of the connate stamen column

Androecium with 9 or 10 stamens; primary leaves with 15–35 leaflets (3–) 5–12 mm long; corolla white to blue or blue-purple, with the epistemonous petals arising laterally from the conate stamen column

Plants annual; legume usually curved to twisted, often forming a complete circle of less than 10 mm diameter
Plants perennial; legume straight to somewhat curved, but not twisted

c2.text: Corollas ochroleucous in life; legume bilocular, usually glabrous

Corollas white to light purple, blue-purple, or purple in life; legume unilocular (note: one of the sutures may be intruded but does not connect to form 2 separate chambers in the fruit), usually pubescent

c3.text: Pubescence of herbage basifixed; legume 30–40 mm long, trigonous in cross-section; principal leaves with 9–13 leaflets
Pubescence of herbage mesifixed; legume 10–20 mm long, terete in cross-section; principal leaves with 13–35 leaflets

c4.text: Principal leaves with 15–25 leaflets [Fig. ]; stems from a subterranean, branched caudex, mat-forming; keel petals not or only slightly shorter than the banner petal; upper suture of fruit prominently sulcate

Principal leaves with 7–15 (–17) leaflets; stems from a surficial crown of a taproot, clustered but not forming mats; keel petals markedly shorter than the banner petal; upper suture of fruit scarcely sulcate

c5.text: Legume (5–) 8–11 (–13) mm long, ± sessile; flowers 6–9 mm long
Legume 13–25 mm long, on a stipe 2–5 mm long; flowers (7–) 10–12 mm long

c1.text: This genus contains exactly one species.
This genus contains exactly one species.
This genus contains exactly one species.
Leaves with 5–7 (–11) leaflets 2–5 (–6) cm long; racemes usually 10–20 cm tall; corollas 12–16 mm long
Leaves with (8–) 11–17 leaflets 7.5–13 cm long; racemes usually 20–40 cm tall; corollas 15–20 mm long
Corollas yellow, 2–3 mm long; inflorescence compact at anthesis, only 1–2 (–3) cm long, elongating in fruit; pedicels ascending, 0.5–1 mm long; legumes 1.5–3 mm long; plants 0.2–0.6 m tall
Corollas yellow or white, (3.5–) 4–7 mm long; inflorescence 3–12 cm long at anthesis, elongating in fruit; pedicels decurved, 1–2 mm long; legumes 2.5–5 mm long; plants 0.5–3 m tall

c2.text: Corollas yellow, 5–7 mm long; wing petals ± as long as the banner petal and usually longer than the keel petals; legumes cross-striate on the outer surface
Corollas white, (3.5–) 4–5 mm long; wing petals shorter than the banner petal and ± as long as the keel petals [Fig. ]; legumes reticulate-patterened on the outer surface

c1.text: Flowers yellow, turning brown after anthesis
Flowers white to pink to purple

c2.text: Central leaflet sessile or on a petiolule of ± similar length as the lateral leaflets; corollas 5–7 mm long; inflorescence 10–17 (–20) mm tall; stipules ± as long as the petioles; style 1–2 mm long

Central leaflet borne on a petiolule conspicuously longer than those of the lateral leaflets [Fig. ]; corollas 3.5–5 (–6) mm long; inflorescence 5–15 mm tall; stipules shorter than the petioles; style less than 1 mm long

c3.text: Petiolule of the central leaflet up to 1 mm long; inflorescence with usually 5–15 flowers; corollas 3–3.5(–4) mm long; banner petal inconspicuously veined
Petiolule of the central leaflet 1–3 mm long; inflorescence with usually 20–30 flowers; corollas (3.5–) 4–5 (–6) mm long; banner petal with 10 conspicuous veins

c4.text: Flowers pedicellate, the pedicels usually longer than 2 mm; petals white or white and pink
Flowers sessile or subsessile, the pedicels (when present) up to 0.5 mm long; petals white to pink to purple

c5.text: Stems creeping along the ground, rooting at the nodes; petals usually concolored; stipules connate to the petiole in the basal portion, then with fused margins for a distance, forming a tube that surrounds the stem
Stems ascending, not rooting at the nodes; petals bicolored; stipules connate to the petiole in the basal portion, then distinct, the tips completely separate and not forming a tube

c6.text: Basal connate portion of calyx more densely pubescent on the upper side, becoming obliquely inflated in fruit, the upper side gibbous; flowers each subtended by a bracteole, resupinate (i.e., twisted within the calyx such that the banner petal is in a lateral or lower position; not resupinate in T. fragiferum ) [Fig. ]

Basal connate portion of calyx uniformly glabrate or pubescent, not becoming obliquely inflated in fruit; flowers lacking bracteoles (with bracteoles in T. glomeratum ), not resupinate (i.e., the banner petal uppermost)

c7.text: Flowers not resupinate; peduncles (20–) 40–80 (–200) mm long; plants perennial, usually stoloniferous
Flowers resupinate; peduncles up to 50 mm long; plants annual, not stoloniferous

c8.text: Inflorescence mostly 10–20 mm in diameter, lobulate in fruit, borne on elongate peduncles 20–50 mm long; stems 10–40 (–60) cm tall
Inflorescence mostly 5–10 mm in diameter, hemispheroid to spherical in fruit, subsessile or borne on a peduncle shorter than 20 mm; stems 5–15 cm tall

c9.text: Outer 2–4 (–6) flowers of each inflorescence bearing petals and fertile, the remaining flowers on the interior apetalous and sterile; inner flowers eventually elongating and producing a mass of woody, plumose stalks that surround the fruiting calyces and form a compact bur that is pushed against the soil surface or below it by downward growth of the peduncle; stems prostrate, stolon-like

All the flowers of each inflorescence bearing petals and fertile; fruiting inflorescence not resembling a compact bur and not pushed against soil surface or below it; stems ascending to erect (sometimes procumbent in T. echinatum and T. glomeratum )

c10.text: Corollas 3–4 mm long, definitely shorter than the calyx; leaflets narrow-oblanceolate to oblanceolate or narrow-oblong, 3–5.5 times as long as wide [Fig. ]

Corollas 4–16 mm long, ± as long as or longer than the calyx; leaflets of lower leaves obovate or obcordate to elliptic, 0.8–3 times as long as wide (sometimes oblanceolate and up to 4 times as long as wide in T. dichotomum )

c11.text: Corollas 4–6 mm long, ± as long as or shortly exceeding the calyx; inflorescences sessile or subsessile
Corollas (6–) 8–25 mm long, definitely longer than the calyx; inflorescences sessile or pedunculate

c12.text: Flowers subtended by bracteoles; basal connate portion of the calyx glabrous
Flowers without bracteoles; basal, connate portion of the calx pubescent

c13.text: Inflorescence sessile or on peduncles to 20 (–30) mm long, subtended either by a pair of opposite leaves or their expanded stipules or by an involucre (i.e., a ring of fused bracts); plants perennial (annual in T. dalmaticum )
Inflorescence borne on peduncles 10–70 mm long, not subtended by a pair of opposite leaves or an involucre (i.e., all the leaves alternate; except T. echinatum ); plants annual

c14.text: Inflorescence subtended by an involucre; corolla 8–10 mm long, pink; plants annual
Inflorescence subtended by a pair of opposite leaves or their expanded stipules [Fig. ]; corolla 12–20 mm long, red-purple to purple-red (very rarely cream-white in T. pratense ); plants perennial

c15.text: Distinct portion of the stipule broad-triangular, shorter than the connate portion; leaflets ovate or obovate to elliptic, 1.2–2.5 times as long as wide, frequently with light mottles on the adaxial surface

Corollas 5–12 mm long; leaflets oblanceolate or elliptic to obovate or obcordate, 8–30 ×3–12 mm

c17.text: Peduncles subtended by a pair of opposite leaves; calyx lobes stiff and spinose, especially in fruit

c1.text: Inflorescence with 1 or 2 (–3) flowers; legume (30–) 40–100 mm long, unarmed, merely curved
Inflorescence with (1–) 2–50 flowers; legume 1–10 mm long, armed with thin prickles or unarmed, curved to coiled up to 7 times (rarely straight in M. falcata and M. lupulina )

c2.text: Corollas 6–12 mm long, blue-purple to purple or rarely yellow; legumes unarmed; plants perennial
Corollas 2–5 (–7) mm long, yellow; legumes armed with thin prickles (always unarmed in M. lupulina , rarely unarmed in M. rigidula ) [Fig. ];

c3.text: Corollas blue-purple to purple, usually 8–11 mm long; legumes coiled (1–) 2–3 times; stems erect to ascending
Corollas yellow, usually 5–8 mm long; legumes falcate-curved (rarely straight or partly coiled); stems prostrate to erect

c4.text: Legume reniform-curved or slightly spiraled near the apex, without prickles [Fig. ], with a single seed; inflorescence with (10–) 14–24 (–50) flowers
Legume 2- to 7-times spiral-coiled, with thin prickles (prickles rarely lacking in M. rigidula ), with several seeds; inflorescence with (1–) 2–5 (–8) flowers

c5.text: Legume in a very tight spiral, extremely hard-walled, usually glandular-puberulent, the young legume concealed within the calyx when the petals drop; prickles of legume (when present) stocky, firm, ± round at the base

Legume in a somewhat tight spiral, soft-walled, glabrous or pubescent with eglandular hairs (sometimes glandular in M. minima , but that species with small fruits 3–5 mm in diameter), the young legume projecting sideways from the calyx when the petals drop; prickles of legume relatively thin, flexible, with 2 roots, 1 root arising in the dorsal surture, the other root arising in the submarginal vein

c6.text: Faces of the fruit coils lacking a reticulum of veins over much of the surface; prickles of legume tending to slant toward the base of the fruit

c7.text: Leaflets broad-obovate to broad-obcordate, 0.7–1.1 times as long as wide, usually with a dark blotch or mottles on the adaxial surface; prickles on legume usually curved and somewhat conforming to the outline of the fruit [Fig. ]
Leaflets elliptic to obovate or obcordate, 1–2 (–2.5) times as long as wide, without dark mottles; prickles on legume relatively straight (except near apex of fruit), diverging from outline of fruit

c8.text: Stipules entire or slightly dentate; legumes sparsely pubescent; stems moderately to densely villous
Stipules lacerate; legumes usually glabrous; stems glabrous or sparsely pubescent

c9.text: Corolla 2–3 (–4) mm long; coils of fruit loosely appressed to each other (i.e., spaces evident between the coils when the fruit is viewed on edge); margin of fruit coils very broad
Corolla (3–) 4–8 mm long; coils of fruit moderately to tightly appressed to each other; margin of fruit coils narrow

c3.text: Corolla 8–11 mm long; calyx lobes acute, shorter than or equal to the length of the basal, connate portion of the calyx; leaflets oval, 1.5–2 times as long as wide; stems solitary or few together from the summit of the root crown, the young stems brown; seeds mottled purple or green

Corollas white or ochroleucous, sometimes with a purple spot on the banner petal; legume not or only slightly exceeding the persistent calyx [Fig. ]

Plants erect to ascending

Leaflets elliptic-oblong to broad-elliptic or obovate, 1–3 (–3.5) times as long as wide

Leaflets strigose to pilose on the adaxial surface; upper 2 calyx lobes distinct or shortly connate above the basal, tubular portion of the calyx; stems usually pilose

Leaflets narrow-oblong to oblong or elliptic, 2.5–8 times as long as wide; middle stem leaves borne on petioles 1–3 (–6) mm long

c12.text: Racemes included in or scarcely exceeding the subtending leaves, with subglobose to short-ovoid clusters of flowers; calyx 8–12 mm long; corolla 8–12 mm long; leaflets elliptic to oblong (rarely narrow-oblong), (2–) 2.5–5 (–8) times as long as wide

Stems erect or ascending; inflorescences terminal or both terminal and axillary; terminal leaflet 1–10 times as long as wide

c2.text: Terminal leaflets (3–) 4–10 times as long as wide, mostly 5–15 mm wide, narrow-lanceolate to oblong or narrow-elliptic [Fig. ]
Terminal leaflets 1.5–4 (–5) times as long as wide, mostly 15–30 mm wide, oblong to broad-ovate

Schizocarp with 1–3 segments that are ± semicircular and gradually rounded on the lower margin; petioles mostly 1–3 (–4) mm long; leaflets subcoriaceous, conspicuously reticulate-veined

Leaf blades abaxially glabrous or pubescent with hairs that are not hooked near the tip

c6.text: Schizocarp segments ± triangular, abruptly curved on the lower margin [Fig. ]
Schizocarp segments ± semicircular, gradually rounded on the lower margin [Fig. ]

Stem pubescent with uncinate hairs (pilose hairs sometimes present at the nodes) [Fig. ]; petiole glabrous or pubescent with uncinate hairs

Corolla 4–5 mm long; calyx 1.5–3 mm long; stipe of fruit 1–3 mm long; schizocarp with (1–) 2 or 3 segments, each segment 3.5–5 mm long

Corolla 10–15 mm long, pink-purple to nearly white; inflorescence often not exceeding the subtending leaves; plants upright or twining

c1.text: Tendrils and/or panicles produced from 3–7 successive nodes; berries 10–20 (–25) mm thick; abaxial surface of leaf blades persistently pubescent with red-brown (later turning gray), tomentose hairs, the surface of the leaf blade largely or completely hidden by the hairs; axis of the inflorescence tomentose

Abaxial surface of leaf blades green, the pubescence, if present, primarily restricted to the veins or occurring in patches; nodes of branchlets not glaucous

Branchlets red to purple throughout, maturing red-brown to dark red-brown; leaf blades acuminate to long-acuminate at the apex; seeds 4–7 mm long

Leaves compound, usually with 5 leaflets; plants native, normally growing on the ground or on other plants

Plants with evident, leafy stems, the peduncles arising from well above the surface of the ground

Plants herbaceous, up to 2 m tall, unarmed or armed with slender bristles near the base of the plant; styles connate about half their length

Leafules (or leafulets on tripinnately compound leaves) pubescent abaxially, with veins essentially running into the marginal teeth, subsessile; branchlets light gray

Inflorescence composed of numerous umbels in a cluster resembling a panicle; stems unarmed; plants of rich, mesic soils; ultimate leaf segments cordate at the base

Umbel with 2–6 pubescent primary branches; beak of schizocarp prominent, narrower than and mostly 25–33% as long as the body; bracteoles linear; plants annual; ultimate segments of leaf blades mostly 5–10 mm long

Umbel with (4–) 6–15 glabrous primary branches; beak of schizocarp short, nearly as thick as and mostly 16–25% as long as the body [Fig. ]; bracteoles narrow-ovate; plants biennial or perennial; ultimate segments of leaf blades mostly 15–50 mm long

Carpellate inflorescence with 2–5 flowers; leaf scar lacking a pubescent band along the upper margin; branchlets with light brown pith; drupes solitary or paired, globose to subglobse; leaflets usually somewhat glossy and ± glabrous when mature

Carpellate inflorescence with 5–20 flowers; leaf scar with a transverse, pubescent band along the upper margin; branchlets with light or dark brown pith; drupes in racemes of (2–) 3–7 or more, ovoid to ovoid-obloid (sometimes subglobose in J. ailantifolia ) [Fig. ]; leaflets usually dull and at least sparingly pubescent adaxially

c2.text: Branchlets with dark brown pith, with relatively thick diaphragms that are nearly as broad as the chambers they alternate with; upper margin of leaf scar straight or scarcely notched; staminate aments 5–8 cm long; exterior of endocarp (i.e., shell) strongly 6- to 8-ridged and with irregular, ± sharp crests and projections

Branchlets with light brown pith, with thin diaphragms that are much narrower than the chambers they alternate with; upper margin of leaf scar with a conspicuous notch; staminate aments 15–30 cm long; exterior of endocarp rugose

c1.text: Terminal bud yellow or orange-yellow to yellow-brown, with 4–6 valvate scales; leaves with (5–) 7–9 (–13) leaflets; exocarp (i.e., husk) 2–3 mm thick, the sutures narrowly winged; staminate aments borne, in part, on reduced, ± leafless shoots that originate on the branches of the previous season

Terminal bud light brown to red-brown or dark brown, with 6–15 imbricate scales; leaves with 3–9 (–11) leaflets; exocarp 3–15 mm thick (as thin as 2 mm in C. glabra ), the sutures usually unwinged; staminate aments borne only at base of leafy shoots on branchlets of the current season

c2.text: Leaflets strongly ciliate with tufts of hairs borne below the apex of the marginal teeth [Fig. ]; leaves with (3–) 5 (–7) leaflets; pedicels and bracts of the staminate flowers glabrous

Leaflets at maturity becoming eciliate or retaining some cilia, but without subapical tufts of hairs on the marginal teeth; leaves with (3–) 5–9 (–11) leaflets; pedicels and/or bracts of staminate flowers pubescent

c3.text: Leaflets abaxially glabrous to pubescent with mostly simple hairs, some compound hairs with 2–4 rays also present; terminal bud 5–15 mm long, the bud scales abaxially glabrous to hirsute; branchlets relatively slender, (1.8–) 2–4.1 (–4.4) mm thick, glabrous or nearly so; exocarp 2–5 mm thick

Leaflets abaxially pubescent with simple hairs and abundant compound hairs with 2–8 (–17) rays; terminal bud 8–20 mm long, the bud scales abaxially tomentose; branchlets stout, (3.5–) 4–9 mm thick, hirsute (sometimes becoming subglabrous in C. laciniosa ); exocarp 4–13 mm thick

c4.text: Petiole and rachis densely hirsute; leaflets usually acute at the apex, pubescent predominately with compound hairs, the simple hairs scarce; branchlets red-brown; bark ridged, not exfoliating; exocarps rough but glabrous

Petiole and rachis sparely pubescent to subglabrous; leaflets usually acuminate at apex, pubescent with both simple and compound hairs; branchlets light orange-brown to light yellow-brown; bark separating into long strips or broad plates; exocarps minutely hirsute

c1.text: This genus contains exactly one species.
Principal leaves simple; plants unarmed
Principal leaves compound; plants usually armed with prickles or stiff bristles (always unarmed in R. pubescens and sometimes unarmed in R. canadensis )

c2.text: Leaf blades (6–) 10–20 cm wide; sepals conspicuously stipitate-glandular; petals 15–30 mm long; stems 10–20 dm tall, woody
Leaf blades 3–9 cm wide; sepals without glands; petals 4–18 mm long, or absent; stems up to 3 dm tall, herbaceous

c3.text: Petals pink-purple (rarely white); sepals provided with elongate, purple, stipitate-glands; aggregate rather dry, scarcely juicy
Petals white (rarely pink); sepals provided with short, yellow-orange, stipitate glands; aggregate juicy

c4.text: Carpels maturing as dry, achene-like drupes; petals 4–8 mm long or absent; leaf blades unlobed, the margin crenate
Carpels maturing as white-yellow, fleshy drupes; petals 10–18 mm long; leaf blades with 5–7 lobes as well as toothed on the margin

c5.text: Stems herbaceous, not clearly differentiated into primocanes and floricanes, unarmed; stipules oblanceolate to obovate; fruit separating from the receptacle only with difficulty

Stems woody, clearly differentiated into primocanes and floricanes (except R. illecebrosus with annual, above-ground stems), usually armed with bristles or prickles; stipules linear or setaceous; fruit separating from the receptacle or not

c6.text: Leaves with 3–9 pinnately arranged leaflets (sometimes palmately arranged in R. occidentalis ); fruit red or black, separating from the dry receptacle, the receptacle remaining behind on the pedicel (separating from the pedicel with the fleshy receptacle in R. illecebrosus )
Leaves with 3 pinnately arranged or 5 palmately arranged leaflets; fruit black at maturity, separating from the pedicel with the fleshy receptacle

c7.text: Petals large, surpassing the sepals; floricane leaves with 5–9 leaflets; leaflets glabrous on the abaxial surface; fruit red, not separating from the receptacle

Petals smaller, equaled or surpassed by the sepals; floricane leaves with 3 leaflets; leaflets densely tomentose with white-gray to gray hairs on the abaxial surface; fruit red or black, separating from the receptacle

c8.text: Fruit purple-black (rarely yellow), the individual drupes separated by bands of tomentum; pedicels with only moderately stout, often curved, prickles [Fig. ]; primocanes very glaucous

Fruit red to orange (rarely yellow), the individual drupes not separated by bands of tomentose pubescence; pedicels with straight bristles or minute prickles and often also glandular hairs; primocanes not, or only slightly, glaucous

c9.text: Rachis of inflorescence, pedicels, and often also the primocanes with stipitate glands or glandular bristles
Rachis of inflorescence, pedicels, and primocanes eglandular

c10.text: Petals white or pink, erect and incurved, appressed to the stamens; pedicels and calyx densely beset with elongate, red to purple, gland-tipped bristles 3–5 mm long [Fig. ]; primocanes arching to doming, sometimes rooting at the tip

Petals white, ascending to erect, but not appressed to the stamens; pedicels and calyx with minute, stipitate glands, these often exceeded by eglandular bristles; primocanes erect to arching, not rooting at the tip (in part)

c11.text: Petals white, ascending to erect, but not appressed to the stamens; terminal leaflet acute to acuminate at the apex; endocarps shallowly pitted (in part)
Petals pink to purple-red, erect and incurved, appressed to the stamens; terminal leaflet obtuse to broad-acute at the apex; endocarps shallowly rugose

c12.text: Inflorescence a panicle, the branches and pedicels armed with stout, flattened prickles [Fig. ]; coarse, scrambling and climbing plants armed with stout, flattened prickles

Inflorescence a raceme, corymb-like raceme, or rarely a solitary flower, the branches and pedicels usually unarmed (never with stout, flattened prickles) [Figs. , , ]; upright to trailing plants with weak to strong armature, the prickles usually ± terete above the base

c13.text: Leaflets laciniately toothed or sometimes again cleft, ± green on the abaxial surface; calyx lobes with prickles, terminated by a narrow, elongate appendage; petals apically 3-lobed
Leaflets toothed, gray-tomentose on the abaxial surface; calyx lobes without prickles, lacking prolonged appendages; petals entire at the apex

c14.text: Primocanes canescent toward apex; prickles curved; petals white or sometimes tinged with pink
Primocanes ± glabrous; prickles ± straight; petals pale pink to red

c15.text: Primocanes doming, prostrate, or trailing, rooting, or with the opportunity to root, at the tip (in some species the depressed forms of the primocane not developing until midsummer when the apex of the stems finally reaches the ground) [Fig. ]
Primocanes arching or erect, not rooting at the tip (sometimes doming in R. vermontanus )

c16.text: Primocanes armed with hairs, bristles, or slender, small-based prickles [Fig. ]; petals 5–12 mm long; leaves usually lustrous, tending to be evergreen, with 3 leaflets 3.5–5 (–7) cm long

Primocanes armed, at least in part, with stout, broad-based prickles [Fig. ]; petals 10–25 mm long; leaves lustrous to, more commonly, dull, usually deciduous, with 3 or 5 leaflets 6–15 (–16) cm long (2–5 cm long in the rare R. cuneifolius )

c17.text: Inflorescence with 1–4 (–5) flowers [Fig. ]; pedicels, when 2 or more flowers are present, erect to ascending, 10–60 (–80) mm long, the uppermost one 10–20 mm long (or the peduncle to 50 mm when only 1 flower is present) [Fig. ]
Inflorescence with (1–) 2–8 (–12) flowers; pedicels ascending to spreading, 3–40 mm long, the uppermost one 3–11 (–15) mm long

c18.text: Stems very slender, 1–2 mm in diameter, with prickles (0.5–) 1–2 mm long; primocane leaves usually with 3 leaflets; inflorescences with 1 (–3) flowers
Stems thicker, 1.5–4 mm in diameter, with prickles 1–3 (–4) mm long; primocane leaves with 3 or 5 leaflets; inflorescences with 1–4 (–5) flowers

c19.text: Leaf blades ± glabrous abaxially, the hairs, when present, essentially confined to the leaflet midribs and primary lateral veins, usually not noticeable to the touch
Leaf blades ± evidently pubescent abaxially, with hairs present across the surface (i.e., between the primary lateral veins), usually noticeable to the touch

c20.text: Leaf blades ± glabrous abaxially, the hairs, when present, essentially confined to the leaflet midribs and primary lateral veins, usually not noticeable to the touch; inflorescence rachis and pedicels sparsely to moderately pubescent

Leaf blades ± evidently pubescent abaxially, with hairs present across the surface (i.e., between the primary lateral veins), usually noticeable to the touch; inflorescence rachis and pedicels moderately to densely pubescent

c21.text: Primocanes armed with hairs, bristles, or slender, small-based prickles [Fig. ]; stems 0.3–1 m tall; axis of inflorescence commonly with stipitate-glands (always lacking in R. elegantulus and often lacking in R. semisetosus )
Primocanes armed, at least in part, with stout, broad-based prickles; stems 0.5–3 m tall; axis of inflorescence lacking stipitate-glands except in R. allegheniensis and hybrids with that species

c22.text: Leaf blades ± evidently pubescent abaxially, with hairs present across the surface (i.e., between the primary lateral veins), usually noticeable to the touch; primocanes armed, at least in part, with slender, small-based prickles
Leaf blades ± glabrous abaxially, the hairs, when present, essentially confined to the leaflet midribs and primary lateral veins, usually not noticeable to the touch; primocane armature various

c23.text: Primocanes armed with hairs or stiff bristles only, the hairs/bristles numbering 600–5000 per 10 cm [Fig. ]
Primocanes armed, at least in part, by slender, small-based prickles, numbering 10–500 per 10 cm

c24.text: Central petiolule of primocane leaves (8–) 14–20 (–30) mm long; inflorescence rachis frequently with stipitate glands; stems 2–4 mm thick
Central petiolule of primocane leaves (15–) 25–40 (–50) mm long; inflorescence rachis never with stipitate glands; stems 3–6 mm thick (in part)

c25.text: Inflorescence, and often also the primocane, pubescent with stipitate glands [Fig. ], the inflorescence (3–) 8–20 cm long and with (3–) 9–22 flowers
Inflorescence and primocane ± lacking stipitate glands, the inflorescence 3–11 (–17) cm long and with (2–) 3–15 (–21) flowers

c26.text: Leaf blades ± glabrous abaxially, the hairs, when present, essentially confined to the leaflet midribs and primary lateral veins, usually not noticeable to the touch
Leaf blades ± evidently pubescent abaxially, with hairs present across the surface (i.e., between the primary lateral veins), usually noticeable to the touch

c27.text: Prickles of the stem absent or few, numbering 0–10 per 10 cm; inflorescence rachis pubescent to subglabrous, usually without prickles
Prickles of the stem more numerous, numbering 10–60 (–100) per 10 cm [Fig. ]; inflorescence rachis pubescent, often with thin prickles (in part)

c28.text: Leaflets oblanceolate to obovate, definitely widest above the middle, densely tomentose abaxially with white to gray hairs (sometimes becoming partly glabrate in late season)
Leaflets elliptic or elliptic-oblanceolate to broad-ovate, widest near or below the middle, pubescent abaxially, but not densely tomentose

c29.text: Terminal leaflet of primocane leaves elliptic-oblanceolate to elliptic, cuneate to narrow-rounded at the base, 2 or more times as long as wide
Terminal leaflet of primocane leaves ovate to broad-ovate, broad-cuneate to cordate at the base, less than 2 times as long as wide

c30.text: Prickles of the stem mostly 2–4 mm long, numbering 0–20 per 10 cm; leaf blades herbaceous; inflorescence with (0–) 1 or 2 (–6) leafy bracts (i.e., most of the pedicels subtended by small, stipule-like bracts)

Prickles of the stem mostly 4–6 mm long, numbering 4–60 per 10 cm; leaf blades tending to be more chartaceous; inflorescence with (0–) 1–7 leafy bracts (i.e., many of the pedicels subtended by foliaceous bracts)

c1.text: This genus contains exactly one species.
This genus contains exactly one species.
Inflorescence a simple umbel or corymb, terminating a short-shoot [Fig. ]
Inflorescence a panicle or compound corymb (i.e., with branches), terminating a long-shoot [Fig. ]

c2.text: Inflorescences (except sometimes the uppermost) borne on a peduncle, with 5–12 flowers; petioles 4–7 mm long; follicles pubescent with appressed hairs
Inflorescences sessile, with 3–7 flowers [Fig. ]; petioles 1–4 mm long; follicles glabrous or sometimes pubescent along the adaxial suture in S. prunifolia

c3.text: Leaf blades ovate to oblong-lanceolate, pubescent on the abaxial surface; pedicels 10–24 mm long, pubescent
Leaf blades narrow-lanceolate, glabrous on the abaxial surface; pedicels 6–10 mm long, glabrous

c4.text: Inflorescence a compound corymb, as wide as or wider than tall; leaf blades (5–) 8–15 cm long
Inflorescence a panicle, mostly taller than wide (except in high-elevation plants) [Fig. ]; leaf blades 3–7 (–8) cm long

c5.text: Mature leaf blades with white or red-brown tomentum abaxially; branchlets tomentose, especially about the nodes; flowers without a nectar disk; sepals reflexed in fruit; follicles pubescent
Mature leaf blades ± glabrous abaxially; branchlets ± glabrous; flowers with a nectar disk; sepals erect in fruit; follicles glabrous

c1.text: This genus contains exactly one species.
This genus contains exactly one species.
This genus contains exactly one species.
This genus contains exactly one species.
Flowers and fruits sessile or subsessile; ovary and drupe densely pubescent; winter branchlets with 3 axillary buds at each node, the lateral ones inflorescence buds, the central one a leaf bud
Flowers and fruits borne on evident pedicels; ovary and drupe glabrous; winter branchlets with a single bud at each node

c2.text: Drupes grooved, often glaucous; endocarp compressed and ± 2-edged; inflorescence in a fascicle that lacks leafy bracts at the base [Fig. ]; sepals pubescent on the adaxial surface (at least near the base; glabrous in P. domestica );

Drupes not grooved, not glaucous; endocarp globose to subglobose (ellipsoid in P. susquehanae ); inflorescence a raceme or a fascicle with leafy bracts at the base from the same winter bud (lacking leafy bracts in P. pumila , P . pensylvanica , and P. susquehanae ) [Fig. ]; sepals glabrous on the adaxial surface; terminal winter buds present

c3.text: Sepals with marginal glands; leaf teeth with a gland (note: the gland sometimes deciduous at maturity of the leaf and its former presence can be detected by observing a small gland scar on the tooth) [Fig. ]
Sepals lacking marginal glands (though they may be toothed); leaf teeth without a gland (though sometimes with a callous point) [Fig. ]

c4.text: Flowers solitary or paired (rarely in trios) [Fig. ]; drupes dark blue to black (red, yellow, or black in P. cerasifera ); leaves convolute in bud; branches sometimes tipped by a spine-like process
Flowers in fascicles of 3–5; drupes red to yellow; leaves conduplicate in bud; branches not tipped by a spine-like process

c5.text: Young branchlets and bracts densely pubescent; pedicels pubescent
Young branchlets and bracts glabrous to sparsely pubescent; pedicels glabrous or sparsely pubescent [Fig. ]

c6.text: Leaf blades 2–4 ×0.8–1.8 cm; drupes 10–15 mm in diameter; endocarp rugose
Leaf blades 3.5–6 (–8) ×2–4 cm; drupes (10–) 15–25 mm in diameter; endocarp nearly smooth

c7.text: Hypanthium pubescent; leaf blades pubescent on the abaxial surface; petioles 10–20 mm long; flowers 10–20 mm in diameter; drupes 40–75 mm in diameter; branches usually lacking thorns

Hypanthium glabrous; leaf blades glabrous on the abaxial surface or sparsely pubescent along the midvein; petioles 6–12 mm long; flowers 20–25 mm in diameter; drupes 20–30 mm in diameter; branches sometimes with thorns

c8.text: Petals 8–13 mm long, usually white changing to pink; sepals and pedicels tinged with or completely red; leaf blades coarsely and sometimes doubly serrate
Petals 5–7 mm long, usually remaining white; sepals and pedicels ± green; leaf blades finely crenulate-serrulate

c9.text: Petals 7–12 mm long; drupes red to yellow, (15–) 20–30 mm in diameter; leaf blades abruptly acuminate at the apex
Petals 3–8 mm long; drupes blue-purple to purple-black (rarely yellow), 10–15 (–25) mm in diameter; leaf blades truncate to acute or gradually acuminate at the apex

c10.text: Leaf blades ovate to elliptic or obovate (suborbicular in var. gravesii ), truncate to acute at the apex, pubescent on the abaxial surface; pedicels pubescent; drupes (10–) 13–15 (–25) mm in diameter

Leaf blades lanceolate to oblong-ovate or narrow-obovate, acute to acuminate at the apex, glabrate to sparsely pubescent on the abaxial surface; pedicels glabrous (rarely pubescent); drupes 10–12 mm in diameter

c11.text: Inflorescence a raceme with 18–64 (–90) flowers, the pedicels shorter than the axis of the inflorescence [Fig. ]
Inflorescence a fascicle with 2–10 flowers, the pedicels much longer than the axis of the inflorescence (if an axis is present)

c12.text: Leaf blades with more than 15 pairs of lateral veins (some of the veins inconspicuous), lanceolate-elliptic to ovate-elliptic, toothed with blunt, callous-tipped teeth, usually pubescent along the abaxial midrib with patches of white, turning red-brown, hairs; sepals oblong to triangular, entire or sparsely glandular-erose, persistent in fruit

Leaf blades with mostly 8–11 pairs of lateral veins, oblong to obovate, toothed with sharply pointed teeth, glabrous on the abaxial surface or with some obscure patches of hairs in the axils of the primary veins; sepals broad-triangular to semi-circular, conspicuously glandular-serrate, deciduous post anthesis

c13.text: Leaf blades with teeth that lack a gland [Fig. ]; low shrubs 0.2–1 (–2.5) m tall

Leaf blades with teeth that possess a gland (note: the gland sometimes deciduous at maturity of the leaf and its former presence can be detected by observing a small gland scar on the tooth) [Fig. ]; tall shrubs to trees, 3–20 m tall

c14.text: Branchlets glabrous; leaf blades narrow-oblanceolate, 5–18 mm wide, 3–6 times as long as wide [Fig. ], scarcely glaucous on the abaxial surface; plants depressed, mat-forming, with short, erect branches commonly 1–6 dm tall [Fig. ]; endocarp subglobse, 6–8 mm wide

Branchlets minutely pubescent; leaf blades oblong to oblong-obovate, 15–30 mm wide, 2–3 times as long as wide, glaucous on the abaxial surface; plants ascending to erect, commonly 3–10 dm tall; endocarp ellipsoid, 5–6 mm wide

c15.text: Leaf blades broad-ovate to suborbicular, broadly rounded to subcordate at the base; young branchlets glandular-puberulent; inflorescence a 4- to 10-flowered raceme with a short axis, the axis present during flowering

Leaf blades lanceolate or elliptic or elliptic-ovate or elliptic-obovate, cuneate to narrowly rounded at the base; branchlets glabrous or pubescent, but lacking glandular hairs; inflorescence a 2- to 5-flowered fascicle without an axis or sometimes with a very short axis in fruit [Fig. ]

c16.text: Petals 4–7 mm long; flowers 12–16 mm in diameter; drupes 5–7 mm in diameter
Petals 10–15 mm long; flowers 25–40 mm in diameter; drupes (8–) 15–25 mm in diameter

c17.text: Petals emarginate at the apex; sepals ascending to spreading; bracts of inflorescence brown to green-brown, usually deciduous; drupe 8–10 mm in diameter, purple-black
Petals entire at the apex [Fig. ]; sepals recurved or reflexed (at least post anthesis); bracts of inflorescence green, persistent; drupe 15–25 mm in diameter, red to purple-black (rarely yellow)

c18.text: Sepals margins glandular-serrate; petiole 10–20 (–25) mm long; proximal margin of leaf teeth much longer than the distal margin, therefore, the gland close to the sinus; leaf blades glabrous or essentially so on the abaxial surface (pubescent in early season)

Sepals margins entire; petiole 20–70 mm long; proximal margin of leaf teeth only slightly longer than distal margin, therefore, the gland well removed from the sinus; leaf blades persistently (though sometimes sparsely) pubescent on the abaxial surface

c1.text: Flowers borne in fascicles of 1–4; leaves imbricate in bud, with the outer ones enfolding the inner ones in bud, at maturity with petioles 2–10 mm long, cuneate at the base; bark often brown; ovary summit conical and pubescent

Flowers borne in racemes of 4–10 (–15); leaves conduplicate and positioned beside one another in bud, at maturity with petioles (8–) 10–30 mm long, rounded to cordate at the base; bark often gray; ovary summit rounded, pubescent or glabrous

c2.text: Petals 3–6 (–7) mm long, sometimes pollen-bearing [Fig. ]; plants colonial, with many close stems up to 2 (–3) m tall
Petals (6–) 7–22 mm long, not bearing pollen; plants colonial or not, 0.3–13 m tall

c3.text: Summit of the ovary pubescent (note: character state visible in flower and fruit); sepals reflexed from near the middle in fruit
Summit of the ovary glabrous; sepals ascending to recurved in fruit

c4.text: Lateral veins of leaf blade visible but not prominent, curved forward, forking 3 or more times, anastomosing and evanescent near the margin, not extending into the teeth [Fig. ]; margin of leaf blade usually serrulate with 6–10 teeth per cm, the teeth more than twice as many as primary lateral veins (caution: leaves on stump sprouts can show fewer, larger teeth); fruit 7–12 mm in diameter

Lateral veins of leaf blade prominent, nearly straight, forking 1 or more times, extending into the teeth or not; margin of leaf blade coarsely serrate-dentate with 0–5 teeth per cm, sometimes entire near the base (or nearly throughout), the teeth less than twice as many as primary lateral veins; fruit 5–8 mm in diameter (up to 10 mm in diameter in A. gaspensis , but that species with leaves sparsely pubescent during flowering)

c5.text: Flowering racemes compact, 20–40 (–50) mm long, the rachis and pedicels densely pubescent; lowest pedicel 9–13 (–15) mm long in flower; expanding leaf blades densely tomentose abaxially, retaining the tomentum long after flowering

Flowering racemes somewhat open, 40–80 mm long, the rachis and pedicels sparsely pubescent; lowest pedicel (7–) 10–30 mm long in flower; expanding leaf blades soon losing much of the abaxial tomentum and becoming glabrescent post flowering

c6.text: Low, colonial plants up to 1 m tall; petals 6–9 mm long; leaf blades with 6–13 pairs of primary veins that mostly anastomose near the margin; hypanthium scutelliform, 3–4 mm wide

Taller shrubs with solitary or clumped stems 1–3 m tall; petals (10–) 11–15 (–20) mm long; leaf blades with 12–15 pairs of primary veins that mostly enter the teeth [Fig. ]; hypanthium open and shallow, (3.5–) 4–6 (–8) mm wide

c7.text: Petals 7–12 mm long; racemes straight, erect or ascending, the axis 2.5–6 cm long; sepals ascending to spreading (infrequently recurving) in fruit; stems several to many, close together, forming clumps; mature leaf blades rounded to subcordate at base
Petals 12–22 mm long; racemes lax or arching, the axis 4–12 cm long; sepals recurved in fruit; stems solitary or few together; mature leaf blades cordate at the base

c8.text: Leaf blades sparsely pubescent and often tinged with purple at anthesis, at maturity truncate to subcordate at the base and acute to short-acuminate at the apex, with 5–7 teeth per cm; petals 9–12 mm long; flowering racemes sparsely pubescent on the rachis and pedicels; lower pedicels 20–35 mm long in fruit; sepals ascending to somewhat recurving in fruit

Leaf blades densely pubescent and green at anthesis (the blade color obscured by the hairs), at maturity rounded at the base and rounded or mucronate at the apex, with 6–11 teeth per cm; petals 7–10 mm long; flowering racemes densely pubescent on the rachis and pedicels; lower pedicels 5–10 mm long in fruit; sepals erect to loosely ascending in fruit

c9.text: Leaf blades at anthesis 50–75% expanded, nearly glabrous, strongly tinged with red-purple or purple, essentially glabrous at maturity; lower pedicels 20–50 mm long in fruit; pomes fleshy and sweet

Leaf blades at anthesis less than 50% expanded, densely tomentose on the abaxial surface, green, retaining some pubescence in maturity especially along the midvein and in the axils of the primary lateral veins; lower pedicels 10–25 mm long in fruit; pomes drier and bland tasting

c1.text: Primary lateral veins of the leaf blades running to the sinuses as well as the points of the lobes [Fig. ]
Primary lateral veins of the leaf blades running only to the points of the lobes or the leaves unlobed and the veins running to the teeth [Fig. ]

c2.text: Flowers with 3–5 styles; leaf blades rounded to subcordate at base, sharply acute at the apex [Fig. ]; anthers non-anthocyanic; thorns (12–) 23–55 mm long
Flowers with 1 style; leaf blades cuneate to broad-cuneate at base, rounded to acute at apex; anthers anthocyanic; thorns 5–17 mm long

c3.text: Androecium with 2 cycles of stamens [Fig. ]
Androecium with 1 cycle of stamens [Fig. ]

c4.text: Inflorescence sparsely to densely pubescent, retaining some hairs at least until full maturity of pome
Inflorescence glabrous

c5.text: Flowers 20–24 mm wide; leaf blades broad-ovate to broad-triangular or suborbicular and (50–) 61–110 mm long at maturity; pomes usually prominently glaucous
Flowers 13–20.5 mm wide; leaf blades usually of narrower shape or of shorter length or both; pomes not or only slightly glaucous

c6.text: Sepals entire or nearly so; leaf blades elliptic to narrow-elliptic-obovate to obovate, usually widest above the middle, barely (if at all) lobed on short shoots, 1.4–2.1 times as long as wide
Sepals glandular-serrate to glandular-pinnatifid; leaf blades not combining the above-mentioned characters

c7.text: Anthers non-anthocyanic; leaf blades near apex of long shoots suborbicular or nearly so, with small, acuminate-tipped lobes
Anthers anthocyanic; leaf blades near apex of long shoots not combining the above mentioned characters

c8.text: Pyrenes with a definite depression occupying most of each half of the inner face (pyrenes plane or with shallow and irregular erosions in the very rare C. pisifera ); anthers 0.7–1 (–1.3) mm long; inflorescence relatively large, with (7–) 12–20 flowers; leaf blades mostly rhombic to obovate, those on short shoots often with obscure lobes

Pyrenes plane on the inner faces; anthers 1.2–1.5 mm long; inflorescence mostly of small to medium size, with 5–12 flowers; leaf blades elliptic or ovate to elliptic-ovate or orbicular, those on short shoots with obscure to evident lobes

c9.text: Pomes 9–13 mm in diameter; pyrenes with a deep excavation on the inner surfaces; inflorescence villous (glabrous or sparsely villous in very rare forms); flowers 15–20.5 mm in diameter (in part)
Pomes 5–9 mm in diameter; pyrenes plane to shallowly and irregularly eroded on the inner surfaces; inflorescence glabrous to sparsely villous; flowers 13–15 mm in diameter (in part)

c10.text: Leaf blades adaxially with relatively long and soft appressed hairs mostly 0.3–0.8 mm long; short shoot leaf blades usually broad-cuneate at the base, the basal margins forming an angle of mostly less than 95 degrees; petioles frequently with a narrow, but evident, wing of green tissue, especially near the apex

Leaf blades adaxially with relatively short and stiff appressed hairs mostly 0.2–0.4 mm long; short shoot leaf blades usually rounded at the base, the basal margins forming an angle of mostly more than 95 degrees; petioles scarcely winged

c11.text: Leaf blades broad-ovate to suborbicular (occasionally some ovate on short shoots), 1–1.2 times as long as wide [Fig. ]; pomes globose to, infrequently, short-obloid (in part)
Leaf blades ovate or elliptic-ovate, infrequently broad-ovate, 1.1–1.6 times as long as wide; pomes obloid to obovoid

c12.text: Pyrenes with a definite depression occupying most of each half of the inner face (pyrenes plane or with shallow and irregular erosions in the very rare C. pisifera ) [Fig. , R]; bracts of leaf opening strongly tinged with red to orange-red and conspicuous; inflorescence relatively large, with (7–) 12–20 flowers; sepals glandular-serrate to glandular-pinnatifid

Pyrenes plane on the inner faces or some faces with irregular and shallow erosions [Fig. , L]; bracts of leaf opening yellow-brown or weakly tinged with red, less conspicuous; inflorescence mostly of small to medium size, with 4–13 flowers; sepals entire to glandular-serrate

c13.text: Pomes 9–13 mm in diameter; pyrenes with a deep excavation on the inner surfaces; inflorescence villous (glabrous or sparsely villous in very rare forms); flowers 15–20.5 mm in diameter (in part)
Pomes 5–9 mm in diameter; pyrenes plane to shallowly and irregularly eroded on the inner surfaces; inflorescence glabrous to sparsely villous; flowers 13–15 mm in diameter (in part)

c14.text: Anthers (1.6–) 1.8–2.3 mm long; flowers 20–23 mm wide; pyrenes plane to shallowly and irregularly eroded on the inner surfaces

Anthers 0.7–1.6 mm long; flowers (16–) 17–21.5 mm wide; pyrenes plane on the inner surfaces (shallowly and irregularly eroded on some pyrenes in C. brainerdii , but that species with 3 styles vs. (4–) 5 styles)

c15.text: Anthers 0.7–1 mm long; pyrenes plane to shallowly and irregularly eroded on the inner surfaces; leaf blades on short shoots mostly cuneate at the base, the basal margins forming an angle of mostly less than 95 degrees

Anthers 1.1–1.6 mm long; pyrenes plane on the inner surfaces; short shoot leaf blades usually broad-cuneate to rounded, truncate, or subcordate at the base, the basal margins forming an angle of mostly more than 95 degrees

c16.text: Leaf blades adaxially with abundant strigae during flowering, these persisting at least along the main veins and/or in patches between the veins until early summer (in some taxa persisting nearly until maturation of the fruit); pomes not or only thinly glaucous; pedicels and short shoot branches not glaucous

Leaf blades adaxially without strigae or the hairs sparse to moderately abundant during flowering and absent on mature, fully expanded blades; pomes moderately to prominently glaucous at maturity; pedicels and short shoot branches often thinly glaucous in late season

c17.text: Leaf blades glabrous adaxially from very early on (rarely with very few hairs); fruiting sepals prominently elevated on a collar 0.5–1.7 mm tall
Leaf blades adaxially with sparse to moderately abundant strigae during flowering; fruiting sepals slightly elevated on a collar 0.3–0.8 mm tall

c18.text: Bracteoles of inflorescence abundant at flowering, with prominently elevated marginal glands on stipes (0.1–) 0.2–1.4 mm long [Fig. ]; petioles prominently glandular, sometimes even glandular-toothed; mature pomes yellow-green to bronze-green or dull red

Bracteoles of inflorescence absent to moderately abundant at flowering, with sessile to slightly elevated marginal glands on stipes as long as 0.2 mm; petioles glandular or not, but usually not glandular-toothed on short shoot leaves; mature pomes usually orange to red, often brightly so

c19.text: Foliage, inflorescence, and pome ± glabrous
Foliage, inflorescence, and pome (at least when young) pubescent

c20.text: Leaf blades with 4 or 5 pairs of acute to subacuminate lobes, the tips of the lobes spreading or even slightly outcurved, those on long shoots with ovate to oblong-ovate blades; flowers 13–17 mm wide; pome obloid to obovoid, 8–13 mm thick

Leaf blades with 3 or 4 pairs of obtuse to subacute lobes, the tips of the lobes ascending, those on long shoots with broad-ovate to suborbicular blades; flowers 17–21 mm wide; pome globose to subglobose (rarely short-obloid), 10–14 mm thick

c21.text: Anthers non-anthocyanic; pome subglobose to depressed-globose; leaf blades broad-cuneate to rounded, truncate, or subcordate at the base
Anthers anthocyanic; pome obovoid to subglobose; leaf blades cuneate at the base

c22.text: Inflorescence glabrous
Inflorescence sparsely to densely villous

c23.text: Petioles 2–12 (–15) mm long; leaf blades (1.2–) 1.5–2.5 times as long as wide, usually broadest at or above the middle of the blade, those on short shoots without lobes or with mostly short, obscure lobes
Petioles 10–40 mm long; leaf blades 1–1.6 times as long as wide, usually broadest at or below the middle of the blade, those on short shoots with obscure to evident lobes

c24.text: Leaf blades 1.5–2.5 times as long as wide, those on short shoots usually unlobed and widest well above the middle, with faint veins on the adaxial surface (in part)
Leaf blades 1.2–1.8 times as long as wide, those on short shoots often with short lobes and widest near or slightly above the middle, with somewhat evident veins on the adaxial surface

c25.text: Leaf blades adaxially with abundant strigae during flowering, the hairs persisting at least along the main veins and/or in patches between the veins until early summer (in some taxa persisting nearly until maturation of the fruit); anthers anthocyanic
Leaf blades adaxially glabrous or with sparse strigae during flowering and then soon glabrous (sometimes with moderately abundant strigae in C. dodgei ); anthers anthocyanic or non-anthocyanic

c26.text: Short shoot leaves mostly cuneate at the base during flowering, the basal margins forming an angle of less than 90 degrees; pyrenes plane to shallowly and irregularly eroded on the inner surfaces (in part)

Short shoot leaves mostly broad-cuneate to rounded or truncate (infrequently subcordate) at the base, the basal margins forming an angle of greater than 90 degrees; pyrenes plane on the inner surfaces

c27.text: Sepals entire or weakly glandular-serrate; flowers 14–16 mm wide
Sepals glandular-serrate, often prominently so; flowers 16–20 mm wide

c28.text: Short shoot leaves elliptic to elliptic-ovate, 1.2–1.5 times as long as wide [Fig. ] (in part)
Short shoot leaves elliptic-ovate to broad-ovate or triangular-ovate, 1.1–1.3 times as long as wide

c29.text: Pomes obloid to obovoid, 8–10 mm in diameter (in part)
Pomes globose to subglobose (rarely short-obloid), 9–12 mm in diameter (in part)

c30.text: Sepals prominently glandular-serrate to glandular-pinnatifid with elongate calyx teeth, the longest teeth (0.3–) 0.5–1.5 mm long; flowers with 4 or 5 styles
Sepals entire to glandular-serrate, the longest teeth (when present) 0.1–0.5 (–0.6) mm long; flowers with 2–4 (–5) styles

c31.text: Short shoot leaves mostly cuneate at the base during flowering, the basal margins forming an angle of less than 90 degrees [Fig. ]; anthers non-anthocyanic

Short shoot leaves mostly broad-cuneate to rounded or truncate (infrequently subcordate) at the base, the basal margins forming an angle of greater than 90 degrees; anthers anthocyanic (non-anthocyanic in some C. handyae , but that species with erosions on the inner surfaces of some pyrenes)

c32.text: Leaf blades on short shoots obtuse to subactue at the apex, with acute lobes, borne on glandular (rarely sparsely so) petioles; sepals weakly to somewhat prominently glandular-serrate
Leaf blades on short-shoots rounded to obtuse at the apex, with rounded to obtuse lobes, borne on eglandular (rarely sparsely glandular) petioles [Fig. ]; sepals entire to weakly glandular-serrate

c33.text: Inner surface of some pyrenes with shallow and irregular erosions; anthers usually non-anthocyanic (in part)
Inner surface of pyrenes plane; anthers anthocyanic

c34.text: Sepals glandular-serrate; branch thorns very fine, usually 1.6–1.7 mm wide at the midpoint; pomes obloid to obpyriform

Sepals entire to weakly glandular-serrate; branch thorns thicker, (1.7–) 1.8–2.5 mm thick at the midpoint; pomes globose to subglobose (to obloid or obovoid in some C. populnea , but that species sparsely pubescent adaxially during flowering)

c35.text: Leaf blades adaxially with sparse to moderately abundant strigae during flowering and then soon glabrous; pomes variable in shape, sometimes elongate and tapering to the base in drying
Leaf blades adaxially glabrous or with very few hairs during flowering; pomes globose to subglobose, rounded to truncate at the base in drying

c36.text: Leaf blades with relatively shallow sinuses, the lobes near the middle of the blade on mature leaves 4–8 mm long
Leaf blades with relatively deep sinuses, the lobes near the middle of the blade on mature leaves 7–15 mm long

c37.text: Pyrenes with a definite depression occupying most of each half of the inner face [Fig. , R]; bracts of leaf opening strongly tinged with red to orange-red and conspicuous; inflorescence relatively large, with (8–) 10–31 flowers; sepals conspicuously glandular-serrate to glandular-pinnatifid; leaf blades mostly rhombic to obovate, those on short shoots often with inconspicuous lobes

Pyrenes plane on the inner faces or some faces with irregular and shallow erosions [Fig. , L]; bracts of leaf opening yellow-brown or weakly tinged with red, less conspicuous; inflorescence mostly of small to medium size, with 3–16 (–19) flowers; sepals entire or weakly to conspicuously glandular-serrate; leaf blades rhombic or elliptic to ovate, suborbicular, or elliptic-ovate (rarely oblong-obovate), those on short shoots with inconspicuous to evident lobes

c38.text: Leaf blades adaxially glabrous or with very sparse strigae during flowering and then soon glabrous

Leaf blades adaxially with abundant strigae during flowering, the hairs persisting at least along the main veins and/or in patches between the veins until early summer (in some taxa persisting nearly until maturation of the fruit)

c39.text: Leaf blades oblanceolate to broad-oblanceolate-elliptic, 1.5–2.5 times as long as wide, borne on petioles 2–12 (–15) mm long, those on short shoots essentially unlobed (in part)

Leaf blades broad-rhombic or broad-elliptic to ovate, rhombic-ovate broad-ovate, or triangular-ovate, 1–1.3 times as long as wide, borne on petioles 17–35 mm long, those on short shoots with evident lobes

c40.text: Flowers 19–22 mm wide; pomes globose; some pyrenes with shallow and irregular erosions in the inner surfaces (in part)
Flowers 14–16 mm wide; pomes obovoid to obpyriform; pyrenes plane on the inner surfaces

c41.text: Short shoot leaves mostly cuneate at the base during flowering, the basal margins forming an angle of less than 95 degrees
Short shoot leaves mostly broad-cuneate to rounded or truncate (infrequently subcordate) at the base, the basal margins forming an angle of greater than 95 degrees

c42.text: Flowers 13–19 mm wide; sepals weakly to conspicuously glandular-serrate

c43.text: Pyrenes plane on the inner surfaces [Fig. , L]; anthers non-anthocyanic (anthocyanic in the very rare C. chrysocarpa var. praecox )
Some pyrenes with shallow and irregular erosions on the inner surfaces; anthers anthocyanic

c44.text: Inflorescence sparsely pubescent; hypanthium glabrous or sparsely pubescent near the base; sepals weakly glandular-serrate
Inflorescence moderately to densely pubescent; hypanthium pubescent ± throughout; sepals conspicuously glandular-serrate

c45.text: Leaf blades broad-rhombic to suborbicular, 36–61 mm long at maturity, 1–1.2 times as long as wide [Fig. ]; pomes globose
Leaf blades rhombic-elliptic to ovate, 48–78 (–87) mm long at maturity, 1.2–1.7 (–1.9) times as long as wide; pomes subglobose to short-obloid

c46.text: Inflorescence moderately villous; hypanthium moderately villous; young branchlets sparsely villous; flowers 18–19 mm wide; pomes obloid to obovoid, sparsely villous; leaf blades elliptic to rhombic or rhombic-ovate, usually widest near the middle, the margins with ± straight taper to the apex

Inflorescence sparsely pubescent; hypanthium glabrous or sparsely pubescent; young branchlets glabrous; flowers 14–18 mm wide; pomes globose to subglobose (rarely to short-obloid), glabrous; leaf blades very variable in shape but usually with one or more features: somewhat oblong in outline; broadest above or below the middle; and/or the margins with concave taper to the apex

c47.text: Branch thorns long, slender, and straight or nearly so, (35–) 45–60 ×1.9–2.1 mm
Branch thorns variable, usually shorter, more stout, and slightly curved, 22–45 (–65) × (1.9–) 2–2.9 mm

c48.text: Most leaf blades on short shoots elliptic to elliptic-obovate to oblong-obovate, with concave taper to the apex; hypanthium usually glabrous (in part)
Most leaf blades on short shoots ovate to rhombic-ovate or broad-ovate, with convex or straight taper to the apex; hypanthium usually sparsely villous near the base

c49.text: Anthers non-anthocyanic; subherbaceous bracteoles sometimes present in the apical half of the inflorescence; stamens ca. 50% as long as the petals; leaf blades permanently pubescent abaxially on and between the primary lateral veins

Anthers anthocyanic; herbaceous bracteoles rarely present in the apical half of the inflorescence; stamens ca. 65–95% as long as the petals; leaf blades abaxially pubescent on only the primary lateral veins at maturity (if at all; sometimes permanently pubescent across the surface in C. holmesiana , but that species usually with obloid to obovoid pomes vs. globose to short-obloid pomes)

c50.text: Flowers 20–26 mm wide; mature leaf blades 55–111 mm long
Flowers 16–17.5 mm wide; mature leaf blades 36–70 mm long

c51.text: Sepals subentire to weakly glandular-serrate (i.e., sepals without marginal glands or these present and then usually sparse and mostly not elevated from the margin more than 0.2 mm), somewhat persistent or deciduous from mature pomes; flowers 15–18 mm wide

Sepals glandular-serrate, often conspicuously so (i.e., some of the glands elevated from the margin of the sepal on teeth 0.2–0.6 mm), somewhat to firmly persistent on the mature pomes; flowers (16–) 17–21 mm wide

c52.text: Leaf blades broad-ovate to suborbicular (rarely some ovate or broad-triangular-ovate), 1–1.2 times as long as wide (in part)
Leaf blades ovate to broad-elliptic or elliptic-ovate, (1.1–) 1.2–1.7 times as long as wide

c53.text: Mature leaf blades (i.e., post-flowering) on short shoots mostly elliptic to elliptic-ovate, 1.2–1.5 times as long as wide [Fig. ] (in part)
Mature leaf blades on short shoots ovate to suborbicular, 1–1.3 times as long as wide

c54.text: Pomes obloid to obovoid; hypanthium glabrous; lobes of the leaf blades with relatively more frequent and more prominent outcurved tips [Fig. ] (in part)
Pomes globose to subglobose (rarely to short-obloid); hypanthium villous (sometimes glabrous in C. coccinea ); lobes of the leaf blades with relatively fewer and less prominent outcurved tips

c55.text: Leaf blades ovate to broad-ovate, usually truncate to subcordate at the base, ± plane in life; thorns (20–) 25–60 mm long (in part)
Leaf blades broad-ovate to suborbicular, usually rounded at the base, often convex in life (i.e., with drooping sides); thorns 15–35 (–42) mm long

c1.text: Pome black, generally falling from the plant in the fall and not persistent through the winter; abaxial surface of leaf blades, branchlets, and pedicels glabrous or nearly so

Pome red or purple, either long-persistent on the plant or falling in autumn; abaxial surface of leaf blades, branchlets, and pedicels varying from sparsely to densely pubescent (rarely one or more surfaces glabrous in A. floribunda )

c2.text: Pome red; leaf blades usually varying from moderately to densely pubescent on the abaxial surface, turning bright red in the fall
Pome purple; leaf blades usually varying from sparsely to moderately pubescent on the abaxial surface, not or only partially turning red in the fall

c1.text: Leaf blades simple; calyx lobes deciduous in fruit
Leaf blades compound; calyx lobes persistent in fruit

c2.text: Leaf blades with 3–7 leaflets; terminal leaflet much larger than the lateral leaflets, often lobed
Leaf blades with 11–17 leaflets; terminal leaflet +/- similar to lateral leaflets, serrate

c3.text: Branchlets, inflorescence, adaxial surface of leaflets, and hypanthium villous; bud scales villous, not glutinous
Branchlets, inflorescence, adaxial surface of leaflets, and hypanthium glabrous or some surfaces sparsely villous; bud scales glabrous or ciliate on the margin, glutinous

c4.text: Leaflets acuminate at the apex, 3–5 times as long as wide [Fig. , R]; winter bud scales eciliate or sparsely ciliate; petals 3–4 mm long; pomes 4–7 mm wide
Leaflets acute to short-acuminate at the apex, 2–3.5 times as long as wide [Fig. , L]; winter bud scales ciliate; petals 4–5 mm long; pomes 7–10 mm wide

c1.text: Branchlets scabrous, becoming verrucose when old; pome 30–40 mm in diameter; leaf blade obovate to spatulate, crenate; sepals ovate (rarely suborbicular), 4–5 mm long
Branchlets smooth, not verrucose when old; pome 40–60 mm in diameter; leaf blade elliptic-ovate to elliptic-oblong (rarely obovate), sharply serrate; sepals suborbicular (rarely ovate), 3–4 mm long
Flowers with 5 styles, 25–30 mm in diamter; hypanthium pubescent; calyx persistent on fruit; pome (5–) 6–16 ×4–12 cm, yellow to green
Flowers with 2 or 3 styles, 20–25 (–28) mm in diameter; hypanthium glabrous; calyx deciduous from fruit; pome 0.9–1.5 ×0.9–1.5 cm, brown to dark brown and with pale dots
Leaf blades (at least those on long shoots) usually lobed, conduplicate in bud; pomes with some sclerenchyma cells
Leaf blades unlobed, convolute in bud (conduplicate in M. floribunda ); pomes lacking sclerenchyma cells

c2.text: Calyx lobes deciduous [Fig. ]; pomes 0.6–1 cm in diameter
Calyx lobes persistent in fruit; pome 2–12 cm in diameter

c3.text: Calyx glabrous; young branchlets glabrous; leaves convolute in bud; petiole 20–50 mm long; gynoecium with (4–) 5 styles; mature pome 8–10 mm in diameter
Calyx pubescent; young branchlets pubescent; leaves conduplicate in bud; petiole 15–25 mm long; gynoecium with usually 4 styles; mature pome 6–8 mm in diameter

c4.text: Leaf blades sharply serrate; pedicels 20–35 mm long, slender; calyx glabrous or somewhat villous; pomes ovoid, 2–3.5 cm in diameter
Leaf blades crenate-serrate; pedicels 10–25 mm long, stout; calyx tomentose; pomes subglobose, (2–) 6–12 cm in diameter

c1.text: This genus contains exactly one species.
Flowering stems scapose or subscapose, with highly reduced stem leaves or lacking leaves altogether; styles ± straight, no portion conspicuously curved, not articulated or articulated at the base
Flowering stems with evident, well-developed leaves; styles articulated near the middle, the basal part hooked at the tip and becoming indurate, the apical part usually deciduous

c2.text: Basal leaves with 3 leaflets, the lateral leaflets not or only somewhat smaller than the terminal leaflet; gynoecium with 2–6 (–10) carpels; styles deciduous at the base in fruit by an articulation point; petals 5–10 mm long
Basal leaves with 1 large terminal leaflet and 0–6 pairs of very small lateral leaflets; gynoecium with 30 or more carpels; styles persistent and plumose in fruit; petals 8–15 mm long

c3.text: Epicalyx absent; cluster of achenes stipitate on a stalk 1–2 mm long, elevated above the persistent calyx; petals 1–2 mm long
Epicalyx present; cluster of achenes sessile or nearly so with respect to the calyx; petals 2–10 mm long

c4.text: Sepals petaloid, purple to red-purple, ascending to erect at anthesis [Fig. ]; petals erect to ascending; flowers somewhat to conspicuously nodding (becoming erect in fruit) [Fig. ]
Sepals sepaloid, green, reflexed at anthesis [Figs. , ]; petals spreading; flowers erect

c5.text: Petals yellow to orange-yellow
Petals white to yellow-white

c6.text: Basal segment of style minutely glandular [Fig. ]; terminal segment of basal leaf blades suborbicular to reniform, truncate to cordate at the base, much larger than the lateral segments; pedicels minutely and densely puberulent, sometimes also with scattered, longer hairs; fruiting receptacle glabrous or inconspicuously short-pubescent, the carpel scars plainly visible on the denuded receptacle

Basal segment of style eglandular; terminal segment of basal leaf blades oblanceolate to obovate, cuneate at the base, not or scarcely larger than the lateral segments; pedicels both conspicuously hirsute and minutely puberulent [Fig. ]; fruiting receptacle hirsute, the hairs partially obscuring the carpel scars on the denuded receptacle

c7.text: Achenes usually numbering 200–250 per cluster, evidently spreading-pubescent near the base of the basal segment of style; petals (5–) 6–10 mm long; pedicels relatively stout, mostly thicker than 1 mm; stipules of stem leaves relatively small, conspicuously reduced compared with the leaflets; leaf teeth usually sharply pointed

Achenes usually numbering fewer than 100 per cluster, the basal segment of the style glabrous; petals 4–7 mm long; pedicels relatively slender, mostly thinner than 1 mm; stipules of stem leaves relatively large, ± appearing as a pair of leaflets set close to the stem; leaf teeth usually blunt to obtusely pointed

c8.text: Pedicels both conspicuously hirsute and minutely puberulent [Fig. ], relatively stout, mostly thicker than 1 mm; basal leaf blades variable, but commonly with 3–7 principal leaflets (smaller leaflets also often present; sometimes with only 1 principal leaflet); achenes usually numbering more than 160 per cluster [Fig. ]

Pedicels minutely and densely puberulent, sometimes also with scattered longer hairs [Fig. ], relatively slender, mostly thinner than 1 mm; basal leaf blades with usually 3 principal leaflets; achenes usually numbering 30–160 per cluster [Fig. ]

c9.text: Petals ochroleucous, 2–4 mm long, much shorter than the sepals; leaf teeth usually blunt to obtusely pointed; stem moderately hirsute (at least in the basal half)
Petals white, (3.5–) 4–9 mm long, nearly as long as or longer than the sepals; leaf teeth sharply pointed; stem glabrous or sparsely hirsute near the base

c1.text: This genus contains exactly one species.
Bractlets definitely larger than the sepals, with 3 conspicous teeth at the apex; receptacle enlarged in fruit, somewhat resembling a “strawberry”, but rather dry and insipid tasting
Bractlets of ± similar size as the sepals or smaller, lacking conspicuous apical teeth (though the margins may have small teeth); receptacle not enlarged and remaining dry

c2.text: Flowers solitary on axillary peduncles [Fig. ]; stems slender, herbaceous, prostrate and trailing (though often ascending at anthesis), rooting at some nodes and/or the apex (usually erect to ascending and not rooting in P. erecta ); style slender, not thickened near the middle or base (conical at base and thickned near apex in P. erecta and P. reptans , both very rare introductions)

Flowers usually few to many in a terminal cyme (the flowers rarely solitary); stems erect to spreading or sometimes prostrate, but not trailing and rooting (trailing and rooting with woody stems in P. verna ), the inflorescence usually with bracts; style thickened near the middle or base

c3.text: Stems erect to ascending, though sometimes procumbent at anthesis, not rooting at the nodes; stem leaves sessile or subsessile; basal rosette ephemeral, usually absent at anthesis
Stems prostrate (though initially ascending), rooting at some nodes and/or the apex; stem leaves petiolate (sometimes sessile or subsessile in P. simplex ); basal rosettes persisting through anthesis

c4.text: Many or all of the flowers with 4 sepals and petals; leaf blades glabrous or glabrate; upper leaves with 3 or 4 leaflets; bractlets lanceolate; stipules narrow-ovate
Flowers with 5 sepals and petals; leaf blades pubescent on the abaxial surface (+/- glabrous in P. reptans ); upper leaves with usually 5 leaflets; bractlets linear-lanceolate; stipules lanceolate

c5.text: Petals (6–) 8–12 mm long; anthers (1–) 1.3–2 mm long; epicalyx segments lanceolate to oblong or elliptic; stems from a slender root
Petals 4–7 (–10) mm long; anthers 0.6–1 mm long; epicalyx segments linear to narrow-lanceolate; stems from a thickened rhizome

c6.text: Flowers from the axil of the first well-developed cauline leaf [Fig. ]; terminal leaflet usually less than 2 times as long as wide; plants shorter, 5–15 cm at anthesis; rhizome 5–20 mm ×4–8 mm
Flowers usually from the axil of the second well-developed cauline leaf; terminal leaflet usually more than 2 times as long as wide; plants taller, 20–40 cm at anthesis; rhizome 20–80 ×5–20 mm

c7.text: Leaf blades sparsely to densely tomentose on the abaxial surface (long, straight or merely curved hairs also present in some species, especially P. inclinata and P. intermedia )
Leaf blades glabrous or pubescent with straight or merely curved hairs on the abaxial surface

c8.text: Styles (1–) 1.5–2.5 (–3) mm long, short-conic near the base and then filiform and prolonged, the longer ones 2–3 times as long as the mature ovary; petals 4–10 (–11) mm long; filaments 1.5–3.5 mm long; anthers 0.7–1.2 (–1.6) mm long
Styles 0.6–1.2 mm long, conic or columnar, shorter than to slightly longer than the mature ovary; petals (2.5–) 4–7 mm long; filaments 0.8–1.5 (–2.5) mm long; anthers 0.3–0.6 (–1.2) mm long

c9.text: Leaflets sparsely tomentose abaxially, toothed with elongate, triangular-lanceolate teeth mostly 5–15 mm long, the sinuses between the teeth usually extending to the distance to the midrib
Leaflets densely tomentose abaxially, crenate to crenate-serrate with teeth mostly 2–5 mm long, the sinuses between the teeth usually extending less than the distance to the midrib

c10.text: Lower leaves with 5–7 leaflets, these pinnately arranged or the upper 3 confluent and appearing subpalmately arranged [Fig. ]; styles glandular at the base
Lower leaves with 4–7 leaflets, these definitely palmately arranged when numbering 5 or more, styles not glandular at the base (though sometimes papillose)

c11.text: Leaflets revolute, each with 2–4 (–6) tooth-like lobes, densely silver-tomentose abaxially; basal leaves much larger than the middle stem leaves; style base papillose

Leaflets with plane or scarcely revolute margins, coarsely serrate to pinnatifid with (3–) 4–10 (–12) teeth or lobes, sparsely to moderately gray-tomentose abaxially; basal leaves relatively similar in size and outline to the middle stem leaves; style base epapillose

c12.text: Leaflets pale green abaxially; petals 4–5 (–5.7) mm long; segments of epicalyx oblong-ovate to oblong, obtuse to acute at the apex (in part)
Leaflets usually gray-green abaxially; petals 5–7 mm long; segments of epicalyx narrow-lanceolate to lanceolate, acute at the apex

c13.text: Lower leaves with 3 leaflets
Lower leaves with (4–) 5–9 leaflets [Fig. ]

c14.text: Plants cespitose or mat-forming, the flowering stems 1–10 (–20) cm tall
Plants simple to branched, but neither cespitose nor mat-forming, the flowering stems (10–) 20–120 cm tall

c15.text: Dwarf, cespitose plants without procumbent woody stems, 1–4 cm tall; stipules ovate, blunt to abruptly pointed at the apex; leaflets 5–13 mm long

Mat-forming plants with numerous, procumbent woody stems that root at the nodes, the flowering stems up to 10 (–20) cm tall; stipules linear to narrow-lanceolate, sharply pointed at the apex; leaflets (5–) 8–35 (–40) mm long (in part)

c16.text: Androecium with 15–20 stamens bearing anthers 0.3–0.5 mm long; stems hirsute; petals 2–5 mm long, slightly shorter than to subequal in length to the sepals; achenes green-brown to brown, striate-ribbed

Androecium with (5–) 10 (–15) stamens bearing anthers 0.2–0.3 mm long [Fig. ]; stems villous, petals 1.3–3 mm long, conspicuously shorter than the sepals [Fig. ]; achenes yellow-brown, smooth (in part)

c17.text: Petals white; leaflets with a few teeth near the apex; achenes smooth

Petals yellow; leaflets with teeth or tooth-like lobes extending from the apex to at least below the middle of the leaflet and often nearly or quite to the base of the leaflet; achenes striate-ribbed or smooth in P. rivalis

c18.text: Mat-forming plants with numerous procumbent woody stems that root at the nodes, the flowering stems 3–10 (–20) cm tall; style slightly dilated near apex (in part)
Simple or branched, erect to spreading plants, without procumbent, rooting stems, the flowering stems (–15) 25–80 cm tall; style slender at apex

c19.text: Androecium with (5–) 10 (–15) stamens bearing anthers 0.2–0.3 mm long [Fig. ]; petals 1.3–3 mm long, conspicuously shorter than the sepals [Fig. ]; achenes smooth (in part)
Androecium with 15–30 stamens bearing anthers 0.6–1.2 (–1.5) mm long; petals subequal to or longer than the sepals; achenes usually striate-ribbed

c20.text: Petals 4–5 (–5.7) mm long, slightly shorter to slightly longer than the sepals; stems without glandular hairs, often tomentose (at least above, varying to nearly glabrous) (in part)
Petals (6–) 7–12 mm long, slightly to evidently longer than the sepals; stems usually with glandular hairs (in addition to longer, eglandular ones), lacking tomentum

c21.text: Stems arising centrally from a withered rosette of leaves (i.e., primary leaves borne on the stem); anthers 0.8–1.2 (–1.5) mm long; stipules lobed; achenes 1.2–1.8 mm long
Stems arising laterally to a persistent basal rosette of leaves (i.e., primary leaves basal); anthers 0.7–0.9 mm long; stipules entire; achenes 1–1.2 mm long

c1.text: Terminal tooth of leaflets commonly less than half as wide as adjacent teeth and surpassed by them [Fig. ]; leaflets usually petiolulate; petals 7–10 (–12) mm long; achenes embedded in the surface of the fruiting receptacle; inflorescence resembling a corymb

Terminal tooth of leaflets commonly more than half as wide as adjacent teeth and surpassing them; leaflets usually sessile or nearly so; petals 4–7 mm long; achenes not or only slightly embedded in the surface of the fruiting receptacle; inflorescence resembling a raceme or panicle
This genus contains exactly one species.
This genus contains exactly one species.
This genus contains exactly one species.

Styles connate (though sometimes becoming distinct, in part, in age), the stigmas conspicuously exserted 3–6 mm from the orifice of the hypanthium and ± equaling the height of the stamens [Fig. ]; inflorescences (1–) 3- to 30-flowered; stems climbing or scrambling

Styles distinct (though often closely connivent), the stigmas barely to slightly exserted beyond the orifice of the hypanthium (i.e., up to 2 mm) and shorter than the stamens; inflorescences 1- to 6 (–15)-flowered; stems erect to arched

c2.text: Leaflets 30–70 (–90) ×10–40 mm, numbering 3 or 5 (–7) per leaf; petals (10–) 20–30 mm long
Leaflets 8–30 (–45) ×8–25 mm, numbering (5–) 7 or 9 (–11) per leaf; petals 7–15 (–20) mm long

c3.text: Petals pink, fading toward white prior to falling; styles glabrous; leaf blades firm-herbaceous to subcoriaceous, dull to sublustrous adaxially, deciduous
Petals white; styles pubescent; leaf blades coriaceous, lustrous adaxially, evergreen or partly evergreen

c4.text: Stipules fimbriately or pectinately toothed; styles glabrous; leaflets oblong or elliptic to obovate, herbaceous, deciduous
Stipules dentate; styles pubescent; leaflets suborbicular to broad-ovate or broad-obovate, firm, sometimes partly evergreen

c5.text: Flowers solitary at the tips of branches (rarely in pairs or trios); peduncle borne from the axil of a leaf but without additional bracts; stems often provided with abundant prickles and bristles (i.e., prickles evidently varying in thickness)

Flowers solitary or 2–6 and arranged in a corymb; peduncle and/or pedicels bracteate [Fig. ]; stems unarmed or provided with sparse to abundant prickles, when prickles abundant, then of relatively uniform thickness (except in R. rugosa , but then the prickle bases pubescent)
