c1.text: This genus contains exactly one species.
Roots tuberous, carrot-shaped; leaf blades narrow-lanceolate to elliptic-lanceolate or oblong-lanceolate (i.e., usually widest at or below the middle); stems erect, 20–50 cm tall; sepals linear
Roots not tuberous, relatively slender; leaf blades oblanceolate to obovate or spatulate (i.e., widest above the middle) [Fig. ]; stems decumbent, 15–40 cm tall; sepals lanceolate
Leaf blades crenate-serrate on the distal portion [Fig. ], ciliate with stout, white hairs along the margin; petals erect at base
Leaf blades entire to obscurely crenate near apex, not or only sparingly ciliate short, blunt, white hairs; petals ascending at the base
Leaves tending to be alternate (but subopposite, opposite, and whorled leaves may also be present on a plant) [Fig. ]; anthers yellow; cymes rounded at the apex
Leaves tending to be opposite (but alternate and whorled leaves may also be present on a plant); anthers violet to purple; cymes relatively flat-topped

c2.text: Flowers with white to green-white petals, 0–10 stamens, and 0–5 carpels; stamens slightly shorter than to ± equaling the petals in length; leaf blades serrate to crenate-serrate
Flowers with pink to purple petals, 10 stamens, and 5 carpels; stamens longer than the petals; leaf blades entire to undulate-dentatate (infrequently crenate-serrate)

c1.text: This genus contains exactly one species.
Stem leaves 1 or none; basal leaf blades rounded to obtuse at the apex; petals light green-yellow, 3–5 mm long; pedicels 1–5 mm long
Stem leaves 2–4; basal leaf blades obtuse to acute at the apex; petals white, 1.8–2.2 mm long; pedicels 1–2 mm long

c2.text: Stem leaves 2, opposite, positioned below the lowest flower
Stems leaves 4, alternate, the uppermost one subtending a flower

c1.text: Leaves opposite and borne on a stem, closely imbricate; petals purple
Leaves alternate or ± all basal [Fig. ], those borne on a stem not closely imbricate; petals white or yellow

c2.text: Primary leaves with orbicular to reniform blades that have 3–7 palmately arranged, tooth like lobes and are borne on evident petioles [Fig. ]
Primary leaves with narrow-oblong or lanceolate to to obovate or obovate-oblong blades, entire or toothed, sessile or tapering to the base [Fig. ]

c3.text: Upper leaves with vegetative bulbils in their axils; inflorescence a solitary, terminal flower; petals 6–10 mm long; stems solitary or a few together, 8–20 cm tall
Upper leaves without vegetative bulbils; inflorescence of 1–4 flowers; petals 3–5 mm long; stems cespitose, 2–10 cm tall

c4.text: Leaf blades entire, without a conspicuous, lime-encrusted pores; petals yellow, often orange-dotted
At least the larger leaf blades toothed, each tooth with a conspicuous, white, lime-encrusted pore [Fig. ]; petals white, without orange dots

c1.text: Inflorescence with usually a single, terminal flower, the lower flowers modified into vegetative bulbils; ovary superior, the hypanthium not adnate to the carpels; leaf blades toothed only near apex
Inflorescence with normal, petal-bearing flowers throughout [Fig. ]; ovary partly inferior, the hypanthium adnate to the base of the carpels; leaf blades often toothed throughout much of the margin

c2.text: Leaf blades (5–) 10–20 (–30) cm long; stems 30–100 cm tall; sepals soon reflexed; petals green-white to purple; plants of wet, low ground
Leaf blades (0.8–) 1–5 (–8) cm long; stems 5–40 cm tall; sepals ascending to spreading; petals white; plants of rocky woods, ledges, and cliffs

c1.text: This genus contains exactly one species.
This genus contains exactly one species.
Stigmas filiform, elongate-tapering, much taller than wide [Fig. ]; fruit a pyxis, circumscissile near the base
Stigmas capitate, dilated near the apex, not or only slightly taller than wide; fruit a utricle or an irregularly rupturing capsule

c2.text: Perianth mostly 4-merous; lobes of the calyx obtuse at the apex; infrastaminal scales bifid and lacking a fringe; seeds ca. 1.5 mm long
Perianth mostly 5-merous [Fig. ]; lobes of the calyx acute at the apex [Fig. ]; infrastaminal scales simple and fringed; seeds up to 1.3 mm long

c3.text: Connate portion of the calyx gold-yellow, lustrous, and with a prominent cellular-reticulate pattern; calyx lobes terminated by a short, fleshy, cylindrical appendage
Connate portion of the calyx not gold-yellow, dull, without a prominent cellular-reticulate pattern; calyx lobes not terminated by a cylindral appendage

c4.text: Sepals distinct; flowers subtended by 3–5 imbricate bracts; seeds (1.9–) 2–2.6 mm long
Sepals connate at the base; flowers not individually provided with bracts; seeds 0.9–2.2 mm long

c5.text: All or many flowers with a 4-merous corolla [Fig. ]
Flowers with a 5-merous corolla [Fig. ]

c6.text: Corolla lobes obtuse or rounded at the apex; tips of the calyx lobes not reaching the sinuses between the corolla lobes
Corolla lobes acute to acuminate at the apex; tips of the calyx lobes reaching or surpassing the sinuses between the corolla lobes

c7.text: Calyx lobes obtuse at the apex; corolla lobes relatively smooth, not granulate-textured, the tip of lobes erect or ascending; pedicels absent or shorter than the flowers; marcescent corolla persistent around the base of the fruit

Calyx lobes acute at the apex; corolla lobes appearing granulate-textured due to thickened outer cells, the tip of lobes inflexed [Fig. ]; pedicels usually as long or longer than the flowers; marcescent corolla forming a cap over the fruit (though sometimes falling off early)

c8.text: Flowers 2–5.3 mm long; infrastaminal scales adnate to the connate portion of the corolla for to (rarely ) of their length, subspathulate to spathulate in outline, rarely 2- or 3-lobed, rounded to truncate at the apex, with (6–) 20–35 (–50) fimbria; dried capsules brown-yellow to light brown, somewhat translucent, 0.8–1.5 times as long as wide, with scarcely depressed suture lines beteen the 2 carpels (in part)

Flowers 1.7–2.6 (–3) mm long; infrastaminal scales united with the connate portion of the corolla for most of their length, oblong, bifid with 1–3 fimbria on each side of the filament attachment (rarely truncate and with 3–6 fimbria); dried capsules brown, opaque, 1.6–2.4 times as long as wide, with depressed suture lines between the carpels that form a groove on each side of the fruit

c9.text: Corolla lobes obtuse at apex, not inflexed at the tip [Fig. ]; tips of the calyx lobes not reaching the sinuses between the corolla lobes (except in var. latiflora ); fruit globose to ovoid to conical; stylopodium present

Corolla lobes acute at apex, usually inflexed at the tip [Fig. ]; tips of the calyx lobes ± reaching or slightly surpassing the sinuses between the corolla lobes (usually not reaching the sinuses in C. indecora ); fruit usually globose to depressed-globose; stylopodium absent

c10.text: Calyx lobes acute to narrow-obtuse at apex; corolla lobes erect to ascending; flowers with a faint sweet smell in life; marcescent corolla calyptrate (i.e., forming a cap over the fruit, eventually detaching at base and pushed off like a lid) (in part)
Calyx lobes broad-obtuse at apex; corolla lobes spreading to reflexed; flowers inodorous in life; marcescent corolla persistent around the base of the fruit

c11.text: Calyx lobes ovate-triangular, not or scarcely overlapping at base (except in some newly opened flowers), thus the calyx ± circular when viewed from above; flowers (1.9–) 2.1–3.6 mm long; anthers (0.3–) 0.4–0.5 mm long; seeds 1.1–1.5 mm long

Calyx lobes broad-ovate to rhombic, broadly overlapping at base, protruding to form angles (note: this most visible on mature flowers, it is often obscured in fruit), thus the calyx 5-angled when viewed from above; flowers 1.4–2.1 (–2.5) mm long; anthers 0.25–0.3 (–0.35) mm long; seeds 0.9–1.1 mm long

c1.text: Corolla usually red (but white and yellow forms are known), ± salverform with an elongate, narrow, tube-like, basal connate portion; stamens and style exserted from the corolla
Corolla blue to purple or pink to white, funnelform to nearly campanulate [Fig. ], the basal connate portion expanding from below the middle; stamens and style not exserted from corolla [Fig. ]

c2.text: Leaf blade pinnately divided into 11–31 linear segments; sepals obtuse to short-apiculate, lacking prolonged awns
Leaf blade entire to lobed with 3–7 lanceolate to ovate lobes, but not divided; sepals with evident, elongate, terminal or subterminal awns

c3.text: Calyx (5–) 6–8 (–9) mm long; fruits reflexed
Calyx 4–4.5 mm long; fruits erect

c4.text: Stigmas 3-lobed; ovary 3-locular; sepals conspicuously hirsute on the basal half
Stigmas 2-lobed or entire; ovary 2-locular; sepals glabrous or sparsely villous on the basal half

c5.text: Leaf blades usually entire; sepals 10–15 mm long, acute to acuminate at apex
Leaf blades usually 3-lobed [Fig. ]; sepals 15–25 mm long, with a linear, spreading to recurved tip

c6.text: Corolla abaxially white below, the limb usually blue to blue-purple (fading to red-purple)
Corolla abaxially white throughout (rarely pink to pale purple)

c7.text: Corolla white (rarely pink to pale purple), 10–23 mm long; sepals 10–15 mm long, acuminate at the apex, often abrubtly so, hirsute-ciliate along the margin
Corolla white with a red to purple center, 50–80 mm long; sepals 13–20 mm long, obtuse or rounded at the apex, eciliate

c1.text: Stems erect, only the tip twining; leaf blades broad-cuneate to subcordate at the base; leaves subtending the flowers with petioles less than 50% of the length of the leaf midvein, those of the basal portion of the plant conspicuously reduced; bracts subtending the calyx cuneate at the base

Stems twining or trailing; leaf blades sagittate to hastate at the base; leaves subtending the flowers with petioles more than 50% of the length of the leaf midvein, those of the basal portion of the plant only slightly reduced; bracts subtending the calyx rounded to cordate at the base

c2.text: Sinus of leaf blade usually rectangular, the leaf tissue not beginning on the interior of the basal lobes for 2–5 (–10) mm from the petiole attachment [Fig. ]; bracteoles rounded to obtuse at apex, saccate at the base [Fig. ], overlapping; peduncles frequently paired at some nodes on the plant, not exceeding the leaves; corolla usually white

Sinus of leaf blade usually V-shaped or U-shaped, the leaf tissue beginning on the interior of the basal lobes 0–2 (–3) mm from the petiole attachment [Fig. ]; bracteoles long-acute to obtuse at the apex, not or slightly saccate at the base [Fig. ], not or scarcely overlapping; peduncles usually solitary, often equaling or exceeding the leaves; corolla white or pink

c3.text: Flowers usually with stamens modified into a second cycle of petals; stems pubescent; petioles of proximal leaves 1–6 cm long
Flowers not modified, with a single series of connate petals; stems glabrous or pubescent in ssp. americana ; petioles of proximal leaves (1.5–) 5–10 cm long

c1.text: This genus contains exactly one species.
This genus contains exactly one species.
Corolla purple-black, minutely pubescent on the adaxial surface, with triangular lobes 1.5–3 mm long [Fig. ]
Corolla paler, usually pink to maroon or yellow-white, glabrous, with lanceolate lobes 2.5–4.5 mm long
Leaves alternate; flowers yellow-orange to orange; latex watery
Leaves predominantly or entirely opposite or whorled; flowers white to pink, red, purple, or green; latex milky

c2.text: Corona with hoods only, the horn lacking [Fig. ]; umbels sessile or on peduncles up to 1 (–2) cm long
Corona with horns within the hoods [Figs. , ]; umbels borne on peduncles 1–10 cm long [Figs. , ]

c3.text: Leaf blades narrow-linear, 1–3 (–5) mm wide, in whorls of 3–6 (some scattered) [Fig. ]
Leaf blades narrow-lanceolate or narrow-oblong to broad-oblong, broad-elliptic, or ovate, the principal ones 20–140 mm wide, opposite or with 1 or 2 whorls of 4 leaves

c4.text: Corona hoods shorter than to ± equaling the height of the gynostegium, with conspicuously exserted horns [Fig. ]
Corona hoods taller than the gynostegium, the horns shorter than to equaling the length of the hoods [Fig. ]

c5.text: Corolla pink to red; corona hoods 2–3 mm long, the lateral margins upwardly divergent (i.e., not parallel), therefore, the hoods scoop-shaped; follicles on erect pedicels; stems branched or, less commonly, simple

Corolla white, green, green-purple, or pale purple; corona hoods 4–6 mm long, the lateral margins parallel, therefore, the hoods tube-shaped [Fig. ]; follicles on declined pedicels; stems usually unbranched

c6.text: Leaf blades cuneate at base, acuminate at apex, with petioles 10–20 mm long; margins of corona hoods prolonged into a short, erect tooth 1–1.5 mm long; umbels 2–4 from both the stem summit and upper nodes

Leaf blades broad-rounded to cordate at the base, obtuse to rounded at apex, sessile or with short petioles to 5 mm long [Fig. ]; margins of corona hoods not prolonged, the hood summit truncate; umbels solitary (rarely paired) from the summit of the stem [Fig. ]

c7.text: Corolla white to pink; pedicels 1–2.5 cm long; leaf blades abaxially glabrous or with hairs along the midvein
Corolla purple-green to light purple or red-purple to purple; pedicels 2–5 cm long; leaf blades abaxially tomentulose

c8.text: Stems with usually 3 or 4 leaf-bearing nodes, the upper and lower nodes with opposite leaves, the middle 1 or 2 nodes with a whorl of 4 leaves (rarely all the leaves opposite); corolla lobes 4.5–6 mm long; lateral margins of corona hoods bearing a tooth near the middle [Fig. ]; leaf blades gradually acuminate at apex; follicles on erect pedicels

Stems with 2–5 leaf-bearing nodes, all with opposite leaves; corolla lobes 7–9 mm long; lateral margins of corona hoods without a tooth; leaf blades obtuse to abruptly acuminate at apex; follicles on declined pedicels

c9.text: Corona hoods 5–7 mm long, red-purple to purple, without marginal lobes; follicles smooth; corolla red-purple to purple
Corona hoods 4–5 mm long, light purple, each with a prominent marginal lobe near the center; follicles covered with conic processes; corolla purple-green to light purple

c1.text: Leaf blades ovate to triangular-ovate, 3–7 cm long, ciliate; calyx lobes 6–12 (–15) mm long, ciliate; corolla with a connate tube 12–20 mm long expanding distally to a limb 35–50 mm wide in life

Leaf blades oblong or lanceolate to narrow-elliptic or ovate, 1.5–5 cm long, eciliate; calyx lobes 2–3 (–4) mm long, eciliate; corolla with a connate tube 8–12 mm long expanding distally to a limb 20–30 mm wide in life

c2.text: Leaf blades smooth, coriaceous, the larger ones 15–23 mm wide; flowering stems erect from creeping horizontal stems; peduncles 11–22 (–28) mm long
Leaf blades scabrous, subherbaceous, the larger ones 7–16 mm wide; flowering stems erect or arching; peduncles 20–40 mm long

c1.text: This genus contains exactly one species.
Corolla pink or white and pink-striped, 6–10 mm long, its lobes spreading or recurving [Fig. ]; flowers spreading to nodding; seeds 2.5–3 mm long; leaf blades wide-spreading to drooping
Corolla white, green-white, or yellow, 3–6 mm long, its lobes erect or slightly spreading [Fig. ]; flowers ascending to spreading; seeds 4–6 mm long; leaf blades erect to spreading
This genus contains exactly one species.
This genus contains exactly one species.
Inflorescence a raceme with (2–) 3–5 whorls of flowers; corolla 19–25 mm wide
Inflorescence consisting of a solitary, terminal umbel; corolla 8–16 mm wide

c2.text: Corolla yellow, the basal, connate portion scarcely (if at all) exceeding the calyx; calyx 9–15 mm long, angled in cross-section; leaf blades pubescent

Corolla commonly pink to purple with a yellow base, the basal, connate portion longer than the calyx; calyx 3–11 mm long, ± round in cross-section (i.e., without wing-angles); leaf blades glabrous (though sometime farinose)

c3.text: Sepals 3–6 mm long; scape 3–21 cm tall; largest leaf blades 10–40 (–60) mm long; bracts of umbel 3–6 mm long, barely (if at all) saccate at the base; capsules 2–3 mm in diameter; seeds rounded, their surface nearly smooth; flowers heterostylous

Sepals 6–9 mm long; scape 10–40 cm tall; largest leaf blades 40–80 mm long; bracts of umbel 6–14 mm long, definitely saccate at the base; capsules 2.5–5 mm in diameter; seeds angled, their surface evidently reticulate; flowers homostylous

c1.text: This genus contains exactly one species.
Petals notched at apex [Fig. ]; leaf blades stiff, with a single primary vein; stems suffrutescent

Petals entire at the apex or sometimes emarginate to shallowly notched in P. divaricata ; leaf blades herbaceous, with a midvein and several primary lateral veins (though the lateral veins often faint; with only a midvein in P. pilosa ); stems herbaceous

c2.text: Leaf blades (15–) 20–40 (–60) mm long; axillary fascicles mostly lacking; apical sinus of petal 0.25–0.5 times as long as entire petal
Leaf blades (5–) 8–20 mm long; axillary fascicles usually present and conspicuous [Fig. ]; apical sinus of petal 0.12–0.25 times as long as entire petal

c3.text: Style short, 1–4 mm long, scarcely (if at all) longer than the stigmas or the ovary; stamens and style at most reaching the midpoint of the basal, connate portion of corolla
Style elongate, (12–) 14–26 mm long, much longer than the stigmas or the ovary; stamens and style reaching at least the orifice of the basal, connate portion of corolla

c4.text: Upper leaves alternate; corolla commonly red, white, or variegated; plants annual
Upper leaves opposite; corolla usually pink, blue, light blue-purple, or light red-purple ; plants perennial

c5.text: Leaf blades linear to lanceolate or narrow-ovate, tapering to a sharp, indurate awn-tip 0.5–3 mm long; basal, connate portion of corolla usually pubescent; both the reproductive stem, as well as the sterile basal offshoots erect to ascending

Leaf blades elliptic or oblong to lanceolate or ovate, obtuse to acute at the apex, sometimes tapering to a short awn-tip up to 0.5 mm; basal, connate portion of the corolla glabrous; reproductive stem erect or decumbent at base, whereas the sterile, basal offshoots are prostrate and rooting

c6.text: Long-creeping, sterile, basal offshoots with spatulate leaf blades present at anthesis; flowering stems 10–40 (–50) cm tall; inflorescence and calyx stipitate-glandular; corolla 25–30 mm wide

Sterile, basal offshoots absent at anthesis or present and short, upcurving, and without spatulate leaf blades; flowering stems 30–200 cm tall; inflorescence and calyx glabrous or pubescent, but not glandular; corolla 12–22 mm wide

c7.text: Leaf blades ciliolate on the margin, with conspicuous lateral veins that connect near the edge to form a submarginal vein around the perimeter of the blade [Fig. ]; anthers pale yellow to white
Leaf blades eciliate on the margin, without a submarginal, connecting vein; anthers yellow

c8.text: Calyx 6–8 (–10) mm long; stems streaked or spotted with red (very rarely green throughout), arising from rhizomes, with 7–15 (or more) nodes below the inflorescence
Calyx (8.5–) 10–13 mm long; stems without red streaks or spots, arising from decumbent stems, with 3–5 nodes below the inflorescence

c1.text: This genus contains exactly one species.
Corolla 2–5 mm long; leaves with 5–15 leaflets; plants annual; stems with abundant stipitate-glands
Corolla 10–20 mm long; primary leaves with 11–29 leaflets; plants perennial; stems with few or no stipitate-glands (though eglandular hairs may be present)

c2.text: Leaflets shortly petiolulate, the petiolules mostly 0.1–1.5 mm long; stamens and style well exserted from corolla [Fig. ]
Leaflets sessile; stamens and style not or shortly exserted from corolla

c3.text: Many or all of the pedicels as long as or longer than the calyx at anthesis; larger leaves with 11–17 leaflets; lowest bracteal leaves with 9–11 leaflets, nearly as large as the stem leaves; pedicels puberulent with eglandular hairs; corolla 12–16 mm long

Most of the pedicels shorter than the calyx at anthesis; larger leaves with 19–29 leaflets; lowest bracteal leaves with 3–7 reduced and crowded leaflets, much reduced compared with the stem leaves; pedicels pubescent with glandular hairs; corolla 15–20 mm long

c1.text: This genus contains exactly one species.
Arachnoid hairs present in the leaf axils and often on the stem; capsule with 2–4 seeds
Arachnoid hairs not present on vegetative organs (though other types of hairs may be present); capsule with 10–36 seeds

c2.text: Corolla ca. 2–3 times as long as calyx, the adaxial surface of connate portion (i.e., inside the basal tube) yellow with purple spots; axis of inflorescence with minute, black stipitate glands; capsule with 16–36 seeds
Corolla ca. 1–2 times as long as calyx, the adaxial surface of connate portion light purple or white; axis of inflorescence eglandular; capsule with 10–18 seeds

c1.text: Stigmas, including the basal lobes, (1.3–) 1.5–2.3 mm long at maturity; petals oblong, rounded to obtuse at the apex and with a short, but prominent, apiculus; anthers apiculate at the apex; capsules dehiscing from the apex to a point proximal to the stigmas; stems with opposite leaves [Fig. ], the nodes becoming progressively more crowded near the base

Stigmas 0.8–1.5 mm long at maturity; petals lanceolate to oblong-lanceolate, acute at the apex and usually without a clear apiculus; anthers rounded at the apex or rarely with an apiculus in B. iodandra ; capsules dehiscing from the apex to the base of the stigmas; stems with alternate leaves, the nodes not or scarcely becoming more crowded near the base

c2.text: Petals lanceolate and acute at the apex; filaments green to yellow-brown, except sometimes near attachment of anther where purple; anthers usually yellow, 0.3–0.5 (–0.6) mm long; branches of inflorescence ascending to spreading; stems often slender and lax, usually green; calyx essentially distinct

Petals oblong-lanceolate, acute at the apex or infrequently with an obscure apiculus; filaments purple (rarely green to yellow-brown); anthers usually purple, (0.4–) 0.5–0.6 (–1) mm long; branches of inflorescence erect to strictly ascending [Fig. ]; stems stouter, strict, usually purple or tinged with purple; calyx often shortly connate near the base

c1.text: This genus contains exactly one species.
Perianth (8–) 9- to 12-merous [Fig. ]; plants perennial, with elongate rhizomes terminating in basal rosettes of leaves
Perianth (4–) 5 (–7)-merous [Fig. ]; plants annual, biennial, or perennial from a short, branched caudex

c2.text: Calyx lobes oblanceolate to spatulate (rarely linear), without a hyaline margin, 1–3 mm wide, with 3–5 distinct nerves; basal, connate portion of the calyx distinctly nerved or corrugated; plants primarily of saline and brackish marshes

Calyx lobes linear, with a thin, hyaline margin, 0.5–1.5 mm wide, with 1–3 obscure nerves; basal, connate portion of the calyx smooth or inconspicuously nerved; plants primarily of sandy and peaty pond shores of the coastal plain

c3.text: Basal, connate portion of the calyx prominently 5-nerved, each nerve rib-like and thinly membranous-winged; lateral veins of the calyx lobes developed more prominently than the midvein

Basal, connate portion of the calyx inconspicuously and/or finely nerved, the nerves neither rib-like nor thinly winged; lateral veins of calyx lobes developed equally or less prominently than the midvein

c4.text: Cyme dichasial (i.e., the axis appearing trichotomously branched because each node has two lateral branches in addition to the central axis); leaf blades of the middle and upper stem ovate to narrow-ovate, broad-rounded to cordate and often clasping at the base; stem strongly tetragonal, with conspicuous wing-angles 0.1–0.5 mm wide

Cyme monochasial (i.e., the axis appearing dichotomously branched because each node has a single, lateral branch in addition to the central axis) [Fig. ]; leaf blades of the middle and upper stem oblong or linear to oblanceolate, narrowed but not clasping at the base; stem terete or irregularly ridge-angled

c5.text: Principal leaf blades linear to oblong or narrow-oval, widest at or below the middle, broadly sessile at the base, not darkening in drying; corolla usually not or only slightly exceeding the calyx; plants perennial from a short, branched caudex, primarily of sandy and peaty pond shores of the coastal plain

Principal leaf blades elliptic to oblanceolate, widest at or above the middle, narrowly tapering to the base [Fig. ], often darkening in drying; corolla usually distinctly surpassing the calyx; plants annual, usually from fibrous roots, primarily of saline and brackish marshes

c1.text: This genus contains exactly one species.
Flowers on pedicels mostly (1.5–) 2–5 mm long; corolla lobes 2–4 mm long; plants lacking a basal rosette of leaves
Flowers sessile or subsessile; corolla lobes usually 5–6 mm long; plants with a basal rosette of leaves
This genus contains exactly one species.
This genus contains exactly one species.

Leaf blades and lobes of the calyx prominently ciliolate (note: the cilia visible at low magnification); lobes of the corolla about as long as or shorter than the appendages in the sinuses of the corolla
Leaf blades and lobes of the calyx lacking cilia or with scattered, minute cilia; lobes of the corolla 1.5–5 times as long as the appendages in the sinuses of the corolla

c2.text: Appendages in the sinuses of the corolla 2- or 3-cleft, about as long as the corolla lobes [Fig. ]; lobes of the corolla broad-rounded at the apex and about as wide as the plaits [Fig. ]; calyx lobes usually broad-lanceolate to obovate

Appendages in the sinuses of the corolla fimbriate, longer than the corolla lobes [Fig. ]; lobes of the corolla truncate and often apiculate, narrower than the plaits [Fig. ]; calyx lobes usually lanceolate to elliptic

c3.text: Involucral leaf blades ascending, linear to linear-lanceolate, 3–15 mm wide; lobes of the corolla 1.5–3 times as long as the appendages in the sinuses of the corolla; leaf blades narrow-lanceolate, dark green, not clasping at the base

Involucral leaf blades spreading, narrow-ovate to ovate, 15–30 mm wide; lobes of the corolla 3–5 times as long as the appendages in the sinuses of the corolla; leaf blades broad-lanceolate, light green, somewhat clasping at the base

c1.text: This genus contains exactly one species.
Corolla 10–15 mm long, with a fringe of hairs on the inside around the base of the lobes; lobes of the corolla 3–5 mm long, obtuse to acute at the apex
Corolla 15–23 mm long, without a fringe at the base of the lobes; lobes of the corolla 4–7 mm long, acute to acuminate at the apex
This genus contains exactly one species.

Leaves opposite throughout, the blades with inequilateral bases [Figs. , ]; stipules present [Fig. ]; involucre with 4 glands that possess petaloid appendages; plants annual, with prostrate to wide-spreading stems (upright in E. nutans )

Leaves of the stem alternate (opposite in E. dentata , E. ipecacuanhae , and E. lathyris ), the blades with equilateral bases, those subtending the cyathiescence whorled (regularly opposite in E. dentata and E. ipecacuanhae , and sometimes opposite in E. marginata ); stipules absent (present in E. marginata ); involucre with 1–4 glands that lack petaloid appendages or with 5 glands that possess petaloid appendages; plants annual or perennial, with ascending to erect stems

c2.text: Leaf blades with entire margins [Fig. ]; seeds 2–2.6 mm long (mostly 0.9-1 mm long in C. serpens ), with ± smooth faces; glands with very small or obsolete appendages
Leaf blades with serrate or partially serrate margins; seeds 0.9–1.6 mm long, with finely wrinkled or ridged faces; glands with small, but evident, appendages

c3.text: Leaf blades broad-oblong to suborbicular, 2–7 mm long; stipules united into a white, scale-like structure that is usually fringed or lobed near apex; capsules 1–1.5 mm long
Leaf blades narrow-oblong to lanceolate-oblong [Fig. ], 8–15 mm long; stipules distinct, usually colored similar to the stem, particularly in the basal of the stipule; capsules 3–3.5 mm long

c4.text: Leaves and stems glabrous; faces of the seed with 2–4 prominent, transverse ridges (smooth to obscurely marked in E. serpyllifolia )
Leaves (at least when young) and stems pubescent [Fig. ]; faces of the seed merely wrinkled or with 3 or 4 prominent, transverse ridges in E. prostrata

c5.text: Faces of the seed with 2–4 prominent, transverse ridges; each cyathium with 1–5 stamens; involucres 0.6–0.9 mm in diameter
Faces of seed smooth or obscurely roughened or pitted; each cyathium with 5–12 (–18) stamens; involucres 0.8–1.2 mm in diameter

c6.text: Ovary and capsule pubescent [Fig. ]
Ovary and capsule glabrous

c7.text: Styles 0.3–0.4 mm long, divided in the apical to ; capsules appressed-puberulent; seeds obtusely angled, usually finely wrinked with inconspicuous transverse ridges on each face
Styles 0.2–0.3 mm long, divided nearly to the base; capsules spreading-villous, at least on the angles; seeds acutely angled, with 3 or 4 prominent transverse ridges on each face

c8.text: Stems prostrate to wide-spreading, usually branched from the base, rather uniformly spreading-hirsute with hairs 0.5–1.5 mm long
Stems ascending to suberect, usually unbranched in the lower portion, puberulent on the younger portions with incurved hairs up to 0.3 mm long, the hairs sometimes confined to a longitudinal strip

c9.text: Leaves of the stem all or mostly all opposite and dentate; cyathiescence irregularly clustered near the apex of the stem, without evident, umbel-like branches; involucre with a solitary gland (rarely more)
Leaves of the stem alternate and entire in most species, never both opposite and toothed; cyathiescence with umbel-like branches; involucre with 4 or 5 glands

c10.text: Involucre with 5 (rarely 4) glands, the glands with evident, white (rarely green), petaloid appendages (the petal appendages small in E. ipecacuanhae ) [Fig. ]
Involucre with 4 glands, these without petaloid appendages

c11.text: Petaloid appendages 0.05–0.6 mm long, shorter than wide, usually green; stems 1.5–3 dm tall
Petaloid appendages (0.5–) 1–4.4 mm long, as long as wide or longer, usually white [Fig. ]; stems 3–10 dm tall

c12.text: Leaves of the cyathiescence white on the margin or entirely white, those of the stem with broad-ovate to elliptic or obovate-oblong blades that are acute at the apex; stems and involucres pubescent; plants annual, with stipules
Leaves of the cyathiescence green, those of the stem with linear to elliptic blades that are obtuse at the apex; stems and involucres glabrous or pubescent; plants perennial, without stipules

c13.text: Leaves of the stem opposite; seeds 4–6 mm long
Leaves of the stem alternate [Fig. ]; seeds 1.2–2.5 mm long

c14.text: Leaf blades serrulate; glands of the involucre orbicular to elliptic
Leaf blades entire; glands of the involucre crescent-shaped, the concave surface facing outwards, often narrowed to horn-like ends

c15.text: Leaf blades blunt or retuse at the apex, cuneate at the base; capsules smooth on the outer surface; seeds conspicuously aereolate-patterned
Leaf blades ± acute at the apex, the upper ones broad-based; capsules verrucose on the outer surface; seeds smooth or very obscurely reticulate-patterned

c16.text: Umbel-like cyathiescence with 3–5 primary branches; plants annual; involucre 1–2 mm tall
Umbel-like cyathiescence with usually 7–17 primary branches; plants perennial from rhizomes; involucre 2.5–3 mm tall

c17.text: Leaf blades of the stem 1–3 ×0.1–0.3 cm [Fig. ]; seeds 1.5–2 mm long; plants 15–40 cm tall
Leaf blades of the stem 3–8 ×0.4–0.8 cm; seeds 2–2.5 mm long; plants 30–70 (–80) cm tall

c18.text: Leaf blades oblanceolate to obovate or obovate-elliptic, 7–15 (–22) mm wide, 3–5 (–6) times as long as wide, usually widest above the middle and tapering to the base, obtuse to emarginate at the apex, of relatively thinner texture; terminal cyathiescence with usually 8–17 primary branches; axillary cyathiescences usually numbering 8–20

Leaf blades linear to lanceolate, 3–10 mm wide, 6–15 times as long as wide, widest below the middle and sometimes widened and rounded at the base, acute to subacute at the apex, of relatively firmer texture; terminal cyathiescence with usually 5–9 primary branches; axillary cyathiescences usually numbering 2–12

c1.text: Each of the 3 styles divided nearly to the base into 4 or more branches; staminate flowers without petals; plants dioecious
Each of the 3 styles dichotomously branched 2 or 3 times; staminate flowers with 5 petals; plants monoecious
This genus contains exactly one species.

Leaf blades linear to narrow-oblong; petioles 2–14 mm long, 9–25 (–30)% as long as the leaf blade; carpellate bracts sparsely to densely beset with sessile, red glands, toothed with triangular to ovate teeth 8–28% as long as the bract

Leaf blades broad-lanceolate to ovate; petioles 7–70 mm long, (23–) 33–89% as long as the leaf blade; carpellate bracts lacking sessile, red glands (though usually with stipitate glands), toothed with linear to lanceolate teeth 21–75% as long as the bract

c2.text: Carpellate bracts with 5–9 lobes, stipitate-glandular, without long, eglandular hairs [Fig. ]; stems usually without long, eglandular hairs; petioles 34–89% as long as the leaf blades, the petioles of the larger leaves commonly more than as long as the blades

Carpellate bracts with 9–15 lobes, hirsute with long, eglandular hairs, short stipitate glands may also be present; stems usually hirsute with long, eglandular hairs; petioles 23–66% as long as the leaf blades

c1.text: This genus contains exactly one species.
This genus contains exactly one species.
Plants annual; achenes light brown, obtuse at the apex, with an apical mucro; tepals 1.5–2 mm long, shorter than the bracts
Plants perennial; achenes dark brown, acute at the apex, without an apical mucro; tepals mostly 2–3.5 mm long, longer than the bracts

Stipules 5–15 mm long, erect; staminate and carpellate flowers usually in separate inflorescences; inflorescence exceeding the length of the petioles of the subtending leaves; plants perennial from rhizomes

Stipules 1–3 mm long, spreading to deflexed; staminate and carpellate flowers usually in the same inflorescence; inflorescence often shorter than the length of the petioles of the subtending leaves; plants annual from a taproot
This genus contains exactly one species.

Achenes 1–1.5 mm wide, dark purple to purple-black except for a narrow, pale, marginal band, with raised, rounded tubercles on the surface [Fig. ]; leaf blades relatively less lustrous and less translucent
Achenes 0.6–1.1 mm wide, largely green to yellow-green, often also with slightly raised purple marks [Fig. ]; leaf blades relatively more lustrous and more translucent
This genus contains exactly one species.
This genus contains exactly one species.
Stipules 2.5–8 mm long; calyx 3.5–5 mm long, each lobe tipped by a prominent awn 0.9–2 mm long; flowers concealed by conspicuous white bracts; plants perennial
Stipules 0.5–3 mm long; calyx 1–3 mm long, each lobe with a tiny apiculus or short awn up to 0.3 mm long; flowers not concealed by bracts; plants annual

c2.text: Stems glabrous; calyx 1–1.5 mm long, the lobes terminated by an inconspicuous apiculus; mature fruit noticeably exceeding the calyx
Stems puberulent; calyx 2–3 mm long, the lobes terminated by a minute awn; mature fruit not or only shortly exceeding the calyx

c1.text: Sepals glabrous or short-ciliate; leaf blades glabrous
Sepals densely pubescent; leaf blades pubescent
This genus contains exactly one species.

Seeds subglobose, sometimes with an equatorial keel or wing up to 0.1 mm wide; flowers with usually 10 stamens; leaf blades revolute, appearing terete in cross-section at low magnification, 15–30 (–50) mm long
Seeds compressed, with a prominent equatorial wing 0.2–0.6 mm wide; flowers with 5 or 10 stamens; leaf blades flat or weakly revolute, 3–15 (–20) mm long

c2.text: Petals lanceolate, ± acute at the apex, generally not contiguous in intact flowers; flowers with usually 5 stamens; equatorial wing of seed white to light brown, (0.3–) 0.4–0.6 mm wide, approximately as wide as the seed body

Petals ovate, narrowly rounded to obtuse at the apex, generally contiguous in intact flowers; flowers with usually 10 stamens; equatorial wing of seed light brown to brown-black (rarely white), 0.2–0.3 (–0.5) mm wide, narrower than the seed body [Fig. ]

c1.text: Seeds 0.4–0.6 mm long, without an equatorial wing; flowers with 6–10 stamens [Fig. ]; plants with evident fascicles of leaves in the axils
Seeds 0.6–1.4 mm long, with or without an equatorial wing; flowers with (1–) 2–4 (–5) stamens; plants without fascicles of leaves in the axils or these sparse and poorly developed

c2.text: Leaf blades obtuse to acute at the apex, but without a minute mucro; seeds 0.8–1.4 mm long, shiny, smooth or with irregular reticulate thickenings on the faces, usually with a ± white, erose, equatorial wing 0.2–0.3 mm wide [Fig. ]; stipules 1–2.8 mm long; pedicels and sepals usually glabrous

Leaf blades minutely mucronate at the apex; seeds 0.6–0.8 mm long, dull, smooth or minutely glandular-papillose on the faces, usually unwinged [Fig. ]; stipules 2–4 mm long; pedicels and sepals usually stipitate-glandular

c1.text: Sepals acute at the apex [Fig. ], spreading to erect in fruit, separate, with a narrow, white-scarious margin up to 0.1 mm wide [Fig. ]; floral bracts equaling or exceeding than flowers
Sepals obtuse to rounded at apex, usually introrse in fruit and overlapping, with a broader white-scarious margin 0.3–0.5 mm wide; floral bracts mostly shorter than flowers
At least the lower leaves with evident petioles; stems pubescent in 1 or 2 lines [Fig. ]
All the leaves sessile; stems glabrous or minutely scabrous (sometimes apically hispidulous in S. holostea )

c2.text: Sepals (3.5–) 4.5–5 (–6) mm long; leaf blades 3–25 mm long; capsules shortly exceeding the persistent sepals
Sepals (7.5–) 8–11 mm long; leaf blades 10–100 mm long; capsules shorter than the persistent sepals

c3.text: Bracts subtending the pedicels herbaceous and green throughout [Fig. ]; inflorescence either of flowers in the axils of normal foliage leaves or at branches in the stem or the inflorescence a terminal cyme
Bracts subtending the flowers either wholly scarious or with only a central green strip [Fig. ]; inflorescence usually a terminal cyme [Fig. ]

c4.text: Sepals 6–8 mm long; petals 8–12 mm long, conspicuously exceeding the sepals (the petals rarely absent); seeds 1.5–2 mm long, coarsely papillose
Sepals 2–5 mm long; petals 1–6 mm long, shorter than or barely exceeding the sepals (petals sometimes absent) [Fig. ]; seeds 0.7–1 mm long, smooth or obscurely marked or roughened

c5.text: Leaf blades 4–15 ×1–5 mm, fleshy, many of the axils bearing sterile tufts or branchlets; capsules slightly shorter than to equaling the length of the persistent sepals; plants halophytic
Leaf blades 7–60 ×2–8 mm, not fleshy, usually without sterile tufts or branchlets; capsules much longer than the persistent sepals; plants not halophytic

c6.text: Cymes produced in the axils of leaves; sepals 2.5–3.5 mm long; petals shorter than the sepals (or the petals absent); seeds 0.3–0.7 mm long
Cymes produced at the apex of the stem; sepals 2–7 mm long; petals nearly as long as or longer than the sepals; seeds 0.7–1.2 mm long

c7.text: Stems smooth; sepals conspicuously 3-veined, 3–7 mm long; leaf blades narrow-lanceolate to elliptic-lanceolate, usually widest below the middle; seeds coarsely rugose-tuberculate

Stems papillate-scabrous on the angles; sepals obscurely 3-veined, 2–4 mm long; leaf blades linear to oblanceolate or narrow-elliptic, usually widest at or above the middle; seeds obscurely sculpted, nearly smooth

c1.text: Petals 3–4.5 mm long, ca. 2 times as long as the sepals [Fig. ]; upper leaf axils of stem usually bearing fascicles of minute, succulent leaves
Petals 0.75–2.5 (–3) mm long, shorter than to shortly exceeding the sepals [Fig. ], or the petals absent; upper stem lacking axillary fascicles of leaves

c2.text: Sepals 4 per flower (rarely some flowers with 5) [Fig. ], spreading in fruit; plants perennial, with basal rosettes of narrow leaves (at least on younger plants), completely glabrous

Sepals 5 per flower (rarely some flowers with 4), erect in fruit; plants annual (rarely short-lived perennial in S. maxima ), usually without basal rosettes of leaves, at least the sepals and apical portion of pedicels stipitate-glandular (infrequently glabrous throughout in S. decumbens )

c3.text: Leaf blades herbaceous; seeds light brown, obliquely triangular in outline, with an abaxial groove; capsules broad-ellipsoid prior to dehiscence, with relatively thin valves
Leaf blades somewhat succulent; seeds red-brown or dark brown, reniform to globose, plump, lacking an abaxial groove; capsules globose prior to dehiscence, with relatively thick valves

c4.text: Seeds dark brown, conspicuously tuberculate with magnification; sepals 2–2.5 mm long; petals 1–2 mm long; capsules 2.5–3 mm long
Seeds red-brown, smooth or inconspicuously tuberculate; sepals (2–) 2.5–3.5 mm long; petals 2–2.5 (–3) mm long; capsules (3–) 3.5–4.5 mm long

c1.text: Plants perennial, with sprawling stems that root at the nodes or with rhizomes and axillary shoots that produce overwintering leaves
Plants annual, usually from taproots, lacking stolons, rhizomes, and axillary shoots

c2.text: Stems and leaf blades densely white-tomentose, the surfaces ± concealed by tomentum
Stems and leaf blades pubescent with villous hairs (rarely the stems subglabrous), the surfaces visible

c3.text: Petals 5–7 mm long, ± equal in length to the sepals; axillary shoots usually lacking; eglandular or occasionally with stipitate glands confined to the inflorescence

Petals 7.5–15 mm long, ca. 2 times as long as the sepals [Fig. ]; axillary clusters of leaves or short shoots produced on lower stem; plants stipitate-glandular in the inflorescence and often also on the upper portion of the stem

c4.text: Petals 7.5–9 (–9.5) mm long; sepals 3.5–6 (–7) mm long; anthers 0.8–0.9 (–1.1) mm long; reproductive stems 5–20 (–30) cm tall; plants growing in pristine as well as human-disturbed habitats
Petals 10–15 mm long; sepals 5–8 mm long; anthers 0.9–1.2 (–1.5) mm long; reproductive stems (15–) 25–35 (–40) cm tall; plants mainly from human-disturbed habitats

c5.text: Flowers usually 4-merous throughout (very rarely 5-merous); capsules usually dehiscing by 8 apical teeth (by 10 teeth in 5-merous flowers)
Flowers 5-merous, with 5 or 10 stamens; capsules dehiscing by 10 apical teeth

c6.text: Sepals and often the bracts apically with long, forward-pointing, white, eglandular hairs that potrude beyond the apex
Sepals and bracts lacking elongate, eglandular hairs that protrude beyond the apex

c7.text: Bracts of inflorescence herbaceous throughout, lacking a scarious margin; leaf blades (10–) 15–50 (–60) mm long; androecium with usually 10 stamens (often only 5 in apetalous forms)
Bracts of inflorescence with a translucent, scarious, distal margin and tip; leaf blades 5–18 mm long; androecium with usually 5 stamens

c8.text: Veins of petals unbranched; petals shorter than the sepals, only slightly notched, the apical sinus up to 0.5 (–1) mm deep [Fig. ]; bracts with a broad scarious margin and apex
Veins of petals branched; petals equaling or shortly surpassing the sepals, prominently notched, the apical sinus 1–1.5 mm deep; bracts with a narrow scarious margin and apex

c1.text: This genus contains exactly one species.
This genus contains exactly one species.
This genus contains exactly one species.
Sepals 3–6 mm long, acute to acuminate at the apex; leaf blades glabrous, acute to acuminate (rarely obtuse) at the apex; seeds 1.3–1.6 mm long
Sepals 2–3 mm long, obtuse to subacute at the apex; leaf blades ciliate, obtuse to subacute at the apex; seeds 1–1.3 (–1.4) mm long
This genus contains exactly one species.
Sepals nerveless or obscurely nerved
Sepals with 3 or 5 strong, longitudinal ribs

c2.text: Leaf blades rigid, triangular in cross-section; stem usually glandular-pubescent above; sepals ovate to broad-ovate; petals entire at apex
Leaf blades soft, flat; stem glabrous; sepals oblong to oblong-ovate; petals slightly retuse at apex

c3.text: Plants perennial, forming small mats, with often dense, sterile, leafy shoots at the base of the plant, found usually in alpine settings at or above 1000 m elevation
Plants annual, not forming mats, lacking sterile, leafy shoots at the base of the plant, found usually on acidic ridges, balds, and outcrops well below 1000 m elevation

c4.text: Sepals herbaceous, rounded at apex [Fig. ]; lower portion of branches densely clothed by coriaceous, marcescent leaves; capsules 6–10 mm long, with valves that are emarginate at the apex
Sepals rigid, acute at apex; leaves deciduous or marcescent, but not densely clothing the lower portion of branches; capsules 3–5 mm long, with valves that are entire at apex

c5.text: Tufts of leaves produced in the axils of the principal leaves; leaf blades with the midvein more prominent than the lateral veins; petals 5–8 mm long, longer than the sepals; seeds 0.8–1.5 mm long
Axillary leaves not produced; leaf blades with 3 ± equally prominent veins; petals 2–4.2 mm long, usually shorter than the sepals; seeds 0.4–0.7 mm long

c1.text: This genus contains exactly one species.
Plants dioecious, the carpellate flowers with 5 styles and the staminate flowers with 1 style; capsules dehiscing by 5 valves, each valve usually splitting again
Plants synoecious, the flowers with 3 (rarely 4) styles; capsules dehiscing by 3 valves that eventually split again (rarely 4 valves that split again)

c2.text: Flowers with white petals, fragrant, opening in the evening; leaf blades oblong-lanceolate to elliptic, 6–30 mm wide; carpophore 1–2 mm long; capsules ovoid, the valves erect or slightly recurved after dehiscence; seeds coarsely tuberculate

Flowers with red petals, inodorous, opening during the day; leaf blades ovate to elliptic, 10–50 mm wide; carpophore absent; capsules broad-ovoid to subglobose, the valves recurved after dehiscence; seeds densely and uniformly papillose

c3.text: Plants matted, pulvinate, alpine, 3–6 cm tall [Fig. ]; flowers solitary at the tips of branches; petals purple
Plants upright, simple or branched, but not matted, of low-elevation habitats, 8–150 cm tall; flowers solitary in the axils of leaves or in terminal cymes; petals white to pink to red (rarely purple)

c4.text: Flowers solitary on peduncles from the axils of the upper leaves
Flowers in a terminal cyme

c5.text: Inflorescence a monochasial cyme, appearing as a secund raceme [Fig. ]
Inflorescence a dichasial cyme (note: the cyme sometimes panicle-like) [Fig. ]

c6.text: Axis of the inflorescence commonly forking; petals lobed to below the middle; stems coarse, 20–100 cm tall
Axis of the inflorescence usually simple; petals retuse or lobed nearly to the middle; stems shorter, 15–45 cm tall

c7.text: Calyx 7–10 mm long in fruit, pubescent with both short, glandular hairs and longer eglandular hairs, the lobes acute at the apex; petals entire to retuse at the apex; flowers erect to ascending; stems erect
Calyx 12–18 mm long in fruit, pubescent with only short, glandular hairs, the lobes obtuse at the apex; petals lobed nearly to the middle; flowers divergent or nodding; stems procumbent to ascending

c8.text: Calyx glabrous (or sometimes minutely pubescent near the base)
Calyx pubescent, especially on the nerves [Fig. ]

c9.text: Stems glutinous below the nodes; calyx fitting rather tightly over the capsule, 10-nerved; plants annual
Stems not glutinous; calyx inflated, fitting loosely over the body of the capsule, 20-nerved; plants biennial or perennial (rarely annual in S. csereii )

c10.text: Calyx with 20 obscure veins of equal length connected by many, smaller, anastomosing veins, 12–18 mm long in fruit; filaments pale for much of their length, sometimes purple near the apex; seeds ± black, 1–1.5 mm long, finely tuberculate
Calyx with 10 long veins and 10 short veins, with few or no anastomosing veins, 9–13 mm long in fruit; filaments dark purple; seeds 0.6–1 mm long, gray-brown, with concentric rings of papillae

c11.text: Stem leaves mostly in whorls of 4 (the lower and upper nodes may have opposite leaves); petals fimbriately lobed into 8–12 apical segments
Stem leaves opposite throughout; petals entire, retuse, or notched at the apex

c12.text: Petals entire or merely retuse at the apex; calyx lobes rounded to obtuse at apex; plants 8–20 (–25) cm tall; seeds 1.3–1.5 mm long, papillose
Petals with a prominent notch, creating a 2-lobed apex; calyx lobes acute to attenuate at apex; plants (15–) 20–80 cm tall; seeds 0.6–1 mm long, tuberculate

c13.text: Calyx with ca. 30 longitudinal nerves [Fig. ], umbilicate at the base in fruit
Calyx with 10 nerves, not umbilicate at base

c14.text: Calyx 15–24 mm long in flower, becoming 25–30 (–40) mm long in fruit; petals pink on the adaxial surface, yellow on the abaxial surface, opening at night, with auricles 1–1.5 mm long; leaf blades lanceolate to narrow-ovate, 20–40 mm wide; plants not clumped, annual
Calyx 7–10 mm long; petals white or pink, open during the day, with inconspicuous auricles; leaf blades narrow-lanceolate to oblanceolate, 5–15 mm wide; plants subcespitose, perennial

c1.text: This genus contains exactly one species.
Plants densely tomentose; calyx lobes twisted; inflorescence with mostly 3–7 flowers
Plants glabrous to pubescent but not tomentose; calyx lobes planar, not twisted; inflorescence with mostly 5–26 flowers

c2.text: Stems pubescent with long hairs, some hairs longer than 1.5 mm, with mostly 10–20 pairs of lanceolate to ovate leaf blades 20–60 mm wide; petals with 2 apical lobes
Stems glabrous or pubescent with short hairs, the hairs shorter than 1 mm, with mostly 2–5 pairs of linear to lanceolate leaf blades 4–15 (–30) mm wide; petals cleft into 4 lobes [Fig. ]

c1.text: This genus contains exactly one species.
Inflorescence a dense, head-like cyme of (1–) 3–7 flowers at the stem summit; bracts brown-scarious, broad-ovate, ± enclosing the 10–13 mm long calyx
Inflorescence a solitary flower (rarely up to 3 flowers) at the tips of branches; bracts of inflorescence herbaceous, narrow-ovate, enclosing up to 50% of the 3–6 mm long calyx
Plants with scattered, solitary flowers borne on slender pedicels 10–40 mm long [Fig. ]; bracts subtending the flowers up to as long as calyx [Fig. ]
Plants with closely crowded, sessile or short-pedicellate flowers borne in terminal cymes [Fig. ]; bracts subtending flowers nearly equaling to exceeding the length of the calyx [Fig. ]

c2.text: Basal leaf blades oblanceolate, 15–30 mm long; at least the lower internodes of the stem puberulent; blade of petals 5–10 mm long, the apex toothed [Fig. ]; calyx equaling the length of the fruit; bracts ca. 50% as long as the calyx

Basal leaf blades linear, 20–80 mm long; stems glabrous; blade of petals 12–18 mm long, fringed-cleft to near the middle; calyx shorter than the length of the fruit; bracts 25–36% as long as the calyx

c3.text: Calyx, including the basal connate portion, pubescent [Fig. ]; plants annual or biennial; stems usually strigose below the nodes
Calyx completely glabrous or only the lobes pubescent [Fig. ]; plants perennial; stems glabrous (sometimes scabrous)

c4.text: Stem leaf blades lanceolate to oblanceolate, (10–) 15–25 (–30) mm wide, sheathing the stem for less than 3 times the stem diameter; calyx lobes glabrous
Stem leaf blades linear, up to 5 mm wide, sheathing the stem more than 3 times the stem diameter; calyx lobes pubescent

c1.text: This genus contains exactly one species.
Plants cespitose; stems 1-flowered
Plants not cespitose; stems usually many-flowered

c2.text: Plants upright, 30–90 cm tall; calyx 15–25 mm long; capsule 10–20 mm
Plants trailing, procumbent, or ascending, 5–25 cm tall; calyx 7–12 mm long; capsule 6–8 mm long

c1.text: This genus contains exactly one species.
Pedicels and sepals glandular-puberulent; leaf blades clasping at the base; apical portion of stem glandular-puberulent

Pedicels and sepals not glandular-puberulent [Fig. ]; leaf blades not clasping (basal leaves clasping in G. elegans ); apical portion of stems glabrous (sometimes the stems pubescent with eglandular or glandular hairs, but then the hairs usually confined to the basal half)

c2.text: Slender annuals with green stems 0.4–3 (–4) dm tall; leaf blades linear, 0.2–2 (–3) mm wide; capsule oblong
Stout annuals or perennials with glaucous stems 2–10 dm tall; leaves lanceolate, (1–) 2–16 mm wide; capsule spherical

c3.text: Plants perennial; petals 1–4 mm long; calyx 1–3 mm long, slightly shorter to nearly as long as the petals; longer pedicels 0.5–12 mm long
Plants usually annual; petals 6–15 mm long; calyx 2.5–5 mm long, ca. 36–50% as long as the petals; longer pedicels 10–35 mm long

c1.text: This genus contains exactly one species.
This genus contains exactly one species.
Silicles with a wrinkled texture due to raised veins or reticulum; racemes borne laterally from the axils of leaves
Silicles with a smooth surface; racemes chiefly terminal and at the tips of branches

c2.text: Silicles with an evident basal and apical sinus, reticulate to rugose over the exterior surface [Fig. ]; styles obsolete
Silicles lacking both basal and apical sinuses, coarsely veined and with protruding, wart-like processes over the exterior surface; styles present, ca. 0.5 mm long

c3.text: Silicles without a notch at the apex; plants perennial from rhizomes or stolons
Silices with a notch or sinus at the apex; plants annual from taproots or fibrous roots

c4.text: Leaf blades sagittate-clasping; silicles subglobose; flowering raceme typically flat or sometimes even concave-topped, the lower pedicels equaling the height of the inflorescence; plants 2–5 dm tall

Leaf blades shortly petiolate or sessile, but not clasping the stem; silicles flattened perpendicular to the septum; flowering raceme typically round-topped, the lower pedicels shorter than the height of the inflorescence; plants (5–) 7–13 dm tall

c5.text: Stem leaves either sagittate- or cordate-clasping [Fig. ]; flowers with 6 stamens
Stem leaves narrowed to the base, not surrounding the stem; flowers with 2 or 4 stamens except L. sativum with 6 stamens

c6.text: Stem leaves cordate-clasping, the basal lobes rounded; lower leaf blades 2 or 3 times divided into linear segments; petals yellow, 1–1.5 mm long; fruiting pedicels glabrous; silicles ca. 3.5–4 mm long

Stem leaves auriculate-clasping, the basal lobes usually acute [Fig. ]; lower leaf blades entire to toothed or sometimes once pinnately lobed; petals white, 1.8–2.8 mm long; fruting pedicels pubescent; silicles 5–6 mm long

c7.text: Style 0.2–0.5 (–0.7) mm long, not or only shortly exserted beyond the apical notch of the fruit; valves of silique papillose; plants annual, without a caudex
Style (0.6–) 1–1.5 mm long, prominently exserted beyond the apical notch of the fruit; valves of silique usually not papillose; plants perennial, with a caudex

c8.text: Flowers with 6 stamens; silicles 5–6 mm long, prominently winged; cotyledons 3-lobed
Flowers with 2 (rarely 4) stamens; silicles 2–4 mm long, without a wing or winged only in the apical portion; cotyledons entire

c9.text: Petals typically present, 1–2 times as long as the sepals [Fig. ]; rachis of raceme, when pubescent, with curved, cylindrical hairs; cotyledons accumbent
Petals obsolete or rudimentary and shorter than the sepals; rachis of raceme pubescent with straight, cyclindrical to subclavate hairs; cotyledons incumbent

c10.text: Racemes densely flowered, with 9–18 fruits per cm; silicles obovate to broad-obovate; plants inodorous; lower surface of fruiting pedicels smooth; seeds with an apical, narrow wing-margin
Racemes relatively sparsely flowered, with 6–10 fruits per cm; silicles elliptic; plants foul-scented; lower surface of fruiting pedicels sparsely papillose; seeds lacking a wing margin

c1.text: Siliques 3–6 mm thick, of uniform diameter through most of its length except for the beak and prominent constrictions between the seeds [Fig. ], longitudinally striate, containing 4–12 seeds; petals usually yellow fading to white; taproot slender

Siliques 5–10 mm thick, widest below the middle and tapering toward the beak, not or scarcely constricted between the seeds, smooth or inconspicuously striate, containing 1–3 (–5) seeds; petals usually purple; taproot usually conspicuously thickened
This genus contains exactly one species.
This genus contains exactly one species.
This genus contains exactly one species.

Leaf blades usually with few and distant, irregular, large teeth (rarely entire); siliques 3–5 mm long; stems hirsute, at least on the lower portion; axis of the inflorescence elongating in fruit, the infructescence resembling a raceme
Leaf blades entire or nearly so; siliques 5.5–7 (–10) mm long; stems glabrous; axis of the inflorescence elongating or not

c2.text: Plants perennial, with evergreen leaves; petals white (sometimes tinged with lilac); axis of the inflorescence elongating in fruit, the infructescence resembling a raceme
Plants annual, with deciduous leaves; petals pink to purple; axis of the inflorescence not or scarcely elongating in fruit, the infructescence resembling an umbel

Siliques 6–12 ×3.5–5 mm, compressed, ± glabrous or with some hairs near the margins of the valves; fruiting pedicels widely ascending; style 1–2 mm long; seeds with a winged margin

Petals bilobed with a deep, apical sinus; stems scapose (i.e., all the leaves confined to a basal cluster)
Petals entire or emarginate at apex; stems with at least 1 leaf-bearing node

c2.text: Plants annual; rachis of infructescence congested, 1–16 (–35) mm long; stem leaves all borne at base just above the basal rosette of leaves
Plants perennial from a caudex; rachis of infructescence relatively elongate, (16–) 20–78 mm long; stem leaves more evenly distributed, usually some produced in the apical half of the stem

c3.text: Lowest 1–3 flowers each subtended by a leafy bract; siliques pubescent with stellate hairs
None of the flowers subtended by leafy bracts; siliques glabrous or sparsely pubescent with simple or forked hairs

c4.text: Stellate hairs of abaxial surface of basal leaves borne on short stalks, the radiating branches of the hairs elevated above the surface of the leaf blade [Fig. ]; styles up to 0.3 (–0.4) mm long; stigmas often bilobed
Stellate hairs of abaxial surface of basal leaves sessile, the radiating branches of the hairs appressed to the leaf surface [Fig. ]; styles (0.3–) 0.4–1 mm long; stigmas scarcely bilobed

c1.text: This genus contains exactly one species.

Plants rough-pubescent with simple hairs 1–2.5 mm long that exceed the length of the branched hairs; silicle body (i.e., excluding the beak and the short, stipe-like base) (2.5–) 3.5–5 (–6) ×2–4 (–5) mm; fruiting pedicels 4–14 (–17) mm long; seeds 0.8–1.4 (–1.5) mm long

Petals white; submersed leaf blades highly dissected into narrow segments; septum incomplete, residual as narrow strips on the inner margins of the replum
Petals yellow or absent; leaf blades subentire to pinnately lobed; septum complete

c2.text: Petals absent; fruiting pedicels 0.5–1.5 (–2) mm long
Petals present; fruiting pedicels 2–15 mm long

c3.text: Petals 0.7–3.5 mm long, shorter than to approximately equaling the length of the sepals; plants usually annual or biennial (rarely short-lived perennial), from tap roots; anthers 0.2–0.5 mm long
Petals (2–) 2.8–5.5 mm long, longer than the sepals; plants perennial from rhizomes or creeping stem bases; anthers 0.4–1.3 mm long

c4.text: Silicles ovoid-obloid to broad-ovoid, (2–) 3–10 mm long; seeds papillose; petals 0.8–3.5 mm long; abaxial leaf blades and lower stem glabrous or pubescent
Silicles spherical to subspherical, 2–3 (–3.5) mm long; seeds reticulate-patterned; petals 0.7–1.3 (–1.5) mm long; abaxial leaf blades and lower stem pubescent

c5.text: Fertile siliques 10–20 mm long, linear in outline, those from unfertilized ovaries developing only 4–8 (–10) mm long; middle and upper stem leaves usually pinnately lobed to pinnately divided
Siliques (2.5–) 3–5 (–6) mm long, ovoid-obloid to subspherical; middle and upper stem leaves entire to coarsely serrate

c6.text: Fruiting pedicels weakly sigmoid-curved downward to somewhat recurved [Fig. ]; silicles ovoid-obloid [Fig. ]; stem leaves clasping at the base or, more commonly, not clasping
Fruiting pedicels straight, widely ascending [Fig. ]; silicles spherical or subspherical [Fig. ]; lower and middle stems leaves auriculate-clasping

c1.text: This genus contains exactly one species.
Fruiting pedicels erect; seeds aligned in 2 rows in each locule; petals 7–10 mm long, white to pink to rose-purple; lower stems usually with some mesifixed hairs or glabrous

Fruiting pedicels widely ascending to reflexed; seeds aligned in 1 row in each locule (rarely partially aligned in 2 irregular rows); petals 3–7 (–8) mm long, white to yellow-white (rarely light purple); lower stems glabrous or with simple or branched hairs, but none of the hairs mesifixed

c2.text: Stem leaves narrowed to the base, not clasping the stem [Fig. ]; siliques 2.5–3.5 mm wide
Stem leaves auriculate-clasping at the base; siliques 1–2.5 mm wide

c3.text: Basal leaf blades sparsely to densely pubescent with compound hairs bearing 2–4 (–7) rays; seeds aligned in 1 row or partially aligned in 2 irregular rows in each locule; sepals abaxially glabrous or pubescent; petals white or sometimes light purple; pollen subspherical
Basal leaf blades glabrous to sparsely pubescent with simple hairs; seeds aligned in 1 row in each locule; sepals glabous; petals white to yellow-white; pollen ellipsoid

c4.text: Petals 3–5 mm long, equaling to slightly exceeding the length of the sepals (i.e., petals up to 1.3 times as long as the sepals); stems glaucous, with relatively fewer leaf-bearing nodes, averaging 13 internodes to the first flower; basal leaf blades serrate to subentire

Petals 5–7 mm long, (1.3–) 1.4–2 times as long as the sepals; stems green, with relatively more leaf-bearing nodes, averaging 25 internodes to the first flower; basal leaf blades serrate to pinnately lobed [Fig. ]

c1.text: This genus contains exactly one species.

Petals 8–10 mm long; fruiting pedicels ± spreading; siliques 12–35 mm long; leaves with entire blades (rarely with a single tooth on one or both margins), those along the stem not clasping at the base
Petals 3–5 mm long; fruiting pedicels erect; siliques 30–50 mm long; leaves with entire to dentate blades, usually the lower with at some form of dentition, those along the stem auriculate-clasping
Fruiting pedicels thick, ± the same diameter as the siliques, widely spreading at or nearly at right angles to the axis [Fig. ]; rachis of inflorescence often flexuous
Fruiting pedicels slender, narrower than the siliques, erect to spreading-ascending; rachis of inflorescence straight

c2.text: Petals (7–) 8–25 (–30) mm long; sepals (4–) 5–14 mm long; siliques (20–) 40–70 mm long
Petals 3.5–7 (–8) mm long; sepals 2–5 (–6) mm long; siliques 15–50 mm long

c3.text: Petals 13–25 (–30) mm long, commonly orange to orange-yellow; sepals 7–14 mm long
Petals (7–) 8–18 mm long, commonly yellow; sepals (4–) 5–10 mm long

c4.text: Petals 12–18 mm long; sepals 6–10 mm long; anthers 2 mm long or longer
Petals (7–) 8–10 (–12) mm long; sepals (4–) 5–6 mm long; anthers 1–2.2 mm long

c5.text: Anthers 0.4–0.6 mm long; sepals 2–3.5 mm long; petals bright yellow, 3.5–5 mm long; siliques glabrous to sparsely pubescent, 15–20 (–30) mm long, pubescent on the inner surface of the valves
Anthers 1.5–2.5 mm long; sepals 4–5 (–6) mm long; petals pale yellow, 5–7 (–8) mm long; siliques pubescent, 30–50 mm long, glabrous on the inner surface of the valves

c1.text: This genus contains exactly one species.
This genus contains exactly one species.
Siliques (15–) 20–40 (–45) ×0.8–1 mm, flat; petals (4–) 6–8 (–10) mm long; seeds 0.8–1.4 mm long; native biennial or perennial plants of cliffs, outcrops, and rocky slopes
Siliques (8–) 10–15 (–18) ×0.5–0.8 mm, ± terete in cross-section; petals 2–3.5 (–4) mm long; seeds 0.3–0.5 mm long; non-native annuals of disturbed soil
Upper stem leaves either shortly petiolate or sessile and then narrowed to the base
Upper stem leaves sessile and auriculate-clasping the stem

c2.text: Siliques terete or subterete, 15–40 mm long, tipped by an indehiscent beak 5–10 mm long; fruiting pedicels ascending, mostly 10–15 mm long; plants usually glabrous
Siliques quadrangular, 10–25 mm long, tipped by an indehiscent beak 1–3 mm long [Fig. ]; fruiting pedicels erect to appressed, 2–5 mm long [Fig. ]; plants usually hirsute-hispid in the lower portion

c3.text: Petals (15–) 18–25 (–30) mm long; plants glabrous throughout; filaments all erect at base; sepals erect; indehiscent, apical beak of fruit (3–) 4–10 mm long, with (0–) 1 (–2) seeds

Petals 6–14 mm long; plants sometimes sparsely pubescent near the base; filaments of lateral stamens curved at base; sepals ascending (rarely suberect); indehiscent, apical beak of fruit 7–15 mm long, with 0 (–1) seeds

c4.text: Plants green; petals 6–10 (–11) mm long, pale yellow; apical beak of silique (8–) 10–15 mm long; seeds 1–1.8 mm long; open flowers of raceme at the same level as or overtopping the flower buds

Plants glaucous; petals 10–14 mm long, deep yellow; apical beak of silique 7–10 (–11) mm long; seeds (1.2–) 1.5–2.5 (–3) mm long; open flowers of raceme usually lower than (rarely at the same level) the flower buds

c1.text: This genus contains exactly one species.

Principal leaf blades palmately lobed or palmately divided into 3–5 segments; stems gradually narrowing at base to a fragile junction with a swollen, fleshy rhizome; siliques with a persistent style beak 5–8 mm long

Principal leaf blades simple or pinnately lobed or pinnately divided [Figs. , , ]; stems arising from caudices, taproots, or rhizomes, when arising from rhizomes the stem widest at base and narrowing upward and/or continuous with rhizome; siliques with a persistent style beak 0.3–6 mm long

c2.text: Rhizome lacking tooth-like projections or these very obscure, formed of segments joined by fragile connectives, the rhizome readily breaking into segments [Fig. ]; stem above the leaves usually pubescent with spreading hairs; stems usually with 3 leaves in a single whorl

Rhizome with tooth-like projections, either continuous [Fig. ] or with alternately enlarged and constricted areas, but not readily breaking into segments; stem above the leaves usually glabrous; stems with usually 2 opposite leaves or with 3 alternate leaves

c3.text: Cilia on leaf margin mostly 0.2–0.3 mm long and spreading; rhizome alternately enlarged and constricted
Cilia on leaf margin mostly 0.1 mm long and ascending or appressed; rhizome continuous or alternately enlarged and constricted

c4.text: Leaflets sessile; rhizome alternately enlarged and constricted
Leaflets usually petiolulate; rhizome continuous [Fig. ]

c5.text: Lower leaf blades, as well as usually the upper, simple
Lower leaf blades, as well as usually the upper, pinnately divided or pinnately lobed with sinuses extending nearly to the midrib

c6.text: Petals up to 5 mm long or absent; fruiting pedicels 1–10 mm long; stems arising from a vertical taproot and caudex or fibrous roots
Petals 7–16 mm long; lower fruiting pedicels 20–30 mm long; stems arising from a stout, tuber-like rhizome

c7.text: Petals absent or up to 1.2 mm long and concealed by the sepals; siliques 5–12 mm long, spreading to ascending [Fig. ]; fruiting pedicels 1–3 mm long; wetland and aquatic plants, primarily of fresh-tidal river shores (in part)
Petals 3–5 mm long, visible; siliques 15–35 mm long, erect; fruiting pedicels 4–10 mm long; dwarf alpine plants

c8.text: Sepals green turning yellow; petals white (rarely pink); stem glabrous or pubescent with appressed hairs shorter than 0.15 mm; stems mostly 20–40 cm tall to the first pedicel
Sepals purple turning brown; petals pink to purple (rarely white); stem pubescent with spreading hairs 0.2–0.8 mm long; stems mostly 8–20 cm tall to the first pedicel

c9.text: Leaf blades with 2 or 3 (rarely up to 5) leaflets [Fig. ]; siliques 5–12 mm long; fruiting pedicels 1–3 mm long [Fig. ]; petals absent or up to 1.2 mm long and not exceeding the sepals (in part)
Principal leaf blades with 5–17 leaflets [Figs. , ]; siliques 10–30 mm long; lower fruiting pedicels (4–) 5–18 mm long; petals 1.5–4 mm long, visible (sometimes absent in C. impatiens )

c10.text: Stem leaves sagittate-auriculate, with sharply toothed to lacerate-margined leaflets that are usually acuminate at the apex [Fig. ]; petals absent or present and 2–3 mm long, scarcely exceeding the sepals
Stem leaves shortly petiolate, not auriculate, with entire to crenate-dentate leaflets that are rounded to acute at the apex [Fig. ]; petals present, 1.5–15 mm long

c11.text: Petals 8–15 mm long; styles 3–6 mm long; lower fruiting pedicels 12–18 mm long; plants perennial
Petals 1.5–4 mm long; styles 0.3–1.5 mm long; lower fruiting pedicels (3–) 5–14 mm long; plants annual or biennial (sometimes short-lived perennial in C. flexuosa )

c12.text: Primary veins of terminal leaflet of basal leaves terminating in a ± triangular, callus tip that is prominently excurrent beyond the leaflet blade tissue [Fig. ]; petals pink to white in life, drying pink to pink-purple; leaflets of upper stem leaves commonly sessile

Primary veins of terminal leaflet of basal leaves terminating in a callus region, but the callus either not excurrent beyond the leaflet blade tissue or scarcely excurrent as a semicircular (i.e., dome-shaped) tip [Fig. ]; petals white in life, drying white, cream, yellow-white, or brown-white; leaflets of upper stem leaves commonly petiolulate

c13.text: Basal leaves numerous, persistent, with hirsute petioles; stems with 2–5 (–6) leaf-bearing nodes; flowers with 4 stamens; siliques usually erect and parallel or nearly so to the raceme axis

Basal leaves few, sometimes absent at anthesis, with glabrous petioles (always with hirsute petioles in C. flexuosa, a very rare introduction); stems with 4–10 (–20) leaf-bearing nodes; flowers with 6 stamens (some individuals rarely with only 4 stamens); siliques usually erect-ascending to ascending and not parallel to the raceme axis (except sometimes in C. parviflora )

Lateral leaflets or segments of stem leaves not decurrent on leaf rachis; petioles usually hirsute; stems flexuous, sometimes decumbent-based; introduced plants primarily of human-disturbed places

c1.text: This genus contains exactly one species.

This genus contains exactly one species.

Siliques narrow-linear, 0.5–1.3 (–1.5) mm wide, acute at the apex; seeds aligned in 1 row in each locule; plants usually eglandular

Basal leaf blades with 4–10 pairs of lateral lobes; siliques (40–) 53–70 (–80) mm long; fruiting pedicels 1.2–1.8 mm thick
Basal leaf blades simple or with 1–4 pairs of lateral lobes; siliques 10–40 (–45) mm long; fruiting pedicels up to 1 mm thick

c2.text: Silique with a persistent style beak 2–3 (–3.5) mm long; petals 6–8 mm long; auricles of uppermost leaves eciliate [Fig. ]; sepals glabrous
Silique with a persistent style beak 0.5–1.6 (–2.3) mm long; petals 3–6 mm long; auricles of uppermost leaves ciliate; sepals usually pubescent near the apex (sometimes glabrous in B. stricta )

Petals 0.5–1 (–1.2) mm wide; siliques (12–) 18–28 (–30) mm long; pedicels 1–3 (–4) mm long in fruit; upper leaf blades usually toothed or with a few shallow sinuses

c1.text: This genus contains exactly one species.

c2.text: Fruiting pedicels nearly as thick as the silique they support [Fig. ]; mature siliques 30–100 mm long
Fruiting pedicels slender, thinner than the silique they support; mature siliques 20–40 mm long

c3.text: Upper stem leaf blades pinnately divided into linear to lanceolate segments; outer sepals corniculate; fruiting pedicels (4–) 6–10 mm long
Upper stem leaf blades simple or hastate (i.e., with 2 outward-pointing basal lobes); outer sepals not corniculate; fruiting pedicels 3–6 mm long

c4.text: Immature siliques often overtopping the flowers in the apical portion of the inflorescence; petals 2.5–4 mm long; plants glabrous or sparsely pubescent; mature siliques 30–40 mm long
Immature siliques not overtopping the flowers in the apical portion of the inflorescence; petals 6–8 mm long; plants sparsely to densely pubescent below; mature siliques 20–35 mm long

c1.text: This genus contains exactly one species.

Leaf blades pinnately divided into distinct leaflets [Fig. ]

c2.text: Sepals 5–7 mm long; mericarps 3–5 mm long; carpel beaks 18–35 mm long; bracts of umbel ovate-orbicular
Sepals 8–15 mm long; mericarps 7.5–11 mm long; carpel beaks (25–) 50–113 mm long; bracts of umbel lanceolate to ovate or triangular

c3.text: Apical pits of mericarp bodies stipitate-glandular within, without furrows below them; umbel with 3–10 flowers
Apical pits of mericarp bodies eglandular within, with 2 furrows below them (lacking furrows in E. cygnorum ); umbel with 1–6 flowers

c4.text: Carpel beaks 60–100 mm long; sepals 12–15 mm long; mericarp bodies 9–11 mm long (in part)
Carpel beaks 25–42 mm long; sepals 8–12 mm long; mericarp bodies 8–9 mm long (in part)

c5.text: Base of stem, as well as upper portion of stem, pubescent with glandular hairs; leaf blades oblong to ovate in outline, with usually 5 or more principal lobes; mericarp bodies with 2 furrows below the apical pits

Base of stem pubescent with eglandular hairs or sometimes glabrate (upper portion of stem glandular-pubescent); leaf blades ovate in outline, with usually 3 principal lobes; mericarp bodies without furrows below the apical pits

c6.text: Carpel beaks (56–) 60–100 mm long; mericarp bodies 9–11 mm long; sepals 12–15 mm long; leaf blades often with small, intercalary lobes/leaflets between the major lobes or leaflets (in part)
Carpel beaks 10–40 mm long; mericarp bodies 4–9 mm long; sepals 5–12 mm long; leaf blades without intercalary leaflets between the major leaflets

c7.text: Mericarp bodies 8–9 mm long; apical pits of mericarp bodies stipitate-glandular within, without furrows below them; sepals 8–12 mm long (in part)
Mericarp bodies 4–7 mm long; apical pits of mericarp bodies eglandular or sessile-glandular within, with 2 furrows or a pit-like furrow below them; sepals 5–9 mm long

c8.text: Leaflets prominently lobed, with sinuses extending to nearly the entire distance from the tips of the lobes to the leaflet midrib [Fig. ]; anther-bearing filaments without basal teeth; apical pits of mericarp bodies eglandular, with 2 furrows below them

c1.text: Leaves palmately compound, the terminal segment petiolulate; mericarp bodies separating from the carpel beaks but remaining attached to the style column for a period of time by 2 subapical filaments
Leaves palmately lobed, the leaf segments confluent; mericarp bodies remaining attached to the carpel beaks, without subapical filaments

c2.text: Petals 12–20 mm long [Fig. ]; anthers 2–2.6 mm long; style beaks 4–8 mm long; plants perennial from a stout rhizome

Petals 2.5–10 mm long; anthers 0.4–1.5 mm long; style beaks 0–6 mm long; plants annual or biennial, commonly from a taproot, or perennial with rhizomes in G. pyrenaicum , G. sibiricum , and G. thunbergii

c3.text: Each cymule of the inflorescence usually 1-flowered; stems with several leaves; petals retuse at the apex, deep red (rarely white)
Each cymule of the inflorescence usually 2-flowered; stems with a single pair of leaves, the other leaves basal; petals entire or very slightly retuse at the apex, blue-purple or pink (rarely white)

c4.text: Sepals, pedicels, and style beaks with stipitate glands [Fig. ]; pedicels deflexed after anthesis; petals blue to blue-purple, 12–13 mm wide, 1.5–2.1 times as long as wide [Fig. ]
Sepals, pedicels, and style beaks pubescent but not glandular; pedicels suberect after anthesis; petals pink to pink-purple (rarely white), 8.5–11.6 mm wide, 1.3–1.4 times as long as wide

c5.text: From 3–5 of the 5 outer stamens sterile and lacking anthers; seeds smooth; petals 2.5–4 mm long
All of the stamens fertile and bearing anthers; seeds reticulate or striate, sometimes obscurely so (+/- smooth in G. aequale and G. pyrenaicum ); petals (3–) 3.2–10 mm long

c6.text: Sepals obtuse to acute at the apex, sometimes with a short mucro 0.1–0.3 mm long; mericarp bodies glabrous on most of the surfaces (pubescent in G. pyrenaicum , ciliate near the base in G. aequale ), cross-wrinkled or smooth; seeds ± smooth or striate
Sepals acuminate at the apex, tipped with an awn 0.5–2 mm long [Figs. , ]; mericarp bodies at least sparsely hirsute (sometimes nearly glabrous in G. columbinum ), smooth; seeds reticulate

c7.text: Mericarp bodies pubescent; plant perennial from a short, vertical rhizome; seeds 2.2–2.7 mm long; petals 7–11 mm long
Mericarp bodies glabrous (though ciliate near the base in G. aequale ); plants annual; seeds 1.4–1.8 mm long; petals (3–) 3.5–8.5 (–10) mm long

c8.text: Mericarp bodies cross-wrinkled, eciliate; seeds striate; anthers 0.7–1.5 mm long; petals (3–) 4.5–8.5 (–10.5) mm long; pedicels 2.3–4.2 times as long as the sepals
Mericarp bodies smooth, densely ciliate near the base; seeds ± smooth; anthers 0.4–0.6 mm long; petals 3.5–4.5 mm long; pedicels 1.5–2.5 times as long as the sepals

c9.text: Pedicels 3–13 mm long, 0.6–2.2 times as long as the sepals; style beak 1–2 mm long
Pedicels 10–60 mm long, 1.8–8.2 times as long as the sepals [Fig. ]; style beak 0–0.5 (–1) mm long or 3.5–4.5 mm long

c10.text: Mericarp bodies pubescent with antrorsely oriented, eglandular hairs ca. 1 mm long; seeds inconspicuously reticulate-patterned with irregular, thin-walled aereolae; ultimate segments of middle and upper stem leaves usually narrow-oblong and obtuse at the apex

Mericarp bodies pubescent with spreading, often glandular, hairs 0.2–0.6 mm long; seeds conspicuously reticulate-patterened with ± uniform, thick-walled aereolae; ultimate segments of middle and upper stem leaves usually linear and acute at the apex

c11.text: Plants perennial, from rhizomes; style beak 0–0.5 (–1) mm long
Plants annual or biennial, without rhizomes; style beak 3.5–4.5 mm long

c12.text: Each cymule of the inflorescence usually 2-flowered; petals 7–10 ×5–5.5 mm, 1.4–1.8 times as long as wide, pubescent on the adaxial surface near the base; eglandular hairs of the pedicels spreading; seeds 1.9–2 mm long

Each cymule of the inflorescence usually 1-flowered; petals 5–7 ×1.5–2 mm, ca. 2.5 times as long as wide, glabrous on the adaxial surface (though ciliate near the base); eglandular hairs of the pedicels retrorsely appressed; seeds 2.6–2.7 mm long
