c7.text: Leaf blades flat, 2–5 mm wide, the basal ones usually withered by anthesis
Leaf blades involute, 0.5–2 mm wide, the basal ones persisting all year in a tuft

c8.text: Anthers globose, 0.2–0.3 (–0.5) mm long; glumes 1–2 mm long; lemmas 0.8–1.2 mm long; spikelets ± evidently clustered near the tips of the panicle branches; pedicels 0.3–2 mm long; reproductive stems often with more than 3 leaf-bearing nodes; plants flowering March through July

Anthers oblong, 0.4–0.8 mm long; glumes 1.8–3.4 mm long; lemmas 1.4–2 mm long; spikelets not appearing clustered; pedicels 0.5–5 mm long; reproductive stems with 3 or fewer leaf-bearing nodes; plants flowering June through November (in part)

c9.text: Leaf blades involute, 0.2–2 mm wide, the basal ones persisting all year in a tuft; reproductive stems with 3 or fewer leaf-bearing nodes (in part)
Leaf blades flat, 1–3 mm wide, the basal ones usually withered prior to anthesis; reproductive stems with usually more than 3 leaf-bearing nodes

c10.text: Glumes 1.7–3 mm long; anthers 1–1.5 mm long; caryopses 0.8–1.2 mm long; stolons usually present
Glumes 2.5–3.8 mm long; anthers 0.5–0.8 mm long; caryopses 1.4–2 mm long; stolons absent

c1.text: Leaves 3–5 mm wide; branches of the panicle ascending to spreading at anthesis, bearing flowers in the distal half of the branches
Leaves 1–3 mm wide; branches of the panicle contracted, erect at anthesis, bearing flowers in both distal and proximal halves of the branches

Pubescence of the callus (130–) 150–200 (–250)% as long as the lemma; rachilla not prolonged; glumes exceeding the lemmas by a distance of (1.5–) 2–3 (–4.5) mm; lemmas 2-nerved apical to the insertion of the awn

Pubescence of the callus 20–120 (–150)% as long as the lemma [Figs. , ]; rachilla prolonged behind the palea as a slender, pubescent bristle; glumes exceeding the lemmas by a distance of (0–) 0.1–2.1 mm; lemmas 4-nerved apical to the insertion of the awn

c2.text: Awn attached well above the middle of the lemma; rachilla pubescent only at apex; caryopsis pubescent at apex
Awn attached at or below the middle of the lemma [Fig. ]; rachilla pubescent throughout; caryopsis glabrous

c3.text: Callus hairs scant, up to 1 mm long, 20–30% as long as the lemma [Fig. ]; awns straight
Callus hairs moderate to copious, (1.5–) 1.7–3.5 (–4.5) mm long, 50–120 (–150)% as long as the lemma [Fig. ]; awns straight or bent

c4.text: Panicle contracted and dense, (7–) 10–20 (–28) mm wide, the longer branches 1.4–5 (–9.5) cm long; pubescence of callus scant to moderate, concentrated in unequal lateral tufts, 20–75 (–100)% as long as the lemma; lemma awn minutely antrorsely scabrous throughout its length, delicate to stout, usually distinguishable from the callus hairs

Panicle loose and somewhat open (less open in C. canadensis var. macouniana ), (10–) 20–40 (–80) mm wide, the longer branches 2.7–6 (–12) cm long; pubescence of callus moderate to dense, uniformly distributed, (70–) 90–120 (–150)% as long as the lemma; lemma awn smooth, as least in the basal half, delicate, often difficult to distinguish from the callus hairs

c1.text: Plants perennial from short, knotty rhizomes; axis of inflorescence scabrous-hispid
Plants annual from fibrous roots; axis of the inflorescence villous and/or hispid or scabrous-hispid in S. verticillata

c2.text: Each spikelet subtended by 4–12 bristles [Fig. ]; spikelets 3–3.5 mm long
Each spikelet subtended by 1–3 bristles (up to 6 in S. faberi ); spikelets 1.6–3 mm long

c3.text: Axis of the panicle retrorsely scabrous-hispid; branches of the panicle verticillate; inflorescence 5–12 mm thick; leaf blades usually spreading; bristles of the inflorescence retrorsely scabrous

Axis of the panicle villous to hispid, but not scabrous; branches of the panicle not verticillate; inflorescence 7–35 mm thick; leaf blades usually ascending (at least the basal portion of the blade); bristles of the inflorescence antrorsely scabrous

c4.text: Fertile lemma smooth (rarely very finely transerve rugose), lustrous; disarticulation above the glumes, the caryopsis falling free from the more persistent glumes; mature caryopsis yellow to red or brown to black
Fertile lemma evidently transversely rugulose, dull; disarticulation below the glumes, the entire spikelet, including the caryopsis, falling intact; mature caryopsis green

c5.text: Leaves pubescent with soft hairs and scabrous on the adaxial surface; spikelets 2.5–3 mm long; inflorescence nodding from near the base [Fig. ], 20–30 mm wide; second glume 65–75% as long as the spikelet
Leaves scabrous on the adaxial surface; spikelets 1.8–2.2 mm long; inflorescence erect or nodding from near the apex [Fig. ], 10–23 mm wide; second glume nearly as long as the spikelet

c1.text: This genus contains exactly one species.
This genus contains exactly one species.

This genus contains exactly one species.

Awn of lemma elongate, 6–12 mm long, geniculate at base, conspicuously surpassing glumes; callus of lemma pubescent with hairs 3.5–12 mm long, up to twice as long as the associated spikelet; ligules 1–2 mm long; plants cespitose, with short rhizomes, forming large clumps

Awn of lemma absent or short, not exceeding the glumes of intact spikelets; callus of lemma pubescent with hairs ca. 8–24 mm long, 2–4 times as long as the associated spikelet; ligules 0.5–1 mm long; plants long-rhizomatous, forming extensive colonies
This genus contains exactly one species.
Sessile spikelets 5–11 mm long; pedicellate spikelets usually well-developed and staminate
Sessile spikelets (2.6–) 3–5 mm long; pedicellate spikelets usually reduced or absent, often only the pedicel present

c2.text: Leaves with scabrous sheaths, the blades (13–) 30–109 cm long; ligules 0.6–2.2 mm long; mature peduncles of the rames (4–) 11–35 (–60) mm long
Leaves with smooth sheaths, the blades 11–30 (–52) cm long; ligules 0.2–1 mm long; mature peduncles of the rames (2–) 3–4 (–10) mm long

c1.text: This genus contains exactly one species.
Reproductive stems decumbent and rooting at nodes in contact with soil; apex of leaf sheath with a prominent and elongate constriction proximal to the leaf blade [Fig. ]
Reproductive stems upright, not rooting from lower nodes; apex of leaf sheath with an inconspicuous and short constriction proximal to the leaf blade
Plants annual or short-lived perennial, lacking rhizomes; leaf blades (5–) 20–100 mm wide; mature spikelets not or only tardily disarticulating
Plants perennial, with rhizomes; leaf blades 8–20 (–40) mm wide; mature spikelets disarticulating

Fertile carpellate lemmas coriaceous to indurate, lustrous, glabrous or with scabrules confined to the veins and a dense patch at the apex [Fig. ]; abortive carpellate spikelets 0.6–2.6 mm wide; carpellate portion of inflorescence 1–8 (–15) cm wide, the branches bearing mature carpellate spikelets appressed (rarely some ascending); leaf blades 3–15 (–20) mm wide; ligules 3–8 (–16) mm long

Fertile carpellate lemmas chartaceous, flexible, dull or sublustrous, with scattered scabrules on and between the veins, the scabrules not or only slightly concentrated near the apex [Fig. ]; abortive carpellate spikelets 0.4–1 mm wide; carpellate portion of inflorescence (5–) 10–50 cm wide, the branches bearing mature carpellate spikelets spreading-ascending to ascending (rarely appressed when bearing mainly abortive spikeletes); leaf blades (3–) 10–55 (–72) mm wide; ligules (5–) 10–15 (–30) mm long
This genus contains exactly one species.
Panicle branches 0.7–2 (–4) cm long, few, distant, simple; leaf blades 3–6 (–10) mm wide; spikelets 2–3 mm long

Panicle branches (1–) 2–10 cm long, variable in number but often crowded, sometimes the longer branches with secondary branches; leaf blades 5–30 mm wide (sometimes narrower in small forms of E. crus-galli ); spikelets 2.5–5 mm long

c2.text: Lower lemmas usually unawned; upper lemmas wider and longer than the upper glumes at maturity, the margins and apex exposed and visible
Lower lemmas usually awned; upper lemmas hardly, if at all, exceeding the upper glumes in length and width, primarily concealed

c3.text: Lower sheaths hispid with pustulose-based hairs; lower 1 or 2 nodes evidently pubescent with long, erect-ascending to spreading-ascending hairs
Sheaths glabrous; lower nodes glabrous or sparsely pubescent with short hairs

c4.text: Coriaceous portion of upper lemmas rounded at apex, abruptly transitioning to an early withering, membranous apex, the two regions separated by a line of minute hairs [Fig. ]
Coriaceous portion of upper lemmas acute to acuminate at apex, gradually transitioning from the coriaceous body into the membranous tip, the two regions not offset by a line of minute hairs [Fig. ]

c1.text: Inflorescence an open panicle, the primary branches usually branched again [Fig. ]; spikelets borne on pedicels 10–40 mm long
Inflorescence a panicle of secund, spike-like racemes, the primary branches usually unbranched [Fig. ]; spikelets borne on pedicels 0.2–3.8 mm long

c2.text: Axis of panicle branches triquetrous, but not wing-margined; reproductive stems usually upright, only rarely rooting at the lower nodes
Axis of panicle branches wing-margined; reproductive stems usually decumbent and rooting from the lower nodes

c3.text: Lower glume present, 0.2–0.4 mm long; upper glume 33–50 (–60)% as long as the entire spikelet; upper lemmas yellow or gray to brown at maturity; spikelets of the middle portion of the primary panicle branches usually borne in pairs on pedicels that are not adnate to the branch axis; leaf sheaths usually pustulose-pubescent

Lower glume absent or a veinless, membranous rim; upper glume (50–) 75–100% as long as the entire spikelet; upper lemmas dark purple-brown at maturity; spikelets of the middle portion of the primary panicle branches usually borne in trios on pedicels that are adnate to the branch axis (at least the longer pedicels of each cluster); leaf sheaths glabrous over the surface (rarely pubescent, the upper margins sometimes ciliate)

c4.text: Spikelets 1.7–2.3 mm long; plants with axillary panicles, these often concealed in the leaf sheaths
Spikelets 1.2–1.7 mm long; plants without axillary panicles

c1.text: Spikelets 1.4–2.5 mm long, paired at each node; ligules 0.2–0.5 mm long
Spikelets 2.3–3.3 mm long, solitary at each node [Fig. ]; ligules 1.5–3.8 mm long
This genus contains exactly one species.

This genus contains exactly one species.
Basal and lower stem leaf blades similar in shape, elongate and narrow, (6.3–) 9.6–30 times as long as wide, erect to ascending, crowded [Fig. ]; reproductive stems with 2–4 leaves

Basal and lower stem leaf blades dissimilar, the crowded basal leaves ovate to lanceolate and spreading, 2.3–7.3 times as long as wide, the stem leaf blades longer and only rarely crowded; reproductive stems with 3–14 leaves

c2.text: Upper glume and lower lemma pointed at the apex and surpassing the upper (i.e., fertile) lemma by (0.2–) 0.5–1 mm; spikelets 3.2–4.3 mm long; terminal panicle with 7–20 (–25) spikelets
Upper glume and lower lemma rounded to subacute at the apex, not surpassing upper lemma or surpassing it by no more than 0.3 mm; spikelets 2–3.2 mm long; terminal panicle with (12–) 20–70 spikelets

c3.text: Leaf blades with a white or green-white cartilaginous margin, cordate at base; spikelets 1.4–1.8 mm long, obovoid-spherical, nearly as wide as long
Leaf blades without or with a poorly developed cartilaginous margin, cordate to narrowed at base; spikelets 0.8–5.2 mm long, ellipsoid to obovoid, distinctly longer than wide

c4.text: Leaf sheaths viscid near the apex, especially on the surface away from the margins, long spreading-pubescent with ± soft hairs except near the base where moderately to densely retorse-pubescent above a prominent, glabrous, viscid band [Fig. ]
Leaf sheaths not viscid near the apex, variously glabrous or pubescent, without or, less commonly, with a prominent band of retrorse pubescence at the base, lacking a viscid band at the base

c5.text: Ligules composed of a membranous base that is ciliate apically; plants from rhizomes (usually from caudices in D. commutatum ); leaf blades 5–40 mm wide, truncate to cordate at base (often narrowed to the base in D. xanthophysum )
Ligules composed entirely of hairs; plants from caudices; leaf blades 2–12 (–15) mm wide, narrowed to rounded at the base (truncate to cordate in D. boreale and some D. dichotomum )

c6.text: Leaf blades strictly ascending to erect; panicle usually cylindrical, 1–4 (–5) cm wide, more than 2 times as tall as wide, with strictly ascending to erect branches [Fig. ]; spikelets rounded at apex
Leaf blades spreading to ascending; panicle usually broader, (3–) 4–13 cm wide, mostly 1–2 times as long as wide, with spreading to ascending branches; spikelets pointed to bluntly pointed at apex

c7.text: Leaf sheaths pubescent with pustulose-based hairs [Fig. ]; rhizomes 3–5 mm thick; reproductive stems with (5–) 7–14 leaves
Leaf sheaths glabrous or pubescent with non-pustulose-based hairs; rhizomes up to 2 mm thick or absent; reproductive stems with 4–6 leaves

c8.text: Upper glume and lower lemma obtuse to subacute (note: those of the secondary panicles often sharply acute at the apex), not or hardly surpassing the upper lemma; leaf blades 15–30 mm wide, flat to the tip; spikelets sparsely pubescent
Upper glume and lower lemma acute to long-acute, surpassing the upper lemma; leaf blades 7–15 mm wide, tapering to an involute tip; spikelets glabrous or sparsely pubescent

c9.text: Stems densely crisp-puberulent; ligules up to 0.3 mm long; spikelets 2.2–3.2 mm long; stem leaf blades 5–10 mm wide; plants from caudices
Stems glabrous or shortly pilose; ligules 0.4–0.9 mm long; spikelets 2.9–5.2 mm long; stem leaf blades 15–40 mm wide; plants from knotty rhizomes

c10.text: Spikelets 2.9–3.9 mm long; nodes nearly glabrous to sparsely (rarely moderately) pubescent with retrorsely oriented hairs, the longer hairs up to 0.8 (–1.4) mm long
Spikelets 3.8–5.2 mm long; nodes moderately to densely (rarely sparsely) pubescent with retrorsely oriented hairs, the longer hairs 1.3–3.4 mm long [Fig. ]

c11.text: Spikelets 2.7–4.2 mm long; upper glumes often with a purple or orange-tan to orange spot or blotch near the base, strongly veined
Spikelets 0.8–2.6 mm long; upper glumes usually without an orange or purple area at base, weakly to strongly veined

c12.text: Ligule a conspicuous band of hairs 1–5 mm tall that protrudes above the summit of the sheath
Ligule nearly absent or up to 1 mm long, the hairs hardly protruding above the summit of the sheath

c13.text: Spikelets 0.8–1 (–1.1) mm long; stems 0.3–0.8 mm thick
Spikelets 1.3–2.6 mm long; stems thicker than (0.8–) 1 mm

c14.text: Spikelets 1.3–2.1 mm long; sheaths glabrous or with hairs usually shorter than 2 (–3) mm
Spikelets 2.1–2.6 mm long; sheaths pubescent with hairs 2–4 mm long

c15.text: Spikelets pubescent; nodes of stem glabrous; leaf blades truncate to cordate at base; uppermost stem leaf erect or ascending; spikelets (1.9–) 2–2.2 (–2.3) mm long

Spikelets glabrous or pubescent; nodes of stem glabrous or the lower nodes slightly to evidently retrorse-pubescent; leaf blades narrowed to the base in common forms (varying to truncate to cordate); uppermost stem leaf usually spreading; spikelets 1.5–2.5 mm long

c1.text: This genus contains exactly one species.
Upper glumes and lower lemmas distinctly verrucose with hemispherical protruberences, faintly veined [Fig. ]
Upper glumes and lower lemmas not verrucose, with distinct veins

c2.text: Plants perennial, from rhizomes
Plants annual, from fibrous roots

c3.text: Panicle open, with ascending to spreading branches; plants sometimes pubescent on the leaf sheaths and/or blades
Panicle contracted, with strictly ascending to appressed branches [Fig. ]; plants glabrous throughout

c4.text: Lower glume truncate to subacute at the apex, 20–33% as long as the upper glume; sheaths ± compressed, glabrous; plants often somewhat spongy near base
Lower glume acute to acuminate at the apex, 33–75% as long as the upper glume; sheaths ± terete, pubescent; plants not spongy near base

c5.text: Spikelets 4–6 mm long; upper (i.e., fertile) florets 2–2.5 mm wide; panicles dense, often arching or nodding at maturity
Spikelets 1.4–4 mm long; upper florets 0.4–0.9 mm wide; panicles open, upright

c6.text: Panicles with ascending to spreading-ascending branches, more than 2 times as tall as wide, 1–6 cm wide, with glabrous axillary pulvini; anthers 1.2–1.5 mm long

Panicles with spreading-ascending to spreading branches, less than 2 times as tall as wide, 4–24 cm wide (narrower in depauperate individuals), with pubescent or glabrous axillary pulvini; anthers 0.7–1.2 mm long

c7.text: Panicle usually more than 50% of the total plant height [Fig. ], often breaking at the base of the peduncle and wind-dispersed; spikelets (1.9–) 2.3–4 mm long; upper floret usually light brown-yellow to light brown (rarely dark brown), 0.45–0.60 times as long as the entire spikelet

Panicle usually less than 50% of the total plant height, not breaking at the base of the peduncle; spikelets 1.4–2.4 mm long; upper floret dark brown at maturity (light brown in P. philadelphicum var. campestre ), 0.54–0.79 times as long as the entire spikelet

c8.text: Anthers (0.75–)0.8–1 mm long; uppermost leaf (i.e., the one immediately below the inflorescence) with a blade length to sheath length ratio of 0.8–1.8(–2.6), usually not enclosing the lower branches of the inflorescence in the sheath (i.e., the inflorescence is exserted); spikelets 1.8–2.4 mm long at maturity; upper florets 1.20–1.55 × 0.60–0.85 mm at maturity; lowest node of the inflorescence usually without pilose hairs

Anthers 0.5–0.75 mm long; uppermost leaf with a blade length to sheath length ratio of 2–3, usually enclosing the lower branches of the inflorescence in the sheath (i.e., the inflorescence partly included); spikelets 1.4–1.8(–2) mm long at maturity; upper florets 0.75–1.3(–1.6) × 0.42–0.65(–0.7) mm at maturity; lowest node of the inflorescence pubescent with pilose hairs

c1.text: This genus contains exactly one species.

Lemmas hispid with hairs (0.2–) 0.4–0.8 (–0.9) mm long [Fig. ], the body (0.8–) 1.1–1.5 (–1.8) mm wide, with conspicuous veins, the midvein much more prominent than the lateral veins; anthers 3.3–6 mm long; ligules 2–3.5 mm long

Lemmas glabrous or minutely scabrous with hairs 0.08–0.14 (–0.2) mm long [Fig. ], the body (0.7–) 0.8–1.2 (–1.4) mm wide, with weak veins of equal prominence; anthers 2–3.5 mm long; ligules 1.8–2.5 mm long
Basal leaf sheaths anthocyanic; stigmas trifid
Basal leaf sheaths not tinged with anthocyanic pigments; stigmas bifid

c2.text: Leaf blades 2.5–6 mm wide, flat; plants colonial from long rhizomes (in part)
Leaf blades 1–3 mm wide, V-shaped in cross-section; plants cespitose, with short rhizomes (in part)

c3.text: Spike 1 per stem
Spikes normally 2 or more per stem

c4.text: Stems 5–20 cm tall, produced singly or few together from long, slender rhizomes; leaf blades 0.3–0.7 mm wide (in part)
Stems 12–70 cm tall, cespitose; widest leaf blades 0.8–1.5 mm wide (in part)

c5.text: Widest leaf blades 4–8 mm wide; anthers 4–6.5 mm long; inflorescences 10–20 mm wide (in part)
Widest leaf blades 1–3 (–3.5) mm wide; anthers (1–) 1.2–3.9 mm long; inflorescences 3–12 (–14) mm wide

c6.text: Spikes 5–18 (–25) per stem; stems produced singly on long rhizomes (in part)
Spikes 2–8 per stem; stems cespitose

c7.text: Ligules 0.3–1.7 mm long; anthers (1–) 1.2–2.2 (–2.3­) mm long; staminate scales 2.2–3.3 mm long (in part)
Ligules 1–3.5 mm long; anthers 1.7–2.9 mm long; staminate scales 2.8–3.9 mm long (in part)

c1.text: Stigmas 2; achenes lenticular to biconvex
Stigmas 3; achenes trigonous

c2.text: Basal sheaths anthocyanic; carpellate scales obtuse at apex; plants of alpine ridges and plateaus
Basal sheaths not tinged with anthocyanic pigments; carpellate scales acute to acuminate at apex; plants of organic soil wetlands

c3.text: Stems 5–20 cm tall, produced singly or few together from long, slender rhizomes; leaves 0.3–0.7 mm wide (in part)
Stems 12–70 cm tall, cespitose; widest leaves 0.8–1.5 mm wide (in part)

c4.text: Spike unisexual; perigynia pubescent (in part)
Spike bisexual; perigynia glabrous

c5.text: Spike gynaecandrous; perigynium with a bidentate beak, the body obconic to obovoid (in part)
Spike androgynous; perigynium beaked or not, the orifice entire to truncate (i.e., without teeth), the body narrow-subulate to globose

c6.text: Perigynia (5–) 5.9–7.8 mm long, narrow-subulate in outline, spreading to reflexed; style persistent on achene
Perigynia 2.5–5.4 mm long, narrow-ellipsoid to ovoid, ascending to appressed; style deciduous from achene

c7.text: Lower carpellate scales foliaceous, surpassing and concealing the perigynium; perigynium with a conspicuous beak; leaves 1.3–5.4 mm wide (in part)
Lower carpellate scales not foliaceous, shorter than to slightly exceeding the perigynium; perigynium beakless; leaves 0.4–1.3 mm wide

c1.text: At least the uppermost spike gynecandrous (i.e., the staminate flowers borne at the base of the spike), the others carpellate or gynecandrous
Spikes androgynous (i.e., the staminate flowers borne at the summit of the spike)

c2.text: Perigynia with flat, wing-like margins (at least in the apical half), not distended to the edges by achene, without spongy tissue at the base; style persisting on summit of achene as a short apiculus
Perigynia with rounded or sharp, unwinged margins, distended to or close to the edges by achene, with spongy tissue at the base; style deciduous from summit of achene

c3.text: Perigynium rounded or with a rounded edge at the margins; achene nearly filling body of perigynium
Perigynium sharp-edged at margins; achene obviously smaller than body of perigynium

c4.text: At least the lower perigynia of each spike spreading; beak of perigynium 0.4–1.7 mm long; style base not enlarged (in part)
Perigynia erect to ascending; beak of perigynium 1.2–2.2 (–2.8) mm long; style base enlarged (in part)

c5.text: Perigynium unequally biconvex (i.e., plump), with a smooth beak up to 0.25 mm long
Perigynium flat or planoconvex, the beak minutely serrulate in most species and 0.3–3.5 mm long

c6.text: Stems produced singly or few together from elongate rhizomes, stolons, or prostrate stems
Stems cespitose, the rhizomes inconspicuous or very short

c7.text: Stems leaning or prostrate, producing upright stems from the axils of dried leaves of the previous year; beak of perigynium 0.3–0.6 mm long; plants of organic soil wetlands
Stems upright, produced from elongate rhizomes; beak of perigynium 0.7–2.7 mm long; plants of sandy, gravelly, or rocky, frequently well-drained, habitats

c8.text: Perigynia sharp-margined but not wing-margined, nerveless or inconspicuously nerved on the adaxial surface; plants phyllopodic, with basal tufts of leaves (in part) (in part)
Perigynia wing-margined, conspicuously nerved on the adaxial surface; plants aphyllopodic, without basal tufts of leaves

c9.text: Leaf sheaths opposite the blade transversely rugose, appearing corrugated
Leaf sheaths opposite the blade smooth, not rugose

c10.text: Spikes 3–10 (–15) per inflorescence, occurring singly at the nodes (in part)
Spikes usually more than 15 per inflorescence, 2 or more produced from some nodes (i.e., the inflorescence branched)

c11.text: Carpellate scales hyaline, with a single vein or 3 veins near the center; culms often wing-angled and easily compressed, usually more than 1 mm wide apically in drying (in part)
Carpellate scales yellow or brown, with hyaline margins, with 3 veins near the center; stems usually firm and less than 1 mm wide apically in drying

c12.text: Perigynia truncate to subcordate at base, tapering from base to apex (in part)
Perigynia cuneate to rounded at base, widened above the base and then tapering to the apex

c13.text: Nodes of the inflorescence with a single spike; leaf sheaths opposite the blade neither red-spotted nor copper-colored (in part)
Some nodes of the inflorescence, especially the basal ones, with 2 or more spikes (i.e., the inflorescence branched); leaf sheaths opposite the blade dotted with red and/or strongly copper-colored

c1.text: Perigynia pubescent, with an evident, bidentate beak ca. 1 mm long
Perigynia glabrous (though minutely papillose in several species), beakless or with a short, ± entire beak 0.1–0.4 mm long (with an obscurely bidentate beak 0.2–0.8 mm long in Carex saxatilis )

c2.text: Perigynia white or gold-orange, biconvex in cross-section; lowest bract of carpellate spikes with a prolonged, closed sheath usually longer than 4 mm
Perigynia green to brown to black, planoconvex to biconvex in cross-section; lowest bract of carpellate spikes lacking a sheath or the sheath shorter than 3 mm

c3.text: Style deciduous from achene in fruit; leaf sheaths with no, or very few, septate partitions; perigynia often minutely papillose, with a short, inconspicuous beak 0.1–0.4 mm long
Style persistent on achene in fruit; leaf sheaths with septate partitions; perigynia smooth, with a distinct beak 0.2–0.8 mm long (in part)

c1.text: Leaf sheaths and blades glabrous or scabrous, but not pubescent
Leaf sheaths and often the blades pubescent

c2.text: Perigynia (5.3–) 6–11.5 mm long, the beak terminated by 2 stiff teeth (1–) 1.2–2.3 (–2.8) mm long (in part)
Perigynia 2.2–6.5 mm long, the beak without teeth or with teeth 0.1–0.8 mm long

c3.text: Lowermost bract of inflorescence (excluding basal spikes) bladeless or with a blade up to 2 mm long, strongly anthocyanic
Lowermost bract of inflorescence with blades more than 3 mm long (usually much longer), not or scarcely anthocyanic

c4.text: Leaf sheaths with cross-septa connecting the longitudinal veins (sometimes the cross-veins are few and obscure); adaxial surface of leaf blades usually with 2 marginal veins that are more prominent than midvein
Leaf sheaths without cross-septa connecting the longitudinal veins or these few and obscure; adaxial surface of leaf blades without 2 marginal veins more prominent than midvein

c5.text: Leaf blades adaxially scabrous; beak of perigynium slightly bent, obscurely bidentate at tip

Leaf blades adaxially smooth or scabrous only along margins and/or near tip; beak of perigynium straight, terminated by two, stiff teeth 0.4–0.8 mm long (with a soft, obscurely toothed tip in C. vestita ) (in part)

c6.text: Vegetative leaf blades involute to triangular-channeled, tapering to an elongate, filiform, curling tip; plants of hydric communities, including peatlands, lakeside fens, and graminoid marshes (in part)

Vegetative leaf blades ± flat to V-shaped in cross-section, pointed at the apex, but not long-prolonged into very thin, curling tips; plants primarily of mesic to xeric soils (frequently of wetlands in C. flacca , but that species with arching or drooping lower spikes)

c7.text: Basal spike of leafy, flowering stems long-peduncled, often arching or even drooping; lateral spikes cylindric, 20–45 mm long, the basalmost with more than 30 perigynia

Basal spike of leafy, flowering stems sessile or short-peduncled, erect to ascending; lateral spikes subglobose to short-obloid or short-ellipsoid, 2–15 mm long, the basalmost with (1–) 3–22 perigynia

c8.text: Style base expanded into a circular ring and persistent at summit of achene; beak of perigynium ca. 0.2 mm long; carpellate scales with a scabrous awn up to 2 mm long
Style base not expanded, deciduous; beak of perigynium 0.4–2 mm long; carpellate scales awnless or with an awn shorter than 1 mm (in part)

c9.text: Perigynia 4.8–12 mm long, with a beak terminated by 2 stiff teeth 0.8–3 mm long; style persistent at summit of achene (in part)
Perigynia 1.7–5 mm long, beakless or beaked and then terminated by teeth up to 0.7 mm long; style deciduous

c10.text: Perigynia 1.7–4 mm long, beakless or essentially so; uppermost spike bearing some perigynia (in part)
Perigynia 3.5–5 mm long, with a prominent, bidentate beak; uppermost spike entirely staminate

c1.text: Leaf sheaths, and often the blades, pubescent
Leaf sheaths and blades glabrous or scabrous, but not pubescent

c2.text: Perigynia (6.5–) 7–12 mm long, with a beak 2.1–4 mm long that is terminated by 2 teeth (1.2–) 1.5–3 mm long; style persistent at summit of achene (in part)
Perigynia 2–5 mm long, without a beak or with a beak up to 1.5 mm long that is terminated by 2 teeth up to 0.5 mm long; style deciduous from achene

c3.text: Perigynia beakless or essentially so; adaxial surface of leaf blades without 2 marginal veins more prominent than midvein (in part)
Perigynia with a distinct beak; adaxial surface of leaf blades usually with 2 marginal veins that are more prominent than midvein (in part)

c4.text: Style persistent on achene; sheaths, and often blades, of larger leaves septate-nodulose
Style deciduous from achene; sheaths and blades not septate-nodulose (except in section Ceratocystis and very rarely others)

c5.text: Body of perigynium obconic, abruptly tapering to the beak; terminal spike gynecandrous or entirely staminate (in part)
Body of perigynium lanceoloid or ellipsoid to ovoid or rhombic-ovoid, gradually to moderately tapering to the beak; terminal spike staminate

c6.text: Perigynia 10–20 mm long; staminate spikes usually 1 per plant; carpellate spikes compact, globose to ovoid or obovoid (in part)
Perigynia (3.2–) 3.6–12.5 mm long; staminate spikes mostly 1–3 per plant; carpellate spikes compact to elongate, obloid or ovoid to cylindric (sometimes nearly globose in a few species)

c7.text: Carpellate scales with a long, scabrous awn, the body of the scale often ciliate on the margins (in part)
Carpellate scales without prominent scabrous awns (sometimes with a smooth awn in C. striata ), without ciliate margins

c8.text: Perigynia with 5–14 (–15) veins, relatively thin-walled (in part)
Perigynia with 14–28 veins, firm, thick-walled (in part)

c9.text: Perigynia with a serrulate wing-margin (this often revolute); achenes 4–7.5 mm long; inflorescence usually composed of 20 or more spikes densely aggregated together into ± a single cluster (the lowest spike sometimes removed from the others) (in part)
Perigynia without a wing-margin; achenes 1–2.7 mm long; inflorescence composed of 1–9 spikes, these not aggregated into a dense cluster (except in C. media )

c10.text: Uppermost spike gynecandrous
Uppermost spike entirely staminate or androgynous

c11.text: Perigynia minutely papillose; adaxial surface of leaf blades without 2 marginal veins more prominent than midvein; leaf blades V-shaped in cross-section (at least when young); lateral spikes globose to obloid, 5–20 (–25) mm long

Perigynia without minute papillae; adaxial surface of leaf blades usually with 2 marginal veins that are more prominent than midvein; leaf blades M-shaped cross-section (at least when young), sometimes ± flat at maturity; lateral spikes cylindric, 15–60 mm long (in part)

c12.text: Perigynia minutely papillose
Perigynia smooth

c13.text: Lateral spikes arching to nodding; some roots with a dense, felt-like pubescence of yellow-brown hairs
Lateral spikes erect or ascending; roots without dense pubescence (in part)

c14.text: Lowest carpellate scales concealing and much surpassing the perigynia, entirely green, leaf-like (in part)
Lowest carpellate scales not surpassing perigynia, green to yellow-green or brown, with hyaline margins, not leaflike

c15.text: Lower perigynia in each spike horizontally spreading to reflexed; leaf sheaths, and often blades, of larger leaves septate-nodulose (in part)
Lower perigynia in each spike ascending to spreading-ascending; leaf sheaths and blades not septate-nodulose

c16.text: Lateral spikes 25–80 mm long; adaxial surface of leaf blades with 2 marginal veins more prominent than midvein; leaf blades M-shaped in cross-section (at least when young), sometimes ± flat at maturity (in part)
Lateral spikes 4.5–11.3 mm long; adaxial surface of leaf blades without 2 marginal veins more prominent than midvein; leaf blades V-shaped in cross-section (at least when young) (in part)

c1.text: Style persistent on achene; perigynia (2.2–) 3.4–19 mm long
Style deciduous from achene; perigynia 1.5–6.8 (–9.5) mm long

c2.text: Teeth of perigynium reflexed; achenes narrow-obloid
Teeth of perigynium erect; achenes obloid-ovoid or obloid-obovoid to ellipsoid, rhomboid, or rhombic-ovoid

c3.text: Body of perigynium obconic, abruptly tapering to the beak; uppermost spike gynecandrous or entirely staminate (in part)
Body of perigynium lanceoloid to ovoid or obovoid, moderately to gradually tapering to the beak; uppermost spike staminate

c4.text: Carpellate scales with a long, scabrous awn, the body of the scale often ciliate on the margins (in part)
Carpellate scales either without prominent scabrous awns or with awns much shorter than the body of the scale, without ciliate margins

c5.text: Perigynia 8.7–12.1 mm long, lanceoloid, 4–7 times as long as wide; basal sheaths yellow-brown to brown, without anthocyanins
Perigynia 11–19 mm long, narrow-ovoid, less than 7 times as long as wide; basal sheaths usually tinged with anthocyanic pigments (in part)

c6.text: Leaf blades V-shaped or U-shaped in cross-section (at least when young); adaxial surface of leaf blades without 2 marginal veins that are more prominent than midvein
Leaf blades M-shaped in cross-section (at least when young), sometimes ± flat at maturity; adaxial surface of leaf blades usually with 2 marginal veins that are more prominent than midvein

c7.text: Bracts of inflorescence consisting of only a sheath; perigynia green, maturing glossy, dark brown
At least the lowest bracts of the inflorescence with a short blade; perigynia variously colored, but not glossy dark brown at maturity

c8.text: Lower perigynia in each spike horizontally spreading to reflexed; carpellate spikes globose to short-ellipsoid or short-cylindric (in part)
Lower perigynia in each spike ascending to spreading-ascending; carpellate spikes short-cylindric or ovoid to narrow-cylindric

c9.text: Abaxial leaf blade and surface of perigynia minutely papillose; plants colonial from long rhizomes, with strongly glaucous leaves (in part)

Abaxial leaf blade and surface of perigynia without papillae; plants loosely to densely cespitose from short rhizomes (colonial from long rhizomes in C. crawei ), with green to moderately glaucous leaves

c10.text: Perigynia rounded at base, apically with convexly rounded sides, often with red-brown or yellow streaks and spots (in part)
Perigynia tapering to base, apically with flat or somewhat convex sides, without streaks or spots

c11.text: Perigynia with 2 evident marginal veins, the remaining veins obscure, the beak erect; achenes 1.2–1.7 mm long; lateral spikes, especially the lower, usually spreading or drooping (ascending in alpine populations)
Perigynia with (22–) 25–32 evident veins, the beak usually curved or bent; achenes 2–2.8 mm long; lateral spikes usually erect or ascending (in part)

c12.text: Perigynium with 2 evident marginal veins, the remaining veins obscure or evident only in the basal portion of the perigynium body
Perigynium with 2 evident marginal veins as well as 8–40+ additional distinct, fine veins that travel ± the length of the perigynium body

c13.text: Perigynium abruptly tapered to a beak 1.7–4 mm long, the beak nearly as long as the perigynium body and terminated by 2 hyaline teeth 0.5–1.4 mm long (in part)
Perigynium beakless or moderately tapering to a beak 0.1–1.8 (–2.2) mm long, the beak definitely shorter than the perigynium body and entire or weakly bidentate with terminal teeth up to 0.1 mm long

c14.text: Perigynium with a curved or abruptly bent beak; plants cespitose, with short rhizomes (in part)
Perigynium beakless or with a straight beak; plants colonial from long rhizomes

c15.text: Perigynium neither streaked nor spotted with red-brown; abaxial leaf blade and surface of perigynia densely and minutely papillose (both usually smooth in C. vaginata ) (in part)
Perigynium often streaked or dotted with red-brown; abaxial leaf blade and surface of perigynia without minute papillae (in part)

c16.text: Perigynia rounded at base, apically with convexly rounded sides
Perigynia tapering to base, apically with flat or somewhat convex sides

c17.text: Perigynia with impressed veins (especially in drying), without red-brown or yellow streaks or dots; carpellate scales with an awn 0.2–6 mm long (sometimes awnless in C. glaucodea )
Perigynia with elevated nerves, often with red-brown or yellow streaks or dots; carpellate scales sharply pointed to shortly awned, the awns up to 0.5 mm long when present (in part)

c18.text: Plants colonial from long rhizomes; abaxial leaf blade and surface of perigynia minutely papillose (view at 20 × or higher magnification; both usually smooth in C. vaginata ) (in part)
Plants loosely to densely cespitose from short rhizomes; abaxial leaf blade and surface of perigynia without minute papillae

c19.text: Perigynia with 8–20 veins; beak of perigynium (when present) terminated by 2 teeth 0.2–1 mm long; uppermost spike gynecandrous or entirely staminate (in part)
Perigynia with (22–) 25–40+ veins; beak of perigynium ± entire, without 2 apical teeth; uppermost spike entirely staminate

c20.text: Perigynia with sharp angles and flat faces, usually with 40 or more closely spaced veins; plants often with a long-peduncled, carpellate spike borne from near the base of the plant
Perigynia with rounded angles and convex faces, mostly with 22–32 veins; plants usually without basal spikes (in part)

c1.text: This genus contains exactly one species.
This genus contains exactly one species.
Vegetative leaf blades pubescent, at least on the abaxial midrib; bracteal leaves subtending the capitula usually shorter than capitula; ray flowers blue, white, or pink
Vegetative leaf blades glabrous; bracteal leaves subtending capitula usually exceeding capitula; ray flowers purple
Pappus of 10 inconspicuous, hyaline scales and 20–35 longer, slender bristles; involucre 7–14 mm tall; basal leaf blades 10–50 mm wide, glabrous; plants perennial from a short caudex

Pappus of 5 evident, flat scales alternating with 5 longer, slender bristles [Fig. ]; involucre 3–7 mm tall; basal leaf blades 1–12 mm wide, villous-hirsute or glandular-hirsute to glabrous; plants annual
This genus contains exactly one species.

Inner (i.e., longer) involucral bracts with a dark, corniculate appendage at the tip [Fig. ]; cypsela body at maturity purple-red to brown-red; leaf blades lacerate-lobed with narrow lobes, the medial lateral lobes of leaf blades 1–10 (–12) mm wide at the base

Inner involucral bracts lacking dark, horn-like appendages at the tip; cypsela body at maturity light brown to gray-brown to brown; leaf blades toothed to lobed, the medial lateral lobes of leaf blades, when present, (5–) 10–32 (–38) mm wide

c2.text: Outer (i.e., shorter) involucral bracts, as well as the inner ones, persistently appressed to ascending; plants 5–10 cm tall; involucres excluding the outer calyculus 12–16 mm tall
Outer involucral bracts becoming reflexed [Fig. ]; plants (1–) 5–75 cm tall; involucres excluding the outer calyculus (13–) 14–25 mm tall

c3.text: Cypsela with a body (2–) 2.5–2.8 (–4) mm long that is muricate only in the apical half [Fig. ], with a beak 7–9 mm long; outermost involucral bracts (i.e., the reflexed ones) lanceolate

Cypsela with a body 2.8–3.8 mm long that is usually muricate also in the basal half (sometimes all the way to the base), with a beak 8–12 mm long; outermost involucral bracts ovate to broad-lanceolate

c1.text: Involucral bracts sparsely to densely long-hirsute (caution: sometimes only a few hairs are present on the involucre of N. serpentarius , look near the base of the inner involucral bracts) [Figs. , ]
Involucral bracts glabrous except for minute, apical cilia [Fig. ]

c2.text: Lower leaf blades simple, broad-oblanceolate to obovate, the middle and upper blades clasping; capitulescence tall and narrow, raceme-like; rays pink to purple (infrequently white); capitula with (9–) 11–29 flowers [Fig. ]

Lower leaf blades pinnately or palmately lobed or simple and then ovate to elliptic, the middle and upper blades short-petioled or sessile, but not clasping; capitulescence broader, corymb- or panicle-like; rays yellow to yellow-white; capitula with 8–14 flowers [Fig. ]

c3.text: Each capitulum with 4–6 inner (i.e., longer) involucral bracts and 5 or 6 flowers
Each capitulum with 7–14 inner involucral bracts and 9–20 flowers [Fig. ]

c4.text: Pappus deep red-brown; rays white to pink to lavender
Pappus light brown to pale yellow-brown; rays green-yellow to yellow-white or white

c5.text: Rays white; axis of capitulescence and often upper portion of stem villous-puberulent; involucral bracts black-green to black, the dark pigmentation resolvable as minute spots or streaks at high magnification (i.e., 30 × and higher); lower leaf blades simple, triangular-sagittate

Rays green-yellow to yellow-white; axis of capitulescence and stem glabrous; involucral bracts green to black, provided with minute, white, waxy papillae (view at 15 × or higher) or with minute, dark spots in exposed situations; lower leaf blades pinnately or palmately lobed

c1.text: Cypselas of 2 kinds—those borne near the margin of the capitulum stout, 7–9 mm long, with a short beak and those from the interior of the capitulum slender, 12–17 mm long, and with a long, slender beak
Cypselas ± uniform, 1.4–7.5 mm long

c2.text: Inner series of involucral bracts glabrous on the adaxial (i.e., inner) surface; cypsela body 1.4–2.5 mm long (up to 4 mm long in the rarely collected C. nicaeensis )
Inner series of involucral bracts pubescent on the adaxial (i.e., inner) surface; cypsela body (2.5–) 3–8 (–9) mm long

c3.text: Abaxial surface of involucral bracts with usually 2 rows of black stipitate glands; involucre 5–8 (–9) mm tall; cypsela body 1.4–2.5 mm long
Abaxial surface of involucral bracts glabrous or glabrate; involucre 8–10 mm tall; cypsela body 2.5–4 mm long

c4.text: Capitula with 10–20 florets; involucral bracts coarsely hispid abaxially; cypsela tapered to a short beak 1–2 mm long

Capitula with 30–100 florets; involucral bracts tomentose to hispidulous abaxially, sometimes also with stipitate glands in C. vesicaria ; cypsela narrowed to summit of ovary and without a beak or with a prominent beak 2–5 mm long

c5.text: Cypsela with a slender beak 2–5 mm long; outer involucral bracts (i.e., the smaller ones) reflexed at maturity, sometimes with stipitate glands on the abaxial surface; abaxial surface of rays red
Cypsela narrowed to summit of ovary but without a beak; outer involucral bracts spreading-ascending to erect, usually without stipitate glands on the abaxial surface; rays entirely yellow

c6.text: Involucre (8–) 10–13 mm tall; cypsela body 4–7.5 mm long, yellow to red-brown, with (10–) 13–20 smooth, longitudinal ribs; pappus 5–7 mm long; stem leaf blades oblanceolate or oblong to spatulate, with plane margins

Involucre 6–9 mm tall; cypsela body (2.5–) 3–4 (–4.5) mm long, red to purple-brown, with 10 minutely scabrous, longitudinal ribs; pappus 4–5 mm long; stem leaf blades linear to lanceolate or oblanceolate, with revolute margins

c1.text: Cypsela body 1.2–2 (–2.2) mm long, each rib on the surface of the ovary projecting to form a crenulate apex [Fig. ]; pappus bristles mostly 25–40 in 1 series [Fig. ]; rays yellow, yellow with an red abaxial stripe, or orange-red; stems scapose, without leaves or with few and reduced leaves; leaves tapering to an ill-defined petiole; plants with a well-developed rosette of basal leaves at anthesis, commonly with stolons [Fig. ]

Cypsela body (2–) 2.5–5 mm long, each rib apically confluent to form an obscure ring [Fig. ]; pappus bristles mostly 30–60 (or more) in 2 series; rays yellow; stems scapose or evidently leafy; lower leaves usually tapering to a ± distinct petiole; plants with a basal rosette of leaves or these withered at anthesis, never with stolons

c2.text: Reproductive stems bearing a solitary capitulum or a capitulescence with 2–4 (–6) capitula on elongate peduncles (5–) 15–150 mm long [Fig. ]; leaf blades 2–4 (–6) times as long as wide; plants 3–25 (–40) cm tall

Reproductive stems bearing (3–) 5–30 (–50) capitula, these usually in compact, corymb-like capitulescences on short peduncles 1–15 (–28) mm long; leaf blades 3–8 times as long as wide; plants (10–) 20–100 cm tall

c3.text: Capitulescence with 1 or 2 (–3) capitula [Fig. ]; involucres 7.5–9 (–10) mm tall; leaf blades densely pubescent with stellate hairs on the abaxial surface, the hairs usually contiguous and concealing the surface
Capitulescence with (1–) 2–4 (–6) capitula; involucres (9–) 10–13 mm tall; leaf blades moderately pubescent with stellate hairs on the abaxial surface, the hairs not so numerous as to be contiguous

c4.text: Ray flowers orange-red (drying dark red); involucral bracts 1.5–3 mm wide
Ray flowers yellow; involucral bracts 0.5–1.25 mm wide

c5.text: Involucres 7.5–9 mm tall; pappus bristles 4–5 (–6) mm long; ray corollas 8–12 mm long; leaf blades green, with abundant setae adaxially; plants with short or, more commonly, long rhizomes and often also short, prostrate stolons

Involucres 5–6 (–7) mm tall; pappus bristles 3–4 mm long; ray corollas 6–9 mm long; leaf blades glaucous, sparsely and unevenly setose to subglabrous adaxially; plants usually with short, praemorse rhizomes and also usually lacking prostrate stolons (sometimes with divergent to ascending branches)

c6.text: Peduncles lacking stellate hairs or with very few stellate hairs; basal leaf blades lacking stellate-hairs on the abaxial surface, either glabrous or with simple, eglandular hairs; involucral bracts mostly 0.5–0.75 mm wide

Peduncles moderately to densely pubescent with stellate hairs; basal leaf blades sometimes with minute stellate-hairs on the abaxial surface (longer, simple, eglandular ones may be present as well); involucral bracts mostly 0.75–1 mm wide

c7.text: Reproductive stems with (4–) 6–50 leaves; basal leaves mostly absent or withered at anthesis, not forming a conspicuous rosette
Reproductive stems with 0–5 (–10) leaves, these often reduced and bract-like; basal leaves present at anthesis, forming a conspicuous rosette

c8.text: Involucres 6–7 mm tall; pappus bristles 4–5 mm long; ray corollas 5–8 mm long; capitula with 8–20 (–30) flowers; peduncles very slender, 0.2–0.3 mm thick
Involucres 7–10 (–11) mm tall; pappus bristles (4.5–) 5–7 mm long; ray corollas 8–18 mm long;

c9.text: Cypsela body tapering to an expanded, circular apex where the pappus bristles attach [Fig. ]; capitula with 20–40 flowers; capitulescence panicle-like, cylindrical in outline, with short lower branches

Cypsela body truncate or scarcely narrowed to the circular apex [Fig. ]; capitula with (30–) 40–100 flowers; capitulescence corymb-like or umbel-like, with elongate lower branches (sometimes narrow and panicle-like in H. scabrum )

c10.text: Peduncles with abundant stipitate glands [Fig. ]; leaf blades entire or remotely denticulate
Peduncles with very few or no stipitate glands; at least the lower leaf blades usually dentate

c11.text: Hairs of the lower stem and leaf surfaces simple, firm, and bulbous-based, short compound hairs usually absent from the leaf surfaces
Hairs of the lower stem and leaf surfaces simple or compound, but not bulbous-based, that of the leaves sometimes compound

c12.text: Involucral bracts tapering to an acuminate apex; reproductive stems 10–35 cm tall, with 4–10 leaves (in part)
Involucral bracts tapering to a narrow-rounded to acute apex; reproductive stems 15–60 (–150) cm tall, with 6–50 leaves

c13.text: Leaf blades linear to lanceolate or narrow-oblong, the principal ones 3–15 (–19) mm wide, mostly 4–12 times as long as wide, provided with abundant stout, rigid, conical hairs, at least toward the margin of the blade
Leaf blades lanceolate to oblong-lanceolate or narrow-ovate, the principal ones (7–) 12–40 mm wide, mostly 2–5 times as long as wide, lacking rigid, conical hairs or these very sparse

c14.text: Leaf blades entire or merely denticulate, adaxially green to glaucous-green and usually with red to purple coloration that closely follows the outline of the veins; ray corollas 7–11 mm long; mid-portion of reproductive stem glabrous or nearly so

At least the lower leaf blades with conspicuous, sharp teeth, adaxially green, red coloration, when present, either more randomly patterned (i.e., mottled) or merely suffusing a region of the blade; ray corollas 12–18 mm long; mid-portion of reproductive stem with setose or glandular hairs or both

c15.text: Basal leaf blades truncate to cordate at the base; reproductive stems with 0–2 leaves
Basal leaf blades tapering to the base; reproductive stems with 2–10 leaves

c16.text: Leaf blades 7–20 mm wide; peduncles lacking stipitate glands; plants 10–35 cm tall (in part)
Leaf blades 15–50 mm wide; peduncles stipitate-glandular; plants 30–60 (–100) cm tall

c17.text: Leaf blades with red to red-purple blotches, streaks, and/or spots [Fig. ]; stem leaves mostly numbering 2–4; involucres with numerous stipitate glands
Leaf blades green, without red to red-purple coloration; stem leaves numbering mostly 2–8; involucres with few to numerous stipitate glands

c1.text: Plants perennial, with deep-seated, creeping rhizomes; capitula 3–5 cm wide in flower; involucre 14–22 mm tall in fruit
Plants annual, with taproots; capitula 1.5–2.5 cm wide in flower; involucre 9–13 mm tall in fruit

c2.text: Cypsela body with 3 (–5) ribs on each face, otherwise smooth; leaf blades relatively firm, with stiff prickles and rounded basal auricles [Fig. ]; peduncles glandular-pubescent

Cypsela body with 5–7 ribs on each face and transversely rugulose; leaf blades relatively soft, with softer prickles and triangular to narrow-triangular basal auricles; peduncles glabrous or infrequently with a few glandular hairs

c1.text: This genus contains exactly one species.
Basal leaf blades of commonly cultivated forms ovate to orbicular, 12–25 cm wide; plants rare escapes from cultivation
Basal leaf blades linear to ovate, 0.6–12 cm wide; plants native or introduced, but not generally cultivated

c2.text: Cypsela apically beakless or with a short, stout beak 0.1–0.5 mm long [Fig. ], the body compressed but not flat; pappus light brown to light olive-brown; capitula with (15–) 20–30 (–55) flowers; corollas blue to white or infrequently yellow
Cypsela apically with a slender, elongate beak 1–6 mm long [Fig. ], the body ± flat; pappus ± white; capitula with 6–24 (–27) flowers; corollas yellow (sometimes blue in age or drying)

c3.text: Cypsela body gray or yellow-gray to light brown, with (3–) 5–9 prominent nerves on each face; leaf blades often prickly setose on the abaxial midrib
Cypsela body brown to dark brown, with 1 prominent nerve on each face, sometimes with an additional pair of faint nerves [Fig. ]; leaf blades not prickly setose

c4.text: Involucre 10–15 mm tall in fruit; cypsela body 4.5–6 mm long including the beak; pappus 5–7 mm long
Involucre 15–22 mm tall in fruit; cypsela body 7–10 mm long including the beak; pappus 8–12 mm long

c1.text: This genus contains exactly one species.

Peduncles slender, not enlarged in flower and scarcely enlarged even in fruit; cypsela body including beak 15–25 mm long; involucre 12–24 mm tall in flower, becoming 19–38 mm tall in fruit; involucral bracts shorter than to equaling the ray flowers in length

Peduncles apically enlarged and fistulous in flower and fruit [Fig. ]; cypsela body 25–40 mm long; involucre 25–40 mm tall in flower, becoming 40–70 mm tall in fruit; involucral bracts exceeding ray flowers in length

c2.text: Ray corollas yellow; pappus white to sordid-white; leaf apex usually straight (i.e., not prominently curved)
Ray corollas purple; pappus light brown; leaf apex usually recurved to recoiled

c1.text: Leaf blades glabrous or puberulent; involucre 8–10 mm tall during anthesis (elongating to 17 mm in fruit); rays relatively inconspicuous, not much exceeding the involucre (if at all) and ca. 2 times as long as wide; body of inner cypselas 6–8.5 (–13.5) mm long; plants annual from a taproot

Leaf blades hispid; involucre 10–15 mm tall during anthesis (elongating to 25 mm in fruit); rays evident, exceeding the involucre and ca. 4 times as long as wide; body of inner cypselas 8–17 mm long; plants perennial from a caudex and fibrous roots (sometimes 1 or more roots thickened as well)
This genus contains exactly one species.

Pappus of inner flowers with an inner series of plumose bristles and an outer series of scales that may be tipped with a scabrous awn, that of the outer flowers reduced to a short, laciniate crown; involucre 6–11 mm tall during anthesis, calyculate

Pappus of inner flowers and outer flowers alike, well-developed, with an inner series of plumose bristles and an outer series of slender scales or barbellate bristles; involucre 10–18 mm tall during anthesis, not calyculate
This genus contains exactly one species.
This genus contains exactly one species.
This genus contains exactly one species.
Upper stem and branches with conspicuous, prickly and undulate-margined wings formed by decurrent leaf bases
Neither the stem nor the branches with decurrent wings

c2.text: Involucre 25–40 mm tall; involucral bracts (or most of them) with prominent spine-tips 2–6 mm long; leaf blades adaxially with abundant, appressed spines
Involucre 10–15 (–20) mm tall; involucral bracts lacking spine tips or with short, vestigial spines up to 1 mm long; leaf blades adaxially with sparse, septate hairs

c3.text: Involucre 10–20 mm tall; capitula with, or with mostly, unisexual flowers by abortion; plants perennial, colonial from deep-seated, creeping roots, the reproductive stems not arising from a rosette of leaves
Involucre 20–50 mm tall; capitula with bisexual flowers; plants biennial or short-lived perennial, not colonial, the reproductive stems arising from a rosette of leaves

c4.text: Capitula closely invested by series of narrow, spiny-margined leaves that form a false involucre sometimes overtopping the true involucre [Fig. ]; corollas yellow (rarely purple); scarious apex of innermost (i.e., longer) involucral bracts slender and not expanded
Capitula either without subtending leaves or with 1 or 2 approximate, reduced leaves; corollas purple to pink (rarely white); scarious apex of innermost involucral bracts expanded or not

c5.text: Leaf blades persistently white-tomentose on the abaxial surface
Leaf blades abaxially thinly tomentose or arachnoid-pubescent when young, becoming glabrate in age

c6.text: Adaxial surface of leaf blades thinly tomentose (rarely glabrate); stem thinly, uniformly, and persistently tomentose; pappus bristles 20–30 mm long; plants from taproots and also with horizontal roots that produce new shoots

Adaxial surface of leaf blades glabrate or sparsely villous with septate hairs; stem glabrate, infrequently with thin tomentum apically; pappus bristles 12–25 mm long; plants from taproots and sometimes also a cluster of coarse, fibrous roots, but without prominent horizontal roots

c7.text: Stem leaf blades with flat margins, unlobed or with short lobes separated by shallow sinuses (rarely with deep sinuses and then with broad-triangular lobes); tips of innermost involucral bracts usually dilated and erose to serrulatae
Stem leaf blades with ± revolute margins, evidently pinnately lobed with narrow-lanceolate lobes; tips of innermost involucral bracts slender, not dilated, entire

c8.text: Outer involucral bracts tipped with a coarse spine 3–6 mm long; cypsela body (3–) 3.5–4 mm long
Outer involucral bracts lacking a spine tip or tipped with a vestigial spinule up to 0.5 (–1) mm long; cypsela body 4.5–5.5 mm long

c1.text: This genus contains exactly one species.
Involucres 20–60 mm wide; involucral bract appendages 2–7 mm wide; capitula often nodding; peduncles 2–30 cm long
Involucres 10–25 mm wide; involucral bract appendages 0.5–1 mm wide; capitula erect [Fig. ]; peduncles up to 4 (–10) cm long

c2.text: Abaxial leaf blade surface with dimorphic hairs—longer, curling septate hairs on the veins and sparse to dense tomentum across the surface; involucres 12–17 mm tall; disk corollas 11–16 mm long
Abaxial leaf blade surface with only curling, septate hairs; involucres 14–20 mm tall; disk corollas 13–20 mm long

c1.text: Involucral bracts tipped by 1 or more spines [Fig. ]; disk corollas yellow, white to pink, or purple
Involucral bracts without spine-tips; disk corollas white to pink, red, or purple, or blue

c2.text: Capitula sessile, closely subtended and partially concealed by a series of non-spine-tipped, foliaceous bracts; pappus composed of 2 series of awns—the outer series smooth or minutely barbellate and 9–10 mm long, the inner series minutely pubescent with spreading hairs and 2–5 mm long
Capitula sessile or borne on peduncles, not concealed by foliaceous bracts; pappus of capillary bristles or absent

c3.text: Apical spine of involucral bracts 2–3 (–5) mm long; involucre 4–5 mm wide; flowers lacking pappus; apical appendage of involucral bracts decurrent on body of bract, therefore the base of the appendage concave; disk corollas usually white to pink or pale purple; stems angled but not winged

Apical spine of involucral bracts 5–25 (–30) mm long; involucre 7–12 (–15) mm wide; at least the central flowers of a capitulum with pappus; apical appendage of involucral bracts not decurrent on body of bract, therefore the base of the appendage ± truncate; disk corollas yellow or varying shades of purple; stems with decurrent wings (except C. calcitrapa )

c4.text: Disk corollas pale purple, pink-purple, or purple; stem leaves not decurrent
Disk corollas yellow; stem leaves long-decurrent

c5.text: Apical spine of involucral bracts 10–15 (–30) mm long; marginal flowers of capitulum lacking pappus; disk corollas eglandular; pappus of inner flowers mostly 3–5 mm long, ca. twice as long as cypsela body
Apical spine of involucral bracts 5–8 mm long; marginal flowers of capitulum with pappus; disk corollas glandular; pappus of inner flowers mostly 1.5–3 mm long, ca. as long as cypsela body

c6.text: Apical appendage of involucral bracts decurrent on body of bract, therefore, the base of the appendage concave [Fig. ]; principal stem leaf blades entire or conspicuously pinnatifid with linear to oblong lobes

Apical appendage of involucral bracts not decurrent on body of bract, therefore the base of the appendage ± truncate [Fig. ]; principal stem leaf blades entire to toothed (infrequently with a few small lobes on larger leaf blades)

c7.text: Plants annual; stem leaf blades linear
Plants perennial; stem leaf blades oblong or lanceolate to ovate

c8.text: Appendage of involucral bracts decurrent nearly to the base of the bract; leaf blades entire (rarely the lower ones obscurely dentate); involucre 10–15 mm wide
Appendage of involucral bracts decurrent only in the apical half of the bract [Fig. ]; leaf blades pinnatifid; involucre narrower than 10 mm or wider than 15 mm

c9.text: Involocural bracts lacking prominent, longitudinal veins; pappus (3–) 4–5 (–6) mm long; involucre 18–25 mm wide; cypsela bodies 4–5.5 mm long; corollas of fertile flowers 20–25 mm long

Involucral bracts with several, prominent longitudinal veins [Fig. ]; pappus 1–2.5 (–3) mm long (rarely absent); involucre 6–8 mm wide; cypsela bodies 2–3.5 mm long; corollas of fertile flowers 12–15 mm long

c10.text: Apical appendage of involucral bracts often recurved, long-tapering to a filiform-fringed tip, the rachis of the appendage 0.2–0.4 mm wide on the middle bracts

Apical appendage of involucral bracts ascending to appressed (rarely some with a loosely spreading apex), obtuse to acute at tip, the rachis of the appendage 0.5–3.5 mm wide on the middle bracts [Figs. , ]

c11.text: Apical appendage of involucral bracts light brown to brown, those of the middle and outer series irregularly lacerate, those of the inner series often bifid; pappus absent; outer flowers of capitulum usually enlarged and falsely appearing as ray flowers (but the corollas still actinomorphic)

Apical appendage of involucral bracts brown to black, those of the middle and outer series regularly pectinate-fringed [Fig. ], usually none of them bifid; pappus absent or present and then consisting of unequal bristles mostly 0.5–1 mm long; outer flowers of capitulum enlarged or not

c12.text: Apical appendage of involucral bracts 1–2 (–2.2) mm long, with 5–8 fringe segments on each margin, relatively narrow, the appendage not completely obscuring the distal portion of adjacent involucral bracts; involucre definitely taller than wide in life, ca. 1.5 times as tall as wide; outer flowers of capitulum sometimes enlarged and falsely appear as ray flowers

Apical appendage of involucral bracts longer than 2 mm, the larger ones (3–) 4–6 mm long, with 7–15 fringe segments on each margin [Fig. ], relatively broad, obscuring the distal portion of the adjacent involucral bracts; involucre nearly as wide or wider than tall in life; outer flowers of capitulum not enlarged

c1.text: This genus contains exactly one species.
Involucral bracts apically prolonged into a filiform tip 2–8 mm long [Fig. ]
Involucral bracts rounded to acuminate at the apex, but not prolonged

c2.text: Leaf blades lanceolate to narrow-lanceolate, (3.3–) 4–6 or more times as long as wide; pappus brown to purple-brown, the 20 outer scales 0.2–0.6 mm long (rarely longer), abruptly transitioning to the longer, slender, inner bristles

Leaf blades lanceolate to ovate, 2.5–3.5 (–4) times as long as wide; pappus stramineous or very pale brown to nearly white, the outer 30 scales 0.5–1.5 mm long (rarely longer), gradually transitioning to the longer, slender, inner bristles

c3.text: Abaxial surface of leaf blades ± glabrous and conspicuously punctate; capitula with 12–25 (–30) flowers
Abaxial surface of leaf blades thinly to densely tomentose, the pubescence usually concealing the puncta; capitula with (30–) 32–55 (–58) flowers

c1.text: Capitula usually with marginal ray flowers, the rays 0.1–6.3 mm long; leaf blades prominently ± palmately lobed with deep sinuses, the sinuses extending more than 50% of the distance from the margin to the leaf midrib [Fig. ]

Capitula without marginal ray flowers [Fig. ]; leaf blades ± dentate, the lobes absent or obscure, the sinuses (when present) extending much less than 50% of the distance from the margin to the leaf midrib

c2.text: Disk corollas cream-white; bracts of scape usually green, the one subtending the lowermost branch of the capitulescence 17–40 mm wide; leaf blades with (4–) 5 (–6) pairs of lateral veins emerging along the inner margins of the basal sinus

Disk corollas largely purple; bracts of scape usually purple or purple-tinged, the one subtending the lowermost branch of the capitulescence 5–16 mm wide; leaf blades with 2–5 pairs of lateral veins emerging along the inner margins of the basal sinus

c1.text: Rosette leaves smaller, 2–15 (–21) mm wide, 1-veined or sometimes with 2 additional, evanescent, lateral veins, the lateral veins (when present) located to the distance from the midrib to the margin (i.e., near the margin)

Rosette leaves larger, (7–) 15–55 mm wide, with 3 or 5 prominent veins, the pair of lateral veins closest to the midrib located to the distance from the midrib to the margin (i.e., near the center of each half of the leaf blade) [Fig. ]

c2.text: Middle and upper stem leaves blunt- to aristate-tipped [Fig. ], only the leaves of the capitulescence with a scarious appendage (in part)
Middle and upper stem leaves tipped by a flat or involute-margined, scarious appendage [Fig. ]

c3.text: New rosette leaves bright green and promptly glabrous on the adaxial surface (in part)
New rosette leaves white or gray-green and tomentose on the adaxial surface

c4.text: Carpellate involucre 5–7 mm tall; central corollas 2.5–4.3 mm long; body of cypselas 1–1.5 mm long; mature pappus 4–5.5 mm long
Carpellate involucre (6–) 7–10 mm tall; central corollas 4.5–7 mm long; body of cypselas 1.3–2.2 mm long; mature pappus 6–9 mm long

c1.text: This genus contains exactly one species.

Leaf blades decurrent on the stem as thin wings [Fig. ], acuminate at the apex
Leaf blades not decurrent on the stem, obtuse to acute at the apex

c2.text: Stems usually with persistent, white tomentum, sometimes only sparsely so, appearing gray or gray-green, eglandular or infrequently stipitate-glandular near the base; capitula wth 4–8 bisexual flowers and 38–96 carpellate flowers; plants relatively inodorous

Stems rapidly losing most of the white tomentum, appearing green, covered with abundant stipitate glands 0.1–0.2 mm tall; capitula with (7–) 11–20 bisexual flowers and 47–78 carpellate flowers; plants fragrant

c1.text: This genus contains exactly one species.
This genus contains exactly one species.

Stem leaf blades obovate-spatulate, loosely tomentose to glabrate abaxially, weakly bicolored (i.e., adaxial and abaxial surfaces of nearly same color); hairs on adaxial surface of leaf blades slender at base; capitulescence usually interrupted; outer involucral bracts acuminate-apiculate at apex; inner involucral bracts 3–3.5 mm long, not apiculate; receptacles deeply concave

Stem leaf blades usually oblanceolate, closely tomentose abaxially, strongly bicolored; hairs on adaxial surface of leaf blades expanded at base; capitulescence usually continuous; outer involucral bracts acute at apex; inner involucral bracts (3.5–) 4–5 mm long, usually with a minute apiculus; receptacles shallowly concave
Pappus bristles distinct and falling separately; principal leaf blades 12–30 mm long; alpine plants 2–10 cm tall, growing at elevation exceeding 1000 m
Pappus bristles united at the base and falling together; principal leaf blades 25–51 mm long; boreal plants 10–70 cm tall, growing at elevation less than 1000 m

Leaf blades firm, 3–7 (–10) ×2–5 (–5.5) cm, obtuse to acute at the apex, with 7–12 well-developed, rounded to bluntly pointed teeth per margin, 4 or more times as long as the associated petiole; petioles 1–15 (–20) mm long (rarely lacking altogether); roots 0.8–1 (–1.5) mm thick; capitula with 10–19 flowers

Leaf blades herbaceous, (5–) 6–18 ×3–11 (–12) cm, short-acuminate to acuminate at the apex, with 9–25 well-developed, pointed teeth per margin, 1.5–5 times as long as the petiole; petioles of principal leaves 20–80 mm long; roots 0.3–0.8 (–1) mm thick; capitula with (9–) 12–25 flowers
Capitula with 9–23 flowers; leaves with either evident petioles longer than 1 cm or the blades connate at the base
Capitula with (3–) 5 (–9) flowers; leaves sessile or subsessile, not connate at the base

c2.text: Leaf blades narrowly to broadly tapering to a distinct petiole
Leaf blades broad-based, usually connate and surrounding the stem

c3.text: Leaf blades linear to elliptic or oblanceolate, cuneate (i.e., tapering) at the base
Leaf blades lanceolate or oblong to suborbicular, broad-cuneate to cordate at the base [Figs. , ]

c4.text: Involucre 8–11 mm tall; involucral bracts glabrous abaxially or sparsely pubescent near the base
Involucre 4–7 mm tall; involucral bracts moderately to densely pubescent over the abaxial surface

c5.text: Involucral bracts acute to acuminate and prominently white-scarious at the apex [Fig. ]
Involucral bracts rounded to obtuse (sometimes acute) at the apex, with only a thin, white-scarious border near apex [Fig. ]

c6.text: Principal leaf blades 8–15 (–20) mm wide, usually ± evenly serrate with narrow, sharp teeth; capitula with 5–7 (–9) disk flowers; body of cypsela 2–3 mm long

Principal leaf blades (10–) 20–40 mm wide, coarsely and sometimes irregularly serrate to crenate-serrate with broad, pointed to blunt teeth [Fig. ]; capitula with (4–) 5 (–6) disk flowers; body of cypsela 3–4 mm long (in part)

c7.text: Leaf blades 8–30 mm wide, lanceolate to elliptic-oblong, mostly 2.5–7 times as long as wide, opposite; nodes without axillary fascicles or these poorly developed and consisting of few leaves

Leaf blades 0.5–10 (–17) mm wide, linear to lanceolate, mostly 6–40 times as long as wide, whorled in 3s or 4s at each node (sometimes opposite or alternate at the upper nodes); nodes often with well-developed axillary fascicles containing many small leaves

c8.text: Leaves usually 4 per node, sometimes only 3 (rarely fewer), with blades 0.5–5 (–10) mm wide, entire or irregularly few-toothed, 10–40 times as long as wide, the principal leaves with blades 2–7 cm long [Fig. ]; reproductive stems 30–100 cm tall

Leaves usually 3 per node, sometimes 2 or 4 per node (rarely only 1), with blades 5–10 (–17) mm wide, serrate to nearly lacerate-toothed, 6–15 times as long as wide, the principal leaves with blades 6–11 cm long; reproductive stems mostly 75–150 cm tall

c9.text: Leaf blades pinnately veined, lanceolate to oblong, acuminate to subacuminate at the apex; stem glabrous
Leaf blades triple-veined from near the base, oblong to suborbicular, rounded to acute at the apex; stem pubescent

c10.text: Leaf blades oblong or oblong-lanceolate to narrow-ovate, each margin with 3–12 coarse teeth, sometimes the blades more incised with lobe-like teeth near the base [Fig. ]; upper leaves and lower branches of capitulescence often alternate (in part)
Leaf blades oblong-ovate to suborbicular, each margin with 8–25 teeth [Fig. ]; upper leaves and lower branches of capitulescence usually opposite

c11.text: Leaf blades triangular-ovate to suborbicular, mostly 1–1.5 (–1.7) times as long as wide, rounded to obtuse at the apex, usually with crenate margins; principal pair of lateral veins originating above base of leaf blade

Leaf blades oblong-ovate to ovate, mostly 1.5–2 times as long as wide, obtuse to acute at apex, usually with serrate margins [Fig. ]; principal pair of lateral veins originating at the base of leaf blade

c1.text: Capitula with (8–) 9–22 flowers; capitulescence or its divisions flat-topped [Fig. ]; stems typically green with anthocyanic spots or streaks

Capitula with (4–) 5–9 (–10) flowers; capitulescence or its divisions slightly to strongly convex [Fig. ]; stems spotted with anthocyanin or anthocyanic only in bands at the nodes or uniformly anthocyanic throughout the stem

c2.text: Leaf blades triple-veined, with the lowest pair of lateral veins more conspicuous and more prolonged than the other lateral veins, abruptly contracted to the petiole; stems spotted or streaked with anthocyanin
Leaf blades pinnately veined or gradually tapered to the petiole or both; stems usually with anthocyanin concentrated in nodal bands or uniformly distributed throughout the stem

c3.text: Stems usually with anthocyanin concentrated in nodal bands 1–2 cm long, not or only scarcely glaucous, solid or developing a slender central cavity near the base; plants typically occurring in upland, deciduous woodlands and in open, well-drained habitats

Stems usually anthocyanic throughout (though often green in deep shade and sometimes spotted when young), prominently glaucous, developing a large central cavity; plants typically occurring in wetlands, riparian communities, and other low, hydric habitats

This genus contains exactly one species.

Capitula borne mostly on short peduncles 10–50 mm long, with (21–) 25–80 flowers [Fig. ]; disk flowers longer than 11 mm, pubescent adaxially (i.e., inside) near the base of the connate tube; involucre 9–17 mm tall
Capitula ± sessile, with 5–10 (–14) flowers; disk flowers 7–11 mm long, glabrous adaxially; involucre 7–11 mm tall

c2.text: Outer involucral bracts obtuse to rounded at apex, erect; axis of capitulescence usually glabrous
Outer involucral bracts acute to short-acuminate at apex, squarrose; axis of capitulescence usually hirsute

c1.text: Corollas green-white to yellow-white (rarely pink-tinged); lower leaf blades triangular-hastate, sharply toothed; cypsela body 5–7 (–9) mm long
Corollas yellow to orange; leaf blades mostly oblong to obovate in outline, coarsely toothed to 1 or more times pinnately lobed; cypsela body 1.5–2.5 mm long

c2.text: Leaf blades linear to filiform (sometimes parted into linear-filiform lobes); subshrubs with the taproots forming a woody crown
Leaf blades oblong or oblanceolate to ovate or obovate, toothed or pinnately lobed to divided [Fig. ]; annuals with taproots lacking a woody crown

c3.text: Leaf blades and stems densely and conspicuously glandular-pubescent [Fig. ]; cypsela body glabrous; shorter, outer series of involucral bracts 2–4 mm long
Leaf blades and stems pubescent to subglabrous, glandular hairs absent or sparse; cypsela body pubescent; shorter, outer series of involucral bracts 1–2 (–2.5) mm long

c4.text: Rays present, though inconspicuous; involucral bracts without a dark apex; involucre with about 13 principal involucral bracts
Rays absent; involucral bracts with a dark apex, this dark red to red-brown, becoming black [Fig. ]; involucre with about 21 principal involucral bracts

c1.text: This genus contains exactly one species.
This genus contains exactly one species.
Annuals from a short taproot; rays very short and inconspicuous, scarcely or not exceeding the mature pappus, or the rays absent altogether [Fig. ]
Perennials from a rhizome, caudex, or crown; rays elongate and conspicuous

c2.text: Involucral bracts with a chartaceous base and chlorophyllous tip, of several conspicuously different lengths; ray flower corolla longer than the style; saltmarsh plants
Involucral bracts, especially the outer, herbaceous, of nearly equal length; ray flower corolla shorter than the style, the style protruding from the corolla; rare introductions in New England

c3.text: Ray flowers numbering 90–110 or more per capitulum, with a short, but evident, strap-like ray 1.5–2 mm long
Ray flowers numbering 75–95 (rarely more), lacking rays altogether (note: these flowers are still recognizable as a ray flower due to the lack of lobes at the summit of the corolla tube)

c4.text: Basal leaves both cordate and borne on a petiole (often merely truncate or broad-rounded at base of the petiolate blade in S. lowrieanum ) [Fig. ]
Basal leaves not both cordate and borne on a petiole

c5.text: Middle and upper stem leaves sessile and conspicuously clasping the stem; leaves usually with low, crenate teeth
Middle and upper stem leaves petiolate or sessile, generally narrowed to the base and not conspicuously clasping; leaves mostly with prominent, sharp teeth

c6.text: Peduncles with few or no bracts, very uneven, some generally exceeding 1 cm; rays 7–15 mm long; involucral bracts usually green at apex, the outer 0.5–1 mm wide

Peduncles copiously bracteate, especially when the peduncles approach or exceed 1 cm in length; rays 4–8 mm long; involucral bracts often with the chlorophyllous tip partly or wholly obscured by anthocyanin, the outer mostly 0.2–0.7 mm wide

c7.text: Involucral bracts acuminate, with a slender, elongate chlorophyllous zone; branches of capitulescence often strongly ascending
Involucral bracts obtuse to narrow-acute, with an apically dilated chlorophyllous zone [Fig. ]; branches of capitulescence spreading to ascending

c8.text: Petioles scarcely or not at all winged; lower leaves deeply cordate with prominent basal sinuses; leaf blades usually pubescent, not glaucous on the abaxial surface, smooth to scabrous on the adaxial surface
Petioles broadly winged; lower leaves usually rounded or truncate to shallowly cordate; leaf blades glabrous, thinly glaucous on the abaxial surface, very smooth on the adaxial surface

c9.text: Leaf blades auriculate- or cordate-clasping
Leaf blades narrowed to the base

c10.text: Involucral bracts stipitate-glandular [Fig. ]
Involucral bracts eglandular [Figs. , ]

c11.text: Capitula with 45–100 ray flowers, red-purple; stem leaves abundant and crowded
Capitula with 15–30 ray flowers, commonly blue; stems with remote to approximate, but not crowded, leaves

c12.text: Involucral bracts long-acuminate to attenuate at the apex, of nearly equal length; at least the lower portion of the stem usually hispid pubescent with stiff, spreading hairs
Involucral bracts mostly obtuse to acute at the apex, often of different lengths; stem glabrous to pubescent, when pubescent the hairs often softer and/or curving toward stem apex

c13.text: Most or all of the stem leaves conspicuously narrowed to a broadly winged and conspicuously clasping petiolar base; stem often notably flexuous, changing angles at successive nodes
Stem leaves not conspicuously narrowed nor with a prominently clasping base; stems straight or weakly flexuous

c14.text: Stem and leaves below the capitulescence glabrous and glaucous; involucral bracts with a short, rhombic chlorophyllous zone; plants from a short, stout rhizome or woody caudex
Stem and leaves glabrous to pubescent, not glaucous; involucral bracts with an elongate chlorophyllous zone, or the outer involucral bracts entirely green; plants from elongate rhizomes

c15.text: Leaf blades narrow-lanceolate to oblanceolate, narrowing to the base, flat, herbaceous to fleshy; most peduncles shorter than 3 cm; involucral bracts often loose or somewhat spreading apically, commonly green in large part (in part)

Leaf blades tending to be narrow-lanceolate, scarcely narrowing to the base, folded along the midrib, coriaceous; many peduncles longer than 3 cm; involucral bracts usually appressed and with a chartaceous base and green apex (rarely loose, expanded and foliaceous apically) (in part)

c16.text: Involucral bracts with a non-chlorophyllous spine tip, with short, stiff cilia on the margins [Fig. ]; leaf blades linear to oblanceolate, moderately to densely pubescent on both surfaces and provided with stiff, marginal cilia

Involucral bracts lacking a spine tip (though with an involute chlorophyllous tip in S. pilosum that is commonly misinterpreted as a spine), eciliate or softly ciliate on the margins [Fig. ]; leaf blades not both narrow and pubescent on both surfaces

c17.text: Many of the involucral bracts with a subulate, involute, chlorophyllous tip [Fig. ]
Involucral bracts without an involute tip [Fig. ]

Involucral bracts glabrous to pubescent, but not sericeous; leaves glabrous to pubescent, but not sericeous on both surfaces, entire to toothed; capitulescence variable, though often broad; cypselas usually sparsely strigose, the nerves visible

Plants variable in habit, habitat, and leaf morphology, not of saltmarshes except varieties of S. novi-belgii ; involucral bracts with a conspicuous chlorophyllous zone in the apical portion or entirely foliaceous

c20.text: Lobes of the disk corolla comprising (45–) 50–75% of the limb, flaring to recurving [Fig. ]
Lobes of the disk corolla comprising 15–45% of the limb, erect to ascending [Fig. ]
