Leaf blades abaxially sparsely to densely pubescent on and between the veins (glabrous in rare forms); disk flowers yellow, turning brown post anthesis; lobes of the disk corolla comprising 45–55 (–65)% of the limb; capitula with (10–) 15–26 ray flowers; plants from slender, elongate rhizomes

c22.text: Branches and peduncles provided with copious, imbricate, short bracts mostly 1–4 mm long that are conspicuously shorter than the leaves of the main stem

Branches and peduncles with relatively fewer bracts, the bracts not crowded, mostly longer than 4 mm, and usually gradually decreasing in size from the leaves of the main stem (abruptly reduced in S. racemosum )

c23.text: Lobes of disk corolla comprising 15–30% of the limb [Fig. ]; ray flowers commonly light blue to purple
Lobes of disk corolla comprising 30–45% of the limb; ray flowers commonly white

c24.text: Leaves with conspicuous veins that connect to form isodiametric aereolae [Fig. ]; stems glabrous and thinly glaucous
Leaves with fainter veins that connect to form aereolae that are longer than wide; stems glabrous to pubescent, not glaucous

c25.text: Leaf blades linear to oblong-linear, often with revolute margins, 2–5 (–9) mm wide; base of stem thinner than 2.5 mm; rhizome thinner than 2 mm; plants mostly of high-pH fens

Leaf blades narrow-lanceolate to lanceolate, elliptic, or oblanceolate, with plane margins, 5–25 mm wide; base of stem thicker than 2.5 mm; rhizome thicker than 2 mm; plants mostly of lake and river shores, saltmarshes, and moist fields

c26.text: Leaf blades narrow-lanceolate to oblanceolate, narrowing to the base, flat, herbaceous to fleshy; most peduncles less than 3 cm long; involucral bracts often loose or somewhat spreading apically, commonly green in large part (in part)

Leaf blades tending to be narrow-lanceolate, scarcely narrowing to the base, folded along the midrib, coriaceous; many peduncles longer than 3 cm; involucral bracts usually appressed and with a chartaceous base and green apex (rarely loose, expanded and foliaceous apically) (in part)

c27.text: Involucre 2.5–3.5 (–4) mm tall; capitula often numerous and secund along the branches
Involucre 4–6 mm tall; capitula usually neither crowded nor notably secund

c28.text: Bracteal leaves usually shorter than 1.5 cm, conspicuously reduced in size from the stem leaves
Bracteal leaves, at least some of them, usually longer than 1.5 cm, gradually reduced in size from the stem leaves (in part)

c29.text: Stems 1–6 dm tall; stems 1–3 mm thick at the base; leaf blades 3–10 ×0.3–1 cm; capitula with 15–30 ray flowers; rays 3–8 mm long; plants of rocky shores

Stems 5–15 dm tall; stems 3–6 mm thick at the base; leaf blades 8–15 ×0.3–3.5 cm; capitula with 20–40 ray flowers; rays 4.5–12 mm long; plants mostly of wet-mesic to hydric fields, ditches, and open swamp edges (in part)

c1.text: This genus contains exactly one species.

Leaf blades usually entire or spinose-toothed; stems ± glabrous; pappus absent, or rarely present on cypselas from near middle of capitulum and then consisting of short, narrow scales; corollas orange, orange-red, or yellow
Leaf blades usually pinnately lobed and spinose-toothed; stems white-tomentose; pappus present, of narrow, ciliate scales; corollas yellow (rarely white)

Plants aquatic, with flaccid stems; leaves whorled, finely dissected into narrow, flaccid segments (except the emersed ones); capitulescence commonly a solitary capitulum [Fig. ]; cypselas nearly terete to weakly 4-angled

Plants terrestrial or of wetlands, with erect stems; leaves opposite, entire or divided into broad, firmer segments; capitulescence commonly composed of 2 or more capitula; cypselas compressed to quadrangular

c2.text: Principal leaf blades 1- to 3-times divided into distinct leaflets, at least the terminal leaflet with a thin petiolule
Leaf blades simple or lobed into 3–7 segments, the segments not divided completely to the midrib and, when lobed, with broadly winged petiolules

c3.text: Ultimate segments of leaf blades linear to narrow-lanceolate, (0.5–) 2–8 (–12) mm wide; marginal flowers of capitulum with well-developed rays 10–30 mm long (except B. tenuisecta , with rays absent or short)

Ultimate segments of leaf blades lanceolate or oblanceolate to ovate, (5–) 7–40 mm wide; marginal flowers of capitulum lacking rays or with short rays up to 5 mm long (except B. alba , with well-developed, white rays)

c4.text: Marginal flowers of capitulum lacking rays or with short rays up to 6 mm long; inner cypselas quadrangular in cross-section, 8–15 mm long
Marginal flowers of capitulum with well-developed rays 10–30 mm long; inner cypselas ± flat, (4–) 5–9 mm long

c5.text: Cypsela body narrow-oblanceolate to cuneate-oblong in outline, 2.5–4 times as long as wide, 0.9–2.5 mm wide, merely antrorsely ciliate on the margin; peduncles glabrous; pappus of 2 setose, very stout awns or awn-scales (rarely absent)

Cypsela body obovate to elliptic-obovate, 1.5–2 (–2.5) times as long as wide, 2.5–5.2 mm wide, with a thin, antrorsely ciliate and often erose-notched wing margin; peduncles pubescent; pappus of 2 (–4) antrorsely or restrorsely barbed awns (rarely absent)

c6.text: Outer, herbaceous series of involucral bracts numbering 8–12 (–16), (4–) 5–7 (–12) mm long, usually shorter than the inner, non-herbaceous series of bracts, eciliate or ciliate on the margin
Outer, herbaceous series of involucral bracts numbering 12–21, (6–) 8–12 (–20) mm long, usually longer than the inner, non-herbaceous series of bracts, coarsely ciliate on the margin

c7.text: Leaf blades 2- or 3-times pinnately divided; cypsela bodies at maturity strongly surpassing (i.e., some 2–3 times as long as) the inner, non-herbaceous series of involucral bracts of intact capitula [Fig. ]; pappus of (2–) 3 or 4 awns [Fig. ]; rays pale yellow (rarely white)

Leaf blades once pinnately divided; cypsela bodies at maturity not or only slightly exceeding (i.e., up to 1.5 times as long as) the inner, non-herbaceous series of involucral bracts of intact capitula; pappus of 2 (–5) awns; rays, when present, white (rarely short yellow rays present)

c8.text: Cypsela body quadrangular in cross-section, linear in outline, 5–9 times as long as wide; marginal flowers of the capitulum with or without well-developed rays longer than 5 mm
Cypsela body definitely compressed, oblanceolate to obovate, 2–3.5 times as long as wide; marginal flowers of capitulum lacking rays or with short rays up to 5 mm long

c9.text: Capitulum with 5–8 ray flowers with well-developed white rays 5–16 mm long; outer involucral bracts (8–) 12 (–16); pappus consisting of 2 awns
Capitulum lacking ray flowers or these present and with short rays up to 3 mm long; outer involucral bracts 7–10; pappus consisting of 2 or 3 (–5) awns

c10.text: Capitula with 3–5 outer, herbaceous involucral bracts; involucral bracts eciliate or only sparsely ciliate; cypsela body 3–6.5 mm long, with awns 0–2.4 mm long
Capitula with 5–21 outer, herbaceous involucral bracts; involucral bracts ciliate-margined; cypsela body 5.3–11.3 mm long, with awns 2–9.5 mm long

c11.text: Capitula with 5–10 outer, herbaceous involucral bracts; disk corollas abruptly ampliate above the herbaceous base, the limb delicate and the lobes prominently pigmented with yellow to yellow-orange, after anthesis collapsing around the exserted anthers and weakly attached to the summit of ovary [Fig. ]

Capitula with 10–21 outer, herbaceous involucral bracts; disk corollas gradually expanded apically, more herbaceous throughout and the lobes only weakly pigmented with yellow, after anthesis becoming chartaceous, scarcely collapsing, with included anthers, and firmly attached to the summit of ovary [Fig. ]

c12.text: Leaf blades sessile, or sometimes the lowermost with a short, narrowed base; cypselas either with a convex, cartilaginous apex or with a truncate apex in B. tripartita
Leaves with distinct petioles 1–4 cm long; cypselas with a truncate apex

c13.text: Disk corollas gradually expanded apically, more herbaceous throughout and the lobes only weakly pigmented with yellow, after anthesis becoming chartaceous, scarcely collapsing, with included anthers, and firmly attached to the summit of ovary [Fig. ]; anthers pale brown; summit of the fruiting ovary with a truncate apex (in part)

Disk corollas abruptly ampliate above the stramineous or herbaceous base, the limb delicate and the lobes prominently pigmented with yellow to yellow-orange, after anthesis collapsing around the exserted anthers and weakly attached to the summit of ovary [Fig. ]; anthers dark brown to black; summit of fruiting ovary with a convex, cartilaginous apex

c14.text: Outer, herbaceous involucral bracts ascending to erect; disk corollas usually 4-lobed; capitula erect; body of cypsela conspicuously marked with 7–15 longitudinal striations on each surface
Outer, herbaceous involucral bracts spreading; disk corollas 5-lobed; capitula arched or nodding in age; body of cypsela not or only inconspicuously marked with longitudinal striae

c15.text: Rays absent or 2–15 (–18) mm long; chaff yellow near apex; body of inner cypselas with a pale, thickened, cartilaginous margin, those of the outer ones (3–) 5–6 mm long, those of the inner ones 4–8 mm long
Rays 15–30 mm long; chaff yellow-orange to orange-red near apex; body of cypselas lacking a pale, thickened margin, those of the outer ones 6–8 mm long, those of the inner ones 8–10 mm long

c16.text: Disk corollas gradually expanded apically, more herbaceous throughout and the lobes only weakly pigmented with yellow, after anthesis becoming chartaceous, scarcely collapsing, with included anthers, and firmly attached to the summit of ovary; anthers pale brown (in part)

Disk corollas abruptly ampliate above the herbaceous base, the limb delicate and the lobes prominently pigmented with yellow to yellow-orange, after anthesis collapsing around the exserted anthers and weakly attached to the summit of ovary; anthers dark brown to black

c17.text: Capitula cylindric to narrow-funnelform, each with (7–) 12–25 (–35) flowers; body of cypsela ± flat, usually striate on each face, lacking tuberculae [Fig. ]; plants restricted to tidal river shores

Capitula funnelform to hemispheric, each with 20–60 (–150) flowers; body of cypsela compressed-quadrangular (varying to almost flat), commonly with few or no striations (immature fruits with more evident striations), usually with minute tubercles [Fig. ]; plants of varied habitats, including tidal river shores, but primarily of inland wetlands and shores

c1.text: Capitulescence resembling a raceme [Fig. ]; capitula sessile or with a short peduncle up to 30 (–90) mm long [Fig. ]; petioles weakly angled; leaf blades narrow- to broad-ovate, acute at the apex
Capitulescence resembling a corymb; capitula with a peduncle mostly (15–) 25–120 mm long; petioles strongly angled; leaf blades broad-ovate to orbicular-ovate, rounded at the apex

c2.text: Involucre 15–25 mm wide, the involucral bracts arachnoid-tomentose; corollas minutely glandular-pubescent; petioles, particularly the lower, often hollow
Involucre 25–45 mm wide, the involucral bracts glabrous to thinly arachnoid-pubescent; corollas glabrous; petioles usually solid

c1.text: Plants definitely woody; capitula homogamous—all the flowers bisexual and with 5-lobed corollas; leaves persistent, the principal ones with blades narrow-obtriangular with three apical teeth

Plants herbaceous, suffrutescent, or ± woody; capitula heterogamous—the marginal flowers carpellate with 2-lobed corollas, the inner flowers bisexual or functionally staminate with 5-lobed corollas; leaves usually deciduous, the principal ones with pinnatifid blades ( A. dracunculus often and A. ludoviciana usually with simple leaves)

c2.text: Central flowers of disk functionally staminate, the gynoecium of these flowers with an abortive ovary and undivided style that is included within the short-tubular to subglobose corolla
Central flowers of disk bisexual, the gynoecium of these flowers with a fertile ovary and divided style that is often exserted beyond the tubular to funnelform corolla

c3.text: Leaf blades 2- or 3-times pinnatifid into narrow segments [Fig. ]; herbage scarcely odorous, if at all
Leaf blades entire or sometimes the lower with 2–5 lobes; herbage faintly to strongly tarragon-scented

c4.text: Receptacle densely and conspicuously hairy between the disk flowers
Receptacle without hairs

c5.text: Reproductive stems 4–6 (–10) dm tall; leaf blades 3–8 cm long, the ultimate segments oblong to oblanceolate, 1.5–4 mm wide
Reproductive stems 1–4 dm tall; leaf blades 0.5–1.5 (–2.5) cm long, the ultimate segments linear, up to 1 mm wide

c6.text: Plants annual or biennial, arising from a taproot; leaf blades glabrous on both surfaces; involucral bracts glabrous
Plants perennial, arising from a rhizome or woody caudex; leaf blades tomentose on one or both surfaces, sometimes sparsely so; involucral bracts tomentose, at least sparsely so

c7.text: Capitulescence dense, resembling a spike, 2–4 cm wide, with inconspicuous peduncles and erect or ascending capitula; involucre 2–3 mm tall; plants inodorous or nearly so; leaf blades 1- or 2-times pinnatifid
Capitulescence open, resembling a panicle, 10–20 cm wide, with conspicuous peduncles and nodding capitula [Fig. ]; involucre 1–2 mm tall; plants sweet-scented; leaf blades 2- or 3-times pinnatifid

c8.text: Plants suffrutescent or ± woody, without rhizomes; leaves 2- or 3-times pinnatifid into linear or filiform segments 0.5–1.5 mm wide; involucre 2–3.5 (–4) mm tall

Plants herbaceous, dying back to the ground each year, with rhizomes; leaves entire or 1- or 2-times pinnatifid into lobes wider than 1.5 mm (the ultimate lobes often narrower than 1.5 mm in A. carruthii ); involucre 2.5–7.5 mm tall

c9.text: Leaf blades 3–6 cm long, thinly tomentose on the abaxial surface, glabrous on the adaxial surface; plants ± shrubby, 5–20 dm tall
Leaf blades 1–3 cm long, tomentose on both surfaces; plants suffrutescent, 4–10 dm tall

c10.text: Leaf blades entire or toothed, the lower sometimes inconspicuously lobed, but the primary lobes without additional teeth or lobes
Principal leaf blades 1- or 2-times pinnatifid, the primary lobes either entire or with additional teeth or lobes

c11.text: Leaf blades concolorous, densely white-tomentose on both faces; involucre 6–7.5 mm tall; disk corollas 3.2–4 mm long
Leaf blades bicolorous, white-tomentose on the abaxial surface, green and glabrous or sparsely pubescent on the adaxial surface; involucre 2.5–4.5 mm tall; disk corollas 1–2.8 mm long

c12.text: Reproductive stems (4–) 6–19 dm tall; leaf blades with ultimate segments wider than 2 mm; capitula with 7–10 marginal carpellate flowers
Reproductive stems 1.5–4 (–7) dm tall; leaf blades with ultimate segments narrower than 2 mm; capitula with 1–5 marginal carpellate flowers

c1.text: Leaf blades lanceolate, tapering to the base, abaxially gray to white and densely strigose; plants with 3-forked, axillary spines
Leaf blades ovate to reniform, truncate to cordate at the base, abaxially ± green, hirtellous; plants without axillary spines

Staminate capitula sessile or subsessile, in a solitary, spike-like capitulescence; staminate involucres prolonged into a long, retrorse, lanceolate to triangular-ovate, hooded, bristly tooth; leaf blades lanceolate to narrow-lanceolate, entire to lobed, when lobed with 1 or 2 pairs of pinnately arranged lobes that are confined to the base of the blade

Staminate capitula peduncled, borne in 1 or more raceme-like capitulescences; staminate involucres without a prolonged, retrorse lobe, actinomorphic or nearly so; leaf blades lanceolate or elliptic to ovate or triangular, 1- or 2-times pinnately lobed, or entire to palmately lobed in A. trifida , but that species with some broad-lanceolate to ovate, unlobed blades on the plant

c2.text: Plants annual, 0.5–5 m high; leaves opposite throughout, the blades entire to palmately lobed with 3 (–5) lobes [Fig. ]; receptacle without chaff; staminate involucre with 3 evident nerves on one side; carpellate involucre 5–10 mm long in fruit

Plants annual or perennial, 0.2–1 (–2.5) m high; leaves usually opposite below and alternate above, once- or twice-pinnatifid; receptacle with chaff; staminate involucre inconspicuously nerved (i.e., the faint nerves of ± equal prominence in all directions); carpellate involucre mostly 3–5 mm long in fruit

c3.text: Plants usually perennial from a creeping rootstock; leaf blades usually once-pinnatifid, relatively thicker; carpellate involucre with 4 tubercles near the apex, these sometimes short and inconspicuous
Plants annual; leaf blades once-, or more commonly, twice-pinnatifid, relatively thinner; carpellate involucre with 4–7 sharp spines near or above the middle [Fig. ]

c1.text: This genus contains exactly one species.
Leaves 2–7 ×0.1–0.4 cm; stems stipitate-glandular only near the summit; capitula 2–5 mm wide after pressing, with 0–5 ray flowers; rays 1.5–3 mm long
Leaves 4–18 ×0.4–1.2 cm; stems conspicuously stipitate-glandular throughout; capitula 6–12 mm wide after pressing, with 5–13 ray flowers; rays 2–7 mm long
This genus contains exactly one species.
Leaf blades glabrous; axis of capitulescence glabrous; petioles 3–10 mm long; peduncles 1–3 mm long; plants suffrutescent perennials of coastal marshes and shores
Leaf blades adaxially strigose-scaberulous; axis of capitulescence pubescent; petioles 5–20 (–30) mm long; peduncles 0–1 mm long; plants annual of moist, often disturbed, inland soils
This genus contains exactly one species.
This genus contains exactly one species.
This genus contains exactly one species.

Peduncles pubescent, in part, with glandular hairs; involucral bracts narrow-lanceolate, gradually tapering to an awn-like point 0.8–2 mm long, the abaxial surface stipitate-glandular, eciliate or sparsely ciliate on the margins
Peduncles pubescent with eglandular hairs; involucral bracts oblong-lanceolate, abruptly tapering to an awn-like point 0.5–1 mm long, the abaxial surface eglandular, ciliate on the margins

Leaf blades toothed with obtuse to rounded teeth, the apex of each tooth with a prominent resin gland (leaves rarely subentire); middle involcural bracts terminated by green appendages (1.2–) 2.5–5.4 mm long
Leaf blades toothed with mostly acute teeth, the apex of each tooth apiculate to setose (leaves rarely subentire); middle involucral bracts terminated by green appendages 1–1.7 (–3) mm long
This genus contains exactly one species.
This genus contains exactly one species.
This genus contains exactly one species.
This genus contains exactly one species.
This genus contains exactly one species.
Rays 4–8 mm long, white; cypsela body with 7–10 ribs
Rays absent or up to 4 mm long and yellow; cypsela body with 5 ribs

c2.text: Leaf blades glabrous or nearly so; disk 5–10 mm wide; capitulescence with (10–) 20–70 (–100) capitula; rays absent
Leaf blades villous; disk 10–18 mm wide; capitulescence with 1–15 (–30) capitula [Fig. ]; rays present, 1–3 (–4) mm long

c1.text: Capitula without ray flowers [Fig. ]; disk corollas 4-lobed, green-yellow; pappus a short crown; ultimate segments of leaf blades short
Capitula with conspicuous, white ray flowers; disk corollas 5-lobed, yellow; pappus absent or a short crown; ultimate segments of leaf blades longer

Involucre 5–12 mm tall; peduncles with glandular hairs; capitula with a series of rayless, carpellate flowers within the series of ray flowers; pappus elongating in fruit and conspicuously surpassing the involcure

Involucre 2–7 mm tall; peduncles without glandular hairs; capitula with carpellate ray flowers and bisexual disk flowers; pappus not or scarcely elongating in fruit, not or only somewhat exceeding the involucre

c2.text: Rays 0.5–1 (–2) mm long [Fig. ]; involucre 2–5 mm wide (sometimes wider in pressed specimens); disk 1–3 (–4) mm wide in life
Rays 4–10 mm long (very rarely wanting) [Fig. ]; involucre 5–20 mm wide; disk (3–) 5–20 mm wide in life

c3.text: Leaves linear to linear-oblanceolate, 1–5 mm wide; stems tufted and bearing axillary, sterile, leafy branches [Fig. ]; capitula with 20–50 ray flowers [Fig. ]; capitula numbering 1–4 (–5) per stem, often solitary

Leaves linear to suborbicular, 2.5–70 mm wide; stems not tufted, usually without sterile, axillary branches; capitula with 50–400 ray flowers; capitula numbering 3–30 (–100) per stem (only 1–4 (–5) in E. pulchellus )

c4.text: Stem leaves gradually tapering to the base; pappus of 2 types—the inner of long, slender bristles, the outer of short scales; pappus of ray flowers shorter than 1 mm
Stem leaves rounded to clasping at the base; pappus of 1 type—long, slender bristles; pappus of all the flowers much longer than 1 mm

c5.text: Principal stem leaves linear to lanceolate, entire or subentire, mostly 2.5–10 (–15) mm wide; pubescence of mid-stem 0.1– 0.4 (–0.8) mm long, usually ascending to appressed (longer and more spreading in var. septentrionalis ); rays 4–6 mm long; basal leaf blades often persistent through flowering

Principal stem leaves broad-lanceolate to ovate, toothed, mostly 10–35 (–70) mm wide; pubescence of mid-stem 0.5–1.2 mm long, spreading; rays 4–10 mm long; basal leaf blades often withering prior to flowering

c6.text: Capitula with 50–100 ray flowers, the rays 0.8–1.7 mm wide; disk corollas (4–) 4.5–6 mm long; body of cypsela 1.3–1.8 mm long; plants with slender, elongate, superficial rhizomes; capitula numbering 1–4 (–5) per stem

Capitula with 150–400 ray flowers, the rays up to 0.5 mm wide; disk corollas (2.1–) 2.5–3.2 mm long; body of cypsela 0.6–1.1 mm long; plants without superficial rhizomes; capitula numbering 3–30 (–40) per stem

c1.text: This genus contains exactly one species.
Rays white or tinged with pink; leaves herbaceous, prominently toothed, with flat margins, the blades 15–60 mm wide, those of the stem below the capitulescence mostly numbering 10–22
Rays pink to purple; leaves firm, entire or nearly so, often with revolute margins, the blades 2–12 mm wide, those of the stem below the capitulescence numbering 40–75
Principal leaf blades oblanceolate to obovate, 10–45 mm wide, at least the lower toothed; each capitulum with 9–20 disk flowers
Principal leaf blades linear to narrow-oblong, 2–12 mm wide, entire; each capitulum with 5–10 disk flowers
This genus contains exactly one species.
This genus contains exactly one species.
Body of cypsela short-hairy; involucre 3–5 mm tall; upright stems borne from elongate creeping rhizomes
Body of cypsela glabrous; involucre 4.5–7 mm tall; upright stems mostly solitary from a fibrous root crown
This genus contains exactly one species.
Rays white, 5–9 mm long; lower leaf blades linear to narrow-oblanceolate, 2–10 mm wide; involucral bracts with a single, thickened midrib; many pappus bristles expanded at apex

Rays yellow, 3–5 mm long; lower leaf blades elliptic or elliptic-oblong to broad-lanceolate or broad-ovate, (15–)24–50(–100) mm wide; involucral bracts few-striate [Fig. ]; pappus bristles slender at the apex
Capitulescence nodding at the summit and/or with branches that have secund capitula [Fig. ]

Capitulescence neither nodding at the summit nor with secund capitula [Fig. ], either terminal and resembling a thryse or panicle or consisting of clusters of capitula in the axils of well-developed leaves

c2.text: Leaves basally disposed (i.e., leaves progressively reduced upward, those of the apical portion of the stem smaller, often of different shape, and less petiolate than those of the basal portion) [Fig. ]; plants usually with basal tufts of leaves

Leaves chiefly cauline (i.e., leaves of the apical portion of the stem of nearly similar shape and not dramatically reduced in size relative to the leaves of the basal portion of the stem) [Fig. ]; plants lacking tufts of basal leaves

c3.text: Stems and often the leaves closely and minutely pubescent [Fig. ]; rays pale yellow
Stems and leaves glabrous or with long, scattered hairs or scabrous; rays bright yellow

c4.text: Leaf blades fleshy, entire; capitula with 7–17 ray flowers; plants of Atlantic coast shorelines and saline marshes (inland along heavily salted roadways)
Leaf blades not fleshy, serrate to subentire; capitula with 1–12 ray flowers; plants not of Atlantic coast shores

c5.text: Leaf blades adaxially strongly scabrous; stems prominently angled, each angle often with a narrow wing
Leaf blades glabrous, pubescent, or slightly scabrous adaxially; stems terete or striate, but without prominent angles

c6.text: Lower leaf blades abruptly contracted to a petiole
Lower leaf blades gradually tapered to the base

c7.text: Abaxial surface of leaf blades hirsute; capitulum with 4–7 disk flowers; cypsela body minutely pubescent (in part)
Abaxial surface of leaf blades glabrous; capitulum with 8–20 disk flowers; cypsela body glabrous

c8.text: Lower leaves conspicuously sheathing, the petiole covering 50–75% of the circumference of the stem; capitulescence taller than wide; capitula with 1–8 ray flowers and 4–8 disk flowers; plants primarily of organic soil wetlands (in part)

Lower leaves not conspicuously sheathing, the petiole covering less than 50% of the circumference of the stem; capitulescence as wide as or wider than tall; capitula with 7–12 ray flowers and 9–14 disk flowers; plants of open or lightly shaded, mineral soils

c9.text: Leaf blades triple-veined (i.e., with 3 conspicuous, parallel veins—a midrib and 2 evident and prolonged, lateral veins) [Fig. ]
Leaf blades pinnately veined (i.e., with much-branched lateral veins that are not aligned parallel to the midrib) [Fig. ]

c10.text: Stem glabrous and glaucous below the capitulescence; involucral bracts obtuse to acute at the apex, green
Stem pubescent in at least the apical half, not glaucous; involucral bracts acuminate at the apex, yellow-green

c11.text: Leaf blades abaxially subglabrous or pubescent only on the midrib and major veins (also pubescent between the veins in var. hargeri ), usually sharply serrate and relatively thin; involucre 2–3 mm tall; disk corollas 2.3–2.7 mm long
Leaf blades abaxially pubescent on and between major veins, usually subentire to remotely serrate and relatively firm; involucre (2.7–) 3–4 (–5) mm tall; disk corollas 3–3.4 mm long

c12.text: Leaf blades translucent-punctate, all entire, usually anise-scented when bruised
Leaf blades not translucent-punctate, some with teeth, not fragrant when bruised

c13.text: Plants from a caudex, without creeping rhizomes; lower leaf blades abruptly tapered to a petiole; capitula with 3–6 ray flowers (in part)
Plants with long, creeping rhizomes; leaf blades sessile or nearly so; capitula with 6–11 (–12) ray flowers

c14.text: Leaf blades abaxially pubescent, the hairs commonly found on the tertiary veins (as well as the midvein and primary lateral veins); stems conspicuously spreading-pubescent (varying to sparsely pubescent in ssp. aspera ); widespread plants found throughout most of New England

Leaf blades ± glabrous abaxially, hairs, when present, few in number and confined to the midrib and primary lateral veins; stems glabrous or with pubescent lines of decurrence from the leaf blades; plants mainly of southern New England and the coastal plain

c15.text: Involucre 2.5–4 mm tall; involucral bracts narrow-lanceolate to narrow-oblong, mostly 0.3–0.6 mm wide, acute at the apex; disk corollas 2.5–3.5 mm long
Involucre 4–6 mm tall; involucral bracts oblong to narrow-ovate, the larger 0.7–1.2 mm wide, obtuse to rounded at the apex; disk corollas 4–5.5 mm long

c16.text: Leaves chiefly cauline (i.e., leaves of the apical portion of the stem of nearly similar shape and not dramatically reduced in size relative to the leaves of the basal portion of the stem) [Fig. ]; plants lacking tufts of basal leaves

Leaves basally disposed (i.e., leaves progressively reduced upward, those of the apical portion of the stem smaller, often of different shape, and less petiolate than those of the basal portion) [Fig. ]; plants usually with basal tufts of leaves

c17.text: Capitula with 30–50 flowers, the ray flowers numbering 10–13; leaves of the stem below the capitulescence numbering 2–4 (–7); plants 5–35 cm tall, of alpine summits and plateaus (in part)

Capitula with 6–13 flowers, the ray flowers numbering (1–) 3–5; leaves of the stem below the capitulescence numbering 7–60; plants 30–150 cm tall, primarily of temperate forests, woodlands, edges, and fields

c18.text: Leaf blades entire to obscurely toothed; cypsela body glabrous; capitulescence terminal, only the lower branches subtended by leaves [Fig. ] (in part)
At least the lower leaf blades with prominent teeth; cypsela body pubescent; capitulescence partly or entirely axillary, only the upper portion (if any) not subtended by leaves

c19.text: Leaf blades elliptic to ovate, 3–10 cm wide, 1.2–2.2 (–2.5) times as long as wide; stem angled, not glaucous
Leaf blades lanceolate to narrow-elliptic, 1–3 cm wide, 3–10 times as long as wide; stem terete, glaucous

c20.text: Involucre 8–11 mm tall, composed of acuminate- to attenuate-tipped involucral bracts; cypsela body 4–5 mm long; lower leaf blades with an acuminate apex
Involucre 3–9 mm tall, composed of round- to acuminate-tipped involucral bracts; cypsela body shorter than 4 mm long; lower leaf blades usually with an obtuse to acute apex

c21.text: Stem and often the leaves pubescent with minute, viscidulous hairs [Fig. ]; involucral bracts narrow, acuminate at the apex, up to 0.5 (–0.75) mm wide at the midpoint
Stem and leaves glabrous or pilose, but not copiously pubescent with minute hairs; involucral bracts wider, rounded to acute at the apex, (0.75–) 1–2 mm wide at the midpoint

c22.text: Leaves conspicuously sheathing, the petioles covering 50–75% of the circumference of the stem; plants primarily of organic soil wetlands (in part)
Leaves not conspicuously sheathing, the petiole covering less than 50% of the circumference of the stem; plants not of organic soil wetlands

c23.text: Involucral bracts, especially the outer, with squarrose tips [Fig. ]; involucre 5–9 mm tall
Involucral bracts appressed to ascending; involucre 3–6 mm tall (up to 9 mm tall in S. leiocarpa )

c24.text: Leaf blades pilose on one or both surfaces; stems often pilose
Leaf blades glabrous or nearly so (sometimes scabrous); stems essentially glabrous (though often pubescent in the capitulescence)

c25.text: Ray flowers white or yellow-white; involucre 3–5 mm long; involucral bracts white-brown or light yellow-brown to light green or white-green at the base, green at the apex, the colors often sharply contrasting
Rays yellow; involucre 4–6 mm long; involucral bracts light green or yellow-green at the base, green at the apex, the colors usually weakly contrasting

c26.text: Cypsela body glabrous; capitula with 5–9 ray flowers; plants of temperate woodlands, edges, and fields
Cypsela body pubescent; capitula with 8–13 ray flowers; plants of mountains, cliffs, and northern river shores

c27.text: Capitulescence panicle-like, usually with several ascending branches [Fig. ]; leaf blades entire or sometimes the lower ones slightly toothed, the middle blades (1.5–) 2–7 cm wide; cypsela body 1.1–2 mm long (in part)

Capitulescence thyrse-like, very slender (infrequently with 1 or more prolonged branches); lower leaf blades crenate to crenate-serrate, the middle blades 0.5–2 (–2.5) cm wide; cypsela body 2.2–3 mm long

c28.text: Involucral bracts oblong to lanceolate, not glutinous, the middle ones 1.2–2 mm wide, green in large part; leaves of the stem below the capitulescence numbering 2–4 (–7) (in part)

Involucral bracts linear to narrow-lanceolate, glutinous, the surface shiny as if covered with varnish, the middle ones 0.7–1.2 mm wide, with chartaceous base and sides, green only at the apex and along the central band; leaves of the stem below the capitulescence numbering 5–40

c1.text: Basal leaf blades both cordate and borne on petioles
Basal leaf blades not cordate, sessile or petiolate [Fig. ]

c2.text: Leaf blades minutely stipitate-glandular (especially on distal portions); branches of capitulescence with minute stipitate glands; rays purple or at least purple-tinged
Leaf blades eglandular; branches of capitulescence without glands (sometimes with sparse, tiny glands in E. schreberi ); rays white

c3.text: Plants with vegetative tufts of leaves produced separately from the flowering stem; involucre slender-cylindric, 5.5–7.5 mm tall; leaves at base of plant relatively firmer, often with rectangular basal sinuses, with mostly 15–30 teeth per margin
Plants without separate vegetative tufts of leaves; involucre funnelform, 5–6.5 mm tall; leaves at base of plant relatively thinner, with a V-shaped basal sinus, with mostly 6–15 teeth per margin

c4.text: Stipitate glands present on involucral bracts and branches of capitulescence; leaves basally disposed; plants of dry, sandy soils along the coastal plain
Stipitate glands lacking; leaves chiefly cauline; plants of peatlands, shores, and moist soils of forests, more common in north-temperate, boreal, and cool, maritime climates

c1.text: Ultimate segments of leaf blades lanceolate to elliptic, 2–5 mm wide; rays pale to bright yellow; cypsela body 15–30 mm long including beak
Ultimate segments of leaf blades linear to filiform, narrower than 1.5 mm; rays usually white to pink to red; cypsela body 7–16 mm long including beak

c2.text: Rays 15–40 mm long; margins of ultimate leaf segments entire
Rays 5–15 mm long; margins of ultimate leaf segments spinulose-ciliate

c1.text: Disk corollas mostly 4-lobed at apex; outer series of involucral bracts much shorter than the inner series [Fig. ]; style branch apex blunt or short-conical
Disk corollas mostly 5-lobed at apex; outer series of involucral bracts nearly or fully as long as inner series (shorter in C. tripteris ); style branch apex acute, long-conical, or cuspidate

c2.text: Rays pink to white; disk corollas yellow; cypsela body lacking wing-like edges; principal leaf blades usually simple (rarely with 2 or 3 lobes) [Fig. ]; plants perennial, from rhizomes

Rays yellow distally with a red-brown base; disk corollas dark red; cypsela body narrowly to broadly winged (infrequently wingless); principal leaf blades 1- to 2-times pinnatifid; plants annual or biennial, from taproots

c3.text: Leaf blades simple or pinnately lobed to compound with 3–9 (or more) segments [Fig. ]; chaff long-attenuate at apex; rays apically with prominent tooth-like lobes

Principal leaf blades palmately or ternately lobed or divided (the central segment sometimes again palmately or ternately lobed or divided) [Fig. ]; chaff rounded to acute at apex; rays apically entire or shortly toothed

c4.text: Disk corollas dark red; principal leaf blades pinnately lobed or pinnately compound with oblong to broad-ovate segments
Disk corollas yellow; principal leaf blades simple or with a pair of basal lobes or pinnatifid with linear to narrow-lanceolate lobes

c5.text: Leaves confined to lower portion of stem; peduncles elongate, scape-like, mostly 20–40 cm long
Leaves borne throughout the stem; peduncles relatively shorter, mostly 5–20 cm long

c6.text: Principal leaf blades pinnatifid into linear to narrow-lanceolate segments; pappus often wanting
Principal leaf blades simple, elliptic to obovate or ovate, sometimes with a pair of smaller lobes at the base; pappus often of 2, short, scale-like teeth

c7.text: Leaf blades borne on evident, narrow petioles that are clearly much narrower than the associated leaf segments; outer involucral bracts 2–3 mm long, ca. to as long as the inner involucral bracts; reproductive stems 10–30 dm tall

Leaf blades sessile or borne on petiole-like structures that are nearly or fully as wide as the associated leaf segments; outer involucral bracts (3–) 4–12 mm long, subequal in length to the inner involucral bracts; reproductive stems 3–10 dm tall

c8.text: Ultimate segments of leaf blades linear to filiform, 0.3–1.5 mm wide; cypsela body 3–5 ×1–1.7 mm
Ultimate segments of leaf blades linear to oval, 2–25 (–30) mm wide; cypsela body 4.5–6.5 ×1.8–4 mm

c9.text: Leaf blades trifurcating well above the base (i.e., the blades appearing to be on a broadly winged petiole) into linear to narrow-oblong segments 2–7 mm wide [Fig. ]; internodes of stem usually glabrous
Leaf blades trifurcating at the base (i.e., the leaf blades definitely sessile) into lanceolate to oval segments (5–) 12–25 (–30) mm wide; internodes of stem usually short-pubescent

Pappus of the disk flowers without an awn-tip; pappus of ray flowers absent or poorly developed; cypselas sparsely pubescent or glabrous

Lower leaf blades narrow-lanceolate to narrow-elliptic, 1–4 cm wide, mostly 5–20 times as long as wide, usually entire, gradually tapered to an often ill-defined petiole; plants from a strong taproot
Plants annual; leaf blades 1- or 2-times pinnatifid
Plants perennial; leaf blades toothed, or some of them lobed near the base
Ray flowers staminate or neutral; receptacle chaffy only near the middle; cypselas glandular-tuberculate; plants ill scented
Ray flowers carpellate; receptacle chaffy throughout; cypselas not tuberculate; plants not ill scented
Rays yellow; stems glandular-punctate
Rays white to pink; stems not glandular-punctate

c2.text: Stems villous; ultimate segments of leaf blades 1.5–8 mm wide; involucral bracts sparsely to moderately pubescent (i.e., the surface not concealed by hairs)
Stems villous-tomentose; ultimate segments of leaf blades usually narrower than 1 mm; involucral bracts moderately to densely pubescent abaxially (i.e., the surface largely concealed by hairs)

c3.text: Leaf blades subentire to serrate with short teeth; rays numbering (5–) 8–10 (–15) per capitulum, 3–5 mm long
Leaf blades pinnately dissected into narrow segments; rays numbering (4–) 5 (–6) per capitulum, 1–3 (–4) mm long

c4.text: Leaves near the middle of the stem usually with 15 or more primary divisions, the blades lanceolate to linear, the divisions usually not plane
Leaves near the middle of the stem with 10 or fewer lobes, the blades elliptic to ovate, with plane lobes

Plants depressed to spreading; capitula 1.5–3 cm wide; ultimate segments of the leaves linear, 1.5–5 mm long; rays 7–12 mm long

Basal and lower stem leaves 10–20 cm broad; rays (10–) 20–30 mm long; disk corollas 7–11 mm long; outer involucral bracts 6–8 (–20) mm wide; involucre (20–) 30–40 mm in diameter; body of cypsela 2–3 mm long

Plants without stolons, or these short and poorly developed, not forming colonies; leaf blades not or very shortly decurrent on petioles; involucral bracts gradually tapering from base or with parallel margins and gradually tapering from near apex

c2.text: Basal leaf blades tapering to petiole, usually cuneate at the base; plants of gravels, ledges, and balds
Blade of basal leaves abruptly contracted to the petiole, usually truncate to cordate at the base [Fig. ]; plants of wet-mesic to hydric soils of fields, low forests, and wetlands

c3.text: Blade of basal leaves usually 1.75–3.5 times as long as wide, sharply and finely toothed, rounded to subcordate at the base, acute to obtuse at the apex [Fig. ]
Blade of basal leaves usually 0.75–1.5 (–1.75) times as long as wide, crenate, strongly cordate at the base, rounded at the apex

Leaf blades with numerous and prominent resin glands [Fig. ], 1–3 (–6) mm wide; plants ± glabrous on the stem and leaf surfaces; axillary fascicles often well developed and conspicuous throughout much of the stem

Leaf blades with few and/or inconspicuous resin glands, usually 3–12 mm wide; plants varying from glabrous to conspicuously pubescent on the stem and abaxial leaf surfaces; axillary fascicles, if present, usually poorly developed and sparse

This genus contains exactly one species.

Involucre 7–12 mm tall, composed of 3–5 involucral bracts; capitula with (1–) 3 ray flowers, the rays 1–2 mm long; disk corollas 3–4 mm long; cypsela body 4.5–7 mm long; pappus of 1 or 2 acuminate scales 2–3 mm long and 3–5 shorter, ovate to lanceolate scales 0.5–1 mm long

Involucre 13–19 mm tall, composed of 7–11 involucral bracts; capitula with 8 or more ray flowers, the rays 10–30 mm long; disk corollas 10–15 mm long; cypsela body 6.5–10 mm long; pappus of 1 or 2 acuminate scales 8–11 mm long and 2 or 3 blunt scales 3–6 mm long

c2.text: Peduncles swollen; capitula 6–10 cm wide; corollas yellow or orange
Peduncles not or only scarcely swollen; capitula 3.5–6 cm wide; corollas partly or entirely red-orange

Rays with 2 or more colors, frequently yellow with a dark red band just above the base, though the apical color of the ray may be various shades of red, orange, pink, or white; outer involucral bracts keeled; cypselas ± flat
Rays yellow; outer involucral bracts not keeled; cypselas compressed-triangular to compressed-columnar or columnar

c2.text: Principal leaf blades toothed to pinnatifid, the rachis of the blade (i.e., excluding the teeth or lobes) wider than 6 mm, clasping the stem (except the lowest leaves which are narrowed to petiole-like base) [Fig. ]; cypsela bodies of center of capitilum subterete, the angles with a prominent rib

Principal leaf blades bipinnatifid, the rachis of the blade narrower than 6 mm, not clasping the stem; cypsela bodies of center of capitulum subterete, the angles with a prominent rib, and also with a minor rib between them

c1.text: Leaves not decurrent on stems and branches, the blades linear to linear-filiform, 1–2 (–4) mm wide; plants annual, from taproots
Leaves decurrent on stems and branches, the blades broad-linear to oblanceolate, elliptic, or narrow-ovate, 5–40 mm wide; plants perennial, from fibrous roots

c2.text: Ray flowers carpellate, numbering mostly 13–21 per capitulum [Fig. ]; disk flowers yellow; larger leaf blades coarsely toothed
Ray flowers neutral, numbering mostly 8–13 per capitulum, rarely absent; disk flowers red-brown to purple-brown; leaf blades entire or subentire

c1.text: This genus contains exactly one species.
This genus contains exactly one species.
Plants annual, 2–10 dm tall; stems without decurrent wing-angles; capitula with 10–15 carpellate ray flowers; leaf blades coarsely serrate
Plants perennial, 10–30 dm tall; stems with prominent wing-angles that are decurrent from the leaf bases; capitula with 2–10 sterile ray flowers; leaf blades serrate to subentire
Disk ellipsoid to spherical, 10–25 ×10–18 mm; plants from fibrous roots; pappus usually absent (rarely consisting of 1 or 2 tooth-like scales); style branches stigmatic in the apical
Disk cylindric, 10–50 ×7–12 mm; plants from a taproot; pappus usually consisting of 1 or 2 tooth-like scales (rarely absent); style branches stigmatic in the apical to
Pappus absent; style appendages elongate and pointed; chaff sharply acute to acuminate and hispidulous near the apex; leaf blades toothed to entire, but not lobed

Pappus present, represented by a minute crown up to 0.2 mm long; style appendages short and blunt; chaff blunt to acute at apex (tipped by a cusp in R. triloba ), glabrous or minutely downy-pubescent near apex; lower leaf blades with 3 or more prominent lobes or entire to toothed in R. fulgida

c2.text: Plants biennial or short-lived perennial, with basal tufts of leaves; leaves basally disposed, decreasing in size upwards, the lower borne on evident petioles
Plants annual, lacking basal tufts of leaves; leaves chiefly cauline, remaining relatively constant in size until near base of capitulescence, all sessile or subsessile

c3.text: Leaf blades not lobed; chaff 2.5–4 mm long
Lower leaf blades with 3 or more prominent lobes; chaff 4–6.5 mm long

c4.text: Chaff tipped by a glabrous cusp; rays 1–2 (–2.5) cm long; plants biennial or infrequently short-lived perennial, lacking rhizomes and leafy offshoots
Chaff obtuse to acute at apex, minutely downy-pubescent near apex; rays 2–6 cm long; plants perennial from rhizomes that produce leafy offshoots

c5.text: Disk flowers yellow; stem ± glabrous; leaf blade surfaces lacking sessile glands; cypsela body flat, obliquely attached to receptacle

Disk flowers dark brown to purple (rarely yellow); stem densely short-pilose, at least in the apical half; leaf blade surfaces with sessile glands; cypsela body equilaterally quadrangular, basally attached to receptacle

Plants perennial, with rhizomes, stolons, tuberous roots, and/or tough, overwintering bases; leaves opposite (except often the upper); receptacle usually convex to some degree; disk corollas yellow (red-purple in H. pauciflorus )

c2.text: Involucral bracts narrow-oblong to ovate, (3–) 5–8 mm wide, abruptly narrowed to the apex, conspicuously long-ciliate; cypselas usually glabrous except near the pubescent apex, 4–8 mm wide; style branches yellow; leaf blades 5–25 cm wide, dentate; plants (0.5–) 1–3 m tall

Involucral bracts lanceolate, 1–4 (–5) mm wide, gradually narrowed to the apex, either eciliate or ciliate with short hairs of similar length to the hairs of the abaxial surface; cypselas pubescent, 1.2–2.5 mm wide; style branches red (rarely yellow in H. debilis ); leaf blades 1.5–9 cm wide, entire to undulate-dentate; plants 0.4–1 (–1.5) m tall

c3.text: Chaff near the center of the disk inconspicuously short-pubescent; cypselas mottled, pubescent with spreading-ascending hairs; stems frequently mottled; leaf blades dark green and scabrous

Chaff near the center of the disk conspicuously pubescent near the apex with long, white hairs; cypselas not mottled, pubescent with appressed-ascending hairs; stems not mottled; leaf blades pale green and strigose

c4.text: Reproductive stems with 3–5 (–8) nodes bearing highly reduced leaves (rarely the lower 2–4 nodes with well-formed blades), often the upper 50% of the stem lacking leaves; plants with a basal rosette of leaves

Reproductive stems with (5–) 6–15 or more leaf-bearing nodes, the blades gradually, if at all, descreasing in size upward, only the upper 25% or less of the stem lacking leaves; plants without a basal rosette of leaves, during anthesis the leaves chiefly cauline (except sometimes in H. pauciflorus )

c5.text: Disk corollas red-purple (sometimes only the lobes red-purple and the remainder of the limb yellow); involucral bracts acute to obtuse at the apex, 3–5 mm wide, appressed, of several, conspicuously different lengths [Fig. ]
Disk corollas yellow; involucral bracts acuminate to attenuate (rarely acute) at the apex, 1.2–3.5 mm wide, at least some merely ascending, of several, inconspicuously different lengths [Fig. ]

c6.text: Stem and axis of capitulescence conspicuously pubescent, not glaucous
Stem glabrous (or very nearly so) and often glaucous, only the axis of the capitulescence pubescent

c7.text: Stem, abaxial surface of leaf blades, and involucral bracts densely pubescent with short, soft hairs; leaf blades sessile, subcordate to cordate at the base

Stem, abaxial surface of leaf blades, and involucral bracts with sparser and/or coarser pubescence; leaf blades short- to long-petioled (sometimes sessile in H. giganteus ), tapering to rounded at the base (sometimes truncate in H. hirsutus )

c8.text: Leaf blades (4–) 5–12 (–15) cm wide, with a petiole (15–) 20–80 mm long; roots forming tubers later in growing season; cypsela body 5–7 mm long
Leaf blades 1–4 (–8) cm wide, with a petiole up to 20 mm long; roots fibrous or fleshy, merely thickened; cypsela body 3–5 mm long

c9.text: Stem strigose; leaf blades sometimes folded and falcate-arched, especially in drying, pinnately veined near the base [Fig. ]
Stem spreading-hirsute; leaf blades flat, usually with 3 prominent, parallel nerves near the base

c10.text: Leaf blades cuneate at base; petioles 0–12 mm long; roots fleshy and somewhat thickened; involucral bracts linear, 1.2–2 mm wide; anther appendages dark brown (in part)
Leaf blades rounded to truncate at base; petioles 4–20 mm long; roots fibrous; involucral bracts lanceolate, 2.5–3.5 mm wide; anther appendages usually yellow

c11.text: Leaves sessile or with short petioles to 5 (–10) mm long [Fig. ]
Well-developed leaves with petioles (5–) 10–60 mm long

c12.text: Leaf blades lanceolate to oblong-lanceolate, widest near middle, narrowly tapering to the base, usually alternately arranged on the upper portion of the stem; disk 15–25 mm wide; anther appendages dark brown (in part)

Leaf blades lanceolate to triangular-ovate, widest near the base, truncate to broadly rounded at the base [Fig. ], usually oppositely arranged throughout the stem; disk 10–15 mm wide; anther appendages yellow

c13.text: Disk 4–10 mm wide; capitula with 5–8 ray flowers
Disk 15–35 mm wide; capitula with 8–20 ray flowers

c14.text: Leaf blades at least somewhat triple-veined, those near the middle of the stem 25–100 mm wide, broad-lanceolate to ovate, usually less than 3 times as long as wide; capitula with 8–15 ray flowers
Leaf blades pinnately veined, those near the middle of the stem 10–40 (–90) mm wide, lanceolate to narrow-ovate, usually 3–8 times as long as wide; capitula with 10–20 ray flowers

c15.text: Involucral bracts spreading, evidently surpassing the disk [Fig. ]; lobes of the disk corollas pubescent; petioles 15–60 mm long; leaves relatively thin, membranaceous to herbaceous, prominently serrate
Involucral bracts ascending, approximately equaling the height of the disk; lobes of the disk corollas glabrous; petioles 5–30 mm long; leaves thick and firm, subentire to shallowly serrate

c16.text: Lobes of the disk corollas glabrous or glabrate; anther appendages yellow; leaf blades slightly, if at all, scabrous on the adaxial surface and pubescent on the abaxial surface with hairs up to 0.5 mm long

Lobes of the disk corollas pubescent; anther appendages red-brown to dark brown; leaf blades strongly scabrous on the adaxial surface and pubescent on the abaxial surface with hairs 1 mm long or longer (in part)

Floral scales with margins dentate or with 3–7 narrow-triangular, long-ciliate lobes; staminate flowers with 5–12 (–15) stamens; carpellate flowers with 2 slender, bifid stigmas
Floral scales with margins conspicuously fimbriate; staminate flowers with 12–80 stamens; carpellate flowers with 2–4 broadly dilated stigmas

c2.text: Floral scales merely dentate; capsules 3–5 mm long
Floral scales with 3–7 narrow-triangular lobes; capsules 5–9 mm long

c3.text: Branchlets (especially about the nodes) and terminal winter bud pubescent; stigmas lacking basal lobes; floral scales of staminate aments with 5–7 lobes; ovary pubescent

Branchlets and terminal winter bud glabrous or nearly so; stigmas with recurved basal lobes; floral scales of staminate aments with 3–5 lobes (usually with more lobes in P. tremula ); ovary glabrous (or sometimes scabridulous in P. tremula )

c4.text: Mature capsules 5–9 mm long; scales of staminate aments with 3–5 lobes
Mature capsules usually shorter than 5 mm; scales of staminate aments usually with more than 5 apical lobes

c5.text: Stigmas borne on elongate styles; staminate flowers with 12–20 stamens; anthers apiculate at the apex; capsules on pedicels 10–15 mm long; terminal winter bud not or scarcely viscid
Stigmas sessile or nearly so; staminate flowers with (15–) 20–80 stamens; capsules on pedicels 2–10 mm long; anthers blunt or emarginate at the apex; terminal winter bud viscid

c6.text: Carpellate flowers with 3 or 4 stigmas; staminate flowers with (30–) 40–80 stamens; capsules 3- or 4-valved
Carpellate flowers with 2 stigmas; staminate flowers with 20–30 stamens; capsules 2-valved

c7.text: Ovules 15–22 per placenta; floral scales of carpellate flowers fimbriate with many, very narrow segments; stigmas spreading, with coarsely toothed, ± orbicular lobes; trees with spreading to ascending branches

Ovules 4–8 per placenta; floral scales of carpellate flowers fimbriate with 9–11 slender segments; stigmas reflexed and retrorsely appressed agaist the ovary, with entire, ± ovate lobes; trees often with strictly ascending branches producing a narrow, columnar form

c1.text: Petioles broad-elliptic to terete in cross-section (sometimes slightly flattened near the apex), usually with a shallow channel on the upper surface
Petioles conspicuously compressed from the lateral surfaces, without a channel on the upper surface

c2.text: Mature leaf blades of long shoots abaxially tomentose, the margins varying from 3- to 5-lobed or irregularly serrate with coarse teeth
Mature leaf blades abaxially glabrous or with pubescence confined to the main veins, the margins regularly serrate or crenate-serrate

c3.text: Leaf blades obtuse to rounded at the apex, cordate at the base [Fig. ], sometimes narrowed to a short, broad base prior to junction with petiole, without orange resin on the abaxial surface, permanently pubescent on the abaxial veins; terminal winter bud not or scarcely viscid
Leaf blades acute to short-acuminate at the apex, broad-cuneate to subcordate at the base, often with streaks of orange resin on the abaxial surface, glabrous; terminal winter bud very viscid

c4.text: Leaf blades with a definite, though sometimes very narrow, translucent margin [Fig. ]
Leaf blades lacking a translucent border [Fig. ]

Leaf blades on long shoots 10–18 cm long, ciliate, serrate with teeth 2–5 mm tall; apex of petiole with 2–5 glands; branchlets often somewhat 4-angled; lateral winter buds ascending

c6.text: Leaf blades narrow-ovate to broad-ovate, (5–) 7–12 cm long; terminal winter buds pubescent
Leaf blades rhombic to suborbicular or reniform, 2–8 (–10) cm long; terminal winter buds glabrous to sparsely pubescent

Leaf blade coarsely sinuate-dentate with mostly 5–10 teeth per margin taller than 1 mm

All carpellate aments alternate

Floral bracts of aments brown or black, at least at the apex [Figs. , ]

Stipes (2–) 3–6 mm long; floral bracts persistent in fruit; branchlets of previous year usually pubescent; styles 0.1–0.4 mm long; aments never branched

c7.text: Aments precocious (i.e., expanding before the leaves)
Aments coetaneous or serotinous (i.e., expanding with or after the leaves, respectively)

Stipe 0.6–2.7 mm long; styles 0–0.5 (–0.6) mm long (up to 1 mm long in S. discolor )

c9.text: Plants of alpine and subalpine areas, elevation near or exceeding 1000 m
Plants not of alpine areas, elevation less than 1000 m

Branchlets not glaucous; adaxial nectaries 0.9–1.4 mm long, longer than the stipe; ovules 18–19 per ovary; non-native plants escaping from cultivation (in part)

Carpellate aments 10–18 mm long, with floral bracts 0.8–1.4 mm long; decumbent shrubs 0.3–0.7 m tall

Stipes 0.6–4 mm long; styles 0–0.5 mm long

c22.text: Floral bracts brown to black (at least at the apex), persisting until after dehiscence of the capsule [Figs. , ]

c24.text: Styles 0.35–1 mm long; floral bracts 1.1–1.8 mm long; aments 11–47 mm long
Styles 0.2–0.4 mm long; floral bracts 0.5–1 mm long; aments 3.2–13 mm long (in part)

c25.text: Floral bracts 0.8–1.6 mm long; styles 0.3–0.6 mm long; stigmas 0.16–0.28 mm wide
Floral bracts 1.2–3 mm long (mean=1.8 mm); styles (0.3–) 0.5–1.3 mm long; stigmas 0.24–0.56 mm wide

c26.text: Dwarf shrubs 0.01–0.15 m tall, of alpine habitats, elevation exceeding 1000 m; aments 3.2–13 mm long, with 2–11 flowers (in part)
Short shrubs to trees, 0.3–25 m tall, not of alpine communities; aments 17–80 mm long, with more than 11 flowers

Aments densely flowered; flowers spirally arranged about the rachis of the ament

Emerging leaf blades without bloom abaxially (though paler than the adaxial surface), generally pubescent, but the pubescence not dense enough to conceal the surface

Floral bracts (1–) 1.5–4 mm long, abaxially sparsely to densely pubescent throughout

Emerging leaf blades thick-membranaceous to herbaceous, opaque or nearly so; stipes 0.2–2.4 mm long; capsules 3–5 mm long (7–12 mm long in S. serissima )

Styles 0.3–0.8 mm long; aments unbranched; expanding leaves closely serrulate

Adaxial nectaries 0.4–0.8 mm long, to fully as long as the stipe; abaxial nectaries present or absent; emerging leaves never with red-brown hairs

Upright or low-spreading shrubs or small trees (0.3–) 1–15 m tall, of various habitats

Leaf blades 2–4 cm long, mostly 1.2–2 times as long as wide; petioles mostly 5–12 mm long; winter buds 3–8 mm long

Leaves alternate throughout

Fresh leaf blades plane, the margins not rolled under

Leaf blades 4–17 cm long; shrubs or small trees to 5 m tall; stipules commonly present
