Leaf blades 1.5–2.5 times as long as wide, broader at the base, widely tapering to truncate or subcordate at the base, the margins crenate, the teeth with inconspicuous, pale glands

c6.text: Leaf blades pubescent on one or both surfaces, sometimes sparsely so; capsules spotted or suffused with purple to purple-brown [Fig. ], the cleistogamous ones borne on prostrate to low-arching peduncles; seeds 1.6–2.1 mm long
Leaf blades glabrous on both surfaces; capsules green (often with minute orange dots in V. pallens ) [Fig. ], the cleistogamous ones borne on ascending to arching peduncles; seeds 1–1.7 mm long

c7.text: Seeds 1–1.4 mm long, brown to nearly black
Seeds 1.5–1.7 mm long, light gray to light brown

c8.text: Rhizomes horizontal to ascending, elongate, slender, mostly 1–3 mm thick
Rhizomes usually ascending, short, stout, mostly 4–6 mm thick

c9.text: Leaf blades cordate-ovate to cordate-suborbicular, acute to obtuse at the apex; basal sinus of leaf blade either narrow or with converging to overlapping lobes; stipules connate to the petiole for a short distance; seeds 1.5–1.9 mm long
Leaf blades cordate-orbicular to reniform, rounded to obtuse at the apex; basal sinus of leaf blade wide open; stipules distinct from the petiole; seeds 1.9–2.4 mm long

c10.text: Leaf blades with conspicuous lobes (though the first leaves to appear in V. palmata are unlobed)
Leaf blades all unlobed

c11.text: Leaf blades oblong-lanceolate to ovate-triangular, 1.5–3 times as long as wide, coarsely serrate to divided into short lobes at the base [Fig. ]; lobes, if present, less than 50% of the total length of the leaf blade (in part)

Leaf blades ± ovate in outline, less than 1.5 times as long as wide, with evident lobes (except for the first leaves to emerge which may be unlobed to weakly lobed); lobes often greater than 50% of the total length of the leaf blade

c12.text: Capsules green [Fig. ]; sepals lanceolate, narrow-acute to acuminate at the apex, eciliate or ciliate
Capsules spotted or suffused with purple to purple-brown on a green background [Fig. ]; sepals ovate, rounded to obtuse at the apex, usually at least sparsely ciliate [Fig. ]

c13.text: Foliage pubescent; rhizome fleshy, barrel-like; cleistogamous flowers not produced; sepals usually ciliate
Foliage glabrous; rhizome ± firm, not barrel-like; cleistogamous flowers produced—these recognized by the coiled style; sepals eciliate [Fig. ]

c14.text: Plants heterophyllous, the early- and late-season leaves unlobed, the middle-season leaves lobed [Fig. ]; leaf blades divided into 3–5 segments, the middle lobe usually without smaller lateral lobes [Fig. ]

Plants homophyllous, all of the leaves with evident lobes [Fig. ]; leaf blades with 5–16 lobes that become progressively smaller and separated by shallower sinuses toward the basal margins, the middle lobe usually with smaller lateral lobes [Fig. ]

c15.text: Leaf blades 1.5–3 times as long as wide, truncate to subcordate at the base, usually more coarsely serrate or even somewhat lobed at the base of the blade (especially in later season leaves; not so in V. japonica )

Leaf blades commonly less than 1.75 times as long as wide, definitely cordate at the base, the teeth at the base of the blade no more obvious than those along the middle of the blade margin (except in V. pectinata )

c16.text: Stipules distinct; roots white-brown to yellow-brown; leaf blade not, or scarcely, decurrent on the petiole (in part)
Stipules connate to the petiole; roots dark brown; leaf blade decurrent on petiole

c17.text: Leaves on spreading petioles, nearly flat to the ground; stipules entire; cleistogamous flowers borne on a horizontal, late-appearing stem, usually 2 or more, the stem appearing raceme-like
Leaves mostly on ascending petioles, held above the ground; stipules ciliate-toothed on the margin; cleistogamous flowers borne singly at the summit of a peduncle

c18.text: Leaf blades with prominent, coarse (i.e., almost lobe-like) teeth near the basal margins that gradually become shorter and narrower toward the apex
Leaf blades with rather uniform teeth along the margin

c19.text: Leaf blades longer than wide, acute to short-acuminate at the apex; sepals eciliate [Figs. , ]
Leaf blades as wide as or wider than long, mostly rounded to obtuse at the apex; sepals usually ciliate (eciliate in V. nephrophylla ) [Fig. ]

c20.text: Sepal auricles 2–5.3 mm long on cleistogamous fruits; cleistogamous flowers borne on ascending peduncles; capsules green, 10–15 mm long; seeds dark brown to black-red or olive-black

Sepal auricles 0.5–1.6 mm long; cleistogamous flowers borne on peduncles that are at first prostrate, later ascending from a declined base; capsules spotted or suffused with purple, 6–10 mm long; seeds light yellow-brown to brown (infrequently to dark brown in V. sororia )

c21.text: Sepals narrow-ovate, rounded to obtuse at apex; peduncles often pubescent; capsules glabrous; seeds brown, sometimes with darker brown markings (rarely yellow-brown)
Sepals lanceolate, narrow-acute to acuminate at apex; peduncles glabrous [Figs. , ]; capsules sometimes pubescent; seeds light yellow-brown

c22.text: Leaf blades glabrous; peduncles of cleistogamous capsules ascending, not declined at base; capsules green

Leaf blades usually with some hairs on one or both surfaces; peduncles of cleistogamous capsules at first prostrate (or even subterranean), later ascending from a declined base; capsules spotted or suffused with purple

c23.text: Pubescence of leaves consisting of silver hairs concentrated on the adaxial surface, the abaxial surface and petioles glabrous or nearly so; leaves usually rounded at apex, often suffused with purple

Pubescence of leaves variable, but not concentrated on adaxial surface and often found on the petioles; leaves rounded, to more commonly, obtusely to acutely pointed at apex, without purple coloration

c24.text: Plants annual from an erect taproot; stipules foliaceous and prominently lobed in a pinnatifid fashion
Plants perennial from rhizomes; stipules scarious to herbaceous or subfoliaceous, entire to lacerate-toothed along the margin [Fig. ]

c25.text: Lower leaf blades usually truncate to subcordate at the base; capsules (6–) 6.5–9.5 mm long
Lower leaf blades usually broad-cuneate to truncate at the base; capsules 4–6.5 mm long

c26.text: Stipules scarious to herbaceous, entire to dentate or undulate; capsules 5–12 mm long; stems often produced singly at the summit of the rhizome

Stipules herbaceous or subfoliaceous, fimbriate to lacerate-toothed (entire in high-elevation plants of V. labradorica ); capsules 4–6 mm long; stems often clustered together at the summit of the rhizome

c27.text: Stipules scarious or subscarious, pale, entire; capsules 5–10 mm long; seeds 1.5–2.2 ×1.2–1.5 mm
Stipules herbaceous, green, mostly dentate or undulate; capsules 10–12 mm long; seeds 2.5–3.2 ×1.5–1.8 mm

c28.text: Sepals ciliate; leaf blade margins with closely set, crenulate teeth
Sepals eciliate [Figs. , ]; leaf blades variously subentire to remotely or regularly crenulate

c29.text: Upper stem leaf blades narrow-ovate, tending to be acuminate at the apex; seeds mostly 1.1–1.4 mm thick
Upper stem leaf blades triangular-lanceolate to ovate or orbicular, rounded to acute at the apex; seeds mostly 0.8–1.1 mm thick

c30.text: Leaves commonly sparsely to densely pubescent, the hairs never restricted to the adaxial ( i.e. , upper) surface only, the blades dark blue-green to dark gray-green in life, subcoriaceous, often with a revolute margin, the upper blades ovate to triangular-lanceolate and mostly truncate at the base; petioles distinctly winged; seeds dark brown to olive-black, mostly 0.8–1.0 mm thick

Leaves commonly glabrous, when pubescent the hairs restricted to the adaxial surface, the blades light green in life, thin, not or barely revolute, the upper blades usually ovate to orbicular, with a cordate base; petioles not distinctly winged; seeds light brown to brown (dark brown), mostly 1–1.1 mm thick

/dkey/viola-key-for-chasmogamous-floweri.title: Viola key for chasmogamous flowering material

c1.text: Plants acaulescent, the leaves and peduncles arising directly from rhizomes or stolons [Figs. , ]
Plants with leafy aerial stems, the peduncles arising from the axils of leaves [Fig. ]

c2.text: Petals entirely yellow; stipules entire; stigma essentially lacking a beak
Petals not entirely yellow, mostly purple, violet, or white; stipules ciliate, toothed, or lacerate on the margin; stigma with a conical, scoop-shaped, or hook-shaped beak

c3.text: Style terminating in a slender, downward-oriented, hook-shaped beak; ovary (and later the capsule) pubescent
Style dilated at apex, terminating in a scoop-shaped or conical beak; ovary and capsule glabrous (capsule rarely pubescent in V. affinis )

c4.text: Spur elongate, 4–10 mm long, 2 or more times as long as wide; flowers with purple, glabrous petals; stipules connate to the petioles
Spur shorter, up to 3.2 mm long and less than 2 times as long as wide; flowers with purple or white petals, when purple then at least the lateral petals pubescent; stipules distinct

c5.text: Leaf blades cordate-ovate to cordate-suborbicular, 0.8–1.3 times as long as wide, with a deep basal sinus, not decurrent on the petiole; spur 4–6 mm long

Leaf blades oblong to broad-lanceolate, becoming narrow-triangular to narrow-ovate post anthesis, 1.5–2.7 times as long as wide, broad-cuneate to subcordate at the base, decurrent on the petiole; spur 5–10 mm long

c6.text: Flowers relatively smaller, mostly 7–12 mm long, with white petals (pale blue in one alpine species); rhizomes slender, mostly less than 3 mm thick, usually horizontal; stolons produced, at least by summer (not produced in V. renifolia )
Flowers relatively larger, mostly 13–22 mm long, with purple petals (rare albino forms said to exist); rhizomes stouter, mostly 4–6 mm thick, usually ascending; stolons not produced

c7.text: Leaf blades 1.5–7 times as long as wide, narrow-cuneate to subcordate at the base
Leaf blades up to 1.5 times as long as wide, cordate at the base

c8.text: Leaf blades 3–7 times as long as wide, narrowly tapering at the base, the margins denticulate, each tooth with a distinct red-brown to black gland at the apex
Leaf blades 1.5–2.5 times as long as wide, broader at the base, widely tapering to truncate or subcordate at the base, the margins crenate, the teeth with inconspicuous, pale glands

c9.text: Corolla violet or at least tinged with violet; lateral petals sparsely pubescent; plants restricted to alpine areas over 900 m elevation
Corolla white; lateral petals glabrous or pubescent;

c10.text: Leaf blades low-crenate or subentire along the margins, thin, strictly glabrous
Leaf blades low-serrate along the margins, thicker, commonly with some pubescence (sometimes glabrous in V. renifolia with characteristically wide leaves––see description)

c11.text: Leaf blades cordate-orbicular to reniform, the midrib usually equaling 50–77 percent of the total blade width; stolons not produced; pubescence variable, but when restricted to a single side of the blade, then found only on the abaxial (i.e., lower) surface

Leaf blades broad cordate-ovate (to cordate-orbicular), the midrib usually equaling 75–90 percent of the total blade width; stolons present, at least later in season; pubescence variable, but when restricted to a single side of the blade, then found only on the adaxial (i.e., upper) surface

c12.text: Leaf blades with conspicuous lobes (though the first leaves to appear in V. palmata are unlobed) [Figs. , ]
Leaf blades all unlobed

c13.text: Leaf blades oblong-lanceolate to ovate-triangular, 1.5–3 times as long as wide, coarsely serrate to divided into short lobes at the base [Fig. ]; lobes, if present, less than 50% of the total length of the leaf blade (in part)

Leaf blades ± ovate in outline, less than 1.5 times as long as wide, with evident lobes (except for the first leaves to emerge which may be unlobed to weakly lobed); lobes often greater than 50% of the total length of the leaf blade

c14.text: Lateral petals glabrous; style lacking a beak, with an asymmetrical concave summit; corolla rotate (i.e., wide open), the stamens clearly visible; corolla either bicolorous with the upper two petals dark purple or concolorous and all the petals light violet

Lateral petals pubescent on inner surface; style with a conical beak on the lower side of the expanded apex; corolla only distally spreading, the stamens somewhat concealed; corolla concolorous with violet to purple petals

c15.text: Sepals lanceolate, narrow-acute to acuminate at the apex, eciliate [Fig. ]; leaf blades and petioles essentially glabrous
Sepals ovate, rounded to obtuse at the apex, usually ciliate [Fig. ]; leaf blades and petioles pubescent

c16.text: Plants heterophyllous, the early- and late-season leaves unlobed, the middle season leaves lobed [Fig. ]; leaf blades divided into 3–5 segments, the middle lobe usually without smaller lateral lobes [Fig. ]

Plants homophyllous, all of the leaves with evident lobes [Fig. ]; leaf blades with 5–16 lobes that become progressively smaller and separated by shallower sinuses toward the basal margins, the middle lobe usually with smaller lateral lobes [Fig. ]

c17.text: Leaf blades 1.5–3 times as long as wide, cuneate to subcordate at the base, often more coarsely serrate or even somewhat lobed at the base of the blade (especially in later season leaves) [Fig. ] (in part)

Leaf blades commonly less than 1.75 times as long as wide, definitely cordate at the base, the teeth at the base of the blade no more obvious than those along the middle of the blade margin (except in V. pectinata )

c18.text: Lateral petals pubescent with hairs shorter than 1 mm and are knob-shaped at the apex [Fig. ]; spurred petal glabrous [Fig. ]
Hairs of three lower petals longer than 1 mm and tapering to broadly rounded at the apex [Fig. ]; spurred petal sparsely pubescent (rarely glabrous in V. sororia ) [Fig. ]

c19.text: Sepals ciliate (sometimes eciliate in V. hirsutula ) [Fig. ]; leaf blades usually as wide as or wider than long and pubescent
Sepals eciliate [Figs. , ]; leaf blades either conspicuously longer than wide or essentially glabrous or both

c20.text: Pubescence of leaves consisting of silver hairs concentrated on the adaxial surface, the abaxial surface and petioles glabrous or nearly so; leaves usually rounded at apex, often suffused with purple abaxially

Pubescence of leaves variable, but not concentrated on the adaxial surface and often found on the petioles; leaves rounded, to more commonly, obtusely to acutely pointed at apex, without purple coloration

c21.text: Sepals lanceolate, narrow-acute to acuminate at apex [Figs. , ]
Sepals ovate to narrow-ovate or ovate-oblong, obtuse to rounded at apex [Fig. ]

c22.text: Leaf blades triangular at chasmogamous anthesis, becoming broad-triangular, later with prominent, coarse teeth near the basal margins that gradually become shorter and narrower toward the apex
Leaf blades narrow-ovate, with rather uniform teeth along the margin

c23.text: Leaf blades longer than wide, often narrow cordate-ovate to triangular; lateral petals spreading, the flowers wide open in life; leaves commonly pubescent
Leaf blades as wide as or wider than long, often broad-cordate-ovate; lateral petal directed forward, the flowers narrow in life; leaves glabrous

c24.text: Plants annual, with taproots; stipules foliaceous, prominently lobed in pinnatifid fashion; style dilated upward into a globose, hollow stigma with a wide orifice on the lower side
Plants perennial from rhizomes; stipules scarious to herbaceous, entire to toothed or lacerate [Fig. ]; style either slender at the apex or capitate, but not globose

c25.text: Flowers longer than 15 mm; petals exceeding the sepals by 2 mm or more; corolla variously colored, often yellow-white or yellow-orange with a yellow center and the upper petals dark blue on the apical half or sometimes dark blue throughout with a yellow center
Flowers up to 10 mm long; petals shorter than the sepals or up to 2 mm longer than the sepals; corolla variously colored, often yellow-white with a yellow center

c26.text: Petals white to cream or violet to purple, the lateral ones pubescent with hairs that taper to the apex (glabrous in V. rostrata ); spur 3–18 mm long, usually 2 or more times as long as wide; style slender throughout or only slightly widened apically, not capitate, bent at the apex (straight in V. rostrata )

Petals yellow or white with yellow at the base, the lateral ones pubescent with hairs that are dilated and rounded or knob-shaped at the apex; spur less than 2 mm long and less than 2 times as long as wide; style capitate at the apex

c27.text: Petals white to cream; sepals ciliate
Petals violet to purple; sepals eciliate

c28.text: Spur 8–15 mm long; lateral petals glabrous; style ± straight
Spur 2.8–7 mm long; lateral petals pubescent on inner surface; style bent near tip

c29.text: Leaf blades commonly with sparse to dense pubescence, the hairs never restricted to the adaxial surface, the upper blades ovate to triangular-lanceolate and mostly truncate at the base; petioles distinctly winged; style slightly expanded apically, terminating in a stout, bent tip as long as the diameter of the style

Leaf blades commonly glabrous, when pubescent the hairs restricted to the adaxial surface, the upper blades usually ovate to orbicular, with a cordate base; petioles not distinctly winged; style of nearly uniform diameter throughout, terminating in a bent tip nearly twice as long as the diameter of the style

c30.text: Petals entirely yellow; stipules herbaceous, green
Petals white with a yellow base, tinged with purple on the outside; stipules scarious or subscarious, pale

c1.text: Perigynium beakless or with a beak shorter than 0.5 mm
Perigynium tapering to a distinct beak 0.6–1.8 mm long

c2.text: Leaves coriaceous, involute, heavily glaucous; perigynia appressed-ascending, tapering to a beakless or short, straight-beaked apex

Leaves herbaceous, flat, folded, or M-shaped in cross-section (at least when young), sometimes ± flat at maturity, not or only slightly glaucous; perigynia ascending to spreading, concavely tapering (at least on one surface) to a short, curved beak

c3.text: Reproductive stems smooth along the angles; lowermost bract of inflorescence short, the blade and sheath mostly 28–58% of the total inflorescence height
Reproductive stems scabrous along the angles (at least near the summit); lowermost bract of inflorescence relatively elongate, the blade and sheath mostly 62–111% of the total inflorescence height

c4.text: Achenes 1.2–1.6 (–1.8) mm wide; ligules of leaves (0.6–) 1–6 mm long, (0.8–) 1–2 times as long as wide; leaf blades green; carpellate spikes 3–5.8 mm thick
Achenes 1.7–2.2 (–2.5) mm wide; ligule of leaves 0.4–3.6 mm long, 0.4–1.2 times as long as wide; leaf blades gray-green; carpellate spikes 3.5–8 mm thick

c5.text: Lower sheaths of reproductive stems pale brown; perigynia and abaxial leaf blade surface not, or only sparsely, minutely papillose; lower perigynia of each spike loosely arranged; plants of forested wetlands

Lower sheaths of reproductive stems strongly tinged with anthocyanin; perigynia and abaxial leaf blade surface minutely papillose; lower perigynia of each spike densely arranged; plants of well-drained, sandy soils

c1.text: This section contains exactly one species.
This section contains exactly one species.
Spikes usually 1 per stem; anthers (2–) 2.2–3.6 mm long; leaf blades involute
Spikes 2 or more per stem; anthers 0.6–2.2 (–2.3) mm long; leaf blades flat or folded

c2.text: Beak of perigynium with smooth margins
Beak of perigynium at least sparsely ciliate-serrulate on the margins

c3.text: Plants subdioecious, the spikes all or nearly all of a single sex on each stem (rarely with entirely carpellate and entirely staminate spikes on the same plant); uppermost spike either entirely staminate or entirely carpellate or mostly carpellate with as many as 3 staminate flowers at the base (i.e., lacking a prolonged, basal staminate portion); anthers (1–) 1.2–2.2 (–2.3) mm long

Plants monoecious, at least the uppermost spike clearly bisexual; uppermost spike gynecandrous, never entirely staminate, usually with a prolonged, slender base of 2–21 staminate flowers; anthers 0.6–1.6 (–2) mm long

c4.text: Widest leaves 2.8–5 mm wide
Widest leaves 0.8–2.7 mm wide

c5.text: Perigynia broad-ovate to suborbicular, 1.5–3 mm wide, 1–1.7 times as long as wide (in part)
Perigynia ovate to broad-ovate, (1.25–) 1.4–2 (–2.1) mm wide, (1.4–) 1.6–2.5 times as long as wide

c6.text: Perigynia (2.6–) 2.9–3.6 (–4) mm long, 1.8–3.2 times as long as wide, with a long beak (0.85–) 0.95–2 mm long and (0.4–) 0.45–0.86 times as long as the body of the perigynium
Perigynia 1.9–3 (–3.3) mm long, (1.15–) 1.3–2 (–2.2) times as long as wide, with a short beak 0.4–0.95 mm long and 0.18–0.5 (–0.63) times as long as the body of the perigynium

c7.text: Perigynia convexly tapered in the apical portion, forming shoulders below the beak, veinless or with as many as 6 faint veins adaxially, with many, fine serrations on the beak
Perigynia gradually or concavely tapered in the apical portion (i.e., without shoulders), with 1–10 veins adaxially, with fewer and coarser serrations on the beak (in part)

c1.text: This section contains exactly one species.
This section contains exactly one species.
Perigynia 0.8–1.3 mm wide, (3.5–) 4–6.1 (–6.6) times as long as wide, with 4–8 usually prominent veins adaxially; leaf blades 1.3–3.1 mm wide
Perigynia 1.3–1.5 (–1.6) mm wide, 2.9–3.8 times as long as wide, veinless or less commonly with 1–5 obscure veins adaxially; widest leaf blades 2.4–4.2 mm wide
This section contains exactly one species.
Carpellate spikes with widely radiating perigynia, the lower of each spike often reflexed; achenes 1.1–1.4 mm wide, with a sinuous, persistent style; beak of perigynium usually smooth

Carpellate spikes with appressed-ascending to ascending perigynia; achenes 1.4–1.7 mm wide, with a partially deciduous style and only the straight basal portion remaining on the achene; beak of perigynium often sparsely scabrous
This section contains exactly one species.
Carpellate scales 1.6–2.2 mm wide, green with a hyaline margin 0.3–0.8 mm wide; uppermost spike with 3–29 staminate flowers; perigynia 1.2–1.7 mm wide; stigmas long, filiform, strongly papillose
Carpellate scales (2–) 2.5–6.5 mm wide, green throughout; uppermost spike with 2 or 3 staminate flowers; perigynia 1.9–3.2 mm wide; stigmas short, clavate-thickened, minutely papillose
This section contains exactly one species.
Longest bract of inflorescence 5–20 cm long, (3–) 5 or more times as long as the inflorescence; distance from apex of achene to apex of perigynium 3–5 mm [Fig. ]
Longest bract of inflorescence rarely exceeding 5 cm, up to 2 times as long as inflorescence; distance from apex of achene to apex of perigynium 1.2–3.1 (–3.7) mm [Figs. , , ]

c2.text: Carpellate scales nearly equaling to slightly exceeding the length of the perigynia, mostly concealing the beaks of the perigynia in intact spikes [Fig. ]
Carpellate scales, excluding the awns (when present), clearly exceeded by the perigynia, the tip of the perigynia beaks visible in intact spikes [Fig. ]

c3.text: Leaves stiff, very glaucous (except in shade), many with rounded auricles at the summit of the sheath; floral scales white or white-brown; plants of Atlantic coast shores and near shore habitats (in part)
Leaves softer, slightly or not at all glaucous, without auricles; floral scales white-green or brown; plants usually not coastal

c4.text: Carpellate scales about as wide as the perigynia they subtend; achenes 1.6–2 mm wide; lowest bract usually broad and flat at base, sometimes exceeding the spike it subtends
Carpellate scales narrower than the perigynia they subtend; achenes 0.7–1.6 mm wide; lowest bract usually setaceous and shorter than the spike it subtends

c5.text: Beak of perigynium flat, winged, and minutely serrulate to the apex [Fig. ]
Beak of perigynium cylindric, unwinged, and entire in the apical (0.3–) 0.4–1 mm [Fig. ]

c6.text: Perigynium body lanceolate, 0.9–1.4 mm wide, with the marginal wing usually conspicuously reduced (or even absent) on the lower half of the body [Fig. ]
Perigynium body ovate, (1.5–) 1.7–2.5 mm wide, with the marginal wing scarcely and gradually (if at all) reduced on the lower half of the body [Fig. ]

c7.text: Perigynia smooth, adaxially without veins or with 4–8 curving veins of unequal length; inflorescence with 3–7 (–11) spikes, the upper ones usually separate; carpellate scales red-brown to green or gold-brown

Perigynia granular-papillose, adaxially with (4–) 5–8 (–10) ± parallel veins of equal length; inflorescence with (3–) 7–15 spikes, the upper ones usually densely aggregated; carpellate scales pale white-green

c8.text: Perigynia 3.4–4.7 (–5.2) mm long; inflorescence usually erect, with approximate spikes, the internode between the second and third spike counting from the base (2.5–) 3–6 mm long; apical, herbaceous portion of leaf sheath smooth

Perigynia (3.7–) 4.5–6 mm long; inflorescence usually open and ± nodding, the internode between the second and third spike (2.5–) 4–10 mm long; apical, herbaceous portion of leaf sheath minutely papillose

c9.text: Perigynia up to 2 mm wide
Perigynia wider than 2 mm

c10.text: Carpellate scales of the basal median portion of the spike tapering to a slender, acuminate point, often prolonged into a short awn tip
Carpellate scales of the basal median portion of the spike obtuse to subacuminate at the apex, without awn tips

c11.text: Perigynia bodies lanceolate, 0.9–1.3 mm wide; achene 0.6–0.8 mm wide; inflorescence congested, the lowest internode 2–3 (–5) mm long
Perigynia bodies lanceolate to ovate, obovate, or nearly orbicular, 1.2–2.9 mm wide; achene 0.7–1.1 mm wide; inflorescence congested to open, the lowest internode 2–18 mm long

c12.text: Perigynia 1.2–2.1 mm wide, 2.6 or more times as long as wide; leaf sheaths opposite the blade with a prolonged, narrow hyaline area
Perigynia 1.8–2.8 mm wide, up to 2.5 times as long as wide; leaf sheaths opposite the blade firm and green-veined nearly to the summit, the hyaline area very short

c13.text: Staminate portion of lateral spikes 2–6 mm long; beak of perigynium spreading, usually 50% or more of the length of the nearly orbicular body; plants of freshwater wetlands
Staminate portion of lateral spikes shorter than 2 mm; beak of perigynium ascending, less than 50% of the length of the narrow-ovate to obovate body; plants of saline-influenced habitats

c14.text: Marginal wing of perigynium usually conspicuously reduced (or even absent) in the lower half of the body; leaves with blades 3–7.5 mm wide, with narrow, decurrent wings on the sheath that are continuous with the blade midrib and margins; vegetative shoots conspicuous, with numerous leaves spaced throughout the apical half of the stem

Marginal wing of perigynium scarcely and gradually (if at all) reduced in the lower half of the body; leaves with blades 1–4.5 mm wide (up to 6.5 mm in C. normalis ), with inconspicuous, rounded edges on the sheath that are continuous with the blade midrib and margins; vegetative shoots inconspicuous, with few leaves clustered near apex of stem

c15.text: Perigynia in basal portion of spike spreading or recurved; spikes spherical or subspherical; carpellate scales 1.6–2.3 mm long
Perigynia in basal portion of spike appressed-ascending to ascending-spreading; spikes subspherical to ovoid or obovoid; carpellate scales 2–3 mm long

c16.text: Inflorescence erect, with congested and overlapping spikes, each spike with (30–) 40 or more perigynia; perigynia appressed-ascending to ascending; apical portion of the leaf sheath opposite the blade firm and green-veined nearly to the summit, the hyaline area 3–8 mm long

Inflorescence arching or nodding, with separate spikes in the basal portion (uncommonly the inflorescence ± congested), each spike with 15–30 perigynia; perigynia ascending to spreading; apical portion of the leaf sheath opposite the blade with a prolonged, hyaline area 4–20 mm long

c17.text: Body of the perigynium elliptic to orbicular or obovate, broadest at or above the middle [Fig. ]
Body of the perigynium broad-lanceolate to ovate, widest below the middle

c18.text: At least some spikes with a pronounced, narrow, staminate base longer than 2 mm; inflorescence arching to nodding; achenes ovate in outline (in part)
Spikes with an inconspicuous staminate base shorter than 2 mm; inflorescence ± erect; achenes narrow-oblong to oblong or elliptic in outline

c19.text: Perigynium body elliptic to suborbicular, broadest near the middle; achenes 0.9–1.3 mm wide; inflorescence congested, the lowest internode 1.5–6 mm long (in part)
Perigynium body obovate [Fig. ]; achenes 0.7–1 mm wide; inflorescence close, but usually not congested near the base, the lowest internode (1–) 3–14 mm

c20.text: Carpellate scales obtuse; perigynium beak triangular [Fig. ], appressed-ascending; styles straight; apical, herbaceous portion of leaf sheath minutely papillose
Carpellate scales acute; perigynium beak slender, spreading [Fig. ]; styles laterally sinuous; apical, herbaceous portion of leaf sheath smooth

c21.text: Inflorescence congested, with crowded spikes, the lowest internode usually shorter than 6 mm
Inflorescence elongate, the lower spikes remote, the lowest internode usually longer than 6 mm

c22.text: Perigynia adaxially with 1–3 faint veins near the base; achenes 0.6–0.9 mm wide
Perigynia adaxially usually with 3–7 conspicuous veins; achenes 0.9–1.2 mm wide

c23.text: Leaves with blades 1.5–3.5 mm wide, with lower sheaths that are tight, ± evenly colored, and sometimes cross-corrugated; apical, herbaceous portion of leaf sheath minutely papillose; mature perigynia tan to brown (in part)

Leaves with blades 2.2–6 (–6.5) mm wide, with lower sheaths that are loose, green and white-mottled or -striped, and not corrugated; apical, herbaceous portion of leaf sheath smooth; perigynia green (at least apically) (in part)

c24.text: Leaves with blades 2.2–6 (–6.5) mm wide, the lower sheaths loose; flowering stems with 3–7 leaves; apical, herbaceous portion of the leaf sheath smooth (in part)

Leaves with blades 1.3–2.5 (–3) mm wide, the lower sheaths tight; flowering stems with 2–4 leaves; apical, herbaceous portion of at least some leaf sheaths minutely papillose (smooth in the very rare C. echinodes )

c25.text: At least some leaf sheaths minutely papillose near the apex on the herbaceous portion, not prominently mottled or striped with white near the base; beaks of perigynia of intact spikes appressed to spreading-ascending, exceeding the subtending scales by 0–0.8 mm; beaks and shoulders of perigynia stramineous to red-brown at maturity; carpellate scales mostly 0.8–1 times as long as the perigynia they subtend

Leaf sheaths smooth near the apex, often mottled or striped with white near the base; beaks of perigynia of intact spikes spreading, exceeding the subtending scales by 0.7–1.6 mm; beaks and shoulders of perigynia green to green-brown at maturity; carpellate scales mostly 0.6–0.85 times as long as the perigynia they subtend

c26.text: Leaves stiff, very glaucous (except in shade), many with rounded auricles at the summit of the sheath; floral scales white or white-brown; plants of Atlantic coast shores and near shore habitats (in part)
Leaves softer, not or only slightly glaucous, without auricles; scales light green to green or white-brown to brown; plants not of coastal shores (except C. hormathodes )

c27.text: Carpellate scales of the basal median portion of the spike tapering to a slender, acuminate point, often prolonged into a short awn tip
Carpellate scales of the basal median portion of the spike obtuse to subacuminate at the apex, without awn tips

c28.text: Perigynia 2.5–3.8 mm wide, broad-obovate; leaf blades 2.5–6 mm wide
Perigynia 1.9–2.8 mm wide, narrow-ovate to orbicular or obovate; leaf blades 1–3 mm wide

c29.text: Perigynia obovate, widest above the middle; apical portion of the leaf sheath opposite the blade firm and green-veined nearly to the summit

Perigynia broad-lanceolate, ovate, elliptic, or orbicular, widest at or below the middle; apical portion of the leaf sheath opposite the blade with a prolonged, hyaline area (except in C. molesta and C. normalis )

c30.text: Leaves with blades 3–6 (–8) mm wide, the summit of the sheaths truncate (unless torn); perigynia adaxially with inconspicuous veins
Leaves with blades 2–4.5 mm wide, the summit of the sheaths concave; perigynia adaxially with 4–many veins

c31.text: Perigynia broad-lanceolate to ovate, green (at least apically); leaves with blades 2.2–6 (–6.5) mm wide, the lower sheaths green and white-mottled or -striped; sheath summits truncate, prolonged up to 2 mm above sheath apex (in part)

Perigynia ovate to broad-ovate or elliptic to orbicular, yellow-brown to tan or brown; leaves with blades 1.5–4 (–5) mm wide, the lower sheaths ± evenly colored; sheath summits usually concave (sometimes truncate and prolonged)

c32.text: Perigynia bodies broad-elliptic to orbicular, broadest near the middle
Perigynia bodies ovate to broad-ovate

c33.text: At least some spikes with a pronounced, narrow, staminate base longer than 2 mm; inflorescence arching to nodding, the lowest internode 3–18 mm long; achenes ovate in outline (in part)
Spikes with an inconspicuous staminate base shorter than 2 mm; inflorescence ± erect, the lowest internode 1.5–6 mm; achenes narrow-oblong to elliptic in outline (in part)

c34.text: Perigynia (1.4–) 1.6–2.4 mm wide; achenes 0.9–1.2 mm wide; hyaline region of leaf sheath opposite leaf blade sometimes cross-corrugated (in part)
Perigynia (2–) 2.3–4.2 mm wide; achenes 1.1–1.8 mm wide; hyaline region of leaf sheath not corrugated

c35.text: Marginal wing of perigynium evenly and minutely serrulate [Fig. ]; apical, herbaceous portion of leaf sheaths smooth
Marginal wing of perigynium often irregularly erose or toothed, in addition to minutely serrulate [Fig. ]; apical, herbaceous portion of leaf sheaths minutely papillose

c36.text: Perigynia 3.3–5 mm long, adaxially veinless or with 1–5 faint veins [Fig. ], exceeding the carpellate scales by 0.2–1.3 mm; anthers 1.3–2.6 mm long
Perigynia (4.5–) 5.1–6.7 (–7.1) mm long, adaxially with 4–8 veins, exceeding the carpellate scales by (1–) 1.4–2.3 mm; anthers (2.4–) 2.8–4.2 mm long

c1.text: Perigynia essentially beakless; inflorescence 6–12 mm tall, consisting of 2–4 aggregated and overlapping spikes
Perigynia definitely, although sometimes shortly, beaked; inflorescence mostly 15–100 mm tall, consisting of (1–) 2–15 aggregated to long-remote spikes

c2.text: Spikes (1–) 2–4 per stem, the lowest widely separated from the upper spikes (when present) and subtended by a prolonged, setaceous bract (2–) 3–10 cm long; spikes composed of 1–5 carpellate flowers; herbaceous portion of leaf sheath white spotted

Spikes 3–15, the lowest approximate to or shortly separated from the upper spikes, subtended by a short, setaceous bract mostly shorter than 3 cm; spikes composed of 5–30 carpellate flowers; herbaceous portion of leaf sheath without white spots

c3.text: Leaf blades (0.8–) 1–1.9 mm wide, flat to partially folded; ligules 0.5–1.9 mm long; inflorescence (14–) 23–55 mm long, with (2–) 3 or 4 spikes, the terminal spike with (1–) 2–5 perigynia
Leaf blades 0.3–0.5 (–0.8) mm wide, involute; ligules 0.3–0.8 (–1.2) mm long; inflorescence 14–32 mm long, with 2 or 3 spikes, the terminal spike with 1–3 perigynia

c4.text: Perigynia ovate in outline, widest near base, with a serrulate-margined beak; inflorescence composed of 5–15 spikes that are aggregated together [Fig. ]

Perigynia elliptic-ovate to elliptic-oblong in outline, widest near the middle, with an entire- or serrulate-margined beak; inflorescence composed of 3–8 (–10) spikes, at the least the lower usually separate [Fig. ]

c5.text: Carpellate scales light red-brown, equaling to shortly exceeding and covering the perigynia; stems smooth on the angles; uppermost spike with a prolonged, basal, staminate portion comprising 33–67% of the entire spike; plants of brackish communities

Carpellate scales gray, gray-green, or light brown, slightly shorter than and not completely covering the perigynia; stems scabrous on the angles; uppermost spike with a short, basal, staminate comprising (0–) 15–54% of the entire spike; plants of freshwater and terrestrial communities

c6.text: Spikes composed of 5–10 (–14) carpellate flowers [Fig. ]; perigynia ascending to ascending-spreading, green, becoming brown; abaxial side of the beak with a distinct longitudinal slit; leaf blades 0.5–2.5 mm wide, green to yellow-green

Spikes composed of (5–) 10–20 (–30) carpellate flowers; perigynia appressed-ascending, gray-green, becoming yellow-brown; abaxial side of the beak without a slit or with an inconspicuous one; leaf blades (1.5–) 2–4 mm wide, gray-green to pale green

c1.text: This section contains exactly one species.
This section contains exactly one species.
This section contains exactly one species.
Sheaths loosely clasping the stem, septate-nodulose (i.e., with cross-veins connecting the elongate veins of the sheath), green and white-striped or -spotted; widest leaf blades 4–10 mm wide
Sheaths tightly clasping the stem, not septate-nodulose, usually not striped or spotted; widest leaf blades 0.9–4 (–5) mm wide

c2.text: Inflorescence elongate, (3–) 4–10 cm long, with remote lower spikes; body of perigynium with a narrow wing 0.1–0.2 mm wide (sometimes narrower in the basal portion of the perigynium)
Inflorescence relatively congested, 2–4 cm long, with crowded lower spikes; body of perigynium with a very narrow wing up to 0.1 mm wide

c3.text: Beak of perigynium entire along the margins
Beak of perigynium minutely serrulate along the margins

c4.text: Inflorescence open, with well-separated lower spikes; basal internodes of inflorescence 2 or more times as long as the lower spikes
Inflorescence dense, with approximate to crowded spikes; basal internodes of inflorescence less than 2 times as long as the lower spikes

c5.text: Stigmas straight, reflexed, or partially coiled, 0.03–0.06 mm wide; spongy base of perigynium 1–1.5 mm long
Stigmas 1- to 3-times coiled, 0.05–0.1 mm wide; spongy base of perigynium 0.5–1.3 mm long

c6.text: Widest leaves 0.9–1.5 mm wide; base of flowering stems 0.7–1.4 mm thick
Widest leaves 1.8–2.6 mm wide; base of flowering stems 1.5–2.2 mm thick

c7.text: Body of carpellate scale 1–1.8 mm long, up to the length of the perigynium it subtends; achenes 1.4–1.5 ×1.3–1.4 mm; inflorescence dense, the individual spikes not distinct

Body of carpellate scale 2.3–4.5 mm long, more than the length of the perigynium it subtends; achenes 1.5–2.3 ×1.3–2.1 mm; inflorescence dense to somewhat elongate, the individual spikes distinct or not

c8.text: Ligules (3.5–) 4–8 mm long, much longer than broad; perigynia 4–5.5 mm long; basal sheaths usually tinged with anthocyanin
Ligules up to 3 mm long, usually wider than long; perigynia 2.7–4.2 mm long; basal sheaths green to brown, without anthocyanic pigments

c9.text: Inflorescence a dense, globose to ovoid cluster 1–1.5 times as long as wide, the individual spikes highly congested and sometimes not even distinct; perigynia weakly veined (if at all) on the abaxial surface; achenes 1.5–1.7 ×1.3–1.5 mm

Inflorescence elongate to rather congested, usually more than 1.5 times as long as wide, at least the lower spikes usually ± distinct; perigynia either with 9–15 veins on the abaxial surface or ± veinless; achenes (1.8–) 1.9–2.2 × (1.8–) 1.9–2.1 mm

c1.text: Perigynia rounded and inconspicuously spongy-thickened at the base, adaxially without veins; sheaths red- or brown-dotted near the margins; achenes circular in outline
Perigynia truncate and conspicuously spongy-thickened at the base, with usually 7 veins adaxially; sheaths not dotted; achenes ovate

c2.text: Leaf sheaths smooth, not corrugated, the summits firm, thickened, yellow, and truncate; leaf blades minutely papillose on the adaxial surface, epistomic; inflorescence 3–6 cm long

Leaf sheaths usually corrugated on surface opposite leaf blade (smooth in C. oklahomensis ), the summits thin, fragile, colorless, and convex; leaf blades smooth on adaxial surface, not epistomic; inflorescence 5–15 cm long

c3.text: Lowermost 2 or 3 leaves with highly reduced blades; leaf sheaths smooth, prolonged above the junction of the blade and forming a tube that surrounds the stem; stems firm; ligules obtuse, up to 4 mm long
Lowermost leaves usually with ± well-developed blades; leaf sheaths corrugated, not prolonged above junction of blade; stems weak, easily compressed; ligules acute, up to 10 mm long

c1.text: Leaves shorter than the flowering stems; perigynia gold-brown at maturity, with a beak ca. as long as the body
Leaves equaling or taller than the flowering stems; perigynia brown at maturity, with a beak ca. to as long as the body

Apical portion of sheath opposite the leaf blade pale and red-dotted on the hyaline surface; perigynia spreading, olive-brown to black, with a pale, depressed stripe on the abaxial surface, not covered by their subtending scales; inflorescence relatively congested, the lowest internode 3–7 (–10) mm long

Apical portion of sheath opposite the leaf blade strongly copper-colored and red- dotted on the hyaline surface; perigynia appressed, light brown, without a pale, depressed stripe, covered by their subtending scales; inflorescence more open, the lowest internode 7–26 (–33) mm long
This section contains exactly one species.

Perigynia becoming gold-orange just prior to being shed, smooth or minutely papillose; lateral spikes relatively sparsely flowered, the internodes of the mid-portion (0.5–) 0.7–1.5 mm long; uppermost spike usually entirely staminate; carpellate scales ovate-oblong, divergent in fruit

Perigynia glaucous-white, densely papillose [Fig. ]; lateral spikes densely flowered, the internodes of the mid-portion 0.2–0.7 mm long; uppermost spike, or at least many in the population, gynecandrous; carpellate scales ovate-orbicular, ascending
At least the lower carpellate scales with the apex prolonged into a conspicuous, usually scabrous, awn [Figs. , ]
Carpellate scales unawned at the apex, at most with a minute, smooth cusp

c2.text: Lowest carpellate spike usually drooping on a peduncle (5–) 14–68 mm long; carpellate scales including awns (2.9–) 3.1–20 mm long, pale brown to copper-brown
Lowest carpellate spike ascending to arching on a peduncle 6–20 mm long; carpellate scales including awns 2.5–9 mm long, brown to red-brown or purple-brown

c3.text: Plants colonial from elongate rhizomes; lowermost spike 8–20 mm thick; plants of saline and brackish marshes and strands
Plants cespitose from short rhizomes; lowermost spike 5–10 mm thick; plants of non-saline wetlands and shorelines

c4.text: Lower sheaths glabrous; apex of carpellate scales retuse or less commonly trunctate [Fig. ]; perigynia obovoid to broad-obovoid (rarely ellipsoid)
Lower sheaths scabrous with short, stiff hairs; apex of carpellate scales acuminate to truncate (sometimes slightly retuse in C. mitchelliana ) [Fig. ]; perigynia ellipsoid to ovoid

c5.text: Apex of carpellate scales acute to acuminate; perigynia smooth or weakly papillose near the apex; achenes with a constriction
Apex of carpellate scales ± truncate; perigynia densely papillose throughout; achenes without a constriciton

c6.text: Perigynia long-papillose, with 2–5 veins on each face; carpellate scales dark brown to purple-brown, with a paler central band 10–33% as wide as the entire scale; achenes dull, with or without folds or constrictions; perigynium beak sometimes with scabrules about the orifice

Perigynia short-papillose, veinless or obscurely veined; carpellate scales bronze to brown, with a central pale band 33–50% as wide as the entire scale; achenes lustrous, with a fold across one face; perigynium beak without scabrules

c7.text: Lowermost spike arching to drooping; perigynium smooth, with a triangular, flat, often twisted, apex
Lowermost spike erect to ascending; perigynium minutely papillose, with a rounded to acute, only somewhat flattened, plane apex

c8.text: Lowest bract of inflorescence exceeding the total height of the inflorescence (often conspicuously so) [Fig. ]; leaf blades amphistomic
Lowest bract of inflorescence shorter than or equaling the total height of the inflorescence; leaf blades hypostomic (except C. nigra , which has stomates on the adaxial surface)

c9.text: Leaves 1.5–3.5 mm wide; perigynia with (3–) 5–7 veins on each surface; achenes dull; plants cespitose from short rhizomes; lateral spike entirely carpellate

Leaves 2.5–8 mm wide; perigynia without veins or with 1–4 obscure (rarely distinct) veins on one surface [Fig. ]; achenes glossy; plants colonial from elongate rhizomes; usually at least some of the lateral spikes androgynous

c10.text: Carpellate scales purple-brown to black; stems arising from the center of the previous year’s leaf tufts, surrounded by senescing leaves
Carpellate scales pale brown to red-brown; stems arising laterally, not surrounded by the previous year’s leaves

c11.text: Perigynia with 3–9 veins on each surface, the beak with scabrules about the orifice [Fig. ]; leaf blades with stomates on the adaxial surface
Perigynia without veins or with 1–4 obscure (rarely distinct) veins on one surface, the beak lacking scabrules; leaf blades lacking stomates on the adaxial surface

c12.text: Lower sheaths not fibrillose; sheaths of stems leaves convex and prolonged at summit; perigynia not spotted with red, with 3–5 veins on each surface

Lower sheaths splitting into an inconspicuous to prominent ladder-network of fibers [Fig. ]; sheaths of stem leaves concave at summit; perigynia sometimes red-spotted in apical portion, with 0–5 veins on each face

c13.text: Carpellate scales shorter than the perigynia (varying to as long as), acute at the apex; perigynia ovoid, acute to obtuse at the apex, with 0–5 veins on each surface, ascending; stems commonly ± equal in height to the leaves; lower leaf sheaths scabrous

Carpellate scales longer than the perigynia, acute to acuminate at the apex; perigynia obovoid, rounded at apex, without veins, divergent; stems commonly surpassing the leaves in height; lower leaf sheaths glabrous

c1.text: Carpellate scales with long, scabrous awns, the awns often equal in length to the body of scale; carpellate spikes ascending to drooping; carpellate scales often ciliate-margined
Carpellate scales awnless or with short, smooth awns shorter than the body of the scale; carpellate spikes erect to ascending; carpellate scales eciliate

c2.text: Stems produced singly or a few together from elongate rhizomes; staminate scales acute to acuminate at the apex (sometimes the lowermost scales with a short awn tip)
Stems cespitose, with short rhizomes connecting the individual stems; at least some of the staminate scales with scabrous awns

c3.text: Perigynia with 5–12 veins that remain separate nearly to the apex of the beak, the bodies broad-ellipsoid to subglobose, (1.8–) 2–4.2 mm wide; achenes papillose

Perigynia with 12–15 veins that converge near the base or middle of the beak (except for the 2 lateral ribs, which remain separate), the bodies ellipsoid to narrow-ovoid, 1–2.2 mm wide; achenes smooth

c4.text: Widest leaves (4–) 4.5–13 mm wide; spikes (12–) 15–22 mm thick; perigynium moderately contracted to a beak 0.7–0.9 (–1) times as long as its body
Widest leaves 2.4–4 (–5) mm wide; spikes 9–14 (–15) mm thick; perigynium abruptly contracted to a beak 0.7–1.3 times as long as its body

c5.text: Perigynium somewhat inflated, nearly terete to mildly compressed, with herbaceous texture, ascending to spreading, with gaps between many of the veins wider than 3 times the width of the veins; beak of perigynium terminated by 2 straight teeth 0.3–0.9 mm long; basal leaf sheaths usually strongly tinged with anthocyanic pigments

Perigynium scarcely inflated, definitely compressed, with coriaceous texture, horizontally spreading to reflexed, with gaps between most veins less than 2 times the width of the veins; beak of perigynium terminated by 2 straight to outwardly arching teeth 0.7–2.1 (–2.8) mm long; basal leaf sheaths usually pale brown, infrequently tinged with faint anthocyanin

c6.text: Perigynium beak terminated with 2 straight or slightly outcurved teeth 0.7–1.2 (–1.4) mm long; carpellate spikes 9–12 mm thick
Perigynium beak terminated with 2 strongly outcurved teeth 1.3–2.1 (–2.8) mm long; carpellate spikes 12–18 mm thick

c7.text: Stigmas 2; achenes biconvex; perigynia obscurely veined
Stigmas 3, achenes triangular in cross-section; perigynia distinctly veined

c8.text: Perigynium beak 0.3–0.9 mm long, obscurely bidentate at tip, the terminal teeth up to 0.3 mm long; leaves filiform, with involute margins, 0.5–2.5 mm wide
Perigynium beak (1–) 1.1–4.8 mm long, with 2 distinct apical teeth (0.2–) 0.3–1.9 mm long; leaves ± flat or folded (rarey U-shaped) in cross-section, 1.5–12 (–15) mm wide

c9.text: Achenes asymmetrical, with an indentation on one of the surfaces; widest perigynia (4–) 4.5–7 mm wide; lowermost bract of carpellate spikes with a blade more than 3 times as long as the inflorescence

Achenes symmetrical, lacking indentations; widest perigynia (1.5–) 2.5–3.5 (–4.5) mm wide; lowermost bract of carpellate spikes with a blade less than 3 times as long as the inflorescence (except in C. retrorsa , which has an elongate bract blade)

c10.text: Bract of lowermost carpellate spike with a blade (2.5–) 3–9 times as long as the inflorescence; perigynia horizontally spreading to reflexed; staminate spike often solitary (infrequently 2 or 3), barely elevated above the crowded cluster of carpellate spikes

Bract of lowermost carpellate spike with a blade up to 2.5 (–3) times as long as the inflorescence; perigynia ascending to spreading; staminate spikes 1–3, usually well elevated above the separate carpellate spikes

c11.text: Perigynium beak 2.4–4.2 (–4.8) mm long, scabrous in the apical portion
Perigynium beak (1–) 1.2–2.7 mm long, smooth

c12.text: Plants cespitose, from short rhizomes, with basally firm stems; ligules of leaves longer than wide; leaf sheaths with few cross-septa connecting the longitudinal veins; perigynia ascending, mostly arranged in 6 or 7 vertical ranks

Plants colonial, from elongate rhizomes, with basally thickened and ± spongy stems; ligules as wide as long; leaf sheaths with many cross-septa connecting the longitudinal veins; perigynia spreading, mostly arranged in 8–12 vertical ranks

c13.text: Leaf blades U-shaped in cross-section, white-green, 1.5–4.5 mm wide, the adaxial surface minutely papillose

Leaf blades flat to V-shaped in cross-section, pale green to green, (2.5–) 4.5–12 (–15) mm wide, smooth or rarely scabrous (note: the scabrules are easily viewed with low magnification and are more widely spaced than are the minute papillae of C. rostrata )

c1.text: Perigynium glabrous; leaf blades minutely papillose abaxially; ligules (6–) 11–45 mm long
Perigynium pubescent [Fig. ]; leaf blades not minutely papillose abaxially; ligules 2–12.5 mm long

c2.text: Leaf sheaths, and often the blades, pubescent; staminate scales, and often the carpellate scales, pubescent
Leaf sheaths and blades glabrous; staminate and carpellate scales glabrous

c1.text: Perigynia 3.7–6 mm long; carpellate scales retuse to obtuse, cuspidate; leaves dark green, mostly equaling or exceeding the reproductive stems; most carpellate spikes borne on long, often arching, peduncles to 13 cm emerging from basal nodes

Perigynia 2.4–2.9 mm long; carpellate scales acute to obtuse, without a cusp; leaves pale green, mostly shorter than the reproductive stems; carpellate spikes all borne above the base on peduncles to 7 cm long
This section contains exactly one species.
Perigynia glabrous; style persistent on the achene; leaf blades (2.6–) 5.5–21 mm wide
Perigynia pubescent; style articulated with the summit of the achene and deciduous from it at maturity; leaf blades 0.7–8.5 mm wide

c2.text: Perigynia 3–4.5 mm long, glaucous; perigynium beak 0.3–0.6 mm long, weakly bidentate, the apical teeth up to 0.2 mm
Perigynia 3.9–7.8 mm long, not glaucous; perigynium beak 0.5–1.6 mm long, terminated by 2 distinct teeth (0.1–) 0.2–0.7 (–0.9) mm long

c3.text: Leaves with blades (5.5–) 8.5–21 mm wide, the longest ligules 13–40 mm long
Leaves with blades 2.6–5 (–6) mm wide, the longest ligules 1.8–12.5 mm long

c4.text: Beak of perigynium with soft, hyaline, obscure teeth; staminate spikes 1 or rarely 2, borne on peduncles 2–20 mm long, usually exceeding the height of the lowest bract of the inflorescence
Beak of perigynium with distinct, firm teeth 0.2–0.8 mm long; staminate spikes 1–3, borne on peduncles (8–) 20–90 mm long, usually equaled or overtopped by the lowest bract

c5.text: Perigynia 4.5–6.5 mm long, the pubescence short and relatively sparse, not concealing the veins or cellular details of the perigynium body; plants of dry, sandy or rocky soil
Perigynia 2.4–5 (–5.2) mm long, the pubescence longer and dense, concealing the veins and cellular details of the perigynium body; plants of shorelines and wetlands

c6.text: Leaf blades M-shaped in cross-section (at least when young), sometimes ± flat at maturity, (2–) 2.2–4.5 (–6) mm wide, not prolonged apically into an elongate, filiform tip, with a prominent midvein that forms a sharp, abaxial keel for much of the lengt
Leaf blades involute, 0.7–2 (–2.2) mm wide, prolonged at the apex into an elongate, sometimes curled, filiform tip, with a low, rounded midvein forming an inconspicuous abaxial keel

c1.text: This section contains exactly one species.
This section contains exactly one species.
All the carpellate spikes of a plant borne well above the base in proximity to a staminate spike on stems with leaf bearing nodes

Some of the carpellate spikes solitary and borne on leafless peduncles originating from the plant base without associated staminate spikes (the solitary carpellate spikes sometimes hidden among the leaf bases), the other carpellate spikes borne on leaf-bearing stems with a staminate spike [Fig. ]

c2.text: Perigynium body (i.e., excluding the beak and stipe-like base) subglobose, about as wide as long as thick
Perigynium body ellipsoid to obovoid, definitely longer than thick

c3.text: Widest leaf blades (2.6–) 3–5 mm wide; plants cespitose, with short rhizomes; remnants of old leaves not or only slightly fibrous; staminate spikes 1–2.5 mm wide
Leaf blades 0.5–3 (–3.6) mm wide; plants extensively colonial, with long rhizomes; remnants of old leaves slightly to strongly fibrous; staminate spikes (1.3–) 2–4.6 mm wide

c4.text: Perigynia with a beak 0.5–0.9 mm long and 0.1–0.5 times as long as the body of the perigynium; uppermost stem leaves with a well-developed blade; apical portion of the sheath opposite the leaf blade shallowly concave, the cleft extending 0.2–1.6 mm below the junction with the leaf blade

Perigynia with a beak 0.9–1.6 mm long and 0.5–1 times as long as the body of the perigynium [Fig. ]; uppermost stem leaves with a poorly developed blade; apical portion of the sheath opposite the leaf blade deeply concave, the cleft extending 0.4–6.9 mm below the junction with the leaf blade

c5.text: Lowest carpellate spike short-pedunculate, separated from the upper spikes by a gap of more than 7 mm; lowest bract of inflorescence usually equaling or exceeding total height of inflorescence

Lowest carpellate spike sessile, approximate to or overlapping the upper spikes, usually with a gap of less than 7 mm from the upper spikes; lowest bract of inflorescence usually shorter than total height of inflorescence (except in C. deflexa and C. reznicekii )

c6.text: Carpellate scales to as long as the perigynia they subtend, therefore, the perigynia clearly visible within the intact spikes
Carpellate scales equaling to slightly exceeding the perigynia, therefore, the perigynia largely concealed within the intact spikes

c7.text: Reproductive stems 5–31 cm tall, usually equaled or exceeded by the leaves; perigynia 2.3–3.1 mm long (in part)
Reproductive stems 21–47 cm tall, usually exceeding the leaves; perigynia 3.2–4.2 mm long

c8.text: Peduncle of staminate spike 0.4–9.9 mm long; remnants of old leaves slightly or not at all fibrous; reproductive stems (10–) 20–45 cm tall; achenes 1.2–1.4 (–1.7) mm long; perigynia 2.3–3.3 mm long

Peduncle of staminate spike (0.2–) 0.3–1.2 mm long; remnants of old leaves slightly to strongly fibrous; reproductive stems 1.9–20 (–27) cm tall; achenes 1.4–2 mm long; perigynia (2.5–) 2.8–3.7 (–3.9) mm long

c9.text: Widest leaf blades (1.9–) 2.3–4.5 mm wide; carpellate scales sometimes with anthocyanic pigment extending from near the margin to the green or brown stripes on either side of the midvein; reproductive stems 8–38 cm tall; longest staminate spike exceeding the carpellate spikes by (0–) 0.5–5.1 (–7.3) mm

Widest leaf blades 1.2–2.2 (–2.5) mm wide; carpellate scales never with anthocyanic pigment extending from near the margin to the green or brown stripes on either side of the midvein; reproductive stems 1.9–9.1 (–13.7) cm tall; longest staminate spike exceeding the carpellate spikes by 0–3.7 mm

c10.text: Carpellate scales to as long as the perigynia they subtend, therefore, the perigynia clearly visible within the intact spikes; remnants of old leaves slightly or not at all fibrous; lowermost bract of inflorescence usually equaling or exceeding total height of inflorescence (in part)

Carpellate scales equaling to slightly exceeding the perigynia, therefore, the perigynia largely concealed within the intact spikes; remnants of old leaves weakly to strongly fibrous; lowermost bract of inflorescence usually shorter than total height of inflorescence

c11.text: Perigynium 3.1–4.7 mm long, with a beak 0.9–2 mm long; leaf blades coriaceous or herbaceous
Perigynium 2.2–3.2 mm long, with a beak 0.4–1 mm long [Fig. ]; leaf blades herbaceous

c1.text: Uppermost spike unisexual, entirely staminate
Uppermost spike bisexual, gynecandrous

c2.text: Perigynia densely pilose; lateral spikes 2–4 mm wide; leaves with ligules longer than wide
Perigynia glabrous or sparsely pilose; lateral spikes (3–) 4–11 mm wide; leaves with ligules shorter than wide to as long as wide (rarely longer than wide)

c3.text: Uppermost spike (5–) 11–20 mm long, densely flowered throughout; anthers 0.7–1.3 (–1.6) mm long
Uppermost spike 20–35 (–40) mm long, loosely flowered near base; anthers (1–) 1.6–2 (–2.8) mm long

c4.text: Carpellate scales awnless or sometimes with a minute mucro; perigynia glabrous, smooth, bluntly triangular in cross-section; anthers 1.3–2.2 mm long
Carpellate scales with an awn 0.5–2 mm long; perigynia sparsely pubescent, papillose, ± terete in cross-section; anthers 2–3 mm long

c1.text: This section contains exactly one species.
Uppermost spike usually gynecandrous
Uppermost spike usually unisexual and staminate

c2.text: Perigynia with 2 prominent, marginal veins, the remaining veins absent or obscure, without red dots; basal leaf sheaths green to green-brown, sometimes with a slight suffusion of anthocyanin
Perigynia with 2 prominent, marginal veins and 7–15 additional, distinct veins, often red-dotted; basal leaf sheaths suffused with dark red to purple-brown

c3.text: Perigynia 4.5–6 mm long, becoming dull orange-brown at maturity; carpellate scales with conspicuous awns 2.5–3 mm long
Perigynia 2–5 mm long, not becoming orange-brown; carpellate scales acute to cuspidate or with a short awn shorter than 1 mm

c4.text: Lateral spikes gynecandrous, the basal 1 or 2 flowers staminate, borne on elongate peduncles usually exceeding the length of the associated spike, 4–6 mm thick; perigynia 3.5–5 mm long, abruptly tapering to a short beak

Lateral spikes unisexual and carpellate, usually borne on peduncles that are shorter than or equal to the length of the associated spike, 2–3.5 mm thick; perigynia 2–3.7 mm long, tapering to a beakless apex

c5.text: Leaf sheaths glabrous; leaf blades 3–9 mm wide
Leaf sheaths pubescent; leaf blades 1.5–3 mm wide

c6.text: Basal leaf sheaths brown, those of previous years persisting as abundant, fibrous remains; perigynia abruptly tapered to a long, tubular beak nearly as long as the perigynium body
Basal sheaths red-purple, those of previous years not fibrous or only inconspicuously so; perigynia gradually tapered to a beak obviously shorter than the perigynium body

c7.text: Leaf blades pubescent; carpellate spikes 8–25 ×4–5 mm; perigynia with 2 prominent lateral veins and 5–7 additional, finer veins
Leaf blades glabrous; carpellate spikes 25–80 ×2–3 mm; perigynia with 2 prominent lateral veins and 10–20 additional, finer veins

c8.text: Perigynia fusiform to narrow-ellipsoid, 5–9.5 mm long; achene elevated above base of perigynium on a stipe 0.5–1.5 mm long; leaf blades 2–5 (–7) mm wide
Perigynia ellipsoid-ovoid, 3–5 mm long; achene sessile at base of perigynium; leaf blades 3–10 (–13) mm wide

c1.text: Carpellate spikes spherical to short-ovoid, 1–4.2 cm long; lowermost bract of inflorescence usually sheathless or with a sheath shorter than 3 mm; achenes ellipsoid to obovoid; beak of perigynium 1.5–4.2 mm long
Carpellate spikes ovoid to cylindric, 1.5–8 cm long; lowermost bract of inflorescence with a closed sheath 5–150 mm long; achenes rhomboid; beak of perigynium 6–10 mm long

c2.text: Carpellate spikes spherical, with 8–35 perigynia radiating in all directions; base of perigynium cuneate; surface of perigynium dull

Carpellate spikes mostly short-ovoid, with 1–12 (–20) usually ascending to spreading perigynia (uncommonly the lower perigynia are reflexed); base of perigynium convexly rounded; surface of perigynium somewhat lustrous

c3.text: Achenes (2.2–) 2.4–3.4 mm wide, nearly as wide as long, the angles knobbed with nipple-like points [Fig. ]
Achenes 1.7–2.6 (–2.8) mm wide, longer than wide, the angles without knobs or only obscurely knobbed [Fig. ]

c1.text: Lowermost carpellate spikes spreading or drooping on long peduncles 10–40 mm long; perigynia dark brown to dark red-brown at maturity; achene filling basal of perigynium or less

Lowermost carpellate spikes ascending to erect, sessile or on short peduncles less than 10 mm long; perigynia pale green to white-green or pale brown to yellow-brown at maturity; achene nearly filling body of perigynium

c2.text: Stems aphyllopodic, arising in tufts from long, horizontal rhizomes; perigynia gray-green or white-green, papillose; carpellate scales usually equaling or exceeding the perigynia; carpellate spikes 10–25 mm long, not forming a dense apical cluster

Stems phyllopodic and cespitose, arising from leafy tufts, without elongate rhizomes; perigynia pale green becoming gold-brown, smooth or inconspicuously papillose; carpellate scales usually shorter than the perigynia; carpellate spikes 5–12 mm long, the upper spikes densely aggregated

c1.text: Carpellate scales longer than the perigynia they subtend [Fig. ]; lowest bract of inflorescence 3–15 cm long, equaling or exceeding the height of the inflorescence; stems usually phyllopodic, with dead leaf remains at base

Carpellate scales shorter than (rarely as long as) the perigynia they subtend [Fig. ]; lowest bract of inflorescence 0.5–7 cm long, shorter than the height of the inflorescence; stems usually aphyllopodic, without dead leaf remains at base (usually phyllopodic and with dead leaf remains at base in C. rariflora )

c2.text: Carpellate scales 1.3–1.8 mm wide, narrower than the perigynia they subtend; lateral spikes usually androgynous, (10–) 25–50 mm long; leaf blades 2–5 mm wide

Carpellate scales 2–3.4 mm wide, wider than (rarely as wide as) the perigynia they subtend; lateral spikes usually unisexual and carpellate (sometimes androgynous in C. limosa ), 6–20 mm long; leaf blades 1–2.5 mm wide

c3.text: Perigynia acute at apex, with a beak 0.1–0.5 mm long; stems usually aphyllopodic, without dead leaf remains at base; lateral spikes with 8–30 perigynia; leaf blades glaucous-green, involute

Perigynia rounded to obtuse at apex, with a beak up to 0.3 mm long; stems usually phyllopodic, with dead leaf remains at base; lateral spikes with 2–10 perigynia [Fig. ]; leaf blades green, relatively flat or sometimes with involute margins

c1.text: Perigynia 1.8–3.9 (–4.2) mm long, the lower of each spike spreading; perigynium beak straight or bent at an angle of 0–15 (–25) degrees from the perigynium body; ligule of apical leaves obsolete
Perigynia 3.5–6.3 mm long, the lower of each spike reflexed; perigynium beak bent at an angle of 13–72 degrees from the perigynium body [Fig. ]; ligule of apical leaves well formed

c2.text: Carpellate scales red-brown, contrasting with color of perigynia; perigynia 4–6.3 mm long, with a moderately to strongly bent, scabrous beak offset (15–) 26–72 degrees from the perigynium body [Fig. ]
Carpellate scales yellow-green, of similar color as the perigynia; perigynia 3.5–4.8 mm long, with a weakly to moderately bent, smooth beak offset 13–48 degrees from the perigynium body

c1.text: This section contains exactly one species.

Widest leaf blades 1.6–3.5 (–4.2) mm wide; upper leaf sheaths and bract sheaths concave at the summit; staminate spikes 6–15 mm long; carpellate scales 33–66% as long as the perigynia, not terminated by an awn

Widest leaf blades 6–18 (–21) mm wide; upper leaf sheaths and bract sheaths convex at the summit; staminate spikes 12–40 mm long; carpellate scales mostly 66–100% as long as the perigynia (rarely surpassing the perigynia), usually prolonged into an awn
This section contains exactly one species.

Staminate spike on a peduncle 1–35 mm long, shorter than to barely exceeding the uppermost carpellate spike; stems cespitose on short, inconspicuous rhizomes; lowermost spike usually arising from upper half of reproductive stem

Staminate spike on a peduncle (4–) 9–76 (–91) mm long, overtopping the uppermost carpellate spike; stems produced singly or a few together from elongate rhizomes; lowermost spike usually arising from lower half of reproductive stem
This section contains exactly one species.
Shoots anthocyanic at the base, ranging from a slight tinging of the brown background to a strong purple coloration
Shoots lacking anthocyanic pigments at the base, mostly pale brown to brown

c2.text: Vegetative leaf blades 10–52 mm wide; blades of upper bracting leaves spathe-like, lanceolate to narrow-lanceolate, 4–16 mm wide; carpellate scales ± truncate and apiculate at the apex, lacking awns; flowering stems 2–2.4 mm wide, distinctly winged (in part)

Vegetative leaf blades 1–12 mm wide; blades of upper bracting leaves not spathe-like, mostly linear, 0.5–6 mm wide; carpellate scales truncate to acuminate at the apex, usually with awns; flowering stems 0.5–2 mm wide, unwinged or with obscure wing angles

c3.text: Longest carpellate spike 19–33 mm long, the basal internode (i.e., the distance between the lowest and next apical flowers) 3.5–14 mm [Fig. ]; perigynia varying from remote to loosely imbricate, with a nearly straight to bent beak; upper portion of flowering stem ± smooth on the angles

Longest carpellate spike 11–21 mm long, with a basal internode of 1.1–3.2 (–4.8) mm [Fig. ]; perigynia closely imbricate, with an abruptly bent beak; upper portion of flowering stem scabrous on the angles

c4.text: Vegetative leaves 10–52 mm wide; blades of upper bracting leaves spathe-like, lanceolate to narrow-lanceolate, 4–16 mm wide; flowering stems 2–2.4 mm wide, distinctly winged (in part)
Vegetative leaves 3–26 mm wide; blades of upper bracting leaves not spathe-like, mostly linear, 0.8–8 mm wide; flowering stems 0.5–2 mm wide, unwinged or with obscure wing angles

c5.text: Perigynia with only 2 evident lateral veins, the remaing 6–16 veins faint; anthers (1.4–) 1.6–2 (–2.4) mm long
Perignynia with 22–39 distinct veins; anthers (2–) 2.4–4 (–4.5) mm long (as short as 1.8 mm in C. blanda )

c6.text: Carpellate spikes 6–20 mm long, with crowded perigynia, the basal internode (i.e., the distance between the lowest and next apical flower) 0.9–2.4 mm long [Fig. ]; upper portion of flowering stem scabrous on the angles

Carpellate spikes 9–62 mm long, the longest usually more than 18 mm, with approximate but not crowded perigynia, the basal internode (2.2–) 2.8–7.5 mm long [Fig. ]; upper portion of flowering stem smooth on the angles

c7.text: Perigynia tapering to a straight or merely outcurved beak 0.5–1.7 mm long; staminate scales 3.2–4.2 ×1–1.2 mm
Perigynia abruptly tapering to a short, bent beak 0.2–0.5 mm long; staminate scales 1.8–3.2 ×1.4–1.8 mm

c8.text: Perigynia 2.6–3.8 mm long, usually more abruptly tapered in the apical portion than in the basal portion; staminate spikes 12–26 mm long
Perigynia 3.4–5 mm long, usually ± evenly tapered in the apical and basal portions; staminate spikes 22–36 mm long

c1.text: Leaf sheaths, and sometimes the blades along the abaxial midrib, hispidulous; beak of perigynium (0.5–) 0.8–1.3 mm long
Leaf sheaths and blades glabrous; beak of perigynium 0–0.6 mm long (up to 1.2 mm long in C. oligocarpa )

c2.text: Basal leaf sheaths of reproductive stems yellow-brown to dark brown, without anthocyanic pigments; carpellate spikes with (6–) 12–45 (–65) perigynia [Fig. ]
Basal leaf sheaths of reproductive stems purple-red to dark purple (very rarely dark brown); carpellate spikes with 2–18 perigynia

c3.text: Peduncles of lateral spikes scaberulous; leaf blades green; carpellate scales with awns (0.2–) 1.2–2.7 mm long (very rarely awnless) [Fig. ]
Peduncles of lateral spikes smooth; leaf blades very glaucous; carpellate scales awnless or with an awn up to 1 (–1.5) mm long [Fig. ]

c4.text: Lowermost bract of inflorescence with a tightly clasping sheath; widest leaf blades (1.8–) 2.4–4 (–4.6) mm wide; carpellate spikes loosely flowered, many of the perigynia borne in 2 ranks; beak of perigynium 0.4–1.2 mm long

Lowermost bract of inflorescence with a loosely clasping sheath; widest leaf blades (3.7–) 4.2–8.2 (–9.1) mm wide; carpellate spikes densely flowered, the perigynia spirally arranged around the spike axis; beak of perigynium (0.2–) 0.3–0.6 mm long

c5.text: Perigynia terete or nearly so in cross-section, (1.8–) 2–2.6 mm wide, 1.8–2.3 (–2.6) times as long as wide; achenes borne on a stipe (0.2–) 0.3–0.4 (–0.5) mm long
Perigynia obtusely trigonous in cross-section, 1.5–1.9 (–2.2) mm wide, (2.2–) 2.5–3.1 times as long as wide; achenes borne on a stipe (0.3–) 0.4–0.6 mm long

c1.text: Sheaths anthocyanic at the base, those borne from the lower half of the flowering stem with blades up to 1.9 cm long [Fig. ]
Sheaths white to brown at the base, those borne from the lower half of the flowering stem producing blades 2–24 cm long

c2.text: Foliage strongly glaucous; leaves dimorphic—those of the vegetative shoots 10–25 mm wide, those of the flowering stems 2–6 mm wide, the former 3.8–9 times as wide as the latter; leaves from the lower half of the flowering stem with blades 2–6.2 cm long

Foliage green or glaucous; leaves slightly dimorphic if at all, 1–12 mm wide, those of the vegetative shoots 1–3.5 times as wide as those of the flowering stem; leaves from the lower half of the flowering stem with blades 4.5–24 cm long

c3.text: Staminate spikes 0.6–1.4 (–1.6) mm wide; staminate scales obtuse at the apex, the middle ones 2.6–3.6 (–3.8) mm long; vegetative shoots much taller than the flowering stems
Staminate spikes (1–) 1.2–2.7 mm wide; staminate scales acute at the apex, the middle ones 3.6–5.5 mm long; vegetative shoots shorter than to slightly taller than the flowering stems

c4.text: Lower 1–3 scales of the carpellate spikes empty or subtending staminate flowers only [Fig. ]; leaves of the vegetative shoots 3–11.8 mm wide, glaucous; lower spikes 4–6 mm thick
All scales of the carpellate spikes subtending carpellate flowers; leaves of the vegetative shoots 1–5.3 mm wide, green; lower spikes 3–4 mm thick

root.text: Woody angiosperms with opposite or whorled leaves
Herbaceous angiosperms with superior ovaries and zygomorphic flowers
Herbaceous angiosperms with superior ovaries, actinomorphic flowers, and 2 or more distinct carpels
Herbaceous angiosperms with superior ovaries, actinomorphic flowers, connate petals, and a solitary carpel or 2 or more connate carpels
Herbaceous angiosperms with superior ovaries, actinomorphic flowers, distinct petals or the petals lacking, and 2 or more connate carpels
